**Tafsir of Surat al-Ma'idah** [It is a Medinan surah] [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah Shayban narrated to us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: "I was holding the reins of al-'Adba', the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when Surat al-Ma'idah was revealed to him in its entirety. Its weight nearly broke the camel's shoulder" [[Musnad (6/455). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/13): "It contains Shahr ibn Hawshab, who is weak, though he has been deemed trustworthy."]].

Ibn Mardawayh related from the hadith of Salih ibn Suhayl, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, who said: "Umm 'Amr narrated to me, from her paternal uncle, that he was on a journey with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when Surat al-Ma'idah was revealed to him, and the neck of the riding beast broke under its weight" [[Also narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in his Musnad, al-Baghawi in his Mu'jam, and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/3).]].

Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Huyayy ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to me, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli [[In R: "al-Khatali"; in A: "al-Jabali".]], from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: "Surat al-Ma'idah was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was riding his camel, and she could not bear him, so he dismounted from her."

Ahmad alone narrated this [[Musnad (2/176). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/13): "It contains Ibn Lahi'ah, and most scholars regard him as weak, though his hadith may be good."]].

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Qutaybah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb, from Huyayy, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: "The last surah to be revealed was Surat al-Ma'idah and al-Fath." Al-Tirmidhi then said: "This is a gharib (rare) hasan hadith." It has also been related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The last surah to be revealed was: ﴿When the help of Allah comes, and victory﴾ [Surat al-Nasr: 1]."

Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak, through the chain of 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb, a version similar to al-Tirmidhi's narration, and then said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3063) and al-Mustadrak (2/311).]].

Al-Hakim also said: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, Bahr ibn Nasr narrated to us, who said: "It was read to 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed me, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: 'I performed Hajj and entered upon 'A'ishah, and she said to me: "O Jubayr, do you recite al-Ma'idah?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed, it is the last surah revealed. Whatever you find in it that is lawful, consider it lawful, and whatever you find in it that is unlawful, consider it unlawful."'" Then he said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it."

Ahmad related it from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, and added: "I asked her about the character (khuluq) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: 'The Qur'an.'" al-Nasa'i also related it from the hadith of Ibn Mahdi [[al-Mustadrak (2/311), al-Musnad (6/188), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11138).]].

* *

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Mis'ar narrated to us, Ma'n and 'Awf narrated to me, or one of them, that a man came to 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] and said: "Give me a charge (u'had ilayya)." He said: "When you hear Allah say: ﴿O you who believe﴾, then give it your attention, for it is either a good that He commands, or an evil that He forbids."

He also said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim (Duhaym) narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: "When Allah says: ﴿O you who believe﴾ and then gives a command, the Prophet ﷺ is among them."

Ahmad ibn Sinan also narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Khaythamah, who said: "Everything in the Qur'an that begins with ﴿O you who believe﴾ is found in the Torah as: 'O you the poor (al-masakin).'"

As for what was related from Zayd ibn Isma'il al-Sa'igh al-Baghdadi, who narrated from Mu'awiyah (i.e., Ibn Hisham), from 'Isa ibn Rashid, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "There is no verse in the Qur'an beginning with ﴿O you who believe﴾ except that 'Ali is its leader (sayyiduha), its noble one (sharifuha), and its prince (amiruha). And none of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ was rebuked in the Qur'an except 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, for he was never rebuked in any matter of it." This is a gharib report, its wording contains a rejected element (nakarah), and its chain is open to question.

Al-Bukhari said: "This 'Isa ibn Rashid is unknown (majhul), and his report is munkar (rejected)." I say: As for 'Ali ibn Badhimah, although he is trustworthy (thiqah), he is an extreme Shi'i, and his report in such matters carries suspicion and is not accepted. As for his statement: "No one among the Companions remained without being rebuked in the Qur'an except 'Ali," it refers only to the verse commanding charity before private consultation (al-najwa). Many have mentioned that no one acted upon it except 'Ali. And the verse was revealed: ﴿Are you apprehensive about offering charity before your private consultation? So when you did not do so and Allah forgave you...﴾ [Surat al-Mujadilah: 13]. Whether this constitutes a rebuke is open to question, for it has been said that the command was recommended (nadb) rather than obligatory (ijab), and that it was then abrogated (nuski'a, i.e., naskh) for them before any act was performed, so no one among them was seen to oppose it. His statement about 'Ali, "He was never rebuked in any part of the Qur'an," is also open to question, for the verse in al-Anfal that rebuked those who accepted ransom encompassed all who advised taking it, and none was spared from it except 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. From this, and from what preceded, the weakness of this report becomes clear. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, Yunus narrated to me, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim said: "I read the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which was written to 'Amr ibn Hazm when he sent him to Najran. The letter was with Abu Bakr ibn Hazm, and in it: 'This is a declaration from Allah and His Messenger: ﴿O you who believe, fulfill the contracts﴾,' and he wrote the verses from it until he reached: ﴿Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/454).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm narrated to me, from his father, who said: "This is the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which is with us, which he wrote to 'Amr ibn Hazm when he sent him to Yemen, to instruct its people in religion, teach them the Sunnah, and collect their charities. He wrote to him a letter and a covenant, and commanded him in it with his orders. He wrote: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. This is a letter from Allah and His Messenger: ﴿O you who believe, fulfill the contracts﴾. A covenant from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to 'Amr ibn Hazm, when he sent him to Yemen, commanding him to fear Allah in all his affairs, for indeed Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good'" [[Also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (5/413) through the chain of Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Yunus ibn Bukayr.]].

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Fulfill the contracts﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and others said: "By contracts ('uqud) is meant covenants ('uhud)." Ibn Jarir related consensus (al-ijma') on this. He said: "The covenants are what they bound themselves to through alliances and other agreements." 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿O you who believe, fulfill the contracts﴾: "By covenants is meant what Allah has made lawful and what He has made unlawful, and what He has obligated and set as limits in the entire Qur'an. So do not betray and do not break them." Then he emphasized this, saying: ﴿And those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined...﴾ up to His words: ﴿the evil home﴾ [Surat al-Ra'd: 25].

Al-Dahhak said concerning ﴿Fulfill the contracts﴾: "It is what Allah has made lawful and unlawful, and what Allah has taken as a covenant from those who acknowledge faith in the Prophet ﷺ and the Book, that they fulfill what Allah has obligated upon them of the obligations concerning the lawful and the unlawful."

Zayd ibn Aslam said concerning ﴿Fulfill the contracts﴾: "They are six: the covenant of Allah, the contract of alliance, the contract of partnership, the contract of sale, the contract of marriage, and the contract of oath."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "They are five, among them: the alliance of the pre-Islamic period (hilf al-jahiliyyah) and the partnership of mufawadah."

Some who held that there is no option (khiyar) in the council of sale (majlis al-bay') have used this verse, ﴿Fulfill the contracts﴾, as evidence. They said: "This indicates the binding nature and validity of the contract, and therefore requires the negation of the option of the council." This is the position of Abu Hanifah and Malik. But al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and the majority disagreed, and their proof is what is established in the two Sahihs from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The two parties to a sale have the option (bi'l-khiyar) as long as they have not separated" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2109) and Sahih Muslim no. (1531).]]. In another wording in al-Bukhari: "When two men engage in a sale, each of them has the option as long as they have not separated" [[The wording in Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2112) and Sahih Muslim no. (1531).]]. This is explicit in establishing the option of the council that follows the conclusion of the sale. It is not contrary to the binding nature of the contract; rather, it is one of its legal requirements, so exercising it is part of fulfilling the contract.

* *

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock﴾ refer to camels, cattle, and sheep. This was said by al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others. Ibn Jarir said: "It is also so in the usage of the Arabs." Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, and others have used this verse as evidence for the permissibility of eating a fetus found dead in its mother's womb when she is slaughtered. There is a hadith on this in the Sunan, related by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, through the chain of Mujalid, from Abu al-Waddak Jabr ibn Nawf, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we slaughter a she-camel, or we slaughter a cow or a sheep, and in its belly is a fetus. Shall we discard it or eat it?' He said: 'Eat it if you wish, for its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother.'" Al-Tirmidhi said: "It is a hasan hadith" [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2827), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1476), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3199).]].

[And] [[Addition from manuscript R.]] Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Faris narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Attab ibn Bashir narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Haddad al-Makki narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The slaughter of the fetus is the slaughter of its mother." Abu Dawud alone narrated it [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2828).]].

* *

The words of Allah: ﴿Except what is recited to you﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "By this is meant carrion (al-maytah), blood, and the flesh of swine." Qatadah said: "By this is meant carrion and that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned."

And the apparent meaning, Allah knows best, is that what is intended by this is His saying: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked, the strangled animal, the animal beaten to death, the animal that falls to its death, the animal gored to death, and what a beast of prey has eaten﴾. Although these are among the livestock (al-an'am), they are forbidden because of these occurrences. For this reason He said: ﴿except what you slaughter properly, and what is sacrificed on the stone altars﴾, meaning from among them. For that is forbidden and cannot be made up for or compensated. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Lawful to you are the beasts of cattle, except what is recited to you﴾, meaning except what will be recited to you of the prohibition of some of them in certain circumstances.

* *

His saying: ﴿not hunting game while you are in the state of ihram (ihram: the state of ritual consecration for pilgrimage)﴾. Some of them said: this is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). What is meant by "the livestock" is that which includes the domesticated, namely camels, cattle and sheep, and that which includes the wild, such as gazelles, oxen and wild asses. So He excepted from the domesticated what was previously mentioned, and He excepted from the wild the hunting of game while in the state of ihram.

It was also said: what is meant is: "We have made lawful to you the livestock, except what is excluded for one who has committed himself to the prohibition of game, and that is forbidden," like His saying: ﴿But whoever is compelled, neither desiring it nor exceeding the limit, (there is no sin upon him)﴾. That is: We permitted the consumption of carrion to the one who is compelled, on condition that he is neither desiring it nor exceeding the limit. That is, just as We made the livestock lawful to you in all circumstances, so forbid yourselves hunting during the state of ihram, for Allah has decreed this, and He is the All-Wise in all that He commands and forbids. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah decrees what He wills﴾.

Then He said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: by this He means the rites of Hajj.

Mujahid said: as-Safa and al-Marwah, and the hadi (sacrificial animals) and the budn (large camels and cattle offered as sacrifice) are among the rites of Allah.

It was also said: the rites of Allah are His sacred prohibitions which He has forbidden, that is: do not violate the sacred prohibitions of Allah which He has forbidden. For this reason He said [the Exalted]: ﴿nor the sacred month﴾, meaning by this: its sanctity and acknowledging its honour, and abandoning what Allah has forbidden of engaging in it, such as initiating fighting, and emphasising avoidance of the prohibitions. As He said: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting therein is great sin﴾ [al-Baqarah: 217]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred. That is the correct religion, so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ [at-Tawbah: 36].

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Abu Bakrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Indeed, time has returned to its original form, the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three consecutive ones, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban."

This indicates the continuation of their sanctity until the end of time, as is the view of a group of the early generations (salaf).

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿nor the sacred month﴾, that is: do not consider fighting in it lawful. Likewise said Muqatil ibn Hayyan and 'Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, and Ibn Jarir also chose this view. The majority, however, held that this ruling is abrogated (mansukh; abrogation is the annulment of a ruling by a later revelation, naskh), and that it is permissible to initiate fighting in the sacred months. They cited His saying: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [at-Tawbah: 5]. They said: the intended months are the four months of travel (ashhur at-tasyir), and He did not exclude any sacred month from the others.

Imam Abu Ja'far (Ibn Jarir al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, related the consensus that Allah has permitted fighting the people of polytheism in the sacred months and other months of the year. He said: likewise they agreed that if a polytheist hung around his neck or on his arms the bark of all the trees of the Sacred Precinct (haram), that would not be a safe-conduct for him from being killed, if no covenant of protection (dhimmah) from the Muslims or a guarantee of safety had preceded for him. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 9/479.) This question has another discussion, which has a more extensive place than this.

His saying: ﴿nor the offerings, nor the garlands﴾, meaning: do not abandon sending offerings to the House, for in that is the glorification of the rites of Allah. And do not abandon garlanding them on their necks, so that they are distinguished thereby from other livestock, and so that it is known that they are an offering to the Ka'bah, so that whoever intends them with harm will avoid them, and whoever sees them will be moved to bring the like of them. For whoever calls to a good offering has a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without their rewards being diminished in any way. For this reason, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj, he spent the night at Dhu al-Hulayfah, which is the valley of al-'Aqiq. When morning came he went around to his wives, and they were nine. Then he bathed, perfumed himself, and prayed two rak'ahs. Then he marked his offering (ash'ara hadyahu) and garlanded it, and he assumed ihram for Hajj and 'Umrah together. His offering consisted of many camels, more than sixty, of the finest forms and colours, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That [is so]; and whoever honours the rites of Allah, indeed it is from the piety of hearts﴾ [al-Hajj: 32].

One of the early scholars said: glorifying them is considering them fine and fat.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to look carefully at the eye and the ear. (Related by the authors of the Sunan.) [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2804; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1498; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/216; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3142.]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿nor the garlands﴾, so do not consider them lawful. In the Jahiliyyah, when they set out from their homelands outside the sacred months, they would garland themselves with hair and wool, and the polytheists of the Sacred Precinct would garland themselves with bark from the trees of the Sacred Precinct, and thereby they were safe.

Ibn Abi Hatim related it, then said: Muhammad ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: two verses of this surah were abrogated: the verse about the garlands, and His saying: ﴿So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 42].

Al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan narrated to us, Zakariyya ibn 'Adi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn who said: I said to al-Hasan: was anything abrogated from al-Ma'idah? He said: No.

'Ata' said: they used to garland themselves with the trees of the Sacred Precinct and thereby they were safe, so Allah forbade cutting its trees. Likewise said Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿nor those who make for the Sacred House, seeking bounty from their Lord and His pleasure﴾, that is: do not consider lawful the fighting of those intending the Sacred House of Allah, whoever enters it is safe. Likewise whoever intends it seeking the bounty of Allah and desiring His good pleasure: so do not hinder him, do not prevent him, and do not agitate him.

Mujahid, 'Ata', Abu al-'Aliyah, Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said concerning His saying: ﴿seeking bounty from their Lord﴾, meaning by it: trade.

This is as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 198].

* *

His saying: ﴿and [seeking] His pleasure (ridwanan)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they seek Allah's pleasure through their Hajj.

'Ikrimah, al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning al-Hutam ibn Hind al-Bakri, who had raided the pasture of Madinah. When the following year came, he performed 'Umrah to the House, and some of the Companions wanted to intercept him on his way to the House. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿nor those who make for the Sacred House, seeking bounty from their Lord and His pleasure﴾.

Ibn Jarir related the consensus that a polytheist may be killed if he has no safe-conduct, even if he is heading for the Sacred House or Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). This ruling is abrogated in their regard, and Allah knows best. As for one who approaches it with deviation (ilhad) in it, associating partners with Allah there, and disbelieving in it, such a person is prevented, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾ [at-Tawbah: 28]. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the year nine, when he had appointed Abu Bakr (al-Siddiq) over the pilgrims, sent 'Ali to proclaim on his behalf, on the authority of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the declaration of immunity (bara'ah), and that no polytheist should perform Hajj after that year, and that no naked person should circumambulate the House. (Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3177, from the hadith of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.)

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿nor those who make for the Sacred House﴾, meaning those who face toward the Sacred House. The believers and the polytheists used to make Hajj to the Sacred House, so Allah forbade the believers to prevent anyone from making Hajj to the House or to obstruct him, whether believer or disbeliever. Then Allah revealed after that: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾ [at-Tawbah: 28]. And He said: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah﴾ [at-Tawbah: 17], and He said: ﴿Only those maintain the mosques of Allah who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ [at-Tawbah: 18]. Thus He removed the polytheists from al-Masjid al-Haram.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿nor the garlands, nor those who make for the Sacred House﴾. He said: it was abrogated. In the Jahiliyyah, a man who set out from his home intending Hajj would garland himself with bark from trees, and no one would intercept him; and when he returned he would garland himself with a garland of hair, and no one would intercept him. The polytheist on that day was not prevented from the House, so they were commanded not to fight in the sacred month nor near the House. Then the saying of Allah abrogated it: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [at-Tawbah: 5].

Ibn Jarir chose that the meaning of His saying ﴿nor the garlands﴾ is: if they garland themselves with a garland from the Sacred Precinct, then grant them safety. He said: the Arabs had always treated as shameful whoever violated that. The poet said: "Did you not kill the two travellers, when they passed by you, carrying the bark twisted"... (The verse is by Hudhayfah ibn Anas al-Hudhali; see Tafsir al-Tabari, 9/470.)

His saying: ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾, that is: when you have finished your ihram and come out of it, We have permitted you what was forbidden to you during the state of ihram of game. This is a command after a prohibition, and the sound view which stands up to examination is that the ruling returns to what it was before the prohibition: if it was obligatory, it returns to being obligatory; if it was recommended, it is recommended; or if it was permissible, it is permissible. Whoever says it is for obligation is refuted by many verses, and whoever says it is for permissibility is met by other verses. What unites all the evidences is this which we have mentioned, as chosen by some of the scholars of legal theory (usul al-fiqh), and Allah knows best.

* *

**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 1–2 (part 3 of 3):**

Allah's words: ﴿And let not the hatred of a people, because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque, incite you to transgress﴾. Some of the reciters read "أَنْ صَدُّوكُمْ" (*an saddukum*) with a fatḥah on the alif of "أَنْ", and its meaning is clear. That is: let not the hatred of a people who had barred you from reaching the Sacred Mosque, which happened in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyah, drive you to transgress against them in the judgment of Allah concerning you [[Added from manuscript D.]] [[In manuscript D and A: "concerning them".]], so that you retaliate against them in injustice and aggression. Rather, judge by what Allah has commanded you of justice toward everyone. This verse is like His words, exalted is He, in another place: ﴿And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 8]. That is: let not the hatred of peoples lead you to abandon justice, for justice is obligatory upon everyone, toward everyone, in every situation.

Some of the early generation (al-Salaf) said: "Do not treat the one who disobeys Allah regarding you in the same way as you would obey Allah regarding him. Justice is that by which the heavens and the earth stand."

Ibn Abi Ḥatim said: My father narrated to us, Sahl ibn 'Uthman narrated to us [[In manuscript A: "Sahl ibn 'Affan".]], 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at al-Ḥudaybiyah with his Companions when the polytheists barred them from the House, and this weighed heavily upon them. Then some polytheists from the people of the East passed by them, intending to perform 'Umrah. The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: "Shall we bar these just as their companions barred us?" So Allah revealed this verse. [[Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul without a chain of narration.]]

Al-Shana'an means hatred. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and others. It is a verbal noun from "shana'tuhu, ash'na'uhu, sha'nan" (with a vowel on the middle letter), like the forms "jamazan," "darajan," and "rafalan," from "jamaza," "daraja," and "rafala." Ibn Jarir said: Among the Arabs there are those who drop the vowel in "shana'an" and say "shannan." He said: I know of no one who recited it that way. From this is the saying of the poet [[He is al-Aḥwas ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī; the verse is in Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (9/487).]]:

*"Life is nothing but what you love and desire,*
*even if the one who hates (shannan) it blames you and rebukes."*

* * *

Allah's words: ﴿And cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression﴾. Allah, exalted is He, commands His believing servants to help one another in doing good, which is righteousness (al-birr), and in abandoning evil deeds, which is piety (al-taqwa). He forbids them from supporting falsehood and from cooperating in sins and the things Allah has forbidden.

Ibn Jarir said: "Sin (al-ithm)" is abandoning what Allah has commanded you to do, and "aggression (al-'udwan)" is exceeding what Allah has set as limits in your religion, and exceeding what He has imposed upon you concerning yourselves and concerning others. [[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (9/490).]]

The Imam Aḥmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Anas narrated to us, from his grandfather Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, we help him when he is oppressed, but how do we help him when he is an oppressor?" He said: "You restrain him and prevent him, for that is his help."

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it from the hadith of Hushaym, with similar wording. [[Al-Musnad (3/99) and Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2443).]] Both of them [[I have not found it through this route in the two Sahihs, and perhaps it is an error. I consulted Tuhfat al-Ashraf by al-Mizzi and did not find it there. Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih no. (2444) through the route of Humayd, from Anas, with it.]] narrated it through the route of Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, we help him when he is oppressed, but how do we help him when he is an oppressor?" He said: "You prevent him from oppression, for that is your help to him."

Al-Imam Aḥmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Wathhab, from a man from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ [[In manuscript D: "the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as a marfu' (directly attributed) narration."]], who said: "The believer who mixes with people and bears patiently their harm is greater in reward than the one who does not mix with people and does not bear patiently their harm." [[Al-Musnad (5/365).]]

It has also been narrated by Aḥmad in the Musnad of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar: Ḥajjaj narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Yahya ibn Wathhab, from a shaykh from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, [al-A'mash said: he is Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ] [[Added from manuscripts R and A.]] that he said: "The believer who mixes with people and bears patiently their harm is better than the one who does not mix with them and does not bear patiently their harm."

Likewise, al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, and Ibn Majah through the route of Ishaq ibn Yusuf; both of them from al-A'mash, with it. [[Al-Musnad (2/32), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2507), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4032).]]

The Ḥafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim ibn 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad Abu Shaybah al-Kufi narrated to us, Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, 'Isa ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Fudayl ibn 'Amr, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The one who guides to good is like the one who does it." Then he said: "We do not know this to be narrated except through this chain."

[[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (154), Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/166): "In it is 'Isa ibn al-Mukhtar, and Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman is alone in narrating from him."]]

I say: It has a witness in the Sahih: "Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, until the Day of Resurrection, without their rewards being diminished in the least. And whoever calls to misguidance will bear a sin like the sins of those who follow him, until the Day of Resurrection, without their sins being diminished in the least." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2674) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: 'Amr ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn al-'Ala ibn Zibriq al-Ḥimsi narrated to us, my father narrated to us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Salim, from al-Zubaydi. 'Abbas ibn Yunus said: Abu al-Hasan Nimran ibn Makhmur narrated to him [[In manuscripts R and A: "narrated to him that Aws ibn Shurahbil, one of the Banu al-Majma', narrated to him."]] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever walks with an oppressor to help him, knowing that he is an oppressor, has indeed left Islam." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/197); in its chain is Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, who is weak.]]

**Tafsir of Surat al-Ma'idah** [It is a Medinan surah] [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah Shayban narrated to us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: "I was holding the reins of al-'Adba', the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when Surat al-Ma'idah was revealed to him in its entirety. Its weight nearly broke the camel's shoulder" [[Musnad (6/455). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/13): "It contains Shahr ibn Hawshab, who is weak, though he has been deemed trustworthy."]].

Ibn Mardawayh related from the hadith of Salih ibn Suhayl, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, who said: "Umm 'Amr narrated to me, from her paternal uncle, that he was on a journey with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when Surat al-Ma'idah was revealed to him, and the neck of the riding beast broke under its weight" [[Also narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in his Musnad, al-Baghawi in his Mu'jam, and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/3).]].

Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Huyayy ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to me, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli [[In R: "al-Khatali"; in A: "al-Jabali".]], from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: "Surat al-Ma'idah was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was riding his camel, and she could not bear him, so he dismounted from her."

Ahmad alone narrated this [[Musnad (2/176). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/13): "It contains Ibn Lahi'ah, and most scholars regard him as weak, though his hadith may be good."]].

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Qutaybah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb, from Huyayy, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: "The last surah to be revealed was Surat al-Ma'idah and al-Fath." Al-Tirmidhi then said: "This is a gharib (rare) hasan hadith." It has also been related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The last surah to be revealed was: ﴿When the help of Allah comes, and victory﴾ [Surat al-Nasr: 1]."

Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak, through the chain of 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb, a version similar to al-Tirmidhi's narration, and then said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3063) and al-Mustadrak (2/311).]].

Al-Hakim also said: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, Bahr ibn Nasr narrated to us, who said: "It was read to 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed me, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: 'I performed Hajj and entered upon 'A'ishah, and she said to me: "O Jubayr, do you recite al-Ma'idah?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed, it is the last surah revealed. Whatever you find in it that is lawful, consider it lawful, and whatever you find in it that is unlawful, consider it unlawful."'" Then he said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it."

Ahmad related it from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, and added: "I asked her about the character (khuluq) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: 'The Qur'an.'" al-Nasa'i also related it from the hadith of Ibn Mahdi [[al-Mustadrak (2/311), al-Musnad (6/188), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11138).]].

* *

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Mis'ar narrated to us, Ma'n and 'Awf narrated to me, or one of them, that a man came to 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] and said: "Give me a charge (u'had ilayya)." He said: "When you hear Allah say: ﴿O you who believe﴾, then give it your attention, for it is either a good that He commands, or an evil that He forbids."

He also said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim (Duhaym) narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: "When Allah says: ﴿O you who believe﴾ and then gives a command, the Prophet ﷺ is among them."

Ahmad ibn Sinan also narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Khaythamah, who said: "Everything in the Qur'an that begins with ﴿O you who believe﴾ is found in the Torah as: 'O you the poor (al-masakin).'"

As for what was related from Zayd ibn Isma'il al-Sa'igh al-Baghdadi, who narrated from Mu'awiyah (i.e., Ibn Hisham), from 'Isa ibn Rashid, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "There is no verse in the Qur'an beginning with ﴿O you who believe﴾ except that 'Ali is its leader (sayyiduha), its noble one (sharifuha), and its prince (amiruha). And none of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ was rebuked in the Qur'an except 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, for he was never rebuked in any matter of it." This is a gharib report, its wording contains a rejected element (nakarah), and its chain is open to question.

Al-Bukhari said: "This 'Isa ibn Rashid is unknown (majhul), and his report is munkar (rejected)." I say: As for 'Ali ibn Badhimah, although he is trustworthy (thiqah), he is an extreme Shi'i, and his report in such matters carries suspicion and is not accepted. As for his statement: "No one among the Companions remained without being rebuked in the Qur'an except 'Ali," it refers only to the verse commanding charity before private consultation (al-najwa). Many have mentioned that no one acted upon it except 'Ali. And the verse was revealed: ﴿Are you apprehensive about offering charity before your private consultation? So when you did not do so and Allah forgave you...﴾ [Surat al-Mujadilah: 13]. Whether this constitutes a rebuke is open to question, for it has been said that the command was recommended (nadb) rather than obligatory (ijab), and that it was then abrogated (nuski'a, i.e., naskh) for them before any act was performed, so no one among them was seen to oppose it. His statement about 'Ali, "He was never rebuked in any part of the Qur'an," is also open to question, for the verse in al-Anfal that rebuked those who accepted ransom encompassed all who advised taking it, and none was spared from it except 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. From this, and from what preceded, the weakness of this report becomes clear. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, Yunus narrated to me, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim said: "I read the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which was written to 'Amr ibn Hazm when he sent him to Najran. The letter was with Abu Bakr ibn Hazm, and in it: 'This is a declaration from Allah and His Messenger: ﴿O you who believe, fulfill the contracts﴾,' and he wrote the verses from it until he reached: ﴿Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/454).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm narrated to me, from his father, who said: "This is the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which is with us, which he wrote to 'Amr ibn Hazm when he sent him to Yemen, to instruct its people in religion, teach them the Sunnah, and collect their charities. He wrote to him a letter and a covenant, and commanded him in it with his orders. He wrote: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. This is a letter from Allah and His Messenger: ﴿O you who believe, fulfill the contracts﴾. A covenant from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to 'Amr ibn Hazm, when he sent him to Yemen, commanding him to fear Allah in all his affairs, for indeed Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good'" [[Also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (5/413) through the chain of Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Yunus ibn Bukayr.]].

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Fulfill the contracts﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and others said: "By contracts ('uqud) is meant covenants ('uhud)." Ibn Jarir related consensus (al-ijma') on this. He said: "The covenants are what they bound themselves to through alliances and other agreements." 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿O you who believe, fulfill the contracts﴾: "By covenants is meant what Allah has made lawful and what He has made unlawful, and what He has obligated and set as limits in the entire Qur'an. So do not betray and do not break them." Then he emphasized this, saying: ﴿And those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined...﴾ up to His words: ﴿the evil home﴾ [Surat al-Ra'd: 25].

Al-Dahhak said concerning ﴿Fulfill the contracts﴾: "It is what Allah has made lawful and unlawful, and what Allah has taken as a covenant from those who acknowledge faith in the Prophet ﷺ and the Book, that they fulfill what Allah has obligated upon them of the obligations concerning the lawful and the unlawful."

Zayd ibn Aslam said concerning ﴿Fulfill the contracts﴾: "They are six: the covenant of Allah, the contract of alliance, the contract of partnership, the contract of sale, the contract of marriage, and the contract of oath."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "They are five, among them: the alliance of the pre-Islamic period (hilf al-jahiliyyah) and the partnership of mufawadah."

Some who held that there is no option (khiyar) in the council of sale (majlis al-bay') have used this verse, ﴿Fulfill the contracts﴾, as evidence. They said: "This indicates the binding nature and validity of the contract, and therefore requires the negation of the option of the council." This is the position of Abu Hanifah and Malik. But al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and the majority disagreed, and their proof is what is established in the two Sahihs from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The two parties to a sale have the option (bi'l-khiyar) as long as they have not separated" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2109) and Sahih Muslim no. (1531).]]. In another wording in al-Bukhari: "When two men engage in a sale, each of them has the option as long as they have not separated" [[The wording in Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2112) and Sahih Muslim no. (1531).]]. This is explicit in establishing the option of the council that follows the conclusion of the sale. It is not contrary to the binding nature of the contract; rather, it is one of its legal requirements, so exercising it is part of fulfilling the contract.

* *

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock﴾ refer to camels, cattle, and sheep. This was said by al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others. Ibn Jarir said: "It is also so in the usage of the Arabs." Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, and others have used this verse as evidence for the permissibility of eating a fetus found dead in its mother's womb when she is slaughtered. There is a hadith on this in the Sunan, related by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, through the chain of Mujalid, from Abu al-Waddak Jabr ibn Nawf, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we slaughter a she-camel, or we slaughter a cow or a sheep, and in its belly is a fetus. Shall we discard it or eat it?' He said: 'Eat it if you wish, for its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother.'" Al-Tirmidhi said: "It is a hasan hadith" [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2827), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1476), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3199).]].

[And] [[Addition from manuscript R.]] Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Faris narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Attab ibn Bashir narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Haddad al-Makki narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The slaughter of the fetus is the slaughter of its mother." Abu Dawud alone narrated it [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2828).]].

* *

The words of Allah: ﴿Except what is recited to you﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "By this is meant carrion (al-maytah), blood, and the flesh of swine." Qatadah said: "By this is meant carrion and that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned."

And the apparent meaning, Allah knows best, is that what is intended by this is His saying: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked, the strangled animal, the animal beaten to death, the animal that falls to its death, the animal gored to death, and what a beast of prey has eaten﴾. Although these are among the livestock (al-an'am), they are forbidden because of these occurrences. For this reason He said: ﴿except what you slaughter properly, and what is sacrificed on the stone altars﴾, meaning from among them. For that is forbidden and cannot be made up for or compensated. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Lawful to you are the beasts of cattle, except what is recited to you﴾, meaning except what will be recited to you of the prohibition of some of them in certain circumstances.

* *

His saying: ﴿not hunting game while you are in the state of ihram (ihram: the state of ritual consecration for pilgrimage)﴾. Some of them said: this is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). What is meant by "the livestock" is that which includes the domesticated, namely camels, cattle and sheep, and that which includes the wild, such as gazelles, oxen and wild asses. So He excepted from the domesticated what was previously mentioned, and He excepted from the wild the hunting of game while in the state of ihram.

It was also said: what is meant is: "We have made lawful to you the livestock, except what is excluded for one who has committed himself to the prohibition of game, and that is forbidden," like His saying: ﴿But whoever is compelled, neither desiring it nor exceeding the limit, (there is no sin upon him)﴾. That is: We permitted the consumption of carrion to the one who is compelled, on condition that he is neither desiring it nor exceeding the limit. That is, just as We made the livestock lawful to you in all circumstances, so forbid yourselves hunting during the state of ihram, for Allah has decreed this, and He is the All-Wise in all that He commands and forbids. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah decrees what He wills﴾.

Then He said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: by this He means the rites of Hajj.

Mujahid said: as-Safa and al-Marwah, and the hadi (sacrificial animals) and the budn (large camels and cattle offered as sacrifice) are among the rites of Allah.

It was also said: the rites of Allah are His sacred prohibitions which He has forbidden, that is: do not violate the sacred prohibitions of Allah which He has forbidden. For this reason He said [the Exalted]: ﴿nor the sacred month﴾, meaning by this: its sanctity and acknowledging its honour, and abandoning what Allah has forbidden of engaging in it, such as initiating fighting, and emphasising avoidance of the prohibitions. As He said: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting therein is great sin﴾ [al-Baqarah: 217]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred. That is the correct religion, so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ [at-Tawbah: 36].

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Abu Bakrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Indeed, time has returned to its original form, the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three consecutive ones, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban."

This indicates the continuation of their sanctity until the end of time, as is the view of a group of the early generations (salaf).

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿nor the sacred month﴾, that is: do not consider fighting in it lawful. Likewise said Muqatil ibn Hayyan and 'Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, and Ibn Jarir also chose this view. The majority, however, held that this ruling is abrogated (mansukh; abrogation is the annulment of a ruling by a later revelation, naskh), and that it is permissible to initiate fighting in the sacred months. They cited His saying: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [at-Tawbah: 5]. They said: the intended months are the four months of travel (ashhur at-tasyir), and He did not exclude any sacred month from the others.

Imam Abu Ja'far (Ibn Jarir al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, related the consensus that Allah has permitted fighting the people of polytheism in the sacred months and other months of the year. He said: likewise they agreed that if a polytheist hung around his neck or on his arms the bark of all the trees of the Sacred Precinct (haram), that would not be a safe-conduct for him from being killed, if no covenant of protection (dhimmah) from the Muslims or a guarantee of safety had preceded for him. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 9/479.) This question has another discussion, which has a more extensive place than this.

His saying: ﴿nor the offerings, nor the garlands﴾, meaning: do not abandon sending offerings to the House, for in that is the glorification of the rites of Allah. And do not abandon garlanding them on their necks, so that they are distinguished thereby from other livestock, and so that it is known that they are an offering to the Ka'bah, so that whoever intends them with harm will avoid them, and whoever sees them will be moved to bring the like of them. For whoever calls to a good offering has a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without their rewards being diminished in any way. For this reason, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj, he spent the night at Dhu al-Hulayfah, which is the valley of al-'Aqiq. When morning came he went around to his wives, and they were nine. Then he bathed, perfumed himself, and prayed two rak'ahs. Then he marked his offering (ash'ara hadyahu) and garlanded it, and he assumed ihram for Hajj and 'Umrah together. His offering consisted of many camels, more than sixty, of the finest forms and colours, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That [is so]; and whoever honours the rites of Allah, indeed it is from the piety of hearts﴾ [al-Hajj: 32].

One of the early scholars said: glorifying them is considering them fine and fat.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to look carefully at the eye and the ear. (Related by the authors of the Sunan.) [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2804; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1498; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/216; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3142.]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿nor the garlands﴾, so do not consider them lawful. In the Jahiliyyah, when they set out from their homelands outside the sacred months, they would garland themselves with hair and wool, and the polytheists of the Sacred Precinct would garland themselves with bark from the trees of the Sacred Precinct, and thereby they were safe.

Ibn Abi Hatim related it, then said: Muhammad ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: two verses of this surah were abrogated: the verse about the garlands, and His saying: ﴿So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 42].

Al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan narrated to us, Zakariyya ibn 'Adi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn who said: I said to al-Hasan: was anything abrogated from al-Ma'idah? He said: No.

'Ata' said: they used to garland themselves with the trees of the Sacred Precinct and thereby they were safe, so Allah forbade cutting its trees. Likewise said Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿nor those who make for the Sacred House, seeking bounty from their Lord and His pleasure﴾, that is: do not consider lawful the fighting of those intending the Sacred House of Allah, whoever enters it is safe. Likewise whoever intends it seeking the bounty of Allah and desiring His good pleasure: so do not hinder him, do not prevent him, and do not agitate him.

Mujahid, 'Ata', Abu al-'Aliyah, Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said concerning His saying: ﴿seeking bounty from their Lord﴾, meaning by it: trade.

This is as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 198].

* *

His saying: ﴿and [seeking] His pleasure (ridwanan)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they seek Allah's pleasure through their Hajj.

'Ikrimah, al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning al-Hutam ibn Hind al-Bakri, who had raided the pasture of Madinah. When the following year came, he performed 'Umrah to the House, and some of the Companions wanted to intercept him on his way to the House. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿nor those who make for the Sacred House, seeking bounty from their Lord and His pleasure﴾.

Ibn Jarir related the consensus that a polytheist may be killed if he has no safe-conduct, even if he is heading for the Sacred House or Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). This ruling is abrogated in their regard, and Allah knows best. As for one who approaches it with deviation (ilhad) in it, associating partners with Allah there, and disbelieving in it, such a person is prevented, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾ [at-Tawbah: 28]. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the year nine, when he had appointed Abu Bakr (al-Siddiq) over the pilgrims, sent 'Ali to proclaim on his behalf, on the authority of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the declaration of immunity (bara'ah), and that no polytheist should perform Hajj after that year, and that no naked person should circumambulate the House. (Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3177, from the hadith of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.)

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿nor those who make for the Sacred House﴾, meaning those who face toward the Sacred House. The believers and the polytheists used to make Hajj to the Sacred House, so Allah forbade the believers to prevent anyone from making Hajj to the House or to obstruct him, whether believer or disbeliever. Then Allah revealed after that: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾ [at-Tawbah: 28]. And He said: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah﴾ [at-Tawbah: 17], and He said: ﴿Only those maintain the mosques of Allah who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ [at-Tawbah: 18]. Thus He removed the polytheists from al-Masjid al-Haram.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿nor the garlands, nor those who make for the Sacred House﴾. He said: it was abrogated. In the Jahiliyyah, a man who set out from his home intending Hajj would garland himself with bark from trees, and no one would intercept him; and when he returned he would garland himself with a garland of hair, and no one would intercept him. The polytheist on that day was not prevented from the House, so they were commanded not to fight in the sacred month nor near the House. Then the saying of Allah abrogated it: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [at-Tawbah: 5].

Ibn Jarir chose that the meaning of His saying ﴿nor the garlands﴾ is: if they garland themselves with a garland from the Sacred Precinct, then grant them safety. He said: the Arabs had always treated as shameful whoever violated that. The poet said: "Did you not kill the two travellers, when they passed by you, carrying the bark twisted"... (The verse is by Hudhayfah ibn Anas al-Hudhali; see Tafsir al-Tabari, 9/470.)

His saying: ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾, that is: when you have finished your ihram and come out of it, We have permitted you what was forbidden to you during the state of ihram of game. This is a command after a prohibition, and the sound view which stands up to examination is that the ruling returns to what it was before the prohibition: if it was obligatory, it returns to being obligatory; if it was recommended, it is recommended; or if it was permissible, it is permissible. Whoever says it is for obligation is refuted by many verses, and whoever says it is for permissibility is met by other verses. What unites all the evidences is this which we have mentioned, as chosen by some of the scholars of legal theory (usul al-fiqh), and Allah knows best.

* *

**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 1–2 (part 3 of 3):**

Allah's words: ﴿And let not the hatred of a people, because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque, incite you to transgress﴾. Some of the reciters read "أَنْ صَدُّوكُمْ" (*an saddukum*) with a fatḥah on the alif of "أَنْ", and its meaning is clear. That is: let not the hatred of a people who had barred you from reaching the Sacred Mosque, which happened in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyah, drive you to transgress against them in the judgment of Allah concerning you [[Added from manuscript D.]] [[In manuscript D and A: "concerning them".]], so that you retaliate against them in injustice and aggression. Rather, judge by what Allah has commanded you of justice toward everyone. This verse is like His words, exalted is He, in another place: ﴿And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 8]. That is: let not the hatred of peoples lead you to abandon justice, for justice is obligatory upon everyone, toward everyone, in every situation.

Some of the early generation (al-Salaf) said: "Do not treat the one who disobeys Allah regarding you in the same way as you would obey Allah regarding him. Justice is that by which the heavens and the earth stand."

Ibn Abi Ḥatim said: My father narrated to us, Sahl ibn 'Uthman narrated to us [[In manuscript A: "Sahl ibn 'Affan".]], 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at al-Ḥudaybiyah with his Companions when the polytheists barred them from the House, and this weighed heavily upon them. Then some polytheists from the people of the East passed by them, intending to perform 'Umrah. The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: "Shall we bar these just as their companions barred us?" So Allah revealed this verse. [[Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul without a chain of narration.]]

Al-Shana'an means hatred. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and others. It is a verbal noun from "shana'tuhu, ash'na'uhu, sha'nan" (with a vowel on the middle letter), like the forms "jamazan," "darajan," and "rafalan," from "jamaza," "daraja," and "rafala." Ibn Jarir said: Among the Arabs there are those who drop the vowel in "shana'an" and say "shannan." He said: I know of no one who recited it that way. From this is the saying of the poet [[He is al-Aḥwas ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī; the verse is in Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (9/487).]]:

*"Life is nothing but what you love and desire,*
*even if the one who hates (shannan) it blames you and rebukes."*

* * *

Allah's words: ﴿And cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression﴾. Allah, exalted is He, commands His believing servants to help one another in doing good, which is righteousness (al-birr), and in abandoning evil deeds, which is piety (al-taqwa). He forbids them from supporting falsehood and from cooperating in sins and the things Allah has forbidden.

Ibn Jarir said: "Sin (al-ithm)" is abandoning what Allah has commanded you to do, and "aggression (al-'udwan)" is exceeding what Allah has set as limits in your religion, and exceeding what He has imposed upon you concerning yourselves and concerning others. [[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (9/490).]]

The Imam Aḥmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Anas narrated to us, from his grandfather Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, we help him when he is oppressed, but how do we help him when he is an oppressor?" He said: "You restrain him and prevent him, for that is his help."

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it from the hadith of Hushaym, with similar wording. [[Al-Musnad (3/99) and Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2443).]] Both of them [[I have not found it through this route in the two Sahihs, and perhaps it is an error. I consulted Tuhfat al-Ashraf by al-Mizzi and did not find it there. Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih no. (2444) through the route of Humayd, from Anas, with it.]] narrated it through the route of Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, we help him when he is oppressed, but how do we help him when he is an oppressor?" He said: "You prevent him from oppression, for that is your help to him."

Al-Imam Aḥmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Wathhab, from a man from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ [[In manuscript D: "the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as a marfu' (directly attributed) narration."]], who said: "The believer who mixes with people and bears patiently their harm is greater in reward than the one who does not mix with people and does not bear patiently their harm." [[Al-Musnad (5/365).]]

It has also been narrated by Aḥmad in the Musnad of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar: Ḥajjaj narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Yahya ibn Wathhab, from a shaykh from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, [al-A'mash said: he is Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ] [[Added from manuscripts R and A.]] that he said: "The believer who mixes with people and bears patiently their harm is better than the one who does not mix with them and does not bear patiently their harm."

Likewise, al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, and Ibn Majah through the route of Ishaq ibn Yusuf; both of them from al-A'mash, with it. [[Al-Musnad (2/32), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2507), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4032).]]

The Ḥafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim ibn 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad Abu Shaybah al-Kufi narrated to us, Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, 'Isa ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Fudayl ibn 'Amr, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The one who guides to good is like the one who does it." Then he said: "We do not know this to be narrated except through this chain."

[[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (154), Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/166): "In it is 'Isa ibn al-Mukhtar, and Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman is alone in narrating from him."]]

I say: It has a witness in the Sahih: "Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, until the Day of Resurrection, without their rewards being diminished in the least. And whoever calls to misguidance will bear a sin like the sins of those who follow him, until the Day of Resurrection, without their sins being diminished in the least." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2674) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: 'Amr ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn al-'Ala ibn Zibriq al-Ḥimsi narrated to us, my father narrated to us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Salim, from al-Zubaydi. 'Abbas ibn Yunus said: Abu al-Hasan Nimran ibn Makhmur narrated to him [[In manuscripts R and A: "narrated to him that Aws ibn Shurahbil, one of the Banu al-Majma', narrated to him."]] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever walks with an oppressor to help him, knowing that he is an oppressor, has indeed left Islam." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/197); in its chain is Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, who is weak.]]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 5, verse 3 (part 1 of 5):

Allah, exalted is He, informs His servants, in a statement that implies a prohibition against consuming these forbidden things, of carrion (al-maytah), which is any animal that dies by its own natural death (hatf anfihi) without ritual slaughter (dhakah) or hunting. This is forbidden only because of the harm in it, namely the coagulated blood it contains. It is therefore harmful to the religion and to the body, and for this reason Allah, mighty and majestic, prohibited it.

Excepted from carrion is fish, which is lawful whether it dies through ritual slaughter or otherwise. This is based on what Malik narrated in his Muwatta', al-Shafi'i and Ahmad in their Musnads, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah in their Sunans, and Ibn Khuzaymah and Ibn Hibban in their Sahihs, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the water of the sea and said: "Its water is pure, and its carrion is lawful."[[The Muwatta' (1/22), Musnad al-Shafi'i no. (25) "Bada'i' al-Minan," Musnad Ahmad (2/237, 361), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (83), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (69), Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/50), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (386), Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah no. (111), and Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (119) "Mawarid." All of them are through Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Sa'id ibn Salamah, from the family of Bani al-Azraq, that al-Mughirah ibn Abi Burdah informed him that he heard Abu Hurayrah narrate it. Ibn Khuzaymah, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi declared this hadith sahih, and al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."]]

Likewise locusts are lawful, due to the hadith that will follow.

As for His saying ﴿And blood﴾, it refers to flowing blood (al-masfuh), based on His saying ﴿or blood poured forth﴾ [al-An'am: 145]. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Kathir ibn Shihab al-Madhhaji narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Sabiq narrated to us, 'Amr (i.e., Ibn Qays) narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he was asked about the spleen, and he said: "Eat it." They said: "It is blood." He said: "Only flowing blood has been forbidden to you."

Similarly, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim, from 'A'ishah, who said: "He only forbade flowing blood."

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two carrions and two bloods have been made lawful for us. As for the two carrions, they are fish and locusts; as for the two bloods, they are the liver and the spleen."[[Musnad al-Shafi'i no. (1734) "Bada'i' al-Minan," Musnad Ahmad (2/97), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3314), Sunan al-Daraqutni (4/271), and al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi (1/254).]] Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ibn Majah, al-Daraqutni and al-Bayhaqi also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and it is weak. The hafiz al-Bayhaqi said: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated it from Usamah, 'Abd Allah and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn 'Umar, as a marfu' report (traced to the Prophet).

I say: All three of them are weak, but some of them are more sound than others. Sulayman ibn Bilal, one of the trustworthy narrators, narrated it from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn 'Umar, but some narrators stopped it at Ibn 'Umar (as a mawquf report). The hafiz Abu Zur'ah al-Razi said: "This is more sound."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, Bashir ibn Surayj narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah (who is Sudayy ibn 'Ajlan), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to my people to call them to Allah and His Messenger, and to present to them the laws of Islam. I came to them, and while we were like that, they brought a bowl of blood, gathered around it and began eating it. They said: "Come, O Sudayy, and eat." I said: "Woe to you! I have only come to you from one who has forbidden this to you, and Allah revealed to him." They said: "And what is that?" So I recited to them this verse: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion and blood [and the flesh of swine]﴾, the verse in full.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi al-Shawarib with a similar chain, and he added after this account: He said: "I began calling them to Islam, but they refused me. So I said to them: 'Woe to you! Give me a drink of water, for I am extremely thirsty.' He said: I was wearing my cloak. They said: 'No, but we will leave you until you die of thirst.' So I grew distressed, I put my head down in the cloak, and I lay on the scorching sand in intense heat. Then a visitor came to me in my sleep with a glass cup of crystal, the like of which people had never seen, and in it was a drink sweeter than anything people had ever tasted. He handed it to me, and I drank it. When I finished my drink, I awoke. By Allah, I was never thirsty again after that drink, nor did I feel any discomfort."[[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/335) through Muhammad ibn Abi al-Shawarib with the same chain. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/387): "In it is Bashir ibn Surayj, who is weak."]] Al-Hakim also narrated it in his Mustadrak, from 'Ali ibn Humshadh, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salamah ibn 'Ayyash al-'Amiri narrated to me, Sadaqah ibn Hurmuz narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, and he mentioned something similar. He added after his words "after that drink": "Then I heard them saying: 'A man of the nobles of your people has come to you, and you did not offer him even a mixed drink (mathqah).' So they brought me a mixed drink, and I said: 'I have no need for it. My Lord has fed me and given me to drink.' I showed them my belly, and they all embraced Islam."[[It is in the Mustadrak (3/642), and in it is Sadaqah ibn Hurmuz, whom Ibn Ma'in and others declared weak.]]

How beautifully al-A'sha recited in his qasidah, which Ibn Ishaq mentioned:[[See the qasidah in: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/386).]]

*And beware of carrion, do not approach it,*
*and do not take a sharp bone so that you bleed.*

That is: do not do as the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) did. Indeed, when one of them was hungry, he would take something sharp, a bone or the like, and cut his camel or any other animal, whatever its kind, and gather the blood that flowed from it and drink it. For this reason Allah forbade blood to this Ummah. Then al-A'sha said:

*And do not approach the idol set up (al-nusub al-mansub),*
*and do not worship idols, but worship Allah.*

As for His saying ﴿and the flesh of swine﴾, it refers to both domestic and wild swine. "Flesh" encompasses all its parts, even the fat. There is no need for the Zahiriyyah (literalist school) to show cleverness and rigid stubbornness here, nor to strain in their argument from His saying ﴿for it is impure or an abomination﴾, meaning the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿except that it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine, for it is impure﴾ [al-An'am: 145]. They returned the pronoun in what they understood to refer to swine alone, so that it would cover all its parts. This is far-fetched linguistically, for a pronoun returns only to the thing being referred to (the mudaf), not to what it is attached to (the mudaf ilayhi). The more evident view is that "flesh" encompasses all parts, as is understood from the language of the Arabs and established usage. In Sahih Muslim, from Buraydah ibn al-Khasib al-Aslami, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever plays nard (backgammon) is as if he dipped his hand in the flesh and blood of swine."[[Sahih Muslim no. (2260).]] If this aversion is for merely touching it, then how severe must the threat and the firm warning be against eating it and nourishing oneself with it? This indicates that "flesh" includes all parts, including fat and other parts.

In the two Sahihs: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has forbidden the sale of wine, carrion, swine and idols." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the fat of carrion? It is used to coat ships, to oil hides, and people use it for lamps." He said: "No, it is forbidden."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2236) and Sahih Muslim no. (1581), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Abu Sufyan, that he said to Heraclius, the king of the Romans: "He (the Prophet) forbade us from carrion and blood."[[I did not find this wording in Sahih al-Bukhari in the places where the hadith of Heraclius is narrated.]]

As for His saying ﴿and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah﴾, that is, whatever is slaughtered and over which the name of other than Allah is mentioned, it is forbidden, because Allah commanded that His creatures be slaughtered in His great name. Whenever it is diverted from this and the name of something else is mentioned over it, such as an idol, a tyrant (taghut), a pagan image, or anything else among all created beings, it is forbidden by consensus (ijma'). The scholars differed only about an animal over which the name of Allah was not mentioned, whether deliberately or through forgetfulness, as will be explained in Surah al-An'am.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hisnjani narrated to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn Jumay', from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Adam received the revelation of the prohibition of four things: carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. These four things were never lawful at any time, and they have remained forbidden since Allah created the heavens and the earth. When the Children of Israel came, Allah forbade them good things that had been lawful for them because of their sins. When Allah sent 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, he restored the first ruling that Adam had brought, and made lawful for them whatever else was excluded, but they rejected him and disobeyed him. This is a strange report (athar gharib).

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Rib'i ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Jarud ibn Abi Sabrah, (he said: he is my grandfather), say: A man from Bani Riyah called Ibn Wathil, who was a poet, competed with Ghalib (the father of al-Farazdaq) over water in the outskirts of Kufa, on the condition that each would hamstring one hundred of his camels when they came to the water. When they came to the water, they both went to them with swords and began hamstringing their hocks. He said: The people came out on donkeys and mules seeking meat. 'Ali was in Kufa. He said: 'Ali came out on the white mule of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), calling out: "O people, do not eat from their meat, for it has been dedicated to other than Allah."

This is a strange report, and what supports its soundness is what Abu Dawud narrated: Harun ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, from 'Awf, from Abu Rayhanah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade mu'aqarah of the Bedouins.

Then Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far (i.e., Ghundar) stopped it at Ibn 'Abbas (as a mawquf report). Abu Dawud alone narrated it.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2820).]]

Abu Dawud also said: Harun ibn Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from al-Zubayr ibn Khirrit, who said: I heard Ikrimah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade eating the food of the two who compete (al-mutabariyayn).

Then Abu Dawud said: Most of those who narrated it from Jarir do not mention Ibn 'Abbas in it. He alone narrated it as well.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3754).]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the strangled animal﴾, this is the one that dies by strangulation, whether intentionally or accidentally, such as when it becomes entangled in its tether and dies because of it. It is therefore forbidden.

As for ﴿the beaten animal﴾ (al-mawquudhah), it is the one that is struck with a heavy, blunt object until it dies. As Ibn 'Abbas and others said: it is the one beaten with a stick until it dies from the blows.

Qatadah said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to beat it with staves, and when it died, they would eat it.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verse 3 (part 2 of 5):

It is related in the Sahih that 'Adi ibn Hatim said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I shoot game with the mi'rad (a blunt-headed arrow or javelin), and I hit it." He said: "If you shoot with the mi'rad and it pierces (khazaqa), then eat it; but if it strikes it with its width (ʿarḍ), then it is a waqidh (an animal killed by a blow), so do not eat it." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 5475, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 1929.]

He distinguished between what is struck by the arrow, or by the mizraq (a spear-like missile) and the like, with its point (ḥadd), so he made it lawful; and what is struck with its width, so he made it a waqidh and did not make it lawful. The jurists have agreed upon this ruling here. They differed regarding the case where the trained hunting animal (al-jāriḥa) strikes the game and kills it by its weight without wounding it, into two opinions, which are two views of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him:

The first: it is not lawful, just as with the arrow, and the common factor is that each of them is a dead animal without a wound, so it is a waqidh.

The second: it is lawful, because he (ﷺ) ruled as lawful what the dog catches and did not ask for details, which indicates the permissibility of what we have mentioned, since it falls within the general wording.

I have written a section on this question, which should be recorded here.

Section:

The scholars, may Allah Most High have mercy on them, differed regarding the case where one releases a dog upon game and it kills it by its weight without wounding it, or strikes it, whether it is lawful or not, into two opinions:

The first: that this is lawful, based on the generality of the words of Allah Most High: ﴿So eat of what they catch for you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 4], and likewise the general wording of the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim [the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim will come in full]. This is a view reported by the companions (al-Ashab) from al-Shafi'i, and some later scholars, such as al-Nawawi and al-Rafi'i, declared it sound.

I say: this is not apparent from al-Shafi'i's words in al-Umm and al-Mukhtasar, for he said in both places: "It admits two meanings." Then he gave a rationale for each of them, so the companions took from this that there are two views from him on the question. However, in his discussion, when he reported the view of permissibility, he slightly favored it without declaring either one or deciding on it. The view of permissibility was transmitted by Ibn al-Sabbagh from Abu Hanifa, through the narration of al-Hasan ibn Ziyad from him, and he mentioned nothing else. As for Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, he reported it in his Tafsir from Salman al-Farisi, Abu Hurayrah, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Ibn 'Umar.
