This is very rare, and it is not found explicitly attributed to them, except that it is from his own (Ibn Jarir's) reasoning, may Allah have mercy on him and be pleased with him.

The second view: that this is not lawful. It is one of the two views of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and al-Muzani chose it. It appears from Ibn al-Sabbagh's words that he also preferred it, and Allah knows best. It was narrated by Abu Yusuf and Muhammad from Abu Hanifa, and it is the well-known position of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him. This view is closer to the truth, and Allah knows best, because it accords more with the principles of usul and is closer to the foundations of the Shari'ah. Ibn al-Sabbagh argued for it with the hadith of Rafi' ibn Khadij: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we will meet the enemy tomorrow and we do not have knives; shall we slaughter with reeds?' He said: 'What makes the blood flow and over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, eat it.'" The hadith in full, and it is in the two Sahihs.

Even though this was given in a specific context, the consideration is the generality of the wording according to the majority of scholars in usul and furu'. Likewise, when the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about al-bat' (a drink made of honey), he said: "Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden." [Narrated by al-Bukhari, no. 242, and Muslim, no. 2001, from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.] Would any jurist say that this wording is restricted to honey drink? Similarly here: they asked him about a matter of slaughter, and he gave a general statement that includes that which was asked about and other things, because he (ﷺ) was given jawami' al-kalim (comprehensive speech).

Having established this, what the dog strikes or crushes with its weight is not something whose blood has been made to flow, so it is not lawful according to the implication (mafhum) of this hadith. If it is said: this hadith is not of this kind at all, because they only asked about the instrument by which slaughter is done, and did not ask about the thing being slaughtered; that is why he excepted the tooth and the nail, when he said: "Not the tooth or the nail, and I will tell you about that: as for the tooth, it is bone; and as for the nail, it is the knife of the Abyssinians." The exception indicates the genus of what is excepted from, otherwise it would not be a connected exception, so it shows that what was asked about is the instrument, and there remains no indication in it for what you have mentioned.

The answer to this: there is in the wording something that is also problematic for you, where he says: "What makes the blood flow and over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, eat it." He did not say: "then slaughter with it." From this two rulings are taken together: the ruling on the instrument by which slaughter is done, and the ruling on the slaughtered animal, and that the blood must be made to flow by an instrument that is neither a tooth nor a nail. This is one approach.

The second approach is the method of al-Muzani, which is that the arrow was explicitly stated: if it kills with its width, do not eat; and if it pierces, eat. The dog was mentioned without restriction, so it is understood in light of the piercing restriction stated there, because both share the same effect, which is hunting, so the application here is required even though the cause differs, just as the absolute manumission in zihar is understood in light of its restriction to belief in the case of killing. Indeed this is more appropriate. This applies to whoever accepts the principle of this rule in itself, and there is no disagreement about it among the companions (al-Ashab) as a whole, so they must have an answer to this. He may say: this animal was killed by the dog's weight, so it is not lawful, by analogy with what was killed by the arrow's width, and the common factor is that each of them is an instrument of hunting, and it died by its weight in both cases. This is not countered by the generality of the verse, because analogy takes precedence over generality, as is the position of the four imams and the majority. This too is a good approach.

Another approach: the words of Allah Most High, ﴿So eat of what they catch for you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 4], are general regarding what they kill, whether by wounding or otherwise, but this killed animal in this disputed form must be either a nati-hah (an animal struck to death by a blow from a horned animal) or in its ruling, or a munkhaniqah (strangled) or in its ruling, and whichever it is, this verse must be given precedence over those, for several reasons:

First: the Lawgiver has taken the ruling of this verse into account in the case of hunting, when he says to 'Adi ibn Hatim: "But if it strikes it with its width, then it is a waqidh, so do not eat it." We do not know of any scholar who distinguished between one ruling and another from this verse, saying that the waqidh is considered in the case of hunting but the nati-hah is not considered. So saying the disputed animal is lawful would be a breach of a consensus with no one holding it, and that is forbidden according to many scholars.

Second: that verse, ﴿So eat of what they catch for you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 4], is not general in its scope by consensus, but rather restricted to what is caught of edible animals, and non-edible animals were excluded from its general wording by agreement, and a protected generality takes precedence over an unprotected one.

Another approach: this game, in this state, has the same ruling as carrion, because blood and what follows it of fluids have been retained in it, so it is not lawful, by analogy with carrion.

Another approach: the verse of prohibition, that is His words, ﴿Forbidden to you is carrion﴾ through to its end, is muhkam (definitive) and has not been affected by abrogation or specification. Likewise the verse of permission should be muhkam, namely His words, ﴿They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: Lawful for you are the good things, and what you have taught of the hunting animals, training them as trainers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 4]. So there should be no contradiction between them at all, and the Sunnah came to explain that. The evidence for this is the story of the arrow, for it mentioned the ruling of what entered under this verse, which is that if the mi'rad pierces it, it is lawful, because it is among the good things; and what entered under the ruling of the other verse, the verse of prohibition, which is that if it strikes it with its width, it is not eaten, because it is a waqidh, so it is one of the instances of the verse of prohibition. Likewise the ruling of this must be the same: if the dog has wounded it, then it falls under the ruling of the verse of permission. But if it has not wounded it, rather struck it or killed it by its weight, then it is a nati-hah or in its ruling, so it is not lawful.

If it is said: why did he not distinguish in the ruling for the dog, and say what you have mentioned: if it wounds it, it is lawful, and if it does not wound it, it is forbidden?

The answer: that is rare, because it is characteristic of the dog to kill with its claw, or its fang, or both together; as for its colliding with the game, that is rare, and likewise killing it by its weight. So there was no need to guard against that because of its rarity, or because its ruling is clear to whoever knows the prohibition of carrion, the strangled, the beaten to death, the fallen, and the gored. As for the arrow and the mi'rad, sometimes they miss due to the poor aim of the shooter, or the wind, or the like; indeed their missing is more frequent than their hitting. Therefore he mentioned each of its two rulings in detail, and Allah knows best. And for this reason, since it is characteristic of the dog that it may eat from the game, he mentioned the ruling for when it eats from the game, saying: "If it eats, then do not eat, for I fear that it has held it for itself." This is authentic and established in the two Sahihs, and it is also excepted from the generality of the verse of permission according to many, so they said: what the dog has eaten from is not lawful. This was reported from Abu Hurayrah and Ibn 'Abbas. It was also the view of al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, and al-Nakha'i. Abu Hanifa and his two companions, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and al-Shafi'i in his well-known view also held this. Ibn Jarir reported in his Tafsir from 'Ali, Sa'd, Salman, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Umar, and Ibn 'Abbas that the game is eaten even if the dog has eaten from it, so much so that Sa'd, Salman, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Umar, and others said: it is eaten even if only a small piece remains. This was the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i in his old view, and he indicated two views in his new view, as reported by Imam Abu Nasr Ibn al-Sabbagh and other companions from him.

Abu Dawud has related with a good, strong chain, from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said concerning the game of the dog: "If you release your dog and mention the name of Allah, then eat, even if it has eaten from it; and eat what your hand has caught for you." [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2852.]

Al-Nasa'i also related it through the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that a Bedouin called Abu Tha'labah said: "O Messenger of Allah," and he mentioned something similar.

Muhammad ibn Jarir said in his Tafsir: Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kalla'i narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Musa (he is al-Lahuni) narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Dinar (he is al-Tahi) narrated to us, from Abu Iyas (he is Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah), from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Salman al-Farisi, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "If a man releases his dog upon game, and it reaches it after it has eaten from it, then let him eat what remains."

Then Ibn Jarir gave as his reason that Qatadah and others narrated it from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Salman, as a mawquf (halted) report. [Tafsir al-Tabari (9/565). Its chain includes Muhammad ibn Dinar al-Azdi in the marfu' version, who is weak.] As for the majority of scholars, they gave precedence to the hadith of "Adi over this, and sought to weaken the hadith of Abu Tha'labah and others. Some scholars interpreted it to mean that if he eats from the game after waiting for his companion, and the time has been prolonged and the companion has not come, and he eats from it out of hunger or the like, then there is no harm in that, because in this situation there is no fear that he withheld it for himself. This differs from when he eats from it at the very first moment, for then it becomes apparent that he withheld it for himself. And Allah knows best.

As for hunting birds (al-jawarih min al-tair), al-Shafi'i explicitly stated that they are like dogs, so what they eat from is forbidden according to the majority, and it is not forbidden according to others. Al-Muzani, one of our companions, chose the view that it is not forbidden to eat what hunting birds and beasts of prey have eaten from, and this is the position of Abu Hanifah and Ahmad. They said: because it is not possible to train them the way a dog is trained by beating and the like, and also because they are only trained by eating from the game, so this is excused. Also, the text was revealed only regarding the dog, not regarding birds. Shaykh Abu 'Ali said in "al-Ifsah": If we say that what the dog has eaten from is forbidden, then regarding the forbiddance of what birds have eaten from there are two opinions. Al-Qadi Abu al-Tayyib rejected this branching and ordering, because of al-Shafi'i's explicit statement, may Allah have mercy on him, on equating the two. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

As for ﴿al-mutaraddiyah﴾ (the animal that falls to its death), it is that which falls from a high place or an elevated spot and dies from that, so it is not lawful.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿al-mutaraddiyah﴾ is the one that falls from a mountain. Qatadah said: it is the one that falls into a well. Al-Suddi said: it is the one that falls from a mountain or falls into a well.

As for ﴿al-nati'ah﴾ (the animal gored to death), it is the one that died because another animal gored it, so it is forbidden, even if the horn wounded it and blood came out of it, even if from its throat.

Al-nati'ah is on the pattern fa'ilah in the sense of maf'ulah, i.e., mantuhah (gored). This pattern commonly occurs in Arabic without the feminine ta' marbutah, so they say: kaff khadib (a dyed hand), and 'ayn kahil (a kohl-darkened eye), and they do not say: kaffun khadibah, nor 'aynun kahilah. As for this word, some grammarians said: the feminine ta' was used with it because it was treated as a noun, as in their saying: tariqah tawilah (a long road). Others said: the feminine ta' was brought with it to indicate femininity right at the outset, unlike 'ayn kahil and kaff khadib, because the femininity is understood from the beginning of the sentence.

* *

His saying ﴿wa ma akala al-sabu'﴾ (and what the beast of prey has eaten) means: what a lion, leopard, tiger, wolf or dog attacked, and it ate part of it so that it died from that, is forbidden, even if blood flowed from it, even from its throat. It is not lawful, by consensus. The people of the Jahiliyyah used to eat what the beast of prey had devoured of the sheep, camel, cow and the like, so Allah forbade that to the believers.

* *

His saying ﴿illa ma dhakkaytum﴾ (except what you slaughter properly) refers to what is possible to return to, from that whose cause of death has begun but which can be remedied by slaughter, and in which there is stable life. This only refers to His saying: ﴿and the strangled, the beaten, the one that falls, the gored, and what the beast of prey has eaten﴾.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿illa ma dhakkaytum﴾: he says, except what you slaughter from these while there is still spirit in it, so eat it, for it is dhaki (properly slaughtered). Similarly it was narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Suddi.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from his father, from Ali, who said: ﴿And what the beast of prey has eaten, except what you slaughter﴾ He said: if it moves its tail or kicks with its leg or blinks its eye, then eat.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Hushaym and 'Abbad narrated to us, both saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Husayn, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Harith, from Ali, who said: If you reach the slaughter of the beaten, the one that falls, or the gored, while it moves a hand or a leg, then eat it.

Similarly it was narrated from Tawus, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, al-Dahhak and others that whenever the slaughtered animal moves with a movement indicating that life remains in it after slaughter, it is lawful. This is the position of the majority of jurists, and Abu Hanifah, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said so. Ibn Wahb said: Malik was asked about a sheep whose belly was torn open by a beast of prey until its intestines came out. Malik said: I do not think any part of it should be slaughtered. Ashhab said: Malik was asked about a hyena that attacks a ram and breaks its back, whether it should be slaughtered before it dies and then eaten? He said: If it has reached the point of final breath (suhrah), I do not think it should be eaten, but if it has only struck its extremities, I see no harm in it. It was said to him: it leapt upon it and broke its back? He said: I do not like this; this one does not live from it. It was said to him: a wolf attacks a sheep and splits its belly but does not split the intestines? He said: If it has split its belly, I do not think it should be eaten.

This is the position of Malik, may Allah have mercy on him. The apparent meaning of the verse is general regarding what Malik excepted, may Allah have mercy on him, of the cases in which the animal reached a state after which it cannot live, so it requires a specifying proof for the verse. And Allah knows best.

In the two Sahihs, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, who said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, we are going to meet the enemy tomorrow and we do not have knives, so may we slaughter with reeds? He said: "What makes the blood flow and the name of Allah is mentioned over it, then eat it, except the tooth and the claw. I will tell you about that: as for the tooth, it is bone, and as for the claw, it is the knife of the Abyssinians." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2507) and Sahih Muslim no. (1968).]

In the hadith narrated by al-Daraqutni [from Abu Hurayrah] (a supplement from manuscripts D and R), marfu', and in it there is scrutiny, and it was narrated from 'Umar mawquf, and it is more authentic: "Verily the slaughter is in the throat and the lower neck, and do not hasten the souls to depart." [Sunan al-Daraqutni (4/283) via Sa'id ibn Salam, from 'Abd Allah ibn Badil, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Budayl ibn Warqa' upon a camel calling out in the paths of Mina: "Verily the slaughter is in the throat and the lower neck, and do not hasten the souls to depart." Sa'id ibn Salam is weak; al-Bukhari said he is cited as one who fabricated hadith. It was narrated mawquf from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (9/278) via Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Furafisah al-Hanafi, from 'Umar.]

In the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan, through the narration of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Abu al-'Ashra' al-Darimi, from his father, who said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, is slaughter only from the lower neck and the throat? He said: "If it were stabbed in its thigh, it would suffice for you." And it is a sahih hadith [Musnad (4/334), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2825), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1481), Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/228), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3184)]. But it is to be understood as applying to the case where one cannot slaughter it at the throat and lower neck.

* *

His saying ﴿wa ma dhubiha 'ala al-nusub﴾ (and what is slaughtered on the stone altars). Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: the nusub were stones around the Ka'bah. Ibn Jurayj said: there were three hundred and sixty of them, and the Arabs in their Jahiliyyah used to slaughter at them, and they would sprinkle what faced the House with the blood of those sacrificial animals, and they would cut up the meat and place it on the nusub.

Similarly, many others mentioned this. Allah forbade the believers this practice, and forbade them to eat these sacrifices which were performed at the nusub, even if the name of Allah was mentioned over them at the slaughter, because of the shirk which Allah and His Messenger have forbidden. This should be understood in light of this, since the forbiddance of what was dedicated to other than Allah has already preceded.

* *

His exalted saying ﴿wa an tastaqsimu bil-azlam﴾ (and that you seek decision by arrows) means: forbidden to you, O believers, is seeking decision by the azlam. Its singular is zulam, and the zay may be pronounced with a fatha, so it is said zalam. The Arabs in their Jahiliyyah used to practice this, and it refers to three arrows: on one is written "Do it," on another "Do not do it," and the third is blank with nothing on it. Some people said: written on the first is "My Lord has commanded me," and on the second "My Lord has forbidden me," and the third is blank with nothing on it. So when he shuffles them and the arrow commanding comes out, he does it, or the forbidding one, he leaves it; and if the blank one comes out, he repeats the seeking.

Istiqsam is derived from seeking the portion (qasm) from these arrows. Thus did Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir establish it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, al-Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj and 'Uthman ibn 'Ata' informed us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and that you seek decision by arrows﴾ He said: The azlam are arrows with which they sought decision in matters.

Similarly it was narrated from Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Ibn 'Abbas said: they are the arrows with which they sought decision in matters. Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others mentioned that the greatest idol of Quraysh was an idol called Hubal, which was inside the Ka'bah, set over a well in which offerings and the wealth of the Ka'bah were placed. With it were seven arrows on which were written what they would judge by, in matters that were unclear to them. Whatever came out for them from these, they would act upon it and would not deviate from it.

It is established in the Sahih that when the Prophet ﷺ entered the Ka'bah, he found images of Ibrahim and Isma'il in it, and in their hands were the arrows, so he said: "May Allah fight them! They knew that the two of them never sought decision by them at all." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4288).]

In the Sahih: that Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum, when he went out seeking the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr, while they were on their way to Madinah as emigrants, said: I sought decision by the arrows whether to harm them or not, and what I disliked came out: do not harm them. He said: So I disobeyed the arrows and followed them. Then he sought decision by them a second and third time, each time what he disliked came out: do not harm them. And it was so. Suraqah had not yet become Muslim at that time, and became Muslim afterward. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3906).]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from Raqabah, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Raja' ibn Haywah, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever practices divination (kahanah), or seeks decision by arrows, or returns from a journey with a bird (as an omen), will never enter the ranks of the elevated." [Also narrated by al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyin no. (2104) and Tammam al-Razi in al-Fawaid no. (1444), through Yahya ibn Dawud, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid with the same. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (10/213): "Its narrators are trustworthy, except that I suspect there is a break in its chain."]

Mujahid said regarding His saying ﴿and that you seek decision by arrows﴾: they are the arrows of the Arabs, and the knucklebones of Persia and Rome, with which they used to gamble.

This is Ibn Kathir's view on the arrows (al-azlam) mentioned in the verse. Mujahid's report that they were used only for gambling is open to question. Unless one says that they used them at times for istikharah (seeking guidance, a prayer for choosing between options) and at other times for gambling, and Allah knows best. Allah, glorified and exalted [added in manuscript A], has distinguished between these and gambling, which is al-maysir (games of chance), when He said at the end of the surah: ﴿O you who believe! Intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are only an abomination of Satan's handiwork. So avoid it that you may be successful. Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you through intoxicants and gambling, and to prevent you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. Will you not then desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:90-91] [Addition from manuscript R; manuscript H reads "up to His words".]

Similarly, here He said: ﴿And that you seek decision by the arrows; that is grave disobedience﴾. That is, engaging in it is wickedness, error, misguidance, ignorance, and polytheism. Allah has commanded the believers, when they are uncertain about their affairs, to seek His guidance (istikharah) by worshipping Him and then asking Him for the good choice in the matter they desire. This is as related by Imam Ahmad, al-Bukhari, and the authors of the Sunan, through various chains from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Mawali, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us the istikharah in matters just as he taught us a surah of the Qur'an, saying: "When one of you intends a matter, let him pray two rak'ahs other than the obligatory prayer, then let him say: 'O Allah, I seek Your guidance through Your knowledge, and I seek ability through Your power, and I ask You of Your great bounty, for You have power and I have none, You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen. O Allah, if You know that this matter'—and he names it—'is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair, then decree it for me, make it easy for me, and bless it for me. O Allah, if You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, decree for me the good wherever it may be, and then make me content with it.'" This is the wording of Ahmad. [Musnad 3/344; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1162; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1538; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 480; Sunan al-Nasa'i 6/80; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 1383.]

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith, which we know only from the hadith of Ibn Abi al-Mawali.

As for His words: ﴿Today those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: That is, they despaired of returning you to their religion. It was also related similarly from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Suddi, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. In this sense the authentic hadith in Sahih [Muslim] applies: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Satan has despaired of being worshipped by the worshippers in the Arabian Peninsula, but he will sow discord among them."

It may also mean that they despaired of resembling the Muslims, because of the distinguishing qualities of the Muslims that oppose polytheism and its people. For this reason He, exalted is He, commanded His believing servants to be patient and steadfast in opposing the disbelievers, and not to fear anyone but Allah, saying: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾. That is: do not fear them for opposing them, but fear Me; I will help you against them, destroy them, grant you victory over them, relieve your hearts of them, and make you superior to them in this world and the Hereafter.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved Islam as your religion﴾. This is the greatest of Allah's blessings, mighty and majestic, upon this nation, in that He perfected their religion for them, so they need no other religion and no prophet other than their Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. For this reason Allah made him the Seal of the Prophets, and sent him to mankind and jinn. There is no lawful thing except what he made lawful, no unlawful thing except what he made unlawful, and no religion except what he legislated. Everything he informed of is true and truthful, with no lie or contradiction in it, as Allah said: ﴿And the word of your Lord is fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am 6:115], that is, truthful in what He reports and just in His commands and prohibitions. When He perfected the religion for them, the blessing was complete upon them. For this reason He said: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved Islam as your religion﴾, that is: so be content with it yourselves, for it is the religion that Allah approved and loved, and sent with His most noble messengers, and revealed in His most honored scriptures.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾, that it is Islam. Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ and the believers that He had perfected faith for them, so they will never need an addition, and Allah has completed it so it will never be diminished, and Allah is pleased with it so He will never be displeased with it.

al-Suddi said, related by Asbat: This verse was revealed on the Day of 'Arafah, and no lawful or unlawful matter was revealed after it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned and died.

Asma' bint 'Umays said: I performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on that pilgrimage. While we were traveling, Jibril appeared to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ leaned on the riding beast, and the beast could not bear the weight of what was upon it of the Qur'an, so it knelt down. I came to him and covered him with a cloak that was on me.

Ibn Jurayj and others said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died eighty-one days after the Day of 'Arafah.

Ibn Jarir related both reports, then said: Sufyan ibn Wakee' narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Harun ibn 'Antarah, from his father, who said: When ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾ was revealed, and that was on the Day of the Greater Hajj, 'Umar wept. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "What makes you weep?" He said: "What made me weep is that we were in increase in our religion, but now it has been perfected, and nothing perfected ever remains without decline." He said: "You have spoken the truth." [Tafsir al-Tabari 9/519.]

This meaning is supported by the authentic hadith: "Islam began as something strange, and it will return to being strange, so blessed are the strangers." [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 145, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, and no. 146, from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]

Imam Ahmad said: Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, Abu al-'Umays narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: A man from the Jews came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab [may Allah be pleased with him] [Addition from manuscript A] and said: "O Commander of the Believers, you recite a verse in your Book; had it been revealed to us, the Jewish community, we would have taken that day as a festival." He said: "Which verse?" He said: His words: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you﴾. 'Umar said: "By Allah, I know the day on which it was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the hour in which it was revealed to him. It was revealed in the evening at 'Arafah, on a Friday."

al-Bukhari related it from al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah, from Ja'far ibn 'Awn, with the same chain. Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i also related it through various chains from Qays ibn Muslim, with the same. [Musnad 1/28; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 45; Sahih Muslim no. 3017; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3043; Sunan al-Nasa'i 5/251.] The wording of al-Bukhari, at the explanation of this verse, through the chain of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Qays, from Tariq, is: The Jews said to 'Umar: "You recite a verse, had it been revealed about us, we would have taken it as a festival." 'Umar said: "I know when it was revealed, and where it was revealed, and where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was when it was revealed: it was on the Day of 'Arafah, and I was by Allah at 'Arafah." Sufyan said: "I doubt whether it was a Friday or not." [The verse:] ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4606.]

As for Sufyan's doubt, may Allah have mercy on him: if it occurred in the narration, it is caution, since he doubted whether his teacher had informed him of it or not. If it was a doubt about whether standing at 'Arafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage was on a Friday, then I do not think this would come from al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, for this is a known and definite matter on which none of the scholars of military campaigns and biography, nor of jurists, disagreed. Many hadiths about it have been transmitted through multiple chains and their authenticity is not doubted. And Allah knows best. This hadith has also been related from more than one route from 'Umar.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, Raja' ibn Abi Salamah informed us, 'Ubadah ibn Nusayy informed us, our commander Ishaq informed us, — Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: He is Ishaq ibn Kharashah — from Qabisah, that is Ibn Dhu'ayb, who said: Ka'b said: "If this verse had been revealed to any other nation than this one, they would have looked at the day on which it was revealed to them and taken it as a festival in which they gather." 'Umar said: "Which verse, O Ka'b?" He said: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾. 'Umar said: "I know the day on which it was revealed and the place where it was revealed. It was revealed on a Friday and on the Day of 'Arafah, and both, praise be to Allah, are a festival for us."

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Qabisah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ammar — he is the client of the Banu Hashim — that Ibn 'Abbas recited: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved Islam as your religion﴾. A Jew said: "Had this verse been revealed to us, we would have taken its day as a festival." Ibn 'Abbas said: "It was revealed on a day of two festivals: a festival day and a Friday." [Tafsir al-Tabari 9/525.]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Kamil narrated to us, Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, Yahya ibn al-Humani narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Salman, from Abu 'Umar al-Bazzar, from Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, from 'Ali [may Allah be pleased with him] [Addition from manuscript A], who said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was standing on the evening of 'Arafah: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu 'Amir Isma'il ibn 'Amr al-Sukuni narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Qays al-Sukuni narrated to us, that he heard Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan on the pulpit reciting this verse: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾ until he finished it, and then said: It was revealed on the Day of 'Arafah, on a Friday.

Ibn Mardawayh related, through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Umar ibn Musa ibn Wajih, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, who said: This verse was revealed: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved Islam as your religion﴾, on the Day of 'Arafah while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing at the place of standing.

And as for what Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh and al-Tabarani narrated through the route of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Khalid ibn Abi Imran, from Hanash ibn Abd Allah al-San'ani, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Your Prophet ﷺ was born on a Monday, [and he received revelation on a Monday] [[Addition from A.]] and he left Makkah on a Monday, and entered Madinah on a Monday, and Surat al-Ma'idah was revealed on a Monday: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾, and the raising of the mention was on a Monday." This is a strange report (athar gharib) [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/530).]], and its chain is weak.

Imam Ahmad also narrated it: Musa ibn Dawud related to us, Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Khalid ibn Abi Imran, from Hanash al-San'ani, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ was born on a Monday, was commissioned on a Monday, departed as an emigrant from Makkah to Madinah on a Monday, arrived in Madinah on a Monday, died on a Monday, and placed [[In A: "raised".]] the Black Stone on a Monday."

This is the wording of Ahmad, and it does not mention the revelation of al-Ma'idah on a Monday [[Al-Musnad (1/277). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/196): "In it is Ibn Lahi'ah, who is weak, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy and from the people of the Sahih."]]. Allah knows best. Perhaps Ibn Abbas meant that it was revealed on the day of two festivals (eid), as mentioned earlier, and so it became confused for the narrator. Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: "It has been said: that is not a day known among the people." Then he narrated through the route of al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾, that he said: "That is not a day known among the people." He said: "It has also been said that it was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during his journey to the Farewell Pilgrimage." Then he narrated it through the route of Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

I say: Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Abu Harun al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that it was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Ghadir Khumm, when he said to Ali: "Whoever I am his mawla, then Ali is his mawla." Then he narrated it from Abu Hurayrah [[In its chain is Abu Harun al-Abdi, a Shi'i narrator who is abandoned (matruk), but Atiyyah al-Awfi has followed him; al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, no. (3737), Majma' al-Bahrayn; and the hadith of Abu Hurayrah was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, no. (3738), Majma' al-Bahrayn. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said in Minhaj al-Sunnah al-Nabawiyyah: "It is not in the Sahihs, but it is among what scholars have related, and people have disputed its authenticity. Al-Bukhari, Ibrahim al-Harbi and a group of the people of hadith criticised it and declared it weak, and it is reported from Ahmad ibn Hanbal that he graded it as hasan, as al-Tirmidhi did." Shaykh Nasir al-Albani collected its routes in al-Silsilah al-Sahihah (1750).]] and in it: that it was the eighteenth day of Dhu al-Hijjah, meaning his return ﷺ from the Farewell Pilgrimage.

Neither this nor that is sound. Rather, the correct view, about which there is no doubt, is that it was revealed on the Day of 'Arafah, and it was a Friday, as was related by the Commander of the Faithful Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ali ibn Abi Talib, the first of the kings of Islam Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, the interpreter of the Qur'an Abd Allah ibn Abbas, and Samurah ibn Jundub, may Allah be pleased with them all. It was also transmitted as a mursal report by Amir al-Sha'bi, Qatadah ibn Di'amah, Shahr ibn Hawshab, and many other imams and scholars. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari chose this view, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿So whoever is compelled by severe hunger, not inclining toward sin, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: that is, whoever is driven by need to consume any of these prohibited things which He mentioned, due to a necessity that compelled him to that, then it is permissible for him to consume that, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful toward him, because He knows the need of His compelled servant and his dependence upon that, so He overlooks it and forgives him. In the Musnad and Sahih Ibn Hibban, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah loves that His concessions be taken, just as He dislikes that His disobedience be committed." [[Al-Musnad (2/108) and Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (545), Mawarid. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (3/162): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]] This is the wording of Ibn Hibban. In a wording of Ahmad: "Whoever does not accept the concession of Allah, upon him is sin like the mountains of 'Arafah." [[Al-Musnad (2/71).]]

For this reason the jurists said: Eating carrion may at times be obligatory, namely when one fears for his life from destruction and finds nothing else; and it may at times be recommended, and it may at times be permissible, according to circumstances. They differed: is one to consume from it only the amount that keeps him from perishing, or may he eat until he is satisfied, or eat until satisfied and take provisions? There are several opinions, as is established in the book al-Ahkam. Regarding the case where one finds carrion and someone else's food, or game while in a state of ihram: may he eat the carrion, or that game and then owe its compensation, or that food and then owe its equivalent? There are two opinions, which are two views of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. It is not a condition for the permissibility of eating carrion that three days pass during which he finds no food, as many common people and others may imagine; rather, whenever he is compelled to it, it is permissible for him. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, al-Awza'i related to us, Hassan ibn Atiyyah related to us, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, that they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are in a land where we are afflicted by hunger, so when is carrion lawful for us there?" He said: "When you have not had a morning meal, nor an evening meal, nor gathered a handful of herbs, then it is your affair with it." [[In A: "tahtafnu".]]

Ahmad narrated it alone through this route, and its chain is sound according to the conditions of the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim). Likewise Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Asadi, from al-Awza'i with it [[Al-Musnad (5/218); Tafsir al-Tabari (9/538). Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (4/125) through al-Awza'i, and said: "It meets the conditions of both, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi criticised this, saying: "In it is a break in the chain (inqita')."]]. But some narrated it from al-Awza'i, from Hassan ibn Atiyyah, from Muslim ibn Yazid, from Abu Waqid, with it [[Both were narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/284) through al-Awza'i with it.]]. Others narrated it from al-Awza'i, from Hassan, from Martad, or Abu Martad, from Abu Waqid, with it [[Both were narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/284) through al-Awza'i with it.]]. Ibn Jarir narrated it from Hannad ibn al-Sari, from Isa ibn Yunus, from Hassan, from a man who was named to him, and he related it. He also narrated it from Hannad, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from al-Awza'i, from Hassan, as a mursal report [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/542).]].

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Awn, who said: "I found with al-Hasan the book of Samurah, and I read it to him, and in it was: 'And it is permitted from the harms (al-adrar): a night drink or a morning drink.'"

Abu Kurayb related to us, Hushaym related to us, from al-Khasib ibn Zayd al-Tamimi [[In A: "Yazid al-Taymi".]], al-Hasan related to us, that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "Until when does the forbidden become lawful for me?" He said: "Until when your family drink of the milk, or their provision comes."

Ibn Humayd related to us, Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, Umar ibn Abd Allah ibn Urwah related to us, from his grandfather Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from his grandmother [[In A: "from one he narrated from".]], that a Bedouin man came to the Prophet ﷺ seeking a ruling about what Allah had forbidden to him and what He had made lawful for him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The good things are lawful for you, and the vile things are forbidden to you, except that you become in need of food that is not lawful for you, and then you eat from it until you are free of need." The man said: "And what is the poverty that makes it lawful for me? And what is the richness that makes me free of that?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "If you are hoping for offspring, so that you will get through with the flesh of your livestock until your offspring, or if you are hoping for wealth, seeking it, and you obtain some of it, then feed your family whatever appears to you, until you are free of it." The Bedouin said: "And what is the richness that I leave behind when I find it?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "When you have given your family a night drink, then avoid what Allah has forbidden to you of food; as for your property, all of it is accessible, and there is nothing unlawful in it." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/540).]]

The meaning of his saying "as long as you have not had a morning drink" (ma lam tasTabihu): it means the morning meal (al-ghada'), and "nor an evening drink" (wa-ma lam taghtabiqu): it means the evening meal (al-'asha'), "or gathered a handful of herbs (takhtafi'u baqlan), then it is your affair with it": that is, then eat from it. Ibn Jarir said: This word is transmitted in four ways: "takhtafi'u" with a hamzah; "tahtafiyu" with the yaa and the haa lightened; "tahtafu" with the faa doubled; and "tahtafu" with the haa and lightened; and the hamzah is possible. Thus he mentioned it in the Tafsir.

Another hadith: Abu Dawud said: Harun ibn Abd Allah related to us, al-Fadl ibn Dukayn related to us, Uqbah ibn Wahb ibn Uqbah al-Amiri related to us [[In A: "Wahb ibn Uqbah ibn Wahb al-Amiri".]], I heard my father narrate from al-Fujay' al-Amiri, that he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "What is lawful for us of carrion?" He said: "What is your food?" We said: "We take a morning drink and an evening drink." Abu Nu'aym said: Uqbah explained it to me: "A bowl in the morning, and a bowl in the evening [[In A: "evening drink".]]." He said: "By my father, that is hunger." And carrion was made lawful for them in this state.

Abu Dawud alone narrated it [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2817).]]. It seems they used to take a morning and evening drink of something that did not suffice them, so carrion was made lawful for them to complete their sufficiency. Whoever holds that it is permissible to eat from it until one reaches satisfaction, and that this is not restricted to merely keeping alive, may take evidence from it. Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Abu Dawud said: Musa ibn Isma'il related to us, Hammad related to us, Simak related to us, from Jabir ibn Samurah, that a man settled in al-Harrah, and with him were his family and his child. A man said to him: "Indeed, a she-camel of mine has strayed; if you find it, then hold on to it." He found it, but did not find its owner. Then it fell ill, and his wife said: "Slaughter it." He refused, and it died. His wife said to him: "Skin it, so that we may dry its fat and its meat and eat it." He said: "Until I ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He went to him and asked him, and he said: "Do you have a sufficiency that suffices you?" He said: "No." He said: "Then eat it." Then its owner came and was informed of the matter, and he said: "Why did you not slaughter it?" He said: "I was ashamed before you."

Abu Dawud alone narrated it [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2817).]]. Whoever holds that eating it is permissible up to satiety, and taking provisions from it for a period in which one is strongly assumed to need it, may also take evidence from it. Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿not inclining toward sin﴾: that is, not indulging in the disobedience of Allah. Allah has permitted that for him and remained silent about the other, as He said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿So whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing, then there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [the verse: 173].

Those who say that a sinner in his travel may not take any concession of travel have used this verse as evidence, because concessions are not attained through acts of disobedience. Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verse 4 (part 1 of 3):

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned what He had forbidden in the preceding verse, of the harmful impurities (al-khaba'ith) that are harmful to the one who consumes them, whether to his body, his religion, or both, and made an exception for what is permitted in a state of necessity, as He said: ﴿And He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to﴾ [al-An'am: 119], He said after it: ﴿They ask you what has been made lawful for them. Say: "Lawful for you are the good things"﴾, just as He said in Surah al-A'raf concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) that he ﴿makes lawful for them the good things and forbids for them the impurities﴾ [al-A'raf: 157].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Lahi'a narrated to me, Ata' ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Adi ibn Hatim and Zayd ibn al-Muhalhil al-Ta'iyyayn, that they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah has forbidden carrion, so what is lawful for us from it?" Then this was revealed: ﴿They ask you what has been made lawful for them. Say: "Lawful for you are the good things"﴾. Sa'id [ibn Jubayr] said: meaning, the slaughtered animals that are lawful and good for them. And Muqatil [ibn Hayyan] said, regarding His words ﴿Say: "Lawful for you are the good things"﴾: the good things are what has been made lawful for them of everything they may obtain, which is the lawful sustenance. And al-Zuhri was asked about drinking urine for treatment, and he said: "It is not among the good things."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2817]. Ibn Wahb said: Malik was asked about the sale of clay that people eat, and he said: "It is not among the good things."

* *

As for His words, ﴿and what you have taught of the trained hunting animals (jawarih), training them as hunters trained them﴾: that is, lawful for you are the slaughtered animals over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, and the good things of sustenance, and lawful for you is what you hunt with the trained animals (jawarih), which are dogs, leopards, falcons and the like, as is the position of the majority (jumhur) of the Companions, the Successors and the imams. Among those who said this: Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and what you have taught of the trained hunting animals (jawarih), training them as hunters trained them﴾, and they are the trained dogs, the falcon, and every bird trained for hunting; and the jawarih: meaning the predatory dogs, leopards, falcons and the like.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this, then said: It is also narrated from Khaytham, Tawus, Mujahid, Makhul and Yahya ibn Abi Kathir something similar. It is narrated from al-Hasan that he said: the hawk and the falcon are among the jawarih. It is narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn something similar. Then it is narrated from Mujahid that he disliked hunting all birds, and he recited the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿and what you have taught of the trained hunting animals (jawarih), training them as hunters trained them﴾. He said: It is also narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr something similar.

Ibn Jarir transmitted it from al-Dahhak and al-Suddi. Then he said: Hannad narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: As for what is caught by birds of prey (al-buzat) and other birds, what you reach (alive and slaughter) is yours, and otherwise do not eat it.

I say: What is reported from the majority is that hunting with birds is like hunting with dogs, because they seize the prey with their talons just as dogs seize it, so there is no difference. This is the position of the four imams and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and he argued for it with what he narrated from Hannad: Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about hunting with the bazi, and he said: "What it holds for you, eat."

Imam Ahmad made an exception for hunting with the black dog, because in his view it is one whose killing is obligatory and whose keeping is not permitted, due to what is established in Sahih Muslim from Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prayer is cut off by a donkey, a woman, and a black dog." I said: "What is the matter with the black dog as opposed to the red one?" He said: "The black dog is a devil."

And in another hadith: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the killing of dogs, then said: "What is the matter with them and the dogs? Kill from them every jet-black one."

These animals with which hunting is done are called jawarih, from al-jarh, which means earning. As the Arabs say: "So-and-so jarah his family good," meaning he earned good for them. And they say: "So-and-so has no jarih," meaning he has no earner. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have earned (jaraḥtum) by day﴾ [al-An'am: 60], meaning what you have earned of good and evil.

The reason for the revelation of this noble verse is mentioned in the hadith narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: Hajjaj ibn Hamza narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Musa ibn Ubayda narrated to me, Aban ibn Salih narrated to me, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Salma Umm Rafi', from Abu Rafi', the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the killing of dogs, so they were killed. People came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is lawful for us from this community which you have ordered to be killed?" He said: So he was silent, and Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you what has been made lawful for them. Say: "Lawful for you are the good things, and what you have taught of the trained hunting animals (jawarih), training them as hunters trained them"﴾, the verse. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a man sends his dog and mentions the name of Allah, and it holds the game for him, then let him eat what it has not eaten from."

Similarly Ibn Jarir narrated it, from Abu Kurayb, from Zayd ibn al-Hubab with its chain, from Abu Rafi', who said: Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) to ask permission to enter upon him. He was given permission and said: "We have given you permission, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Indeed, but we do not enter a house in which there is a dog." Abu Rafi' said: So he commanded me to kill every dog in Medina, and I killed them, until I came to a woman who had a dog barking at her, so I left it out of mercy for her. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him, and he commanded me, so I returned to the dog and killed it. Then they came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is lawful for us from this community which you have ordered to be killed?" He said: So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was silent. He said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They ask you what has been made lawful for them. Say: "Lawful for you are the good things, and what you have taught of the trained hunting animals (jawarih), training them as hunters trained them"﴾.

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Aban ibn Salih, with it, and said: "Sahih, but they did not record it." [Ibn Jarir narrated it in his tafsir (9/545) through the route of Zayd ibn al-Hubab, and al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/326) through the route of Musa ibn Ubayda. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/42): "In it is Musa ibn Ubayda al-Rabadhi, who is weak." I say: It has been corroborated: Muhammad ibn Ishaq corroborated him. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (9/235), and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/311), through the route of Mu'alla ibn Mansur, from Ibn Abi Za'ida, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, with it in abridged form.]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrima, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Abu Rafi' to kill the dogs, until he reached al-'Awali. Then Asim ibn Adi, Sa'd ibn Khaythama and Uwaym ibn Sa'ida came in and said: "What has been made lawful for us, O Messenger of Allah?" So this was revealed: ﴿They ask you what has been made lawful for them. Say: "Lawful for you are the good things, and what you have taught of the trained hunting animals (jawarih), training them as hunters trained them"﴾ [the verse].

Al-Hakim narrated it through the route of Simak, from Ikrima. [Tafsir al-Tabari (9/546) and al-Mustadrak (2/311).] Likewise Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said regarding the reason for the revelation of this verse: that it concerns the killing of dogs.

* *

As for His words, ﴿training them﴾ (mukallibin): it may be a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in ﴿you have taught﴾ (allamtum), so it is a circumstantial clause from the agent; and it may be a circumstantial clause from the object, which is ﴿the trained hunting animals (jawarih)﴾, meaning: "and what you have taught of the trained hunting animals, while they are training (mukallibat) for the prey." This is because the jawarih seize the prey with their claws or nails. From this, in such a case, it is inferred that if the jarihah kills the prey by its impact, or by its beak or its talon, it is not lawful. This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i and a group of scholars. Therefore He said: ﴿You teach them from what Allah has taught you﴾, which is that when he sends it, it runs out, and when he calls it, it comes back, and when it catches the prey, it holds it for its master until he comes to it and does not keep it for itself. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So eat of what they hold for you, and mention the name of Allah over it﴾. So whenever the jarihah is trained and holds the prey for its master, and he mentioned the name of Allah when he sent it, the prey is lawful, even if it killed it, by consensus.

The Sunnah has come with the same as what this noble verse indicates, as is established in the two Sahihs from Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I send trained dogs and mention the name of Allah." He said: "When you send your trained dog and mention the name of Allah, then eat what it holds for you." I said: "Even if they kill?" He said: "Even if they kill, so long as no dog that is not one of them has joined it, for you only mentioned the name over your dog and did not mention it over another." I said to him: "Indeed I shoot the prey with a mi'rad (a throwing stick) and hit it?" He said: "When you shoot with the mi'rad and it pierces, then eat it; but if it strikes with its breadth, then it is waqidh (killed by blow), so do not eat it." And in one wording of both of them: "When you send your dog, mention the name of Allah, and if it holds for you and you reach it alive, then slaughter it; and if you reach it already killed and it has not eaten from it, then eat it, for the seizure of the dog is its slaughter." And in one narration of both: "But if it has eaten, then do not eat, for I fear that it held it for itself." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5483 and Sahih Muslim no. 1929.]

This is evidence for the jumhur, and it is the sound position of the school of al-Shafi'i: that if the dog eats from the prey, it becomes unlawful absolutely, and they did not distinguish, as the hadith has come. And it is reported from a group of the earlier generation that they said: it is not unlawful absolutely.

Mention of the reports on this:

Ibn Jarir said: Hannad narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Qatada, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Salman al-Farisi said: "Eat, even if it has eaten two-thirds of it" — meaning the prey — "if the dog has eaten from it." Likewise Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah and Umar ibn Amir narrated it from Qatada. Likewise Muhammad ibn Zayd narrated it from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Salman.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Mujahid ibn Musa, from Yazid, from Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani and al-Qasim, that Salman said: "If the dog eats, then eat, even if it has eaten two-thirds of it."

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Makhrama ibn Bukayr informed me, from his father, from Humayd ibn Malik ibn Khuthaym al-Du'ali; that he asked Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas about game from which a dog has eaten. He said: "Eat, even if nothing remains of it but a scrap" – i.e., "except a morsel."[[In A: "Bakr".]][[In A: "Hashim".]][[In R: "Jadhiyya".]][[Addition from R.]]

Shu'ba narrated it from Abd Rabbih ibn Sa'id, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "Eat, even if it has eaten two-thirds of it."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, Abd al-A'la related to us, Dawud related to us, from Amir, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "If you release your dog and it eats from it, then if it has eaten two-thirds and one-third remains, eat."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, al-Mu'tamir related to us, who said: I heard Ubayd Allah [[In A: "Abd Allah".]] – and Hannad related to us, Abda related to us, from Ubayd Allah [[In A: "Abd Allah".]] ibn Umar – from Nafi', from Abd Allah ibn Umar, who said: "When you release your trained dog and mention the name of Allah, then eat what it holds for you, whether it has eaten or not."

Similarly, Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, Ibn Abi Dhi'b and others narrated it from Nafi'.

These reports are established from Salman, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Abu Hurayra and Ibn Umar. It is also related from Ali and Ibn Abbas. It has been differed upon from Ata' and al-Hasan al-Basri. It is the view of al-Zuhri, Rabi'a and Malik. Al-Shafi'i adopted it in his earlier (qadim) view, and alluded to it in his later (jadid) view.

It has also been related with a marfu' chain from the route of Salman al-Farisi. Ibn Jarir said: Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kula'i related to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Musa al-Lahuni related to us, Muhammad ibn Dinar – he is al-Tahi – related to us, from Abu Iyas Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Salman al-Farisi, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "If a man releases his dog at game and reaches it after it has eaten from it, let him eat what remains."

Then Ibn Jarir said: There is scrutiny in the chain of this hadith, and Sa'id is not known to have heard from Salman; the reliable narrators relate it as the words of Salman, not as a marfu' report.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/565, 566).]]

What Ibn Jarir said is correct. However, this meaning has been related as marfu' through other routes. Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Minhal al-Darir related to us, Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, Habib al-Mu'allim related to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that a Bedouin – called Abu Tha'laba – said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have trained dogs, so give me a ruling concerning their game." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If you have trained dogs, eat from what they hold for you." He said: "Even if they are slaughtered and not slaughtered?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Even if it has eaten from it?" He said: "Yes, even if it has eaten from it." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, give me a ruling concerning my bow." He said: "Eat what your bow returns to you." He said: "Even if it is slaughtered and not slaughtered?" He said: "Even if it disappears from you as long as it has not reached it, or you find in it a trace other than your arrow." He said: "Give me a ruling concerning the vessels of the Magians when we are compelled to use them." He said: "Wash them and eat in them."[[In A: "minha".]]

Thus Abu Dawud related it,[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2857).]] and al-Nasa'i also recorded it. Abu Dawud also related it through the route of Busr ibn Ubayd Allah [[In R: "Yusuf ibn Sayf"; in A: "Yunus ibn Sayf".]] from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu Tha'laba, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you release your dog and mention the name of Allah, then eat, even if it has eaten from it, and eat what your hand returns to you."[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2852); I did not find it in Sunan al-Nasa'i.]]

These are two good chains. Al-Thawri related from Simak ibn Harb, from Adi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whatever a harmful dog holds for you, eat." I said: "Even if it has eaten?" He said: "Yes."

Abd al-Malik ibn Habib related: Asad ibn Musa related to us, from Ibn Abi Za'ida, from al-Sha'bi, from Adi, the same.[[Also related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (5475) and Muslim in his Sahih no. (1929) through the route of Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida, with the same wording.]]

These reports indicate that it is excused if the dog has eaten from it. Those who did not make game unlawful because a dog ate from it, or something similar, have used them as evidence, as has been mentioned earlier from those we related from. Others took a middle position, saying: if it eats immediately after holding it, it becomes unlawful, based on the hadith of Adi ibn Hatim, and for the reason the Prophet (ﷺ) pointed to: "If it has eaten, do not eat, for I fear it held it for itself." As for if he holds it, then waits for its owner, and it takes long and he becomes hungry, so it eats from the game out of its hunger, this does not affect its unlawfulness. They applied the hadith of Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani to this case. This is a good distinction, and reconciling the two hadiths in this way is sound. Al-Ustadh Abu al-Ma'ali al-Juwayni wished in his book "al-Nihaya" that some expositor would detail this distinction, and Allah fulfilled his wish. A group of the companions of al-Shafi'i held this view and this distinction. Others stated a fourth view on the question: distinguishing between a dog's eating, which makes it unlawful based on the hadith of Adi, and the eating of falcons and the like, which does not make it unlawful, because such birds accept training only through eating.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Asbat ibn Muhammad related to us, Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani related to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Abbas, that he said concerning birds: "If you release it and it kills, then eat, for a dog, when you strike it, does not return. If a bird has been trained to return to its owner and does not strike, then when it eats from the game and plucks the feathers, eat."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/557).]]

Similarly said Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, and Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman.

These may be supported by what Ibn Abi Hatim related: Abu Sa'id related to us, al-Muharibi related to us, Mujalid related to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are a people who hunt with dogs and hawks, so what is lawful for us from them?" He said: "What you have taught of the hunting animals, training them, teaching them what Allah has taught you, so eat of what they hold for you, and mention the name of Allah over it." Then he said: "Whatever you release of a dog and mention the name of Allah over it, eat what it holds for you." I said: "Even if it kills?" He said: "Even if it kills, as long as it has not eaten." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if our dogs mix with other dogs?" He said: "Do not eat until you know that it was your dog that held it." He said: "I said: We are a people who shoot. What is lawful for us?" He said: "Whatever you mention the name of Allah over and it pierces, eat."

The argument for them is that he stipulated for the dog that it not eat, and did not stipulate that for hawks, which shows the distinction between them in ruling.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So eat of what they hold for you, and mention the name of Allah over it﴾, meaning at the time of release, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Adi ibn Hatim: "When you release your trained dog and mention the name of Allah, then eat what it holds for you." In the hadith of Abu Tha'laba, which is also recorded in the two Sahihs: "When you release your dog, mention the name of Allah, and when you shoot your arrow, mention the name of Allah." For this reason, some imams, such as Ahmad ibn Hanbal, according to the well-known report from him, required saying the basmala at the release of the dog and the shooting of the arrow, based on this verse and this hadith. This is the well-known view of the majority, that the intended meaning of this verse is the command to say the basmala at the time of release, as al-Suddi and others said.

Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿and mention the name of Allah over it﴾, that he said: "When you release your hunting animal, say: In the name of Allah. If you forget, there is no blame."

Some people said: The intended meaning of this verse is the command to say the basmala at the time of eating, as is established in the Sahih, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught his stepson Umar ibn Abi Salama, saying: "Say the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is near you."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5376) and Sahih Muslim no. (2022).]] In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Aisha, that they said: "O Messenger of Allah, a people come to us – recently converted from disbelief – with meat, and we do not know whether the name of Allah was mentioned over it or not?" He said: "Say the name of Allah yourselves and eat."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5507).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yazid related to us, Hisham related to us, from Budayl, from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, from Aisha, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to eat food with six of his companions, and a Bedouin came and ate it in two mouthfuls. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, if he had mentioned the name of Allah, it would have sufficed you. When any of you eats, let him mention the name of Allah, and if he forgets to mention the name of Allah at the beginning, let him say: In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end."

This was also related by Ibn Majah from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, from Yazid ibn Harun, with the same chain.[[Musnad (6/143) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3264).]] This is an interrupted chain between Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr and Aisha, for he did not hear this hadith from her, as shown by what Imam Ahmad related:

Abd al-Wahhab related to us, Hisham – meaning Ibn Abi Abd Allah al-Dastuwa'i – informed us, from Budayl, from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, that a woman from among them – called Umm Kulthum – related to him, from Aisha, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was eating food with six of his companions, and a hungry Bedouin came and ate it in two mouthfuls. He said: "Indeed, if he had mentioned the name of Allah, it would have sufficed you. When any of you eats, let him mention the name of Allah, and if he forgets the name of Allah at its beginning, let him say: In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end."

[And] it was also related by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i through several routes, from Hisham al-Dastuwa'i, with the same wording.[[Musnad (6/265), (6/246); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3767); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1858); al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i no. (10112).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih.

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Ali ibn Abd Allah related to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, Jabir ibn Subh related to us, al-Muthanna ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Khuza'i related to me, and I accompanied him to Wasit. He would say the basmala at the beginning of his meal, and at the last morsel he would say: In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end.

I said to him: You say the basmala at the beginning of what you eat; what do you think of your saying at the end of what you eat: In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end? He said: I will tell you about that. My grandfather Umayya ibn Mukhashsha – and he was among the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) – I heard him say: A man was eating while the Prophet was watching, and he did not say the basmala until, at the end of his meal, there was one morsel left, and he said: In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, the Shaytan kept eating with him until he said the basmala, so nothing remained in his stomach until he vomited it up."

This is how Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also narrated it, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Subh [in A: "Sabih"] al-Rasibi, Abu Bishr al-Basri.[[Al-Musnad (4/336), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3768), and al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i no. (10113).]] Ibn Ma'in and al-Nasa'i declared him trustworthy (thiqah), but Abu al-Fath al-Azdi said: "The proof is not established by him."[[In A: "He is not a proof."]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Khaythama, from Abu Hudhayfa. Abu Abd al-Rahman Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: his name is Salama ibn al-Haytham ibn Suhayb, one of the companions of Ibn Mas'ud, from Hudhayfa, who said: "When we were present with the Prophet [ﷺ][[Addition from A.]] at a meal, we would not put our hands out until the Messenger of Allah [ﷺ][[Addition from A.]] began and put his hand forward. Once we were present with him at a meal when a girl came as though she were being pushed, and she went to put her hand in the food. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ seized her hand. Then a bedouin came as though he were being pushed, and he went to put his hand in the food, and the Messenger of Allah [ﷺ][[Addition from W, A.]] seized his hand. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Indeed, the Shaytan makes lawful the food when the name of Allah is not mentioned over it. He brought this girl so that he might make it lawful through her, so I seized her hand. He brought this bedouin so that he might make it lawful through him, so I seized his hand. By the One in whose hand my soul is, his hand is in my hand along with their two hands,' meaning the Shaytan." Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also narrated it through the hadith of al-A'mash with this chain.[[Al-Musnad (5/382), Sahih Muslim no. (2017), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3766), and al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i no. (6754).]]

Another hadith: Muslim and the authors of the Sunan, except al-Tirmidhi,[[Sahih Muslim no. (2018), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3765), al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i no. (6757), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3887).]] narrated through the route of Ibn Juraij, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When a man enters his house and mentions Allah at his entering and at his meal, the Shaytan says: 'There is no night lodging for you and no dinner.' And when he enters and does not mention the name of Allah at his entering, the Shaytan says: 'You have gained the night lodging.' And if he does not mention the name of Allah at his meal, he says: 'You have gained the night lodging and the dinner.'" This is the wording of Abu Dawud.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Wahshi ibn Harb ibn Wahshi ibn Harb, from his father, from his grandfather, that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We eat and are not satisfied?" He said: "Perhaps you eat separately. Gather around your food and mention the name of Allah, and it will be blessed for you."

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah also narrated it through the route of al-Walid ibn Muslim.[[Al-Musnad (3/501), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3764), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3286).]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verse 5 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned what He had forbidden to His believing servants of the foul things and what He had permitted them of the good things, He said after that: ﴿Today the good things have been made lawful for you﴾.

Then He mentioned the ruling on the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, and said: ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Umamah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Hasan, Makhul, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Suddi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it means their slaughtered animals.

This is a matter on which the scholars have reached consensus (ijma'): their slaughtered animals are lawful for the Muslims, because they believe in the prohibition of slaughtering for other than Allah, and they mention upon their slaughtered animals only the name of Allah, even if they hold concerning Him things that are far removed from His majesty; He is exalted and sanctified above what they say. It is established in the Sahih that 'Abdullah ibn Mughaffal said: "A waterskin of fat was lowered down to us on the day of Khaybar. [He said:] I embraced it [in another version: "I held it back"] and said: 'I will not give any of this to anyone today.' Then I turned and saw the Prophet (ﷺ) smiling."

The jurists used this to show that it is permissible to take what one needs of food and the like from the spoils before they are divided, and this is clear. The jurists of the Hanafis, the Shafi'is and the Hanbalis also used it against the followers of Malik in their prohibition of eating what the Jews believe to be forbidden of their slaughtered animals, such as fats and the like of what was forbidden to them. The Malikis do not permit the Muslims to eat it, on the basis of Allah's words: ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾, and they said: this is not part of their food. The majority answered them with this hadith, but there is room for scrutiny in that, because it is a specific incident (qadiyyat 'ayn), and it is possible that it was fat which they believed to be lawful, such as the fat of the back and the intestinal fat and the like. And Allah knows best.

More decisive in its indication is what is established in the Sahih: that the people of Khaybar presented the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a roasted sheep, and they had poisoned its foreleg; and the Prophet (ﷺ) liked the foreleg, so he took it and tore off a bite from it, and the foreleg informed him that it was poisoned. He spat it out, and the poison affected the molars of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his aorta. Bishr ibn al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur ate with him from it, and he died. So the Prophet (ﷺ) killed the Jewish woman who had poisoned it, whose name was Zaynab, and she was put to death in retaliation for Bishr ibn al-Bara'. [Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan (no. 4512) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

The point of the indication in it is that he resolved to eat it, and he and those with him ate it, and he did not ask them whether they had removed from it what they believe to be forbidden of its fat or not.

In another hadith: a Jew hosted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with barley bread and rancid fat (ihalah sinakhah), meaning rancid fat (wadak zanikhan). [Ahmad related it in his Musnad (3/211) from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read to al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Mazyad: Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb informed us: al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir informed me, from Makhul, who said: Allah revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾ [al-An'am: 121], then the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, abrogated (naskh) it, and had mercy upon the Muslims, and said: ﴿Today the good things have been made lawful for you, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾. Thus He abrogated it by that, and made the food of the People of the Book lawful.

In what Makhul said, may Allah have mercy on him, there is room for scrutiny, because permitting the food of the People of the Book does not necessarily entail permitting what has not had the name of Allah mentioned over it, since they mention the name of Allah over their slaughtered animals and their offerings, and they are obliged to do so. For this reason He did not permit the slaughtered animals of others among the people of polytheism and those resembling them, because they do not mention the name of Allah over their slaughtered animals; rather, they do not even stop to consider the ritual slaughter (dhakah) regarding what they eat of meat, but eat carrion. This is unlike the two groups of the People of the Book and those who resemble them among the Samaritans and the Sabians, and those who hold to the religion of Abraham, Seth and other prophets, according to one of the two opinions of the scholars; and the Arab Christians such as the Banu Taghlib, Tanukh, Bahra', Judham, Lakhm, 'Amilah and those similar to them, whose slaughtered animals are not eaten according to the majority.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told us: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubaydah, who said: 'Ali said: Do not eat the slaughtered animals of the Banu Taghlib, for they only cling to Christianity through drinking wine.

Similar was said by more than one of the later and earlier scholars.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah related from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Hasan, that both of them did not see any harm in the slaughtered animal of the Christians of the Banu Taghlib.
