As for the Magians (Majus), although the jizyah (poll tax) is taken from them by extension and by attaching them to the People of the Book, their slaughtered animals are not eaten and their women are not married, contrary to Abu Thawr Ibrahim ibn Khalid al-Kalbi, one of the jurists of the followers of al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. When he said that and it became known of him, the jurists rejected it against him, until Imam Ahmad said of him: "Abu Thawr is like his name!" meaning in this issue. It seems he clung to the generality of a hadith related as a mursal (a hadith whose chain omits a Companion) from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Treat them as you treat the People of the Book (sunnu bihim sunnata ahl al-kitab)." [Malik related it in the Muwatta' (1/278), and through his chain al-Shafi'i in the Sunan (1183), and al-Bayhaqi in the Sunan al-Kubra (9/189), from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab mentioned the Magians and said: "I do not know how to deal with their affair." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf said: "I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Treat them as you treat the People of the Book.'" Muhammad ibn 'Ali did not hear from 'Umar, so it is munqati' (a hadith with a break in the chain).]

But it is not established with this wording. What is in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the jizyah from the Magians of Hajar. [Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 3156).] Even if the soundness of this hadith is granted, its generality is restricted by the implication (mafhum) of this verse: ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾. Its implication (mafhum al-mukhalafah, implication of contrast) indicates that the food of those other than them among the adherents of other religions (in one copy: "idols") is not lawful.

* *

His words: ﴿And your food is lawful for them﴾ mean: it is lawful for you to feed them from your slaughtered animals. This is not a report about the ruling as it applies to them, unless it is a report about what they were commanded to do, namely to eat of every food over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, whether it comes from people of their own religion or from others. The first meaning is more apparent: that is, you may feed them from your slaughtered animals just as they fed you from theirs. This is of the nature of reciprocity, reward and recompense, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) put his garment on 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul when he died and shrouded him in it. They said: this was because he had clothed al-'Abbas with his garment when he came to Madinah, so the Prophet (ﷺ) repaid him in kind. As for the hadith in which it says: "Do not keep company except with a believer, and let none but a pious person eat your food," [Abu Dawud related it in the Sunan (no. 4832), and Ibn Majah in the Sunan (no. 2395), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.] it is to be understood as recommendation and preference (nadb wa istihbab). And Allah knows best.

* *

His words: ﴿And the chaste women from among the believing women﴾ mean: and it is lawful for you to marry free, chaste women from among the believing women. The mention of this is a preface to what follows, which is His words: ﴿And the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾. It was said: by "chaste women" He meant free women, not slave girls; this is related by Ibn Jarir from Mujahid. Mujahid said: "al-Muhsanat" means "al-hara'ir" (free women), so it is possible that he meant what is related from him, and it is possible that he meant by the free woman the chaste one, as Mujahid said in the other narration from him. This is the view of the majority here, and it is the more likely, lest there be combined in her that she is a dhimmiyyah (a protected non-Muslim) and at the same time not chaste, which would utterly ruin her condition and bring her husband what is said in the proverb: "Rotten dates and bad measure" (hashfan wa su' kaylah). [Al-hashf: the worst of dates. See Majma' al-Amthal of al-Maydani (1/207).] The apparent meaning of the verse is that by "chaste women" is meant those who are chaste with respect to fornication, as He said in another verse: ﴿chaste, not fornicators, nor those who take paramours﴾ [al-Nisa': 25].

Then the exegetes and scholars differed concerning His words: ﴿And the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾: does it include every chaste woman of the People of the Book, whether she is free or a slave girl? Ibn Jarir related this from a group of the earlier scholars who interpreted "muhsanah" as chaste. It was also said: what is meant by the People of the Book here is the women of the Children of Israel (al-israiliyyat), and this is the position of al-Shafi'i. It was also said: what is meant is the dhimmiyyat (protected women) and not the harbiyyat (women of the hostile, non-treaty lands), on the basis of His words: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, and who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and who do not adopt the religion of truth, from among those who were given the Scripture, until they pay the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29].

'Abdullah ibn 'Umar did not regard marriage with a Christian woman as permissible, and he used to say: "I know of no polytheism greater than that she should say: her lord is Jesus," and Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 221], and so on.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us: Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Sulayman al-Mu'addib told us: al-Qasim ibn Malik, that is al-Muzanni, told us: Isma'il ibn Sami' told us, from Abu Malik al-Ghifari, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾, the people held back from them, until the following one was revealed: ﴿And the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾, and then the people married women of the People of the Book.

A group of the Companions married Christian women and saw no harm in it, following this noble verse: ﴿And the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾. They made this verse a specifier (mukhassisah) of the verse of al-Baqarah: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 221], if it is held that the women of the Book are included in its generality; otherwise there is no contradiction between them, because the People of the Book are often mentioned separately from the polytheists in more than one place, as He said: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist until there came to them clear evidence﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 1], and as His words: ﴿And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered: "Have you submitted?" If they submit, then they are guided﴾ [Al 'Imran: 20]. And His words: ﴿when you have given them their wages﴾, meaning their dowries (mahur), that is: since they are chaste and virtuous, give them their dowries willingly.

Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Amir al-Sha'bi and al-Hasan al-Basri issued a legal opinion that if a man marries a woman and she commits fornication before he has consummated the marriage with her, then the marriage is to be annulled between him and her, and she is to return to him what he gave her of the dowry. Ibn Jarir related it from them.

* *

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verse 5 (part 2 of 2):

His saying: ﴿chaste, not fornicators, nor taking secret lovers﴾. Just as He stipulated ihsan (chastity, here meaning abstention from unlawful sexual intercourse) for women, He likewise stipulated it for men, namely that the man too be muhsan, chaste and abstaining. For this reason He said: ﴿not fornicators﴾, meaning the adulterers who do not refrain from sin and do not restrain themselves from whoever approaches them. ﴿Nor taking secret lovers﴾, meaning those who have mistresses (ʿashiqat) with whom they engage in illicit relations alone, as has already been mentioned in Surat an-Nisa' in the same manner.

For this reason, Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, held that the marriage of a prostitute (al-baghi) is not valid until she repents, and as long as she remains in that state it is not valid to marry her to a chaste man. Likewise, according to him, the contract of a dissolute man over a chaste woman is not valid until he repents and gives up the adultery in which he is engaged, based on this verse and on the other hadith: "The adulterer who has been flogged shall not marry except one like himself." [Abu Dawud reported it in his Sunan, no. 2052, through ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from Saʿid al-Maqbari, from Abu Hurayrah.]

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab [may Allah be pleased with him] said: "I had resolved not to leave anyone who had committed a grave sin in Islam without forbidding him to marry a chaste woman." Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, shirk is greater than that, and it is accepted from him if he repents." [Tafsir al-Tabari (9/584).]

The discussion of this matter will be treated at length, Allah willing, at His saying: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist, and that has been forbidden to the believers﴾ [an-Nur: 3]. For this reason, He, exalted is He, says here: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deed has become worthless, and he is in the Hereafter among the losers.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verse 6 (part 1 of 5):

Many of the early scholars (salaf) said: His saying, ﴿When you rise to prayer﴾, means "while you are in a state of minor impurity (muhdithun)."

Others said: "When you rise from sleep to prayer." Both views are close to one another.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is more general than that. The verse commands wudu' (ablution) when one stands up for prayer. For one who is in a state of impurity (hadath), it is obligatory; for one who is already in a state of purity (tahara), it is recommended and preferred (mustahabb). It has also been said that the command to perform wudu' for every prayer was obligatory at the beginning of Islam, and then it was abrogated (naskh).

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Alqamah ibn Martad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah [in A: "Yazid"], from his father, who said: The Prophet ﷺ used to perform wudu' for every prayer. But when the Day of the Conquest (Yawm al-Fath) came, he performed wudu' and wiped over his leather socks (khuffayn), and he prayed the prayers with one wudu'. Umar said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, you did something you were not accustomed to doing?" He said: "I did it deliberately, O Umar."

This was also narrated by Muslim and the authors of the Sunan from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Alqamah ibn Martad [Al-Musnad (5/358), Sahih Muslim no. (277), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (172), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (61), Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/86), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (510).] But in Sunan Ibn Majah it occurs from Sufyan, from Muharib ibn Dithar (in place of Alqamah ibn Martad), both from Sulayman ibn Buraydah [in A: "Yazid"], with the same wording. al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Musa narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Tufayl al-Bakka'i informed us, al-Fadl ibn al-Mubashshir narrated to us, who said: I saw Jabir ibn Abd Allah praying the prayers with one wudu'. When he urinated or broke wudu', he performed wudu' and wiped over his khuffayn with the remainder of his water for purification. I said: "Abu Abd Allah, is this something you do by your own opinion?" He said: "Rather, I saw the Prophet ﷺ doing it, so I do it, just as I saw the Messenger of Allah [ﷺ] doing it." [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/11), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (511). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/202): "This chain is weak; al-Fadl ibn al-Mubashshir was declared weak by the majority, but it is in al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik."]

Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban al-Ansari narrated to me, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar, who said: I asked him: "What do you think of the wudu' of Abd Allah ibn Umar for every prayer, whether he was in a state of purity or not? From whom is it (derived)?" He said: Asma' bint Zayd ibn al-Khattab narrated to her that Abd Allah ibn Handhalah ibn Abi Amir ibn al-Ghasil narrated to her that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been commanded to perform wudu' for every prayer, whether in a state of purity or not. When that became difficult for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he was commanded to use the miswak at every prayer, and wudu' was lifted from him except for (after) a breach of wudu' (hadath). Abd Allah used to see that he had the strength for it, and he continued doing it until he died. [Al-Musnad (5/225).]

Abu Dawud also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Awf al-Himsi, from Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Dhahabi, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (48)]. Then Abu Dawud said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ishaq and said: "Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar," meaning as was previously mentioned in the narration of Imam Ahmad.

In any case, it is a sahih chain. Ibn Ishaq explicitly stated the transmission and hearing from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, so the concern of tadlis is removed. However, al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir said: Salamah ibn al-Fadl and Ali ibn Mujahid narrated it from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Talhah ibn Yazid ibn Rukanah, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, with the same wording; and Allah knows best. In the action of Ibn Umar and his constant practice of performing thorough wudu' for every prayer, there is evidence for the recommendation of this, as is the position of the majority (jumhur).

Ibn Jarir said: Zakariya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, Azhar narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, from Ibn Sirin, that the caliphs used to perform wudu' for every prayer.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard Mas'ud ibn Ali al-Shaybani, I heard Ikrimah say: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, used to perform wudu' for every prayer and would recite this verse: ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer﴾, to the end of the verse.

Ibn al-Muthanna also narrated to us, Wahb ibn Jarir told me, Shu'bah informed us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah, who said: I saw Ali pray the Zuhr prayer, then he sat for the people in al-Rahbah. Then water was brought to him, and he washed his face and hands, then wiped his head and feet, and said: "This is the wudu' of one who has not broken wudu'."

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim also narrated to me, Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: that Ali [in H: "adara"; the text here follows R and A] was given a drink of love (hubb), so he performed wudu' in a manner that was lenient (tajawwuz), and said: "This is the wudu' of one who has not broken wudu'." These are good chains from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, which strengthen one another.

Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab performed wudu' in a light, lenient manner, and said: "This is the wudu' of one who has not broken wudu'." This is a sahih chain [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/13)]. Muhammad ibn Sirin also said: The caliphs used to perform wudu' for every prayer.

As for what Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated, from Abu Hilal, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: "Wudu' without a breach is transgression (i'tida')" — this is gharib from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. Furthermore, it is to be understood as referring to one who believes it to be obligatory, for he is a transgressor; as for its legislation as a recommendation, the Sunnah has indicated it.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Amir al-Ansari, I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet ﷺ used to perform wudu' for every prayer. I said: "Then how did you used to act?" He said: "We would pray the prayers with one wudu' so long as we did not break wudu'."

This was narrated by al-Bukhari and the authors of the Sunan through more than one route from Amr ibn Amir, with the same wording [Al-Musnad (3/132), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (214), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (171), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (60), Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/85), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (509).]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Sa'id al-Baghdadi narrated to me, Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Huraym, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad (he is al-Ifriqi), from Abu Ghutayf, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever performs wudu' upon purity, ten good deeds are recorded for him."

He also narrated it from the hadith of Isa ibn Yunus, from al-Ifriqi, from Abu Ghutayf, from Ibn Umar, and mentioned it, and in it there is a story [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/21, 22)].

Likewise, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of al-Ifriqi, with similar wording [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (62), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (59), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (512)]. al-Tirmidhi said: This is a weak chain.

Ibn Jarir said: Some people said that this verse was revealed as an announcement from Allah that wudu' is only obligatory when rising to prayer, and not for other acts; this is because the Prophet ﷺ, whenever he broke wudu', would refrain from all acts until he performed wudu'.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Sufyan [in A: "Shaybān"], from Jabir, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm, from Abd Allah ibn Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa', from his father, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ urinated, we would speak to him and he would not answer us, and we would greet him and he would not return our greeting, until the verse of dispensation was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer﴾, to the end of the verse.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Kurayb, with a similar wording [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/23). al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (18/6) through Abu Kurayb. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/276): "It contains Jabir al-Ju'fi, who is weak."] This is an extremely gharib hadith, and this Jabir is Ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, whom they declared weak.

Abu Dawud said: Musaddad narrated to us, Isma'il narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Abd Allah ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out from the place of relief (al-khala'), and food was brought to him. They said: "Shall we not bring you water for wudu'?" He said: "I was only commanded to perform wudu' when I rise to prayer."

Likewise, al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ahmad ibn Mani', and al-Nasa'i from Ziyad ibn Ayyub, from Isma'il (Ibn Ulayyah), with the same wording [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3760), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1847), Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/85)]. al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith.

Muslim narrated from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn al-Huwayrith, from Ibn Abbas, who said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ when he went to the place of relief, then he returned and food was brought to him. It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you not perform wudu'?" He said: "Why? Am I to pray that I should perform wudu'?" [Sahih Muslim no. (374).]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿wash your faces﴾, some scholars have used His saying, ﴿When you rise to prayer, wash your faces﴾, as evidence for the obligation of intention (niyyah) in wudu'. This is because the sense of the statement is: "When you rise to prayer, wash your faces for it," just as the Arabs say: "When you see the amir, stand up," meaning: for him. It is firmly established in the two Sahihs the hadith: "Actions are only by intentions, and every person has only what he intended." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1), Sahih Muslim no. (1907).] It is also recommended, before washing the face, to mention the name of Allah over one's wudu', because of what has come in the hadith through good routes, from a group of the Companions, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "There is no wudu' for one who does not mention the name of Allah over it." [It was narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Abu Dawud in the Sunan no. (101); from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: Ibn Majah in the Sunan no. (397); from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd: Ibn Majah in the Sunan no. (400).]

It is also recommended to wash one's two palms before putting them into the vessel, and this is emphasized upon rising from sleep, because of what is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you wakes up from his sleep, let him not put his hand into the vessel until he has washed it three times, for none of you knows where his hand spent the night." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (162), Sahih Muslim no. (278).]

The definition of the face (wajh) according to the jurists is: the area between the roots of the hair of the head (and no account is taken of baldness or of hair that has receded) down to the end of the two jaws and the chin in length, and from ear to ear in width. Scholars differ about the two receding hairline areas (al-nazatayn) and the hair at the temples (al-tahdhif), whether they belong to the head or to the face. Regarding the hair of the beard that hangs beyond the area of obligatory washing (al-mustarsil), there are two opinions. The first is that water must be poured over it, because facing another person is accomplished through it.

It is narrated in a hadith that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw a man covering his beard, and said: "Uncover it, for the beard is part of the face."¹ Mujahid said: "It is part of the face. Do you not hear the saying of the Arabs about a boy when his beard has grown: 'His face has come forth (ṭala'a wajhuhu)'?"

It is recommended for the one performing ablution (wudu') to run water through his beard (takhlil al-liḥyah, i.e., passing wet fingers through the beard) if it is thick. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Amir ibn Shaqiq ibn Jamra, from Abu Wa'il, who said: "I saw Uthman perform ablution..." [and he mentioned the hadith], and he said: "He ran water through his beard three times when he washed his face, then he said: 'I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) do what you have seen me do.'"

It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq.² Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (sound and authentic), and al-Bukhari graded it as sound.

Abu Dawud said: Abu Tawba al-Rabi' ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Abu al-Malih narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Zawran³ narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he performed ablution, would take a handful of water and put it under his chin, running it through his beard, and he said: "My Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded me to do this."

Abu Dawud alone narrated it,⁴ and this has been narrated from more than one route from Anas. Al-Bayhaqi said: "We have also narrated concerning running water through the beard from Ammar, Aisha and Umm Salamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ); then from Ali and others. And we have narrated a concession for leaving it out from Ibn Umar, al-Hasan ibn Ali, then from al-Nakha'i and a group of the Successors (tabi'un)."⁵

It has been firmly established from the Prophet (ﷺ), through more than one route in the Sahih collections and others, that when he performed ablution he rinsed his mouth and snuffed water into his nose (madmada wa-istanshaqa). The scholars differed about this: are these two obligatory in ablution and in the full ritual washing (ghusl), as is the position of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him? Or are they recommended in both, as is the position of al-Shafi'i and Malik? This is based on the hadith narrated by the compilers of the Sunan, and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah, from Rifa'ah ibn Rafi' al-Zuraqi, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the one who prayed badly: "Perform ablution as Allah has commanded you."⁶ Or are they obligatory in ghusl but not in wudu', as is the position of Abu Hanifah? Or is snuffing (istinshaq) obligatory without rinsing (madmada), as is a narration from Imam Ahmad, based on what is established in the two Sahihs: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs ablution, let him snuff water out (fal-yastanthir)." And in another narration: "When one of you performs ablution, let him put water into his nostrils and then blow it out (linthatherha)." Intithar means exaggerating in snuffing.⁷

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Salamah al-Khuza'i narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Ibn Abbas, that he performed ablution, washed his face, then took a handful of water, rinsed his mouth with it and snuffed it out. Then he took a handful and [put it over] his face with both hands together, and washed his face with them. Then he took a handful of water and washed his right hand with it, then took a handful and washed his left hand with it, then wiped his head, then took a handful of water and sprinkled it over his right foot until he had washed it, then took another handful and washed his left foot with it. Then he said: "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) perform ablution."

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim, from Abu Salamah Mansur ibn Salamah al-Khuza'i, with the same chain.⁸

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and your hands up to the elbows﴾, that is, "together with the elbows", as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And do not consume their wealth along with your own wealth. Indeed, it is a great sin.﴾ [An-Nisa': 2]

Al-Hafiz al-Daraqutni and Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi narrated, through the route of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from his grandfather, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed ablution he would turn the water around his elbows." But this al-Qasim is abandoned in narration (matruk al-hadith), and his grandfather is weak.⁹ And Allah knows best.

It is recommended for the one performing ablution to extend the washing to the upper arm (al-'adud) so as to wash it along with the forearms, based on what al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Nu'aym al-Mujmir, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My community will be called on the Day of Resurrection with bright faces and white limbs (ghurran muhajjalin) from the traces of ablution. So whoever among you is able to extend his brightness, let him do so."¹⁰

In Sahih Muslim: from Qutayba, from Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Abu Malik al-Ashja'i, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "I heard my beloved friend (khalili) (ﷺ) say: 'The adornment (al-hilyah) of the believer will reach as far as the ablution reaches.'"¹¹

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and wipe over your heads﴾, the scholars differed regarding this "ba'" (the particle "bi"): is it for adhesion (al-ilsaq), which is the more apparent, or for partiality (al-tab'id)? This requires examination, and there are two opinions. Among the legal theorists (al-usuliyyun) are those who said: this is ambiguous (mujmal), so its explanation is to be sought in the Sunnah. It has been established in the two Sahihs, through the route of Malik, from Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father, that a man said to Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Asim, who was the grandfather of Amr ibn Yahya and was one of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Can you show me how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to perform ablution?" Abdullah ibn Zayd said: "Yes." He asked for water for ablution, poured it over his hands, washed his hands twice twice, then rinsed his mouth and snuffed water three times, washed his face three times, then washed his hands twice twice up to the elbows, then wiped with his hands, moving them forward and backward: he began with the front of his head, then took them to the back of his neck, then brought them back to the place where he had begun. Then he washed his feet.¹²

In the hadith of Abd Khayr, from Ali, regarding the description of the Prophet's (ﷺ) ablution, there is something similar. Abu Dawud also narrated from Mu'awiyah and al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib, describing the Prophet's (ﷺ) ablution, something similar.¹³

In these hadiths there is evidence for those who hold that it is obligatory to complete the wiping of the entire head, as is the position of Imam Malik and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, especially according to the view of those who claim that these hadiths came as an explanation of what was general (mujmal) in the Qur'an.

The Hanafis went to the position that wiping a quarter of the head is obligatory, which is the amount of the forelock (al-nasiyah).

Our companions (the Shafi'is) went to the position that what is obligatory is only what is called "wiping" (mash), without any fixed limit. Rather, if one wipes some of the hair of his head, it suffices.

Both parties argued from the hadith of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) fell behind, and I fell behind with him. When he had finished his need, he said: 'Do you have any water?' So I brought him a water vessel (mitharah), and he washed his palms and face. Then he went to roll up his sleeves from his forearms, but the sleeve of the cloak was tight, so he took his hands out from under the cloak and threw the cloak over his shoulders, and washed his forearms and wiped over his forelock, and over the turban and over his two socks..." and he mentioned the rest of the hadith, which is in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere.¹⁴

The companions of Imam Ahmad said to them: "He only limited himself to wiping the forelock because he completed the wiping of the rest of the head over the turban. We also say this, and it occurs in place of the wiping (yaqa'u 'an al-mawqi'), as many hadiths have been narrated concerning it, and because he used to wipe over the turban and over the two socks, so this is more appropriate. There is no evidence for you here for permitting limiting oneself to wiping the forelock or part of the head without completing it over the turban. And Allah knows best."

Then they differed as to whether it is recommended to repeat the wiping of the head three times, as is the well-known position of al-Shafi'i, or whether only one wiping is recommended, as is the position of Ahmad ibn Hanbal and those who follow him. Abd al-Razzaq said: from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Ata' ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Humran ibn Aban, who said: "I saw Uthman ibn Affan perform ablution: he poured water over his hands three times and washed them, then rinsed his mouth and snuffed water, then washed his face three times, then washed his right hand up to the elbow three times, then washed the left likewise, then wiped his head, then washed his right foot three times, then the left three times likewise." Then he said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) perform ablution like this ablution of mine, then he said: 'Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak'ahs without speaking to himself during them, will have his previous sins forgiven.'"

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in the two Sahihs through the route of al-Zuhri with something similar.¹⁵ And in the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from the narration of Abdullah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Uthman, in the description of the ablution: "and he wiped his head once." And similarly from the narration of Abd Khayr, from Ali, something similar.¹⁶

Those who recommended repeating the wiping of the head argued from the general wording of the hadith narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, from Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) "performed ablution three times three times."

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Wardan narrated to us, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, Humran narrated to me, who said: "I saw Uthman ibn Affan perform ablution," and he mentioned something similar, but did not mention rinsing the mouth and snuffing water. In it he said: "Then he wiped his head three times, then washed his feet three times, then said: 'I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) perform ablution like this,' and he said: 'Whoever performs ablution less than this, it suffices him.'"

تَفَرَّدَ بِهِ أَبُو دَاوُدَ [[Sunan Abi Dawud, hadith no. (107).]] ثُمَّ قَالَ: وَأَحَادِيثُ عُثْمَانَ الصِّحَاحُ تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّهُ مَسَحَ الرَّأْسَ مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ﴾ [And your feet up to the ankles]. قُرِئَ: ﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾ بِالنَّصْبِ عَطْفًا عَلَى ﴿فَاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ﴾ [with the accusative (naṣb) case, as a conjunction with "wash your faces and your hands"].

وَقَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو زُرْعَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو سَلَمَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا وُهَيْبٌ، عَنْ خَالِدٍ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ؛ أَنَّهُ قَرَأَهَا: ﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾ يَقُولُ: رَجَعَتْ إِلَى الْغَسْلِ.

وَرُوِيَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، وَعُرْوَةَ، وَعَطَاءٍ، وَعِكْرِمَةَ، وَالْحَسَنِ، وَمُجَاهِدٍ، وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَالضَّحَّاكِ، وَالسُّدِّيِّ، وَمُقَاتِلِ بْنِ حَيَّانَ، وَالزُّهْرِيِّ، وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ التَّيْمِيِّ، نَحْوُ ذَلِكَ.

وَهَذِهِ قِرَاءَةٌ ظَاهِرَةٌ فِي وُجُوبِ الْغَسْلِ، كَمَا قَالَهُ السَّلَفُ، وَمِنْ هَاهُنَا ذَهَبَ مَنْ ذَهَبَ إِلَى وُجُوبِ التَّرْتِيبِ [[في أ: "الترتيب في الوضوء".]] (tartib: the required sequence of the washing acts) كَمَا هُوَ مَذْهَبُ الْجُمْهُورِ، خِلَافًا لِأَبِي حَنِيفَةَ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَشْتَرِطِ التَّرْتِيبَ، بَلْ لَوْ غَسَلَ قَدَمَيْهِ ثُمَّ مَسَحَ رَأْسَهُ وَغَسَلَ يَدَيْهِ ثُمَّ وَجْهَهُ أَجْزَأَهُ ذَلِكَ؛ لِأَنَّ الْآيَةَ أَمَرَتْ بِغَسْلِ هَذِهِ الْأَعْضَاءِ، وَ"الْوَاوُ" لَا تَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّرْتِيبِ. وَقَدْ سَلَكَ الْجُمْهُورُ فِي الْجَوَابِ عَنْ هَذَا الْبَحْثِ طُرُقًا، فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَالَ: الْآيَةُ دَلَّتْ عَلَى وُجُوبِ غَسْلِ الْوَجْهِ ابْتِدَاءً عِنْدَ الْقِيَامِ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ؛ لِأَنَّهُ مَأْمُورٌ بِهِ بِفَاءِ التَّعْقِيبِ، وَهِيَ مُقْتَضِيَةٌ لِلتَّرْتِيبِ، وَلَمْ يَقُلْ أَحَدٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ بِوُجُوبِ غَسْلِ الْوَجْهِ أَوَّلًا ثُمَّ لَا يَجِبُ التَّرْتِيبُ بَعْدَهُ، بَلِ الْقَائِلُ اثْنَانِ، أَحَدُهُمَا: يُوجِبُ التَّرْتِيبَ، كَمَا هُوَ وَاقِعٌ فِي الْآيَةِ. وَالْآخَرُ يَقُولُ: لَا يَجِبُ التَّرْتِيبُ مُطْلَقًا، وَالْآيَةُ دَلَّتْ عَلَى وُجُوبِ غَسْلِ الْوَجْهِ ابْتِدَاءً، فَوَجَبَ [[في أ: "فيجب".]] التَّرْتِيبُ فِيمَا بَعْدَهُ بِالْإِجْمَاعِ، حَيْثُ لَا فَارِقَ. وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَالَ: لَا نُسَلِّمُ أَنَّ "الْوَاوَ" لَا تَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّرْتِيبِ، بَلْ هِيَ دَالَّةٌ -كَمَا هُوَ مَذْهَبُ طَائِفَةٍ مِنَ النُّحَاةِ (grammarians) وَأَهْلِ اللُّغَةِ وَبَعْضِ الْفُقَهَاءِ. ثُمَّ نَقُولُ [[في أ: "يقول".]] -بِتَقْدِيرِ تَسْلِيمِ كَوْنِهَا لَا تَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّرْتِيبِ اللُّغَوِيِّ-: هِيَ دَالَّةٌ عَلَى التَّرْتِيبِ شَرْعًا فِيمَا مِنْ شَأْنِهِ أَنْ يُرَتَّبَ، وَالدَّلِيلُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ [[في أ: "أن رسول الله".]] (ﷺ) لَمَّا طَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ، خَرَجَ مِنْ بَابِ الصَّفَا وَهُوَ يَتْلُو قَوْلَهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 158] ثُمَّ قَالَ: "أَبْدَأُ بِمَا بَدَأَ اللَّهُ بِهِ" لَفْظُ مُسْلِمٍ، وَلَفْظُ النَّسَائِيِّ: "ابْدَءُوا بِمَا بَدَأَ اللَّهُ بِهِ". وَهَذَا لَفْظُ أَمْرٍ، وَإِسْنَادُهُ صَحِيحٌ، فَدَلَّ عَلَى وُجُوبِ الْبُدَاءَةِ بِمَا بَدَأَ اللَّهُ بِهِ، وَهُوَ مَعْنَى كَوْنِهَا تَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّرْتِيبِ شَرْعًا، وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.

وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَالَ: لَمَّا ذَكَرَ تَعَالَى هَذِهِ الصِّفَةَ فِي هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ عَلَى هَذَا التَّرْتِيبِ، فَقَطَعَ النَّظِيرَ عَنِ النَّظِيرِ، وَأَدْخَلَ الْمَمْسُوحَ بَيْنَ الْمَغْسُولَيْنِ، دَلَّ ذَلِكَ عَلَى إِرَادَةِ التَّرْتِيبِ.

وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَالَ: لَا شَكَّ أَنَّهُ قَدْ رَوَى أَبُو دَاوُدَ وَغَيْرُهُ مِنْ طَرِيقِ عَمْرِو بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ؛ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) تَوَضَّأَ مَرَّةً مَرَّةً، ثُمَّ قَالَ: "هَذَا وُضُوءٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ اللَّهُ الصَّلَاةَ إِلَّا بِهِ" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, hadith no. (135), from the hadith of Amr ibn Shu'ayb from his father from his grandfather, but its wording differs from this wording. This wording was narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, hadith no. (419), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] قَالُوا: فَلَا يَخْلُو إِمَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ تَوَضَّأَ مُرَتِّبًا فَيَجِبُ التَّرْتِيبُ، أَوْ يَكُونَ تَوَضَّأَ غَيْرَ مُرَتِّبٍ فَيَجِبُ عَدَمُ التَّرْتِيبِ، وَلَا قَائِلَ بِهِ، فَوَجَبَ مَا ذَكَرَهُ. [[في أ: "ما ذكرناه".]]

وَأَمَّا الْقِرَاءَةُ الْأُخْرَى، وَهِيَ قِرَاءَةُ مَنْ قَرَأَ: ﴿وَأَرْجُلِكُمْ﴾ بِالْخَفْضِ (khafd: the genitive/kasra case). فَقَدِ احْتَجَّ بِهَا الشِّيعَةُ فِي قَوْلِهِمْ بِوُجُوبِ مَسْحِ الرِّجْلَيْنِ؛ لِأَنَّهَا عِنْدَهُمْ مَعْطُوفَةٌ عَلَى مَسْحِ الرَّأْسِ. وَقَدْ رُوِيَ عَنْ طَائِفَةٍ مِنَ السَّلَفِ مَا يُوهِمُ الْقَوْلَ بِالْمَسْحِ، فَقَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ:

حَدَّثَنِي يَعْقُوبُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ عُلَيَّةَ، حَدَّثَنَا حُمَيْدٌ قَالَ: قَالَ مُوسَى بْنُ أَنَسٍ لِأَنَسٍ وَنَحْنُ عِنْدَهُ: يَا أَبَا حَمْزَةَ، إِنَّ الْحَجَّاجَ خَطَبَنَا بِالْأَهْوَازِ وَنَحْنُ مَعَهُ، فَذَكَرَ الطَّهُورَ فَقَالَ: اغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ، وَامْسَحُوا بِرُءُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ، وَأَنَّهُ لَيْسَ شَيْءٌ مِنِ ابْنِ آدَمَ أَقْرَبَ مِنْ خَبَثِهِ مِنْ قَدَمَيْهِ، فَاغْسِلُوا بُطُونَهُمَا وَظُهُورَهُمَا وَعَرَاقِيبَهُمَا. فَقَالَ أَنَسٌ: صَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَكَذَبَ الْحَجَّاجُ، قَالَ اللَّهُ [تَعَالَى] ﴿وَامْسَحُوا بِرُءُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾. قَالَ: وَكَانَ أَنَسٌ إِذَا مَسَحَ قَدَمَيْهِ بَلَّهُمَا. إِسْنَادٌ صَحِيحٌ إِلَيْهِ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ سَهْلٍ، حَدَّثَنَا مُؤَمَّلٌ، حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادٌ، حَدَّثَنَا عَاصِمٌ الْأَحْوَلُ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ [[في ر: "عن الحسن".]] قَالَ: نَزَلَ الْقُرْآنُ بِالْمَسْحِ، وَالسُّنَّةُ الْغَسْلُ. وَهَذَا أَيْضًا إِسْنَادٌ صَحِيحٌ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو كُرَيْبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ الْخُرَاسَانِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ: الْوُضُوءُ غَسْلَتَانِ وَمَسْحَتَانِ. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (10/58), and narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, no. (55), through Ibn Jurayj.]]

وَكَذَا رَوَى سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَرُوبَةَ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ: حَدَّثَنِي أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مَعْمَرٍ الْمِنْقَرِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَهَّابِ، حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ يُوسُفَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: ﴿وَامْسَحُوا بِرُءُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ﴾ قَالَ: هُوَ الْمَسْحُ. ثُمَّ قَالَ: وَرُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ وَعَلْقَمَةَ، وَأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، وَالْحَسَنِ -فِي إِحْدَى الرِّوَايَاتِ- وَجَابِرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، وَمُجَاهِدٍ -فِي إِحْدَى الرِّوَايَاتِ- نَحْوُهُ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: حَدَّثَنَا يَعْقُوبُ، حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ عُلَيَّةَ، حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ، قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ عِكْرِمَةَ يَمْسَحُ عَلَى رِجْلَيْهِ، قَالَ: وَكَانَ يَقُولُهُ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو السَّائِبِ، حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ إِدْرِيسَ، عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ أَبِي هِنْدٍ، عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ قَالَ: نَزَلَ جِبْرِيلُ بِالْمَسْحِ. ثُمَّ قَالَ الشَّعْبِيُّ: أَلَا تَرَى أَنَّ "التَّيَمُّمَ" أَنْ يَمْسَحَ مَا كَانَ غَسْلًا وَيَكْفِيَ [[في أ: "ويلغي".]] مَا كَانَ مَسْحًا؟

وَحَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ أَبِي زِيَادٍ، حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ، أَخْبَرَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ، قُلْتُ لِعَامِرٍ: إِنَّ نَاسًا يَقُولُونَ: إِنَّ جِبْرِيلَ نَزَلَ بِغَسْلِ الرِّجْلَيْنِ؟ فَقَالَ: نَزَلَ جِبْرِيلُ بِالْمَسْحِ.

فَهَذِهِ آثَارٌ غَرِيبَةٌ جِدًّا، وَهِيَ مَحْمُولَةٌ عَلَى أَنَّ الْمُرَادَ بِالْمَسْحِ هُوَ الْغَسْلُ الْخَفِيفُ، لِمَا سَنَذْكُرُهُ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ الثَّابِتَةِ [[في أ: "الثانية".]] فِي وُجُوبِ غَسْلِ الرِّجْلَيْنِ. وَإِنَّمَا جَاءَتْ هَذِهِ الْقِرَاءَةُ بِالْخَفْضِ إِمَّا عَلَى الْمُجَاوَرَةِ وَتَنَاسُبِ الْكَلَامِ، كَمَا فِي قَوْلِ الْعَرَبِ: "جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ"، وَكَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُنْدُسٍ خُضْرٌ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٌ﴾ [Al-Insan: 21]. وَهَذَا سَائِغٌ ذَائِعٌ، فِي لُغَةِ الْعَرَبِ شَائِعٌ. وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَالَ: هِيَ مَحْمُولَةٌ عَلَى مَسْحِ الْقَدَمَيْنِ إِذَا كَانَ عَلَيْهِمَا الْخُفَّانِ، قَالَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الشَّافِعِيُّ، رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ. وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَالَ: هِيَ دَالَّةٌ عَلَى مَسْحِ الرِّجْلَيْنِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْمُرَادَ بِذَلِكَ الْغَسْلُ الْخَفِيفُ، كَمَا وَرَدَتْ بِهِ السُّنَّةُ. وَعَلَى كُلِّ تَقْدِيرٍ فَالْوَاجِبُ غَسْلُ الرِّجْلَيْنِ فَرْضًا، لَا بُدَّ مِنْهُ لِلْآيَةِ وَالْأَحَادِيثِ الَّتِي سَنُورِدُهَا.

وَمِنْ أَحْسَنِ مَا يُسْتَدَلُّ بِهِ عَلَى أَنَّ الْمَسْحَ يُطْلَقُ عَلَى الْغَسْلِ الْخَفِيفِ مَا رَوَاهُ الْحَافِظُ الْبَيْهَقِيُّ، حَيْثُ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو عَلِيٍّ الرُّوذَبَارِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرٍ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مَحْمَوَيْهِ الْعَسْكَرِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الْقَلَانِسِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا آدَمُ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْمَلِكِ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ، سَمِعْتُ النَّزَّالَ بْنَ سَبْرَةَ يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، أَنَّهُ صَلَّى الظُّهْرَ، ثُمَّ قَعَدَ فِي حَوَائِجِ النَّاسِ فِي رَحَبَةِ الْكُوفَةِ حَتَّى حَضَرَتْ صَلَاةُ الْعَصْرِ، ثُمَّ أُتِيَ بِكُوزٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ، فَأَخَذَ مِنْهُ حَفْنَةً وَاحِدَةً، فَمَسَحَ بِهَا وَجْهَهُ وَيَدَيْهِ وَرَأْسَهُ وَرِجْلَيْهِ، ثُمَّ قَامَ فَشَرِبَ [[في ر: "فشرب منه".]] فَضْلَهُ وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: إِنَّ نَاسًا يَكْرَهُونَ الشُّرْبَ قَائِمًا، وَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) صَنَعَ مَا صَنَعْتُ. وَقَالَ: "هَذَا وُضُوءُ مَنْ لَمْ يُحْدِثْ".

رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ فِي الصَّحِيحِ، عَنْ آدَمَ، بِبَعْضِ مَعْنَاهُ. [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra (1/75) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5616).]]

وَمَنْ أَوْجَبَ مِنَ الشِّيعَةِ مَسْحَهُمَا كَمَا يَمْسَحُ الْخُفَّ، فَقَدْ ضَلَّ وَأَضَلَّ. وَكَذَا مَنْ جَوَّزَ مَسْحَهُمَا وَجَوَّزَ غَسْلَهُمَا فَقَدْ أَخْطَأَ أَيْضًا، وَمَنْ نَقَلَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ بْنِ جَرِيرٍ أَنَّهُ أَوْجَبَ غَسْلَهُمَا لِلْأَحَادِيثِ، وَأَوْجَبَ مَسْحَهُمَا لِلْآيَةِ، فَلَمْ يُحَقِّقْ مَذْهَبَهُ فِي ذَلِكَ، فَإِنَّ كَلَامَهُ فِي تَفْسِيرِهِ إِنَّمَا يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّهُ أَرَادَ أَنَّهُ يَجِبُ دَلْكُ الرِّجْلَيْنِ مِنْ دُونِ سَائِرِ أَعْضَاءِ الْوُضُوءِ؛ لِأَنَّهُمَا يَلِيَانِ الْأَرْضَ وَالطِّينَ وَغَيْرَ ذَلِكَ، فَأَوْجَبَ [[في أ: "فالواجب".]] دَلْكَهُمَا لِيَذْهَبَ مَا عَلَيْهِمَا، وَلَكِنَّهُ عَبَّرَ عَنِ الدَّلْكِ بِالْمَسْحِ، فَاعْتَقَدَ مَنْ لَمْ يَتَأَمَّلْ كَلَامَهُ أَنَّهُ أَرَادَ وُجُوبَ الْجَمْعِ بَيْنَ غَسْلِ الرِّجْلَيْنِ وَمَسْحِهِمَا، فَحَكَاهُ مَنْ حَكَاهُ كَذَلِكَ؛ وَلِهَذَا يَسْتَشْكِلُهُ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ الْفُقَهَاءِ وَهُوَ مَعْذُورٌ، فَإِنَّهُ لَا مَعْنَى لِلْجَمْعِ بَيْنَ الْمَسْحِ وَالْغَسْلِ، سَوَاءٌ تَقَدَّمَهُ أَوْ تَأَخَّرَ عَلَيْهِ؛ لِانْدِرَاجِهِ فِيهِ، وَإِنَّمَا أَرَادَ الرَّجُلُ مَا ذَكَرْتُهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ. ثُمَّ تَأَمَّلْتُ كَلَامَهُ أَيْضًا فَإِذَا هُوَ يُحَاوِلُ الْجَمْعَ بَيْنَ الْقِرَاءَتَيْنِ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾ خَفْضًا عَلَى الْمَسْحِ وَهُوَ الدَّلْكُ، وَنَصْبًا عَلَى الْغَسْلِ، فَأَوْجَبَهُمَا أَخْذًا بِالْجَمْعِ بَيْنَ هَذِهِ وَهَذِهِ.

ذِكْرُ الْأَحَادِيثِ الْوَارِدَةِ فِي غَسْلِ الرِّجْلَيْنِ وَأَنَّهُ لَا بُدَّ مِنْهُ:

قَدْ تَقَدَّمَ فِي حَدِيثِ أَمِيرَيِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عُثْمَانَ وَعَلِيٍّ، وَابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَمُعَاوِيَةَ، وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ زَيْدِ بْنِ عَاصِمٍ، وَالْمِقْدَادِ بْنِ مَعْدِ يَكْرِبَ؛ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) غَسَلَ الرِّجْلَيْنِ [[في ر: "الوجه".]] فِي وُضُوئِهِ، إِمَّا مَرَّةً، وَإِمَّا مَرَّتَيْنِ، أَوْ ثَلَاثًا، عَلَى اخْتِلَافِ رِوَايَاتِهِمْ.

وَفِي حَدِيثِ عَمْرِو بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) تَوَضَّأَ فَغَسَلَ قَدَمَيْهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: "هَذَا وُضُوءٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ اللَّهُ الصَّلَاةَ إِلَّا بِهِ".

وَفِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ (the two Sahihs: al-Bukhari and Muslim)، مِنْ رِوَايَةِ أَبِي عَوَانَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي بِشْرٍ، عَنْ يُوسُفَ بْنِ مَاهَكَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قَالَ: تَخَلَّفَ عَنَّا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) فِي سَفْرَةٍ سَافَرْنَاهَا، فَأَدْرَكَنَا وَقَدْ أَرْهَقَتْنَا الصَّلَاةُ، صَلَاةُ الْعَصْرِ وَنَحْنُ نَتَوَضَّأُ، فَجَعَلْنَا نَمْسَحُ عَلَى أَرْجُلِنَا، فَنَادَى بِأَعْلَى صَوْتِهِ: "أَسْبِغُوا الْوُضُوءَ، وَيْلٌ لِلْأَعْقَابِ مِنَ النَّارِ". [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (60), and Sahih Muslim, no. (241).]]

وَكَذَلِكَ هُوَ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (165), and Sahih Muslim, no. (242).]] وَفِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) أَنَّهُ قَالَ: "أَسْبِغُوا الْوُضُوءَ، وَيْلٌ لِلْأَعْقَابِ مِنَ النَّارِ". [[Sahih Muslim, no. (240).]]

And Layth ibn Sa'd narrated from Haywah ibn Shurayh, from 'Uqbah ibn Muslim, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Juz' [in manuscript A: "Surad"], that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Woe to the heels and the soles of the feet from the Fire." Al-Bayhaqi and al-Hakim related it [[As-Sunan al-Kubra (1/70) and al-Mustadrak (1/162). Ibn Khuzaymah also related it in his Sahih, no. 163, through Layth with this chain.]] and this chain (isnad, the chain of narrators) is sahih (sound).

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq: that he heard Sa'id ibn Abi Karb, or Shu'ayb ibn Abi Karb [in manuscript A: "Ibn Abi Kurayb"], say: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, while he was on a camel, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Woe to the heels from the Fire." [[Al-Musnad (3/369).]]

Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, Isra'il informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Abi Karb [in manuscript A: "Kurayb"], from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ saw on the foot of one of our men a spot the size of a dirham that he had not washed, so he said: "Woe to the heel from the Fire."

It was also related by Ibn Majah, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from al-Ahwas [in manuscripts R and A: "from Abu al-Ahwas"], from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id, with the same meaning. [[Al-Musnad (3/390); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 454. Al-Busiri said in az-Zawa'id (1/182): "This is a chain whose narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."]] Likewise Ibn Jarir related it from the hadith of Sufyan ath-Thawri, Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj and others, from Abu Ishaq as-Sabi'i, from Sa'id ibn Abi Karb [in manuscript A: "Kurayb"], from Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ, the same as this. Then he said:

Ali [in manuscript R: "Affan"] ibn Muslim narrated to us, 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, Hafs narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw some people performing wudu' (ablution) whose heels had not been reached by the water, so he said: "Woe to the heels from the Fire." [[Tafsir at-Tabari (10/71).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ayyub ibn 'Utbah narrated to us, from Yahya [in manuscript R: "Muhammad"; in manuscript A: "'Awn"] ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Mu'aygib, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Woe to the heels from the Fire." Ahmad alone related it. [[Al-Musnad (3/426). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/240): "It contains Ayyub ibn 'Utbah, and most scholars have weakened him."]]

Ibn Jarir said: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Mutarrih ibn Yazid, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Zahr, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Woe to the heels from the Fire, woe to the heels from the Fire." He said: "Then no one remained in the mosque, noble or lowly, except that I looked at him turning over his heels and looking at them." [[Tafsir at-Tabari (10/73). In its chain is Mutarrih ibn Yazid, who is weak.]]

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Layth, Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sabit narrated to me, from Abu Umamah, or from the brother of Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw people performing wudu' [in manuscript R: "praying"], and on the heel of one of them, or the foot of one of them, was a spot the size of a dirham, or the size of a fingernail, which the water had not touched, so he said: "Woe to the heels from the Fire." He said: "So a man, whenever he saw something on his heel that the water had not reached, would repeat his wudu'." [[Tafsir at-Tabari (10/74). Al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/347) through Layth ibn Abi Sulaym. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/240): "All its chains revolve around Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, and he became confused (ikhtalata)."]]

The point of evidence from these hadiths is clear. If the obligatory duty for the two feet were wiping, or if wiping them were permissible, he would not have threatened those who neglect it, because wiping does not cover the entire foot; rather, what applies to wiping over the khuff (leather sock) applies to it. This is also the line of argument taken by the Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him.

Muslim related in his Sahih, through the route of Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, that a man performed wudu' and left a spot the size of a fingernail on his foot [in manuscript A: "feet"], and the Prophet ﷺ saw it and said: "Go back and perfect your wudu'." [[Sahih Muslim no. 243.]]

Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi, the hafiz, said: Abu 'Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq as-Saghani [in manuscript A: "as-San'ani"] narrated to us, Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us: that he heard Qatadah ibn Di'amah say: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ having performed wudu', and had left on his foot a spot the size of a fingernail, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Go back and perfect your wudu'."

Abu Dawud related it in the same way from Harun ibn Ma'ruf, and Ibn Majah from Harmalah ibn Yahya, both of them from Ibn Wahb with it. [[As-Sunan al-Kubra (1/70); Sunan Abi Dawud no. 173; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 665.]] This chain is good (jayyid), all its narrators are trustworthy, but Abu Dawud said: "This hadith is not well known; no one related it except Ibn Wahb."

Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Yunus and Humayd informed us, from al-Hasan: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ... with the meaning of the hadith of Qatadah.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-'Abbas narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, Bahir ibn Sa'd narrated to me, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man praying while on the top of his foot was a spot the size of a dirham that the water had not reached, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered him to repeat the wudu'.

Abu Dawud related it from the hadith of Baqiyyah, [[Al-Musnad (3/424); Sunan Abi Dawud no. 175. Note: in both al-Musnad and Sunan Abi Dawud it reads: "from one of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ."]] and added: "and the prayer." This chain is good, strong and sahih, and Allah knows best.

In the hadith of Humran, from 'Uthman, describing the wudu' of the Prophet ﷺ: that he passed (the water) between his fingers (takhlil). The compilers of the Sunan related from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Kathir, from 'Asim ibn Laqit ibn Sabirah, from his father, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me about wudu'." He said: "Perfect the wudu', pass water between the fingers, and be thorough in istinshaq (rinsing the nose) unless you are fasting." [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. 142; Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. 788; Sunan an-Nasa'i (1/66); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 448.]]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abdullah ibn Yazid, Abu 'Abd ar-Rahman al-Muqri' [in manuscript A: "al-Maqbari"] narrated to us, 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Shaddad ibn 'Abdullah ad-Dimashqi narrated to us, [in manuscript A: "narrated to us Shaddad ibn 'Abdullah ad-Dimashqi, and the two said"] said: Abu Umamah said: 'Amr ibn 'Abasah narrated to us, saying: I said: "O Prophet of Allah, tell me about wudu'." He said: "There is none of you who brings near his wudu', then rinses his mouth, sniffs water into the nose and blows it out, except that his sins fall from his mouth and nostrils with the water when he blows it out; then he washes his face as Allah commanded, except that the sins of his face fall from the edges of his beard with the water; then he washes his hands up to the elbows, except that the sins of his hands fall from the tips of his fingers; then he wipes his head, except that the sins of his head fall from the ends of his hair with the water; then he washes his feet up to the ankles as Allah commanded, except that the sins of his feet fall from the tips of his toes with the water; then he stands and praises Allah and extols Him with what is fitting for Him, then he prays two rak'ahs, and he comes out from his sins like the day his mother bore him." Abu Umamah said: "O 'Amr, consider what you are saying. Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Is this man given all of that in one place?" 'Amr ibn 'Abasah said: "O Abu Umamah, my age has grown great, my bones have grown weak, and my end has drawn near, and I have no need to lie about Allah and His Messenger ﷺ. Even if I had heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only once, or twice, or three times, I would still have heard it seven times or more than that." [[Al-Musnad (4/112).]]

This chain is sahih, and it is in Sahih Muslim through another route, and in it: "then he washes his feet as Allah commanded." This shows that the Qur'an commands washing.

Likewise Abu Ishaq as-Sabi'i related from al-Harith, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Wash the feet up to the ankles as you have been commanded."

From here the intended meaning of the hadith of 'Abd Khayr, from 'Ali, becomes clear: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sprinkled water on his feet while they were in his sandals, and rubbed them. He only meant a light washing while they were in the sandals. There is no obstacle to washing the foot while it is in its shoe. However, this is a refutation of those who are excessive and rigorous, the obsessive who are overly scrupulous. Likewise is the hadith that Ibn Jarir cited against himself, which is of his own narration, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to a refuse dump of a people and urinated standing, then he asked for water and performed wudu', and wiped over his sandals. [[Tafsir at-Tabari (10/75).]] This is a sahih hadith. Ibn Jarir answered it by saying that the trustworthy, reliable narrators related it from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Hudhayfah, who said: "He urinated standing, then performed wudu' and wiped over his khuffs."

I say: It is possible to reconcile the two by saying that he had khuffs on his feet, and over them sandals.

Likewise is the hadith that Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal related: Yahya narrated to us from Shu'bah, Ya'la narrated to me, from his father, from Aws ibn Abi Aws, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform wudu' and wipe over his sandals, then he stood up to pray. Abu Dawud also related it from Musaddad and 'Abbad ibn Musa, both from Hushaym, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', from his father, from Aws ibn Abi Aws, who said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ come to a refuse dump of a people and urinate, and he performed wudu' and wiped over his sandals and his feet." [[Al-Musnad (4/8); Sunan Abi Dawud no. 160; Tafsir at-Tabari (10/76).]]

Ibn Jarir related it through the route of Shu'bah and through the route of Hushaym, then said: "This is to be understood as meaning that he performed wudu' in that manner while he was not in a state of hadath (ritual impurity), since it is not permissible that the obligations of Allah and the sunnah of His Messenger should be contradictory and conflicting. It has been established from him ﷺ, by widely transmitted and conclusive report, the command to wash the two feet in wudu' with water in its general sense, which removes the excuse of anyone who has reached it and heard it."

And since the Qur'an commands washing the two feet, as in the reading in the accusative (an-nasb), and as is necessary in interpreting the reading in the genitive (al-khafd) according to it, some of the early scholars (salaf) thought that this verse abrogates (naskh) the concession of wiping over the two khuffs. This was related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, but its chain is not sahih, and what is established from him is the opposite. It is not as they claimed, for it has been established that the Prophet ﷺ wiped over the two khuffs after the revelation of this noble verse.

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Ziyad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Ulathah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, from Mujahid, from Jarir ibn 'Abdullah al-Bajali, who said: I embraced Islam after the revelation of Surat al-Ma'idah, and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiping after I had embraced Islam. Ahmad alone related it. [[Al-Musnad (4/363).]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verse 6 (part 5 of 5):

It is related in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Hammam, who said: Jarir urinated, then performed ablution and wiped over his khuffs (leather socks). It was said to him: "Do you do this?" He said: "Yes, I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) urinate, then perform ablution and wipe over his khuffs." Al-A'mash said: Ibrahim said: "This hadith used to impress them, because Jarir's conversion to Islam came after the revelation of Surat al-Ma'idah." This is the wording of Muslim. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (387) and Sahih Muslim no. (272).]

It has been established through mass-transmission (tawatur) from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that wiping over the khuffs is legislated, both by his words and by his actions, as is established in the book "al-Ahkam al-Kabir", and what needs to be mentioned there concerning whether the wiping is time-limited or not, or the detail regarding it, as is expounded in its place. The Rawafid (Rafidah) have opposed all of this without any evidence, rather out of ignorance and misguidance, even though it is authenticated in Sahih Muslim, through the narration of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him. Likewise, it is established in the two Sahihs from him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that marriage by mut'ah (temporary marriage) is forbidden, while they permit it. Similarly, this noble verse indicates the obligation of washing the two feet, together with what has been established through mass-transmission of the action of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in accordance with what this noble verse indicates. They oppose all of that, and they have no sound proof in reality. All praise is due to Allah.

Likewise, they opposed the Imams and the early generation (salaf) regarding the two ankles (al-ka'bayn) which are on the feet. According to them, they are on the upper part of the foot, so according to them each foot has one ankle. According to the majority, the two ankles are the two protruding bones at the joint of the leg and the foot. Al-Rabi' said: Al-Shafi'i said: "I know of no dissenter in the view that the two ankles which Allah mentioned in His Book regarding ablution are the two protruding ones, and they are the meeting point of the joint of the leg and the foot." This is his wording. Thus, according to the Imams, may Allah have mercy on them, there are two ankles on each foot, as is well known among people, and as the Sunnah indicates. In the two Sahihs, through the chain of Humran from Uthman: he performed ablution and washed his right foot up to the ankles, and the left likewise.

Al-Bukhari related it as a mu'allaq (suspended narration) stated with certainty, and Abu Dawud and Ibn Khuzaymah in his Sahih, through the narration of Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn al-Harith al-Jadali, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned to us with his face and said: "Straighten your rows" three times, "By Allah, you will straighten your rows, or Allah will cause discord between your hearts." He said: "I saw the man pressing his ankle against the ankle of his companion, his knee against the knee of his companion, and his shoulder against the shoulder of his companion." This is the wording of Ibn Khuzaymah. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (662) and Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah no. (160).]

It is not possible for a person to press his ankle against the ankle of his companion except that what is meant is the protruding bone in the leg, so that it lines up with the other's ankle. This indicates what we have mentioned, that they are the two protruding bones at the joint of the leg and the foot, as is the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Isma'il ibn Musa related to us, Shurayk informed us, from Yahya ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, meaning al-Jabir, who said: "I looked among the slain companions of Zayd and found the ankle above the top of the foot." This was a punishment with which the Shi'ah were punished after their killing, as a deterrent against them for their opposition to the truth and their persistence in it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then take for yourselves clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it﴾, all of this has already been discussed in the interpretation of the verse in Surat al-Nisa', so there is no need for us to repeat it, lest the discussion become lengthy. We have mentioned the occasion of revelation of the verse of tayammum there. However, al-Bukhari related here a hadith specific to this noble verse, so he said:

Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us, Ibn Wahb related to us, Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim related to him, from his father, from Aisha: My necklace fell off at al-Bayda', while we were entering Madinah, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) halted his camel and dismounted, and he laid his head on my lap while sleeping. Abu Bakr came and struck me a severe blow in the back and said: "You have detained the people over a necklace!" Death was almost upon me because of the position of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it pained me. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) awoke and the dawn prayer time arrived, so he sought water but none was found. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces﴾ to the end of this verse. Usayd ibn al-Hudayr said: "May Allah bless the people through you, O family of Abu Bakr; you are nothing but a blessing for them." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4608).]

As for His saying: ﴿Allah does not intend to place upon you any hardship﴾, meaning: for this reason He made it easy for you, facilitated, and did not make it difficult. Rather, He permitted tayammum when ill and when water is absent, as a widening for you and a mercy towards you, and He made it, in a right of the Law of Allah, stand in the place of water except in some respects, as has been explained previously, and as is established in the book "al-Ahkam al-Kabir".

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But He wishes to purify you and to complete His favour upon you that you may be grateful﴾, meaning: that you may be grateful for His blessings upon you in what He has legislated for you of ease, kindness, mercy, facilitation and tolerance. The Sunnah has come with encouragement to supplicate after ablution, that the one who does it becomes among those who purify themselves and are included in complying with this noble verse, as Imam Ahmad, Muslim and the authors of the Sunan related from Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: We were responsible for herding the camels, and my turn came, so I brought them back in the evening, and I found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing and addressing the people. I caught from his words: "There is no Muslim who performs ablution and does it well, then stands and prays two rak'ahs, attentive to them with his heart and face, except that Paradise becomes due for him." He said: I said: "How excellent this is!" Then a speaker before me said: "The one before it is better than it." I looked, and it was Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I saw you came just now." He said: "There is none of you who performs ablution and completes (or perfects) the ablution, then says: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, except that the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, he entering through whichever he wishes." This is the wording of Muslim. [Al-Musnad (4/153), Sahih Muslim no. (234), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (169) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/95).]

Malik said: From Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Muslim servant (or the believer) performs ablution and washes his face, every sin that he looked at with his eyes departs from his face with the water (or with the last drop of water). When he washes his hands, every sin his hands committed departs from his hands with the water (or with the last drop of water). When he washes his feet, every sin his feet walked to departs with the water (or with the last drop of water), until he emerges pure from sins."

Muslim related it from Abu al-Tahir, from Ibn Wahb, from Malik, with this wording. [Al-Muwatta' (1/32) and Sahih Muslim no. (244).]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ka'b ibn Murrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no man who performs ablution and washes his hands (or his forearms) except that his sins come out from them. When he washes his face, his sins come out from his face. When he wipes his head, his sins come out from his head. When he washes his feet, his sins come out from his feet." [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/87).]

This is his wording. Imam Ahmad also related it, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, from Salim, from Murrah ibn Ka'b, or Ka'b ibn Murrah al-Sulami, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When the servant performs ablution and washes his hands, his sins come out from between his hands. When he washes his face, his sins come out from his face. When he washes his forearms, his sins come out from his forearms. When he washes his feet, his sins come out from his feet." Shu'bah said: He did not mention wiping the head. And this is a sound chain. [Al-Musnad (4/334). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/224): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Ibn Jarir related through the route of Shamir ibn Atiyyah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs ablution and does it well, then stands up to pray, his sins come out from his hearing, his sight, his hands and his feet." [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/86); Ahmad related it in his Musnad (5/252) through the route of Shamir ibn Atiyyah with the same wording.]

Muslim related in his Sahih, from the hadith of Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Zayd ibn Sallam, from his grandfather Mamtur, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Purity is half of faith; al-hamdu lillah fills the scale; subhan Allah and al-hamdu lillah fill what is between the heavens and the earth; prayer is light; charity is proof; patience is illumination; and the Qur'an is a proof for you or against you. Every person goes out in the morning, selling his soul, so he either frees it or destroys it." [Sahih Muslim no. (223).]

In Sahih Muslim, through the narration of Simak ibn Harb, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah does not accept charity from misappropriated wealth, nor prayer without purification." [Sahih Muslim no. (224).]

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'bah related to us, from Qatadah, I heard Abu al-Malih al-Hudhali narrating from his father, who said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a house, and I heard him say: 'Indeed Allah does not accept prayer without purification, nor charity from misappropriated wealth.'"

Likewise, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of Shu'bah. [Musnad al-Tayalisi no. (153), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (59), Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/87) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (271).]

The Exalted says, reminding His believing servants of His blessing upon them in prescribing for them this great religion and in sending to them this noble Messenger, and of the covenant and pledge He took from them in pledging allegiance (bay'ah, the oath of allegiance) to him, to follow him, to support him and to aid him, to uphold his religion, to convey it from him and to accept it from him. So He said [Exalted is He]: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey."﴾ This is the pledge with which the people used to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) upon their conversion to Islam, as they said: "We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey, in ease and in hardship, and in situations where we are given no preference, and not to dispute the affair with its people." And the Exalted said: ﴿And why should you not believe in Allah while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord and He has already taken your covenant, if you are believers?﴾ [al-Hadid: 8]

It has been said that this is a reminder to the Jews of the covenants and pacts that were taken from them concerning following Muhammad (ﷺ) and submitting to his law. This was narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas. It has also been said that it is a reminder of the covenant that Allah took from the descendants of Adam when He brought them forth from his loins and made them bear witness against themselves: ﴿Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes, we bear witness.'﴾ [al-A'raf: 172]. This was said by Mujahid and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. The first view is more apparent, and it is the one reported from Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, an emphasis and an exhortation to persist in taqwa (God-consciousness) in every state.

Then He informed them that He knows what passes through the hearts and the innermost secrets and thoughts, so He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿O you who believe, be persistently standing firm for Allah⦆ means: be persistently standing firm for the truth for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not for the sake of people or for reputation. And be ﴿witnesses in justice﴾, meaning witnesses with justice and not with injustice. It is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir that he said: My father gave me a gift (nahl), but my mother, Amrah bint Rawahah, said: "I will not be satisfied until you have the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) bear witness to it." So he came to him to have him witness his gift, and he (ﷺ) said: "Did you give all your children the like of this?" He said: "No." He said: "Fear Allah and be just among your children." And he said: "I will not bear witness to an injustice." He said: So my father returned and took back that gift.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just﴾ means: do not let the enmity of a people lead you to abandon justice concerning them, but apply justice to everyone, whether a friend or an enemy. For this reason He said: ﴿Be just; that is nearer to righteousness﴾, meaning your justice is nearer to taqwa than abandoning it. The verb indicates the verbal noun to which the pronoun refers, as in its parallels in the Qur'an and elsewhere, such as His saying: ﴿And if you are told, "Return," then return; it is purer for you﴾ [al-Nur: 28].

* *

His saying: ﴿It is nearer to righteousness﴾ is from the usage of the elative form (af'al al-tafdil) in a context where there is nothing at all on the other side of the comparison, as in His saying: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, are better in residence and finer in resting place﴾ [al-Furqan: 24], and as in the saying of one of the female Companions to Umar: "You are harsher and rougher than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." [Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim]

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ meaning: He will recompense you for what He knows of your deeds that you have done, whether good, then good, or evil, then evil. For this reason He said after it: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness﴾, meaning for their sins, ﴿and a great reward﴾, which is Paradise, which is of His mercy upon His servants. They do not attain it by their deeds alone, but by mercy and bounty from Him, although the means by which mercy reaches them are their deeds. He, the Exalted, is the One who made these means to attain His mercy, His bounty, His pardon and His good pleasure. So all of it is from Him and belongs to Him. To Him belongs praise and grace.

Then He said: ﴿But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs – those are the companions of Hellfire.﴾ This is part of His justice, His wisdom and His judgment, in which there is no injustice. Rather, He is the Just Judge, the Wise, the Powerful.

* *

His saying: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you﴾. ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who mentioned it from Abu Salamah, from Jabir, that the Prophet (ﷺ) stopped at a place, and the people scattered among the acacia trees seeking shade beneath them. The Prophet (ﷺ) hung his sword on a tree. A bedouin came to the sword of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), took it, drew it, and then turned toward the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Who will protect you from me?" He said: "Allah!" The bedouin said twice or thrice: "Who will protect you from me?" And the Prophet (ﷺ) kept saying: "Allah!" He said: So the bedouin sheathed the sword, and the Prophet (ﷺ) called his companions and informed them of the bedouin's story, while he was sitting beside him, and he did not punish him. Ma'mar said: Qatadah used to mention something similar, and mentioned that a group of the Arabs wanted to assassinate the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so they sent this bedouin. And he interpreted: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you...﴾ the verse.

The story of this bedouin, who was Ghawrath ibn al-Harith, is established in the Sahih. [Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq; and al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih from the route of Abd al-Razzaq.]

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you﴾. That is because a group of the Jews prepared food for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions in order to kill them. Allah the Exalted revealed to him their plot, so the food did not come, and he ordered his Companions, so they did not come to him. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Abu Malik said: It was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions, when they wanted to betray Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions in the house of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, Mujahid, Ikrimah, and others besides them mentioned that it was revealed concerning the Banu al-Nadir, when they wanted to drop a millstone on the head of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he came to them seeking their help regarding the blood money of the two men from Banu Amir. They commissioned Amr ibn Jahhash ibn Ka'b for this, and they instructed him that if the Prophet (ﷺ) sat under the wall and they gathered around him, he should drop that millstone on him from above. But Allah informed His Messenger of what they were plotting, so he returned to Madinah, and his Companions followed him. Then Allah [Exalted] revealed concerning that: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you. And fear Allah; and upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that he go out against them, and he besieged them until he brought them down, and then he expelled them.

* *

His saying: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ means: whoever relies upon Allah, Allah will suffice him in what concerns him, protect him from the evil of people, and preserve him.

The Exalted says, reminding His believing servants of His blessing upon them in prescribing for them this great religion and in sending to them this noble Messenger, and of the covenant and pledge He took from them in pledging allegiance (bay'ah, the oath of allegiance) to him, to follow him, to support him and to aid him, to uphold his religion, to convey it from him and to accept it from him. So He said [Exalted is He]: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey."﴾ This is the pledge with which the people used to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) upon their conversion to Islam, as they said: "We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey, in ease and in hardship, and in situations where we are given no preference, and not to dispute the affair with its people."
