His saying: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you﴾. ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who mentioned it from Abu Salamah, from Jabir, that the Prophet (ﷺ) stopped at a place, and the people scattered among the acacia trees seeking shade beneath them. The Prophet (ﷺ) hung his sword on a tree. A bedouin came to the sword of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), took it, drew it, and then turned toward the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Who will protect you from me?" He said: "Allah!" The bedouin said twice or thrice: "Who will protect you from me?" And the Prophet (ﷺ) kept saying: "Allah!" He said: So the bedouin sheathed the sword, and the Prophet (ﷺ) called his companions and informed them of the bedouin's story, while he was sitting beside him, and he did not punish him. Ma'mar said: Qatadah used to mention something similar, and mentioned that a group of the Arabs wanted to assassinate the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so they sent this bedouin. And he interpreted: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you...﴾ the verse.

The story of this bedouin, who was Ghawrath ibn al-Harith, is established in the Sahih. [Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq; and al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih from the route of Abd al-Razzaq.]

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you﴾. That is because a group of the Jews prepared food for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions in order to kill them. Allah the Exalted revealed to him their plot, so the food did not come, and he ordered his Companions, so they did not come to him. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Abu Malik said: It was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions, when they wanted to betray Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions in the house of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, Mujahid, Ikrimah, and others besides them mentioned that it was revealed concerning the Banu al-Nadir, when they wanted to drop a millstone on the head of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he came to them seeking their help regarding the blood money of the two men from Banu Amir. They commissioned Amr ibn Jahhash ibn Ka'b for this, and they instructed him that if the Prophet (ﷺ) sat under the wall and they gathered around him, he should drop that millstone on him from above. But Allah informed His Messenger of what they were plotting, so he returned to Madinah, and his Companions followed him. Then Allah [Exalted] revealed concerning that: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you. And fear Allah; and upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that he go out against them, and he besieged them until he brought them down, and then he expelled them.

* *

His saying: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ means: whoever relies upon Allah, Allah will suffice him in what concerns him, protect him from the evil of people, and preserve him.

When God, exalted is He, commanded His believing servants to fulfil His covenant and His pact, which He had taken from them through the tongue of His servant and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and commanded them to uphold the truth and bear witness with justice, and reminded them of His favours upon them, both outward and inward, in that He guided them to the truth and the guidance, this is a law that explains to them how He took covenants and pacts from those before them among the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians. When they broke His covenants and pacts, that brought upon them His curse, His expulsion from His door and His presence, and a veil over their hearts ["in manuscript r: 'to their faults'"] from reaching guidance and the religion of truth, which is beneficial knowledge and righteous action. That is, leaders (nuqaba', sing. naqib, meaning a chief or representative) over their tribes, to pledge allegiance, to hear and obey God, His Messenger and His Book.

I have seen in the Fourth Book of the Torah a enumeration of the chiefs over the tribes of the Children of Israel, with names differing from what Ibn Ishaq mentioned, and God knows best. In it it says: over the sons of Reuben, "Al-Sawni ibn Sadun"; over the sons of Simeon, "Shamwal ibn Sawrshaki"; over the sons of Judah, "Yahshun ibn 'Amibadhab" ["in manuscript r: 'Amina Dhab'"]; over the sons of Issachar, "Shal ibn Sa'un"; over the sons of Zebulun, "Eliab ibn Halub" ["in manuscript r: 'Jalut'"]; over the sons of Joseph, Ephraim: "Manshа ibn 'Amanhud" ["in manuscript r: 'wa-Manasha'"]; over the sons of Manasseh: "Hamli'il ibn Yarsun"; over the sons of Benjamin: "Abidan ibn Jad'un"; over the sons of Dan: "Ja'ayadhar ibn 'Amishadhai"; over the sons of Asher: "Nahayil ibn 'Ajran"; over the sons of Hazar: "Al-Sayf ibn Da'wayil"; over the sons of Naphtali: "Ajza' ibn 'Aminan".

Likewise, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) pledged allegiance to the Ansar on the night of 'Aqaba, there were twelve chiefs among them: three from the Aws, namely Usayd ibn al-Hudayr, Sa'd ibn Khaythama and Rifa'a ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir, and it is said that instead of him it was Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan, may God be pleased with them; and nine from the Khazraj, namely Abu Umama As'ad ibn Zurara, Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, Rafi' ibn Malik ibn al-'Ajlan ["in manuscript a: 'Ajlan'"], al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, Sa'd ibn 'Ubada, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram, and al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr ibn Khunays, may God be pleased with them. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: "We were sitting with 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud while he was teaching us the Qur'an, when a man said to him: 'O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, did you ask the Messenger of God (ﷺ): how many caliphs will rule this community?' This is not the awaited one whom the Rafidah (Shi'a who reject the first caliphs) imagine to exist and then to emerge from the underground chamber in Samarra'. That has no reality or existence at all; rather it is one of the delusions of feeble minds and the imaginings of weak fancies. * *

And His saying: ﴿"Whoever among you disbelieves after that has certainly strayed from the right way"﴾, that is, whoever opposes this covenant after its conclusion, its affirmation and its binding, and denies it and treats it as one who does not know it, has certainly erred from the true path and turned away from guidance to misguidance.

Then God, exalted is He, informed of the punishment that befell them when they opposed His covenant and broke His pact, and He said: ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant We cursed them﴾, that is, because of their breaking the covenant that was taken from them, We cursed them, that is, We removed them far from the truth and expelled them from guidance. ﴿And We made their hearts hard﴾, that is, so they do not benefit from admonition because of their coarseness and hardness. ﴿They distort words from their places﴾, that is, their understandings became corrupt, and their handling of the signs of God became evil; they interpreted His Book in other than what He revealed, carried it to other than its intended meaning, and said about Him what He did not say, seeking refuge in God from that. ﴿And they have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of﴾, that is, they abandoned acting upon it out of aversion to it.

Al-Hasan said: They abandoned the handholds of their religion and the duties of God without which no deed is accepted. Others said: They abandoned action and came to a wretched state, so there are no sound hearts, no upright natures, and no righteous deeds.

﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery from them﴾, that is, their deception and their betrayal against you and your companions.

Mujahid and others said: this refers to their conspiring to assassinate the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿So pardon them and overlook﴾. This is indeed the very essence of victory and triumph, as some of the early generations said: "I have never treated one who disobeys God regarding you with anything like obeying God regarding him." Through this they are brought together and united upon the truth, and perhaps God will guide them. Therefore God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed God loves the doers of good﴾, meaning by this: forgiving those who wrong you.

Qatadah said: this verse ﴿So pardon them and overlook﴾ has been abrogated by His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God or the Last Day, nor forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, nor adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Book, until they give the jizya willingly while they are humbled﴾ [al-Tawba: 29].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "From the tribe of Reuben was Shammu' ibn Zakur ["in manuscript r: 'Zakun'"]; from the tribe of Simeon, Shafat ibn Huri; from the tribe of Judah, Caleb ibn Yufuna; from the tribe of Abin, Figha'il ibn Yusuf; from the tribe of Joseph, which is the tribe of Ephraim, Joshua ibn Nun; from the tribe of Benjamin, Falti ibn Raphun; from the tribe of Zebulun ["in manuscript r: 'Zaykun', and in manuscript a: 'Zaylun'"] Jadi ibn Sawdi; from the tribe of Joseph, namely the tribe of Manasseh, Jadi ibn Sausa; from the tribe of Dan, Hamla'il ibn Jumal; from the tribe of Asher, Sator ibn Mulkil; from the tribe of Naphtali ["in manuscript r: 'Thaqal'"], Nahhi ibn Wafsa; from the tribe of Gad, Jawla'il ibn Miki ["in manuscript r: 'Mulidan'"]." I have seen in the Fourth Book of the Torah a enumeration of the chiefs over the tribes of the Children of Israel, with names differing from what Ibn Ishaq mentioned, and God knows best. In it it says: over the sons of Reuben, "Al-Sawni ibn Sadun"; over the sons of Simeon, "Shamwal ibn Sawrshaki"; over the sons of Judah, "Yahshun ibn 'Amibadhab" ["in manuscript r: 'Amina Dhab'"]; over the sons of Issachar, "Shal ibn Sa'un"; over the sons of Zebulun, "Eliab ibn Halub" ["in manuscript r: 'Jalut'"]; over the sons of Joseph, Ephraim: "Manshа ibn 'Amanhud" ["in manuscript r: 'wa-Manasha'"]; over the sons of Manasseh: "Hamli'il ibn Yarsun"; over the sons of Benjamin: "Abidan ibn Jad'un"; over the sons of Dan: "Ja'ayadhar ibn 'Amishadhai"; over the sons of Asher: "Nahayil ibn 'Ajran"; over the sons of Hazar: "Al-Sayf ibn Da'wayil"; over the sons of Naphtali: "Ajza' ibn 'Aminan".

Likewise, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) pledged allegiance to the Ansar on the night of 'Aqaba, there were twelve chiefs among them: three from the Aws, namely Usayd ibn al-Hudayr, Sa'd ibn Khaythama and Rifa'a ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir, and it is said that instead of him it was Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan, may God be pleased with them; and nine from the Khazraj, namely Abu Umama As'ad ibn Zurara, Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, Rafi' ibn Malik ibn al-'Ajlan ["in manuscript a: 'Ajlan'"], al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, Sa'd ibn 'Ubada, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram, and al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr ibn Khunays, may God be pleased with them. Ka'b ibn Malik mentioned them in a poem of his, as Ibn Ishaq related, may God have mercy on him. [See: al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham (1/443).]

The meaning here is that these were chiefs over their people that night, by the Prophet's (ﷺ) command to them, and they were the ones entrusted with the pledge and the contract on behalf of their people to the Prophet (ﷺ), to hear and obey.

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: "We were sitting with 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud while he was teaching us the Qur'an, when a man said to him: 'O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, did you ask the Messenger of God (ﷺ): how many caliphs will rule this community?' 'Abd Allah said: 'No one has asked me about this since I came to Iraq before you.' Then he said: 'Yes, indeed we asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: "Twelve, like the number of the chiefs of the Children of Israel."'"

This is a gharib (singular, weak in transmission) hadith through this chain [al-Musnad (1/398). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/190): "In it is Mujalid ibn Sa'id, whom al-Nasa'i declared trustworthy and most scholars declared weak, while the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]. The root of this hadith is firmly established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Jabir ibn Samura, who said: "I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'This affair of the people will continue to prosper as long as twelve men rule over them.'" Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said a word which I did not hear, so I asked my father: 'What did the Prophet (ﷺ) say?' He said: "All of them are from Quraysh."

This is the wording of Muslim [Sahih Muslim, no. 1822]. The meaning of this hadith is the glad tidings of the existence of twelve righteous caliphs who establish the truth and rule justly among them. This does not necessarily mean that they succeed one another consecutively in an unbroken sequence, for indeed four of them existed in succession, and they are the Four Rightly-Guided Caliphs: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali, may God be pleased with them. Among them is 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, without doubt according to the scholars, and some of the 'Abbasids. The Hour will not come until their rule is certain to occur. It is apparent that among them is the Mahdi, who is given good news of in the hadiths that mention him: that his name coincides with the name of the Prophet (ﷺ), and his father's name with the name of his father, and he will fill the earth with justice and equity, just as it was filled with oppression and injustice. This is not the awaited one whom the Rafidah (Shi'a who reject the first caliphs) imagine to exist and then to emerge from the underground chamber in Samarra'. That has no reality or existence at all; rather it is one of the delusions of feeble minds and the imaginings of weak fancies. Nor do these twelve caliphs refer to the twelve Imams whom the Twelver Rafidah believe in, out of their ignorance and feebleness of intellect. The Torah contains good news of Isma'il, peace be upon him, that God would raise up from his loins twelve great ones, and these are the twelve caliphs mentioned in the hadiths of Ibn Mas'ud and Jabir ibn Samura. Some ignorant people among the Jews who have embraced Islam, when some Shi'a associate with them, lead them to imagine that they are the twelve Imams, so many of them become Shi'a out of ignorance and folly, because of the scarcity of their knowledge and the knowledge of those who taught them that, contrary to the established Sunnah of the Prophet (ﷺ).

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And God said: "Indeed I am with you"﴾, that is, by My protection, My guardianship and My help. ﴿"If you establish prayer, give zakat, believe in My messengers"﴾, that is, affirm them in what they bring you of revelation, ﴿"and support them"﴾, that is, help them and back them up in the truth, ﴿"and lend to God a goodly loan"﴾, which is spending in His cause and seeking His pleasure. ﴿"I will surely remove from you your misdeeds"﴾, that is, your sins I will erase and cover, and I will not hold you accountable for them, ﴿"and surely admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow"﴾, that is, I will repel what you dread and obtain for you what you desire.

* *

And His saying: ﴿"Whoever among you disbelieves after that has certainly strayed from the right way"﴾, that is, whoever opposes this covenant after its conclusion, its affirmation and its binding, and denies it and treats it as one who does not know it, has certainly erred from the true path and turned away from guidance to misguidance.

Then God, exalted is He, informed of the punishment that befell them when they opposed His covenant and broke His pact, and He said: ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant We cursed them﴾, that is, because of their breaking the covenant that was taken from them, We cursed them, that is, We removed them far from the truth and expelled them from guidance. ﴿And We made their hearts hard﴾, that is, so they do not benefit from admonition because of their coarseness and hardness. ﴿They distort words from their places﴾, that is, their understandings became corrupt, and their handling of the signs of God became evil; they interpreted His Book in other than what He revealed, carried it to other than its intended meaning, and said about Him what He did not say, seeking refuge in God from that. ﴿And they have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of﴾, that is, they abandoned acting upon it out of aversion to it.

Al-Hasan said: They abandoned the handholds of their religion and the duties of God without which no deed is accepted. Others said: They abandoned action and came to a wretched state, so there are no sound hearts, no upright natures, and no righteous deeds.

﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery from them﴾, that is, their deception and their betrayal against you and your companions.

Mujahid and others said: this refers to their conspiring to assassinate the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿So pardon them and overlook﴾. This is indeed the very essence of victory and triumph, as some of the early generations said: "I have never treated one who disobeys God regarding you with anything like obeying God regarding him." Through this they are brought together and united upon the truth, and perhaps God will guide them. Therefore God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed God loves the doers of good﴾, meaning by this: forgiving those who wrong you.

Qatadah said: this verse ﴿So pardon them and overlook﴾ has been abrogated by His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God or the Last Day, nor forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, nor adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Book, until they give the jizya willingly while they are humbled﴾ [al-Tawba: 29].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And from those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant﴾, that is, from those who claimed for themselves that they were Christians following Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, when they were not so, We took from them covenants and pacts to follow the Messenger, to support him, to aid him and to follow his traces, and to believe in every prophet God sends to the people of the earth. That is, they did as the Jews did: they opposed the covenants and broke the pacts. Therefore He said: ﴿But they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of, so We stirred up among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, We cast among them enmity and mutual hatred, and they remain so until the establishment of the Hour. Likewise the groups of Christians, despite the variety of their kinds, remain mutually hating and hostile, each declaring the others disbelievers and cursing one another. Each sect forbids the other and does not let it enter its place of worship: the Melkites declare the Jacobites disbelievers, and likewise the others; the Nestorians and the Arians too, each sect declares the other a disbeliever in this world, and on the Day when the witnesses stand.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And God will surely inform them of what they used to do﴾. This is a severe threat and a strong warning to the Christians for what they committed of lying against God and His Messenger, and for what they ascribed to the Lord, Mighty and Majestic is He, and He is exalted and sanctified far above what they say, a great exaltation, by their making for Him a consort and a son. Exalted is the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and to whom no one is equal.

Allah, the Exalted, says, telling about Himself, the Generous: that He sent His Messenger Muhammad with guidance and the religion of truth to all the people of the earth, Arabs and non-Arabs, the unlettered among them and the People of the Book. He sent him with clear proofs and with the criterion distinguishing truth from falsehood. So Allah the Exalted said:

﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture﴾. That is, he makes clear what they altered, distorted, and misinterpreted, and what they fabricated against Allah concerning it. And he remains silent about much of what they changed, for there is no benefit in explaining it.

Al-Hakim, in his Mustadrak, narrated through the hadith of Al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Yazid al-Nahwi (the grammarian), from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Whoever denies stoning (al-rajm) has denied the Qur'an without realizing it." His statement, "﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture﴾," refers to stoning, which was among what they concealed.

Then he said: "Its chain is sound, but the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it."

[Al-Mustadrak (4/359).]

Then Allah, the Exalted, told about the Great Qur'an which He sent down to His noble Prophet, saying:

﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book. By it Allah guides whoever follows His good pleasure to the ways of peace﴾. That is, the paths of salvation and safety and the methods of uprightness. ﴿And He brings them out of darkness into light by His permission and guides them to a straight path﴾. That is, He saves them from destruction, makes clear for them the clearest of paths, averts from them what is feared, secures for them the best of matters, removes misguidance from them, and guides them to the most upright state.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 5, verses 17–18:

He, Exalted is He, says, informing of and judging the disbelief of the Christians in their claim about the Messiah, the son of Mary, who is (only) a servant among the servants of God and a creature among His creation, that he is God. Exalted is God far above what they say, a great exaltation.

Then He said, informing of His power over things and that they are under His dominion and authority: ﴿Say: "Who could prevent God at all if He willed to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on earth together?"﴾ That is: even if He willed that, who would prevent Him from it? Or who would be able to turn Him away from it?

Then He said: ﴿And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills.﴾ That is: all existing things belong to Him and are His creation, and He is capable of whatever He wills. He is not questioned about what He does, because of His power, authority, justice and greatness. This is a refutation of the Christians, upon whom be the successive curses of God until the Day of Resurrection.

Then God, Exalted is He, said, refuting the Jews and the Christians in their lying and fabrication: ﴿The Jews and the Christians said, "We are the children of God and His beloved."﴾ That is: we are related to His prophets, and they are His sons, and He has special care for them, and He loves us. They transmitted from their Scripture that God [Exalted is He] (*addition from A*) said to His servant Israel: "You are My son, My firstborn." So they took this in a sense other than its intended meaning and distorted it. Several of their intelligent men who embraced Islam refuted them and said: this term is used among them to mean honour and esteem, just as the Christians transmitted from their Scripture that Jesus said to them: "I am going to my Father and your Father," meaning: my Lord and your Lord. It is well known that they did not claim for themselves the sonship that they claimed for Jesus, peace be upon him. They only meant by that their nearness to Him and their favour with Him. For this reason they said: "We are the children of God and His beloved."

God, Exalted is He, said, refuting them: ﴿Say: "Then why does He punish you for your sins?"﴾ That is: if you were as you claim, His sons and His beloved, then why has He prepared for you the Fire of Hell because of your disbelief, your lying and your fabrication? Some of the shaykhs of the Sufis said to some of the jurists: "Where do you find in the Qur'an that the beloved does not punish his beloved?" He did not answer him, so the Sufi recited this verse: ﴿Say: "Then why does He punish you for your sins?"﴾

What he said is good, and it has a witness in the *Musnad* of Imam Ahmad, where he said: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by with a group of his companions, and there was a child in the road. When his mother saw the people she feared for her child that he would be trampled, so she came running and saying: "My son, my son!" She ran and took him. The people said: "O Messenger of God, this woman would never throw her son into the Fire." He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) turned them away and said: "No, by God, He does not throw His beloved into the Fire." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[*al-Musnad* (3/104).]]

[And His saying] (*addition from A*) ﴿Rather, you are human beings among those He has created.﴾ That is: you are like other human beings, the descendants of Adam, for you. He, Exalted is He, is the Judge over all His servants: ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills.﴾ That is: He does what He intends; there is no one to reverse His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning. ﴿And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them.﴾ That is: all of it is His dominion and under His power and authority. ﴿And to Him is the final return.﴾ That is: the return and the resort are to Him, so He judges His servants as He wills, and He is the Just who does not oppress.

[And] (*addition from A*) Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Nu'man ibn Adaa [[In A: "Utman ibn Sa"]], Bahri ibn 'Amr and Shas ibn 'Adi came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). They spoke with him, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) spoke with them, called them to God and warned them of His vengeance. They said: "What are you frightening us with, O Muhammad? By God, we are the children of God and His beloved, like the saying of the Christians." So God (*addition from A*) revealed concerning them: ﴿The Jews and the Christians said, "We are the children of God and His beloved."﴾ to the end of the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated, by way of Asbat, from As-Suddi, concerning God's saying (*addition from A*) ﴿The Jews and the Christians said, "We are the children of God and His beloved."﴾ As for their saying, "We are the children of God and His beloved," they said: God revealed to Israel that "your son, your firstborn among the children," [[In A: "my son"]] will enter them into the Fire, and they will remain in it for forty nights until it purifies them and consumes their sins. Then a caller will call out: "Bring out every circumcised one from the children of Israel." So they will be brought out. That is their saying: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 24] [[Thus in all the manuscripts; the text of al-Tabari reads: "that a son of yours will enter them into the Fire" (6/106).]]

God, exalted is He, addresses the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians: "He has indeed sent to you His Messenger Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets (khatam al-nabiyyin), after whom there is no prophet and no messenger. Rather, he is the one who follows all of them." Therefore He said: ﴿after a gap between the messengers﴾, meaning after a long period between his sending and that of 'Isa ibn Maryam.

They differed about the length of this gap (fatrah, a period without messengers). Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi and Qatadah, in one of his reports, said it was six hundred years. Al-Bukhari narrated it from Salman al-Farisi. From Qatadah there is also: five hundred and sixty years. Ma'mar said, from some of his companions: five hundred and forty years. Al-Dahhak said: four hundred and thirty-some years.

Ibn 'Asakir mentioned, in the biography of 'Isa, peace be upon him, [Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn 'Asakir (14/30, manuscript section) and Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (20/86)], from al-Sha'bi that he said: "From the raising of the Messiah to the Hijrah of the Prophet ﷺ was nine hundred and thirty-three years."

The well-known view is the first, that it was six hundred years. Some say six hundred and twenty years. There is no contradiction between them: the first speaker meant six solar years, and the other meant lunar years. Between every hundred solar years and lunar years there is about three years' difference. For this reason God said about the people of the Cave: ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾ [al-Kahf: 25], meaning lunar years, to complete the three hundred solar years that were known to the People of the Book. The gap between 'Isa ibn Maryam, the last of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and Muhammad ﷺ, the Seal of the Prophets from the children of Adam without exception, was as established in Sahih al-Bukhari from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed I am [the one] most worthy of Ibn Maryam, because there is no prophet between me and him." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3442]. This is a refutation of those who claimed that a prophet was sent after 'Isa, peace be upon him, called Khalid ibn Sinan, as related by al-Qudda'i and others.

The point is that Allah, [exalted is He], sent Muhammad ﷺ during a gap in the messengers, a fading of the paths, a change of religions, and the great worship of idols, fires and crosses. So the blessing through him was the most complete of blessings, and the need for him was general, for corruption had spread throughout the lands and transgression and ignorance had appeared among all the servants, except a few who clung to remnants of the religion of the earlier prophets, some rabbis of the Jews, worshippers among the Christians and the Sabians. As Imam Ahmad said:

Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us; Hisham narrated to us; Qatadah narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from 'Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ once delivered a sermon, and in his sermon he said: "Indeed my Lord commanded me to teach you what you do not know, of what He taught me on this day of mine: every property I have given My servants is lawful. I created My servants as hanifs (upright in faith), all of them, but the devils came to them and led them away from their religion, made unlawful for them what I had made lawful, and commanded them to associate with Me what I had not sent down any authority for. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, looked at the people of the earth and despised them, Arabs and non-Arabs alike, except for remnants of the People of the Book. He said: 'I have sent you only to test you and to test through you, and I have sent down to you a Book that water cannot wash away; you recite it asleep and awake.' Then Allah commanded me to burn Quraysh. I said: 'My Lord, then they would crush my head and leave it like a loaf.' He said: 'Expel them as they expelled you, fight them and We will fight for you, spend on them and We will spend on you, send an army and We will send five times its number, and fight with those who obey you against those who disobey you.' The people of Paradise are three: a ruler who is just, charitable and successful; a man who is merciful and tender-hearted toward every relative and every Muslim; and a chaste, poor man who gives charity. The people of the Fire are five: the weak one who has no means, who follow you without family or wealth [Yahya was unsure whether he said 'followers' or 'those who follow'], the treacherous one for whom no greed is hidden, however small, but he betrays it; and a man who does not rise in the morning or go to sleep in the evening without deceiving you about your family and your property." He also mentioned the miser or the liar, and "al-shinzir" means the coarse, foul-mouthed person. [Musnad, 4/162].

Then Imam Ahmad, Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated it through different chains, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Shakhkhir. In Sa'id's narration from Qatadah there is an explicit statement of Qatadah hearing this hadith from Mutarrif. Imam Ahmad mentioned in his Musnad that Qatadah did not hear it from Mutarrif directly but heard it from four people who had it from him. Then he narrated it through Rawh, from 'Awf, from Hakim al-Athram, from al-Hasan who said: "Mutarrif narrated to me, from 'Iyad ibn Himar," and mentioned it. Al-Nasa'i also narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Ghundar, from 'Awf al-A'rabi. [Musnad, 4/162; Sahih Muslim, no. 2865; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 8071].

The purpose of quoting this hadith is his words: "Indeed Allah looked at the people of the earth and despised them, Arabs and non-Arabs, except for remnants of the Children of Israel." In Muslim's wording: "from the People of the Book." The religion had become confused for all the people of the earth, until Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ, who guided the creation, and through him Allah brought them out of darkness into light, and left them upon the clear path and the bright law. For this reason God, exalted is He, said: ﴿lest you should say, "There came to us no bringer of good news and no warner"﴾, meaning: so that you could not argue and say (O you who changed and altered your religion): "No messenger came to us who gives good news of good and warns of evil." But now there has come to you a bringer of good news and a warner, meaning Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿And Allah is over all things competent.﴾

Ibn Jarir said: its meaning is: I am able to punish whoever disobeys Me and to reward whoever obeys Me.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 1 of 3):

God, exalted is He, says, telling of His servant, messenger and interlocutor Musa (Moses) son of 'Imran, peace be upon him, in what he reminded his people of, the blessings of God upon them and His favours toward them, in that He gathered for them the good of this world and the Hereafter, if they remained upright on their straight path. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when Musa said to his people: "O my people, remember the favour of God upon you when He appointed prophets among you﴾. That is: whenever a prophet died, another prophet arose among you, from your forefather Ibrahim (Abraham) onward and after him. [In manuscript A: "wa-lidhalika" (and therefore).] Thus they were: prophets never ceased among them, calling to God and warning of His vengeance, until they were concluded with 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him. Then God [exalted] [addition from manuscript R] revealed to the Seal of the Messengers and Prophets, absolutely, Muhammad son of 'Abdullah, who is traced to Isma'il son of Ibrahim, [manuscript A: "upon them both"] peace be upon him, and he is more noble than every one of them who preceded him, ﷺ.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from al-Thawri, from Mansur, from al-Hakam or another, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾, that he said: "The servant, the wife and the house."

Al-Hakim also narrated in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of al-Thawri as well, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The wife and the servant." ﴿And He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾, he said: "Those who were among them at that time." Then al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhari and Muslim]" [manuscript D: "according to their condition"], but they did not record it. [Al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/311, 312).]

Maymun ibn Mihran said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "A man from the Children of Israel, if he had a wife, a servant and a house, was called a king."

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Hani' informed us, that he heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli say: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, and a man asked him, saying: "Are we not [manuscript R: "Are you not"; manuscript D: "I am one of the poor"] among the poor Emigrants?" 'Abdullah said: "Do you have a wife to whom you retire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you have a dwelling in which you live?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are among the rich." He said: "I have a servant." [Manuscript A: "Then he said."] He said: "Then you are among the kings." [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/163).]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Is kingship anything but a mount, a servant and a house?"

Ibn Jarir narrated it. Then it was related from Mansur, al-Hakam, Mujahid and Sufyan al-Thawri something similar to this. Ibn Abi Hatim also related it from Maymun ibn Mihran.

Ibn Shawdhab said: "A man from the Children of Israel, if he had a dwelling and a servant, and he was asked permission to enter upon him, then he was a king."

Qatadah said: "They were the first to possess servants as property [literally: to own servants]."

al-Suddi said regarding His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾: "A man among you possesses his own self, his family and his wealth." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Ibn Lahi'a, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "When one of the Children of Israel had a servant, a beast of burden and a wife, he was recorded as a king." [Within its chain are Ibn Lahi'a and Darraj, both weak, and Darraj's narration from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

And this is a strange (gharib) hadith from this route.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar narrated to us, Abu Dhamrah Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, [he said] [addition from manuscript A] I heard Zayd ibn Aslam say: ﴿and He made you kings﴾, then I know of nothing except that he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever has a house and a servant, he is a king."

This is a mursal (a report whose chain omits the Companion) and strange. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/161).] Malik said: "A house, a servant and a wife."

It has come in a hadith: "Whoever among you wakes up healthy in his body, secure in his dwelling, having the sustenance of his day, it is as if the whole world has been gathered for him." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (2346), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (4141), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mihsan al-Ansari.]

* *

And His saying: ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾. He means the worlds of your time. So they were the most noble of people in their time, among the Greeks, the Copts and all other kinds of the children of Adam, as He said: ﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Scripture and judgement and prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 16]. And God, exalted is He, said, reporting about Musa when they said: ﴿Make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. Indeed, these — what they are in is destroyed, and worthless is what they have been doing." He said, "Is it other than God I should seek for you as a god while He has preferred you over the worlds?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 138–140].

The intended meaning is that they were the best people of their time. Otherwise, this community (ummah) is more noble than them, more excellent before God, more complete in law, more upright in method, more honoured in prophet, greater in dominion, more abundant in provisions, greater in wealth and offspring, more extensive in realm, and more lasting in honour. God [exalted and majestic] [addition from manuscript R; manuscript A: "exalted"] said: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110], and He said: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. We have mentioned the mutawatir hadiths concerning the excellence, nobility and honour of this community before God, at His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ in the surah of Al 'Imran.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that they said regarding His saying: ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾, that it means: the community of Muhammad ﷺ. It seems they intended that this address in His saying ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾ is together with this community. The majority hold that it is an address from Musa to his people, and it is to be understood as the worlds of their time, as we have previously mentioned.

It was also said: The meaning of ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾ is: what He sent down to them of manna and quails, and what He shaded them with of clouds, and other things, of the extraordinary matters (khawariq al-'adat) with which God specifically favoured them. And God knows best.

Then God, exalted is He, said, reporting about the urging by Musa, peace be upon him, of the Children of Israel to jihad and to entering Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), which had been in their hands in the time of their forefather Ya'qub (Jacob), when he, his sons and his family migrated to the land of Egypt in the days of Yusuf, peace be upon him. Then they remained there until they went out with Musa [peace be upon him] [addition from manuscript A], and they found therein a people of the 'Amaliqah, the tyrannical giants, who had seized it and taken possession of it. So the Messenger of God, Musa, peace be upon him, commanded them to enter it and to fight their enemies, and gave them the good news of victory and triumph over them. But they shrank back, disobeyed and opposed his command, so they were punished by wandering in the wilderness (al-tih) and persisting in their journey bewildered, not knowing how to head toward a destination in it, for a period of forty years, as a punishment for them for their neglect of the command of God [exalted] [addition from manuscript A]. God, exalted is He, said, reporting about Musa that he said: ﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land﴾, that is: the purified.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Enter the Holy Land﴾, that he said: "It is al-Tur and what surrounds it." Mujahid and others said the same.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Sa'id al-Baqqal, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "It is Jericho (Ariha)." Similarly, more than one of the exegetes mentioned this.

But this is open to scrutiny, because Jericho was not the intended land for conquest, nor was it on their route to Bayt al-Maqdis, and they had come from the land of Egypt, after God had destroyed their enemy Pharaoh. Unless "Jericho" is meant as the land of Bayt al-Maqdis, as al-Suddi said, in what Ibn Jarir narrated from him, not that the intended meaning is this well-known town at the edge of the Ghawr east of Bayt al-Maqdis.

* *

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿which God has prescribed for you﴾, that is: which God promised you through the tongue of your forefather Isra'il (Israel), that it is an inheritance [manuscript A: "He inherited it"] for whoever among you believes. ﴿And do not turn back on your heels, for you will turn back as losers﴾, that is: do not shrink back from jihad. ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed in it are a people of tyrants, and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. And if they leave it, then indeed we will enter."﴾ [Manuscript R reads: "and indeed we will never enter it as long as they remain in it," which is an error.] That is: they made an excuse that in this town, which you commanded us to enter and to fight its people, there are tyrannical people, that is, those of frightful appearance and mighty strength, and that we are not able to withstand them or to contend with them, and we cannot enter it as long as they are in it. If they leave it, we will enter it [manuscript A: "from it, then we will enter"]; otherwise we have no power against them.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id [manuscript R: "Abu Sa'd"] said, Ikrimah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Musa was commanded to enter the city of the tyrants. He said: So Musa set out with those who were with him until he camped near the city, which was Jericho, and he sent to them twelve spies, one from each tribe, to bring him news of the people. He said: They entered the city and saw a great matter of their appearance, their bodies and their size. They entered an orchard belonging to one of them, and the owner of the orchard came to pick fruit from his orchard, and he began picking fruit and looking at their traces, and he followed them. Whenever he caught one of them, he took him and put him in his sleeve along with the fruit, until all twelve were gathered, and he put them in his sleeve with the fruit, and he went to their king and scattered them before him. The king said to them: You have seen our state and our affair, so go and inform your companion. He said: So they returned to Musa and informed him of what they had seen of their affair.

There is an open question concerning this chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/173).]

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: When Musa and his people camped, he sent from among them twelve men [manuscript A: "a leader (naqib)"], who are the nuqaba' (chiefs) whom God mentioned, and he sent them to bring him news of them. They set out, and a man from the tyrants met them, and he put them in his cloak, carried them until he brought them to the city, and called out to his people, and they gathered to him. They said: "Who are you?" They said: "We are the people of Musa; he sent us to come to him with news of you." So they gave them a grape, one grape sufficient for a man, and they said to them: "Go to Musa and his people and say to them: 'Measure the measure of your fruit.'" When they came to them, they said: "O Musa, ﴿so go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here.﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Had, Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: I saw Anas ibn Malik take a staff, and he measured with it something, I do not know how much he measured, then he measured the earth with it fifty or fifty-five [manuscript A: "fifty-five"] times, then he said: "Thus is the length of the 'Amaliqah."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah, verses 20–26 (Part 2 of 3)

Many of the exegetes have mentioned here reports originating from the Children of Israel (isra'iliyyat), concerning the great stature of these tyrants, and that among them was 'Awj ibn 'Unuq, a daughter of Adam (ﷺ)... [the text reads: "'Awj ibn 'Unuq, bint Adam, 'alayhi al-salam"], and that his height was three thousand, three hundred and thirty-three and a third cubits, a precise calculation! And this is something one is ashamed to mention. Moreover, it contradicts what is established in the Sahih [in D and A: "al-Sahihayn"] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah (Exalted) created Adam, and his height was sixty cubits. Then creation continued to decrease until now." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3326, and by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2841, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Then they have mentioned that this man was a disbeliever, that he was an illegitimate child, that he refused to board the ship, and that the flood did not reach his knees [in R and A: "his knees"]. This is a lie and a fabrication. Allah mentioned that Nuh prayed against the disbelievers of the earth, saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers as a dweller﴾ [Nuh: 26]. Allah (Exalted) also said: ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship; then We drowned the remaining ones﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 119–120]. And Allah (Exalted) said: ﴿There is no protector today from the command of Allah, except for whom He has mercy﴾ [Hud: 43]. If the disbelieving son of Nuh drowned, how could 'Awj ibn 'Unuq survive, when he was a disbeliever and an illegitimate child?! This is not acceptable to reason or to the Shari'ah. Moreover, the existence of a man called "'Awj ibn 'Unuq" is open to question, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Two men from among those who feared, upon whom Allah had bestowed favour, said﴾ means: when the Children of Israel shrank back from obeying Allah and following the Messenger of Allah, Musa (ʿalayhi al-salam), two men, upon whom Allah had bestowed a great blessing, urged them on. They were among those who feared the command of Allah and dreaded His punishment.

Some of them recited: ﴿Two men from among those who are feared﴾, meaning: among those who had dignity and standing among the people. It is said that the two were "Yusha' ibn Nun" and "Kalib ibn Yufuna". This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Atiyyah, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others among the earlier and later scholars, may Allah have mercy on them. They said: ﴿Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will surely be victorious. And upon Allah rely, if you are believers﴾, meaning: whenever you rely upon Allah, follow His command, and agree with His Messenger, Allah will grant you victory over your enemies, support you, make you triumph over them, and you will enter the land which Allah has decreed for you. But that did not benefit them at all. ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here."﴾ This was a refusal on their part to engage in jihad, an opposition to their Messenger, and a failure to fight the enemies.

It is said that when they refused to engage in jihad and resolved to turn back and return to their lands, Musa and Harun, upon them be peace, prostrated in front of a gathering of the Children of Israel, out of magnifying what they had resolved upon. Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalib ibn Yufuna tore their garments and rebuked their people for this. It is said that they stoned them. A great matter occurred and a grave danger arose.

How excellent was the answer given by the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all [in A: "may Allah be pleased with them all"], on the Day of Badr, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consulted them concerning fighting the army (al-nafir) that had come to protect the caravan (al-'ir) which was with Abu Sufyan. When the caravan had escaped their grasp, and the army drew near to them, and he resolved to fight a force of between nine hundred and a thousand, equipped with weapons, armour and gear, Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, spoke and spoke well. Then some of the Companions from the Muhajirun spoke, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was saying: "Advise me, O Muslims." He only said this to learn what the Ansar had to say, because they were the majority of the people at that time. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It seems you are referring to us, O Messenger of Allah. By the One who sent you with the truth, if you were to lead us into this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge in with you, and not one man among us would stay behind. We do not dislike that you should meet our enemy with us tomorrow. Indeed, we are patient in war and truthful in encounters. Perhaps Allah will show you from us what will please your eyes. So march with us in the blessing of Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delighted by the words of Sa'd, and it energized him. [See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/615).]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us from Anas, that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for Badr, he consulted the Muslims. 'Umar gestured toward him [i.e., signalled his support]. Then he consulted them again, and the Ansar said: "O assembly of the Ansar, it is you whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intends!" They said: "Then we will not say to him what the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. By the One who sent you with the truth, even if you were to drive your mounts to Bark al-Ghimad [a distant place], we would follow you."

Ahmad also narrated it, from 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas, with the same wording. Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Khalid ibn al-Harith, from Humayd, with the same. Ibn Hibban narrated it from Abu Ya'la, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman, from Humayd, with the same. [Al-Musnad (3/105), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11141, and Musnad Abi Ya'la al-Mawsili (6/407).]

Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far informed us, Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah informed us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, from al-Hasan [in A: "al-Hakam", and the established reading is from al-Jarh] ibn Ayyub, from 'Abd Allah ibn Nasikh, from 'Utbah ibn 'Abd al-Sulami who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his Companions: "Will you not fight?" They said: "Yes, and we will not say as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting alongside you both." [Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (4/183) through the chain of al-Hasan ibn Ayyub.]

Among those who responded that day was al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr al-Kindi, may Allah be pleased with him, as Imam Ahmad said:

Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Mukhariq ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ahmasi, from Tariq, that is Ibn Shihab: that al-Miqdad said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the Day of Badr: "O Messenger of Allah, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting alongside you both."

Thus Ahmad narrated it through this route. He also narrated it through another route, saying:

Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Mukhariq, from Tariq ibn Shihab who said: 'Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I witnessed from al-Miqdad a stance which I would rather be his companion in than have anything else compared to it. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was supplicating against the polytheists, and said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we will not say as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, we will fight on your right and on your left, before you and behind you.' I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brighten at that, and he was pleased by it." [Al-Musnad (1/389).]

Likewise, al-Bukhari narrated it in "al-Maghazi" and in "al-Tafsir" through several routes from Mukhariq, with the same. Its wording in "Kitab al-Tafsir" from 'Abd Allah is: He said: Al-Miqdad said on the Day of Badr: "O Messenger of Allah, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather [in A: "and we"], [we say] go on, and we are with you." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved [as if relieved of his anxiety]. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 3952, 4609.]

Then al-Bukhari said: Waki' narrated it from Sufyan, from Mukhariq, from Tariq: that al-Miqdad said to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah who said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his Companions on the Day of al-Hudaybiyyah, when the polytheists blocked the offering animals and they were prevented from their rites: "I am going with the offering animals, and I will slaughter them at the House." Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said to him: "By Allah, we will not be like the assembly of the Children of Israel when they said to their Prophet: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting with you." When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard it, they pledged allegiance upon that. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/186).]

And this: if it is preserved as having occurred at al-Hudaybiyyah, then it is possible that he repeated this statement on that day just as he had said it on the Day of Badr.

* *

His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have no control except over myself and my brother, so part us from the defiant people."﴾ means: when the Children of Israel shrank back from fighting, Musa, upon him be peace, became angry with them and said, supplicating against them: ﴿My Lord, indeed I have no control except over myself and my brother﴾, meaning: there is no one among them who obeys me, complies with the command of Allah, and responds to what I have called them to, except myself and my brother Harun. ﴿So part us from the defiant people﴾. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it means "judge between us and them." Ali ibn Abi Talhah also said this from Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise al-Dahhak said: "Judge between us and them, and open [the matter] between us and them." Others said: "Furq" means: separate between us and them, as the poet said:

"O Lord, then separate him and me
with the sharpest of separations between two..."

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿[He said], "Indeed, it is forbidden for them for forty years; they will wander in the land. So do not grieve over the defiant people."﴾ When Musa, upon him be peace, supplicated against them when they shrank back from jihad, Allah decreed against them that they be forbidden from entering it for a period of forty years. They fell into the wandering (al-tih), continually traveling without being guided to the way out of it. In this period there occurred wondrous events and many extraordinary signs: among them, the shading of them with clouds, the sending down of manna and quails upon them, and the bringing forth of flowing water from a hard rock which was carried with them on a beast; when Musa struck it with his staff, twelve springs gushed forth from that rock, each tribe having its own spring, along with other miracles with which Allah supported Musa ibn 'Imran. There the Torah was sent down, the laws were prescribed for them, and the Tent of the Covenant was made, which is also called the "Dome of Time."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 3 of 3):

Yazid ibn Harun said, from Asbagh ibn Zayd [[In R and A: "Yazid".]], from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: I asked Ibn Abbas about His saying: ﴿Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land﴾ [[In R and H: "Inna-ha" (إنها); the correct reading is what we have adopted.]] and the rest of the verse. He said: They wandered in the land for forty years. Each morning they would travel, having no place of settlement. Then the clouds were made to shade them in the wilderness, and manna and quails were sent down upon them. This is a portion of the hadith of "al-Futun" (the Trials). Then Harun, peace be upon him, died. After him, three years later, Musa al-Kalim (Moses, the one who spoke with God), peace be upon him, died. God appointed among them "Yusha' ibn Nun" (Joshua son of Nun), peace be upon him, as a prophet and successor to Musa ibn Imran. Most of the Children of Israel died there during that period. It is said that none of them remained except "Yusha'" and "Kalib" (Caleb). It is from here that some of the commentators (mufassirun, scholars of Qur'anic exegesis) said, regarding His saying ﴿He said: "Then it is forbidden to them"﴾, that this is a complete pause, and His saying ﴿for forty years﴾ is governed by His saying ﴿they will wander in the land﴾. When the period ended, Yusha' ibn Nun, peace be upon him, led them out, or led those who remained of them and the rest of the Children of Israel of the second generation. He headed with them to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and besieged it. Its conquest occurred on Friday after the afternoon prayer. When the sun began to set and he feared that the Sabbath would begin upon them, he said: "You are commanded and I am commanded. O God, hold it back for me." God Most High held it back until he conquered it. God commanded Yusha' ibn Nun to order the Children of Israel, when they entered Bayt al-Maqdis, to enter its gate prostrating while saying: "Hittah" (a request for remission), meaning: "Remove our sins from us." But they changed what they had been commanded, and they entered crawling on their buttocks, saying: "A grain in a hair." All of this has already been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Umar al-Adani related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Abu Sa'id, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land﴾. He said: They wandered for forty years. Musa and Harun died in the wilderness, along with everyone who had passed forty years of age. When the forty years had passed, Yusha' ibn Nun rose up with them. He was the one who took charge of the affair after Musa, and he was the one who conquered it. He was the one to whom it was said: "Today is Friday." They resolved to conquer it, and the sun drew near to setting. He feared that if the night of Saturday came, they would be unable to work, so he called out to the sun: "I am commanded and you are commanded," and it stood still until he conquered it. He found in it wealth the like of which had never been seen. They brought it near the fire, but it did not come. He said: "There is embezzlement (ghulul) among you." He summoned the heads of the tribes, who were twelve men, and gave them his pledge. The hand of one man of them stuck to his hand. He said: "The embezzlement is with you." So he brought it out, and it was the head of a calf of gold, with two eyes of ruby and teeth of pearl. He placed it with the offerings, and the fire came and consumed it.

This narration has a witness in the Sahih. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose that His saying ﴿Then it is forbidden to them﴾ is the governing element for ﴿forty years﴾, and that they remained, not entering it for forty years, while they were wandering in the desert, not guided to any destination. He said: Then they went out with Musa, peace be upon him, and he conquered Bayt al-Maqdis with them. Then he argued for this, saying: By the consensus of the scholars of the reports of the earlier peoples, that Awj ibn Anaq was killed by Musa, peace be upon him. He said: If his killing had occurred before the wandering, the Children of Israel would not have feared the Amalekites. This shows that it occurred after the wandering. He said: And they agreed that Bal'am ibn Ba'ura aided the tyrants by invoking curses against Musa. He said: That was only after the wandering, because before the wandering they did not fear Musa and his people. This is his line of reasoning. Then he said:

Abu Kurayb related to us, Ibn Atiyyah related to us, Qays related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The staff of Musa was ten cubits long, his leap was ten cubits, and his height was ten cubits. He leapt and struck the ankle of Awj and killed him, and his body became a bridge for the people of the Nile for a year [[In A: "years".]].

It is also narrated from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, who related to us from Mu'ammal, who related to us from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf al-Bikali, who said: The bed of Awj was eight hundred [[In R and A: "three hundred".]] cubits long. Musa's height was ten cubits, and his staff was ten cubits. He leapt into the sky ten cubits and struck Awj, hitting his ankle, and he fell dead. His body was a bridge that people passed over. [[The narration of Awj ibn Anaq is a long, false report. Nothing that is mentioned about his descriptions is authentic. Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may God have mercy on him, discussed it sufficiently in al-Manar al-Munif (p. 76).]]

* *

His Most High saying: ﴿So do not grieve over the defiant people﴾ is a consolation to Musa, peace be upon him, concerning them. That is: do not be distressed or saddened over them; whatever you decree against them, they deserve it.

This story contains a rebuke of the Jews, an exposure of their disgrace, their opposition to God and His Messenger, and their refusal to obey them in what they were commanded regarding jihad. Their souls were too weak to endure and wrestle with the enemies and fight them, even though the Messenger of God ﷺ, His interlocutor and chosen one from among His creation in that time, was among them, promising them victory and triumph over their enemies. Moreover, they had witnessed what God had brought down upon their enemy Pharaoh of punishment, retribution, and drowning for him and his soldiers in the sea, while they were watching so that their eyes would be comforted, and it was not long ago. Then they recoiled from fighting the people of a city which, compared to the lands of Egypt, does not equal a tenth of a tenth in the number of its people and its troops. Thus the ugliness of their conduct became apparent to the elite and the common alike, and they were disgraced with a disgrace that neither night can cover nor a cloak can conceal. Yet they remained in their ignorance, wandering blindly, and hesitating in their error. They are the most hateful to God and His enemies, yet they still say: ﴿We are the children of God and His beloved﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 18]. So may God disfigure their faces, from which He transformed them into swine and apes, and bind them with a curse that accompanies them into the blazing Fire, where they will be decreed eternal abiding forever. He has done so, and to Him belongs praise from all of existence.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 1 of 3):

God, exalted is He, says, telling of His servant, messenger and interlocutor Musa (Moses) son of 'Imran, peace be upon him, in what he reminded his people of, the blessings of God upon them and His favours toward them, in that He gathered for them the good of this world and the Hereafter, if they remained upright on their straight path. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when Musa said to his people: "O my people, remember the favour of God upon you when He appointed prophets among you﴾. That is: whenever a prophet died, another prophet arose among you, from your forefather Ibrahim (Abraham) onward and after him. [In manuscript A: "wa-lidhalika" (and therefore).] Thus they were: prophets never ceased among them, calling to God and warning of His vengeance, until they were concluded with 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him. Then God [exalted] [addition from manuscript R] revealed to the Seal of the Messengers and Prophets, absolutely, Muhammad son of 'Abdullah, who is traced to Isma'il son of Ibrahim, [manuscript A: "upon them both"] peace be upon him, and he is more noble than every one of them who preceded him, ﷺ.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from al-Thawri, from Mansur, from al-Hakam or another, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾, that he said: "The servant, the wife and the house."

Al-Hakim also narrated in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of al-Thawri as well, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The wife and the servant." ﴿And He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾, he said: "Those who were among them at that time." Then al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhari and Muslim]" [manuscript D: "according to their condition"], but they did not record it. [Al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/311, 312).]

Maymun ibn Mihran said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "A man from the Children of Israel, if he had a wife, a servant and a house, was called a king."

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Hani' informed us, that he heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli say: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, and a man asked him, saying: "Are we not [manuscript R: "Are you not"; manuscript D: "I am one of the poor"] among the poor Emigrants?" 'Abdullah said: "Do you have a wife to whom you retire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you have a dwelling in which you live?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are among the rich." He said: "I have a servant." [Manuscript A: "Then he said."] He said: "Then you are among the kings." [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/163).]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Is kingship anything but a mount, a servant and a house?"

Ibn Jarir narrated it. Then it was related from Mansur, al-Hakam, Mujahid and Sufyan al-Thawri something similar to this. Ibn Abi Hatim also related it from Maymun ibn Mihran.

Ibn Shawdhab said: "A man from the Children of Israel, if he had a dwelling and a servant, and he was asked permission to enter upon him, then he was a king."

Qatadah said: "They were the first to possess servants as property [literally: to own servants]."

al-Suddi said regarding His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾: "A man among you possesses his own self, his family and his wealth." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Ibn Lahi'a, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "When one of the Children of Israel had a servant, a beast of burden and a wife, he was recorded as a king." [Within its chain are Ibn Lahi'a and Darraj, both weak, and Darraj's narration from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

And this is a strange (gharib) hadith from this route.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar narrated to us, Abu Dhamrah Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, [he said] [addition from manuscript A] I heard Zayd ibn Aslam say: ﴿and He made you kings﴾, then I know of nothing except that he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever has a house and a servant, he is a king."

This is a mursal (a report whose chain omits the Companion) and strange. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/161).] Malik said: "A house, a servant and a wife."

It has come in a hadith: "Whoever among you wakes up healthy in his body, secure in his dwelling, having the sustenance of his day, it is as if the whole world has been gathered for him." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (2346), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (4141), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mihsan al-Ansari.]

* *

And His saying: ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾. He means the worlds of your time. So they were the most noble of people in their time, among the Greeks, the Copts and all other kinds of the children of Adam, as He said: ﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Scripture and judgement and prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 16]. And God, exalted is He, said, reporting about Musa when they said: ﴿Make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. Indeed, these — what they are in is destroyed, and worthless is what they have been doing." He said, "Is it other than God I should seek for you as a god while He has preferred you over the worlds?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 138–140].

The intended meaning is that they were the best people of their time. Otherwise, this community (ummah) is more noble than them, more excellent before God, more complete in law, more upright in method, more honoured in prophet, greater in dominion, more abundant in provisions, greater in wealth and offspring, more extensive in realm, and more lasting in honour. God [exalted and majestic] [addition from manuscript R; manuscript A: "exalted"] said: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110], and He said: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. We have mentioned the mutawatir hadiths concerning the excellence, nobility and honour of this community before God, at His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ in the surah of Al 'Imran.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that they said regarding His saying: ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾, that it means: the community of Muhammad ﷺ. It seems they intended that this address in His saying ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾ is together with this community. The majority hold that it is an address from Musa to his people, and it is to be understood as the worlds of their time, as we have previously mentioned.

It was also said: The meaning of ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾ is: what He sent down to them of manna and quails, and what He shaded them with of clouds, and other things, of the extraordinary matters (khawariq al-'adat) with which God specifically favoured them. And God knows best.

Then God, exalted is He, said, reporting about the urging by Musa, peace be upon him, of the Children of Israel to jihad and to entering Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), which had been in their hands in the time of their forefather Ya'qub (Jacob), when he, his sons and his family migrated to the land of Egypt in the days of Yusuf, peace be upon him. Then they remained there until they went out with Musa [peace be upon him] [addition from manuscript A], and they found therein a people of the 'Amaliqah, the tyrannical giants, who had seized it and taken possession of it. So the Messenger of God, Musa, peace be upon him, commanded them to enter it and to fight their enemies, and gave them the good news of victory and triumph over them. But they shrank back, disobeyed and opposed his command, so they were punished by wandering in the wilderness (al-tih) and persisting in their journey bewildered, not knowing how to head toward a destination in it, for a period of forty years, as a punishment for them for their neglect of the command of God [exalted] [addition from manuscript A]. God, exalted is He, said, reporting about Musa that he said: ﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land﴾, that is: the purified.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Enter the Holy Land﴾, that he said: "It is al-Tur and what surrounds it." Mujahid and others said the same.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Sa'id al-Baqqal, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "It is Jericho (Ariha)." Similarly, more than one of the exegetes mentioned this.

But this is open to scrutiny, because Jericho was not the intended land for conquest, nor was it on their route to Bayt al-Maqdis, and they had come from the land of Egypt, after God had destroyed their enemy Pharaoh. Unless "Jericho" is meant as the land of Bayt al-Maqdis, as al-Suddi said, in what Ibn Jarir narrated from him, not that the intended meaning is this well-known town at the edge of the Ghawr east of Bayt al-Maqdis.

* *

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿which God has prescribed for you﴾, that is: which God promised you through the tongue of your forefather Isra'il (Israel), that it is an inheritance [manuscript A: "He inherited it"] for whoever among you believes. ﴿And do not turn back on your heels, for you will turn back as losers﴾, that is: do not shrink back from jihad. ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed in it are a people of tyrants, and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. And if they leave it, then indeed we will enter."﴾ [Manuscript R reads: "and indeed we will never enter it as long as they remain in it," which is an error.] That is: they made an excuse that in this town, which you commanded us to enter and to fight its people, there are tyrannical people, that is, those of frightful appearance and mighty strength, and that we are not able to withstand them or to contend with them, and we cannot enter it as long as they are in it. If they leave it, we will enter it [manuscript A: "from it, then we will enter"]; otherwise we have no power against them.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id [manuscript R: "Abu Sa'd"] said, Ikrimah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Musa was commanded to enter the city of the tyrants. He said: So Musa set out with those who were with him until he camped near the city, which was Jericho, and he sent to them twelve spies, one from each tribe, to bring him news of the people. He said: They entered the city and saw a great matter of their appearance, their bodies and their size. They entered an orchard belonging to one of them, and the owner of the orchard came to pick fruit from his orchard, and he began picking fruit and looking at their traces, and he followed them. Whenever he caught one of them, he took him and put him in his sleeve along with the fruit, until all twelve were gathered, and he put them in his sleeve with the fruit, and he went to their king and scattered them before him. The king said to them: You have seen our state and our affair, so go and inform your companion. He said: So they returned to Musa and informed him of what they had seen of their affair.

There is an open question concerning this chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/173).]

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: When Musa and his people camped, he sent from among them twelve men [manuscript A: "a leader (naqib)"], who are the nuqaba' (chiefs) whom God mentioned, and he sent them to bring him news of them. They set out, and a man from the tyrants met them, and he put them in his cloak, carried them until he brought them to the city, and called out to his people, and they gathered to him. They said: "Who are you?" They said: "We are the people of Musa; he sent us to come to him with news of you." So they gave them a grape, one grape sufficient for a man, and they said to them: "Go to Musa and his people and say to them: 'Measure the measure of your fruit.'" When they came to them, they said: "O Musa, ﴿so go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here.﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Had, Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: I saw Anas ibn Malik take a staff, and he measured with it something, I do not know how much he measured, then he measured the earth with it fifty or fifty-five [manuscript A: "fifty-five"] times, then he said: "Thus is the length of the 'Amaliqah."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah, verses 20–26 (Part 2 of 3)

Many of the exegetes have mentioned here reports originating from the Children of Israel (isra'iliyyat), concerning the great stature of these tyrants, and that among them was 'Awj ibn 'Unuq, a daughter of Adam (ﷺ)... [the text reads: "'Awj ibn 'Unuq, bint Adam, 'alayhi al-salam"], and that his height was three thousand, three hundred and thirty-three and a third cubits, a precise calculation! And this is something one is ashamed to mention. Moreover, it contradicts what is established in the Sahih [in D and A: "al-Sahihayn"] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah (Exalted) created Adam, and his height was sixty cubits.
