Then he argued for this, saying: By the consensus of the scholars of the reports of the earlier peoples, that Awj ibn Anaq was killed by Musa, peace be upon him. He said: If his killing had occurred before the wandering, the Children of Israel would not have feared the Amalekites. This shows that it occurred after the wandering. He said: And they agreed that Bal'am ibn Ba'ura aided the tyrants by invoking curses against Musa. He said: That was only after the wandering, because before the wandering they did not fear Musa and his people. This is his line of reasoning. Then he said:

Abu Kurayb related to us, Ibn Atiyyah related to us, Qays related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The staff of Musa was ten cubits long, his leap was ten cubits, and his height was ten cubits. He leapt and struck the ankle of Awj and killed him, and his body became a bridge for the people of the Nile for a year [[In A: "years".]].

It is also narrated from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, who related to us from Mu'ammal, who related to us from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf al-Bikali, who said: The bed of Awj was eight hundred [[In R and A: "three hundred".]] cubits long. Musa's height was ten cubits, and his staff was ten cubits. He leapt into the sky ten cubits and struck Awj, hitting his ankle, and he fell dead. His body was a bridge that people passed over. [[The narration of Awj ibn Anaq is a long, false report. Nothing that is mentioned about his descriptions is authentic. Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may God have mercy on him, discussed it sufficiently in al-Manar al-Munif (p. 76).]]

* *

His Most High saying: ﴿So do not grieve over the defiant people﴾ is a consolation to Musa, peace be upon him, concerning them. That is: do not be distressed or saddened over them; whatever you decree against them, they deserve it.

This story contains a rebuke of the Jews, an exposure of their disgrace, their opposition to God and His Messenger, and their refusal to obey them in what they were commanded regarding jihad. Their souls were too weak to endure and wrestle with the enemies and fight them, even though the Messenger of God ﷺ, His interlocutor and chosen one from among His creation in that time, was among them, promising them victory and triumph over their enemies. Moreover, they had witnessed what God had brought down upon their enemy Pharaoh of punishment, retribution, and drowning for him and his soldiers in the sea, while they were watching so that their eyes would be comforted, and it was not long ago. Then they recoiled from fighting the people of a city which, compared to the lands of Egypt, does not equal a tenth of a tenth in the number of its people and its troops. Thus the ugliness of their conduct became apparent to the elite and the common alike, and they were disgraced with a disgrace that neither night can cover nor a cloak can conceal. Yet they remained in their ignorance, wandering blindly, and hesitating in their error. They are the most hateful to God and His enemies, yet they still say: ﴿We are the children of God and His beloved﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 18]. So may God disfigure their faces, from which He transformed them into swine and apes, and bind them with a curse that accompanies them into the blazing Fire, where they will be decreed eternal abiding forever. He has done so, and to Him belongs praise from all of existence.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 1 of 3):

God, exalted is He, says, telling of His servant, messenger and interlocutor Musa (Moses) son of 'Imran, peace be upon him, in what he reminded his people of, the blessings of God upon them and His favours toward them, in that He gathered for them the good of this world and the Hereafter, if they remained upright on their straight path. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when Musa said to his people: "O my people, remember the favour of God upon you when He appointed prophets among you﴾. That is: whenever a prophet died, another prophet arose among you, from your forefather Ibrahim (Abraham) onward and after him. [In manuscript A: "wa-lidhalika" (and therefore).] Thus they were: prophets never ceased among them, calling to God and warning of His vengeance, until they were concluded with 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him. Then God [exalted] [addition from manuscript R] revealed to the Seal of the Messengers and Prophets, absolutely, Muhammad son of 'Abdullah, who is traced to Isma'il son of Ibrahim, [manuscript A: "upon them both"] peace be upon him, and he is more noble than every one of them who preceded him, ﷺ.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from al-Thawri, from Mansur, from al-Hakam or another, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾, that he said: "The servant, the wife and the house."

Al-Hakim also narrated in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of al-Thawri as well, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The wife and the servant." ﴿And He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾, he said: "Those who were among them at that time." Then al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhari and Muslim]" [manuscript D: "according to their condition"], but they did not record it. [Al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/311, 312).]

Maymun ibn Mihran said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "A man from the Children of Israel, if he had a wife, a servant and a house, was called a king."

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Hani' informed us, that he heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli say: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, and a man asked him, saying: "Are we not [manuscript R: "Are you not"; manuscript D: "I am one of the poor"] among the poor Emigrants?" 'Abdullah said: "Do you have a wife to whom you retire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you have a dwelling in which you live?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are among the rich." He said: "I have a servant." [Manuscript A: "Then he said."] He said: "Then you are among the kings." [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/163).]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Is kingship anything but a mount, a servant and a house?"

Ibn Jarir narrated it. Then it was related from Mansur, al-Hakam, Mujahid and Sufyan al-Thawri something similar to this. Ibn Abi Hatim also related it from Maymun ibn Mihran.

Ibn Shawdhab said: "A man from the Children of Israel, if he had a dwelling and a servant, and he was asked permission to enter upon him, then he was a king."

Qatadah said: "They were the first to possess servants as property [literally: to own servants]."

al-Suddi said regarding His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾: "A man among you possesses his own self, his family and his wealth." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Ibn Lahi'a, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "When one of the Children of Israel had a servant, a beast of burden and a wife, he was recorded as a king." [Within its chain are Ibn Lahi'a and Darraj, both weak, and Darraj's narration from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

And this is a strange (gharib) hadith from this route.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar narrated to us, Abu Dhamrah Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, [he said] [addition from manuscript A] I heard Zayd ibn Aslam say: ﴿and He made you kings﴾, then I know of nothing except that he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever has a house and a servant, he is a king."

This is a mursal (a report whose chain omits the Companion) and strange. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/161).] Malik said: "A house, a servant and a wife."

It has come in a hadith: "Whoever among you wakes up healthy in his body, secure in his dwelling, having the sustenance of his day, it is as if the whole world has been gathered for him." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (2346), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (4141), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mihsan al-Ansari.]

* *

And His saying: ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾. He means the worlds of your time. So they were the most noble of people in their time, among the Greeks, the Copts and all other kinds of the children of Adam, as He said: ﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Scripture and judgement and prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 16]. And God, exalted is He, said, reporting about Musa when they said: ﴿Make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. Indeed, these — what they are in is destroyed, and worthless is what they have been doing." He said, "Is it other than God I should seek for you as a god while He has preferred you over the worlds?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 138–140].

The intended meaning is that they were the best people of their time. Otherwise, this community (ummah) is more noble than them, more excellent before God, more complete in law, more upright in method, more honoured in prophet, greater in dominion, more abundant in provisions, greater in wealth and offspring, more extensive in realm, and more lasting in honour. God [exalted and majestic] [addition from manuscript R; manuscript A: "exalted"] said: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110], and He said: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. We have mentioned the mutawatir hadiths concerning the excellence, nobility and honour of this community before God, at His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ in the surah of Al 'Imran.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that they said regarding His saying: ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾, that it means: the community of Muhammad ﷺ. It seems they intended that this address in His saying ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾ is together with this community. The majority hold that it is an address from Musa to his people, and it is to be understood as the worlds of their time, as we have previously mentioned.

It was also said: The meaning of ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾ is: what He sent down to them of manna and quails, and what He shaded them with of clouds, and other things, of the extraordinary matters (khawariq al-'adat) with which God specifically favoured them. And God knows best.

Then God, exalted is He, said, reporting about the urging by Musa, peace be upon him, of the Children of Israel to jihad and to entering Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), which had been in their hands in the time of their forefather Ya'qub (Jacob), when he, his sons and his family migrated to the land of Egypt in the days of Yusuf, peace be upon him. Then they remained there until they went out with Musa [peace be upon him] [addition from manuscript A], and they found therein a people of the 'Amaliqah, the tyrannical giants, who had seized it and taken possession of it. So the Messenger of God, Musa, peace be upon him, commanded them to enter it and to fight their enemies, and gave them the good news of victory and triumph over them. But they shrank back, disobeyed and opposed his command, so they were punished by wandering in the wilderness (al-tih) and persisting in their journey bewildered, not knowing how to head toward a destination in it, for a period of forty years, as a punishment for them for their neglect of the command of God [exalted] [addition from manuscript A]. God, exalted is He, said, reporting about Musa that he said: ﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land﴾, that is: the purified.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Enter the Holy Land﴾, that he said: "It is al-Tur and what surrounds it." Mujahid and others said the same.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Sa'id al-Baqqal, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "It is Jericho (Ariha)." Similarly, more than one of the exegetes mentioned this.

But this is open to scrutiny, because Jericho was not the intended land for conquest, nor was it on their route to Bayt al-Maqdis, and they had come from the land of Egypt, after God had destroyed their enemy Pharaoh. Unless "Jericho" is meant as the land of Bayt al-Maqdis, as al-Suddi said, in what Ibn Jarir narrated from him, not that the intended meaning is this well-known town at the edge of the Ghawr east of Bayt al-Maqdis.

* *

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿which God has prescribed for you﴾, that is: which God promised you through the tongue of your forefather Isra'il (Israel), that it is an inheritance [manuscript A: "He inherited it"] for whoever among you believes. ﴿And do not turn back on your heels, for you will turn back as losers﴾, that is: do not shrink back from jihad. ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed in it are a people of tyrants, and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. And if they leave it, then indeed we will enter."﴾ [Manuscript R reads: "and indeed we will never enter it as long as they remain in it," which is an error.] That is: they made an excuse that in this town, which you commanded us to enter and to fight its people, there are tyrannical people, that is, those of frightful appearance and mighty strength, and that we are not able to withstand them or to contend with them, and we cannot enter it as long as they are in it. If they leave it, we will enter it [manuscript A: "from it, then we will enter"]; otherwise we have no power against them.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id [manuscript R: "Abu Sa'd"] said, Ikrimah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Musa was commanded to enter the city of the tyrants. He said: So Musa set out with those who were with him until he camped near the city, which was Jericho, and he sent to them twelve spies, one from each tribe, to bring him news of the people. He said: They entered the city and saw a great matter of their appearance, their bodies and their size. They entered an orchard belonging to one of them, and the owner of the orchard came to pick fruit from his orchard, and he began picking fruit and looking at their traces, and he followed them. Whenever he caught one of them, he took him and put him in his sleeve along with the fruit, until all twelve were gathered, and he put them in his sleeve with the fruit, and he went to their king and scattered them before him. The king said to them: You have seen our state and our affair, so go and inform your companion. He said: So they returned to Musa and informed him of what they had seen of their affair.

There is an open question concerning this chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/173).]

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: When Musa and his people camped, he sent from among them twelve men [manuscript A: "a leader (naqib)"], who are the nuqaba' (chiefs) whom God mentioned, and he sent them to bring him news of them. They set out, and a man from the tyrants met them, and he put them in his cloak, carried them until he brought them to the city, and called out to his people, and they gathered to him. They said: "Who are you?" They said: "We are the people of Musa; he sent us to come to him with news of you." So they gave them a grape, one grape sufficient for a man, and they said to them: "Go to Musa and his people and say to them: 'Measure the measure of your fruit.'" When they came to them, they said: "O Musa, ﴿so go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here.﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Had, Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: I saw Anas ibn Malik take a staff, and he measured with it something, I do not know how much he measured, then he measured the earth with it fifty or fifty-five [manuscript A: "fifty-five"] times, then he said: "Thus is the length of the 'Amaliqah."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah, verses 20–26 (Part 2 of 3)

Many of the exegetes have mentioned here reports originating from the Children of Israel (isra'iliyyat), concerning the great stature of these tyrants, and that among them was 'Awj ibn 'Unuq, a daughter of Adam (ﷺ)... [the text reads: "'Awj ibn 'Unuq, bint Adam, 'alayhi al-salam"], and that his height was three thousand, three hundred and thirty-three and a third cubits, a precise calculation! And this is something one is ashamed to mention. Moreover, it contradicts what is established in the Sahih [in D and A: "al-Sahihayn"] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah (Exalted) created Adam, and his height was sixty cubits. Then creation continued to decrease until now." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3326, and by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2841, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Then they have mentioned that this man was a disbeliever, that he was an illegitimate child, that he refused to board the ship, and that the flood did not reach his knees [in R and A: "his knees"]. This is a lie and a fabrication. Allah mentioned that Nuh prayed against the disbelievers of the earth, saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers as a dweller﴾ [Nuh: 26]. Allah (Exalted) also said: ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship; then We drowned the remaining ones﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 119–120]. And Allah (Exalted) said: ﴿There is no protector today from the command of Allah, except for whom He has mercy﴾ [Hud: 43]. If the disbelieving son of Nuh drowned, how could 'Awj ibn 'Unuq survive, when he was a disbeliever and an illegitimate child?! This is not acceptable to reason or to the Shari'ah. Moreover, the existence of a man called "'Awj ibn 'Unuq" is open to question, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Two men from among those who feared, upon whom Allah had bestowed favour, said﴾ means: when the Children of Israel shrank back from obeying Allah and following the Messenger of Allah, Musa (ʿalayhi al-salam), two men, upon whom Allah had bestowed a great blessing, urged them on. They were among those who feared the command of Allah and dreaded His punishment.

Some of them recited: ﴿Two men from among those who are feared﴾, meaning: among those who had dignity and standing among the people. It is said that the two were "Yusha' ibn Nun" and "Kalib ibn Yufuna". This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Atiyyah, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others among the earlier and later scholars, may Allah have mercy on them. They said: ﴿Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will surely be victorious. And upon Allah rely, if you are believers﴾, meaning: whenever you rely upon Allah, follow His command, and agree with His Messenger, Allah will grant you victory over your enemies, support you, make you triumph over them, and you will enter the land which Allah has decreed for you. But that did not benefit them at all. ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here."﴾ This was a refusal on their part to engage in jihad, an opposition to their Messenger, and a failure to fight the enemies.

It is said that when they refused to engage in jihad and resolved to turn back and return to their lands, Musa and Harun, upon them be peace, prostrated in front of a gathering of the Children of Israel, out of magnifying what they had resolved upon. Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalib ibn Yufuna tore their garments and rebuked their people for this. It is said that they stoned them. A great matter occurred and a grave danger arose.

How excellent was the answer given by the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all [in A: "may Allah be pleased with them all"], on the Day of Badr, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consulted them concerning fighting the army (al-nafir) that had come to protect the caravan (al-'ir) which was with Abu Sufyan. When the caravan had escaped their grasp, and the army drew near to them, and he resolved to fight a force of between nine hundred and a thousand, equipped with weapons, armour and gear, Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, spoke and spoke well. Then some of the Companions from the Muhajirun spoke, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was saying: "Advise me, O Muslims." He only said this to learn what the Ansar had to say, because they were the majority of the people at that time. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It seems you are referring to us, O Messenger of Allah. By the One who sent you with the truth, if you were to lead us into this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge in with you, and not one man among us would stay behind. We do not dislike that you should meet our enemy with us tomorrow. Indeed, we are patient in war and truthful in encounters. Perhaps Allah will show you from us what will please your eyes. So march with us in the blessing of Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delighted by the words of Sa'd, and it energized him. [See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/615).]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us from Anas, that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for Badr, he consulted the Muslims. 'Umar gestured toward him [i.e., signalled his support]. Then he consulted them again, and the Ansar said: "O assembly of the Ansar, it is you whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intends!" They said: "Then we will not say to him what the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. By the One who sent you with the truth, even if you were to drive your mounts to Bark al-Ghimad [a distant place], we would follow you."

Ahmad also narrated it, from 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas, with the same wording. Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Khalid ibn al-Harith, from Humayd, with the same. Ibn Hibban narrated it from Abu Ya'la, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman, from Humayd, with the same. [Al-Musnad (3/105), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11141, and Musnad Abi Ya'la al-Mawsili (6/407).]

Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far informed us, Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah informed us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, from al-Hasan [in A: "al-Hakam", and the established reading is from al-Jarh] ibn Ayyub, from 'Abd Allah ibn Nasikh, from 'Utbah ibn 'Abd al-Sulami who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his Companions: "Will you not fight?" They said: "Yes, and we will not say as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting alongside you both." [Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (4/183) through the chain of al-Hasan ibn Ayyub.]

Among those who responded that day was al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr al-Kindi, may Allah be pleased with him, as Imam Ahmad said:

Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Mukhariq ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ahmasi, from Tariq, that is Ibn Shihab: that al-Miqdad said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the Day of Badr: "O Messenger of Allah, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting alongside you both."

Thus Ahmad narrated it through this route. He also narrated it through another route, saying:

Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Mukhariq, from Tariq ibn Shihab who said: 'Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I witnessed from al-Miqdad a stance which I would rather be his companion in than have anything else compared to it. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was supplicating against the polytheists, and said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we will not say as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, we will fight on your right and on your left, before you and behind you.' I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brighten at that, and he was pleased by it." [Al-Musnad (1/389).]

Likewise, al-Bukhari narrated it in "al-Maghazi" and in "al-Tafsir" through several routes from Mukhariq, with the same. Its wording in "Kitab al-Tafsir" from 'Abd Allah is: He said: Al-Miqdad said on the Day of Badr: "O Messenger of Allah, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather [in A: "and we"], [we say] go on, and we are with you." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved [as if relieved of his anxiety]. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 3952, 4609.]

Then al-Bukhari said: Waki' narrated it from Sufyan, from Mukhariq, from Tariq: that al-Miqdad said to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah who said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his Companions on the Day of al-Hudaybiyyah, when the polytheists blocked the offering animals and they were prevented from their rites: "I am going with the offering animals, and I will slaughter them at the House." Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said to him: "By Allah, we will not be like the assembly of the Children of Israel when they said to their Prophet: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting with you." When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard it, they pledged allegiance upon that. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/186).]

And this: if it is preserved as having occurred at al-Hudaybiyyah, then it is possible that he repeated this statement on that day just as he had said it on the Day of Badr.

* *

His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have no control except over myself and my brother, so part us from the defiant people."﴾ means: when the Children of Israel shrank back from fighting, Musa, upon him be peace, became angry with them and said, supplicating against them: ﴿My Lord, indeed I have no control except over myself and my brother﴾, meaning: there is no one among them who obeys me, complies with the command of Allah, and responds to what I have called them to, except myself and my brother Harun. ﴿So part us from the defiant people﴾. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it means "judge between us and them." Ali ibn Abi Talhah also said this from Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise al-Dahhak said: "Judge between us and them, and open [the matter] between us and them." Others said: "Furq" means: separate between us and them, as the poet said:

"O Lord, then separate him and me
with the sharpest of separations between two..."

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿[He said], "Indeed, it is forbidden for them for forty years; they will wander in the land. So do not grieve over the defiant people."﴾ When Musa, upon him be peace, supplicated against them when they shrank back from jihad, Allah decreed against them that they be forbidden from entering it for a period of forty years. They fell into the wandering (al-tih), continually traveling without being guided to the way out of it. In this period there occurred wondrous events and many extraordinary signs: among them, the shading of them with clouds, the sending down of manna and quails upon them, and the bringing forth of flowing water from a hard rock which was carried with them on a beast; when Musa struck it with his staff, twelve springs gushed forth from that rock, each tribe having its own spring, along with other miracles with which Allah supported Musa ibn 'Imran. There the Torah was sent down, the laws were prescribed for them, and the Tent of the Covenant was made, which is also called the "Dome of Time."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 3 of 3):

Yazid ibn Harun said, from Asbagh ibn Zayd [[In R and A: "Yazid".]], from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: I asked Ibn Abbas about His saying: ﴿Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land﴾ [[In R and H: "Inna-ha" (إنها); the correct reading is what we have adopted.]] and the rest of the verse. He said: They wandered in the land for forty years. Each morning they would travel, having no place of settlement. Then the clouds were made to shade them in the wilderness, and manna and quails were sent down upon them. This is a portion of the hadith of "al-Futun" (the Trials). Then Harun, peace be upon him, died. After him, three years later, Musa al-Kalim (Moses, the one who spoke with God), peace be upon him, died. God appointed among them "Yusha' ibn Nun" (Joshua son of Nun), peace be upon him, as a prophet and successor to Musa ibn Imran. Most of the Children of Israel died there during that period. It is said that none of them remained except "Yusha'" and "Kalib" (Caleb). It is from here that some of the commentators (mufassirun, scholars of Qur'anic exegesis) said, regarding His saying ﴿He said: "Then it is forbidden to them"﴾, that this is a complete pause, and His saying ﴿for forty years﴾ is governed by His saying ﴿they will wander in the land﴾. When the period ended, Yusha' ibn Nun, peace be upon him, led them out, or led those who remained of them and the rest of the Children of Israel of the second generation. He headed with them to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and besieged it. Its conquest occurred on Friday after the afternoon prayer. When the sun began to set and he feared that the Sabbath would begin upon them, he said: "You are commanded and I am commanded. O God, hold it back for me." God Most High held it back until he conquered it. God commanded Yusha' ibn Nun to order the Children of Israel, when they entered Bayt al-Maqdis, to enter its gate prostrating while saying: "Hittah" (a request for remission), meaning: "Remove our sins from us." But they changed what they had been commanded, and they entered crawling on their buttocks, saying: "A grain in a hair." All of this has already been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Umar al-Adani related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Abu Sa'id, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land﴾. He said: They wandered for forty years. Musa and Harun died in the wilderness, along with everyone who had passed forty years of age. When the forty years had passed, Yusha' ibn Nun rose up with them. He was the one who took charge of the affair after Musa, and he was the one who conquered it. He was the one to whom it was said: "Today is Friday." They resolved to conquer it, and the sun drew near to setting. He feared that if the night of Saturday came, they would be unable to work, so he called out to the sun: "I am commanded and you are commanded," and it stood still until he conquered it. He found in it wealth the like of which had never been seen. They brought it near the fire, but it did not come. He said: "There is embezzlement (ghulul) among you." He summoned the heads of the tribes, who were twelve men, and gave them his pledge. The hand of one man of them stuck to his hand. He said: "The embezzlement is with you." So he brought it out, and it was the head of a calf of gold, with two eyes of ruby and teeth of pearl. He placed it with the offerings, and the fire came and consumed it.

This narration has a witness in the Sahih. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose that His saying ﴿Then it is forbidden to them﴾ is the governing element for ﴿forty years﴾, and that they remained, not entering it for forty years, while they were wandering in the desert, not guided to any destination. He said: Then they went out with Musa, peace be upon him, and he conquered Bayt al-Maqdis with them. Then he argued for this, saying: By the consensus of the scholars of the reports of the earlier peoples, that Awj ibn Anaq was killed by Musa, peace be upon him. He said: If his killing had occurred before the wandering, the Children of Israel would not have feared the Amalekites. This shows that it occurred after the wandering. He said: And they agreed that Bal'am ibn Ba'ura aided the tyrants by invoking curses against Musa. He said: That was only after the wandering, because before the wandering they did not fear Musa and his people. This is his line of reasoning. Then he said:

Abu Kurayb related to us, Ibn Atiyyah related to us, Qays related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The staff of Musa was ten cubits long, his leap was ten cubits, and his height was ten cubits. He leapt and struck the ankle of Awj and killed him, and his body became a bridge for the people of the Nile for a year [[In A: "years".]].

It is also narrated from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, who related to us from Mu'ammal, who related to us from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf al-Bikali, who said: The bed of Awj was eight hundred [[In R and A: "three hundred".]] cubits long. Musa's height was ten cubits, and his staff was ten cubits. He leapt into the sky ten cubits and struck Awj, hitting his ankle, and he fell dead. His body was a bridge that people passed over. [[The narration of Awj ibn Anaq is a long, false report. Nothing that is mentioned about his descriptions is authentic. Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may God have mercy on him, discussed it sufficiently in al-Manar al-Munif (p. 76).]]

* *

His Most High saying: ﴿So do not grieve over the defiant people﴾ is a consolation to Musa, peace be upon him, concerning them. That is: do not be distressed or saddened over them; whatever you decree against them, they deserve it.

This story contains a rebuke of the Jews, an exposure of their disgrace, their opposition to God and His Messenger, and their refusal to obey them in what they were commanded regarding jihad. Their souls were too weak to endure and wrestle with the enemies and fight them, even though the Messenger of God ﷺ, His interlocutor and chosen one from among His creation in that time, was among them, promising them victory and triumph over their enemies. Moreover, they had witnessed what God had brought down upon their enemy Pharaoh of punishment, retribution, and drowning for him and his soldiers in the sea, while they were watching so that their eyes would be comforted, and it was not long ago. Then they recoiled from fighting the people of a city which, compared to the lands of Egypt, does not equal a tenth of a tenth in the number of its people and its troops. Thus the ugliness of their conduct became apparent to the elite and the common alike, and they were disgraced with a disgrace that neither night can cover nor a cloak can conceal. Yet they remained in their ignorance, wandering blindly, and hesitating in their error. They are the most hateful to God and His enemies, yet they still say: ﴿We are the children of God and His beloved﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 18]. So may God disfigure their faces, from which He transformed them into swine and apes, and bind them with a curse that accompanies them into the blazing Fire, where they will be decreed eternal abiding forever. He has done so, and to Him belongs praise from all of existence.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 1 of 3):

God, exalted is He, says, telling of His servant, messenger and interlocutor Musa (Moses) son of 'Imran, peace be upon him, in what he reminded his people of, the blessings of God upon them and His favours toward them, in that He gathered for them the good of this world and the Hereafter, if they remained upright on their straight path. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when Musa said to his people: "O my people, remember the favour of God upon you when He appointed prophets among you﴾. That is: whenever a prophet died, another prophet arose among you, from your forefather Ibrahim (Abraham) onward and after him. [In manuscript A: "wa-lidhalika" (and therefore).] Thus they were: prophets never ceased among them, calling to God and warning of His vengeance, until they were concluded with 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him. Then God [exalted] [addition from manuscript R] revealed to the Seal of the Messengers and Prophets, absolutely, Muhammad son of 'Abdullah, who is traced to Isma'il son of Ibrahim, [manuscript A: "upon them both"] peace be upon him, and he is more noble than every one of them who preceded him, ﷺ.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from al-Thawri, from Mansur, from al-Hakam or another, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾, that he said: "The servant, the wife and the house."

Al-Hakim also narrated in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of al-Thawri as well, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The wife and the servant." ﴿And He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾, he said: "Those who were among them at that time." Then al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhari and Muslim]" [manuscript D: "according to their condition"], but they did not record it. [Al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/311, 312).]

Maymun ibn Mihran said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "A man from the Children of Israel, if he had a wife, a servant and a house, was called a king."

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Hani' informed us, that he heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli say: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, and a man asked him, saying: "Are we not [manuscript R: "Are you not"; manuscript D: "I am one of the poor"] among the poor Emigrants?" 'Abdullah said: "Do you have a wife to whom you retire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you have a dwelling in which you live?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are among the rich." He said: "I have a servant." [Manuscript A: "Then he said."] He said: "Then you are among the kings." [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/163).]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Is kingship anything but a mount, a servant and a house?"

Ibn Jarir narrated it. Then it was related from Mansur, al-Hakam, Mujahid and Sufyan al-Thawri something similar to this. Ibn Abi Hatim also related it from Maymun ibn Mihran.

Ibn Shawdhab said: "A man from the Children of Israel, if he had a dwelling and a servant, and he was asked permission to enter upon him, then he was a king."

Qatadah said: "They were the first to possess servants as property [literally: to own servants]."

al-Suddi said regarding His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾: "A man among you possesses his own self, his family and his wealth." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Ibn Lahi'a, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "When one of the Children of Israel had a servant, a beast of burden and a wife, he was recorded as a king." [Within its chain are Ibn Lahi'a and Darraj, both weak, and Darraj's narration from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

And this is a strange (gharib) hadith from this route.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar narrated to us, Abu Dhamrah Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, [he said] [addition from manuscript A] I heard Zayd ibn Aslam say: ﴿and He made you kings﴾, then I know of nothing except that he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever has a house and a servant, he is a king."

This is a mursal (a report whose chain omits the Companion) and strange. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/161).] Malik said: "A house, a servant and a wife."

It has come in a hadith: "Whoever among you wakes up healthy in his body, secure in his dwelling, having the sustenance of his day, it is as if the whole world has been gathered for him." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (2346), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (4141), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mihsan al-Ansari.]

* *

And His saying: ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾. He means the worlds of your time. So they were the most noble of people in their time, among the Greeks, the Copts and all other kinds of the children of Adam, as He said: ﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Scripture and judgement and prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 16]. And God, exalted is He, said, reporting about Musa when they said: ﴿Make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. Indeed, these — what they are in is destroyed, and worthless is what they have been doing." He said, "Is it other than God I should seek for you as a god while He has preferred you over the worlds?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 138–140].

The intended meaning is that they were the best people of their time. Otherwise, this community (ummah) is more noble than them, more excellent before God, more complete in law, more upright in method, more honoured in prophet, greater in dominion, more abundant in provisions, greater in wealth and offspring, more extensive in realm, and more lasting in honour. God [exalted and majestic] [addition from manuscript R; manuscript A: "exalted"] said: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110], and He said: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. We have mentioned the mutawatir hadiths concerning the excellence, nobility and honour of this community before God, at His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ in the surah of Al 'Imran.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that they said regarding His saying: ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾, that it means: the community of Muhammad ﷺ. It seems they intended that this address in His saying ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾ is together with this community. The majority hold that it is an address from Musa to his people, and it is to be understood as the worlds of their time, as we have previously mentioned.

It was also said: The meaning of ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾ is: what He sent down to them of manna and quails, and what He shaded them with of clouds, and other things, of the extraordinary matters (khawariq al-'adat) with which God specifically favoured them. And God knows best.

Then God, exalted is He, said, reporting about the urging by Musa, peace be upon him, of the Children of Israel to jihad and to entering Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), which had been in their hands in the time of their forefather Ya'qub (Jacob), when he, his sons and his family migrated to the land of Egypt in the days of Yusuf, peace be upon him. Then they remained there until they went out with Musa [peace be upon him] [addition from manuscript A], and they found therein a people of the 'Amaliqah, the tyrannical giants, who had seized it and taken possession of it. So the Messenger of God, Musa, peace be upon him, commanded them to enter it and to fight their enemies, and gave them the good news of victory and triumph over them. But they shrank back, disobeyed and opposed his command, so they were punished by wandering in the wilderness (al-tih) and persisting in their journey bewildered, not knowing how to head toward a destination in it, for a period of forty years, as a punishment for them for their neglect of the command of God [exalted] [addition from manuscript A]. God, exalted is He, said, reporting about Musa that he said: ﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land﴾, that is: the purified.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Enter the Holy Land﴾, that he said: "It is al-Tur and what surrounds it." Mujahid and others said the same.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Sa'id al-Baqqal, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "It is Jericho (Ariha)." Similarly, more than one of the exegetes mentioned this.

But this is open to scrutiny, because Jericho was not the intended land for conquest, nor was it on their route to Bayt al-Maqdis, and they had come from the land of Egypt, after God had destroyed their enemy Pharaoh. Unless "Jericho" is meant as the land of Bayt al-Maqdis, as al-Suddi said, in what Ibn Jarir narrated from him, not that the intended meaning is this well-known town at the edge of the Ghawr east of Bayt al-Maqdis.

* *

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿which God has prescribed for you﴾, that is: which God promised you through the tongue of your forefather Isra'il (Israel), that it is an inheritance [manuscript A: "He inherited it"] for whoever among you believes. ﴿And do not turn back on your heels, for you will turn back as losers﴾, that is: do not shrink back from jihad. ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed in it are a people of tyrants, and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. And if they leave it, then indeed we will enter."﴾ [Manuscript R reads: "and indeed we will never enter it as long as they remain in it," which is an error.] That is: they made an excuse that in this town, which you commanded us to enter and to fight its people, there are tyrannical people, that is, those of frightful appearance and mighty strength, and that we are not able to withstand them or to contend with them, and we cannot enter it as long as they are in it. If they leave it, we will enter it [manuscript A: "from it, then we will enter"]; otherwise we have no power against them.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id [manuscript R: "Abu Sa'd"] said, Ikrimah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Musa was commanded to enter the city of the tyrants. He said: So Musa set out with those who were with him until he camped near the city, which was Jericho, and he sent to them twelve spies, one from each tribe, to bring him news of the people. He said: They entered the city and saw a great matter of their appearance, their bodies and their size. They entered an orchard belonging to one of them, and the owner of the orchard came to pick fruit from his orchard, and he began picking fruit and looking at their traces, and he followed them. Whenever he caught one of them, he took him and put him in his sleeve along with the fruit, until all twelve were gathered, and he put them in his sleeve with the fruit, and he went to their king and scattered them before him. The king said to them: You have seen our state and our affair, so go and inform your companion. He said: So they returned to Musa and informed him of what they had seen of their affair.

There is an open question concerning this chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/173).]

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: When Musa and his people camped, he sent from among them twelve men [manuscript A: "a leader (naqib)"], who are the nuqaba' (chiefs) whom God mentioned, and he sent them to bring him news of them. They set out, and a man from the tyrants met them, and he put them in his cloak, carried them until he brought them to the city, and called out to his people, and they gathered to him. They said: "Who are you?" They said: "We are the people of Musa; he sent us to come to him with news of you." So they gave them a grape, one grape sufficient for a man, and they said to them: "Go to Musa and his people and say to them: 'Measure the measure of your fruit.'" When they came to them, they said: "O Musa, ﴿so go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here.﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Had, Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: I saw Anas ibn Malik take a staff, and he measured with it something, I do not know how much he measured, then he measured the earth with it fifty or fifty-five [manuscript A: "fifty-five"] times, then he said: "Thus is the length of the 'Amaliqah."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah, verses 20–26 (Part 2 of 3)

Many of the exegetes have mentioned here reports originating from the Children of Israel (isra'iliyyat), concerning the great stature of these tyrants, and that among them was 'Awj ibn 'Unuq, a daughter of Adam (ﷺ)... [the text reads: "'Awj ibn 'Unuq, bint Adam, 'alayhi al-salam"], and that his height was three thousand, three hundred and thirty-three and a third cubits, a precise calculation! And this is something one is ashamed to mention. Moreover, it contradicts what is established in the Sahih [in D and A: "al-Sahihayn"] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah (Exalted) created Adam, and his height was sixty cubits. Then creation continued to decrease until now." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3326, and by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2841, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Then they have mentioned that this man was a disbeliever, that he was an illegitimate child, that he refused to board the ship, and that the flood did not reach his knees [in R and A: "his knees"]. This is a lie and a fabrication. Allah mentioned that Nuh prayed against the disbelievers of the earth, saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers as a dweller﴾ [Nuh: 26]. Allah (Exalted) also said: ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship; then We drowned the remaining ones﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 119–120]. And Allah (Exalted) said: ﴿There is no protector today from the command of Allah, except for whom He has mercy﴾ [Hud: 43]. If the disbelieving son of Nuh drowned, how could 'Awj ibn 'Unuq survive, when he was a disbeliever and an illegitimate child?! This is not acceptable to reason or to the Shari'ah. Moreover, the existence of a man called "'Awj ibn 'Unuq" is open to question, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Two men from among those who feared, upon whom Allah had bestowed favour, said﴾ means: when the Children of Israel shrank back from obeying Allah and following the Messenger of Allah, Musa (ʿalayhi al-salam), two men, upon whom Allah had bestowed a great blessing, urged them on. They were among those who feared the command of Allah and dreaded His punishment.

Some of them recited: ﴿Two men from among those who are feared﴾, meaning: among those who had dignity and standing among the people. It is said that the two were "Yusha' ibn Nun" and "Kalib ibn Yufuna". This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Atiyyah, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others among the earlier and later scholars, may Allah have mercy on them. They said: ﴿Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will surely be victorious. And upon Allah rely, if you are believers﴾, meaning: whenever you rely upon Allah, follow His command, and agree with His Messenger, Allah will grant you victory over your enemies, support you, make you triumph over them, and you will enter the land which Allah has decreed for you. But that did not benefit them at all. ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here."﴾ This was a refusal on their part to engage in jihad, an opposition to their Messenger, and a failure to fight the enemies.

It is said that when they refused to engage in jihad and resolved to turn back and return to their lands, Musa and Harun, upon them be peace, prostrated in front of a gathering of the Children of Israel, out of magnifying what they had resolved upon. Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalib ibn Yufuna tore their garments and rebuked their people for this. It is said that they stoned them. A great matter occurred and a grave danger arose.

How excellent was the answer given by the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all [in A: "may Allah be pleased with them all"], on the Day of Badr, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consulted them concerning fighting the army (al-nafir) that had come to protect the caravan (al-'ir) which was with Abu Sufyan. When the caravan had escaped their grasp, and the army drew near to them, and he resolved to fight a force of between nine hundred and a thousand, equipped with weapons, armour and gear, Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, spoke and spoke well. Then some of the Companions from the Muhajirun spoke, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was saying: "Advise me, O Muslims." He only said this to learn what the Ansar had to say, because they were the majority of the people at that time. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It seems you are referring to us, O Messenger of Allah. By the One who sent you with the truth, if you were to lead us into this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge in with you, and not one man among us would stay behind. We do not dislike that you should meet our enemy with us tomorrow. Indeed, we are patient in war and truthful in encounters. Perhaps Allah will show you from us what will please your eyes. So march with us in the blessing of Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delighted by the words of Sa'd, and it energized him. [See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/615).]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us from Anas, that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for Badr, he consulted the Muslims. 'Umar gestured toward him [i.e., signalled his support]. Then he consulted them again, and the Ansar said: "O assembly of the Ansar, it is you whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intends!" They said: "Then we will not say to him what the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. By the One who sent you with the truth, even if you were to drive your mounts to Bark al-Ghimad [a distant place], we would follow you."

Ahmad also narrated it, from 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas, with the same wording. Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Khalid ibn al-Harith, from Humayd, with the same. Ibn Hibban narrated it from Abu Ya'la, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman, from Humayd, with the same. [Al-Musnad (3/105), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11141, and Musnad Abi Ya'la al-Mawsili (6/407).]

Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far informed us, Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah informed us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, from al-Hasan [in A: "al-Hakam", and the established reading is from al-Jarh] ibn Ayyub, from 'Abd Allah ibn Nasikh, from 'Utbah ibn 'Abd al-Sulami who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his Companions: "Will you not fight?" They said: "Yes, and we will not say as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting alongside you both." [Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (4/183) through the chain of al-Hasan ibn Ayyub.]

Among those who responded that day was al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr al-Kindi, may Allah be pleased with him, as Imam Ahmad said:

Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Mukhariq ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ahmasi, from Tariq, that is Ibn Shihab: that al-Miqdad said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the Day of Badr: "O Messenger of Allah, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting alongside you both."

Thus Ahmad narrated it through this route. He also narrated it through another route, saying:

Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Mukhariq, from Tariq ibn Shihab who said: 'Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I witnessed from al-Miqdad a stance which I would rather be his companion in than have anything else compared to it. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was supplicating against the polytheists, and said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we will not say as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, we will fight on your right and on your left, before you and behind you.' I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brighten at that, and he was pleased by it." [Al-Musnad (1/389).]

Likewise, al-Bukhari narrated it in "al-Maghazi" and in "al-Tafsir" through several routes from Mukhariq, with the same. Its wording in "Kitab al-Tafsir" from 'Abd Allah is: He said: Al-Miqdad said on the Day of Badr: "O Messenger of Allah, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather [in A: "and we"], [we say] go on, and we are with you." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved [as if relieved of his anxiety]. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 3952, 4609.]

Then al-Bukhari said: Waki' narrated it from Sufyan, from Mukhariq, from Tariq: that al-Miqdad said to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah who said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his Companions on the Day of al-Hudaybiyyah, when the polytheists blocked the offering animals and they were prevented from their rites: "I am going with the offering animals, and I will slaughter them at the House." Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said to him: "By Allah, we will not be like the assembly of the Children of Israel when they said to their Prophet: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting with you." When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard it, they pledged allegiance upon that. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/186).]

And this: if it is preserved as having occurred at al-Hudaybiyyah, then it is possible that he repeated this statement on that day just as he had said it on the Day of Badr.

* *

His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have no control except over myself and my brother, so part us from the defiant people."﴾ means: when the Children of Israel shrank back from fighting, Musa, upon him be peace, became angry with them and said, supplicating against them: ﴿My Lord, indeed I have no control except over myself and my brother﴾, meaning: there is no one among them who obeys me, complies with the command of Allah, and responds to what I have called them to, except myself and my brother Harun. ﴿So part us from the defiant people﴾. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it means "judge between us and them." Ali ibn Abi Talhah also said this from Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise al-Dahhak said: "Judge between us and them, and open [the matter] between us and them." Others said: "Furq" means: separate between us and them, as the poet said:

"O Lord, then separate him and me
with the sharpest of separations between two..."

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿[He said], "Indeed, it is forbidden for them for forty years; they will wander in the land. So do not grieve over the defiant people."﴾ When Musa, upon him be peace, supplicated against them when they shrank back from jihad, Allah decreed against them that they be forbidden from entering it for a period of forty years. They fell into the wandering (al-tih), continually traveling without being guided to the way out of it. In this period there occurred wondrous events and many extraordinary signs: among them, the shading of them with clouds, the sending down of manna and quails upon them, and the bringing forth of flowing water from a hard rock which was carried with them on a beast; when Musa struck it with his staff, twelve springs gushed forth from that rock, each tribe having its own spring, along with other miracles with which Allah supported Musa ibn 'Imran. There the Torah was sent down, the laws were prescribed for them, and the Tent of the Covenant was made, which is also called the "Dome of Time."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 3 of 3):

Yazid ibn Harun said, from Asbagh ibn Zayd [[In R and A: "Yazid".]], from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: I asked Ibn Abbas about His saying: ﴿Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land﴾ [[In R and H: "Inna-ha" (إنها); the correct reading is what we have adopted.]] and the rest of the verse. He said: They wandered in the land for forty years. Each morning they would travel, having no place of settlement. Then the clouds were made to shade them in the wilderness, and manna and quails were sent down upon them. This is a portion of the hadith of "al-Futun" (the Trials). Then Harun, peace be upon him, died. After him, three years later, Musa al-Kalim (Moses, the one who spoke with God), peace be upon him, died. God appointed among them "Yusha' ibn Nun" (Joshua son of Nun), peace be upon him, as a prophet and successor to Musa ibn Imran. Most of the Children of Israel died there during that period. It is said that none of them remained except "Yusha'" and "Kalib" (Caleb). It is from here that some of the commentators (mufassirun, scholars of Qur'anic exegesis) said, regarding His saying ﴿He said: "Then it is forbidden to them"﴾, that this is a complete pause, and His saying ﴿for forty years﴾ is governed by His saying ﴿they will wander in the land﴾. When the period ended, Yusha' ibn Nun, peace be upon him, led them out, or led those who remained of them and the rest of the Children of Israel of the second generation. He headed with them to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and besieged it. Its conquest occurred on Friday after the afternoon prayer. When the sun began to set and he feared that the Sabbath would begin upon them, he said: "You are commanded and I am commanded. O God, hold it back for me." God Most High held it back until he conquered it. God commanded Yusha' ibn Nun to order the Children of Israel, when they entered Bayt al-Maqdis, to enter its gate prostrating while saying: "Hittah" (a request for remission), meaning: "Remove our sins from us." But they changed what they had been commanded, and they entered crawling on their buttocks, saying: "A grain in a hair." All of this has already been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Umar al-Adani related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Abu Sa'id, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land﴾. He said: They wandered for forty years. Musa and Harun died in the wilderness, along with everyone who had passed forty years of age. When the forty years had passed, Yusha' ibn Nun rose up with them. He was the one who took charge of the affair after Musa, and he was the one who conquered it. He was the one to whom it was said: "Today is Friday." They resolved to conquer it, and the sun drew near to setting. He feared that if the night of Saturday came, they would be unable to work, so he called out to the sun: "I am commanded and you are commanded," and it stood still until he conquered it. He found in it wealth the like of which had never been seen. They brought it near the fire, but it did not come. He said: "There is embezzlement (ghulul) among you." He summoned the heads of the tribes, who were twelve men, and gave them his pledge. The hand of one man of them stuck to his hand. He said: "The embezzlement is with you." So he brought it out, and it was the head of a calf of gold, with two eyes of ruby and teeth of pearl. He placed it with the offerings, and the fire came and consumed it.

This narration has a witness in the Sahih. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose that His saying ﴿Then it is forbidden to them﴾ is the governing element for ﴿forty years﴾, and that they remained, not entering it for forty years, while they were wandering in the desert, not guided to any destination. He said: Then they went out with Musa, peace be upon him, and he conquered Bayt al-Maqdis with them. Then he argued for this, saying: By the consensus of the scholars of the reports of the earlier peoples, that Awj ibn Anaq was killed by Musa, peace be upon him. He said: If his killing had occurred before the wandering, the Children of Israel would not have feared the Amalekites. This shows that it occurred after the wandering. He said: And they agreed that Bal'am ibn Ba'ura aided the tyrants by invoking curses against Musa. He said: That was only after the wandering, because before the wandering they did not fear Musa and his people. This is his line of reasoning. Then he said:

Abu Kurayb related to us, Ibn Atiyyah related to us, Qays related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The staff of Musa was ten cubits long, his leap was ten cubits, and his height was ten cubits. He leapt and struck the ankle of Awj and killed him, and his body became a bridge for the people of the Nile for a year [[In A: "years".]].

It is also narrated from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, who related to us from Mu'ammal, who related to us from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf al-Bikali, who said: The bed of Awj was eight hundred [[In R and A: "three hundred".]] cubits long. Musa's height was ten cubits, and his staff was ten cubits. He leapt into the sky ten cubits and struck Awj, hitting his ankle, and he fell dead. His body was a bridge that people passed over. [[The narration of Awj ibn Anaq is a long, false report. Nothing that is mentioned about his descriptions is authentic. Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may God have mercy on him, discussed it sufficiently in al-Manar al-Munif (p. 76).]]

* *

His Most High saying: ﴿So do not grieve over the defiant people﴾ is a consolation to Musa, peace be upon him, concerning them. That is: do not be distressed or saddened over them; whatever you decree against them, they deserve it.

This story contains a rebuke of the Jews, an exposure of their disgrace, their opposition to God and His Messenger, and their refusal to obey them in what they were commanded regarding jihad. Their souls were too weak to endure and wrestle with the enemies and fight them, even though the Messenger of God ﷺ, His interlocutor and chosen one from among His creation in that time, was among them, promising them victory and triumph over their enemies. Moreover, they had witnessed what God had brought down upon their enemy Pharaoh of punishment, retribution, and drowning for him and his soldiers in the sea, while they were watching so that their eyes would be comforted, and it was not long ago. Then they recoiled from fighting the people of a city which, compared to the lands of Egypt, does not equal a tenth of a tenth in the number of its people and its troops. Thus the ugliness of their conduct became apparent to the elite and the common alike, and they were disgraced with a disgrace that neither night can cover nor a cloak can conceal. Yet they remained in their ignorance, wandering blindly, and hesitating in their error. They are the most hateful to God and His enemies, yet they still say: ﴿We are the children of God and His beloved﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 18]. So may God disfigure their faces, from which He transformed them into swine and apes, and bind them with a curse that accompanies them into the blazing Fire, where they will be decreed eternal abiding forever. He has done so, and to Him belongs praise from all of existence.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 1 of 3):

God, exalted is He, says, telling of His servant, messenger and interlocutor Musa (Moses) son of 'Imran, peace be upon him, in what he reminded his people of, the blessings of God upon them and His favours toward them, in that He gathered for them the good of this world and the Hereafter, if they remained upright on their straight path. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when Musa said to his people: "O my people, remember the favour of God upon you when He appointed prophets among you﴾. That is: whenever a prophet died, another prophet arose among you, from your forefather Ibrahim (Abraham) onward and after him. [In manuscript A: "wa-lidhalika" (and therefore).] Thus they were: prophets never ceased among them, calling to God and warning of His vengeance, until they were concluded with 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him. Then God [exalted] [addition from manuscript R] revealed to the Seal of the Messengers and Prophets, absolutely, Muhammad son of 'Abdullah, who is traced to Isma'il son of Ibrahim, [manuscript A: "upon them both"] peace be upon him, and he is more noble than every one of them who preceded him, ﷺ.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from al-Thawri, from Mansur, from al-Hakam or another, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾, that he said: "The servant, the wife and the house."

Al-Hakim also narrated in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of al-Thawri as well, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The wife and the servant." ﴿And He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾, he said: "Those who were among them at that time." Then al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhari and Muslim]" [manuscript D: "according to their condition"], but they did not record it. [Al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/311, 312).]

Maymun ibn Mihran said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "A man from the Children of Israel, if he had a wife, a servant and a house, was called a king."

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Hani' informed us, that he heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli say: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, and a man asked him, saying: "Are we not [manuscript R: "Are you not"; manuscript D: "I am one of the poor"] among the poor Emigrants?" 'Abdullah said: "Do you have a wife to whom you retire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you have a dwelling in which you live?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are among the rich." He said: "I have a servant." [Manuscript A: "Then he said."] He said: "Then you are among the kings." [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/163).]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Is kingship anything but a mount, a servant and a house?"

Ibn Jarir narrated it. Then it was related from Mansur, al-Hakam, Mujahid and Sufyan al-Thawri something similar to this. Ibn Abi Hatim also related it from Maymun ibn Mihran.

Ibn Shawdhab said: "A man from the Children of Israel, if he had a dwelling and a servant, and he was asked permission to enter upon him, then he was a king."

Qatadah said: "They were the first to possess servants as property [literally: to own servants]."

al-Suddi said regarding His saying: ﴿and He made you kings﴾: "A man among you possesses his own self, his family and his wealth." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Ibn Lahi'a, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "When one of the Children of Israel had a servant, a beast of burden and a wife, he was recorded as a king." [Within its chain are Ibn Lahi'a and Darraj, both weak, and Darraj's narration from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

And this is a strange (gharib) hadith from this route.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar narrated to us, Abu Dhamrah Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, [he said] [addition from manuscript A] I heard Zayd ibn Aslam say: ﴿and He made you kings﴾, then I know of nothing except that he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever has a house and a servant, he is a king."

This is a mursal (a report whose chain omits the Companion) and strange. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/161).] Malik said: "A house, a servant and a wife."

It has come in a hadith: "Whoever among you wakes up healthy in his body, secure in his dwelling, having the sustenance of his day, it is as if the whole world has been gathered for him." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (2346), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (4141), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mihsan al-Ansari.]

* *

And His saying: ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾. He means the worlds of your time. So they were the most noble of people in their time, among the Greeks, the Copts and all other kinds of the children of Adam, as He said: ﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Scripture and judgement and prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 16]. And God, exalted is He, said, reporting about Musa when they said: ﴿Make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. Indeed, these — what they are in is destroyed, and worthless is what they have been doing." He said, "Is it other than God I should seek for you as a god while He has preferred you over the worlds?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 138–140].

The intended meaning is that they were the best people of their time. Otherwise, this community (ummah) is more noble than them, more excellent before God, more complete in law, more upright in method, more honoured in prophet, greater in dominion, more abundant in provisions, greater in wealth and offspring, more extensive in realm, and more lasting in honour. God [exalted and majestic] [addition from manuscript R; manuscript A: "exalted"] said: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110], and He said: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. We have mentioned the mutawatir hadiths concerning the excellence, nobility and honour of this community before God, at His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ in the surah of Al 'Imran.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that they said regarding His saying: ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾, that it means: the community of Muhammad ﷺ. It seems they intended that this address in His saying ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾ is together with this community. The majority hold that it is an address from Musa to his people, and it is to be understood as the worlds of their time, as we have previously mentioned.

It was also said: The meaning of ﴿and He gave you what He had not given anyone of the worlds﴾ is: what He sent down to them of manna and quails, and what He shaded them with of clouds, and other things, of the extraordinary matters (khawariq al-'adat) with which God specifically favoured them. And God knows best.

Then God, exalted is He, said, reporting about the urging by Musa, peace be upon him, of the Children of Israel to jihad and to entering Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), which had been in their hands in the time of their forefather Ya'qub (Jacob), when he, his sons and his family migrated to the land of Egypt in the days of Yusuf, peace be upon him. Then they remained there until they went out with Musa [peace be upon him] [addition from manuscript A], and they found therein a people of the 'Amaliqah, the tyrannical giants, who had seized it and taken possession of it. So the Messenger of God, Musa, peace be upon him, commanded them to enter it and to fight their enemies, and gave them the good news of victory and triumph over them. But they shrank back, disobeyed and opposed his command, so they were punished by wandering in the wilderness (al-tih) and persisting in their journey bewildered, not knowing how to head toward a destination in it, for a period of forty years, as a punishment for them for their neglect of the command of God [exalted] [addition from manuscript A]. God, exalted is He, said, reporting about Musa that he said: ﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land﴾, that is: the purified.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Enter the Holy Land﴾, that he said: "It is al-Tur and what surrounds it." Mujahid and others said the same.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Sa'id al-Baqqal, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "It is Jericho (Ariha)." Similarly, more than one of the exegetes mentioned this.

But this is open to scrutiny, because Jericho was not the intended land for conquest, nor was it on their route to Bayt al-Maqdis, and they had come from the land of Egypt, after God had destroyed their enemy Pharaoh. Unless "Jericho" is meant as the land of Bayt al-Maqdis, as al-Suddi said, in what Ibn Jarir narrated from him, not that the intended meaning is this well-known town at the edge of the Ghawr east of Bayt al-Maqdis.

* *

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿which God has prescribed for you﴾, that is: which God promised you through the tongue of your forefather Isra'il (Israel), that it is an inheritance [manuscript A: "He inherited it"] for whoever among you believes. ﴿And do not turn back on your heels, for you will turn back as losers﴾, that is: do not shrink back from jihad. ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed in it are a people of tyrants, and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. And if they leave it, then indeed we will enter."﴾ [Manuscript R reads: "and indeed we will never enter it as long as they remain in it," which is an error.] That is: they made an excuse that in this town, which you commanded us to enter and to fight its people, there are tyrannical people, that is, those of frightful appearance and mighty strength, and that we are not able to withstand them or to contend with them, and we cannot enter it as long as they are in it. If they leave it, we will enter it [manuscript A: "from it, then we will enter"]; otherwise we have no power against them.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id [manuscript R: "Abu Sa'd"] said, Ikrimah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Musa was commanded to enter the city of the tyrants. He said: So Musa set out with those who were with him until he camped near the city, which was Jericho, and he sent to them twelve spies, one from each tribe, to bring him news of the people. He said: They entered the city and saw a great matter of their appearance, their bodies and their size. They entered an orchard belonging to one of them, and the owner of the orchard came to pick fruit from his orchard, and he began picking fruit and looking at their traces, and he followed them. Whenever he caught one of them, he took him and put him in his sleeve along with the fruit, until all twelve were gathered, and he put them in his sleeve with the fruit, and he went to their king and scattered them before him. The king said to them: You have seen our state and our affair, so go and inform your companion. He said: So they returned to Musa and informed him of what they had seen of their affair.

There is an open question concerning this chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/173).]

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: When Musa and his people camped, he sent from among them twelve men [manuscript A: "a leader (naqib)"], who are the nuqaba' (chiefs) whom God mentioned, and he sent them to bring him news of them. They set out, and a man from the tyrants met them, and he put them in his cloak, carried them until he brought them to the city, and called out to his people, and they gathered to him. They said: "Who are you?" They said: "We are the people of Musa; he sent us to come to him with news of you."
