So they gave them a grape, one grape sufficient for a man, and they said to them: "Go to Musa and his people and say to them: 'Measure the measure of your fruit.'" When they came to them, they said: "O Musa, ﴿so go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here.﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Had, Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: I saw Anas ibn Malik take a staff, and he measured with it something, I do not know how much he measured, then he measured the earth with it fifty or fifty-five [manuscript A: "fifty-five"] times, then he said: "Thus is the length of the 'Amaliqah."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah, verses 20–26 (Part 2 of 3)

Many of the exegetes have mentioned here reports originating from the Children of Israel (isra'iliyyat), concerning the great stature of these tyrants, and that among them was 'Awj ibn 'Unuq, a daughter of Adam (ﷺ)... [the text reads: "'Awj ibn 'Unuq, bint Adam, 'alayhi al-salam"], and that his height was three thousand, three hundred and thirty-three and a third cubits, a precise calculation! And this is something one is ashamed to mention. Moreover, it contradicts what is established in the Sahih [in D and A: "al-Sahihayn"] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah (Exalted) created Adam, and his height was sixty cubits. Then creation continued to decrease until now." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3326, and by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2841, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Then they have mentioned that this man was a disbeliever, that he was an illegitimate child, that he refused to board the ship, and that the flood did not reach his knees [in R and A: "his knees"]. This is a lie and a fabrication. Allah mentioned that Nuh prayed against the disbelievers of the earth, saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers as a dweller﴾ [Nuh: 26]. Allah (Exalted) also said: ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship; then We drowned the remaining ones﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 119–120]. And Allah (Exalted) said: ﴿There is no protector today from the command of Allah, except for whom He has mercy﴾ [Hud: 43]. If the disbelieving son of Nuh drowned, how could 'Awj ibn 'Unuq survive, when he was a disbeliever and an illegitimate child?! This is not acceptable to reason or to the Shari'ah. Moreover, the existence of a man called "'Awj ibn 'Unuq" is open to question, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Two men from among those who feared, upon whom Allah had bestowed favour, said﴾ means: when the Children of Israel shrank back from obeying Allah and following the Messenger of Allah, Musa (ʿalayhi al-salam), two men, upon whom Allah had bestowed a great blessing, urged them on. They were among those who feared the command of Allah and dreaded His punishment.

Some of them recited: ﴿Two men from among those who are feared﴾, meaning: among those who had dignity and standing among the people. It is said that the two were "Yusha' ibn Nun" and "Kalib ibn Yufuna". This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Atiyyah, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others among the earlier and later scholars, may Allah have mercy on them. They said: ﴿Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will surely be victorious. And upon Allah rely, if you are believers﴾, meaning: whenever you rely upon Allah, follow His command, and agree with His Messenger, Allah will grant you victory over your enemies, support you, make you triumph over them, and you will enter the land which Allah has decreed for you. But that did not benefit them at all. ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here."﴾ This was a refusal on their part to engage in jihad, an opposition to their Messenger, and a failure to fight the enemies.

It is said that when they refused to engage in jihad and resolved to turn back and return to their lands, Musa and Harun, upon them be peace, prostrated in front of a gathering of the Children of Israel, out of magnifying what they had resolved upon. Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalib ibn Yufuna tore their garments and rebuked their people for this. It is said that they stoned them. A great matter occurred and a grave danger arose.

How excellent was the answer given by the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all [in A: "may Allah be pleased with them all"], on the Day of Badr, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consulted them concerning fighting the army (al-nafir) that had come to protect the caravan (al-'ir) which was with Abu Sufyan. When the caravan had escaped their grasp, and the army drew near to them, and he resolved to fight a force of between nine hundred and a thousand, equipped with weapons, armour and gear, Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, spoke and spoke well. Then some of the Companions from the Muhajirun spoke, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was saying: "Advise me, O Muslims." He only said this to learn what the Ansar had to say, because they were the majority of the people at that time. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It seems you are referring to us, O Messenger of Allah. By the One who sent you with the truth, if you were to lead us into this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge in with you, and not one man among us would stay behind. We do not dislike that you should meet our enemy with us tomorrow. Indeed, we are patient in war and truthful in encounters. Perhaps Allah will show you from us what will please your eyes. So march with us in the blessing of Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delighted by the words of Sa'd, and it energized him. [See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/615).]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us from Anas, that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for Badr, he consulted the Muslims. 'Umar gestured toward him [i.e., signalled his support]. Then he consulted them again, and the Ansar said: "O assembly of the Ansar, it is you whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intends!" They said: "Then we will not say to him what the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. By the One who sent you with the truth, even if you were to drive your mounts to Bark al-Ghimad [a distant place], we would follow you."

Ahmad also narrated it, from 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas, with the same wording. Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Khalid ibn al-Harith, from Humayd, with the same. Ibn Hibban narrated it from Abu Ya'la, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman, from Humayd, with the same. [Al-Musnad (3/105), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11141, and Musnad Abi Ya'la al-Mawsili (6/407).]

Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far informed us, Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah informed us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, from al-Hasan [in A: "al-Hakam", and the established reading is from al-Jarh] ibn Ayyub, from 'Abd Allah ibn Nasikh, from 'Utbah ibn 'Abd al-Sulami who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his Companions: "Will you not fight?" They said: "Yes, and we will not say as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting alongside you both." [Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (4/183) through the chain of al-Hasan ibn Ayyub.]

Among those who responded that day was al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr al-Kindi, may Allah be pleased with him, as Imam Ahmad said:

Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Mukhariq ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ahmasi, from Tariq, that is Ibn Shihab: that al-Miqdad said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the Day of Badr: "O Messenger of Allah, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting alongside you both."

Thus Ahmad narrated it through this route. He also narrated it through another route, saying:

Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Mukhariq, from Tariq ibn Shihab who said: 'Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I witnessed from al-Miqdad a stance which I would rather be his companion in than have anything else compared to it. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was supplicating against the polytheists, and said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we will not say as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, we will fight on your right and on your left, before you and behind you.' I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brighten at that, and he was pleased by it." [Al-Musnad (1/389).]

Likewise, al-Bukhari narrated it in "al-Maghazi" and in "al-Tafsir" through several routes from Mukhariq, with the same. Its wording in "Kitab al-Tafsir" from 'Abd Allah is: He said: Al-Miqdad said on the Day of Badr: "O Messenger of Allah, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather [in A: "and we"], [we say] go on, and we are with you." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved [as if relieved of his anxiety]. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 3952, 4609.]

Then al-Bukhari said: Waki' narrated it from Sufyan, from Mukhariq, from Tariq: that al-Miqdad said to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah who said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his Companions on the Day of al-Hudaybiyyah, when the polytheists blocked the offering animals and they were prevented from their rites: "I am going with the offering animals, and I will slaughter them at the House." Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said to him: "By Allah, we will not be like the assembly of the Children of Israel when they said to their Prophet: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here﴾. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting with you." When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard it, they pledged allegiance upon that. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/186).]

And this: if it is preserved as having occurred at al-Hudaybiyyah, then it is possible that he repeated this statement on that day just as he had said it on the Day of Badr.

* *

His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have no control except over myself and my brother, so part us from the defiant people."﴾ means: when the Children of Israel shrank back from fighting, Musa, upon him be peace, became angry with them and said, supplicating against them: ﴿My Lord, indeed I have no control except over myself and my brother﴾, meaning: there is no one among them who obeys me, complies with the command of Allah, and responds to what I have called them to, except myself and my brother Harun. ﴿So part us from the defiant people﴾. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it means "judge between us and them." Ali ibn Abi Talhah also said this from Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise al-Dahhak said: "Judge between us and them, and open [the matter] between us and them." Others said: "Furq" means: separate between us and them, as the poet said:

"O Lord, then separate him and me
with the sharpest of separations between two..."

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿[He said], "Indeed, it is forbidden for them for forty years; they will wander in the land. So do not grieve over the defiant people."﴾ When Musa, upon him be peace, supplicated against them when they shrank back from jihad, Allah decreed against them that they be forbidden from entering it for a period of forty years. They fell into the wandering (al-tih), continually traveling without being guided to the way out of it. In this period there occurred wondrous events and many extraordinary signs: among them, the shading of them with clouds, the sending down of manna and quails upon them, and the bringing forth of flowing water from a hard rock which was carried with them on a beast; when Musa struck it with his staff, twelve springs gushed forth from that rock, each tribe having its own spring, along with other miracles with which Allah supported Musa ibn 'Imran. There the Torah was sent down, the laws were prescribed for them, and the Tent of the Covenant was made, which is also called the "Dome of Time."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 3 of 3):

Yazid ibn Harun said, from Asbagh ibn Zayd [[In R and A: "Yazid".]], from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: I asked Ibn Abbas about His saying: ﴿Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land﴾ [[In R and H: "Inna-ha" (إنها); the correct reading is what we have adopted.]] and the rest of the verse. He said: They wandered in the land for forty years. Each morning they would travel, having no place of settlement. Then the clouds were made to shade them in the wilderness, and manna and quails were sent down upon them. This is a portion of the hadith of "al-Futun" (the Trials). Then Harun, peace be upon him, died. After him, three years later, Musa al-Kalim (Moses, the one who spoke with God), peace be upon him, died. God appointed among them "Yusha' ibn Nun" (Joshua son of Nun), peace be upon him, as a prophet and successor to Musa ibn Imran. Most of the Children of Israel died there during that period. It is said that none of them remained except "Yusha'" and "Kalib" (Caleb). It is from here that some of the commentators (mufassirun, scholars of Qur'anic exegesis) said, regarding His saying ﴿He said: "Then it is forbidden to them"﴾, that this is a complete pause, and His saying ﴿for forty years﴾ is governed by His saying ﴿they will wander in the land﴾. When the period ended, Yusha' ibn Nun, peace be upon him, led them out, or led those who remained of them and the rest of the Children of Israel of the second generation. He headed with them to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and besieged it. Its conquest occurred on Friday after the afternoon prayer. When the sun began to set and he feared that the Sabbath would begin upon them, he said: "You are commanded and I am commanded. O God, hold it back for me." God Most High held it back until he conquered it. God commanded Yusha' ibn Nun to order the Children of Israel, when they entered Bayt al-Maqdis, to enter its gate prostrating while saying: "Hittah" (a request for remission), meaning: "Remove our sins from us." But they changed what they had been commanded, and they entered crawling on their buttocks, saying: "A grain in a hair." All of this has already been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Umar al-Adani related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Abu Sa'id, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land﴾. He said: They wandered for forty years. Musa and Harun died in the wilderness, along with everyone who had passed forty years of age. When the forty years had passed, Yusha' ibn Nun rose up with them. He was the one who took charge of the affair after Musa, and he was the one who conquered it. He was the one to whom it was said: "Today is Friday." They resolved to conquer it, and the sun drew near to setting. He feared that if the night of Saturday came, they would be unable to work, so he called out to the sun: "I am commanded and you are commanded," and it stood still until he conquered it. He found in it wealth the like of which had never been seen. They brought it near the fire, but it did not come. He said: "There is embezzlement (ghulul) among you." He summoned the heads of the tribes, who were twelve men, and gave them his pledge. The hand of one man of them stuck to his hand. He said: "The embezzlement is with you." So he brought it out, and it was the head of a calf of gold, with two eyes of ruby and teeth of pearl. He placed it with the offerings, and the fire came and consumed it.

This narration has a witness in the Sahih. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose that His saying ﴿Then it is forbidden to them﴾ is the governing element for ﴿forty years﴾, and that they remained, not entering it for forty years, while they were wandering in the desert, not guided to any destination. He said: Then they went out with Musa, peace be upon him, and he conquered Bayt al-Maqdis with them. Then he argued for this, saying: By the consensus of the scholars of the reports of the earlier peoples, that Awj ibn Anaq was killed by Musa, peace be upon him. He said: If his killing had occurred before the wandering, the Children of Israel would not have feared the Amalekites. This shows that it occurred after the wandering. He said: And they agreed that Bal'am ibn Ba'ura aided the tyrants by invoking curses against Musa. He said: That was only after the wandering, because before the wandering they did not fear Musa and his people. This is his line of reasoning. Then he said:

Abu Kurayb related to us, Ibn Atiyyah related to us, Qays related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The staff of Musa was ten cubits long, his leap was ten cubits, and his height was ten cubits. He leapt and struck the ankle of Awj and killed him, and his body became a bridge for the people of the Nile for a year [[In A: "years".]].

It is also narrated from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, who related to us from Mu'ammal, who related to us from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf al-Bikali, who said: The bed of Awj was eight hundred [[In R and A: "three hundred".]] cubits long. Musa's height was ten cubits, and his staff was ten cubits. He leapt into the sky ten cubits and struck Awj, hitting his ankle, and he fell dead. His body was a bridge that people passed over. [[The narration of Awj ibn Anaq is a long, false report. Nothing that is mentioned about his descriptions is authentic. Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may God have mercy on him, discussed it sufficiently in al-Manar al-Munif (p. 76).]]

* *

His Most High saying: ﴿So do not grieve over the defiant people﴾ is a consolation to Musa, peace be upon him, concerning them. That is: do not be distressed or saddened over them; whatever you decree against them, they deserve it.

This story contains a rebuke of the Jews, an exposure of their disgrace, their opposition to God and His Messenger, and their refusal to obey them in what they were commanded regarding jihad. Their souls were too weak to endure and wrestle with the enemies and fight them, even though the Messenger of God ﷺ, His interlocutor and chosen one from among His creation in that time, was among them, promising them victory and triumph over their enemies. Moreover, they had witnessed what God had brought down upon their enemy Pharaoh of punishment, retribution, and drowning for him and his soldiers in the sea, while they were watching so that their eyes would be comforted, and it was not long ago. Then they recoiled from fighting the people of a city which, compared to the lands of Egypt, does not equal a tenth of a tenth in the number of its people and its troops. Thus the ugliness of their conduct became apparent to the elite and the common alike, and they were disgraced with a disgrace that neither night can cover nor a cloak can conceal. Yet they remained in their ignorance, wandering blindly, and hesitating in their error. They are the most hateful to God and His enemies, yet they still say: ﴿We are the children of God and His beloved﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 18]. So may God disfigure their faces, from which He transformed them into swine and apes, and bind them with a curse that accompanies them into the blazing Fire, where they will be decreed eternal abiding forever. He has done so, and to Him belongs praise from all of existence.

The Most High says, explaining the dreadful end of rebellion, envy and injustice in the story of the two sons of Adam from his own loins, according to the majority view, who are Habil (Abel) and Qabil (Cain). One of them transgressed against the other and killed him out of rebellion and envy, because of the blessing Allah had bestowed and the acceptance of the offering that he had made sincerely for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The one who was killed was victorious, having his sins removed and entering Paradise, while the killer was defeated and returned with a losing bargain in this world and the next. Allah the Most High said: ﴿And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam in truth﴾. That is: relate to these rebellious, envious people, the brothers of pigs and apes among the Jews and their like and counterparts, the story of the two sons of Adam, Habil and Qabil, as related by more than one of the early (al-Salaf) and later (al-Khalaf) scholars.
* *
His saying ﴿in truth﴾ means: clearly, with a matter that has no confusion, no falsehood, no delusion, no alteration, and no addition or deficiency, as Allah the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:62], and He said: ﴿We relate to you their story in truth﴾ [al-Kahf 18:13], and He said: ﴿That is Jesus, son of Mary, the word of truth about which they dispute﴾ [Maryam 19:34].

The account of the two of them, as related by more than one of the early and later scholars, is that Allah the Most High had prescribed for Adam, upon him be peace, that he should marry his daughters to his sons because of necessity. However, they said: a male and a female were born to him in every birth, so he would marry the female of one birth to the male of the other birth. The sister of Habil was unattractive, while the sister of Qabil was beautiful, so Qabil wished to keep her for himself to the exclusion of his brother. Adam refused this except on the condition that they both offer an offering, and whoever's offering is accepted, she will be his. They both offered, and Habil's offering was accepted while Qabil's was not. So the matter between them was as Allah related in His Book.

Mention of the statements of the commentators here:

As-Suddi, in what he related, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ: that no child was born to Adam except that a girl was born with him, so he would marry the boy of this birth to the girl of the other birth, and the girl of this birth to the boy of the other birth, until two sons were born to him called Qabil and Habil. Qabil was a farmer, and Habil was a herdsman. Qabil was the elder of them, and he had a sister more beautiful than Habil's sister. Habil asked to marry Qabil's sister, but Qabil refused and said: "She is my sister, born with me, and she is more beautiful than your sister, and I have more right to marry her." So their father commanded him to let Habil marry her, but he refused. They both offered an offering to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to see which of them had more right to the girl. Adam, upon him be peace, had gone away from them to Makkah to look at it. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Do you know that I have a House on earth?" He said: "No, O Lord." He said: "Indeed, I have a House in Makkah, so go to it." Adam said to the heaven: "Guard my son with trust," but it refused. He said to the earth, and it refused. He said to the mountains, and they refused. Then he said to Qabil, and he said: "Yes, go and return, and you will find your family as pleasing to you." When Adam set out, they offered their offerings. Qabil was boasting over him, saying: "I have more right to her than you. She is my sister, I am older than you, and I am the executor of my father's will." When they offered, Habil offered a fat young ram, and Qabil offered a bundle of ears of grain, from which he found one large ear, rubbed it and ate it. Then fire descended and consumed Habil's offering and left Qabil's offering. He became angry and said: "I will surely kill you so that you will not marry my sister." Habil said: "Indeed Allah accepts only from the righteous." Related by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn as-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, Ibn Khuthaym informed me, he said: I came with Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he related to me from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "A woman was forbidden to marry her twin brother, and was commanded to marry someone else from her brothers. In every birth there was a male and a female. While they were in this state, a beautiful woman was born to him, and another ugly, unattractive woman was born to him. The brother of the unattractive one said: 'Marry me to your sister and I will marry you to my sister.' He said: 'No, I have more right to my sister.' So they offered an offering, and the offering of the owner of the ram was accepted, and the offering of the owner of the crop was not accepted, so he killed him." Its chain is good.

And Abi narrated to us, Abu Salamah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his saying ﴿when they offered an offering﴾: they offered their offerings, and the owner of the flock brought a ram, large-eyed, horned and white, and the owner of the field brought a heap of food. Allah accepted the ram and stored it in Paradise for forty autumns, and it is the ram that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) sacrificed. Its chain is good.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, 'Awf narrated to us, from Abu al-Mughirah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: "The two sons of Adam who offered an offering, and the offering of one of them was accepted and the other's was not, one of them was a farmer and the other a herdsman. They were commanded to offer an offering. The herdsman offered the most noble, fattest and finest of his flock, with a willing soul. The farmer offered the worst of his crop, the poorest grain and tares, with an unwilling soul. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, accepted the offering of the herdsman and did not accept the offering of the farmer. This was their story as Allah related in His Book." He said: "By Allah, the one who was killed was the stronger of the two men, but his restraint prevented him from stretching his hand [his hand] against his brother."

Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani al-Qass said: "It reached me that when the two sons of Adam were commanded to offer an offering, one of them was a herdsman, and a lamb was born to him in his flock. He loved it so much that he preferred it at night, and he would carry it on his back out of love, until he had no property more beloved to him than it. When he was commanded to offer an offering, he offered it to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and Allah accepted it from him. It continued grazing in Paradise until it was ransomed for the son of Ibrahim, upon him be peace." Related by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Ansari narrated to us, al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Adam, upon him be peace, said to Habil and Qabil: "My Lord has covenanted with me that among my offspring there will be one who offers an offering. So offer an offering so that my eye may be comforted when your offering is accepted." So they offered. Habil was a herdsman and offered the best fattened sheep of his property, and Qabil was a farmer and offered a bundle of his crop. Adam went with them, and their offerings with them. They climbed the mountain and placed their offerings, then all three of them, Adam and the two of them, sat watching the offerings. Allah sent a fire until it was above them, and a neck approached it, and it took Habil's offering and left Qabil's offering, and they departed. Adam knew that Qabil was displeased with him, and said: "Woe to you, O Qabil, return your offering to yourself." Qabil said: "You loved him, so you prayed over his offering and supplicated for him, and his offering was accepted, and my offering was returned to me." Qabil said to Habil: "I will surely kill you so that I may be relieved of you. Your father prayed for you and prayed over your offering, so it was accepted from you." He kept threatening him with killing, until Habil was delayed one evening with his flock. Adam said: "O Qabil, where is your brother?" He said: "Did you send me to be his shepherd? I do not know." Adam said to him: "Woe to you, O Qabil. Go and seek your brother." Qabil said to himself: "Tonight I will kill him." He took with him an iron tool, met him as he was returning, and said: "O Habil, your offering was accepted and mine was returned to me; I will surely kill you." Habil said: "I offered the best of my property, and you offered the worst of your property, and indeed Allah accepts only the good. Allah accepts only from the righteous." When he said this, Qabil became angry, raised the iron tool and struck him with it, saying: "Woe to you, O Qabil, where are you before Allah? How will He repay you for your deed?" So he killed him, threw him into a pit in the earth, and covered him with some dirt. [The Shaykh Ahmad Shakir said in "'Umdat al-Tafsir" (4/124): "This is from the stories of the People of the Book, having no sound basis. Then the author, the Hafiz, has related here many reports on this matter, of the kind that fill the books of the commentators, and we have turned away from them, keeping some of them that are the best in their chains, as an example, not as a sound transmitted report," then he mentioned the report from Ibn 'Abbas as will come.]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from some people of knowledge of the earlier Book: Adam commanded his son Qayn (Cain) to marry his twin sister of Habil, and commanded Habil to marry his twin sister of Qayn. Habil submitted to this and was content, but Qayn refused and disliked it, out of honor regarding Habil's sister, and was averse to his own sister marrying Habil, and said: "We are the offspring of Paradise, and they are from the offspring of the earth, and I have more right to my sister." Some people of knowledge of the earlier Book say: Qayn's sister was among the most beautiful of people, so he begrudged her to his brother and wanted her for himself. Allah knows best which of these was the case. His father said to him: "O my son, she is not lawful for you." Qabil refused to accept that from his father's words. His father said to him: "O my son, offer an offering, and your brother Habil will offer an offering, and whichever of you has his offering accepted, he has more right to her." Qayn was a sower of the land, and Habil was a keeper of livestock. Qayn offered wheat, and Habil offered firstborn animals from his flock — some of them say he offered a cow. Allah sent a white fire which consumed Habil's offering and left Qayn's offering. By this, an offering used to be accepted when it was accepted. Related by Ibn Jarir.

And Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The matter of the two of them was that there was no needy person who was given charity, and a man would only bring an offering (qurban) by himself. Then, while the two sons of Adam were sitting, they said, 'If we were to offer an offering...' And when a man offered an offering that Allah accepted, He would send a fire that would consume it, and if Allah did not accept it, the fire would die down. So they both offered an offering. One of them was a shepherd and the other was a farmer. The owner of the sheep offered the best and fattest of his sheep, and the other offered some of his crops. Then the fire came down between them, consumed the sheep and left the crops. The son of Adam said to his brother, 'Will you walk among the people, when they know that you offered an offering and it was accepted from you, while mine was rejected? By Allah, people will not look at you and at me, while you are better than me.' He said, 'I will surely kill you.' His brother said to him, 'What is my fault? Allah only accepts from the God-fearing (al-muttaqin).'" Ibn Jarir related it.

This report indicates that the offering was made without any cause and without a dispute over a woman, as was mentioned earlier from a group of those previously mentioned. This is also the apparent meaning of the Qur'an: ﴿When they both offered an offering, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other. He said, "I will surely kill you." He said, "Allah only accepts from the God-fearing."﴾ The context indicates that he was angry and envious only because his offering was accepted instead of his.

Then, the well-known view among the majority is that the one who offered the sheep was Habil (Abel), and the one who offered the food was Qabil (Cain). His sheep was accepted from Habil, so much so that Ibn 'Abbas and others said it was the ram with which the sacrificed one was ransomed, and this is fitting, and Allah knows best. Nothing was accepted from Qabil. Many of the early and later scholars explicitly stated this, and it is also the well-known view from Mujahid. However, Ibn Jarir related from him that he said: "The one who offered the crops was Qabil, and it was his that was accepted," but this is contrary to the well-known view, and perhaps it was not transmitted from him accurately, and Allah knows best.

The meaning of His saying ﴿Allah only accepts from the God-fearing﴾ is: from those who feared Allah in that act of theirs.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ibrahim ibn al-'Ala' ibn Zibriq related to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash related to us, Safwan ibn 'Amr related to me, from Tamim, that is Ibn Malik al-Muqri, who said: "I heard Abu al-Darda' say: 'For me to be certain that Allah has accepted from me one prayer is dearer to me than the world and all that is in it. Indeed Allah says: ﴿Allah only accepts from the God-fearing.﴾'"

And my father related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Imran related to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi related to us, from al-Mughira ibn Muslim, from Maymun ibn Abi Hamza, who said: "I was sitting with Abu Wa'il, when a man called Abu 'Afif, one of the companions of Mu'adh, entered upon us. Shaqiq ibn Salama said to him: 'O Abu 'Afif, will you not tell us about Mu'adh ibn Jabal?' He said: 'Yes. I heard him say: "People will be held in one plain, and a caller will call out, 'Where are the God-fearing?' They will stand in the shelter of the Most Merciful. Allah will not veil Himself from them or hide Himself."' I said: 'Who are the God-fearing?' He said: 'A people who avoided shirk and the worship of idols, and made their worship sincere. They will pass into Paradise.'"

* *

His saying: ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you. Indeed I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ His brother, the righteous man whose offering Allah accepted because of his piety, says this to him when his brother threatened to kill him without any wrong on his part toward him. ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you﴾, meaning: I will not repay your corrupt deed with its like, so that I and you would be equal in sin. ﴿Indeed I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: lest I do as you wish to do. Rather, I will be patient and seek reward.

'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr said: "By Allah, he was indeed the stronger of the two men, but his scrupulousness (al-taharruj) prevented him, meaning his piety (al-wara')."

For this reason it is established in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim), from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "When two Muslims confront each other with their swords, the killer and the killed are in the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the killer, but what about the killed?" He said: "Indeed he was eager to kill his companion." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (31) and Sahih Muslim no. (2888), from the hadith of Abu Bakrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id related to us, Layth ibn Sa'd related to us, from 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas, from Bukayr ibn 'Abd Allah, from Busr ibn Sa'id, that Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said during the fitnah of 'Uthman: "I bear witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'There will be a fitnah in which the one who sits is better than the one who stands, the one who stands is better than the one who walks, and the one who walks is better than the one who runs.'" He said: "What do you think if someone enters my house and stretches his hand toward me to kill me?" He said: "Be like the son of Adam."

Al-Tirmidhi also related it similarly from Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and said: "This hadith is hasan. On this topic there are also reports from Abu Hurayrah, Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, Abu Bakrah, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Waqid, Abu Musa, and Kharashah." Some related it from al-Layth ibn Sa'd and added a man to the chain of narration.

The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir said: "The man is Husayn al-Ash'ari."

I say: Abu Dawud also related it through his route, saying: Yazid ibn Khalid al-Ramli related to us, al-Mufaddal related to us, from 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas, from Bukayr, from Busr ibn Sa'id, from Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ash'ari, that he heard Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet ﷺ, in this hadith, saying: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if someone enters my house and stretches his hand toward me to kill me?" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be like the son of Adam." And Yazid recited: ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you. Indeed I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4257).]

Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani said: "The first person from this Ummah to act upon this verse: ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you. Indeed I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ was 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him." Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Imam Ahmad said: Marhum related to us, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni related to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ rode a donkey and had me ride behind him, and said: 'O Abu Dharr, what do you think if people are struck by a severe hunger, so that you cannot rise from your bed to go to your mosque; how will you act?' He said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Be chaste.' He said: 'O Abu Dharr, what do you think if people are struck by a severe death, and the house will be with the servant, meaning the grave; how will you act?' I said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Be patient.' He said: 'O Abu Dharr, what do you think if people kill one another, to the extent that the stones of Zayt (a place in Medina) are soaked with blood; how will you act?' He said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Stay in your house and close your door upon yourself.' He said: 'What if I am not left alone?' He said: 'Then go to those among whom you are, and be among them.' He said: 'Should I take my weapon?' He said: 'Then you would be sharing in what they are doing. But if you fear that the gleam of the sword will startle you, then cast the edge of your garment over your face, so that he will bear his sin and your sin.'" [Musnad (5/149).]

Muslim and the authors of the Sunan, except al-Nasa'i, related it through several routes from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, with the same wording. [Sahih Muslim no. (648), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (431), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (176), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1256).] Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah also related it, through the route of Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Imran, from al-Mush'ath ibn Tarif, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, with similar wording. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4261), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3958).]

Abu Dawud said: "Al-Mush'ath did not mention in this hadith anyone other than Hammad ibn Zayd."

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Duhaym related to us, Ahmad ibn Hazim related to us, Qabisah ibn 'Uqbah related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ribi'i, who said: "We were at the funeral of Hudhayfah, and I heard a man say: 'I heard this man say to some people, from what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If you fight one another, I will surely look at the farthest room in my house, and I will enter it. If so-and-so enters upon me, I will surely say: 'Bear my sin and your sin,' and I will be like the better of the two sons of Adam.'"

* *

His saying: ﴿I intend that you should bear my sin and your sin, and so you will be among the companions of the Fire, and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and al-Suddi said, regarding His saying ﴿I intend that you should bear my sin and your sin﴾: that is, the sin of killing me and your sin that you had before that.

Ibn Jarir said: "Others said: it means that I intend that you should bear my sin, so that you would bear its burden, along with your sin in killing me. This is a view I found from Mujahid, but I fear it may be an error, because the authentic transmission from him is contrary to it." That is, what Sufyan al-Thawri related from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿I intend that you should bear my sin﴾, he said: "by your killing me," ﴿and your sin﴾, he said: "by what came from you before that."

Likewise, 'Isa related from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly. And Shibl related from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿I intend that you should bear my sin and your sin﴾, he says: "I intend that my wrongdoing and my blood be upon you, so that you bear both of them together."

I say: Many people may take this view to be correct, and they cite a hadith that has no basis: "The killer leaves no sin upon the one killed."

And the Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar related a hadith resembling this, but it is not the same. He said: 'Amr ibn 'Ali related to us, 'Amir ibn Ibrahim al-Asbahani related to us, Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, 'Utbah ibn Sa'id related to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Killing in patience (qatl al-sabr) does not pass by any sin without erasing it."

This with this is not authentic. [Musnad al-Bazzar no. (1545), Kashf al-Astar. al-Bazzar said: "We do not know it to be related from the Prophet ﷺ except through this route, and we do not know anyone to have traced it back except Ya'qub."] Even if it were authentic, its meaning would be that Allah expiates the sins of the one killed through the pain of being killed, but it cannot be applied to the killer. However, this may happen in some individuals, and that is the common case: the one killed will demand from the killer on the Plain of Judgment, and some of his good deeds will be taken to match the size of the wrong done to him. If his good deeds are exhausted and his right is not fully recovered, some of the sins of the one killed will be taken and placed upon the killer. Thus, perhaps no sin of the one killed will remain without being placed upon the killer. The hadith has been authentically related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning all wrongs, and killing is among the greatest and most severe of them. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said [in one version "qala," in another "fa-innahu qala"]: The correct view on this matter is that its interpretation is: "I want you to bear the sin of your killing me." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿I wish that you would bear my sin﴾. As for the meaning of ﴿and your sin﴾, it is his sin apart from [in one version "yaʻni," meaning] his killing of him, namely his disobedience to God, the Mighty and Majestic, in other deeds besides this.

We only said this is the correct view because of the consensus of the people of ta'wil (interpretation) upon it, and because God, the Mighty and Majestic, informed us that every doer of deeds will receive the recompense of his deeds, for or against him. Since this is His ruling over His creation, it is not permissible that the sins of the one who was killed be charged to this killer. Rather, the killer is held accountable for his own sin in killing unlawfully and for all the other sins of disobedience that he committed himself, not for what his victim bore.

This is his wording. Then he raised a question, the gist of which is: How could Habil wish for his brother Qabil to bear the sin of his killing and his own sin, when killing him is forbidden? He answered, in substance, that Habil was informing about himself that he would not fight his brother if his brother fought him, but would restrain his hand from him, seeking, should a killing occur, that it be done by his brother and not by himself.

I say: This statement contains an admonition to him, if he had heeded it, and a deterrent for him, if he had been deterred. That is why He said: ﴿I wish that you would bear my sin and your sin﴾, meaning: you would bear my sin and your sin, ﴿and so be among the companions of the Fire. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾.

Ibn ʻAbbas said: He frightened him with the Fire, but he did not desist and was not deterred.

* *

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So his soul made the killing of his brother seem good to him, and he killed him, and so became among the losers﴾. That is: his soul made it seem fair to him, and encouraged him to kill his brother, and so he killed him, that is, after this admonition and this deterrent.

It has already been mentioned in a report from Abu Jaʻfar al-Baqir, who is Muhammad ibn ʻAli ibn al-Husayn, that he killed him with an iron implement in his hand.

As-Suddi said, on the authority of Abu Malik and Abu Salih, from Ibn ʻAbbas, and from Murrah, from ʻAbdullah [ibn Masʻud], and from some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿So his soul made the killing of his brother seem good to him﴾: he sought him in order to kill him, and the youth fled from him into the mountain tops. Then one day he came upon him while he was tending his sheep, and he was asleep. So he lifted a rock and smashed his head with it, and he died. He left him in the open. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

From some of the People of the Book: he killed him by strangling and biting, the way wild beasts kill. Ibn Jarir [in one version "Ibn Jurayj"] said: When he wanted to kill him, he began twisting his neck. Then Iblis took an animal and placed its head on a stone, then took another stone and struck its head with it until it killed it, while the son of Adam watched. So he did the same to his brother. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

ʻAbdullah ibn Wahb said, from ʻAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father: [Qabil] took hold of his head to kill him, and he lay down for him and began pressing his head and bones, not knowing how to kill him. Then Iblis came to him and said: "Do you want to kill him?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then take this rock and drop it on his head." So he took it and dropped it upon him, and it smashed his head. Then Iblis came quickly to Hawwa' (Eve) and said: "O Hawwa', Qabil has killed Habil." She said to him: "Woe to you! What is killing?" He said: "He does not eat, drink, or move." She said: "That is death." He said: "It is death." So she began to cry out until Adam entered upon her while she was crying out. He said: "What is wrong with you?" She did not speak to him. He returned to her twice, and she did not speak to him. So he said: "Upon you be the cry, and upon your daughters. As for me and my sons, we are free of her." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

His saying: ﴿So he became among the regretful﴾ — meaning: in this world and the Hereafter. And what loss is greater than this?

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muʻawiyah and Waki' narrated to us, both saying: al-Aʻmash narrated to us, from ʻAbdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from ʻAbdullah ibn Masʻud, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No soul is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam bears a share of its blood, because he was the first to establish killing."

It was narrated by the group [of compilers of the six books] except Abu Dawud, through various chains, from al-Aʻmash, with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3335; Sahih Muslim no. 1677; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2673; al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i no. 3447; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 2616.]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: One of the killer's legs was bound to his thigh from that day until the Day of Resurrection, and his face is in the sun wherever it turns. In summer there is an enclosure of fire upon him, and in winter an enclosure of ice upon him. He said: ʻAbdullah ibn ʻAmr said: "We find that the son of Adam who is the killer divides with the people of the Fire an exact portion of punishment, and he bears half of their punishment."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Hakim ibn Hakim, that he reported from ʻAbdullah ibn ʻAmr that he used to say: "The most wretched of the people of the Fire is the man, the son of Adam, who killed his brother. No blood has been shed on earth since he killed his brother until the Day of Resurrection without some evil reaching him from it, because he was the first to establish killing." [Tafsir al-Tabari 10/219.]

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "No one is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam and Satan bear a share of it."

Narrated also by Ibn Jarir.

* *

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Then God sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal the nakedness of his brother. He said: "Woe is me! Was I unable to be like this crow and conceal the nakedness of my brother?" So he became among the regretful﴾. As-Suddi said, with his chain mentioned earlier going back to the Companions: When the youth died, he left him in the open, not knowing how to bury him. So God sent two crows, brothers, and they fought, and one of them killed the other. Then it dug a hole for it and covered it with earth. When he saw this, he said: ﴿Woe is me! Was I unable to be like this crow and conceal the nakedness of my brother?﴾

ʻAli ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn ʻAbbas: A crow came to a dead crow and scratched earth upon it until it covered it. So the one who had killed his brother said: ﴿Woe is me! Was I unable to be like this crow and conceal the nakedness of my brother?﴾

al-Dahhak said, from Ibn ʻAbbas: He carried his brother in a bag on his shoulder for a year, until God sent the two crows. He saw them digging, and said: ﴿Was I unable to be like this crow?﴾ and buried his brother.

Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said, from Mujahid: He carried him on his shoulder for a hundred years, dead, not knowing what to do with him, carrying him and setting him down on the ground, until he saw a crow burying a crow. So he said: ﴿Woe is me! Was I unable to be like this crow and conceal the nakedness of my brother? So he became among the regretful.﴾ Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

ʻAtiyyah al-ʻAwfi said: When he killed him, he regretted. He embraced him until he became exhausted, and the birds and beasts gathered around him, waiting for when he would throw him down so they could eat him. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from some scholars of the earlier Scripture: When he killed him, he was struck with despair and did not know how to conceal him. That was, as they claim, the first killing among the sons of Adam and the first dead person. ﴿So God sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal the nakedness of his brother. He said: "Woe is me! Was I unable to be like this crow and conceal the nakedness of my brother?" So he became among the regretful.﴾ He said: The people of the Torah (Tawrah) claim that Qayn (Cain), when he killed his brother Habil, God, the Mighty and Majestic, said to him: "O Qayn, where is your brother Habil?" He said: "I do not know; am I my brother's keeper?" God said: "The voice of your brother's blood cries out to Me from the earth. Now you are cursed from the earth, which has opened its mouth and received your brother's blood from your hand. If you work the earth, it will no longer yield its produce to you, and you will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth."

* *

His saying: ﴿So he became among the regretful﴾. al-Hasan al-Basri said: God raised him to regret after loss.

These are the sayings of the commentators regarding this story, and all of them agree that these two were sons of Adam by his own loins, as is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, and as the hadith affirms in His saying (ﷺ): "...except that the first son of Adam bears a share of its blood, because he was the first to establish killing." This is clear and evident. But Ibn Jarir said:

Ibn Wakiʻ narrated to us, Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from ʻAmr, from al-Hasan (that is, al-Basri), who said: The two men mentioned in the Qur'an, of whom God said: ﴿And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth﴾, were from the Children of Israel, and they were not sons of Adam by his own loins. The offering (qurban) was among the Children of Israel, and Adam was the first to die. This is very strange, and its chain is questionable.

ʻAbd al-Razzaq said, from Maʻmar, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The two sons of Adam, peace be upon him, were struck as an example for this nation, so take the good from them."

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated it from ʻAsim al-Ahwal, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God has struck for you the two sons of Adam as an example, so take from the best of them and leave the evil."

Likewise Bakr ibn ʻAbdullah al-Muzani transmitted this hadith as a mursal (a report in which the Companion is omitted from the chain). Ibn Jarir narrated all of this. [Tafsir al-Tabari 10/320.]

Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam remained a hundred years grieving and not laughing. Then he was approached and it was said to him: "May God give you life and make you cheerful," meaning: make you laugh.

Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then he said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Salamah narrated to us, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, who said: ʻAli ibn Abi Talib said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam wept for him and said:

The lands have changed, and whoever is upon them,
So the color of the earth is dusty and ugly.
Every thing of color and taste has changed,
And the radiance of the beautiful face has diminished.

Then Adam, peace be upon him, was answered:

O Abu Habil, both have been killed together,
And the living has become like the slaughtered dead.
And he came with a complexion which he had once
Upon fear, so he came with it crying out. [Tafsir al-Tabari 10/209-210.]

The Shaykh Muhammad Abu Shahba said in his valuable book "al-Israʼiliyyat wa Atharuha fi Kutub al-Tafsir" (Israelite narratives and their effect on books of tafsir), p. 183: "The scholar al-Dhahabi cast doubt on attributing these verses to God's prophet Adam in his book 'Mizan al-Iʻtidal' (The Balance of Moderation), and said: The defect in it is from al-Makhrami or his shaykh.

The poetry they mention is nothing but fabricated and invented, and prophets do not compose poetry. Al-Zamakhshari spoke the truth when he said: 'It is related that Adam remained a hundred years after the killing of his son without laughing, and that he lamented him with poetry. This is pure falsehood. Poetry is nothing but fabricated and corrupted, and it is established that the prophets are protected from poetry.'"

And God, blessed and exalted, has said: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾.

Imam al-Alusi said in his tafsir: It is narrated from Maymun ibn Mihran, from the scholar Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "Whoever says that Adam (peace be upon him) composed a poem has lied. Muhammad (ﷺ) and all the prophets are alike in forbidding poetry. But when Qabil (Cain) killed Habil (Abel), Adam wept for him in Syriac, and it kept being transmitted until it reached Ya'rib ibn Qahtan, who spoke Arabic and Syriac. He put it forward and back and made it an Arabic poem." Some scholars of the Arabic language have said that this contains solecism (lahn), irregular rhyme (iqwa'), and the commission of a poetic license (irtikab darurah), and it is better not to attribute it to Ya'rib, because of its obvious weakness.
The truth is that it is a poem of extreme weakness. It is more likely that this poem is an Israelite fabrication that has little share of Arabic, or a storyteller who wants to win people's hearts with such nonsense.

Apparently Qabil was hastened with punishment, as Mujahid ibn Jabr mentioned: that his shin was attached to his thigh on the day he killed, and Allah turned his face toward the sun wherever it turned, as a punishment and a humiliation for him. The Hadith has come from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no sin more deserving that Allah hastens its punishment in this world, along with what He stores up for its doer in the Hereafter, than rebellion (baghy) and severing the ties of kinship." Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 4902, and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 4211, from the Hadith of Abu Bakrah, may Allah be pleased with him. The act of Qabil combined both of these, so "indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we return."

The Most High says, explaining the dreadful end of rebellion, envy and injustice in the story of the two sons of Adam from his own loins, according to the majority view, who are Habil (Abel) and Qabil (Cain). One of them transgressed against the other and killed him out of rebellion and envy, because of the blessing Allah had bestowed and the acceptance of the offering that he had made sincerely for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The one who was killed was victorious, having his sins removed and entering Paradise, while the killer was defeated and returned with a losing bargain in this world and the next. Allah the Most High said: ﴿And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam in truth﴾. That is: relate to these rebellious, envious people, the brothers of pigs and apes among the Jews and their like and counterparts, the story of the two sons of Adam, Habil and Qabil, as related by more than one of the early (al-Salaf) and later (al-Khalaf) scholars.
* *
His saying ﴿in truth﴾ means: clearly, with a matter that has no confusion, no falsehood, no delusion, no alteration, and no addition or deficiency, as Allah the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:62], and He said: ﴿We relate to you their story in truth﴾ [al-Kahf 18:13], and He said: ﴿That is Jesus, son of Mary, the word of truth about which they dispute﴾ [Maryam 19:34].

The account of the two of them, as related by more than one of the early and later scholars, is that Allah the Most High had prescribed for Adam, upon him be peace, that he should marry his daughters to his sons because of necessity. However, they said: a male and a female were born to him in every birth, so he would marry the female of one birth to the male of the other birth. The sister of Habil was unattractive, while the sister of Qabil was beautiful, so Qabil wished to keep her for himself to the exclusion of his brother. Adam refused this except on the condition that they both offer an offering, and whoever's offering is accepted, she will be his. They both offered, and Habil's offering was accepted while Qabil's was not. So the matter between them was as Allah related in His Book.

Mention of the statements of the commentators here:

As-Suddi, in what he related, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ: that no child was born to Adam except that a girl was born with him, so he would marry the boy of this birth to the girl of the other birth, and the girl of this birth to the boy of the other birth, until two sons were born to him called Qabil and Habil. Qabil was a farmer, and Habil was a herdsman. Qabil was the elder of them, and he had a sister more beautiful than Habil's sister. Habil asked to marry Qabil's sister, but Qabil refused and said: "She is my sister, born with me, and she is more beautiful than your sister, and I have more right to marry her." So their father commanded him to let Habil marry her, but he refused. They both offered an offering to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to see which of them had more right to the girl. Adam, upon him be peace, had gone away from them to Makkah to look at it. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Do you know that I have a House on earth?" He said: "No, O Lord." He said: "Indeed, I have a House in Makkah, so go to it." Adam said to the heaven: "Guard my son with trust," but it refused. He said to the earth, and it refused. He said to the mountains, and they refused. Then he said to Qabil, and he said: "Yes, go and return, and you will find your family as pleasing to you." When Adam set out, they offered their offerings. Qabil was boasting over him, saying: "I have more right to her than you. She is my sister, I am older than you, and I am the executor of my father's will." When they offered, Habil offered a fat young ram, and Qabil offered a bundle of ears of grain, from which he found one large ear, rubbed it and ate it. Then fire descended and consumed Habil's offering and left Qabil's offering. He became angry and said: "I will surely kill you so that you will not marry my sister." Habil said: "Indeed Allah accepts only from the righteous." Related by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn as-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, Ibn Khuthaym informed me, he said: I came with Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he related to me from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "A woman was forbidden to marry her twin brother, and was commanded to marry someone else from her brothers. In every birth there was a male and a female. While they were in this state, a beautiful woman was born to him, and another ugly, unattractive woman was born to him. The brother of the unattractive one said: 'Marry me to your sister and I will marry you to my sister.' He said: 'No, I have more right to my sister.' So they offered an offering, and the offering of the owner of the ram was accepted, and the offering of the owner of the crop was not accepted, so he killed him." Its chain is good.

And Abi narrated to us, Abu Salamah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his saying ﴿when they offered an offering﴾: they offered their offerings, and the owner of the flock brought a ram, large-eyed, horned and white, and the owner of the field brought a heap of food. Allah accepted the ram and stored it in Paradise for forty autumns, and it is the ram that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) sacrificed. Its chain is good.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, 'Awf narrated to us, from Abu al-Mughirah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: "The two sons of Adam who offered an offering, and the offering of one of them was accepted and the other's was not, one of them was a farmer and the other a herdsman. They were commanded to offer an offering. The herdsman offered the most noble, fattest and finest of his flock, with a willing soul. The farmer offered the worst of his crop, the poorest grain and tares, with an unwilling soul. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, accepted the offering of the herdsman and did not accept the offering of the farmer. This was their story as Allah related in His Book." He said: "By Allah, the one who was killed was the stronger of the two men, but his restraint prevented him from stretching his hand [his hand] against his brother."

Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani al-Qass said: "It reached me that when the two sons of Adam were commanded to offer an offering, one of them was a herdsman, and a lamb was born to him in his flock. He loved it so much that he preferred it at night, and he would carry it on his back out of love, until he had no property more beloved to him than it. When he was commanded to offer an offering, he offered it to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and Allah accepted it from him. It continued grazing in Paradise until it was ransomed for the son of Ibrahim, upon him be peace." Related by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Ansari narrated to us, al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Adam, upon him be peace, said to Habil and Qabil: "My Lord has covenanted with me that among my offspring there will be one who offers an offering. So offer an offering so that my eye may be comforted when your offering is accepted." So they offered. Habil was a herdsman and offered the best fattened sheep of his property, and Qabil was a farmer and offered a bundle of his crop. Adam went with them, and their offerings with them. They climbed the mountain and placed their offerings, then all three of them, Adam and the two of them, sat watching the offerings. Allah sent a fire until it was above them, and a neck approached it, and it took Habil's offering and left Qabil's offering, and they departed. Adam knew that Qabil was displeased with him, and said: "Woe to you, O Qabil, return your offering to yourself." Qabil said: "You loved him, so you prayed over his offering and supplicated for him, and his offering was accepted, and my offering was returned to me." Qabil said to Habil: "I will surely kill you so that I may be relieved of you. Your father prayed for you and prayed over your offering, so it was accepted from you." He kept threatening him with killing, until Habil was delayed one evening with his flock. Adam said: "O Qabil, where is your brother?" He said: "Did you send me to be his shepherd? I do not know." Adam said to him: "Woe to you, O Qabil. Go and seek your brother." Qabil said to himself: "Tonight I will kill him." He took with him an iron tool, met him as he was returning, and said: "O Habil, your offering was accepted and mine was returned to me; I will surely kill you." Habil said: "I offered the best of my property, and you offered the worst of your property, and indeed Allah accepts only the good. Allah accepts only from the righteous." When he said this, Qabil became angry, raised the iron tool and struck him with it, saying: "Woe to you, O Qabil, where are you before Allah? How will He repay you for your deed?" So he killed him, threw him into a pit in the earth, and covered him with some dirt. [The Shaykh Ahmad Shakir said in "'Umdat al-Tafsir" (4/124): "This is from the stories of the People of the Book, having no sound basis. Then the author, the Hafiz, has related here many reports on this matter, of the kind that fill the books of the commentators, and we have turned away from them, keeping some of them that are the best in their chains, as an example, not as a sound transmitted report," then he mentioned the report from Ibn 'Abbas as will come.]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from some people of knowledge of the earlier Book: Adam commanded his son Qayn (Cain) to marry his twin sister of Habil, and commanded Habil to marry his twin sister of Qayn. Habil submitted to this and was content, but Qayn refused and disliked it, out of honor regarding Habil's sister, and was averse to his own sister marrying Habil, and said: "We are the offspring of Paradise, and they are from the offspring of the earth, and I have more right to my sister." Some people of knowledge of the earlier Book say: Qayn's sister was among the most beautiful of people, so he begrudged her to his brother and wanted her for himself. Allah knows best which of these was the case. His father said to him: "O my son, she is not lawful for you." Qabil refused to accept that from his father's words. His father said to him: "O my son, offer an offering, and your brother Habil will offer an offering, and whichever of you has his offering accepted, he has more right to her." Qayn was a sower of the land, and Habil was a keeper of livestock. Qayn offered wheat, and Habil offered firstborn animals from his flock — some of them say he offered a cow. Allah sent a white fire which consumed Habil's offering and left Qayn's offering. By this, an offering used to be accepted when it was accepted. Related by Ibn Jarir.

And Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The matter of the two of them was that there was no needy person who was given charity, and a man would only bring an offering (qurban) by himself. Then, while the two sons of Adam were sitting, they said, 'If we were to offer an offering...' And when a man offered an offering that Allah accepted, He would send a fire that would consume it, and if Allah did not accept it, the fire would die down. So they both offered an offering. One of them was a shepherd and the other was a farmer. The owner of the sheep offered the best and fattest of his sheep, and the other offered some of his crops. Then the fire came down between them, consumed the sheep and left the crops. The son of Adam said to his brother, 'Will you walk among the people, when they know that you offered an offering and it was accepted from you, while mine was rejected? By Allah, people will not look at you and at me, while you are better than me.' He said, 'I will surely kill you.' His brother said to him, 'What is my fault? Allah only accepts from the God-fearing (al-muttaqin).'" Ibn Jarir related it.

This report indicates that the offering was made without any cause and without a dispute over a woman, as was mentioned earlier from a group of those previously mentioned. This is also the apparent meaning of the Qur'an: ﴿When they both offered an offering, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other. He said, "I will surely kill you." He said, "Allah only accepts from the God-fearing."﴾ The context indicates that he was angry and envious only because his offering was accepted instead of his.

Then, the well-known view among the majority is that the one who offered the sheep was Habil (Abel), and the one who offered the food was Qabil (Cain). His sheep was accepted from Habil, so much so that Ibn 'Abbas and others said it was the ram with which the sacrificed one was ransomed, and this is fitting, and Allah knows best. Nothing was accepted from Qabil. Many of the early and later scholars explicitly stated this, and it is also the well-known view from Mujahid. However, Ibn Jarir related from him that he said: "The one who offered the crops was Qabil, and it was his that was accepted," but this is contrary to the well-known view, and perhaps it was not transmitted from him accurately, and Allah knows best.

The meaning of His saying ﴿Allah only accepts from the God-fearing﴾ is: from those who feared Allah in that act of theirs.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ibrahim ibn al-'Ala' ibn Zibriq related to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash related to us, Safwan ibn 'Amr related to me, from Tamim, that is Ibn Malik al-Muqri, who said: "I heard Abu al-Darda' say: 'For me to be certain that Allah has accepted from me one prayer is dearer to me than the world and all that is in it. Indeed Allah says: ﴿Allah only accepts from the God-fearing.﴾'"

And my father related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Imran related to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi related to us, from al-Mughira ibn Muslim, from Maymun ibn Abi Hamza, who said: "I was sitting with Abu Wa'il, when a man called Abu 'Afif, one of the companions of Mu'adh, entered upon us. Shaqiq ibn Salama said to him: 'O Abu 'Afif, will you not tell us about Mu'adh ibn Jabal?' He said: 'Yes. I heard him say: "People will be held in one plain, and a caller will call out, 'Where are the God-fearing?' They will stand in the shelter of the Most Merciful. Allah will not veil Himself from them or hide Himself."' I said: 'Who are the God-fearing?' He said: 'A people who avoided shirk and the worship of idols, and made their worship sincere. They will pass into Paradise.'"

* *

His saying: ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you. Indeed I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ His brother, the righteous man whose offering Allah accepted because of his piety, says this to him when his brother threatened to kill him without any wrong on his part toward him. ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you﴾, meaning: I will not repay your corrupt deed with its like, so that I and you would be equal in sin. ﴿Indeed I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: lest I do as you wish to do. Rather, I will be patient and seek reward.

'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr said: "By Allah, he was indeed the stronger of the two men, but his scrupulousness (al-taharruj) prevented him, meaning his piety (al-wara')."

For this reason it is established in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim), from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "When two Muslims confront each other with their swords, the killer and the killed are in the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the killer, but what about the killed?" He said: "Indeed he was eager to kill his companion." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (31) and Sahih Muslim no. (2888), from the hadith of Abu Bakrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id related to us, Layth ibn Sa'd related to us, from 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas, from Bukayr ibn 'Abd Allah, from Busr ibn Sa'id, that Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said during the fitnah of 'Uthman: "I bear witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'There will be a fitnah in which the one who sits is better than the one who stands, the one who stands is better than the one who walks, and the one who walks is better than the one who runs.'" He said: "What do you think if someone enters my house and stretches his hand toward me to kill me?" He said: "Be like the son of Adam."

Al-Tirmidhi also related it similarly from Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and said: "This hadith is hasan. On this topic there are also reports from Abu Hurayrah, Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, Abu Bakrah, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Waqid, Abu Musa, and Kharashah." Some related it from al-Layth ibn Sa'd and added a man to the chain of narration.

The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir said: "The man is Husayn al-Ash'ari."

I say: Abu Dawud also related it through his route, saying: Yazid ibn Khalid al-Ramli related to us, al-Mufaddal related to us, from 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas, from Bukayr, from Busr ibn Sa'id, from Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ash'ari, that he heard Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet ﷺ, in this hadith, saying: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if someone enters my house and stretches his hand toward me to kill me?" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be like the son of Adam." And Yazid recited: ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you. Indeed I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4257).]

Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani said: "The first person from this Ummah to act upon this verse: ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you. Indeed I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ was 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him." Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Imam Ahmad said: Marhum related to us, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni related to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ rode a donkey and had me ride behind him, and said: 'O Abu Dharr, what do you think if people are struck by a severe hunger, so that you cannot rise from your bed to go to your mosque; how will you act?' He said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Be chaste.' He said: 'O Abu Dharr, what do you think if people are struck by a severe death, and the house will be with the servant, meaning the grave; how will you act?' I said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Be patient.' He said: 'O Abu Dharr, what do you think if people kill one another, to the extent that the stones of Zayt (a place in Medina) are soaked with blood; how will you act?' He said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Stay in your house and close your door upon yourself.' He said: 'What if I am not left alone?' He said: 'Then go to those among whom you are, and be among them.' He said: 'Should I take my weapon?' He said: 'Then you would be sharing in what they are doing. But if you fear that the gleam of the sword will startle you, then cast the edge of your garment over your face, so that he will bear his sin and your sin.'" [Musnad (5/149).]

Muslim and the authors of the Sunan, except al-Nasa'i, related it through several routes from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, with the same wording. [Sahih Muslim no. (648), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (431), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (176), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1256).] Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah also related it, through the route of Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Imran, from al-Mush'ath ibn Tarif, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, with similar wording. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4261), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3958).]

Abu Dawud said: "Al-Mush'ath did not mention in this hadith anyone other than Hammad ibn Zayd."

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Duhaym related to us, Ahmad ibn Hazim related to us, Qabisah ibn 'Uqbah related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ribi'i, who said: "We were at the funeral of Hudhayfah, and I heard a man say: 'I heard this man say to some people, from what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If you fight one another, I will surely look at the farthest room in my house, and I will enter it. If so-and-so enters upon me, I will surely say: 'Bear my sin and your sin,' and I will be like the better of the two sons of Adam.'"

* *

His saying: ﴿I intend that you should bear my sin and your sin, and so you will be among the companions of the Fire, and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and al-Suddi said, regarding His saying ﴿I intend that you should bear my sin and your sin﴾: that is, the sin of killing me and your sin that you had before that.

Ibn Jarir said: "Others said: it means that I intend that you should bear my sin, so that you would bear its burden, along with your sin in killing me. This is a view I found from Mujahid, but I fear it may be an error, because the authentic transmission from him is contrary to it." That is, what Sufyan al-Thawri related from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿I intend that you should bear my sin﴾, he said: "by your killing me," ﴿and your sin﴾, he said: "by what came from you before that."

Likewise, 'Isa related from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly. And Shibl related from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿I intend that you should bear my sin and your sin﴾, he says: "I intend that my wrongdoing and my blood be upon you, so that you bear both of them together."

I say: Many people may take this view to be correct, and they cite a hadith that has no basis: "The killer leaves no sin upon the one killed."

And the Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar related a hadith resembling this, but it is not the same.
