Does the amputation of the hand also fall away or not? On this there are two opinions among the scholars.

The apparent meaning of the verse requires that all of these fall away, and this was the practice of the Companions, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Harithah ibn Badr al-Tamimi, from the people of Basrah, had spread corruption in the land and waged war. He spoke to men of Quraysh, among them al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas and 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, and they spoke to 'Ali, but he did not grant him safe conduct. Then Sa'id ibn Qays al-Hamdani came, took him in and hid him in his house; then he went to Ali and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what do you think of one who wages war against Allah and His Messenger and strives upon the earth to cause corruption? And he recited until he reached: ﴿except those who repent before you gain power over them﴾. He said: So he wrote him a pledge of safe conduct. Sa'id ibn Qays said: That was Harithah ibn Badr.

Ibn Jarir also related it through other chains, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, with the same wording, and he added: Harithah ibn Badr said:

Ah, let me convey to Hamdan, if I should meet them,
Across distance, that no enemy who disparages them will be safe...

Ibn Kathir's *Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim* on Surah 5, verses 32–34 (part 4 of 4):

By the life of her father, Hamdan fears Allah,
and her orator judges by the Book. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/280).]

Ibn Jarir narrated through Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-Suddi, and through Ash'ath; both of them from 'Amir al-Sha'bi, who said: A man from Murad came to Abu Musa, who was governor of Kufa during the caliphate of 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, after he had prayed the obligatory prayer, and said: "O Abu Musa, this is the place of one seeking refuge with you. I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so, al-Muradi. I had waged war against Allah and His Messenger and had spread corruption in the land, and I have repented before I was overpowered." Abu Musa stood up and said: "This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and he had waged war against Allah and His Messenger, and had spread corruption in the land, and he has repented before he was overpowered. Whoever meets him, let him not approach him except with good. If he is truthful, then the path belongs to one who is truthful; and if he is lying, his sins will overtake him." The man remained as long as Allah willed, then he went out, and Allah overtook him with his sins and he was killed.

Ibn Jarir then said: Ali narrated to me, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, who said: al-Layth said, and Musa ibn Ishaq al-Madani, who is the amir (commander) in our view, similarly narrated to me: that 'Ali al-Asadi waged war, terrorized the road, and committed killing and theft. The rulers and the common people pursued him, but he eluded them and could not be seized, until he came repentant. That was because he heard a man reciting this verse: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [Az-Zumar 53]. So he stood before him and said: "O servant of Allah, repeat its recitation." The man repeated it to him, so he sheathed his sword and came in repentance. He arrived in Medina at dawn, performed ghusl (ritual washing), then went to the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and prayed the dawn prayer. Then he sat down with Abu Hurayrah among his companions. When it became light, the people recognized him, and they stood up toward him. He said: "There is no path for you over me. I have come repentant before you could overpower me." Abu Hurayrah said: "He has spoken the truth." Abu Hurayrah took him by the hand until he came to Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who was then governor of Medina during the time of Mu'awiyah, and said: "This is 'Ali; he has come repentant, and there is no path for you over him, nor any killing." He said: So he was left alone regarding all of that. He said: 'Ali went out repentant, striving in the cause of Allah by sea. They encountered the Romans, and they brought his ship close to one of their ships, so he stormed onto the Romans' ship. They fled from him to its other side, and the ship tilted with him and with them, and they all drowned. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/284).]

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His believing servants to have taqwa (God-consciousness) of Him. When taqwa is paired with obedience, it means refraining from what is forbidden and abandoning what is prohibited. After this He says: ﴿And seek the means of approach (al-wasilah) to Him﴾. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Ḥaddathanā Abī, from Ṭalḥah, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "That is, the nearness (al-qurbah)." Mujāhid, [ʿAṭāʾ] (addition from MS r), Abū Wāʾil, al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr, al-Suddī and Ibn Zayd said the same.

Qatādah said: "That is, draw near to Him through obedience to Him and by acting in what pleases Him." Ibn Zayd recited: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek the means of approach to their Lord﴾ [al-Isrāʾ 17:57]. What these Imams said is not disputed among the exegetes [in MS r: "there is no disagreement among the exegetes about it"]. Ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] cited as evidence the verse of the poet:

*When the slanderers are heedless, we return to our union,*
*and the sincere friendship between us returns, and the means of approach.*

Al-wasīlah is that by which one reaches the attainment of the desired goal. Al-wasīlah is also a designation for the highest rank in Paradise, the station and abode of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Paradise. It is the closest of Paradise's places to the Throne. It is established in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, through the route of Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, when he hears the call to prayer: 'O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and of the established prayer, grant Muḥammad al-wasīlah and al-faḍīlah, and raise him to the praiseworthy station which You have promised him,' will be granted my intercession on the Day of Resurrection."

Another ḥadīth in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from the narration of Kaʿb, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "When you hear the muʾadhdhin, say the same as he says, then send blessings upon me, for whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah sends blessings upon him tenfold. Then ask Allah for al-wasīlah for me, for it is a station in Paradise, fitting only for one of the servants of Allah, and I hope that I will be he. Whoever asks Allah for al-wasīlah for me, intercession will be granted to him."

Another ḥadīth: Imam Aḥmad said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd al-Razzāq, akhbaranā Sufyān, from Layth, from Kaʿb, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you send blessings upon me, ask for al-wasīlah for me." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-wasīlah?" He said: "The highest rank in Paradise, which none will attain except one man, and I hope that I will be he."

al-Tirmidhī narrated it from Bundār, from Abū ʿĀṣim, from Sufyān, that is al-Thawrī, from Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, from Kaʿb, who said: Abū Hurayrah narrated to me, with it. Then he said: "Gharīb (strange). Kaʿb is not well known. We do not know of anyone who narrated from him except Layth ibn Abī Sulaym." [Musnad (2/265) and Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. 3612.]

Another route: from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. Abū Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd al-Bāqī ibn Qāniʿ, ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Naṣr al-Tirmidhī, ḥaddathanā ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Ṣāliḥ, ḥaddathanā Abū Shihāb, from Layth, from al-Muʿallā, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, from Abū Hurayrah, raising it (to the Prophet ﷺ), who said: "Send blessings upon me as you would send blessings, and ask Allah for al-wasīlah for me." They asked him, and he informed them: "al-Wasīlah is a rank in Paradise, which none will attain except one man, and I hope to be him." [In it is Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, who is weak. al-Bazzār narrated it in his Musnad no. 252 (Kashf al-Astār) by another route, from Dāwūd ibn ʿUlayyah, from Layth, from Mujāhid, from Abū Hurayrah, in similar wording. al-Haythamī said: "Dāwūd ibn ʿUlayyah is weak."]

Another ḥadīth: The Ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarānī said: Akhbaranā Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī al-Abbār, ḥaddathanā al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Ḥarrānī, ḥaddathanā Mūsā ibn Aʿyan, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb [in MS h: "Ibn Abī Ḥabīb," which is an error], from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask Allah for al-wasīlah for me, for no servant asks it for me in this world except that I will be a witness for him, or an intercessor, on the Day of Resurrection."

Then al-Ṭabarānī said: "No one narrated it from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb except Mūsā ibn Aʿyan." Thus he said, but Ibn Mardawayh narrated it: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Duḥaym, ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn Ḥāzim, ḥaddathanā ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā, ḥaddathanā Mūsā ibn ʿUbaydah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, and he mentioned its chain with a similar wording. [al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ of al-Ṭabarānī no. 639, Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn. al-Haythamī said in al-Majmaʿ (1/333): "In it is al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Ḥarrānī, whom Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned among the trustworthy and said: 'Sound in narration when he narrates from the trustworthy.' I say: this is from his narration from Mūsā ibn Aʿyan, who is trustworthy."]

Another ḥadīth: Ibn Mardawayh narrated, with his chain, from ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Mūsā ibn Wardān, that he heard Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "al-Wasīlah is a rank with Allah, above which there is no rank, so ask Allah to grant me al-wasīlah above His creation." [al-Ṭabarānī also narrated it in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ nos. 640, 641, Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn, by the route of ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah with it.]

Another ḥadīth: Ibn Mardawayh also narrated by two routes, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Baḥr: Ḥaddathanā Sharīk, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "In Paradise there is a rank called al-wasīlah, so when you ask Allah, ask for al-wasīlah for me." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who will dwell with you?" He said: "ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn." [This ḥadīth is gharīb (strange) and munkar (rejected) through this route. Its strangeness is that it is narrated by ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Baḥr al-Baṣrī, of whom Ibn Ḥibbān said: "He used to steal ḥadīths." Al-Ḥārith is al-Aʿwar, whom al-Shaʿbī called a liar, and a group weakened him.]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, ḥaddathanā al-Ḥasan al-Dashtakī, ḥaddathanā Abū Zuhayr, ḥaddathanā Saʿd [in MS r: "Saʿīd"] ibn Ṭarīf, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Azdī, mawlā of Sālim ibn Thawbān, who said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib calling out from the pulpit of Kufa: "O people, in Paradise there are two pearls: one white and one yellow. As for the yellow one, it is near the bottom of the Throne. The praiseworthy station is in the white pearl, seventy thousand chambers, each house of which is three miles, and its chambers, doors and couches are as if of one vein. Its name is al-Wasīlah, and it belongs to Muḥammad (ﷺ) and his household. The yellow one has the same, and it belongs to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his household."

This is also a gharīb report. [In its chain is Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf al-Iskāfī. Ibn Maʿīn said: "It is not lawful for anyone to narrate from him." Aḥmad and Abū Ḥātim said: "Weak." al-Nasāʾī and al-Dāraquṭnī said: "Matrūk al-ḥadīth (abandoned in narration)." Ibn Ḥibbān said: "He used to fabricate ḥadīths on the spot." Mīzān al-iʿtidāl (2/122).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And strive in His way, that you may prosper﴾. When He commanded them to abandon what is forbidden and to perform acts of obedience, He commanded them to fight the enemies among the disbelievers and polytheists who deviate from the straight path and abandon the upright religion. He encouraged them to do so by what He has prepared for those who strive in His way on the Day of Resurrection: success and great, eternal, lasting happiness that does not perish, change or cease, in lofty, elevated, secure chambers, whose views are beautiful and whose dwellings are good, where whoever dwells is blessed and never despairs, lives and never dies, whose garments do not wear out and whose youth does not fade.

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed of what He has prepared for His enemies, the disbelievers, of punishment and torment on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them; and they will have a painful punishment﴾. That is: even if one of them came on the Day of Resurrection with the earth filled with gold, and the like of it, to ransom himself thereby from the punishment of Allah, which has encompassed him and whose arrival he is certain of, that would not be accepted from him. Rather, there is no escape from it, no refuge, and no way out for him. Therefore He said: ﴿And they will have a painful punishment﴾, that is, agonizing. ﴿They wish to leave the Fire, but they will not be ones who leave it; and for them is a enduring punishment﴾. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Every time they wish to leave it, out of distress, they will be returned into it﴾ [al-Ḥajj 22:22]. So they continually wish to leave what they are in of its severity and painful touch, but there is no way for them to do so. Whenever the flame lifts them and they reach the upper parts of Hell, the angels of punishment strike them with iron maces and return them to its bottom. ﴿And for them is an enduring punishment﴾, that is, lasting and continuous, with no exit for them from it and no escape from it.

Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated from Thābit, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man from the people of the Fire will be brought, and He will say: 'O son of Adam, how did you find your resting place?' He will say: 'The worst resting place.' He will say: 'Would you ransom yourself with the earth's fill of gold?' He will say: 'Yes, my Lord!' He will say: 'You have lied! I asked you for less than that and you did not do it,' and he will be commanded to the Fire."

Muslim and al-Nasāʾī narrated it through the route of Ḥammād ibn Salamah in similar wording. [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 2807, Sunan al-Nasāʾī (6/36).] [In MS d: "al-Bukhārī."] Likewise al-Bukhārī and Muslim narrated it through the route of Muʿādh ibn Hishām al-Dastawāʾī, from his father, from Qatādah, from Anas, with it. [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. 6538 and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 2805.] Likewise they both narrated it through the route of Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, whose name is ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ḥabīb, from Anas ibn Mālik, with it. [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. 6557 and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 2805.] Maṭar al-Warrāq narrated it from Anas ibn Mālik, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through his route, from him.

Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of al-Masʿūdī, from Yazīd ibn Ṣuhayb al-Faqīr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [said] (addition from MSS a, r): "A people will come out of the Fire and enter Paradise." He said: I said to Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh: "Allah says: ﴿They wish to leave the Fire, but they will not be ones who leave it﴾." He said: "Recite the beginning of the verse: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby﴾," to the end of the verse. "Those are the ones who disbelieved."

Imam Aḥmad and Muslim also narrated this ḥadīth through another route, from Yazīd al-Faqīr, from Jābir. [al-Musnad (3/355) and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 191.] This version is more detailed in its wording.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba [in one manuscript: "Ibn Abi Shayba"; in another: "al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba al-Wasiti"] al-Wasiti narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Mubarak ibn Fadala informed us: Yazid al-Faqir narrated to me, saying: I sat with Jabir ibn Abdullah while he was narrating, and he related that some people (in one manuscript: "nasan") would come out of the Fire. He said: At that time I denied this, so I became angry and said: "How strange are people! But I am more amazed at you, O Companions of Muhammad! You claim that Allah brings people out of the Fire, while Allah says: ﴿They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not come out of it, and theirs is a lasting punishment﴾ [Allah's words in the verse are added from another manuscript; in another: "the verse"]. Then his companions rebuked me, and he was the most forbearing of them, and said: "Leave the man alone. That applies only to the disbelievers: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection﴾ until he reached ﴿and theirs is a lasting punishment﴾. Do you not read the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes, indeed, I have memorised it." He said: "Did not Allah say: ﴿And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional [prayer] for you; it is expected that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾? [Al-Isra: 79]. That is that station: Allah [Ta'ala] (added from another manuscript) detains peoples in the Fire for their sins for as long as He wills, not speaking to them; then when He wills to bring them out, He brings them out." He said: After that I never again denied it.

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Daʿlaj ibn Ahmad narrated to us: Amr ibn Hafs al-Sadusi narrated to us: Asim ibn Ali narrated to us: al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl narrated to us: Said ibn al-Muhallab narrated to us: Talq ibn Habib narrated to me, saying: I was among the strongest of people in denying intercession, until I met Jabir ibn Abdullah, and I recited to him every verse I could that mentions the eternal abiding of the people of the Fire (in one manuscript: "and I recited"), in which Allah [Ta'ala] (added from another manuscript) is mentioned. He said: "O Talq, do you think you are a better reciter of the Book of Allah, and more knowledgeable of the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (added from other manuscripts) than I am? Those whom you recited about are its people: they are the polytheists. But these are people who committed sins and were punished, then they were brought out of it." Then he pointed with his hands to his ears and said: "May my ears be deaf if I have not heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'They will come out of the Fire after they had entered it.' And we recite as you recite."

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His believing servants to have taqwa (God-consciousness) of Him. When taqwa is paired with obedience, it means refraining from what is forbidden and abandoning what is prohibited. After this He says: ﴿And seek the means of approach (al-wasilah) to Him﴾. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Ḥaddathanā Abī, from Ṭalḥah, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "That is, the nearness (al-qurbah)." Mujāhid, [ʿAṭāʾ] (addition from MS r), Abū Wāʾil, al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr, al-Suddī and Ibn Zayd said the same.

Qatādah said: "That is, draw near to Him through obedience to Him and by acting in what pleases Him." Ibn Zayd recited: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek the means of approach to their Lord﴾ [al-Isrāʾ 17:57]. What these Imams said is not disputed among the exegetes [in MS r: "there is no disagreement among the exegetes about it"]. Ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] cited as evidence the verse of the poet:

*When the slanderers are heedless, we return to our union,*
*and the sincere friendship between us returns, and the means of approach.*

Al-wasīlah is that by which one reaches the attainment of the desired goal. Al-wasīlah is also a designation for the highest rank in Paradise, the station and abode of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Paradise. It is the closest of Paradise's places to the Throne. It is established in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, through the route of Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, when he hears the call to prayer: 'O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and of the established prayer, grant Muḥammad al-wasīlah and al-faḍīlah, and raise him to the praiseworthy station which You have promised him,' will be granted my intercession on the Day of Resurrection."

Another ḥadīth in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from the narration of Kaʿb, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "When you hear the muʾadhdhin, say the same as he says, then send blessings upon me, for whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah sends blessings upon him tenfold. Then ask Allah for al-wasīlah for me, for it is a station in Paradise, fitting only for one of the servants of Allah, and I hope that I will be he. Whoever asks Allah for al-wasīlah for me, intercession will be granted to him."

Another ḥadīth: Imam Aḥmad said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd al-Razzāq, akhbaranā Sufyān, from Layth, from Kaʿb, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you send blessings upon me, ask for al-wasīlah for me." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-wasīlah?" He said: "The highest rank in Paradise, which none will attain except one man, and I hope that I will be he."

al-Tirmidhī narrated it from Bundār, from Abū ʿĀṣim, from Sufyān, that is al-Thawrī, from Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, from Kaʿb, who said: Abū Hurayrah narrated to me, with it. Then he said: "Gharīb (strange). Kaʿb is not well known. We do not know of anyone who narrated from him except Layth ibn Abī Sulaym." [Musnad (2/265) and Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. 3612.]

Another route: from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. Abū Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd al-Bāqī ibn Qāniʿ, ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Naṣr al-Tirmidhī, ḥaddathanā ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Ṣāliḥ, ḥaddathanā Abū Shihāb, from Layth, from al-Muʿallā, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, from Abū Hurayrah, raising it (to the Prophet ﷺ), who said: "Send blessings upon me as you would send blessings, and ask Allah for al-wasīlah for me." They asked him, and he informed them: "al-Wasīlah is a rank in Paradise, which none will attain except one man, and I hope to be him." [In it is Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, who is weak. al-Bazzār narrated it in his Musnad no. 252 (Kashf al-Astār) by another route, from Dāwūd ibn ʿUlayyah, from Layth, from Mujāhid, from Abū Hurayrah, in similar wording. al-Haythamī said: "Dāwūd ibn ʿUlayyah is weak."]

Another ḥadīth: The Ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarānī said: Akhbaranā Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī al-Abbār, ḥaddathanā al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Ḥarrānī, ḥaddathanā Mūsā ibn Aʿyan, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb [in MS h: "Ibn Abī Ḥabīb," which is an error], from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask Allah for al-wasīlah for me, for no servant asks it for me in this world except that I will be a witness for him, or an intercessor, on the Day of Resurrection."

Then al-Ṭabarānī said: "No one narrated it from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb except Mūsā ibn Aʿyan." Thus he said, but Ibn Mardawayh narrated it: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Duḥaym, ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn Ḥāzim, ḥaddathanā ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā, ḥaddathanā Mūsā ibn ʿUbaydah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, and he mentioned its chain with a similar wording. [al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ of al-Ṭabarānī no. 639, Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn. al-Haythamī said in al-Majmaʿ (1/333): "In it is al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Ḥarrānī, whom Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned among the trustworthy and said: 'Sound in narration when he narrates from the trustworthy.' I say: this is from his narration from Mūsā ibn Aʿyan, who is trustworthy."]

Another ḥadīth: Ibn Mardawayh narrated, with his chain, from ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Mūsā ibn Wardān, that he heard Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "al-Wasīlah is a rank with Allah, above which there is no rank, so ask Allah to grant me al-wasīlah above His creation." [al-Ṭabarānī also narrated it in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ nos. 640, 641, Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn, by the route of ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah with it.]

Another ḥadīth: Ibn Mardawayh also narrated by two routes, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Baḥr: Ḥaddathanā Sharīk, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "In Paradise there is a rank called al-wasīlah, so when you ask Allah, ask for al-wasīlah for me." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who will dwell with you?" He said: "ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn." [This ḥadīth is gharīb (strange) and munkar (rejected) through this route. Its strangeness is that it is narrated by ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Baḥr al-Baṣrī, of whom Ibn Ḥibbān said: "He used to steal ḥadīths." Al-Ḥārith is al-Aʿwar, whom al-Shaʿbī called a liar, and a group weakened him.]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, ḥaddathanā al-Ḥasan al-Dashtakī, ḥaddathanā Abū Zuhayr, ḥaddathanā Saʿd [in MS r: "Saʿīd"] ibn Ṭarīf, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Azdī, mawlā of Sālim ibn Thawbān, who said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib calling out from the pulpit of Kufa: "O people, in Paradise there are two pearls: one white and one yellow. As for the yellow one, it is near the bottom of the Throne. The praiseworthy station is in the white pearl, seventy thousand chambers, each house of which is three miles, and its chambers, doors and couches are as if of one vein. Its name is al-Wasīlah, and it belongs to Muḥammad (ﷺ) and his household. The yellow one has the same, and it belongs to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his household."

This is also a gharīb report. [In its chain is Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf al-Iskāfī. Ibn Maʿīn said: "It is not lawful for anyone to narrate from him." Aḥmad and Abū Ḥātim said: "Weak." al-Nasāʾī and al-Dāraquṭnī said: "Matrūk al-ḥadīth (abandoned in narration)." Ibn Ḥibbān said: "He used to fabricate ḥadīths on the spot." Mīzān al-iʿtidāl (2/122).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And strive in His way, that you may prosper﴾. When He commanded them to abandon what is forbidden and to perform acts of obedience, He commanded them to fight the enemies among the disbelievers and polytheists who deviate from the straight path and abandon the upright religion. He encouraged them to do so by what He has prepared for those who strive in His way on the Day of Resurrection: success and great, eternal, lasting happiness that does not perish, change or cease, in lofty, elevated, secure chambers, whose views are beautiful and whose dwellings are good, where whoever dwells is blessed and never despairs, lives and never dies, whose garments do not wear out and whose youth does not fade.

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed of what He has prepared for His enemies, the disbelievers, of punishment and torment on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them; and they will have a painful punishment﴾. That is: even if one of them came on the Day of Resurrection with the earth filled with gold, and the like of it, to ransom himself thereby from the punishment of Allah, which has encompassed him and whose arrival he is certain of, that would not be accepted from him. Rather, there is no escape from it, no refuge, and no way out for him. Therefore He said: ﴿And they will have a painful punishment﴾, that is, agonizing. ﴿They wish to leave the Fire, but they will not be ones who leave it; and for them is a enduring punishment﴾. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Every time they wish to leave it, out of distress, they will be returned into it﴾ [al-Ḥajj 22:22]. So they continually wish to leave what they are in of its severity and painful touch, but there is no way for them to do so. Whenever the flame lifts them and they reach the upper parts of Hell, the angels of punishment strike them with iron maces and return them to its bottom. ﴿And for them is an enduring punishment﴾, that is, lasting and continuous, with no exit for them from it and no escape from it.

Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated from Thābit, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man from the people of the Fire will be brought, and He will say: 'O son of Adam, how did you find your resting place?' He will say: 'The worst resting place.' He will say: 'Would you ransom yourself with the earth's fill of gold?' He will say: 'Yes, my Lord!' He will say: 'You have lied! I asked you for less than that and you did not do it,' and he will be commanded to the Fire."

Muslim and al-Nasāʾī narrated it through the route of Ḥammād ibn Salamah in similar wording. [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 2807, Sunan al-Nasāʾī (6/36).] [In MS d: "al-Bukhārī."] Likewise al-Bukhārī and Muslim narrated it through the route of Muʿādh ibn Hishām al-Dastawāʾī, from his father, from Qatādah, from Anas, with it. [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. 6538 and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 2805.] Likewise they both narrated it through the route of Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, whose name is ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ḥabīb, from Anas ibn Mālik, with it. [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. 6557 and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 2805.] Maṭar al-Warrāq narrated it from Anas ibn Mālik, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through his route, from him.

Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of al-Masʿūdī, from Yazīd ibn Ṣuhayb al-Faqīr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [said] (addition from MSS a, r): "A people will come out of the Fire and enter Paradise." He said: I said to Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh: "Allah says: ﴿They wish to leave the Fire, but they will not be ones who leave it﴾." He said: "Recite the beginning of the verse: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby﴾," to the end of the verse. "Those are the ones who disbelieved."

Imam Aḥmad and Muslim also narrated this ḥadīth through another route, from Yazīd al-Faqīr, from Jābir. [al-Musnad (3/355) and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 191.] This version is more detailed in its wording.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba [in one manuscript: "Ibn Abi Shayba"; in another: "al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba al-Wasiti"] al-Wasiti narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Mubarak ibn Fadala informed us: Yazid al-Faqir narrated to me, saying: I sat with Jabir ibn Abdullah while he was narrating, and he related that some people (in one manuscript: "nasan") would come out of the Fire. He said: At that time I denied this, so I became angry and said: "How strange are people! But I am more amazed at you, O Companions of Muhammad! You claim that Allah brings people out of the Fire, while Allah says: ﴿They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not come out of it, and theirs is a lasting punishment﴾ [Allah's words in the verse are added from another manuscript; in another: "the verse"]. Then his companions rebuked me, and he was the most forbearing of them, and said: "Leave the man alone. That applies only to the disbelievers: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection﴾ until he reached ﴿and theirs is a lasting punishment﴾. Do you not read the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes, indeed, I have memorised it." He said: "Did not Allah say: ﴿And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional [prayer] for you; it is expected that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾? [Al-Isra: 79]. That is that station: Allah [Ta'ala] (added from another manuscript) detains peoples in the Fire for their sins for as long as He wills, not speaking to them; then when He wills to bring them out, He brings them out." He said: After that I never again denied it.

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Daʿlaj ibn Ahmad narrated to us: Amr ibn Hafs al-Sadusi narrated to us: Asim ibn Ali narrated to us: al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl narrated to us: Said ibn al-Muhallab narrated to us: Talq ibn Habib narrated to me, saying: I was among the strongest of people in denying intercession, until I met Jabir ibn Abdullah, and I recited to him every verse I could that mentions the eternal abiding of the people of the Fire (in one manuscript: "and I recited"), in which Allah [Ta'ala] (added from another manuscript) is mentioned. He said: "O Talq, do you think you are a better reciter of the Book of Allah, and more knowledgeable of the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (added from other manuscripts) than I am? Those whom you recited about are its people: they are the polytheists. But these are people who committed sins and were punished, then they were brought out of it." Then he pointed with his hands to his ears and said: "May my ears be deaf if I have not heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'They will come out of the Fire after they had entered it.' And we recite as you recite."

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His believing servants to have taqwa (God-consciousness) of Him. When taqwa is paired with obedience, it means refraining from what is forbidden and abandoning what is prohibited. After this He says: ﴿And seek the means of approach (al-wasilah) to Him﴾. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Ḥaddathanā Abī, from Ṭalḥah, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "That is, the nearness (al-qurbah)." Mujāhid, [ʿAṭāʾ] (addition from MS r), Abū Wāʾil, al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr, al-Suddī and Ibn Zayd said the same.

Qatādah said: "That is, draw near to Him through obedience to Him and by acting in what pleases Him." Ibn Zayd recited: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek the means of approach to their Lord﴾ [al-Isrāʾ 17:57]. What these Imams said is not disputed among the exegetes [in MS r: "there is no disagreement among the exegetes about it"]. Ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] cited as evidence the verse of the poet:

*When the slanderers are heedless, we return to our union,*
*and the sincere friendship between us returns, and the means of approach.*

Al-wasīlah is that by which one reaches the attainment of the desired goal. Al-wasīlah is also a designation for the highest rank in Paradise, the station and abode of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Paradise. It is the closest of Paradise's places to the Throne. It is established in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, through the route of Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, when he hears the call to prayer: 'O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and of the established prayer, grant Muḥammad al-wasīlah and al-faḍīlah, and raise him to the praiseworthy station which You have promised him,' will be granted my intercession on the Day of Resurrection."

Another ḥadīth in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from the narration of Kaʿb, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "When you hear the muʾadhdhin, say the same as he says, then send blessings upon me, for whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah sends blessings upon him tenfold. Then ask Allah for al-wasīlah for me, for it is a station in Paradise, fitting only for one of the servants of Allah, and I hope that I will be he. Whoever asks Allah for al-wasīlah for me, intercession will be granted to him."

Another ḥadīth: Imam Aḥmad said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd al-Razzāq, akhbaranā Sufyān, from Layth, from Kaʿb, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you send blessings upon me, ask for al-wasīlah for me." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-wasīlah?" He said: "The highest rank in Paradise, which none will attain except one man, and I hope that I will be he."

al-Tirmidhī narrated it from Bundār, from Abū ʿĀṣim, from Sufyān, that is al-Thawrī, from Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, from Kaʿb, who said: Abū Hurayrah narrated to me, with it. Then he said: "Gharīb (strange). Kaʿb is not well known. We do not know of anyone who narrated from him except Layth ibn Abī Sulaym." [Musnad (2/265) and Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. 3612.]

Another route: from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. Abū Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd al-Bāqī ibn Qāniʿ, ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Naṣr al-Tirmidhī, ḥaddathanā ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Ṣāliḥ, ḥaddathanā Abū Shihāb, from Layth, from al-Muʿallā, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, from Abū Hurayrah, raising it (to the Prophet ﷺ), who said: "Send blessings upon me as you would send blessings, and ask Allah for al-wasīlah for me." They asked him, and he informed them: "al-Wasīlah is a rank in Paradise, which none will attain except one man, and I hope to be him." [In it is Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, who is weak. al-Bazzār narrated it in his Musnad no. 252 (Kashf al-Astār) by another route, from Dāwūd ibn ʿUlayyah, from Layth, from Mujāhid, from Abū Hurayrah, in similar wording. al-Haythamī said: "Dāwūd ibn ʿUlayyah is weak."]

Another ḥadīth: The Ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarānī said: Akhbaranā Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī al-Abbār, ḥaddathanā al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Ḥarrānī, ḥaddathanā Mūsā ibn Aʿyan, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb [in MS h: "Ibn Abī Ḥabīb," which is an error], from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask Allah for al-wasīlah for me, for no servant asks it for me in this world except that I will be a witness for him, or an intercessor, on the Day of Resurrection."

Then al-Ṭabarānī said: "No one narrated it from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb except Mūsā ibn Aʿyan." Thus he said, but Ibn Mardawayh narrated it: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Duḥaym, ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn Ḥāzim, ḥaddathanā ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā, ḥaddathanā Mūsā ibn ʿUbaydah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, and he mentioned its chain with a similar wording. [al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ of al-Ṭabarānī no. 639, Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn. al-Haythamī said in al-Majmaʿ (1/333): "In it is al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Ḥarrānī, whom Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned among the trustworthy and said: 'Sound in narration when he narrates from the trustworthy.' I say: this is from his narration from Mūsā ibn Aʿyan, who is trustworthy."]

Another ḥadīth: Ibn Mardawayh narrated, with his chain, from ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Mūsā ibn Wardān, that he heard Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "al-Wasīlah is a rank with Allah, above which there is no rank, so ask Allah to grant me al-wasīlah above His creation." [al-Ṭabarānī also narrated it in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ nos. 640, 641, Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn, by the route of ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah with it.]

Another ḥadīth: Ibn Mardawayh also narrated by two routes, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Baḥr: Ḥaddathanā Sharīk, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "In Paradise there is a rank called al-wasīlah, so when you ask Allah, ask for al-wasīlah for me." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who will dwell with you?" He said: "ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn." [This ḥadīth is gharīb (strange) and munkar (rejected) through this route. Its strangeness is that it is narrated by ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Baḥr al-Baṣrī, of whom Ibn Ḥibbān said: "He used to steal ḥadīths." Al-Ḥārith is al-Aʿwar, whom al-Shaʿbī called a liar, and a group weakened him.]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, ḥaddathanā al-Ḥasan al-Dashtakī, ḥaddathanā Abū Zuhayr, ḥaddathanā Saʿd [in MS r: "Saʿīd"] ibn Ṭarīf, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Azdī, mawlā of Sālim ibn Thawbān, who said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib calling out from the pulpit of Kufa: "O people, in Paradise there are two pearls: one white and one yellow. As for the yellow one, it is near the bottom of the Throne. The praiseworthy station is in the white pearl, seventy thousand chambers, each house of which is three miles, and its chambers, doors and couches are as if of one vein. Its name is al-Wasīlah, and it belongs to Muḥammad (ﷺ) and his household. The yellow one has the same, and it belongs to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his household."

This is also a gharīb report. [In its chain is Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf al-Iskāfī. Ibn Maʿīn said: "It is not lawful for anyone to narrate from him." Aḥmad and Abū Ḥātim said: "Weak." al-Nasāʾī and al-Dāraquṭnī said: "Matrūk al-ḥadīth (abandoned in narration)." Ibn Ḥibbān said: "He used to fabricate ḥadīths on the spot." Mīzān al-iʿtidāl (2/122).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And strive in His way, that you may prosper﴾. When He commanded them to abandon what is forbidden and to perform acts of obedience, He commanded them to fight the enemies among the disbelievers and polytheists who deviate from the straight path and abandon the upright religion. He encouraged them to do so by what He has prepared for those who strive in His way on the Day of Resurrection: success and great, eternal, lasting happiness that does not perish, change or cease, in lofty, elevated, secure chambers, whose views are beautiful and whose dwellings are good, where whoever dwells is blessed and never despairs, lives and never dies, whose garments do not wear out and whose youth does not fade.

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed of what He has prepared for His enemies, the disbelievers, of punishment and torment on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them; and they will have a painful punishment﴾. That is: even if one of them came on the Day of Resurrection with the earth filled with gold, and the like of it, to ransom himself thereby from the punishment of Allah, which has encompassed him and whose arrival he is certain of, that would not be accepted from him. Rather, there is no escape from it, no refuge, and no way out for him. Therefore He said: ﴿And they will have a painful punishment﴾, that is, agonizing. ﴿They wish to leave the Fire, but they will not be ones who leave it; and for them is a enduring punishment﴾. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Every time they wish to leave it, out of distress, they will be returned into it﴾ [al-Ḥajj 22:22]. So they continually wish to leave what they are in of its severity and painful touch, but there is no way for them to do so. Whenever the flame lifts them and they reach the upper parts of Hell, the angels of punishment strike them with iron maces and return them to its bottom. ﴿And for them is an enduring punishment﴾, that is, lasting and continuous, with no exit for them from it and no escape from it.

Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated from Thābit, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man from the people of the Fire will be brought, and He will say: 'O son of Adam, how did you find your resting place?' He will say: 'The worst resting place.' He will say: 'Would you ransom yourself with the earth's fill of gold?' He will say: 'Yes, my Lord!' He will say: 'You have lied! I asked you for less than that and you did not do it,' and he will be commanded to the Fire."

Muslim and al-Nasāʾī narrated it through the route of Ḥammād ibn Salamah in similar wording. [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 2807, Sunan al-Nasāʾī (6/36).] [In MS d: "al-Bukhārī."] Likewise al-Bukhārī and Muslim narrated it through the route of Muʿādh ibn Hishām al-Dastawāʾī, from his father, from Qatādah, from Anas, with it. [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. 6538 and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 2805.] Likewise they both narrated it through the route of Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, whose name is ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ḥabīb, from Anas ibn Mālik, with it. [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. 6557 and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 2805.] Maṭar al-Warrāq narrated it from Anas ibn Mālik, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through his route, from him.

Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of al-Masʿūdī, from Yazīd ibn Ṣuhayb al-Faqīr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [said] (addition from MSS a, r): "A people will come out of the Fire and enter Paradise." He said: I said to Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh: "Allah says: ﴿They wish to leave the Fire, but they will not be ones who leave it﴾." He said: "Recite the beginning of the verse: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby﴾," to the end of the verse. "Those are the ones who disbelieved."

Imam Aḥmad and Muslim also narrated this ḥadīth through another route, from Yazīd al-Faqīr, from Jābir. [al-Musnad (3/355) and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 191.] This version is more detailed in its wording.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba [in one manuscript: "Ibn Abi Shayba"; in another: "al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba al-Wasiti"] al-Wasiti narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Mubarak ibn Fadala informed us: Yazid al-Faqir narrated to me, saying: I sat with Jabir ibn Abdullah while he was narrating, and he related that some people (in one manuscript: "nasan") would come out of the Fire. He said: At that time I denied this, so I became angry and said: "How strange are people! But I am more amazed at you, O Companions of Muhammad! You claim that Allah brings people out of the Fire, while Allah says: ﴿They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not come out of it, and theirs is a lasting punishment﴾ [Allah's words in the verse are added from another manuscript; in another: "the verse"]. Then his companions rebuked me, and he was the most forbearing of them, and said: "Leave the man alone. That applies only to the disbelievers: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection﴾ until he reached ﴿and theirs is a lasting punishment﴾. Do you not read the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes, indeed, I have memorised it." He said: "Did not Allah say: ﴿And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional [prayer] for you; it is expected that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾? [Al-Isra: 79]. That is that station: Allah [Ta'ala] (added from another manuscript) detains peoples in the Fire for their sins for as long as He wills, not speaking to them; then when He wills to bring them out, He brings them out." He said: After that I never again denied it.

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Daʿlaj ibn Ahmad narrated to us: Amr ibn Hafs al-Sadusi narrated to us: Asim ibn Ali narrated to us: al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl narrated to us: Said ibn al-Muhallab narrated to us: Talq ibn Habib narrated to me, saying: I was among the strongest of people in denying intercession, until I met Jabir ibn Abdullah, and I recited to him every verse I could that mentions the eternal abiding of the people of the Fire (in one manuscript: "and I recited"), in which Allah [Ta'ala] (added from another manuscript) is mentioned. He said: "O Talq, do you think you are a better reciter of the Book of Allah, and more knowledgeable of the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (added from other manuscripts) than I am? Those whom you recited about are its people: they are the polytheists. But these are people who committed sins and were punished, then they were brought out of it." Then he pointed with his hands to his ears and said: "May my ears be deaf if I have not heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'They will come out of the Fire after they had entered it.' And we recite as you recite."

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, commentary on Surah 5, verses 38–40 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, says, judging and commanding the cutting off of the hand of the male thief and the female thief. Al-Thawri narrated from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from 'Amir ibn Sharahil al-Sha'bi, that Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it: "And the male thief and the female thief, cut off their right hands." This is an irregular recitation (*qira'ah shadhdhah*), and although the ruling is in agreement with it among all the scholars, it is not based on it. Rather, it is derived from another proof. Cutting off the hand was practiced in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period), and Islam confirmed it, with other conditions added, as we will mention, if Allah the Exalted wills. Likewise, the *qasama* (oath procedure in homicide cases), the *diyya* (blood money), the *qiradh* (profit-sharing partnership) and other matters were confirmed by the Law as they were, along with additions that complete the public interests.

It is said that the first to cut off hands in the Jahiliyyah were the Quraysh. They cut off the hand of a man called Duwayk, a freed slave of the Banu Mulayh ibn 'Amr of Khuza'ah, who had stolen the treasure of the Ka'bah. It is also said that a group stole it and then placed it with him.

Some jurists of the Zahiriyyah (literalist school) held that whenever a thief steals anything, his hand is cut off for it, whether it is little or much, based on the generality of this verse: ﴿And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands﴾. They did not consider the minimum amount (*nisab*) or the protected place (*hirz*), but acted on the mere act of theft.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through 'Abd al-Mu'min, from Najdah al-Hanafi, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about His saying: ﴿And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands﴾, "Is it specific or general?" He said: "Rather, it is general."

This may be an agreement by Ibn 'Abbas with what those people held, and it may be otherwise, and Allah knows best.

They also relied on what is established in the two *Sahihs* (Bukhari and Muslim), from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "May Allah curse the thief who steals an egg and has his hand cut off, and steals a rope and has his hand cut off." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6799, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1687.]

As for the majority, they considered the *nisab* in theft, although they differed about its amount. Each of the four Imams went to a separate position. According to Imam Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, the *nisab* is three minted dirhams of pure silver. Whenever he steals them, or something whose value reaches them or exceeds them, the cutting is obligatory. He argued for this with what he narrated from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut off the hand for a shield (*mijann*) whose price was three dirhams. Both (Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the two *Sahihs*. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6797, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1686.]

Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, cut off the hand in the case of a citron (*utrujjah*) that was valued at three dirhams, and this is the most beloved of what I have heard on this matter." This report from 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, was narrated by Malik from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from his father, from 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman: that a thief stole a citron during the time of 'Uthman, so 'Uthman ordered that it be valued, and it was valued at three dirhams in exchange for twelve dirhams to a dinar, and 'Uthman cut off his hand. [Al-Muwatta' (2/832).]

The companions of Malik said: "Such an action becomes well known and is not denounced, and from this kind of thing the silent consensus (*ijma' sukuti*) is reported." In it there is evidence for cutting off the hand for fruits, contrary to the Hanafis, and for the reckoning of three dirhams, contrary to them in their view that ten dirhams are required. The Shafi'is hold a quarter dinar, and Allah knows best.

Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, held that the standard for cutting off the thief's hand is a quarter of a dinar or what equals it in currency or goods, or more. His proof is what the two Shaykhs, al-Bukhari and Muslim, recorded through the chain of al-Zuhri, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The hand of the thief is cut off for a quarter of a dinar or more." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6789, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1684.]

Muslim also has, through the chain of Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The hand of the thief is not cut off except for a quarter of a dinar or more." [Sahih Muslim (1684).]

Our companions said: "This hadith is decisive on the issue and explicit in establishing the quarter dinar, not what equals it." They said: "The hadith of the price of the shield, that it was three dirhams, does not contradict this, because at that time the dinar was equal to twelve dirhams, so three dirhams was the price of a quarter dinar. Thus reconciliation is possible in this way."

This view is reported from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'Uthman ibn 'Affan and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with them. It is also the view of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i and his companions, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh (in one of his reports), Abu Thawr, and Dawud ibn 'Ali al-Zahiri, may Allah have mercy on them all.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh (in one of his reports) held that each of the quarter dinar and the three dirhams is a legal standard (*marad shar'i*). So whoever steals either one of them, or what equals it, has his hand cut off, acting upon the hadith of Ibn 'Umar and the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them both. In a wording in the *Musnad* of Imam Ahmad, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Cut off (the hand) for a quarter of a dinar, and do not cut off for what is less than that." A quarter of a dinar at that time was three dirhams, and the dinar was twelve dirhams. In a wording of al-Nasa'i: "The hand of the thief is not cut off for less than the price of the shield." It was said to 'A'ishah: "What is the price of the shield?" She said: "A quarter of a dinar." [Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/80).]

All of these are texts indicating that ten dirhams is not a requirement, and Allah knows best.

As for Imam Abu Hanifah and his companions, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad, Zufar, and likewise Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on them, they held that the *nisab* is ten minted dirhams that are not adulterated. They argued that the price of the shield for which the thief was cut off during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was ten dirhams. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated: "Ibn Numayr and 'Abd al-A'la told us, and from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The price of the shield during the time of the Prophet ﷺ was ten dirhams." [Al-Musannaf (9/474). Al-Daraqutni narrated it in al-Sunan (3/191) through the chain of Muhammad ibn Ishaq.]

Then he said: "'Abd al-A'la told us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'The hand of the thief is not cut off for less than the price of the shield.' And the price of the shield was ten dirhams." [Al-Musannaf (9/474). Al-Daraqutni narrated it in al-Sunan (3/190) through the chain of Muhammad ibn Ishaq. The hadith is confused (*mudtarib*): it was narrated differently on Muhammad ibn Ishaq, as you see, and it has been narrated through many other routes.]

They said: "Here Ibn 'Abbas and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr have contradicted Ibn 'Umar regarding the price of the shield, so caution lies in taking the higher figure, because the *hudud* (fixed punishments) are averted by doubts."

Some of the early scholars (*salaf*) held that the hand of the thief is cut off for ten dirhams, or one dinar, or whatever its value reaches of either of them. This is reported from 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, may Allah have mercy on them all.

Some of the early scholars said: "The five is not cut off except for five," that is, five dinars or fifty dirhams. This is reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, may Allah have mercy on him.

The majority have answered what the Zahiris relied upon from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, "He steals an egg and has his hand cut off, and steals a rope and has his hand cut off," with several answers:

First: It has been abrogated (*mansukh*) by the hadith of 'A'ishah. But this is open to scrutiny, because the date (of the two hadiths) must be established.

Second: It is to be interpreted as referring to an iron helmet (*bayd al-hadid*) and the rope of ships, as said by al-A'mash, as narrated by al-Bukhari and others from him.

Third: This is a means of gradual progression in theft, from the small to the large amount for which the hand is cut off. It is possible that this was stated as a report about what the situation was in the Jahiliyyah, when they cut off hands for little and much, so the curse fell upon the thief who spends a precious hand on lowly things.

It is mentioned that Abu al-'Ala' al-Ma'arri, when he came to Baghdad, became known for raising an objection against the jurists for making the *nisab* of theft a quarter of a dinar. He composed poetry on this which showed his ignorance and his lack of intellect. He said:

"A hand is worth five hundred gold dinars, so why is it cut off for a quarter dinar...
There is nothing for us but silence about it, and that we seek refuge in our Lord from the Fire."

[Al-Dhahabi narrated both in *Siyar A'lam al-Nubala'* (18/30).]

When he said that, and it became known about him, the jurists sought him, and he fled from them. People answered him on this matter. The response of the Maliki judge 'Abd al-Wahhab, may Allah have mercy on him, was that he said: "When it was trustworthy, it was valuable; when it betrayed, it became worthless." Others said: "This is part of the complete wisdom, the public interest, and the great secrets of the Shari'ah. In the chapter on injuries (*jinayat*), it is fitting that the value of the hand be made five hundred dinars, so that it is not harmed. In the chapter on theft, it is fitting that the amount for which the hand is cut off be a quarter of a dinar, so that people do not rush to steal property. This is the very wisdom according to people of understanding."

For this reason He, the Exalted, said: ﴿As a recompense for what they earned, a punishment from Allah. And Allah is Almighty and All-Wise﴾, that is, as a repayment for their evil action in taking people's property with their hands. So it is fitting that what they used in that be cut off. ﴿A punishment from Allah﴾, that is, a deterrent from Allah against them for committing it. ﴿And Allah is Almighty﴾, that is, in His retribution. ﴿All-Wise﴾, that is, in His command, His prohibition, His legislation and His decree.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and makes amends, indeed Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is: whoever repents after his theft and turns back to Allah, then Allah will turn to him in forgiveness regarding what is between him and Allah. As for the property of people, it must be returned to them or its equivalent given, according to the majority.

Abu Hanifah said: Whenever the hand is cut off and the property has been destroyed in his possession, he does not return its equivalent. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni narrated through the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thawban, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought a thief who had stolen a cloak (*shamlah*). He said: "I do not think he stole," but the thief said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Take him away and cut off his hand, then cauterize the stump, then bring him back to me." His hand was cut off and he was brought back, and he said: "Repent to Allah." He said: "I have repented to Allah." He said: "May Allah accept your repentance." [Sunan al-Daraqutni (3/102). Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (4/381) through the chain of Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thawban, connected to the Prophet ﷺ, and said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi remained silent about it.]

And it has been narrated by another route as a *mursal* (a report whose chain omits the Companion). Ali ibn al-Madini and Ibn Khuzaymah preferred its *irsal* (being *mursal*), may Allah have mercy on them both. [[Narrated by al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan (3/103), Abu Dawud in al-Marasil (no. 244), and Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (no. 13583), through Sufyan from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Thawban as a mursal.]] Ibn Majah narrated, through Ibn Lahi'ah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Tha'labah al-Ansari, from his father: [[In manuscript A: "And it has been narrated."]] that Amr ibn Samurah ibn Habib ibn Abd Shams came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have stolen a camel belonging to so-and-so, so purify me!" The Prophet ﷺ sent for them, and they said: "We have missed a camel of ours." So he ordered that his hand be cut off. Tha'labah said: "I was looking at him when his hand fell, and he was saying: 'Praise be to Allah who purified me from you! You wanted to bring my body into the Fire.'" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2588. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/317): "This isnad is weak because of the weakness of Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah."]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Hayy ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: A woman stole some jewelry. Those whose property she had stolen came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this woman stole from us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Cut off her right hand." The woman said: "Is there any repentance for me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Today you are free of your sin as on the day your mother bore you!" He said: Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿So whoever repents after his wrongdoing and makes amends, indeed Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (10/299).]]

Imam Ahmad narrated this with a fuller version. He said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Hayy ibn Abdullah narrated to me, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abdullah ibn Amr: that a woman stole during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Those whose property she had stolen brought her and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this woman stole from us!" Her people said: "We will ransom her." The Messenger of Allah said: "Cut off her hand." They said: "We will ransom her for five hundred dinars." He said: "Cut off her hand." He said: So her right hand was cut off. The woman said: "Is there any repentance for me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes. Today you are free of your sin as on the day your mother bore you." Then Allah revealed in Surat al-Ma'idah: ﴿So whoever repents after his wrongdoing and makes amends, indeed Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾ [[Al-Musnad (2/177).]]

This woman was the Makhzumiyyah who stole, and her story is authentic in the *Sahihayn* (the two *Sahih* collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim), through al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah: that the Quraysh were concerned about the matter of the woman who stole during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, at the conquest (Ghazwat al-Fath). They said: "Who will speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about her?" They said: "Who would dare to do it except Usamah ibn Zayd, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" So she was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Usamah ibn Zayd spoke to him about her. The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed color, and he said: "Do you intercede concerning one of the *hudud* (fixed punishments) of Allah, mighty and majestic?" Usamah said to him: "Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allah." When evening came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and gave a sermon. He praised Allah as is fitting for Him, then said: "To proceed: Those before you were destroyed because when a noble person stole among them, they left him, and when a weak person stole among them, they enforced the punishment upon him. By the One in whose hand my soul is, if Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, were to steal, I would cut off her hand." Then he ordered that the woman who had stolen be brought, and her hand was cut off. Aishah said: "Her repentance was good afterward, she married, and she would come afterward and I would raise her needs to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." [[Aishah's narration in the Sahihayn is a text of Muslim.]]

This is the wording of Muslim [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2648; Sahih Muslim, no. 1688.]]. In another wording of his, from Aishah, she said: "There was a woman from the Makhzum who would borrow goods and deny having them, so the Prophet of Allah ﷺ ordered that her hand be cut off." [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1688.]]

And from Ibn Umar, who said: "There was a woman from the Makhzum who would borrow goods through the tongues of her neighbors and deny them, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that her hand be cut off." It was narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i [[Al-Musnad (2/151); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4395; Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/70).]], and this is the wording of al-Nasa'i. In another wording of his: "A woman used to borrow jewelry from people and then keep it, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Let this woman repent to Allah and His Messenger, and return what she takes from the people.' Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Stand up, O Bilal, take her by the hand and cut it off.'" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/71).]]

Many hadiths concerning the rulings on theft have been recorded in the book *al-Ahkam* (the Book of Rulings), and to Allah belong praise and favor.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ That is, He is the Owner of all of that, the Judge over it, whose judgment none can reverse, and He is the one who does whatever He wills. ﴿He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills﴾ [[In manuscript R: "He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wwills", which is an error.]] ﴿and Allah is over all things Competent.﴾

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, commentary on Surah 5, verses 38–40 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, says, judging and commanding the cutting off of the hand of the male thief and the female thief. Al-Thawri narrated from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from 'Amir ibn Sharahil al-Sha'bi, that Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it: "And the male thief and the female thief, cut off their right hands." This is an irregular recitation (*qira'ah shadhdhah*), and although the ruling is in agreement with it among all the scholars, it is not based on it. Rather, it is derived from another proof. Cutting off the hand was practiced in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period), and Islam confirmed it, with other conditions added, as we will mention, if Allah the Exalted wills. Likewise, the *qasama* (oath procedure in homicide cases), the *diyya* (blood money), the *qiradh* (profit-sharing partnership) and other matters were confirmed by the Law as they were, along with additions that complete the public interests.

It is said that the first to cut off hands in the Jahiliyyah were the Quraysh. They cut off the hand of a man called Duwayk, a freed slave of the Banu Mulayh ibn 'Amr of Khuza'ah, who had stolen the treasure of the Ka'bah. It is also said that a group stole it and then placed it with him.

Some jurists of the Zahiriyyah (literalist school) held that whenever a thief steals anything, his hand is cut off for it, whether it is little or much, based on the generality of this verse: ﴿And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands﴾. They did not consider the minimum amount (*nisab*) or the protected place (*hirz*), but acted on the mere act of theft.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through 'Abd al-Mu'min, from Najdah al-Hanafi, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about His saying: ﴿And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands﴾, "Is it specific or general?" He said: "Rather, it is general."

This may be an agreement by Ibn 'Abbas with what those people held, and it may be otherwise, and Allah knows best.

They also relied on what is established in the two *Sahihs* (Bukhari and Muslim), from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "May Allah curse the thief who steals an egg and has his hand cut off, and steals a rope and has his hand cut off." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6799, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1687.]

As for the majority, they considered the *nisab* in theft, although they differed about its amount. Each of the four Imams went to a separate position. According to Imam Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, the *nisab* is three minted dirhams of pure silver. Whenever he steals them, or something whose value reaches them or exceeds them, the cutting is obligatory. He argued for this with what he narrated from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut off the hand for a shield (*mijann*) whose price was three dirhams. Both (Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the two *Sahihs*. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6797, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1686.]

Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, cut off the hand in the case of a citron (*utrujjah*) that was valued at three dirhams, and this is the most beloved of what I have heard on this matter." This report from 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, was narrated by Malik from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from his father, from 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman: that a thief stole a citron during the time of 'Uthman, so 'Uthman ordered that it be valued, and it was valued at three dirhams in exchange for twelve dirhams to a dinar, and 'Uthman cut off his hand. [Al-Muwatta' (2/832).]

The companions of Malik said: "Such an action becomes well known and is not denounced, and from this kind of thing the silent consensus (*ijma' sukuti*) is reported." In it there is evidence for cutting off the hand for fruits, contrary to the Hanafis, and for the reckoning of three dirhams, contrary to them in their view that ten dirhams are required. The Shafi'is hold a quarter dinar, and Allah knows best.

Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, held that the standard for cutting off the thief's hand is a quarter of a dinar or what equals it in currency or goods, or more. His proof is what the two Shaykhs, al-Bukhari and Muslim, recorded through the chain of al-Zuhri, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The hand of the thief is cut off for a quarter of a dinar or more." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6789, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1684.]

Muslim also has, through the chain of Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The hand of the thief is not cut off except for a quarter of a dinar or more." [Sahih Muslim (1684).]

Our companions said: "This hadith is decisive on the issue and explicit in establishing the quarter dinar, not what equals it." A quarter of a dinar at that time was three dirhams, and the dinar was twelve dirhams. In a wording of al-Nasa'i: "The hand of the thief is not cut off for less than the price of the shield." It was said to 'A'ishah: "What is the price of the shield?" She said: "A quarter of a dinar." [Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/80).]
