He lifted it, and the verse of stoning was shining forth. He said, "O Muhammad, indeed in it is the verse of stoning, but we have been concealing it among ourselves." So he commanded that the two be stoned.

In Muslim's version: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought a Jewish man and a Jewish woman who had committed adultery. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out until he came to the Jews and said, "What do you find in the Torah concerning one who commits adultery?" They said, "We blacken their faces, put them on a donkey facing backwards, and we parade them about." He said, ﴿Then bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾. He said: They brought it and read it, until when he came to the verse of stoning, the young man who was reading placed his hand over the verse of stoning and read what was before it and what was after it. Abdullah ibn Salam, who was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said to him, "Tell him to lift his hand." He lifted his hand, and beneath it was the verse of stoning. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that the two be stoned. Abdullah ibn Umar said, "I was among those who stoned them, and I saw him shielding her from the stones with his own body."

Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, that Zayd ibn Aslam related to him, from Ibn Umar, who said: A group of Jews came, and they invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to al-Quff, so he came to them in the house of study. They said, "O Abu al-Qasim, a man among us has committed adultery with a woman, so judge." He said: They placed a cushion for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he sat upon it. Then he said, "Bring me the Torah." It was brought, so he pulled the cushion from beneath him and placed the Torah upon it, and said, "I believe in you and in the One who revealed you." Then he said, "Bring me your most learned man." A young man was brought, and then he related the story of stoning similar to the hadith of Malik from Nafi'.

Al-Zuhri said: I heard a man of Muzaynah, one of those who follow knowledge and retain it, while we were with Ibn al-Musayyib, relating from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A Jewish man committed adultery with a woman. Some of them said to others, "Go to this Prophet, for he was sent with leniency. If he gives us a ruling short of stoning, we will accept it and argue with it before Allah, saying, 'It is the ruling of one of Your prophets.'" They came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was sitting in the mosque among his companions, and said, "O Abu al-Qasim, what do you say about a man and a woman among us who committed adultery?" He did not speak to them a word until he came to their house of study, and stood at the door, and said, "I adjure you by Allah, who revealed the Torah to Musa: what do you find in the Torah concerning one who commits adultery when he is married?" They said, "He is blackened, humiliated, and flogged." Al-Tajbiyah is that the two adulterers are placed upon a donkey with their backs facing each other, and they are paraded about. He said: A young man among them remained silent. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw that he was silent, he pressed him with the adjuration, saying, "O Allah, since You have made us swear, indeed we find stoning in the Torah." The Prophet ﷺ said, "What was the first thing by which you relaxed the command of Allah?" He said, "A close relative of one of our kings committed adultery, so they delayed stoning for him. Then a man among the common people committed adultery after him, and they wanted to stone him, but his people intervened and said, 'Our companion shall not be stoned until you bring your companion and stone him!' So they agreed upon this punishment among themselves." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Then I judge by what is in the Torah," and he commanded that the two be stoned. Al-Zuhri said: It reached us that this verse was revealed concerning them: ﴿Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which is guidance and light, by which the prophets who submitted judged﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:44]. And the Prophet ﷺ was among them.

Ahmad and Abu Dawud related it, and this is the wording of Abu Dawud, as did Ibn Jarir.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: A Jewish man who had been blackened and flogged passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He summoned them and said, "Is this how you find the prescribed punishment for an adulterer in your Book?" They said, "Yes." He summoned a man of their scholars and said, "I adjure you by Him who revealed the Torah to Musa: is this how you find the prescribed punishment for an adulterer in your Book?" He said, "No, by Allah, and were it not that you adjured me by this, I would not have told you. We find the punishment for an adulterer in our Book to be stoning, but it became widespread among our nobles. When we seized a nobleman, we left him, and when we seized a weak person, we enforced the punishment upon him. So we said, 'Come, let us establish something to apply to both the noble and the lowly.' So we agreed upon blackening and flogging." The Prophet ﷺ said, "O Allah, I am the first to revive Your command after they had caused it to die." He said: So he commanded that the man be stoned. He said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O Messenger, let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelief﴾ up to His saying ﴿They say, "If you are given this, take it"﴾, meaning they say, "Go to Muhammad. If he rules for you with blackening and flogging, take it, but if he rules for you with stoning, beware," up to His saying ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers﴾. He said: concerning the Jews, up to His saying ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the wrongdoers﴾. He said: concerning the Jews [in one version: the Christians], ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the defiantly disobedient﴾. He said: concerning the disbelievers in general.

Muslim alone among the compilers reported it, apart from al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, through several chains, from al-A'mash, with the same wording.

Imam Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi said in his Musnad: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Mujalid ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: A man from the people of Fadak committed adultery, so the people of Fadak wrote to some Jews in Medina: "Ask Muhammad about this. If he orders you to flog, then accept it from him, but if he orders you to stone, then do not accept it from him." They asked him about it. He said, "Send for me the two most learned men among you." They brought a one-eyed man, called Ibn Suriya, and another. The Prophet ﷺ said to them, "Are you the most learned of those who came before you?" They said, "Our people have summoned us for this." The Prophet ﷺ said to them, "Do you not have the Torah in which is the judgment of Allah?" They said, "Yes." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Then I adjure you by Him who split the sea for the Children of Israel, shaded you with clouds, delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, and sent down manna and quail upon the Children of Israel: what do you find in the Torah concerning the matter of stoning?" One of them said to the other, "I have never been adjured with the like of this." They said, "We find that prolonged gazing is adultery, embracing is adultery, and kissing is adultery. If four witnesses testify that they saw him inserting and withdrawing, like the kohl stick entering the kohl pot, then stoning is obligatory." The Prophet ﷺ said, "That is it." He commanded that he be stoned, and it was stoned. Then this was revealed: ﴿So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:42].

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah related it through the hadith of Mujalid, similarly. The wording of Abu Dawud from Jabir is: The Jews brought a man and a woman from among them who had committed adultery. He said, "Bring me the two most learned men among you." They brought the two sons of Suriya. He adjured them: "How do you find the matter of these two in the Torah?" They said, "We find in the Torah that when four witnesses testify that they saw his member in her private part like the kohl stick in the kohl pot, they are stoned." He said, "Then what prevents you from stoning them?" They said, "Our authority has gone, so we disliked killing." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for the witnesses, and four came and testified that they saw his member in her private part like the kohl stick in the kohl pot. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that the two be stoned.

Then Abu Dawud related it from al-Sha'bi and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i as a mursal report [a report in which the Companion is omitted from the chain], and he did not mention in it: "He called the witnesses, and they testified."

Therefore these are hadiths indicating that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) judged in accordance with the ruling of the Torah. This is not a case of obligating them to what they themselves hold to be authentic, for they are in any case commanded to follow the Muhammadan Law. Rather, this was by a special revelation from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to him concerning that, and his questioning of them about it was to make them acknowledge what was in their hands, which they had agreed to conceal and deny, and not to act upon, for those long ages. So when they admitted it while their practice was contrary to it, it showed that their deviation, their obstinacy, and their denial of what they themselves held to be authentic from the Book that was in their hands, and their turning to the arbitration of the Messenger (ﷺ), was only from their own caprice and desire, to match their opinions, not from belief in the validity of what he judged. Hence they said: ﴿If you are given this, then accept it﴾, i.e., accept it, ﴿but if you are not given it, then beware﴾, i.e., beware of accepting and following it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whomever Allah intends for trial, you will not control for him anything from Allah. Those are the ones whose hearts Allah did not intend to purify. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. They are listeners to falsehood, devourers of unlawful gain﴾, i.e., the prohibited, which is bribery, as said by Ibn Mas'ud and others. That is: how can Allah purify the heart of one who has this description, and how could He respond to him?

Then He said to His Prophet: ﴿So if they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all﴾, i.e., there is no blame upon you for not judging between them, because they do not seek by their arbitration to you to follow the truth, but rather whatever matches their desire.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Zayd ibn Aslam, and 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: it is abrogated by His saying: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 49], and ﴿And if you judge, then judge between them with justice﴾, i.e., with truth and fairness, even if they are wrongdoers who have departed from the path of justice. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.﴾

Then He said, exed, denouncing them for their corrupt opinions and their deviant intentions, in their abandoning what they held to be authentic from the Book that was in their hands, which they claim they are commanded to adhere to forever, and then they departed from its ruling and turned to something else, which they in reality believe to be void and not binding upon them. He said: ﴿And how do they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is the judgement of Allah? Then they turn away after that. And those are not believers.﴾

Then He praised the Torah which He sent down to His servant and messenger Musa son of 'Imran, saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light. By it the prophets who submitted judge for the Jews, and the rabbis and scholars [judge] by what they were entrusted of the Book of Allah.﴾ That is, they do not depart from its ruling, nor alter it, nor distort it. ﴿And the rabbis and the scholars﴾, i.e., likewise the rabbis among them, who are the scholarly worshippers, and the scholars, who are the learned ones, ﴿by what they were entrusted of the Book of Allah﴾, i.e., by what was deposited with them of the Book of Allah, which they were commanded to make manifest and act upon. ﴿And they were witnesses over it. So do not fear the people, but fear Me.﴾ That is, do not be afraid of them, and fear Me. ﴿And do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers.﴾ Concerning this there are two opinions which will come with their explanation. Another cause of revelation of these noble verses:

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn al-'Abbas narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from his father, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah sent down: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾, and ﴿those are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 45], ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 47]. He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah sent them down concerning the two groups of the Jews. One of them had overpowered the other in the Jahiliyyah, until they agreed or made peace on the basis that for every person slain by the strong from the weak, the blood-money would be fifty wasq, and for every person slain by the weak from the strong, the blood-money would be one hundred wasq. They remained upon that until the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah, and both groups were humbled by the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), though at that time he had not yet prevailed, and had not yet made them subject to him, and they were in a state of truce. Then the weak group killed a man from the strong group, and the strong group sent to the weak group: Send us one hundred wasq. The weak group said: Has there ever been such a thing between two tribes whose religion is one, whose lineage is one, and whose land is one: the blood-money of one part is half the blood-money of the other? We only gave you this out of oppression from you toward us and fear of you. But now that Muhammad has come, we will not give you that. War nearly erupted between them. Then they agreed to make the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) an arbiter between them. Then the strong group remembered and said: By Allah, Muhammad will not give you from them double what he gives them from you. And indeed they spoke truly; they had only given us this out of oppression from us and subjugation of them. So they sent to Muhammad a person to find out his opinion: if he gives you what you want, you will accept his judgement, and if he does not give you, be wary, and do not accept his judgement. They sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) some hypocrites to find out the opinion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of all their affair and what they intended. Then Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿O Messenger, do not let those grieve you who race to disbelief﴾ up to His saying ﴿the defiantly disobedient﴾. By Allah, it was concerning them that it was sent down, and it was them whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, meant. [Al-Musnad (1/246)]

Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi al-Zinad, from his father, similarly.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Hannad ibn al-Sari and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, both saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the verses in al-Ma'idah, from His saying ﴿so judge between them or turn away from them﴾ up to ﴿the just﴾, were revealed only concerning the blood-money among the Banu al-Nadir and the Banu Qurayzah. That was because the slain of the Banu al-Nadir had nobility, and the blood-money was paid in full, while the Banu Qurayzah were paying half the blood-money. They brought their dispute to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah sent down that concerning them, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) directed them to the truth in that matter, and made the blood-money equal in that — and Allah knows best which of these it was.

Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/326), al-Musnad (1/363), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3591), Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/19)]

Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Salih, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Qurayzah and al-Nadir — al-Nadir was more noble than Qurayzah. So if a man of Qurayzah killed a man of al-Nadir, he was killed for him; and if a man of al-Nadir killed a man of Qurayzah, he paid one hundred wasq of dates as blood-money. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent, a man of al-Nadir killed a man of Qurayzah. They said: Hand him over to us. They said: Between us and you is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So ﴿And if you judge, then judge between them with justice﴾ was revealed.

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak narrated it from the hadith of 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa, similarly. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/327), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4494), Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/18), al-Mustadrak (4/366)]

Likewise said Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Ibn Zayd, and others.

It has also been narrated by al-'Awfi and 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah al-Walibi, from Ibn 'Abbas, that these verses were revealed concerning the two Jews who committed adultery, as the hadiths concerning that have already preceded. It may be that these two causes coincided at one time, so these verses were revealed concerning all of that, and Allah knows best.

Hence He said after that: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein that the soul is for the soul, and the eye for the eye﴾ up to its end. This strengthens that the cause of revelation was the matter of retaliation (qisas), and Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾, al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Mijlaz, Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, 'Ikrimah, 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah, al-Hasan al-Basri, and others said: it was revealed concerning the People of the Book. Al-Hasan al-Basri added: and it is binding upon us.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: These verses were revealed concerning the Children of Israel, and Allah was pleased with them for this Ummah. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Jarir also said: Ya'qub narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman informed us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from 'Alqamah and Masruq that they both asked Ibn Mas'ud about bribery. He said: It is from the unlawful gain. They said: And what about in judgement? He said: That is disbelief! Then he recited: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾ means: whoever does not judge by what I have sent down, abandoning it deliberately, or acts unjustly while knowing, he is among the disbelievers [in it].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾, that he said: Whoever denies what Allah has revealed has disbelieved; and whoever affirms it but does not judge by it is a wrongdoer and a defiantly disobedient sinner. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Then he (Ibn Jarir) preferred that the verse is meant concerning the People of the Book, or whoever denies the ruling of Allah revealed in the Book.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from al-Thawri, from Zakariyya, from al-Sha'bi: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed﴾ — he said: it is for the Muslims.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi al-Safar, from al-Sha'bi: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾ — he said: this is concerning the Muslims. ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the wrongdoers﴾ — he said: this is concerning the Jews. ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ — he said: this is concerning the Christians.

Similarly narrated Hushaym and al-Thawri, from Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah, from al-Sha'bi.

Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, [[In A: "Abbas".]] from his father, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about His saying: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then they are the disbelievers﴾ [[Addition from A; in H: "the verse".]] He said: "It is disbelief (kufr) by it." Ibn Tawus said: "But it is not like one who disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers."

Al-Thawri said, from Ibn Juraij, [[In R: "Jarir".]] from Ata', that he said: "It is disbelief short of disbelief, injustice short of injustice, and sinfulness short of sinfulness." Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Waki' said, from Sufyan, from Sa'id al-Makki, from Tawus, regarding ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then they are the disbelievers﴾: "It is not a disbelief that removes one from the religion (millah)." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (10/355).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hujayr, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then they are the disbelievers﴾: he said, "It is not the disbelief to which they go."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyayna, and said: "Sahih according to the condition of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." [[Al-Mustadrak (2/313).]]

These verses were revealed concerning those who hasten to disbelief, who depart from the obedience of Allah and His Messenger, and who put their own opinions and desires above the laws of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. ﴿Among those who say, "We believe," with their mouths, but their hearts have not believed﴾, meaning they displayed faith with their tongues while their hearts were ruined and empty of it. These are the hypocrites. ﴿And among those who are Jews﴾, the enemies of Islam and its people. All of these are ﴿listeners to falsehood﴾, meaning they respond to it and are affected by it. ﴿Listeners for another people who have not come to you﴾, meaning they respond to other peoples who do not attend your assembly, O Muhammad. It has also been said that the meaning is that they eavesdrop on speech and convey it to other peoples who are not present with you, from among your enemies. ﴿They distort words from their places﴾, meaning they interpret them other than their true interpretation, and they alter them after they had understood them, ﴿while they know﴾.

﴿They say, "If you are given this, take it, but if you are not given it, then beware."﴾
It has been said: this was revealed concerning groups of Jews who killed a slain man and said, "Come, let us bring our dispute to Muhammad. If he gives us a ruling of blood money, then take what he says, but if he rules for retaliation, then do not listen to him."

The correct view is that it was revealed concerning the two Jews who committed adultery. They had altered the Book of Allah that was in their hands, regarding the command to stone one who was married. They distorted it and agreed among themselves on flogging one hundred lashes, along with blackening the face and riding them backwards on a donkey. When that incident occurred after the Hijrah of the Prophet ﷺ, they said among themselves, "Come, let us bring our dispute to him. If he rules with flogging and blackening, then accept it from him and make it a proof between you and Allah, and say that a prophet among the prophets of Allah has judged between you by this. But if he rules with stoning, then do not follow him in that."

Hadiths have been related to this effect. Malik related from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, that he said: The Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned to him that a man and a woman among them had committed adultery. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them, "What do you find in the Torah concerning the punishment of stoning?" They said, "We expose them and they are flogged." Abdullah ibn Salam said, "You have lied. In it is stoning." So they brought the Torah and unrolled it, and one of them placed his hand over the verse of stoning, reading what came before it and what came after it. Abdullah ibn Salam said to him, "Lift your hand." He lifted his hand, and there in it was the verse of stoning. They said, "You have spoken truly, O Muhammad, it contains the verse of stoning!" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that the two be stoned, and I saw the man bending over the woman to shield her from the stones.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both reported it, and this is the wording of al-Bukhari. In another wording of his: He said to the Jews, "What do you do with them both?" They said, "We blacken their faces and disgrace them." He said, ﴿Then bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:93]. So they came and told a man among them whom they trusted, who was one-eyed, "Read." He read until he came to a place in it, then placed his hand upon it. He said, "Lift your hand." He lifted it, and the verse of stoning was shining forth. He said, "O Muhammad, indeed in it is the verse of stoning, but we have been concealing it among ourselves." So he commanded that the two be stoned.

In Muslim's version: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought a Jewish man and a Jewish woman who had committed adultery. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out until he came to the Jews and said, "What do you find in the Torah concerning one who commits adultery?" They said, "We blacken their faces, put them on a donkey facing backwards, and we parade them about." He said, ﴿Then bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾. He said: They brought it and read it, until when he came to the verse of stoning, the young man who was reading placed his hand over the verse of stoning and read what was before it and what was after it. Abdullah ibn Salam, who was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said to him, "Tell him to lift his hand." He lifted his hand, and beneath it was the verse of stoning. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that the two be stoned. Abdullah ibn Umar said, "I was among those who stoned them, and I saw him shielding her from the stones with his own body."

Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, that Zayd ibn Aslam related to him, from Ibn Umar, who said: A group of Jews came, and they invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to al-Quff, so he came to them in the house of study. They said, "O Abu al-Qasim, a man among us has committed adultery with a woman, so judge." He said: They placed a cushion for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he sat upon it. Then he said, "Bring me the Torah." It was brought, so he pulled the cushion from beneath him and placed the Torah upon it, and said, "I believe in you and in the One who revealed you." Then he said, "Bring me your most learned man." A young man was brought, and then he related the story of stoning similar to the hadith of Malik from Nafi'.

Al-Zuhri said: I heard a man of Muzaynah, one of those who follow knowledge and retain it, while we were with Ibn al-Musayyib, relating from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A Jewish man committed adultery with a woman. Some of them said to others, "Go to this Prophet, for he was sent with leniency. If he gives us a ruling short of stoning, we will accept it and argue with it before Allah, saying, 'It is the ruling of one of Your prophets.'" They came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was sitting in the mosque among his companions, and said, "O Abu al-Qasim, what do you say about a man and a woman among us who committed adultery?" He did not speak to them a word until he came to their house of study, and stood at the door, and said, "I adjure you by Allah, who revealed the Torah to Musa: what do you find in the Torah concerning one who commits adultery when he is married?" They said, "He is blackened, humiliated, and flogged." Al-Tajbiyah is that the two adulterers are placed upon a donkey with their backs facing each other, and they are paraded about. He said: A young man among them remained silent. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw that he was silent, he pressed him with the adjuration, saying, "O Allah, since You have made us swear, indeed we find stoning in the Torah." The Prophet ﷺ said, "What was the first thing by which you relaxed the command of Allah?" He said, "A close relative of one of our kings committed adultery, so they delayed stoning for him. Then a man among the common people committed adultery after him, and they wanted to stone him, but his people intervened and said, 'Our companion shall not be stoned until you bring your companion and stone him!' So they agreed upon this punishment among themselves." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Then I judge by what is in the Torah," and he commanded that the two be stoned. Al-Zuhri said: It reached us that this verse was revealed concerning them: ﴿Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which is guidance and light, by which the prophets who submitted judged﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:44]. And the Prophet ﷺ was among them.

Ahmad and Abu Dawud related it, and this is the wording of Abu Dawud, as did Ibn Jarir.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: A Jewish man who had been blackened and flogged passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He summoned them and said, "Is this how you find the prescribed punishment for an adulterer in your Book?" They said, "Yes." He summoned a man of their scholars and said, "I adjure you by Him who revealed the Torah to Musa: is this how you find the prescribed punishment for an adulterer in your Book?" He said, "No, by Allah, and were it not that you adjured me by this, I would not have told you. We find the punishment for an adulterer in our Book to be stoning, but it became widespread among our nobles. When we seized a nobleman, we left him, and when we seized a weak person, we enforced the punishment upon him. So we said, 'Come, let us establish something to apply to both the noble and the lowly.' So we agreed upon blackening and flogging." The Prophet ﷺ said, "O Allah, I am the first to revive Your command after they had caused it to die." He said: So he commanded that the man be stoned. He said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O Messenger, let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelief﴾ up to His saying ﴿They say, "If you are given this, take it"﴾, meaning they say, "Go to Muhammad. If he rules for you with blackening and flogging, take it, but if he rules for you with stoning, beware," up to His saying ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers﴾. He said: concerning the Jews, up to His saying ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the wrongdoers﴾. He said: concerning the Jews [in one version: the Christians], ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the defiantly disobedient﴾. He said: concerning the disbelievers in general.

Muslim alone among the compilers reported it, apart from al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, through several chains, from al-A'mash, with the same wording.

Imam Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi said in his Musnad: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Mujalid ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: A man from the people of Fadak committed adultery, so the people of Fadak wrote to some Jews in Medina: "Ask Muhammad about this. If he orders you to flog, then accept it from him, but if he orders you to stone, then do not accept it from him." They asked him about it. He said, "Send for me the two most learned men among you." They brought a one-eyed man, called Ibn Suriya, and another. The Prophet ﷺ said to them, "Are you the most learned of those who came before you?" They said, "Our people have summoned us for this." The Prophet ﷺ said to them, "Do you not have the Torah in which is the judgment of Allah?" They said, "Yes." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Then I adjure you by Him who split the sea for the Children of Israel, shaded you with clouds, delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, and sent down manna and quail upon the Children of Israel: what do you find in the Torah concerning the matter of stoning?" One of them said to the other, "I have never been adjured with the like of this." They said, "We find that prolonged gazing is adultery, embracing is adultery, and kissing is adultery. If four witnesses testify that they saw him inserting and withdrawing, like the kohl stick entering the kohl pot, then stoning is obligatory." The Prophet ﷺ said, "That is it." He commanded that he be stoned, and it was stoned. Then this was revealed: ﴿So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:42].

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah related it through the hadith of Mujalid, similarly. The wording of Abu Dawud from Jabir is: The Jews brought a man and a woman from among them who had committed adultery. He said, "Bring me the two most learned men among you." They brought the two sons of Suriya. He adjured them: "How do you find the matter of these two in the Torah?" They said, "We find in the Torah that when four witnesses testify that they saw his member in her private part like the kohl stick in the kohl pot, they are stoned." He said, "Then what prevents you from stoning them?" They said, "Our authority has gone, so we disliked killing." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for the witnesses, and four came and testified that they saw his member in her private part like the kohl stick in the kohl pot. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that the two be stoned.

Then Abu Dawud related it from al-Sha'bi and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i as a mursal report [a report in which the Companion is omitted from the chain], and he did not mention in it: "He called the witnesses, and they testified."

Therefore these are hadiths indicating that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) judged in accordance with the ruling of the Torah. This is not a case of obligating them to what they themselves hold to be authentic, for they are in any case commanded to follow the Muhammadan Law. Rather, this was by a special revelation from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to him concerning that, and his questioning of them about it was to make them acknowledge what was in their hands, which they had agreed to conceal and deny, and not to act upon, for those long ages. So when they admitted it while their practice was contrary to it, it showed that their deviation, their obstinacy, and their denial of what they themselves held to be authentic from the Book that was in their hands, and their turning to the arbitration of the Messenger (ﷺ), was only from their own caprice and desire, to match their opinions, not from belief in the validity of what he judged. Hence they said: ﴿If you are given this, then accept it﴾, i.e., accept it, ﴿but if you are not given it, then beware﴾, i.e., beware of accepting and following it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whomever Allah intends for trial, you will not control for him anything from Allah. Those are the ones whose hearts Allah did not intend to purify. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. They are listeners to falsehood, devourers of unlawful gain﴾, i.e., the prohibited, which is bribery, as said by Ibn Mas'ud and others. That is: how can Allah purify the heart of one who has this description, and how could He respond to him?

Then He said to His Prophet: ﴿So if they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all﴾, i.e., there is no blame upon you for not judging between them, because they do not seek by their arbitration to you to follow the truth, but rather whatever matches their desire.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Zayd ibn Aslam, and 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: it is abrogated by His saying: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 49], and ﴿And if you judge, then judge between them with justice﴾, i.e., with truth and fairness, even if they are wrongdoers who have departed from the path of justice. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.﴾

Then He said, exed, denouncing them for their corrupt opinions and their deviant intentions, in their abandoning what they held to be authentic from the Book that was in their hands, which they claim they are commanded to adhere to forever, and then they departed from its ruling and turned to something else, which they in reality believe to be void and not binding upon them. He said: ﴿And how do they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is the judgement of Allah? Then they turn away after that. And those are not believers.﴾

Then He praised the Torah which He sent down to His servant and messenger Musa son of 'Imran, saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light. By it the prophets who submitted judge for the Jews, and the rabbis and scholars [judge] by what they were entrusted of the Book of Allah.﴾ That is, they do not depart from its ruling, nor alter it, nor distort it. ﴿And the rabbis and the scholars﴾, i.e., likewise the rabbis among them, who are the scholarly worshippers, and the scholars, who are the learned ones, ﴿by what they were entrusted of the Book of Allah﴾, i.e., by what was deposited with them of the Book of Allah, which they were commanded to make manifest and act upon. ﴿And they were witnesses over it. So do not fear the people, but fear Me.﴾ That is, do not be afraid of them, and fear Me. ﴿And do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers.﴾ Concerning this there are two opinions which will come with their explanation. Another cause of revelation of these noble verses:

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn al-'Abbas narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from his father, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah sent down: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾, and ﴿those are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 45], ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 47]. He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah sent them down concerning the two groups of the Jews. One of them had overpowered the other in the Jahiliyyah, until they agreed or made peace on the basis that for every person slain by the strong from the weak, the blood-money would be fifty wasq, and for every person slain by the weak from the strong, the blood-money would be one hundred wasq. They remained upon that until the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah, and both groups were humbled by the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), though at that time he had not yet prevailed, and had not yet made them subject to him, and they were in a state of truce. Then the weak group killed a man from the strong group, and the strong group sent to the weak group: Send us one hundred wasq. The weak group said: Has there ever been such a thing between two tribes whose religion is one, whose lineage is one, and whose land is one: the blood-money of one part is half the blood-money of the other? We only gave you this out of oppression from you toward us and fear of you. But now that Muhammad has come, we will not give you that. War nearly erupted between them. Then they agreed to make the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) an arbiter between them. Then the strong group remembered and said: By Allah, Muhammad will not give you from them double what he gives them from you. And indeed they spoke truly; they had only given us this out of oppression from us and subjugation of them. So they sent to Muhammad a person to find out his opinion: if he gives you what you want, you will accept his judgement, and if he does not give you, be wary, and do not accept his judgement. They sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) some hypocrites to find out the opinion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of all their affair and what they intended. Then Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿O Messenger, do not let those grieve you who race to disbelief﴾ up to His saying ﴿the defiantly disobedient﴾. By Allah, it was concerning them that it was sent down, and it was them whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, meant. [Al-Musnad (1/246)]

Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi al-Zinad, from his father, similarly.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Hannad ibn al-Sari and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, both saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the verses in al-Ma'idah, from His saying ﴿so judge between them or turn away from them﴾ up to ﴿the just﴾, were revealed only concerning the blood-money among the Banu al-Nadir and the Banu Qurayzah. That was because the slain of the Banu al-Nadir had nobility, and the blood-money was paid in full, while the Banu Qurayzah were paying half the blood-money. They brought their dispute to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah sent down that concerning them, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) directed them to the truth in that matter, and made the blood-money equal in that — and Allah knows best which of these it was.

Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/326), al-Musnad (1/363), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3591), Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/19)]

Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Salih, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Qurayzah and al-Nadir — al-Nadir was more noble than Qurayzah. So if a man of Qurayzah killed a man of al-Nadir, he was killed for him; and if a man of al-Nadir killed a man of Qurayzah, he paid one hundred wasq of dates as blood-money. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent, a man of al-Nadir killed a man of Qurayzah. They said: Hand him over to us. They said: Between us and you is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So ﴿And if you judge, then judge between them with justice﴾ was revealed.

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak narrated it from the hadith of 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa, similarly. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/327), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4494), Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/18), al-Mustadrak (4/366)]

Likewise said Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Ibn Zayd, and others.

It has also been narrated by al-'Awfi and 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah al-Walibi, from Ibn 'Abbas, that these verses were revealed concerning the two Jews who committed adultery, as the hadiths concerning that have already preceded. It may be that these two causes coincided at one time, so these verses were revealed concerning all of that, and Allah knows best.

Hence He said after that: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein that the soul is for the soul, and the eye for the eye﴾ up to its end. This strengthens that the cause of revelation was the matter of retaliation (qisas), and Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾, al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Mijlaz, Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, 'Ikrimah, 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah, al-Hasan al-Basri, and others said: it was revealed concerning the People of the Book. Al-Hasan al-Basri added: and it is binding upon us.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: These verses were revealed concerning the Children of Israel, and Allah was pleased with them for this Ummah. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Jarir also said: Ya'qub narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman informed us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from 'Alqamah and Masruq that they both asked Ibn Mas'ud about bribery. He said: It is from the unlawful gain. They said: And what about in judgement? He said: That is disbelief! Then he recited: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾ means: whoever does not judge by what I have sent down, abandoning it deliberately, or acts unjustly while knowing, he is among the disbelievers [in it].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾, that he said: Whoever denies what Allah has revealed has disbelieved; and whoever affirms it but does not judge by it is a wrongdoer and a defiantly disobedient sinner. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Then he (Ibn Jarir) preferred that the verse is meant concerning the People of the Book, or whoever denies the ruling of Allah revealed in the Book.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from al-Thawri, from Zakariyya, from al-Sha'bi: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed﴾ — he said: it is for the Muslims.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi al-Safar, from al-Sha'bi: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾ — he said: this is concerning the Muslims. ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the wrongdoers﴾ — he said: this is concerning the Jews. ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ — he said: this is concerning the Christians.

Similarly narrated Hushaym and al-Thawri, from Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah, from al-Sha'bi.

Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, [[In A: "Abbas".]] from his father, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about His saying: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then they are the disbelievers﴾ [[Addition from A; in H: "the verse".]] He said: "It is disbelief (kufr) by it." Ibn Tawus said: "But it is not like one who disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers."

Al-Thawri said, from Ibn Juraij, [[In R: "Jarir".]] from Ata', that he said: "It is disbelief short of disbelief, injustice short of injustice, and sinfulness short of sinfulness." Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Waki' said, from Sufyan, from Sa'id al-Makki, from Tawus, regarding ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then they are the disbelievers﴾: "It is not a disbelief that removes one from the religion (millah)." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (10/355).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hujayr, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then they are the disbelievers﴾: he said, "It is not the disbelief to which they go."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyayna, and said: "Sahih according to the condition of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." [[Al-Mustadrak (2/313).]]

This is also among the things for which the Jews were rebuked and reproached. In their Torah, as it stands with them, is the text: "a life for a life." Yet they deliberately and obstinately oppose this. They execute the Nadri for the Qurazi, but do not execute the Qurazi for the Nadri, and instead they resort to blood money (diyah). They likewise opposed the explicit ruling of the Torah among them concerning stoning the married adulterer, and turned instead to what they had agreed upon among themselves: flogging, blackening the face, and parading the offender. For this reason, there Allah said: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers﴾, because they denied Allah's ruling knowingly, obstinately and deliberately. And here He said: ﴿then those are the wrongdoers﴾, because they did not give the wronged party justice against the wrongdoer in the matter in which Allah commanded justice and equality among all. So they opposed it and did wrong, and some of them transgressed against others. [[In A: "wa-ta'addaw 'ala ba'diha ba'dan" ("and they transgressed against one another").]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Yunus ibn Yazid, from Abu 'Ali ibn Yazid, the brother of Yunus ibn Yazid, from al-Zuhri, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein that a life is for a life, and an eye for an eye﴾, putting "the life" in the accusative and raising "the eye."

Similarly, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it through the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak. [[Musnad (3/215), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3977), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2929).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib."

Al-Bukhari said: "Ibn al-Mubarak alone narrated this hadith." [[In A: "tafarrada bihi Ibn al-Mubarak".]]

Many of the usulis (scholars of legal theory) and jurists who held that the law of those before us is law for us, when it is related in an affirmed manner and has not been abrogated, which is the well-known view of the majority, have cited this verse. So did Shaykh Abu Ishaq al-Isfara'ini, who related it from the explicit text of al-Shafi'i and most of the companions (of al-Shafi'i's school), with this verse, since the ruling among us in cases of bodily injury (jinayat) follows it, as do all the imams.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "It applies to them and to the people generally." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Shaykh Abu Zakariya al-Nawawi recorded three positions on this question. The third is that the law of Ibrahim is a valid proof, but not the law of anyone else. He also favored the position that it is not a valid proof. Abu Ishaq al-Isfara'ini related several opinions from al-Shafi'i and preferred that it is a valid proof according to the majority of our companions. And Allah knows best.

Imam Abu Nasr ibn al-Sabbagh, may Allah have mercy on him, related in his book "al-Shamil" the consensus of the scholars on citing this verse as evidence for what it indicates. All the imams have argued from the generality of this noble verse that a man is killed for killing a woman. Likewise, it is recorded in the hadith narrated by al-Nasa'i and others that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote in the letter to 'Amr ibn Hazm: "A man is killed for a woman." And in another hadith: "The blood of Muslims is equal." [[Narrated from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas, recorded by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (2683), via Sulayman, from his father, from Hanash, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/353): "This chain is weak, because Hanash, whose name is Husayn ibn Qays, is weak." It is also narrated from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As: recorded by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (4531), via Yahya, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather.]] This is the view of the majority of scholars.

It is related from Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali ibn Abi Talib that when a man kills a woman, he is not killed for her, unless her guardian pays to the family of the killer half the blood money, because her blood money is half that of a man. This is the view adopted by Ahmad in one of his narrations [from him]. [[Added from R, A.]] It is also reported [[In R: "wa-yuhka" ("and it is reported").]] [this] [[Added from R, A.]] from al-Hasan al-Basri [[Added from R, A.]], 'Ata', 'Uthman al-Batti, and in another narration from Ahmad [[In R, A: "wa-'an Ahmad riwayah".]] [that] [[Added from A.]] when a man kills a woman he is not killed for her, but her blood money is due.

In the same way, Abu Hanifa, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, argued from the generality of this verse that a Muslim is killed for a dhimmi non-Muslim, and a free person for a slave. The majority opposed him on both points. In the two Sahihs it is related from Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6903).]] As for the slave, there are several reports from the early scholars (al-salaf) that they did not retaliate against a slave for a free person, nor did they kill a free person for a slave. Some hadiths were reported on this, but they are not authentic. Al-Shafi'i related a consensus against the position of the Hanafis on this, but the invalidity of their position does not follow except by an evidence that specifies the noble verse.

What supports what Ibn al-Sabbagh said regarding citing this noble verse is the authentic hadith on the matter, as Imam Ahmad said:

Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, Humayd related to us, from Anas ibn Malik: that al-Rubayyi', the paternal aunt of Anas, broke the front tooth of a girl. They asked the people for pardon, but they refused. So they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Retaliation (qisas)." Anas ibn al-Nadr, her brother, said: "O Messenger of Allah, will her front tooth be broken?!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Anas, the Book of Allah prescribes retaliation." He said: "No, by the One who sent you with the truth, her tooth will not be broken." He said: So the people were content, pardoned, and gave up retaliation. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said: "Indeed among the servants of Allah are those who, if they swear by Allah, He fulfills it for them."

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the two Sahihs. [[Musnad (3/128), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6894), Sahih Muslim no. (1675).]] Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Muthanna al-Ansari also narrated it in his well-known part (juz') of hadith, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, that al-Rubayyi' bint al-Nadr, his paternal aunt, slapped a girl and broke her front tooth. They offered them the compensation (arsh), but they refused. They then asked for compensation and pardon, and they refused. So they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he ordered them to retaliate. Her brother Anas ibn al-Nadr came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, will the front tooth of al-Rubayyi' be broken? By the One who sent you with the truth, do not break her tooth." The Prophet ﷺ said: "O Anas, the Book of Allah prescribes retaliation." The people then pardoned, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed among the servants of Allah are those who, if they swear by Allah, He fulfills it for them." Al-Bukhari related it from al-Ansari.

As for the hadith which Abu Dawud related:

Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, from my father, from Qatada, from Abu Nadra, from Imran ibn Husayn: that a slave of poor people cut off the ear of a slave of rich people. The family of the injured went to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are poor people." So he did not impose anything upon him. Similarly, al-Nasa'i related it from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, from Mu'adh ibn Hisham al-Dastawa'i, from his father, from Qatada, with it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4590), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (6953).]] This is a strong chain, all of whose narrators are trustworthy, but it is a problematic hadith. Unless it is said that the offender was below the age of puberty, in which case there is no retaliation against him, and perhaps he bore the compensation for what was lost from the child of the wealthy, or the wealthy family excused him from it.

* *

As for the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the wounds, retaliation﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas, who said: A life is taken for a life, an eye is put out for an eye, a nose is cut off for a nose, a tooth is pulled out for a tooth, and wounds are avenged with wounds.

This applies equally among free Muslims, men and women among them, in cases of intentional killing and lesser injuries. It also applies equally among slaves, men and women among them, in cases of intentional killing and lesser injuries. Narrated by Ibn Jarir [[In D: "Jurayj".]] and Ibn Abi Hatim.

An important principle:

Wounds may sometimes be at a joint (mafsil), in which case retaliation is required by consensus, such as cutting off the hand, the foot, the palm, the sole, and the like. But when the wound is not at a joint and is instead on a bone, Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Retaliation is required for it, except in the thigh and similar places, because it is dangerous and perilous. Abu Hanifa and his two companions said: Retaliation is not required for any bone except the tooth. Al-Shafi'i said: Retaliation is not required for any bone whatsoever. This is also related from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn Abbas, and it is the view of 'Ata', al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Zuhri, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. Sufyan al-Thawri and al-Layth ibn Sa'd also held this, and it is the well-known position in the school of Imam Ahmad.

Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, argued by the hadith of al-Rubayyi' bint al-Nadr for his position that there is no retaliation for a bone except the tooth. But the hadith of al-Rubayyi' is not an argument, because it came with the wording: "she broke the front tooth of a girl," and it is possible that the tooth fell out without being broken, in which case retaliation is required by consensus in this situation. They also completed the argument with what Ibn Majah related through the route of Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from Dahtham [[In A: "Duhaym".]] ibn Qarran, from Nimran ibn Jariya, from his father Jariya ibn Zafar al-Hanafi: that a man struck another man on his forearm with a sword, not at the joint, and cut it off. He complained to the Prophet ﷺ, who ordered compensation for him. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I want retaliation." He said: "Take the compensation, may Allah bless you in it." He did not rule retaliation for him. [[Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2636).]]

Shaykh Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: This hadith has no other chain than this one. Dahtham ibn Qarran al-'Ukli is a weak Bedouin (a'rabi), and his hadith is not used as evidence. Nimran ibn Jariya is also a weak Bedouin, and his father Jariya ibn Zafar is mentioned among the Companions. [[Al-Istidhkar (25/287).]]

Then they said: It is not permissible to take retaliation for a wound until the injured person's wound has healed. If he takes retaliation before it heals and the wound then worsens, he has no claim. The proof for this is what Imam Ahmad related: Ya'qub related to us, my father related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who mentioned a hadith. Ibn Ishaq said: And 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb mentioned, from his father, from his grandfather: that a man stabbed another man with a horn in his knee. He came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Retaliate against me." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not hasten until your wound heals." The man refused except to take retaliation. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ retaliated against him. The one who took retaliation became lame, and the one against whom retaliation was taken healed. The one who had taken retaliation came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I became lame, and my companion healed." He said: "I forbade you, but you disobeyed me. May Allah distance you, and your lameness is void." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade taking retaliation for a wound until its victim has healed. Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Musnad (2/217).]]

Question:

If the injured party takes retribution (qisas) from the offender and dies from it, then according to Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal there is nothing owed. This is also the view of the majority of the Companions (Sahabah) and the Successors (Tabi'un) and others. Abu Hanifa said: the blood money (diyah) is owed from the property of the one who inflicted the retribution. Amir al-Sha'bi, 'Ata', Tawus, 'Amr ibn Dinar, al-Harith al-'Ukli, Ibn Abi Layla, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, al-Zuhri, and al-Thawri said: the blood money is owed from the 'aqilah (the paternal kinsmen who bear such liabilities) of the one for whom retribution was taken. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah [[In ر and أ: "'Uyaynah".]], and 'Uthman al-Batti said: the portion equal to that injury is dropped from the one for whom retribution was taken, and the remainder is owed from his property.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿But whoever forgoes it, it is an expiation for him﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿But whoever forgoes it, it is an expiation for him﴾, that he said: meaning, whoever pardons the offender and gives charity to him, it is an expiation for the one who wronged him (al-matlub), and a reward for the one who was wronged (al-talib).

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿But whoever forgoes it, it is an expiation for him﴾, that he said: it is an expiation for the one who inflicted the injury, and the reward of the one who was injured is with God, Mighty and Majestic. Ibn Abi Hatim related this. Then he said: It has also been narrated from Khaythamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, Mujahid, Ibrahim (in one of his two opinions), 'Amir al-Sha'bi, and Jabir ibn Zayd something similar to this second view. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Hammad ibn Zadhan narrated to us: Harami, meaning Ibn 'Umarah, narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Umarah, meaning Ibn Abi Hafsah, from a man, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, regarding the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic [[In أ: "Exalted".]] ﴿But whoever forgoes it, it is an expiation for him﴾, that he said: it is for the one who was injured. And it was narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i (in one of his two opinions), Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, something similar to this.

Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Amir al-Sha'bi and Qatadah the like of this.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib narrated to us, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qays, meaning Ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Tariq ibn Shihab narrating from al-Haytham Abu al-'Uryan [[In هـ and ر: "ibn". The adopted reading is from al-Tabari.]] al-Nakha'i, who said: I saw 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr with Mu'awiyah, reddish, resembling the mawali (non-Arab clients). So I asked him about the saying of God [Mighty and Majestic] [[Addition from أ.]] ﴿But whoever forgoes it, it is an expiation for him﴾, and he said: it erases from his sins an amount equal to what he forgave.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated the same from Qays ibn Muslim, and Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise through the chains of Sufyan and Shu'bah.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali narrated to me, 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad al-Mujashi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj al-Mahri narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Ju'fi narrated to us, Mu'alla, meaning Ibn Hilal [[In ر: "Bilal".]], that he heard Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu al-'Uryan al-Haytham ibn al-Aswad, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr; and from Aban ibn Taghlib, from al-Sha'bi, from a man of the Ansar, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying ﴿But whoever forgoes it, it is an expiation for him﴾, that he said: it is the one whose tooth is broken, or whose hand is cut off, or whose limb is cut, or whose body is wounded, and he pardons that. And he said: his sins are reduced by an amount equal to his offence. If it is a quarter of the blood money, then a quarter of his sins are removed; if it is a third, then a third of his sins; and if it is the full blood money, then his sins are removed in the same manner. [[Narrated by al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws (3/153) through the chain of Yahya ibn Salam, from his father, from al-Mu'alla, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from al-Sha'bi; and from al-'Uryan ibn al-Haytham, from his father, from Ibn 'Umar, as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report.]]

Then Ibn Jarir said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from Abu al-Safar, who said: A man from Quraysh pushed a man from the Ansar, and his front tooth was broken. The Ansari took him to Mu'awiyah, and when the man insisted, he said: It is your affair and your companion's. He said: Abu al-Darda' was with Mu'awiyah, and Abu al-Darda' said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "No Muslim is afflicted with anything in his body and then forgives it, except that God raises him a degree thereby and removes from him a sin because of it." The Ansari said: Did you hear it from the Messenger of God (ﷺ)? He said: My ears heard it and my heart retained it. So he let the Qurashi go free, and Mu'awiyah said: Give him money.

This was narrated by Ibn Jarir [[Tafsir al-Tabari (10/364).]]. Imam Ahmad narrated it as well, saying: Waki' narrated to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, from Abu al-Safar, who said: A man from Quraysh broke the tooth of a man from the Ansar, so the Ansari sought Mu'awiyah's judgment against him. The Qurashi said: This man broke my tooth? Mu'awiyah said: We will certainly satisfy him. But the Ansari insisted, and Mu'awiyah said: It is your affair with your companion. Abu al-Darda' was sitting there, and Abu al-Darda' said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "No Muslim is afflicted with anything in his body and then gives it in charity, except that God raises him a degree or removes from him a sin because of it." The Ansari said: Then I, meaning: I have pardoned.

Likewise it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi through the narration of Ibn al-Mubarak, and Ibn Majah through the narration of Waki', both from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, with it [[Musnad (6/448), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1393), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2693).]]. Then al-Tirmidhi said: It is gharib (a report transmitted through a single line); we only know it through this route, and I do not know that Abu al-Safar heard from Abu al-Darda'.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Da'laj ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Zayd narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Zabyan, from 'Adi ibn Thabit: that a man had his mouth broken by another man during the time of Mu'awiyah, may God be pleased with him. He was offered blood money, but he refused except that retribution be taken. He was offered double, and he refused; he was offered triple, and he refused. Then a man from the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever gives in charity blood or less than it, it is an expiation for him from the day he was born until the day he dies." [[Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Sunan no. (762), and Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (12/284), and al-Tabari in his Tafsir (10/368), through the chain of 'Imran ibn Zabyan. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/302): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except 'Imran ibn Zabyan, who was declared trustworthy by Ibn Hibban, but he has some weakness."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Surayj ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi: that 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "No man is wounded in his body with a wound, and then gives it in charity, except that God expiates for him the equivalent of what he gave in charity."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from 'Ali ibn Hujr, from Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, and Ibn Jarir narrated it from Mahmud ibn Khidash, from Hushaym; both of them from al-Mughirah, with it [[Musnad (5/316), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11146), and Tafsir al-Tabari (10/364).]].

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, from Mujalid, from 'Amir, from al-Mahharar ibn Abi Hurayrah, from a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever is afflicted with something in his body and leaves it for God's sake, it will be an expiation for him." [[Musnad (5/412). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/302): "In its chain is Mujalid, who became confused in his memory."]]
* *
As for His saying: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the wrongdoers﴾, it has already been mentioned from Tawus and 'Ata' that they said: it is disbelief short of disbelief, wrongdoing short of wrongdoing, and transgression short of transgression.

Allah, the Exalted, says: "And We caused to follow" means We sent after them, ﴿in their footsteps﴾, meaning the prophets of the Children of Israel [peace be upon him] [[added from A.]], ﴿Jesus, son of Mary, confirming what was before him of the Torah﴾, meaning believing in it and ruling by what is in it. ﴿And We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light﴾, meaning guidance to the truth and a light by which one is illuminated in removing doubts and resolving difficulties. ﴿Confirming what was before him of the Torah﴾ means following it, not contradicting what is in it, except for a little which he made clear to the Children of Israel regarding some matters they disputed. As Allah, the Exalted, said, reporting about the Messiah that he said to the Children of Israel: ﴿and to make lawful for you some of that which was forbidden to you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 50]. For this reason, the more well-known of the two opinions of the scholars is that the Gospel abrogated (naskh, the cancelling of an earlier ruling by a later one) some rulings of the Torah.

* *

His saying: ﴿And a guidance and an admonition for the righteous﴾ means: We made the Gospel ﴿a guidance﴾ by which one is guided, ﴿and an admonition﴾, meaning a restrainer ["in D: 'i.e., restrainer'"] from committing what is prohibited and sinful, ﴿for the righteous﴾, meaning for those who fear Allah and dread His threat and punishment.

* *

His saying: ﴿And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein﴾. It was read ﴿wa-liyahkum﴾ with a fatha (the accusative), on the basis that the lam is the lam of purpose (lam kay), meaning: We gave him the Gospel [in it was guidance and light] [[added from R, A.]] so that the people of his religion would judge by it in their time. It was also read ﴿wa-liyahkum﴾ with a sukun (the jussive), the lam being the lam of command, meaning: let them believe in all that is in it, let them establish what they were commanded in it, and among what is in it is the good news of the sending of Muhammad [ﷺ] [[added from D, A.]], and the command to follow him and affirm him when he appears. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, O People of the Scripture, you are not standing on anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 68]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and makes lawful for them what is good and prohibits for them what is evil, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them. So those who believe in him, honor him, support him, and follow the light that has been sent down with him - it is those who are the successful﴾ [al-A'raf: 157] [[added from R; in H: "up to his saying"]]. For this reason He said here: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then those are the defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning those who depart from obedience to their Lord, who incline toward falsehood, who abandon the truth. It has already been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning the Christians, and this is the apparent meaning of the context.

For this reason, the more well-known of the two opinions of the scholars is that the Gospel abrogated (naskh, the cancelling of an earlier ruling by a later one) some rulings of the Torah.
