Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah 5:48–50 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, may He be exalted, mentioned the Torah that He sent down to Musa (Moses), His interlocutor, [peace be upon him] [[addition from A.]], and praised it and commended it, and commanded [[in A: "and We commanded"]] that it be followed wherever it was valid to follow, and mentioned the Gospel and praised it, and commanded its people to establish it and follow what is in it, as was explained earlier, He began to mention the Mighty Qur'an, which He sent down to His servant and noble messenger. He said: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book with the truth﴾, meaning with the truth that has no doubt that it is from Allah, ﴿confirming what came before it of the Scripture﴾, meaning of the earlier books that contain its mention and praise, and that it would be sent down from Allah upon His servant and messenger Muhammad ﷺ. Its descent came as they had foretold, which increased its truthfulness in the eyes of those who bore it from people of insight, who submitted to Allah's command, followed His laws, and believed in His messengers, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces in prostration and say, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord is ever fulfilled."﴾ [Al-Isra 17:107–108], meaning: if what Allah promised through the tongues of the earlier messengers, regarding the coming of Muhammad, peace be upon him, was indeed ﴿fulfilled﴾, meaning certain to occur without fail.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and as a guardian over it﴾, Sufyan al-Thawri and others narrated from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas that it means: entrusted with it. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: al-Muhaymin means al-Amin (the trustworthy); he said: the Qur'an is trustworthy over every book before it.

Similar things were narrated from 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, 'Atiyyah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd.

Ibn Juraij said: the Qur'an is a guardian over the earlier books; whatever in them agrees with it is true, and whatever contradicts it is false.

It was narrated from al-Walibi, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and as a guardian﴾ means a witness. Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi also said likewise.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and as a guardian﴾ means a judge over what came before it of the books.

All these statements are close in meaning, for the name "al-Muhaymin" comprises all of this. He is trustworthy, a witness, and a judge over every book before it. Allah made this Mighty Book, which He sent down as the last and seal of the books, the most comprehensive, the greatest and the most perfect [[in R, D: "and the most complete"]], since it gathers the excellences of what came before it and adds to it perfections not found in any other. For this reason He made it a witness, a trustworthy guardian and a judge over all of them. Allah, may He be exalted, took upon Himself its preservation by His own noble self, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [Al-Hijr 15:9].

As for what Ibn Abi Hatim related from 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid, that they said regarding His saying ﴿and as a guardian over it﴾, meaning Muhammad ﷺ is trustworthy over the Qur'an, this is correct in meaning, but there is room for doubt in explaining it this way, and also in construing it grammatically (i'rab) in this manner. In sum, the first view is the correct one. Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said, after relating this from Mujahid: "This interpretation is far from what is understood in the speech of the Arabs; rather, it is an error. That is because al-Muhaymin is coordinated with al-Musaddiq (the confirmer), so it can only describe what al-Musaddiq describes." He said: "Had it been as Mujahid said, it would have said: 'And We sent down to you the Book confirming what came before it of the Scripture, a guardian over it,' without a conjunction."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So judge between them by what Allah has revealed﴾, meaning: so judge, O Muhammad, between the people, their Arabs and non-Arabs, their unlettered and their People of the Book, ﴿by what Allah has revealed﴾ to you in this Mighty Book, and by what He has established for you of the rulings of those prophets who came before you and which He did not abrogate (naskh) in your law. Ibn Jarir gave this meaning.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Ammar related to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam related to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was given a choice: if he wished, he would judge between them, and if he wished, he would turn away from them. [Then] they returned him to their own rulings, so this was revealed: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires﴾. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to judge between them by what is in our Book.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and do not follow their desires﴾, meaning their opinions which they had agreed upon, and because of which they abandoned what Allah revealed to His messenger. For this reason He said: ﴿and do not follow their desires, away from the truth that has come to you﴾, meaning do not turn away from the truth that Allah has commanded you to, toward the desires of these ignorant wretched people.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿For each of you, We have made a law (shir'ah) and a method (minhaj)﴾, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar related to us, from Yusuf ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿For each of you, We have made a law﴾, he said: a path.

And Abu Sa'id related to us, Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and a method﴾, he said: and a sunnah (way). Likewise al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿a law and a method﴾: a path and a sunnah.

Likewise it was narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and Abu Ishaq al-Sab'i, that they said regarding His saying ﴿a law and a method﴾: meaning a path and a sunnah.

And from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and 'Ata' al-Khurasani also, the reverse: ﴿a law and a method﴾ meaning a sunnah and a path. The first is more appropriate, for shir'ah, which is also the shari'ah (sacred law), is that toward which one begins; from it one says "shara'a fi kadha" (he began in such and such), meaning he started it. Likewise the shari'ah is that from which one goes down to the water. As for minhaj, it is the clear, easy road, and the sunan (ways) are the paths. So interpreting His saying ﴿a law and a method﴾ as a path and a sunnah is more apparent in its appropriateness than the reverse, and Allah knows best.

Then this is information about the nations of differing religions, with regard to what Allah sent His noble messengers with, of laws differing in rulings, yet agreeing in tawhid (the oneness of Allah), as is established in Sahih al-Bukhari from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ said: "We, the company of the prophets, are half-brothers, and our religion is one." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3443] He meant by this tawhid, with which Allah sent every messenger He dispatched, and which He included in every book He revealed, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [Al-Anbiya 21:25], and He said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid false deities"﴾ [Al-Nahl 16:36]. As for the laws, they differ in commands and prohibitions. Something may be forbidden in one law and then made lawful in another, and vice versa; something light in one may be made more severe in another. This is due to Allah's perfect wisdom and conclusive proof.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah regarding His saying ﴿For each of you, We have made a law and a method﴾: he said: a path and a sunnah. The sunan differ: in the Torah there is a law, in the Gospel there is a law, and in the Furqan (Qur'an) there is a law, in which Allah makes lawful what He wills and forbids what He wills, so that He may know who obeys Him from among those who disobey Him. And the religion that Allah will not accept other than is tawhid and sincere devotion to Allah, which the messengers brought.

It was also said: the addressees of this are this Ummah (community). Its meaning is: ﴿For each of you﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿We have made a law and a method﴾, O community, meaning it is for all of you, that you may follow it. The object pronoun in His saying ﴿For each of you, We have made﴾ is omitted, meaning: We have made it, namely the Qur'an, ﴿a law and a method﴾, meaning a path to the correct goals, and a sunnah, meaning a clear, evident road and course.

This is the substance of what Ibn Jarir related from Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him. The correct view is the first, and what supports it is His saying: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation﴾. Had this been an address to this Ummah alone, it would not be correct to say ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation﴾, for they are one nation. Rather, this is an address to all the nations, and information about His great power, by which, had He willed, He would have gathered all people upon one religion and one law, none of which would be abrogated. But He, may He be exalted, legislated for each messenger a distinct law, then abrogated them or some of them through the mission of the next one, until He abrogated all of them through what He sent His servant and messenger Muhammad ﷺ with, whom He sent to all the people of the earth, and whom He made the seal of all the prophets. For this reason He said: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation, but He wanted to test you in what He has given you﴾, meaning that He, may He be exalted, legislated laws that differ in order to test His servants regarding what He prescribed for them, and to reward them or punish them for their obedience and disobedience, by what they did or resolved upon of all that.

'Abdullah ibn Kathir said: ﴿in what He has given you﴾ means: of the Book.

Then He, may He be exalted, urged them to hasten toward good deeds and to be quick to them, saying: ﴿So race toward good deeds﴾. These are obedience to Allah and following His law, which He made abrogating what came before it, and believing in His Book, the Qur'an, which is the last book He revealed.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you﴾, meaning your return and your destination, O people, and your final place is with Him on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And He will inform you about that over which you used to differ﴾, meaning He will inform you about what you differed over concerning the truth, rewarding the truthful for their truthfulness and punishing the disbelievers, the deniers, those who reject the truth and turn away from it to something else without evidence or proof, indeed those who obstinately oppose the decisive proofs, the conclusive arguments and the clear evidences.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿So race toward good deeds﴾ means the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. The first view is more apparent.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their desires﴾, it is an emphasis on what came before of the command to this, and the prohibition of opposing it.

Then Allah said [Addition from MS A.]: ﴿And beware of them, lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you.﴾ That is, beware of your enemies, the Jews, lest they distort the truth to you in the matters they bring to you. Do not be deceived by them, for they are liars, disbelievers, and treacherous.

﴿But if they turn away﴾ means from what you judge between them in truth and oppose the law of Allah, ﴿then know that Allah intends only to afflict them for some of their sins.﴾ That is, know that this happens by the decree and wisdom of Allah concerning them, that He turns them away from guidance because of the earlier sins they have committed, which required their misguidance and their punishment.

﴿And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient.﴾ That is, most people are outside the obedience of their Lord, opposing the truth and turning away from it, as He said: ﴿And most people, however eager you are, will not be believers.﴾ [Yusuf: 103]. And He said: ﴿And if you obeyed most of those on earth, they would mislead you from the way of Allah﴾ [Al-An'am: 116] [Addition from MS A.].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client (mawla) of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ka'b ibn Asad, Ibn Sallubha, Abdullah ibn Suriya, and Shas ibn Qays said to one another: "Come, let us go to Muhammad; perhaps we can tempt him away from his religion!" So they came to him and said: "O Muhammad, you know that we are the rabbis of the Jews, their nobles and their leaders. If we follow you, the Jews will follow us and will not oppose us. Between us and our people there is a dispute, so we will bring them to you to judge, and you will rule for us against them, and we will believe in you and affirm you!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused that. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning them: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you﴾ up to His saying: ﴿for a people who are certain﴾. Related by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Do they then desire the judgment of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam)? And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who are certain?﴾, Allah rebukes those who depart from the firm judgment of Allah, which encompasses every good and forbids every evil, and turn instead to other opinions, desires, and conventions that men have devised without any basis in the law of Allah. This is like the judgments of the Jahiliyyah, with their misguidance and ignorance, which they devised by their own opinions and desires. It is also like the Tatars, who rule by the royal policies taken from their king Genghis Khan (Jinkizkhan), who laid down for them the Yasa (Yasiq), which is a compiled book of rulings borrowed from various laws: Judaism, Christianity, and the Islamic religion. In it are many rulings he took from his own mere opinion and desire, and they became a law followed by his descendants, whom they preferred over judgment by the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ). Whoever among them does this is a disbeliever who must be fought until he returns to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), and judges by nothing else, in little or in much. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they desire the judgment of the Jahiliyyah?﴾ That is, they seek and desire it, and they deviate from the judgment of Allah. ﴿And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who are certain?﴾ That is, who is more just than Allah in His judgment for one who understands the law of Allah, believes in it, is certain of it, and knows that He, the Exalted, is the most judicious of judges and more merciful to His creatures than a mother to her child, for He is the All-Knowing of everything, the All-Powerful over everything, and the Just in everything.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hilal ibn Fayyad narrated to us, Abu Ubaydah al-Najiyy [in MS D and A: al-Bajiyy] narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: "Whoever judges by other than the judgment of Allah, his judgment is the judgment of the Jahiliyyah" [Addition from MSS R and A.].

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us by reading to him: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: When a man asked Tawus, "Shall I show preference between my children in gifts?", he would recite: ﴿Do they then desire the judgment of the Jahiliyyah? And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who are certain?﴾ [Addition from MSS R, D, and A.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani, the memorizer, said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Wahhab ibn Najdah al-Khawti narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi narrated to us, Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah informed us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn, from Nafi ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most hated of people to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is one who seeks in Islam the sunnah of the Jahiliyyah, and one who demands the blood of a man without right, so that he may shed his blood." Al-Bukhari also related, from Abu al-Yaman with his chain, something similar [Addition in MSS R and A: "with additions"]. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/374) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6882.]

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah 5:48–50 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, may He be exalted, mentioned the Torah that He sent down to Musa (Moses), His interlocutor, [peace be upon him] [[addition from A.]], and praised it and commended it, and commanded [[in A: "and We commanded"]] that it be followed wherever it was valid to follow, and mentioned the Gospel and praised it, and commanded its people to establish it and follow what is in it, as was explained earlier, He began to mention the Mighty Qur'an, which He sent down to His servant and noble messenger. He said: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book with the truth﴾, meaning with the truth that has no doubt that it is from Allah, ﴿confirming what came before it of the Scripture﴾, meaning of the earlier books that contain its mention and praise, and that it would be sent down from Allah upon His servant and messenger Muhammad ﷺ. Its descent came as they had foretold, which increased its truthfulness in the eyes of those who bore it from people of insight, who submitted to Allah's command, followed His laws, and believed in His messengers, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces in prostration and say, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord is ever fulfilled."﴾ [Al-Isra 17:107–108], meaning: if what Allah promised through the tongues of the earlier messengers, regarding the coming of Muhammad, peace be upon him, was indeed ﴿fulfilled﴾, meaning certain to occur without fail.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and as a guardian over it﴾, Sufyan al-Thawri and others narrated from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas that it means: entrusted with it. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: al-Muhaymin means al-Amin (the trustworthy); he said: the Qur'an is trustworthy over every book before it.

Similar things were narrated from 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, 'Atiyyah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd.

Ibn Juraij said: the Qur'an is a guardian over the earlier books; whatever in them agrees with it is true, and whatever contradicts it is false.

It was narrated from al-Walibi, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and as a guardian﴾ means a witness. Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi also said likewise.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and as a guardian﴾ means a judge over what came before it of the books.

All these statements are close in meaning, for the name "al-Muhaymin" comprises all of this. He is trustworthy, a witness, and a judge over every book before it. Allah made this Mighty Book, which He sent down as the last and seal of the books, the most comprehensive, the greatest and the most perfect [[in R, D: "and the most complete"]], since it gathers the excellences of what came before it and adds to it perfections not found in any other. For this reason He made it a witness, a trustworthy guardian and a judge over all of them. Allah, may He be exalted, took upon Himself its preservation by His own noble self, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [Al-Hijr 15:9].

As for what Ibn Abi Hatim related from 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid, that they said regarding His saying ﴿and as a guardian over it﴾, meaning Muhammad ﷺ is trustworthy over the Qur'an, this is correct in meaning, but there is room for doubt in explaining it this way, and also in construing it grammatically (i'rab) in this manner. In sum, the first view is the correct one. Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said, after relating this from Mujahid: "This interpretation is far from what is understood in the speech of the Arabs; rather, it is an error. That is because al-Muhaymin is coordinated with al-Musaddiq (the confirmer), so it can only describe what al-Musaddiq describes." He said: "Had it been as Mujahid said, it would have said: 'And We sent down to you the Book confirming what came before it of the Scripture, a guardian over it,' without a conjunction."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So judge between them by what Allah has revealed﴾, meaning: so judge, O Muhammad, between the people, their Arabs and non-Arabs, their unlettered and their People of the Book, ﴿by what Allah has revealed﴾ to you in this Mighty Book, and by what He has established for you of the rulings of those prophets who came before you and which He did not abrogate (naskh) in your law. Ibn Jarir gave this meaning.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Ammar related to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam related to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was given a choice: if he wished, he would judge between them, and if he wished, he would turn away from them. [Then] they returned him to their own rulings, so this was revealed: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires﴾. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to judge between them by what is in our Book.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and do not follow their desires﴾, meaning their opinions which they had agreed upon, and because of which they abandoned what Allah revealed to His messenger. For this reason He said: ﴿and do not follow their desires, away from the truth that has come to you﴾, meaning do not turn away from the truth that Allah has commanded you to, toward the desires of these ignorant wretched people.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿For each of you, We have made a law (shir'ah) and a method (minhaj)﴾, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar related to us, from Yusuf ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿For each of you, We have made a law﴾, he said: a path.

And Abu Sa'id related to us, Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and a method﴾, he said: and a sunnah (way). Likewise al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿a law and a method﴾: a path and a sunnah.

Likewise it was narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and Abu Ishaq al-Sab'i, that they said regarding His saying ﴿a law and a method﴾: meaning a path and a sunnah.

And from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and 'Ata' al-Khurasani also, the reverse: ﴿a law and a method﴾ meaning a sunnah and a path. The first is more appropriate, for shir'ah, which is also the shari'ah (sacred law), is that toward which one begins; from it one says "shara'a fi kadha" (he began in such and such), meaning he started it. Likewise the shari'ah is that from which one goes down to the water. As for minhaj, it is the clear, easy road, and the sunan (ways) are the paths. So interpreting His saying ﴿a law and a method﴾ as a path and a sunnah is more apparent in its appropriateness than the reverse, and Allah knows best.

Then this is information about the nations of differing religions, with regard to what Allah sent His noble messengers with, of laws differing in rulings, yet agreeing in tawhid (the oneness of Allah), as is established in Sahih al-Bukhari from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ said: "We, the company of the prophets, are half-brothers, and our religion is one." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3443] He meant by this tawhid, with which Allah sent every messenger He dispatched, and which He included in every book He revealed, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [Al-Anbiya 21:25], and He said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid false deities"﴾ [Al-Nahl 16:36]. As for the laws, they differ in commands and prohibitions. Something may be forbidden in one law and then made lawful in another, and vice versa; something light in one may be made more severe in another. This is due to Allah's perfect wisdom and conclusive proof.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah regarding His saying ﴿For each of you, We have made a law and a method﴾: he said: a path and a sunnah. The sunan differ: in the Torah there is a law, in the Gospel there is a law, and in the Furqan (Qur'an) there is a law, in which Allah makes lawful what He wills and forbids what He wills, so that He may know who obeys Him from among those who disobey Him. And the religion that Allah will not accept other than is tawhid and sincere devotion to Allah, which the messengers brought.

It was also said: the addressees of this are this Ummah (community). Its meaning is: ﴿For each of you﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿We have made a law and a method﴾, O community, meaning it is for all of you, that you may follow it. The object pronoun in His saying ﴿For each of you, We have made﴾ is omitted, meaning: We have made it, namely the Qur'an, ﴿a law and a method﴾, meaning a path to the correct goals, and a sunnah, meaning a clear, evident road and course.

This is the substance of what Ibn Jarir related from Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him. The correct view is the first, and what supports it is His saying: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation﴾. Had this been an address to this Ummah alone, it would not be correct to say ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation﴾, for they are one nation. Rather, this is an address to all the nations, and information about His great power, by which, had He willed, He would have gathered all people upon one religion and one law, none of which would be abrogated. But He, may He be exalted, legislated for each messenger a distinct law, then abrogated them or some of them through the mission of the next one, until He abrogated all of them through what He sent His servant and messenger Muhammad ﷺ with, whom He sent to all the people of the earth, and whom He made the seal of all the prophets. For this reason He said: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation, but He wanted to test you in what He has given you﴾, meaning that He, may He be exalted, legislated laws that differ in order to test His servants regarding what He prescribed for them, and to reward them or punish them for their obedience and disobedience, by what they did or resolved upon of all that.

'Abdullah ibn Kathir said: ﴿in what He has given you﴾ means: of the Book.

Then He, may He be exalted, urged them to hasten toward good deeds and to be quick to them, saying: ﴿So race toward good deeds﴾. These are obedience to Allah and following His law, which He made abrogating what came before it, and believing in His Book, the Qur'an, which is the last book He revealed.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you﴾, meaning your return and your destination, O people, and your final place is with Him on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And He will inform you about that over which you used to differ﴾, meaning He will inform you about what you differed over concerning the truth, rewarding the truthful for their truthfulness and punishing the disbelievers, the deniers, those who reject the truth and turn away from it to something else without evidence or proof, indeed those who obstinately oppose the decisive proofs, the conclusive arguments and the clear evidences.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿So race toward good deeds﴾ means the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. The first view is more apparent.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their desires﴾, it is an emphasis on what came before of the command to this, and the prohibition of opposing it.

Then Allah said [Addition from MS A.]: ﴿And beware of them, lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you.﴾ That is, beware of your enemies, the Jews, lest they distort the truth to you in the matters they bring to you. Do not be deceived by them, for they are liars, disbelievers, and treacherous.

﴿But if they turn away﴾ means from what you judge between them in truth and oppose the law of Allah, ﴿then know that Allah intends only to afflict them for some of their sins.﴾ That is, know that this happens by the decree and wisdom of Allah concerning them, that He turns them away from guidance because of the earlier sins they have committed, which required their misguidance and their punishment.

﴿And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient.﴾ That is, most people are outside the obedience of their Lord, opposing the truth and turning away from it, as He said: ﴿And most people, however eager you are, will not be believers.﴾ [Yusuf: 103]. And He said: ﴿And if you obeyed most of those on earth, they would mislead you from the way of Allah﴾ [Al-An'am: 116] [Addition from MS A.].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client (mawla) of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ka'b ibn Asad, Ibn Sallubha, Abdullah ibn Suriya, and Shas ibn Qays said to one another: "Come, let us go to Muhammad; perhaps we can tempt him away from his religion!" So they came to him and said: "O Muhammad, you know that we are the rabbis of the Jews, their nobles and their leaders. If we follow you, the Jews will follow us and will not oppose us. Between us and our people there is a dispute, so we will bring them to you to judge, and you will rule for us against them, and we will believe in you and affirm you!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused that. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning them: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you﴾ up to His saying: ﴿for a people who are certain﴾. Related by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Do they then desire the judgment of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam)? And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who are certain?﴾, Allah rebukes those who depart from the firm judgment of Allah, which encompasses every good and forbids every evil, and turn instead to other opinions, desires, and conventions that men have devised without any basis in the law of Allah. This is like the judgments of the Jahiliyyah, with their misguidance and ignorance, which they devised by their own opinions and desires. It is also like the Tatars, who rule by the royal policies taken from their king Genghis Khan (Jinkizkhan), who laid down for them the Yasa (Yasiq), which is a compiled book of rulings borrowed from various laws: Judaism, Christianity, and the Islamic religion. In it are many rulings he took from his own mere opinion and desire, and they became a law followed by his descendants, whom they preferred over judgment by the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ). Whoever among them does this is a disbeliever who must be fought until he returns to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), and judges by nothing else, in little or in much. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they desire the judgment of the Jahiliyyah?﴾ That is, they seek and desire it, and they deviate from the judgment of Allah. ﴿And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who are certain?﴾ That is, who is more just than Allah in His judgment for one who understands the law of Allah, believes in it, is certain of it, and knows that He, the Exalted, is the most judicious of judges and more merciful to His creatures than a mother to her child, for He is the All-Knowing of everything, the All-Powerful over everything, and the Just in everything.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hilal ibn Fayyad narrated to us, Abu Ubaydah al-Najiyy [in MS D and A: al-Bajiyy] narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: "Whoever judges by other than the judgment of Allah, his judgment is the judgment of the Jahiliyyah" [Addition from MSS R and A.].

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us by reading to him: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: When a man asked Tawus, "Shall I show preference between my children in gifts?", he would recite: ﴿Do they then desire the judgment of the Jahiliyyah? And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who are certain?﴾ [Addition from MSS R, D, and A.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani, the memorizer, said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Wahhab ibn Najdah al-Khawti narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi narrated to us, Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah informed us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn, from Nafi ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most hated of people to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is one who seeks in Islam the sunnah of the Jahiliyyah, and one who demands the blood of a man without right, so that he may shed his blood." Al-Bukhari also related, from Abu al-Yaman with his chain, something similar [Addition in MSS R and A: "with additions"]. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/374) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6882.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Ammar related to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam related to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was given a choice: if he wished, he would judge between them, and if he wished, he would turn away from them. [Then] they returned him to their own rulings, so this was revealed: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires﴾. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to judge between them by what is in our Book.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and do not follow their desires﴾, meaning their opinions which they had agreed upon, and because of which they abandoned what Allah revealed to His messenger. For this reason He said: ﴿and do not follow their desires, away from the truth that has come to you﴾, meaning do not turn away from the truth that Allah has commanded you to, toward the desires of these ignorant wretched people.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿For each of you, We have made a law (shir'ah) and a method (minhaj)﴾, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar related to us, from Yusuf ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿For each of you, We have made a law﴾, he said: a path.

And Abu Sa'id related to us, Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and a method﴾, he said: and a sunnah (way). Likewise al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿a law and a method﴾: a path and a sunnah.

Likewise it was narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and Abu Ishaq al-Sab'i, that they said regarding His saying ﴿a law and a method﴾: meaning a path and a sunnah.

And from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and 'Ata' al-Khurasani also, the reverse: ﴿a law and a method﴾ meaning a sunnah and a path. The first is more appropriate, for shir'ah, which is also the shari'ah (sacred law), is that toward which one begins; from it one says "shara'a fi kadha" (he began in such and such), meaning he started it. Likewise the shari'ah is that from which one goes down to the water. As for minhaj, it is the clear, easy road, and the sunan (ways) are the paths. So interpreting His saying ﴿a law and a method﴾ as a path and a sunnah is more apparent in its appropriateness than the reverse, and Allah knows best.

Then this is information about the nations of differing religions, with regard to what Allah sent His noble messengers with, of laws differing in rulings, yet agreeing in tawhid (the oneness of Allah), as is established in Sahih al-Bukhari from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ said: "We, the company of the prophets, are half-brothers, and our religion is one." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3443] He meant by this tawhid, with which Allah sent every messenger He dispatched, and which He included in every book He revealed, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [Al-Anbiya 21:25], and He said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid false deities"﴾ [Al-Nahl 16:36]. As for the laws, they differ in commands and prohibitions. Something may be forbidden in one law and then made lawful in another, and vice versa; something light in one may be made more severe in another. This is due to Allah's perfect wisdom and conclusive proof.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah regarding His saying ﴿For each of you, We have made a law and a method﴾: he said: a path and a sunnah. The sunan differ: in the Torah there is a law, in the Gospel there is a law, and in the Furqan (Qur'an) there is a law, in which Allah makes lawful what He wills and forbids what He wills, so that He may know who obeys Him from among those who disobey Him. And the religion that Allah will not accept other than is tawhid and sincere devotion to Allah, which the messengers brought.

It was also said: the addressees of this are this Ummah (community). Its meaning is: ﴿For each of you﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿We have made a law and a method﴾, O community, meaning it is for all of you, that you may follow it. The object pronoun in His saying ﴿For each of you, We have made﴾ is omitted, meaning: We have made it, namely the Qur'an, ﴿a law and a method﴾, meaning a path to the correct goals, and a sunnah, meaning a clear, evident road and course.

This is the substance of what Ibn Jarir related from Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him. The correct view is the first, and what supports it is His saying: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation﴾. Had this been an address to this Ummah alone, it would not be correct to say ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation﴾, for they are one nation. Rather, this is an address to all the nations, and information about His great power, by which, had He willed, He would have gathered all people upon one religion and one law, none of which would be abrogated. But He, may He be exalted, legislated for each messenger a distinct law, then abrogated them or some of them through the mission of the next one, until He abrogated all of them through what He sent His servant and messenger Muhammad ﷺ with, whom He sent to all the people of the earth, and whom He made the seal of all the prophets. For this reason He said: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation, but He wanted to test you in what He has given you﴾, meaning that He, may He be exalted, legislated laws that differ in order to test His servants regarding what He prescribed for them, and to reward them or punish them for their obedience and disobedience, by what they did or resolved upon of all that.

'Abdullah ibn Kathir said: ﴿in what He has given you﴾ means: of the Book.

Then He, may He be exalted, urged them to hasten toward good deeds and to be quick to them, saying: ﴿So race toward good deeds﴾. These are obedience to Allah and following His law, which He made abrogating what came before it, and believing in His Book, the Qur'an, which is the last book He revealed.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you﴾, meaning your return and your destination, O people, and your final place is with Him on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And He will inform you about that over which you used to differ﴾, meaning He will inform you about what you differed over concerning the truth, rewarding the truthful for their truthfulness and punishing the disbelievers, the deniers, those who reject the truth and turn away from it to something else without evidence or proof, indeed those who obstinately oppose the decisive proofs, the conclusive arguments and the clear evidences.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿So race toward good deeds﴾ means the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. The first view is more apparent.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their desires﴾, it is an emphasis on what came before of the command to this, and the prohibition of opposing it.

Then Allah said [Addition from MS A.]: ﴿And beware of them, lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you.﴾ That is, beware of your enemies, the Jews, lest they distort the truth to you in the matters they bring to you. Do not be deceived by them, for they are liars, disbelievers, and treacherous.

﴿But if they turn away﴾ means from what you judge between them in truth and oppose the law of Allah, ﴿then know that Allah intends only to afflict them for some of their sins.﴾ That is, know that this happens by the decree and wisdom of Allah concerning them, that He turns them away from guidance because of the earlier sins they have committed, which required their misguidance and their punishment.

﴿And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient.﴾ That is, most people are outside the obedience of their Lord, opposing the truth and turning away from it, as He said: ﴿And most people, however eager you are, will not be believers.﴾ [Yusuf: 103]. And He said: ﴿And if you obeyed most of those on earth, they would mislead you from the way of Allah﴾ [Al-An'am: 116] [Addition from MS A.].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client (mawla) of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ka'b ibn Asad, Ibn Sallubha, Abdullah ibn Suriya, and Shas ibn Qays said to one another: "Come, let us go to Muhammad; perhaps we can tempt him away from his religion!" So they came to him and said: "O Muhammad, you know that we are the rabbis of the Jews, their nobles and their leaders. If we follow you, the Jews will follow us and will not oppose us. Between us and our people there is a dispute, so we will bring them to you to judge, and you will rule for us against them, and we will believe in you and affirm you!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused that. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning them: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you﴾ up to His saying: ﴿for a people who are certain﴾. Related by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Do they then desire the judgment of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam)? And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who are certain?﴾, Allah rebukes those who depart from the firm judgment of Allah, which encompasses every good and forbids every evil, and turn instead to other opinions, desires, and conventions that men have devised without any basis in the law of Allah. This is like the judgments of the Jahiliyyah, with their misguidance and ignorance, which they devised by their own opinions and desires. It is also like the Tatars, who rule by the royal policies taken from their king Genghis Khan (Jinkizkhan), who laid down for them the Yasa (Yasiq), which is a compiled book of rulings borrowed from various laws: Judaism, Christianity, and the Islamic religion. In it are many rulings he took from his own mere opinion and desire, and they became a law followed by his descendants, whom they preferred over judgment by the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ). Whoever among them does this is a disbeliever who must be fought until he returns to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), and judges by nothing else, in little or in much. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they desire the judgment of the Jahiliyyah?﴾ That is, they seek and desire it, and they deviate from the judgment of Allah. ﴿And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who are certain?﴾ That is, who is more just than Allah in His judgment for one who understands the law of Allah, believes in it, is certain of it, and knows that He, the Exalted, is the most judicious of judges and more merciful to His creatures than a mother to her child, for He is the All-Knowing of everything, the All-Powerful over everything, and the Just in everything.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hilal ibn Fayyad narrated to us, Abu Ubaydah al-Najiyy [in MS D and A: al-Bajiyy] narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: "Whoever judges by other than the judgment of Allah, his judgment is the judgment of the Jahiliyyah" [Addition from MSS R and A.].

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us by reading to him: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: When a man asked Tawus, "Shall I show preference between my children in gifts?", he would recite: ﴿Do they then desire the judgment of the Jahiliyyah? And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who are certain?﴾ [Addition from MSS R, D, and A.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani, the memorizer, said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Wahhab ibn Najdah al-Khawti narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi narrated to us, Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah informed us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn, from Nafi ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most hated of people to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is one who seeks in Islam the sunnah of the Jahiliyyah, and one who demands the blood of a man without right, so that he may shed his blood." Al-Bukhari also related, from Abu al-Yaman with his chain, something similar [Addition in MSS R and A: "with additions"]. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/374) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6882.]

Ibn Kathir's Commentary on Surah 5 (al-Ma'idah), verses 51–53:

God the Exalted forbids His believing servants from taking the Jews and the Christians as allies (muwalah), those who are the enemies of Islam and its people, may God curse them. Then He informed that some of them are allies of others. Then He threatened and warned whoever engages in that, saying: ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Kathir ibn Shihab narrated to us, Muhammad—meaning Ibn Sa'id ibn Sabiq—narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Abi Qays narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Iyad: that 'Umar commanded Abu Musa al-Ash'ari to raise to him an account of what he had received and what he had given in a single ledger. He had a Christian scribe, so he presented that to him. 'Umar was amazed and said: "Indeed, this is a skilled one. Would you read for us a book that came from Syria in the mosque?" He said: "Indeed, he is not able to enter the mosque." 'Umar said: "Is he in a state of major impurity (junub)?" He said: "No, rather he is a Christian." He said: "So he rebuked me and struck my thigh, then said: Expel him. Then he recited: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾"

Then al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah said: Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn informed us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah said: "Let each of you beware of being a Jew or a Christian while he does not realize it." He said: "We thought he meant this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them﴾," and the verse etc.

And Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from 'Asim, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he was asked about the slaughtered animals of the Christians of the Arabs. He said: "Eat. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them.﴾"

It is also narrated from Abu al-Zinad something similar to that.

* *

His saying: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ means: doubt, uncertainty, and hypocrisy. ﴿They hasten toward them﴾ means: they hurry to their alliance and affection, inwardly and outwardly. ﴿They say, "We fear lest a misfortune strike us"﴾ means: they make excuses for their affection and alliance, claiming they fear that some event might occur in which the disbelievers gain victory over the Muslims, so that they would have favors with the Jews and Christians, which would benefit them. At that point Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a command from Him﴾. Al-Suddi said: this means the conquest of Makkah. Others said: it means the judgment and decision. ﴿Or a command from Him﴾—al-Suddi said: this means imposing the jizyah upon the Jews and Christians. ﴿And they will become﴾—meaning: those among the hypocrites who allied themselves with the Jews and Christians—﴿regretful for what they concealed within themselves﴾ of the alliance. ﴿Regretful﴾ means: over what they had done, which did not avail them anything nor repel any harm from them, but was rather the very source of corruption. For they were exposed, and Allah made their condition manifest to His believing servants in this world, after they had been concealed and it was not known how their state was. When the causes that exposed them came together, their matter became clear to the servants of Allah, the believers, and they marvelled at them: how they used to show that they were among the believers, swear to that, and make excuses, and so their lying and fabrication became evident. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who believed will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that they were with you?" Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers.﴾

The reciters differed regarding this letter. The majority recited it with the waw affixed in His saying ﴿And those who believe say﴾. Among them, some put ﴿wa-yaqulu﴾ in the nominative as a new beginning, and some put it in the accusative, coordinating it with His saying ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a command from Him﴾, its estimated form being "an yaʼtiya" and "wa-an yaqula". The people of Madinah recited ﴿yaqulu alladhina amanu﴾ without the waw, and likewise it is in their codices, as mentioned by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a command from Him﴾, then ﴿Then those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that they were with you? Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers."﴾

The exegetes differed concerning the occasion of revelation of these noble verses. Al-Suddi mentioned that they were revealed concerning two men, one of whom said to his companion after the Battle of Uhud: "As for me, I am going to that Jew, so I will take refuge with him and become a Jew with him, perhaps he will benefit me if an event occurs or a calamity befalls!" And the other said: "As for me, I will go to so-and-so the Christian in Syria, take refuge with him, and become a Christian with him." So Allah [the Mighty and Majestic] revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾ and the verses.

'Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to Banu Qurayzah. They asked him: "What is he going to do with us?" He pointed with his hand to his throat, meaning that it would be slaughter. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

It was also said: it was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, as Ibn Jarir said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard my father, from 'Atiyyah ibn Sa'd, who said: 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, from Banu al-Khazraj, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have many Jewish clients, and I disavow to Allah and His Messenger the alliance with the Jews, and I take Allah and His Messenger as my allies." 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said: "I am a man who fears reverses; I will not disavow the alliance of my clients." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy: "O Abu al-Hubab, whatever you have withheld from the alliance of the Jews in favor of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, it is yours instead of him." He said: "I accept!" So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/395)]

Then Ibn Jarir said: Hannad narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-Zuhri who said: When the people of Badr were defeated, the Muslims said to their Jewish allies: "Believe before Allah strikes you with a day like the day of Badr!" Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "Does it deceive you that you struck a group of Quraysh who had no knowledge of fighting? Had we resolved firmly to gather against you, you would have had no power to fight us!" 'Ubadah said: "O Messenger of Allah, my Jewish allies are strong in their persons, abundant in their weapons, and mighty in their power, and I disavow to Allah [Exalted] and to His Messenger the alliance with the Jews; I have no ally except Allah and His Messenger." 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said: "But I do not disavow the alliance of the Jews; I am a man who cannot do without them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu al-Hubab, do you see what you withheld from the alliance of the Jews in favor of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit—is it yours instead of him?" He said: "Then I accept!" He said: So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67]. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/396)]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The first tribe of the Jews to break what was between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was Banu Qaynuqa'. 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged them until they came down under his judgment. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul stood up to him when Allah had enabled him over them, and said: "O Muhammad, be good to my clients." They were allies of the Khazraj. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed in responding to him, so he said: "O Muhammad, be good to my clients." He said: So he turned away from him. Then he put his hand into the collar of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ coat of mail. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Let me go!" And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry until his face showed darkness, then he said: "Woe to you, let me go!" He said: "No, by Allah, I will not let you go until you are good to my clients: four hundred unarmored men and three hundred mail-clad men, who protected me from the red and the black; will you mow them down in a single morning? Indeed I am a man who fears reverses." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "They are yours." [Sirat Ibn Ishaq, no. 498]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abu Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: When Banu Qaynuqa' fought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy clung to their affair and stood up on their behalf. 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who was from Banu 'Awf of the Khazraj and had the same alliance with them as 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had, went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, left them to him, disavowed to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ their alliance, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I disavow to Allah and to His Messenger their alliance, and I take Allah and His Messenger and the believers as allies, and I disavow the alliance and allegiance of the disbelievers." Concerning him and 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy the verses in al-Ma'idah were revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another﴾ up to His saying: [in a: "the verses"] ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies, indeed the party of Allah—they are the victorious﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 56]. [Sirat Ibn Ishaq, no. 499; see also Sirat Ibn Hisham (2/49) and Tafsir al-Tabari (10/396, 397)]

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from Usamah ibn Zayd who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy to visit him when he was ill. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "I used to forbid you from loving the Jews." 'Abd Allah said: "Surely As'ad ibn Zurarah hated them, and he died."

Abu Dawud also narrated it similarly, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq. [Musnad (5/201) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. 3094]

Among them, some put ﴿wa-yaqulu﴾ in the nominative as a new beginning, and some put it in the accusative, coordinating it with His saying ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a command from Him﴾, its estimated form being "an yaʼtiya" and "wa-an yaqula". The people of Madinah recited ﴿yaqulu alladhina amanu﴾ without the waw, and likewise it is in their codices, as mentioned by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a command from Him﴾, then ﴿Then those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that they were with you? Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers."﴾

The exegetes differed concerning the occasion of revelation of these noble verses. Al-Suddi mentioned that they were revealed concerning two men, one of whom said to his companion after the Battle of Uhud: "As for me, I am going to that Jew, so I will take refuge with him and become a Jew with him, perhaps he will benefit me if an event occurs or a calamity befalls!" And the other said: "As for me, I will go to so-and-so the Christian in Syria, take refuge with him, and become a Christian with him." So Allah [the Mighty and Majestic] revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾ and the verses.

'Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to Banu Qurayzah. They asked him: "What is he going to do with us?" He pointed with his hand to his throat, meaning that it would be slaughter. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

It was also said: it was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, as Ibn Jarir said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard my father, from 'Atiyyah ibn Sa'd, who said: 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, from Banu al-Khazraj, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have many Jewish clients, and I disavow to Allah and His Messenger the alliance with the Jews, and I take Allah and His Messenger as my allies." 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said: "I am a man who fears reverses; I will not disavow the alliance of my clients." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy: "O Abu al-Hubab, whatever you have withheld from the alliance of the Jews in favor of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, it is yours instead of him." He said: "I accept!" So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/395)]

Then Ibn Jarir said: Hannad narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-Zuhri who said: When the people of Badr were defeated, the Muslims said to their Jewish allies: "Believe before Allah strikes you with a day like the day of Badr!" Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "Does it deceive you that you struck a group of Quraysh who had no knowledge of fighting? Had we resolved firmly to gather against you, you would have had no power to fight us!" 'Ubadah said: "O Messenger of Allah, my Jewish allies are strong in their persons, abundant in their weapons, and mighty in their power, and I disavow to Allah [Exalted] and to His Messenger the alliance with the Jews; I have no ally except Allah and His Messenger." 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said: "But I do not disavow the alliance of the Jews; I am a man who cannot do without them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu al-Hubab, do you see what you withheld from the alliance of the Jews in favor of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit—is it yours instead of him?" He said: "Then I accept!" He said: So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67]. [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/396)]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The first tribe of the Jews to break what was between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was Banu Qaynuqa'. 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged them until they came down under his judgment. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul stood up to him when Allah had enabled him over them, and said: "O Muhammad, be good to my clients." They were allies of the Khazraj. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed in responding to him, so he said: "O Muhammad, be good to my clients." He said: So he turned away from him. Then he put his hand into the collar of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ coat of mail. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Let me go!" And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry until his face showed darkness, then he said: "Woe to you, let me go!" He said: "No, by Allah, I will not let you go until you are good to my clients: four hundred unarmored men and three hundred mail-clad men, who protected me from the red and the black; will you mow them down in a single morning? Indeed I am a man who fears reverses." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "They are yours." [Sirat Ibn Ishaq, no. 498]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abu Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: When Banu Qaynuqa' fought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy clung to their affair and stood up on their behalf. 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who was from Banu 'Awf of the Khazraj and had the same alliance with them as 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had, went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, left them to him, disavowed to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ their alliance, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I disavow to Allah and to His Messenger their alliance, and I take Allah and His Messenger and the believers as allies, and I disavow the alliance and allegiance of the disbelievers." Concerning him and 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy the verses in al-Ma'idah were revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another﴾ up to His saying: [in a: "the verses"] ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies, indeed the party of Allah—they are the victorious﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 56]. [Sirat Ibn Ishaq, no. 499; see also Sirat Ibn Hisham (2/49) and Tafsir al-Tabari (10/396, 397)]

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from Usamah ibn Zayd who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy to visit him when he was ill. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "I used to forbid you from loving the Jews." 'Abd Allah said: "Surely As'ad ibn Zurarah hated them, and he died."

Abu Dawud also narrated it similarly, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq. [Musnad (5/201) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. 3094]

Ibn Kathir's Commentary on Surah 5 (al-Ma'idah), verses 51–53:

God the Exalted forbids His believing servants from taking the Jews and the Christians as allies (muwalah), those who are the enemies of Islam and its people, may God curse them. Then He informed that some of them are allies of others. Then He threatened and warned whoever engages in that, saying: ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Kathir ibn Shihab narrated to us, Muhammad—meaning Ibn Sa'id ibn Sabiq—narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Abi Qays narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Iyad: that 'Umar commanded Abu Musa al-Ash'ari to raise to him an account of what he had received and what he had given in a single ledger. He had a Christian scribe, so he presented that to him. 'Umar was amazed and said: "Indeed, this is a skilled one. Would you read for us a book that came from Syria in the mosque?" He said: "Indeed, he is not able to enter the mosque." 'Umar said: "Is he in a state of major impurity (junub)?" He said: "No, rather he is a Christian." He said: "So he rebuked me and struck my thigh, then said: Expel him. Then he recited: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾"

Then al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah said: Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn informed us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah said: "Let each of you beware of being a Jew or a Christian while he does not realize it." He said: "We thought he meant this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them﴾," and the verse etc.

And Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from 'Asim, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he was asked about the slaughtered animals of the Christians of the Arabs. He said: "Eat. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them.﴾"

It is also narrated from Abu al-Zinad something similar to that.

* *

His saying: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ means: doubt, uncertainty, and hypocrisy. ﴿They hasten toward them﴾ means: they hurry to their alliance and affection, inwardly and outwardly. ﴿They say, "We fear lest a misfortune strike us"﴾ means: they make excuses for their affection and alliance, claiming they fear that some event might occur in which the disbelievers gain victory over the Muslims, so that they would have favors with the Jews and Christians, which would benefit them. At that point Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a command from Him﴾. Al-Suddi said: this means the conquest of Makkah. Others said: it means the judgment and decision. ﴿Or a command from Him﴾—al-Suddi said: this means imposing the jizyah upon the Jews and Christians. ﴿And they will become﴾—meaning: those among the hypocrites who allied themselves with the Jews and Christians—﴿regretful for what they concealed within themselves﴾ of the alliance. ﴿Regretful﴾ means: over what they had done, which did not avail them anything nor repel any harm from them, but was rather the very source of corruption. For they were exposed, and Allah made their condition manifest to His believing servants in this world, after they had been concealed and it was not known how their state was. When the causes that exposed them came together, their matter became clear to the servants of Allah, the believers, and they marvelled at them: how they used to show that they were among the believers, swear to that, and make excuses, and so their lying and fabrication became evident. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who believed will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that they were with you?" Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers.﴾

The reciters differed regarding this letter. The majority recited it with the waw affixed in His saying ﴿And those who believe say﴾. Among them, some put ﴿wa-yaqulu﴾ in the nominative as a new beginning, and some put it in the accusative, coordinating it with His saying ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a command from Him﴾, its estimated form being "an yaʼtiya" and "wa-an yaqula". Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a command from Him﴾, then ﴿Then those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that they were with you? Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers."﴾

So Allah [the Mighty and Majestic] revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾ and the verses.

'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged them until they came down under his judgment. Then he put his hand into the collar of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ coat of mail. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Let me go!" And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry until his face showed darkness, then he said: "Woe to you, let me go!" Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abu Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: When Banu Qaynuqa' fought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy clung to their affair and stood up on their behalf.
