[Sirat Ibn Ishaq, no. 499; see also Sirat Ibn Hisham (2/49) and Tafsir al-Tabari (10/396, 397)]

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from Usamah ibn Zayd who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy to visit him when he was ill. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "I used to forbid you from loving the Jews." 'Abd Allah said: "Surely As'ad ibn Zurarah hated them, and he died."

Abu Dawud also narrated it similarly, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq. [Musnad (5/201) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. 3094]

God, may He be exalted, says, informing of His great power, that whoever turns away from supporting His religion and establishing His law, Allah will replace him with one who is better than him for it, and stronger in defense, and more upright in the path, as He says: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be the likes of you﴾ [Muhammad: 38]. And He says: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away, O people, and bring others﴾ [an-Nisa': 133]. And He says: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 19-20], meaning, not unattainable or hard. And He says here: ﴿O you who have believed, whoever among you reverts from his religion﴾, meaning, turns back from the truth to falsehood.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It was revealed concerning the rulers from Quraysh. And al-Hasan al-Basri said: It was revealed concerning the people of apostasy (ridda, renunciation of Islam) in the days of Abu Bakr.

﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾. Al-Hasan said: By Allah, they are Abu Bakr and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash say concerning His saying ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾: they are the people of al-Qadisiyyah. And Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Mujahid: they are a people from Saba'.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn al-Ajlah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, he said: They are people from the people of Yemen, then from Kindah, then from as-Sakun.

And my father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa narrated to us, Mu'awiyah, meaning Ibn Hafs, narrated to us, from Abu Ziyad al-Hilfani, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked concerning His saying: ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, and he said: "They are a people from the people of Yemen, then from Kindah, then from as-Sakun, then from Tujib."[[It was also narrated by at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat under no. (3312) (Majma' al-Bahrayn), through the route of Mu'awiyah ibn Hafs, from Abu Ziyad Isma'il ibn Zakariyya, from Muhammad ibn Qays al-Asadi, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir with it. He said: "No one narrated it from Muhammad ibn Qays al-Asadi except Abu Ziyad, and none narrated from him except Mu'awiyah. Abu Hamid reported it alone, adding here Muhammad ibn Qays al-Asadi."

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned it in al-'Ilal (2/95) without mentioning Muhammad ibn Qays in its chain, as it is here in his tafsir, and said: I heard my father say: "This hadith is baseless."

Note: Here it occurs as Abu Ziyad al-Hilfani, while in al-'Ilal it is al-Khilqani, and that is the correct form, "al-Khilqani," as in "al-Istighna' fi al-Mashhurin min Hamalat al-'Ilm bi al-Kuna" by Ibn 'Abd al-Barr (2/1199).]] This is a very strange hadith.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to us, 'Abd as-Samad, meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Warith, narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, I heard 'Iyad narrating from al-Ash'ari, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are the people of this one [pointing to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari's people]." Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah in similar wording.[[Tafsir at-Tabari (10/414). Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it in al-Musannaf (12/123), Ibn Sa'd in at-Tabaqat (4/107), at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/371), and Abu Nu'aym in Tarikh Asbahan (1/59), all through the route of Shu'bah. Al-Haythami said in Majma' az-Zawa'id (7/16): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

* *

His saying ﴿humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾: these are the attributes of the perfect believers, that each of them is humble toward his brother and ally, and firm against his opponent and enemy, as He says: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. And in the description of the Prophet (ﷺ) it is said that he was "the smiling, the fighter": he smiled toward his allies and fought against his enemies.

* *

His saying ﴿who strive in the way of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic﴾: meaning, nothing turns them away from what they are engaged in of obedience to Allah, fighting His enemies, establishing the prescribed punishments, and enjoining good and forbidding evil. No one turns them away from that, no one prevents them from it, and the blame of a blamer or the reproach of a reproacher does not affect them.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Sallam Abu al-Mundhir narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Wasi', from 'Abdullah ibn as-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: My beloved (ﷺ) commanded me with seven things: He commanded me to love the poor and to be near them; he commanded me to look to someone below me and not to look to someone above me; he commanded me to maintain ties of kinship even if they turn away; he commanded me not to ask anyone for anything; he commanded me to say the truth even if it is bitter; he commanded me not to fear the blame of a blamer in the matter of Allah; and he commanded me to frequently say: "There is no power and no strength except with Allah," for they are from a treasure beneath the Throne.[[al-Musnad (5/159).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, from Abu al-Muthanna, that Abu Dharr said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took five pledges from me, bound me by seven, and made Allah a witness over me by nine: that I would not fear the blame of a blamer in the matter of Allah. Abu Dharr said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me and said: "Would you like to pledge allegiance to me, and for you is Paradise?" I said: Yes. He said: And I extended my hands, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said, while stipulating: "On condition that you do not ask people for anything?" I said: Yes. He said: "Nor your whip, even if it falls from you, until you descend to it and pick it up."[[al-Musnad (5/172).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Mu'alla al-Qurdusi, from al-Hasan, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [in another version: "from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet"], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware! Let not fear of people prevent any one of you from speaking the truth when he sees it or witnesses it, for it does not bring near a term nor distance a provision [in another version: "it does not distance from a term nor bring near a provision"] to say the truth or to remind of something great." Ahmad alone narrated it.[[al-Musnad (3/50).]]

Ahmad said: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from Zubayd, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [in another version: "from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet"], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let none of you belittle himself by seeing a matter in which Allah has a word, and then not speaking about it. He will be asked on the Day of Resurrection: 'What prevented you from saying such and such about Me?' He will say: 'Fear of people.' He will be told: 'It was I who had more right that you should fear Me.'"

Ibn Majah narrated it through the hadith of al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah with it.[[al-Musnad (3/73) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4008). Al-Busiri said in az-Zawa'id (3/242): "This chain is sahih."]] Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated, through the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi Tuwalah [in another version: "'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi Tuwalah"], from Nahar ibn 'Abdullah al-'Abdi al-Madani, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [in another version: "from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet"], from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed Allah will question the servant on the Day of Resurrection, until He asks him, saying: 'O My servant, you saw an evil and did not forbid it?' When Allah makes the servant recall his argument, he will say: 'O Lord, I trusted in You and feared the people.'"[[al-Musnad (3/77) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4017). Al-Busiri said in az-Zawa'id (3/244): "This chain is sahih."]]

And it is established in the Sahih: "It is not befitting for a believer to humiliate himself." They said: "And how does he humiliate himself, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "He takes on a trial that he cannot bear."[[I did not find it in my search of the two Sahihs, but perhaps I will check it later. It was narrated by at-Tirmidhi in as-Sunan no. (2254) and Ibn Majah in as-Sunan no. (4016), through the route of 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from al-Hasan, from Jundub, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him. At-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan gharib hadith." In its chain is 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who is weak.]]

﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾, meaning: whoever is characterized by these attributes, then it is from Allah's bounty upon him and His granting him success. ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾, meaning: vast in bounty, knowing of who deserves that, and of who He withholds it from.

* *

His saying: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed﴾, meaning: the Jews are not your allies; rather, your allegiance returns to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those who establish prayer and give zakah [while bowing in prayer]﴾, meaning: the believers characterized by these attributes, from establishing the prayer, which is the greatest of the pillars of Islam and is for Him alone with no partner, and giving zakah, which is the right of the created beings and assistance to the needy among the weak and the poor.

As for His saying ﴿while bowing﴾, some of them have supposed that this clause is in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to His saying ﴿and give zakah﴾, meaning: during their bowing. If this were so, giving zakah during bowing would be better than other times, because it would be praiseworthy; but this is not the view of any of the scholars we know among the imams of legal opinion. Some of them even mentioned in this regard a report from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib that this verse was revealed concerning him: that a beggar passed by him while he was bowing, and he gave him his ring.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: ar-Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Muradi narrated to us, Ayyub ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from 'Utbah ibn Abi Hakim, concerning His saying: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed﴾, he said: They are the believers and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.[[Narrated by at-Tabari in his tafsir (10/426) through the route of Isma'il ar-Ramli, from Ayyub ibn Suwayd with it.]]

And Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Dukayn Abu Nu'aym al-Ahwal narrated to us, Musa ibn Qays al-Hadrami narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: 'Ali gave charity with his ring while he was bowing, so this was revealed: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed, those who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Harith narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Ghalib ibn 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, I heard Mujahid say concerning His saying: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger﴾ to the end of the verse: It was revealed concerning 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who gave charity while bowing.[[Tafsir at-Tabari (10/426).]]

'Abd ar-Razzaq said: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger﴾ to the end of the verse: It was revealed concerning 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.

'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid is not relied upon as evidence.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Sufyan ath-Thawri, from Abu Sinan, from ad-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib was standing praying, and a beggar passed by while he was bowing, so he gave him his ring, and this was revealed: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger﴾ to the end of the verse.

ad-Dahhak did not meet Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated through the route of Muhammad ibn as-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, who is abandoned (matruk), from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the mosque while the people were praying, some bowing, some prostrating, some standing, some sitting. A needy man was asking, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered and said: "Has anyone given you anything?" He said: Yes. He said: "Who?" He said: "That standing man." He said: "In what state did he give it to you?" He said: While he was bowing. He said: "That is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib." He said: At that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said "Allahu Akbar," and he was saying: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed as allies, indeed the party of Allah will be the victorious﴾.

This is an isnad that is not to be relied upon.

Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, himself, and of Ammar ibn Yasir, and Abu Rafi'. But none of them is authentic at all, due to the weakness of their chains and the obscurity of their narrators. Then he narrated with his chain, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Your only walī (protector, ally) is Allah and His Messenger﴾, that it was revealed concerning the believers, and Ali ibn Abi Talib was the first of them.

Ibn Jarir said: Hannad narrated to us, Abdah narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Abu Ja'far, who said: I asked him about this verse: ﴿Your only walī is Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, those who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing (in ruku')﴾. We said: Who are "those who believe"? He said: "Those who believe!" We said: It has reached us that it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib! He said: Ali is among those who believe.

Asbat narrated from al-Suddi: This verse was revealed concerning all the believers, but Ali ibn Abi Talib was passed by a beggar while he was bowing in the mosque, so he gave him his ring.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah al-Walibi narrated from Ibn Abbas: "Whoever embraces Islam has indeed taken Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as walī." Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

It has already been mentioned in the narrations we have cited that all these verses were revealed concerning Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, when he disavowed the alliance with the Jews and was content with the walāyah (protection and allegiance) of Allah, His Messenger, and the believers. For this reason, after all of this, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as walī, then indeed the party of Allah are the victorious.﴾ As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Mighty. You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred. Those – He has written within their hearts faith and supported them with spirit from Him, and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah – they are the successful.﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21, 22].

So whoever is content with the walāyah of Allah, His Messenger, and the believers is successful in this world and the Hereafter, and victorious in this world and the Hereafter. For this reason, Allah the Exalted said in this noble verse: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as walī, then indeed the party of Allah are the victorious.﴾

God, may He be exalted, says, informing of His great power, that whoever turns away from supporting His religion and establishing His law, Allah will replace him with one who is better than him for it, and stronger in defense, and more upright in the path, as He says: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be the likes of you﴾ [Muhammad: 38]. And He says: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away, O people, and bring others﴾ [an-Nisa': 133]. And He says: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 19-20], meaning, not unattainable or hard. And He says here: ﴿O you who have believed, whoever among you reverts from his religion﴾, meaning, turns back from the truth to falsehood.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It was revealed concerning the rulers from Quraysh. And al-Hasan al-Basri said: It was revealed concerning the people of apostasy (ridda, renunciation of Islam) in the days of Abu Bakr.

﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾. Al-Hasan said: By Allah, they are Abu Bakr and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash say concerning His saying ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾: they are the people of al-Qadisiyyah. And Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Mujahid: they are a people from Saba'.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn al-Ajlah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, he said: They are people from the people of Yemen, then from Kindah, then from as-Sakun.

And my father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa narrated to us, Mu'awiyah, meaning Ibn Hafs, narrated to us, from Abu Ziyad al-Hilfani, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked concerning His saying: ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, and he said: "They are a people from the people of Yemen, then from Kindah, then from as-Sakun, then from Tujib."[[It was also narrated by at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat under no. (3312) (Majma' al-Bahrayn), through the route of Mu'awiyah ibn Hafs, from Abu Ziyad Isma'il ibn Zakariyya, from Muhammad ibn Qays al-Asadi, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir with it. He said: "No one narrated it from Muhammad ibn Qays al-Asadi except Abu Ziyad, and none narrated from him except Mu'awiyah. Abu Hamid reported it alone, adding here Muhammad ibn Qays al-Asadi."

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned it in al-'Ilal (2/95) without mentioning Muhammad ibn Qays in its chain, as it is here in his tafsir, and said: I heard my father say: "This hadith is baseless."

Note: Here it occurs as Abu Ziyad al-Hilfani, while in al-'Ilal it is al-Khilqani, and that is the correct form, "al-Khilqani," as in "al-Istighna' fi al-Mashhurin min Hamalat al-'Ilm bi al-Kuna" by Ibn 'Abd al-Barr (2/1199).]] This is a very strange hadith.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to us, 'Abd as-Samad, meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Warith, narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, I heard 'Iyad narrating from al-Ash'ari, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are the people of this one [pointing to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari's people]." Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah in similar wording.[[Tafsir at-Tabari (10/414). Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it in al-Musannaf (12/123), Ibn Sa'd in at-Tabaqat (4/107), at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/371), and Abu Nu'aym in Tarikh Asbahan (1/59), all through the route of Shu'bah. Al-Haythami said in Majma' az-Zawa'id (7/16): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

* *

His saying ﴿humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾: these are the attributes of the perfect believers, that each of them is humble toward his brother and ally, and firm against his opponent and enemy, as He says: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. And in the description of the Prophet (ﷺ) it is said that he was "the smiling, the fighter": he smiled toward his allies and fought against his enemies.

* *

His saying ﴿who strive in the way of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic﴾: meaning, nothing turns them away from what they are engaged in of obedience to Allah, fighting His enemies, establishing the prescribed punishments, and enjoining good and forbidding evil. No one turns them away from that, no one prevents them from it, and the blame of a blamer or the reproach of a reproacher does not affect them.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Sallam Abu al-Mundhir narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Wasi', from 'Abdullah ibn as-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: My beloved (ﷺ) commanded me with seven things: He commanded me to love the poor and to be near them; he commanded me to look to someone below me and not to look to someone above me; he commanded me to maintain ties of kinship even if they turn away; he commanded me not to ask anyone for anything; he commanded me to say the truth even if it is bitter; he commanded me not to fear the blame of a blamer in the matter of Allah; and he commanded me to frequently say: "There is no power and no strength except with Allah," for they are from a treasure beneath the Throne.[[al-Musnad (5/159).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, from Abu al-Muthanna, that Abu Dharr said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took five pledges from me, bound me by seven, and made Allah a witness over me by nine: that I would not fear the blame of a blamer in the matter of Allah. Abu Dharr said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me and said: "Would you like to pledge allegiance to me, and for you is Paradise?" I said: Yes. He said: And I extended my hands, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said, while stipulating: "On condition that you do not ask people for anything?" I said: Yes. He said: "Nor your whip, even if it falls from you, until you descend to it and pick it up."[[al-Musnad (5/172).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Mu'alla al-Qurdusi, from al-Hasan, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [in another version: "from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet"], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware! Let not fear of people prevent any one of you from speaking the truth when he sees it or witnesses it, for it does not bring near a term nor distance a provision [in another version: "it does not distance from a term nor bring near a provision"] to say the truth or to remind of something great." Ahmad alone narrated it.[[al-Musnad (3/50).]]

Ahmad said: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from Zubayd, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [in another version: "from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet"], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let none of you belittle himself by seeing a matter in which Allah has a word, and then not speaking about it. He will be asked on the Day of Resurrection: 'What prevented you from saying such and such about Me?' He will say: 'Fear of people.' He will be told: 'It was I who had more right that you should fear Me.'"

Ibn Majah narrated it through the hadith of al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah with it.[[al-Musnad (3/73) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4008). Al-Busiri said in az-Zawa'id (3/242): "This chain is sahih."]] Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated, through the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi Tuwalah [in another version: "'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi Tuwalah"], from Nahar ibn 'Abdullah al-'Abdi al-Madani, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [in another version: "from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet"], from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed Allah will question the servant on the Day of Resurrection, until He asks him, saying: 'O My servant, you saw an evil and did not forbid it?' When Allah makes the servant recall his argument, he will say: 'O Lord, I trusted in You and feared the people.'"[[al-Musnad (3/77) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4017). Al-Busiri said in az-Zawa'id (3/244): "This chain is sahih."]]

And it is established in the Sahih: "It is not befitting for a believer to humiliate himself." They said: "And how does he humiliate himself, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "He takes on a trial that he cannot bear."[[I did not find it in my search of the two Sahihs, but perhaps I will check it later. It was narrated by at-Tirmidhi in as-Sunan no. (2254) and Ibn Majah in as-Sunan no. (4016), through the route of 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from al-Hasan, from Jundub, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him. At-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan gharib hadith." In its chain is 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who is weak.]]

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated through the route of Muhammad ibn as-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, who is abandoned (matruk), from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the mosque while the people were praying, some bowing, some prostrating, some standing, some sitting. Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, himself, and of Ammar ibn Yasir, and Abu Rafi'. Note: Here it occurs as Abu Ziyad al-Hilfani, while in al-'Ilal it is al-Khilqani, and that is the correct form, "al-Khilqani," as in "al-Istighna' fi al-Mashhurin min Hamalat al-'Ilm bi al-Kuna" by Ibn 'Abd al-Barr (2/1199).]] This is a very strange hadith.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to us, 'Abd as-Samad, meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Warith, narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, I heard 'Iyad narrating from al-Ash'ari, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are the people of this one [pointing to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari's people]." Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah in similar wording.[[Tafsir at-Tabari (10/414). Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it in al-Musannaf (12/123), Ibn Sa'd in at-Tabaqat (4/107), at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/371), and Abu Nu'aym in Tarikh Asbahan (1/59), all through the route of Shu'bah. Al-Haythami said in Majma' az-Zawa'id (7/16): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

* *

His saying ﴿humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾: these are the attributes of the perfect believers, that each of them is humble toward his brother and ally, and firm against his opponent and enemy, as He says: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. And in the description of the Prophet (ﷺ) it is said that he was "the smiling, the fighter": he smiled toward his allies and fought against his enemies.

* *

His saying ﴿who strive in the way of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic﴾: meaning, nothing turns them away from what they are engaged in of obedience to Allah, fighting His enemies, establishing the prescribed punishments, and enjoining good and forbidding evil. No one turns them away from that, no one prevents them from it, and the blame of a blamer or the reproach of a reproacher does not affect them.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Sallam Abu al-Mundhir narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Wasi', from 'Abdullah ibn as-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: My beloved (ﷺ) commanded me with seven things: He commanded me to love the poor and to be near them; he commanded me to look to someone below me and not to look to someone above me; he commanded me to maintain ties of kinship even if they turn away; he commanded me not to ask anyone for anything; he commanded me to say the truth even if it is bitter; he commanded me not to fear the blame of a blamer in the matter of Allah; and he commanded me to frequently say: "There is no power and no strength except with Allah," for they are from a treasure beneath the Throne.[[al-Musnad (5/159).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, from Abu al-Muthanna, that Abu Dharr said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took five pledges from me, bound me by seven, and made Allah a witness over me by nine: that I would not fear the blame of a blamer in the matter of Allah. Abu Dharr said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me and said: "Would you like to pledge allegiance to me, and for you is Paradise?" I said: Yes. He said: And I extended my hands, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said, while stipulating: "On condition that you do not ask people for anything?" I said: Yes. He said: "Nor your whip, even if it falls from you, until you descend to it and pick it up."[[al-Musnad (5/172).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Mu'alla al-Qurdusi, from al-Hasan, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [in another version: "from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet"], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware! Let not fear of people prevent any one of you from speaking the truth when he sees it or witnesses it, for it does not bring near a term nor distance a provision [in another version: "it does not distance from a term nor bring near a provision"] to say the truth or to remind of something great." Ahmad alone narrated it.[[al-Musnad (3/50).]]

Ahmad said: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from Zubayd, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [in another version: "from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet"], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let none of you belittle himself by seeing a matter in which Allah has a word, and then not speaking about it. He will be asked on the Day of Resurrection: 'What prevented you from saying such and such about Me?' He will say: 'Fear of people.' He will be told: 'It was I who had more right that you should fear Me.'"

Ibn Majah narrated it through the hadith of al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah with it.[[al-Musnad (3/73) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4008). Al-Busiri said in az-Zawa'id (3/242): "This chain is sahih."]] Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated, through the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi Tuwalah [in another version: "'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi Tuwalah"], from Nahar ibn 'Abdullah al-'Abdi al-Madani, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [in another version: "from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet"], from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed Allah will question the servant on the Day of Resurrection, until He asks him, saying: 'O My servant, you saw an evil and did not forbid it?' When Allah makes the servant recall his argument, he will say: 'O Lord, I trusted in You and feared the people.'"[[al-Musnad (3/77) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4017). Al-Busiri said in az-Zawa'id (3/244): "This chain is sahih."]]

And it is established in the Sahih: "It is not befitting for a believer to humiliate himself." They said: "And how does he humiliate himself, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "He takes on a trial that he cannot bear."[[I did not find it in my search of the two Sahihs, but perhaps I will check it later. It was narrated by at-Tirmidhi in as-Sunan no. (2254) and Ibn Majah in as-Sunan no. (4016), through the route of 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from al-Hasan, from Jundub, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him. At-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan gharib hadith." In its chain is 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who is weak.]]

﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾, meaning: whoever is characterized by these attributes, then it is from Allah's bounty upon him and His granting him success. ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾, meaning: vast in bounty, knowing of who deserves that, and of who He withholds it from.

* *

His saying: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed﴾, meaning: the Jews are not your allies; rather, your allegiance returns to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those who establish prayer and give zakah [while bowing in prayer]﴾, meaning: the believers characterized by these attributes, from establishing the prayer, which is the greatest of the pillars of Islam and is for Him alone with no partner, and giving zakah, which is the right of the created beings and assistance to the needy among the weak and the poor.

As for His saying ﴿while bowing﴾, some of them have supposed that this clause is in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to His saying ﴿and give zakah﴾, meaning: during their bowing. If this were so, giving zakah during bowing would be better than other times, because it would be praiseworthy; but this is not the view of any of the scholars we know among the imams of legal opinion. Some of them even mentioned in this regard a report from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib that this verse was revealed concerning him: that a beggar passed by him while he was bowing, and he gave him his ring.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: ar-Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Muradi narrated to us, Ayyub ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from 'Utbah ibn Abi Hakim, concerning His saying: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed﴾, he said: They are the believers and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.[[Narrated by at-Tabari in his tafsir (10/426) through the route of Isma'il ar-Ramli, from Ayyub ibn Suwayd with it.]]

And Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Dukayn Abu Nu'aym al-Ahwal narrated to us, Musa ibn Qays al-Hadrami narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: 'Ali gave charity with his ring while he was bowing, so this was revealed: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed, those who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Harith narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Ghalib ibn 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, I heard Mujahid say concerning His saying: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger﴾ to the end of the verse: It was revealed concerning 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who gave charity while bowing.[[Tafsir at-Tabari (10/426).]]

'Abd ar-Razzaq said: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger﴾ to the end of the verse: It was revealed concerning 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.

'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid is not relied upon as evidence.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Sufyan ath-Thawri, from Abu Sinan, from ad-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib was standing praying, and a beggar passed by while he was bowing, so he gave him his ring, and this was revealed: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger﴾ to the end of the verse.

ad-Dahhak did not meet Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated through the route of Muhammad ibn as-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, who is abandoned (matruk), from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the mosque while the people were praying, some bowing, some prostrating, some standing, some sitting. A needy man was asking, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered and said: "Has anyone given you anything?" He said: Yes. He said: "Who?" He said: "That standing man." He said: "In what state did he give it to you?" He said: While he was bowing. He said: "That is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib." He said: At that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said "Allahu Akbar," and he was saying: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed as allies, indeed the party of Allah will be the victorious﴾.

This is an isnad that is not to be relied upon.

Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, himself, and of Ammar ibn Yasir, and Abu Rafi'. But none of them is authentic at all, due to the weakness of their chains and the obscurity of their narrators. Then he narrated with his chain, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Your only walī (protector, ally) is Allah and His Messenger﴾, that it was revealed concerning the believers, and Ali ibn Abi Talib was the first of them.

Ibn Jarir said: Hannad narrated to us, Abdah narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Abu Ja'far, who said: I asked him about this verse: ﴿Your only walī is Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, those who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing (in ruku')﴾. We said: Who are "those who believe"? He said: "Those who believe!" We said: It has reached us that it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib! He said: Ali is among those who believe.

Asbat narrated from al-Suddi: This verse was revealed concerning all the believers, but Ali ibn Abi Talib was passed by a beggar while he was bowing in the mosque, so he gave him his ring.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah al-Walibi narrated from Ibn Abbas: "Whoever embraces Islam has indeed taken Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as walī." Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

It has already been mentioned in the narrations we have cited that all these verses were revealed concerning Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, when he disavowed the alliance with the Jews and was content with the walāyah (protection and allegiance) of Allah, His Messenger, and the believers. For this reason, after all of this, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as walī, then indeed the party of Allah are the victorious.﴾ As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Mighty. You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred. Those – He has written within their hearts faith and supported them with spirit from Him, and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah – they are the successful.﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21, 22].

So whoever is content with the walāyah of Allah, His Messenger, and the believers is successful in this world and the Hereafter, and victorious in this world and the Hereafter. For this reason, Allah the Exalted said in this noble verse: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as walī, then indeed the party of Allah are the victorious.﴾

This is a mockery of those who take the best of deeds, the pure and firm laws of Islam that contain every worldly and otherworldly good, as ﴿a mockery and a game﴾. They ridicule them, and ﴿a game﴾ means they consider them a kind of play, in their corrupt view and their cold thinking, as the poet said [[It is Abu al-Tayyib al-Mutanabbi, as in the margin of the Dar al-Sha'b edition.]]:

*How many a critic faults a sound saying,*
*Its flaw lying in a sick understanding.*

* *

As for His saying: ﴿from those who were given the Scripture before you, and the disbelievers﴾, the "min" here is for specifying the category, as in His saying: ﴿so avoid the abomination of idols﴾ [al-Hajj 22:30]. Some readers recited ﴿and the disbelievers﴾ in the genitive (*al-khafd*) as a conjunction, while others recited it in the accusative (*al-nasb*), as an object of the verb. The meaning is: ﴿Do not take as allies those who took your religion as a mockery and a game from those who were given the Scripture before you﴾, and [do not take] the disbelievers either; that is, do not take these or those as allies.

The "disbelievers" here means the polytheists, and this is also what appears in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, as narrated by Ibn Jarir: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies those who took your religion as a mockery and a game from those who were given the Scripture before you, and the disbelievers﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And fear Allah, if you are believers﴾, that is: fear Allah by taking these enemies of yours and of your religion as allies, ﴿if you are believers﴾ in the law of Allah, which they took as a mockery and a game. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The believers should not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah, unless you fear them as a precaution. And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the final return﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:28].

* *

As for His saying [the Exalted] [[Addition from A.]]: ﴿And when you call to the prayer, they take it as a mockery and a game﴾, that is: likewise, when you make the call to prayer, summoning to the prayer which is the best of deeds for one who has understanding and knowledge among the people of reason, ﴿they take it also as a mockery and a game. That is because they are a people who do not understand﴾ the meanings of the worship of Allah and His laws. These are the attributes of the followers of Satan, who, "when he hears the adhan, turns his back and breaks wind (*hussas*, meaning a fart), so that he does not hear the call. When the adhan is finished, he comes back; when the iqamah for the prayer is called, he turns back again; and when the iqamah is finished, he comes back and whispers between a man and his heart, saying: 'Remember such and such, remember such and such,' things he did not remember, until the man does not know how much he has prayed. When any of you experiences that, let him perform two prostrations before the salam." Agreed upon (*muttafaq 'alayh*).

Al-Zuhri said: Allah has mentioned the adhan in His Book, saying: ﴿And when you call to the prayer, they take it as a mockery and a game. That is because they are a people who do not understand﴾. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Asbat narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And when you call to the prayer, they take it as a mockery and a game﴾, that he said: There was a Christian man in Medina who, whenever he heard the caller proclaim, "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," would say: "Burn the liar!" One night a servant girl came in with fire while he was asleep and his family was asleep, and a spark fell and set the house on fire, and he and his family were burned. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar mentioned in the *Sirah* that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the Ka'bah on the day of the Conquest, with Bilal, and he commanded him to make the adhan. Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, 'Attab ibn Usayd and al-Harith ibn Hisham were sitting in the courtyard of the Ka'bah. 'Attab ibn Usayd said: "Allah has honored Usayd by not letting him hear this, so that he would not hear from it what would anger him." Al-Harith ibn Hisham said: "By Allah, if I knew that he was truthful, I would follow him." Abu Sufyan said: "I will say nothing; if I spoke, these pebbles would inform on me." The Prophet ﷺ then came out to them and said: "I know what you said." Then he related it to them. Al-Harith and 'Attab said: "We bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah. No one was present with us who could have informed you, so we say that you were informed by Allah." [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/413).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Ibn Juraij narrated to us, Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Mahdhurah informed us, that Abdullah ibn Muhayriz informed him, and he was an orphan in the care of Abu Mahdhurah, that he said: I said to Abu Mahdhurah: "O uncle, I am leaving for Syria, and I fear I will be asked about your adhan." He informed me that Abu Mahdhurah said to him: "Yes. I went out with a group of men, and we were on part of the road to Hunayn, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was returning from Hunayn. We met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on part of the road, and the muezzin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the call to prayer in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We heard the voice of the muezzin while we were reclining, so we shouted, imitating him and mocking him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard the voice, so he sent for us, and we stood before him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Which of you is the one whose voice I heard raised?' All the people pointed to me, and they were truthful. So he sent them all away and kept me back, and said: 'Stand and make the call to prayer.' I stood, and there was nothing more hateful to me than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor than what he commanded me. I stood before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself taught me the adhan, saying: 'Say: Allah is most great, Allah is most great. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' Then he said to me: 'Return and raise your voice.' Then he said: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, come to the prayer, come to the prayer, come to success, come to success, Allah is most great, Allah is most great, there is no god but Allah.'" Then he called me when I had finished the adhan, and gave me a purse containing some silver. Then he placed his hand on the forelock of Abu Mahdhurah, and passed it over his face, then over his chest, then over his liver, until the hand of the Messenger of Allah reached the navel of Abu Mahdhurah. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "May Allah bless you and bless you." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, command me to make the adhan in Mecca." He said: "I have indeed commanded you to do so." All the aversion that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had felt toward me disappeared, and all of it turned into love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I then came to 'Attab ibn Usayd, the governor of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Mecca, and I made the adhan with him for the prayer by the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Those among my family whom I met, of those who had known Abu Mahdhurah, related this to me in the same way that Abdullah ibn Muhayriz had related it to me.

Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it. Muslim included it in his *Sahih*, and the authors of the four *Sunan* collections narrated it through another chain from Abdullah ibn Muhayriz, from Abu Mahdhurah [[Al-Musnad (3/408); Sahih Muslim no. (379); Sunan Abi Dawud (502); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (191); Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/4); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (708).]]. His name is Samurah ibn Mi'yar ibn Lawdhan. He was one of the four muezzins of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was the muezzin of the people of Mecca, and his days were long. May Allah be pleased with him and please him.

Then he said: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, come to the prayer, come to the prayer, come to success, come to success, Allah is most great, Allah is most great, there is no god but Allah.'" Then he called me when I had finished the adhan, and gave me a purse containing some silver. Then he placed his hand on the forelock of Abu Mahdhurah, and passed it over his face, then over his chest, then over his liver, until the hand of the Messenger of Allah reached the navel of Abu Mahdhurah. All the aversion that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had felt toward me disappeared, and all of it turned into love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I then came to 'Attab ibn Usayd, the governor of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Mecca, and I made the adhan with him for the prayer by the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Those among my family whom I met, of those who had known Abu Mahdhurah, related this to me in the same way that Abdullah ibn Muhayriz had related it to me.

Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it. Muslim included it in his *Sahih*, and the authors of the four *Sunan* collections narrated it through another chain from Abdullah ibn Muhayriz, from Abu Mahdhurah [[Al-Musnad (3/408); Sahih Muslim no. (379); Sunan Abi Dawud (502); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (191); Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/4); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (708).]]. His name is Samurah ibn Mi'yar ibn Lawdhan. He was one of the four muezzins of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was the muezzin of the people of Mecca, and his days were long. May Allah be pleased with him and please him.

Therefore He said: ﴿and they left with it﴾, singling them out from others.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah knows best what they used to conceal.﴾ That is: Allah is aware of their inner secrets and what their hearts harbor, even if they show to His creation the opposite of that and adorn themselves with what is not in them. Indeed the Knower of the unseen and the seen knows them better than they know themselves, and He will recompense them for that with the most complete recompense.

* *

His saying: ﴿And you see many of them hastening toward sin and aggression and consuming unlawful gain (al-suht).﴾ That is: they race to that by engaging in sins and prohibitions and transgressing against people, and consuming their wealth falsely. ﴿Evil indeed is what they used to do.﴾ That is: evil was their deed, and evil was their transgression.

His saying: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from uttering sin and consuming unlawful gain? Evil indeed is what they used to produce.﴾ That is: why did the rabbis and scholars not forbid them from engaging in that? The rabbaniyyun are the learned workers who hold authority over them, and the ahbar are the scholars only.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿Evil indeed is what they used to produce﴾, that he meant the rabbaniyyun: "evil indeed is what they used to produce," that is, in their abandonment of that.

Then they left while it remained lodged within them; they did not benefit from the knowledge they heard from you, and neither admonitions nor warnings had any effect on them. Therefore He said: ﴿and they left with it﴾, singling them out from others.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah knows best what they used to conceal.﴾ That is: Allah is aware of their inner secrets and what their hearts harbor, even if they show to His creation the opposite of that and adorn themselves with what is not in them. Indeed the Knower of the unseen and the seen knows them better than they know themselves, and He will recompense them for that with the most complete recompense.

* *

His saying: ﴿And you see many of them hastening toward sin and aggression and consuming unlawful gain (al-suht).﴾ That is: they race to that by engaging in sins and prohibitions and transgressing against people, and consuming their wealth falsely. ﴿Evil indeed is what they used to do.﴾ That is: evil was their deed, and evil was their transgression.

His saying: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from uttering sin and consuming unlawful gain? Evil indeed is what they used to produce.﴾ That is: why did the rabbis and scholars not forbid them from engaging in that? The rabbaniyyun are the learned workers who hold authority over them, and the ahbar are the scholars only.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿Evil indeed is what they used to produce﴾, that he meant the rabbaniyyun: "evil indeed is what they used to produce," that is, in their abandonment of that.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: He said this to these when they did not forbid, and to those when they knew. He said: and that is the pillars. He said: "ya'malun" and "yasna'un" are the same. Ibn Abi Hatim reported it.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, Qays narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from Khalid ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: There is no verse in the Qur'an more severe in rebuke than this verse: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from uttering sin and consuming unlawful gain? Evil indeed is what they used to produce.﴾ He said: thus he read it.

Similarly al-Dahhak said: There is no verse in the Qur'an more frightening to me than it: "We do not forbid." Reported by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib mentioned it, narrating to us Abu Dawud, narrating to us Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Wadday', narrating to us Thabit ibn Sa'id al-Hamadhani, who said: I met him in al-Rayy and he narrated from Yahya ibn Ya'mar, who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib gave a sermon, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: O people, those before you were destroyed only by their committing sins, and the rabbis and scholars did not forbid them. When they persisted in sins and the rabbis and scholars did not forbid them, punishments seized them. So enjoin the good and forbid the evil before there descends upon you what descended upon them, and know that enjoining good and forbidding evil does not cut off provision nor bring nearer a term.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Shurayk informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no people among whom there is someone who commits sins while they are stronger and more able to prevent him, and they do not change it, except that Allah will afflict them with punishment from Him."

Ahmad alone narrated it through this route. [Musnad (4/363); al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/331) through Yazid ibn Harun.]

Abu Dawud also narrated it from Musaddad, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from Jarir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "There is no man among a people who commits sins among them, while they are able to change it, yet they do not change it, except that Allah will afflict them with punishment before they die." [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4339; al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/332) through Musaddad, from Abu al-Ahwas.]

Ibn Majah also narrated it from 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Waki', from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Jarir, from his father, with the same wording. [Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4009.]

The Hafiz al-Mizzi said: Likewise Shu'bah narrated it from Ishaq, with the same. [Tuhfat al-Ashraf (2/426); al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/331), who said: "Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us," and he mentioned it.]

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 5, verses 64–66 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, informs about the Jews, upon whom be the successive curses of Allah until the Day of Resurrection [in A: "al-tabi'ah"], that they described Allah, may He be exalted far above what they say, as miserly. They also described Him as poor while they themselves are rich, and they expressed this miserliness by their saying: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained up﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Tihrani narrated to us, Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Chained up﴾, meaning: miserly.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding his statement: ﴿And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained up"﴾. He said: They do not mean by this that the hand of Allah is bound [in R: "spending"], but they say: "A miser who keeps what he has." Allah is exalted far above what they say.

Similarly it was reported from 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Mujahid and al-Dahhak. [Ibn 'Abbas] recited: ﴿And do not make your hand chained up to your neck, nor extend it fully outstretched, lest you sit reproached and destitute﴾ [al-Isra' 29]. Meaning: He forbids miserliness and extravagance (tabdhir), which is excessive spending in other than its proper place. He expressed miserliness by His saying: ﴿Do not make your hand chained up to your neck﴾.

This is what those Jews, upon whom be the curses of Allah, intended. 'Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning Finhas the Jew, upon him be the curse of Allah. It has already been mentioned that he is the one who said: ﴿Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich﴾ [Al 'Imran 181], and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, struck him.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Sa'id or 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man from the Jews, called Shas [in A: "al-Nabbas"] ibn Qays, said: "Indeed your Lord is miserly, He does not spend." So Allah revealed: ﴿And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained up." Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they said. Rather, both His hands are outstretched; He spends as He wills﴾.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, refuted what they said and repaid them for what they fabricated, invented and falsified. He said: ﴿Their hands are chained up and they are cursed for what they said﴾. Thus it happened to them, for among them is a great deal of miserliness, envy, cowardice and humiliation, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Or do they have a share in the kingdom? Then they would not give people even a speck. Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? We had already given the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom and given them a great kingdom. Among them were those who believed in it and among them were those who averted from it, and Hell is sufficient as a blazing fire﴾ [al-Nisa' 53–55]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Humiliation has been struck upon them wherever they are found, except with a rope from Allah and a rope from the people﴾ [Al 'Imran 112], and the rest of the verse.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Rather, both His hands are outstretched; He spends as He wills﴾. That is: rather, He is abundant in bounty, generous in giving, the One for whom are the treasuries of everything, and whatever blessing is in His creation is from Him alone, with no partner. He created for us everything we need, in our night and our day, in our residence and our travel, and in all our conditions, as He said: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him. And if you tried to count the favours of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is a wrongdoer and ungrateful﴾ [Ibrahim 34], and the rest of the verse. The verses on this are many. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us," who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the right hand of Allah is full; spending does not diminish it, flowing night and day. Have you considered what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? Yet it has not diminished what is in His right hand." And he said: "His Throne is upon the water, and in His other hand is the qabd (grasping), He raises and lowers." He said: Allah, the Exalted, said: "Spend, I will spend upon you." [Both] compiled it in the Sahihayn: al-Bukhari in "al-Tawhid" from 'Ali ibn al-Madini, and Muslim in it from Muhammad ibn Rafi', and both of them from 'Abd al-Razzaq, with this chain. [Al-Musnad 2/313; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 7419; Sahih Muslim no. 993.]

* *

His statement: ﴿But surely much of them, the revelation that has been sent down to you from your Lord, will increase them in transgression and disbelief﴾. That is: what Allah has brought you, O Muhammad, of blessing becomes a calamity for your enemies among the Jews and their likes. Just as the believers increase in faith, righteous deeds and beneficial knowledge through it, the disbelievers who envy you and your community increase in ﴿transgression﴾, which is exaggeration and exceeding the limit in matters, and ﴿disbelief﴾, that is, denial.

As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "It is, for those who believe, a guidance and a healing. But as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a distant place"﴾ [Fussilat 44]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and mercy for the believers, but it increases the wrongdoers in nothing but loss﴾ [al-Isra' 82].

* *

His statement: ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾. That is: their hearts do not unite; rather, enmity is constantly present between their factions, one against another, because they do not unite upon truth, and they have opposed you and denied you.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said regarding ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred﴾: "It is disputes and argumentation over the religion." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

His statement: ﴿Every time they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it﴾. That is: every time they tie up means by which they plot against you, and every time they arrange affairs by which they wage war against you, Allah nullifies them and turns their plot back upon them, and their evil scheming encompasses them.

﴿And they strive upon the earth in corruption, and Allah does not love the corrupters﴾. That is: it is their nature that they constantly strive in corruption on the earth, and Allah does not love one who has this description.

Then Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, said: ﴿And if the People of the Book had believed and been mindful [of Allah]﴾. That is: if they had believed in Allah and His Messenger, and had been mindful of the prohibited things and sins which they engaged in, ﴿We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to gardens of pleasure﴾. That is: We would have removed from them what they feared, and granted them what they sought.

﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and others said: this means the Qur'an. ﴿They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾. That is: because they would have acted upon what is in the books in their hands from the prophets, as it is, without distortion, alteration or change, that would have led them to follow the truth and act upon what Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with; for their books clearly testify to his truth and command following him, definitely and without doubt.

* *

His statement: ﴿They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ means by this the abundance of provision descending upon them from the sky and growing for them from the earth.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿They would have eaten from above them﴾ means: He would have sent the sky upon them in abundant rain, ﴿and from beneath their feet﴾ means: He would bring forth from the earth its blessings.

Likewise Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and al-Suddi said, as Allah said: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful, We would have opened to them blessings from the heaven and the earth, but they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn﴾ [al-A'raf 96]. And He said: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea by what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste part of what they have done, so that they might return﴾ [al-Rum 41].

Some of them said: its meaning, ﴿They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾, is: without toil, hardship, difficulty or exertion.

Ibn Jarir said: Some of them said its meaning is: they would have been in good, as one says: "He is in good from his horn to his foot." Then this statement was rejected for contradicting the statements of the early pious predecessors (al-salaf). [The speaker of this statement is al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (1/315), as cited from the margin of Tafsir al-Tabari, which al-Tabari mentioned in his tafsir (10/464).]

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned, at His statement: ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel﴾, a hadith from 'Alqamah, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Knowledge is about to be lifted." Ziyad ibn Labid said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can knowledge be lifted when we have recited the Qur'an and taught it to our sons?" He said: "May your mother be bereaved of you, O son of Labid! Indeed I used to see you as one of the most learned people of Madinah. Are not the Torah and the Gospel in the hands of the Jews and Christians? What did they gain from them when they abandoned the command of Allah?" Then he recited: ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this hadith with its initial chain suspended (mu'allaq), and its end is mursal. [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (18/43), and al-Bazzar in his Musnad no. 232 (Kashf al-Astar), from another route: from Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ablah, from al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from 'Awf ibn Malik, with similar wording.] But Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated it connected (mawsul), saying: Waki' narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ziyad ibn Labid, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned something and said: "And that is at the time of the disappearance of knowledge." He said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can knowledge disappear when we recite the Qur'an and teach it to our sons, and our sons teach it to their sons until the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "May your mother be bereaved of you, O son of Umm Labid! Indeed I used to see you as one of the most learned men in Madinah. Are not these Jews and Christians reading the Torah and the Gospel, yet they benefit nothing from what is in them?"

Likewise Ibn Majah narrated it, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Waki', with its chain, similarly. [Al-Musnad (4/160); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4048. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/253): "Its narrators are trustworthy, except that it is disconnected (munqati'). Al-Bukhari said in al-Tarikh al-Saghir: 'Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd did not hear from Ziyad ibn Labid.'"] This is a sound chain.

* *

His statement: ﴿Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—evil is what they do﴾. It is like His statement: ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it establish justice﴾ [al-A'raf 159], and like His statement about the followers of Jesus: ﴿So We gave those who believed among them their reward, but many of them are defiant﴾ [al-Hadid 27]. He made the highest of their ranks moderation (iqtisad), which is the middle rank of this community. Above that is the rank of those foremost in good deeds (al-sabiqun), as in His statement: ﴿Then We gave the Book to those We chose from Our servants; and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one moderate, and among them is one foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah. That is the great bounty: gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾, and the rest of the verse [Fatir 32–33]. The correct view is that all three categories of this community will enter Paradise.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Dabbi narrated to us, Asim ibn Ali narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid ibn Talha, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he said: "The nation of Musa divided into seventy-one sects (milla), seventy of them in the Fire and one in Paradise, and the nation of Isa divided into seventy-two sects, one of them in Paradise and seventy-one of them in the Fire, and my nation will surpass both groups together. One in Paradise and seventy-two in the Fire." They said: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The main body (al-jama'at), the main body."

Ya'qub ibn Yazid said: Whenever Ali ibn Abi Talib (raḍiyallahu ʿanhu) narrated this hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would recite in connection with it a Qur'an verse: ﴿And if the People of the Scripture had believed and feared Allah, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Pleasure﴾ up to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Among them is a moderate nation, but many of them - evil is what they do﴾. And he also recited: ﴿And among those whom We created is a nation who guide by truth and by it establish justice﴾ [al-A'raf: 181], meaning: the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ).

[Abu Ya'la narrated it in his Musnad (6/340) by way of Abu Ma'shar, from Ya'qub ibn Zayd, with the same wording from a long hadith. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/257): "In its chain is Abu Ma'shar Najih, who is weak."]

This is a very strange (gharib) hadith from this route and with this wording. The hadith about the nations dividing into some seventy sects has been related through many routes, and we have mentioned it in another place. And to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Then this statement was rejected for contradicting the statements of the early pious predecessors (al-salaf). [The speaker of this statement is al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (1/315), as cited from the margin of Tafsir al-Tabari, which al-Tabari mentioned in his tafsir (10/464).]

Ziyad ibn Labid said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can knowledge be lifted when we have recited the Qur'an and taught it to our sons?" He said: "May your mother be bereaved of you, O son of Labid! Indeed I used to see you as one of the most learned people of Madinah. Are not the Torah and the Gospel in the hands of the Jews and Christians? What did they gain from them when they abandoned the command of Allah?" Then he recited: ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel﴾.

* *

His statement: ﴿Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—evil is what they do﴾. He made the highest of their ranks moderation (iqtisad), which is the middle rank of this community. Above that is the rank of those foremost in good deeds (al-sabiqun), as in His statement: ﴿Then We gave the Book to those We chose from Our servants; and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one moderate, and among them is one foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah. That is the great bounty: gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾, and the rest of the verse [Fatir 32–33]. The correct view is that all three categories of this community will enter Paradise.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Dabbi narrated to us, Asim ibn Ali narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid ibn Talha, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he said: "The nation of Musa divided into seventy-one sects (milla), seventy of them in the Fire and one in Paradise, and the nation of Isa divided into seventy-two sects, one of them in Paradise and seventy-one of them in the Fire, and my nation will surpass both groups together. [Abu Ya'la narrated it in his Musnad (6/340) by way of Abu Ma'shar, from Ya'qub ibn Zayd, with the same wording from a long hadith. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/257): "In its chain is Abu Ma'shar Najih, who is weak."]
