Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 5, verses 64–66 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, informs about the Jews, upon whom be the successive curses of Allah until the Day of Resurrection [in A: "al-tabi'ah"], that they described Allah, may He be exalted far above what they say, as miserly. They also described Him as poor while they themselves are rich, and they expressed this miserliness by their saying: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained up﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Tihrani narrated to us, Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Chained up﴾, meaning: miserly.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding his statement: ﴿And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained up"﴾. He said: They do not mean by this that the hand of Allah is bound [in R: "spending"], but they say: "A miser who keeps what he has." Allah is exalted far above what they say.

Similarly it was reported from 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Mujahid and al-Dahhak. [Ibn 'Abbas] recited: ﴿And do not make your hand chained up to your neck, nor extend it fully outstretched, lest you sit reproached and destitute﴾ [al-Isra' 29]. Meaning: He forbids miserliness and extravagance (tabdhir), which is excessive spending in other than its proper place. He expressed miserliness by His saying: ﴿Do not make your hand chained up to your neck﴾.

This is what those Jews, upon whom be the curses of Allah, intended. 'Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning Finhas the Jew, upon him be the curse of Allah. It has already been mentioned that he is the one who said: ﴿Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich﴾ [Al 'Imran 181], and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, struck him.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Sa'id or 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man from the Jews, called Shas [in A: "al-Nabbas"] ibn Qays, said: "Indeed your Lord is miserly, He does not spend." So Allah revealed: ﴿And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained up." Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they said. Rather, both His hands are outstretched; He spends as He wills﴾.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, refuted what they said and repaid them for what they fabricated, invented and falsified. He said: ﴿Their hands are chained up and they are cursed for what they said﴾. Thus it happened to them, for among them is a great deal of miserliness, envy, cowardice and humiliation, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Or do they have a share in the kingdom? Then they would not give people even a speck. Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? We had already given the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom and given them a great kingdom. Among them were those who believed in it and among them were those who averted from it, and Hell is sufficient as a blazing fire﴾ [al-Nisa' 53–55]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Humiliation has been struck upon them wherever they are found, except with a rope from Allah and a rope from the people﴾ [Al 'Imran 112], and the rest of the verse.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Rather, both His hands are outstretched; He spends as He wills﴾. That is: rather, He is abundant in bounty, generous in giving, the One for whom are the treasuries of everything, and whatever blessing is in His creation is from Him alone, with no partner. He created for us everything we need, in our night and our day, in our residence and our travel, and in all our conditions, as He said: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him. And if you tried to count the favours of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is a wrongdoer and ungrateful﴾ [Ibrahim 34], and the rest of the verse. The verses on this are many. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us," who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the right hand of Allah is full; spending does not diminish it, flowing night and day. Have you considered what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? Yet it has not diminished what is in His right hand." And he said: "His Throne is upon the water, and in His other hand is the qabd (grasping), He raises and lowers." He said: Allah, the Exalted, said: "Spend, I will spend upon you." [Both] compiled it in the Sahihayn: al-Bukhari in "al-Tawhid" from 'Ali ibn al-Madini, and Muslim in it from Muhammad ibn Rafi', and both of them from 'Abd al-Razzaq, with this chain. [Al-Musnad 2/313; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 7419; Sahih Muslim no. 993.]

* *

His statement: ﴿But surely much of them, the revelation that has been sent down to you from your Lord, will increase them in transgression and disbelief﴾. That is: what Allah has brought you, O Muhammad, of blessing becomes a calamity for your enemies among the Jews and their likes. Just as the believers increase in faith, righteous deeds and beneficial knowledge through it, the disbelievers who envy you and your community increase in ﴿transgression﴾, which is exaggeration and exceeding the limit in matters, and ﴿disbelief﴾, that is, denial.

As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "It is, for those who believe, a guidance and a healing. But as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a distant place"﴾ [Fussilat 44]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and mercy for the believers, but it increases the wrongdoers in nothing but loss﴾ [al-Isra' 82].

* *

His statement: ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾. That is: their hearts do not unite; rather, enmity is constantly present between their factions, one against another, because they do not unite upon truth, and they have opposed you and denied you.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said regarding ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred﴾: "It is disputes and argumentation over the religion." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

His statement: ﴿Every time they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it﴾. That is: every time they tie up means by which they plot against you, and every time they arrange affairs by which they wage war against you, Allah nullifies them and turns their plot back upon them, and their evil scheming encompasses them.

﴿And they strive upon the earth in corruption, and Allah does not love the corrupters﴾. That is: it is their nature that they constantly strive in corruption on the earth, and Allah does not love one who has this description.

Then Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, said: ﴿And if the People of the Book had believed and been mindful [of Allah]﴾. That is: if they had believed in Allah and His Messenger, and had been mindful of the prohibited things and sins which they engaged in, ﴿We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to gardens of pleasure﴾. That is: We would have removed from them what they feared, and granted them what they sought.

﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and others said: this means the Qur'an. ﴿They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾. That is: because they would have acted upon what is in the books in their hands from the prophets, as it is, without distortion, alteration or change, that would have led them to follow the truth and act upon what Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with; for their books clearly testify to his truth and command following him, definitely and without doubt.

* *

His statement: ﴿They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ means by this the abundance of provision descending upon them from the sky and growing for them from the earth.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿They would have eaten from above them﴾ means: He would have sent the sky upon them in abundant rain, ﴿and from beneath their feet﴾ means: He would bring forth from the earth its blessings.

Likewise Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and al-Suddi said, as Allah said: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful, We would have opened to them blessings from the heaven and the earth, but they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn﴾ [al-A'raf 96]. And He said: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea by what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste part of what they have done, so that they might return﴾ [al-Rum 41].

Allah says, addressing His servant and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) by the title of Messenger, and commanding him to convey everything that Allah sent him with. The blessings and peace of Allah be upon him carried out this command and fulfilled it in the most complete way.

Al-Bukhari said, in his commentary on this verse: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma'il, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'A'isha, who said: "Whoever tells you that Muhammad (ﷺ) [[Addition from manuscript A.]] concealed anything of what was revealed to him [[In manuscript D: "what Allah revealed to him".]] has lied. Allah says: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, to the end of the verse."

Ibn Kathir: He narrated it here in abridged form. Al-Bukhari included it in fuller form in several places in his Sahih. Muslim narrated it in the "Book of Faith", and al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in the "Book of Tafsir" of their Sunans, through several chains, from 'Amir al-Sha'bi, from Masruq ibn al-Ajda', from her, may Allah be pleased with her. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4612), and no. (4855, 7380); Sahih Muslim, no. (177); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3068); al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i, no. (11147).]]

In the two Sahihs, also from her, that she said: "If Muhammad (ﷺ) had concealed anything of the Qur'an, he would have concealed this verse: ﴿And you would conceal within yourself what Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37]." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7420), but he narrated it from the hadith of Anas. The author here followed his shaykh al-Mizzi, who mentioned it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf (11/385) from the hadith of Anas from 'A'isha, and he may have relied on the narration of al-Dawudi, as Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned in Fath al-Bari. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, no. (177).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Abbad narrated to us, from Harun ibn 'Antara, from his father, who said: "I was with Ibn 'Abbas when a man came to him and said: 'Some people come to us and tell us that you have something that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not reveal to the people.' He said: 'Do you not know that Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾? By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not bequeath to us a black mark on white paper.'"

This is a good chain. The same is found in Sahih al-Bukhari through the narration of Abu Juhayfa Wahb ibn 'Abd Allah al-Suwa'i, who said: "I said to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him: 'Do you have anything of the revelation that is not in the Qur'an?' He said: 'No, by the One who split the grain and created the soul, except an understanding that Allah gives a man concerning the Qur'an, and what is in this sheet.' I said: 'And what is in this sheet?' He said: 'The blood money, the freeing of captives, and that a Muslim is not to be executed for killing a disbeliever.'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (111).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Al-Zuhri said: "The message is from Allah, the conveying is upon the Messenger, and submission is upon us." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (13/503) with Fath al-Bari. Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "This occurred in a story narrated by al-Humaydi, and from his route by al-Khatib. Al-Humaydi said: Sufyan narrated to us: A man said to al-Zuhri: 'O Abu Bakr, the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "He is not of us who tears the collars" — what does it mean?' Al-Zuhri said: 'From Allah is the knowledge, upon His Messenger is the conveying, and upon us is submission.' This man was al-Awza'i. Ibn Abi 'Asim narrated it in the Book of Adab, and Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from Duhaym, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from al-Awza'i who said: 'I said to al-Zuhri,' and he mentioned it."]]

His community has testified for him to the conveying of the message and the fulfilment of the trust. He had them testify to this in the greatest of gatherings, in his sermon on the Day of the Farewell Pilgrimage, and there were present with him from the Companions about forty thousand [[In manuscript D: "more than seventy thousand".]], as is established in Sahih Muslim, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said in his sermon on that day: "O people, you will be asked about me, so what will you say?" They said: "We testify that you have conveyed, fulfilled, and advised." He began raising his finger to the sky and turning it toward them, saying: "O Allah, have I conveyed? O Allah, have I conveyed?" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1218).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Fudayl, that is Ibn Ghazwan, narrated to us, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "O people, what day is this?" They said: "A sacred day." He said: "What land is this?" They said: "A sacred land." He said: "What month is this?" They said: "A sacred month." He said: "Indeed your wealth, your blood, and your honour are sacred to you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this land of yours, in this month of yours." Then he repeated it several times. Then he raised his finger to the sky and said: "O Allah, have I conveyed!" several times. Ibn 'Abbas said: "By Allah, it was a charge to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic." Then he said: "Let the one present convey it to the one absent. Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking one another's necks."

Al-Bukhari narrated something similar from 'Ali ibn al-Madini, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, with the same content. [[Al-Musnad (1/230) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1739).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾ means: and if you do not deliver to the people what I sent you with, ﴿then you have not conveyed His message﴾, that is, while He knows what would follow from that, had it occurred.

'Ali ibn Abi Talha said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾ means: if you conceal a single verse of what was revealed to you from your Lord, you have not conveyed His message.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Qubaysa ibn 'Uqba narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from a man, from Mujahid, who said: When the verse was revealed: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, he said: "O Lord, how shall I do it, when I am alone? They will gather against me." Then this was revealed: ﴿And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the route of Sufyan, that is al-Thawri, with the same content.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ means: you convey My message, and I am your protector, your helper, your supporter against your enemies, and I will grant you victory over them. So do not fear and do not grieve, for none of them will reach you with any harm that would hurt you.

Before the revelation of this verse, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to be guarded, as Imam Ahmad said:

Yazid narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'a narrate that 'A'isha used to relate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stayed awake one night while she was beside him. She said: I said: "What is the matter with you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "I wish a righteous man of my Companions would guard me tonight." She said: While I was like that, I heard the sound of weapons. He said: "Who is this?" He said: "I am Sa'd ibn Malik." He said: "What brought you?" He said: "I came to guard you, O Messenger of Allah." She said: Then I heard the snoring of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his sleep. The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in the two Sahihs through the route of Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, with the same content. [[Al-Musnad (6/140), Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2885), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2410).]]

In another wording: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stayed awake one night when he arrived in Madina, meaning following his migration there, after he had consummated his marriage to 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, and that was in the second year after the migration.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ibrahim ibn Marzuq al-Basri, resident of Egypt, narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, al-Harith ibn 'Ubayd, that is Abu Qudama, narrated to us, from al-Juraybiri, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, from 'A'isha [may Allah be pleased with her] [[Addition from manuscript A.]], who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to be guarded until this verse was revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾. She said: So the Prophet (ﷺ) put his head out of the tent and said: "O people, disperse, for Allah the Mighty and Majestic has protected me."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way, from 'Abd ibn Humayd and from Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami, both from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, with the same chain. Then he said: "This is a gharib (strange) hadith." [[Gharib: a classification of a hadith transmitted through a single narrator at some point in its chain, or with an unusual wording.]]

Ibn Jarir and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it in the same way through the routes of Muslim ibn Ibrahim, with the same chain. Then al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sahih, but the two Shaykhs did not narrate it." Likewise, Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from al-Harith ibn 'Ubayd Abu Qudama [al-Iyadi] [[Addition from manuscript A.]], from al-Juraybiri, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, from 'A'isha, with the same content. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (5037); Tafsir al-Tabari (10/469); al-Mustadrak (2/313); Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur, no. (768).]]

Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Some of them narrated this from al-Juraybiri, from Ibn Shaqiq, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to be guarded," and he did not mention 'A'isha.

I say: Ibn Jarir narrated it in this way through the route of Isma'il ibn 'Ulayya, and Ibn Mardawayh through the route of Wuhayb [[In manuscript A: "Wahb".]]; both of them from al-Juraybiri, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, as a mursal (a report whose chain omits the Companion) [[Tafsir al-Tabari (10/469). Shaykh Sa'd al-Humayyid, may Allah preserve him, said in his commentary on the Sunan of Sa'id ibn Mansur (4/1505): "The narration of Ibn 'Ulayya alone is more likely than the narration of al-Harith, because he is more reliable than him and heard from Sa'id before his confusion; how much more so when Wuhayb agrees with him?" End of quote.]]. This has also been transmitted as mursal from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi; Ibn Jarir narrated both of them. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (10/468, 469).]] Al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, then said:

Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Rushdin al-Misri narrated to us, Khalid ibn 'Abd al-Salam al-Saddafi narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah [[In manuscript R: "'Ubayd Allah".]] ibn Mawhab, from 'Isma ibn Malik al-Khatmi [[In manuscript R: "al-Khatami".]], who said: "We used to guard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at night until this verse was revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾, and he abandoned the guard."

[[In its chain is Ahmad ibn Rushdin, who is extremely weak, and some of the imams accused him of lying; al-Fadl ibn al-Mukhtar is weak and narrated objectionable reports. Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Isaba in the biography of 'Isma ibn Malik al-Khatmi: "He has hadiths narrated by al-Daraqutni, al-Tabarani and others, all of which revolve around al-Fadl ibn al-Mukhtar, who is extremely weak."]]

Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Hamad [[In manuscript A: "Humayd".]] ibn Muhammad ibn Hamad Abu Nasr al-Katib al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Kurdus ibn Muhammad al-Wasiti narrated to us, Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman [[In manuscripts R and A: "Ya'la"; corrected from al-Mu'jam al-Awsat and the books of biographies.]] narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: al-'Abbas, the paternal uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was among those who guarded him. When this verse was revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) abandoned the guard. [[It is in al-Tabarani's al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (3314), Majma' al-Bahrayn. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/17): "In it is 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, who is weak."]]

'Ali ibn Abi Hamid al-Madini narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Mufadal ibn Ibrahim al-Ash'ari narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, my father narrated to us, who said: I heard Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki narrate from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, Abu Talib would send someone with him to guard him, until this verse was revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾. So he went to send someone with him, but he said: "O uncle, Allah has protected me; I have no need of anyone you send."

This is a gharib hadith and it contains an objectionable element [[In its chain is someone I do not know, and Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar has been criticized especially in his narration from Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir.]], for this verse is Madinan, while this hadith implies that it is Makkan.

Then he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani narrated to us, from al-Nadr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was being guarded, and Abu Talib would send with him, every day, men from the Banu Hashim to guard him, until this verse was revealed to him: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people.﴾ He said: So his uncle wanted to send with him someone to guard him, and he (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has protected me from the jinn and mankind."

Al-Tabarani narrated it from Ya'qub ibn Ghaylan al-Amani, from Abu Kurayb, with the same chain. [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/257). al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/17): "In its chain is al-Nadr ibn Abd al-Rahman, who is weak."]] This too is strange. The correct view is that this verse is Madani, indeed among the last of what was revealed in Madinah, and Allah knows best.

From Allah's protection of His Messenger is that He guarded him from the people of Makkah, their chieftains, their envious ones, their opponents and their affluent ones, despite their intense enmity, hatred, and their waging war against him night and day, through great means that Allah the Exalted creates by His power and His great wisdom. At the beginning of his mission, He protected him through his uncle Abu Talib, who was a great, obeyed leader among the Quraysh. Allah placed in his heart a natural love for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), not a legislated love. Had he embraced Islam, their disbelievers and great ones would have dared to act against him. But since there was a shared measure of disbelief between him and them, they feared him and respected him. When Abu Talib died, the polytheists inflicted on him a slight harm. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prepared for him the Ansar, who pledged allegiance to him upon Islam and that he would relocate to their home, which is Madinah. When he arrived there, they protected him from the red and the black. Whenever any of the polytheists or the People of the Book intended harm against him, Allah thwarted them and turned their plot back upon them. When the Jews practised sorcery against him, Allah protected him from them and revealed to him the two surahs of refuge (al-Mu'awwidhatayn) as a cure for that ailment. When the Jews poisoned the foreleg of that sheep at Khaybar, Allah informed him of it and protected him from it. There are many similar instances, too long to mention. Among them is what the commentators mentioned concerning this noble verse:

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: al-Harith narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others, who said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alighted at a place, his companions would select for him a shady tree, and he would rest beneath it at midday. A Bedouin came to him, drew his sword and said: "Who will protect you from me?" He (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." The Bedouin's hand trembled and the sword fell from him. He said: And he struck his head against the tree until his brain spilled out. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people.﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (10/470).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Musa ibn Ubaydah narrated to us, Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) campaigned against Banu Anmar, he stopped at Dhat al-Riqa' at the highest part of a palm grove. While he was sitting on the edge of a well with his legs dangling, Ghawrath ibn al-Harith from Banu al-Najjar said: "I will surely kill Muhammad." His companions said to him: "How will you kill him?" He said: "I will say to him: 'Give me your sword.' When he gives it to me, I will kill him with it." He said: So he came to him and said: "O Muhammad, give me your sword so I may examine it." He gave it to him, but his hand trembled until the sword fell from his hand. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has come between you and what you intended." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people.﴾

This narration is strange through this route, but the story of "Ghawrath ibn al-Harith" is well known in the Sahih. [[In the chain of Ibn Abi Hatim is Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is weak. The story originally appears in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4136).]] Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abu Amr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Whenever we accompanied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey, we would leave for him the largest and shadiest tree, and he would descend beneath it. One day he descended beneath a tree and hung his sword upon it. A man came, took it, and said: "O Muhammad, who will protect you from me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah protects me from you. Put down the sword." He put it down, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people.﴾

Abu Hatim ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mu'ammil ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same wording. [[Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (1739), Mawarid edition.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard Abu Isra'il, meaning al-Jushami, say: I heard Ja'dah, who is the son of Khalid ibn al-Simmah al-Jushami, may Allah be pleased with him, say: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) and he saw a fat man, and the Prophet (ﷺ) began pointing to his belly with his hand and saying: "If this were in something other than this, it would have been better for you." He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was then brought a man and it was said: "This man intended to kill you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not be alarmed, do not be alarmed. Even if you had intended that, Allah would not have given you power over me." [[al-Musnad (3/471). al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (8/226): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Abu Isra'il al-Jushami, who is trustworthy."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ means: You (O Messenger) only convey, and it is Allah who guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, as He said: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 272], and He said: ﴿Upon you is only the conveying, and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd: 40].

Allah the Exalted says: Say, O Muhammad: "O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything" meaning, of the religion, "until you establish the Torah and the Gospel," meaning, until you believe in all the books that are in your hands which were sent down from Allah upon the prophets, and act by what is in them, and among what is in them is the command to follow Muhammad ﷺ, to believe in his being sent, and to follow his law. Therefore Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "and what has been sent down to you from your Lord," that it means the Great Qur'an.

* *

As for His saying: "And what has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief," its explanation has already preceded. "So do not grieve over the disbelieving people" meaning: do not grieve over them, and do not let that from them weaken your resolve.

Then He said: "Indeed, those who believed," and they are the Muslims, "and those who were Jews," and they are the bearers of the Torah, "and the Sabeans" (the Sabians) — since the separation was long, the conjunction with the nominative case is proper. The Sabeans are a sect between the Christians and the Magians, having no religion. This was said by Mujahid. And he also related: between the Jews and the Magians. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: between the Jews and the Christians. And from al-Hasan [and al-Hakam] (an addition from manuscript A): they are like the Magians. Qatadah said: they are a people who worship the angels, pray facing other than the qiblah, and recite the Psalms. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: they are a people who know Allah alone, and they have no law by which they act, and they have not introduced disbelief.

Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Abi al-Zinad informed me, from his father, who said: The Sabeans are a people from the direction of Iraq, and they are at Kuthaa; they believe in all the prophets, fast thirty days every year, and pray toward Yemen five prayers every day. And it has been said otherwise.

As for the Christians, they are well known, and they are the bearers of the Gospel.

The intended meaning is that every group that believed in Allah and the Last Day, which is the Return and the Recompense, the Day of Judgment, and did righteous deeds, that will not be so until it conforms to the law of Muhammad after the sending of its bearer, who was sent to all of mankind and jinn. Whoever is characterized by that: "there is no fear concerning them" regarding what they will face, "nor will they grieve" over what they left behind them. "And they will not grieve." The discussion of their counterparts has already preceded in Surah al-Baqarah, sufficient to dispense with repeating it.

Allah the Exalted says: Say, O Muhammad: "O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything" meaning, of the religion, "until you establish the Torah and the Gospel," meaning, until you believe in all the books that are in your hands which were sent down from Allah upon the prophets, and act by what is in them, and among what is in them is the command to follow Muhammad ﷺ, to believe in his being sent, and to follow his law. Therefore Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "and what has been sent down to you from your Lord," that it means the Great Qur'an.

* *

"So do not grieve over the disbelieving people" meaning: do not grieve over them, and do not let that from them weaken your resolve.

Then He said: "Indeed, those who believed," and they are the Muslims, "and those who were Jews," and they are the bearers of the Torah, "and the Sabeans" (the Sabians) — since the separation was long, the conjunction with the nominative case is proper. The Sabeans are a sect between the Christians and the Magians, having no religion. This was said by Mujahid. And he also related: between the Jews and the Magians. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: between the Jews and the Christians. And from al-Hasan [and al-Hakam] (an addition from manuscript A): they are like the Magians. Qatadah said: they are a people who worship the angels, pray facing other than the qiblah, and recite the Psalms. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: they are a people who know Allah alone, and they have no law by which they act, and they have not introduced disbelief.

Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Abi al-Zinad informed me, from his father, who said: The Sabeans are a people from the direction of Iraq, and they are at Kuthaa; they believe in all the prophets, fast thirty days every year, and pray toward Yemen five prayers every day. And it has been said otherwise.

As for the Christians, they are well known, and they are the bearers of the Gospel.

The intended meaning is that every group that believed in Allah and the Last Day, which is the Return and the Recompense, the Day of Judgment, and did righteous deeds, that will not be so until it conforms to the law of Muhammad after the sending of its bearer, who was sent to all of mankind and jinn. Whoever is characterized by that: "there is no fear concerning them" regarding what they will face, "nor will they grieve" over what they left behind them. "And they will not grieve." The discussion of their counterparts has already preceded in Surah al-Baqarah, sufficient to dispense with repeating it.

It mentions, exalted is He, that He took covenants and pledges from the Children of Israel to hear and obey Allah and His Messenger. They broke those covenants and pledges, followed their own opinions and desires, and put them ahead of the laws (sharai'). Whatever agreed with them they accepted, and whatever opposed them they rejected. Therefore He said: ﴿Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group they denied and a group they killed, and they thought there would be no trial﴾, meaning: and they thought no evil would befall them for what they did. But evil did befall them, namely that they became blind to the truth and deaf, so they would not hear any truth [[In manuscript D: "so they would not listen to any good."]] nor be guided to it. ﴿Then Allah turned to them in forgiveness﴾, meaning: from what they were in. ﴿Then they became blind and deaf again﴾

meaning: after that, ﴿many of them [became blind and deaf]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript R.]] ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, meaning: He is aware of them and knowing of who deserves guidance and who deserves misguidance.

It mentions, exalted is He, that He took covenants and pledges from the Children of Israel to hear and obey Allah and His Messenger. They broke those covenants and pledges, followed their own opinions and desires, and put them ahead of the laws (sharai'). Whatever agreed with them they accepted, and whatever opposed them they rejected. Therefore He said: ﴿Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group they denied and a group they killed, and they thought there would be no trial﴾, meaning: and they thought no evil would befall them for what they did. But evil did befall them, namely that they became blind to the truth and deaf, so they would not hear any truth [[In manuscript D: "so they would not listen to any good."]] nor be guided to it. ﴿Then Allah turned to them in forgiveness﴾, meaning: from what they were in. ﴿Then they became blind and deaf again﴾

meaning: after that, ﴿many of them [became blind and deaf]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript R.]] ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, meaning: He is aware of them and knowing of who deserves guidance and who deserves misguidance.

Allah the Exalted says, ruling on the disbelief of the sects of the Christians, from the Melkites, the Jacobites and the Nestorians, those among them who said that the Messiah is Allah. Allah is exalted and far above what they say, Glorified and Sanctified, high above that by a great elevation.

Moreover, the Messiah had already addressed them as the servant of Allah and His Messenger. The first word he uttered while still a small child in the cradle was: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet﴾. He did not say: "I am Allah," nor "I am the son of Allah." Rather, he said: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet﴾, up to his saying: ﴿And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path﴾ [Maryam 19:30-36].

Likewise, he said to them when he had reached maturity and prophethood, commanding them to worship Allah, his Lord and their Lord, alone, without any partner. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the Messiah said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah"﴾, meaning: so he worships others along with Him, ﴿then Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire﴾, meaning: He has made the Fire obligatory for him and forbidden Paradise to him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:48, 116], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water or from what Allah has provided you." They will say, "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers"﴾ [Al-A'raf 7:50].

And in the Sahih (of Muslim): that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a caller to proclaim among the people: "Indeed, Paradise will not be entered except by a Muslim soul," and in another wording: "a believing soul." [Sahih Muslim, no. 111.]

And it has preceded at the beginning of Surat an-Nisa', at His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:48, 116], the hadith of Yazid [in A: "Zayd"] ibn Babanus from Aishah: "The registers are three," and he mentioned among them a register which Allah will not forgive, which is associating others with Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise, [and his refuge is the Fire]﴾ [[addition from A.]] The hadith is in the Musnad of Ahmad. [Musnad (6/240).]

Therefore Allah [[addition from A.]] the Exalted, reporting about the Messiah, said that he said to the Children of Israel: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾.

That is: he has no helper, no supporter and no rescuer from what he is in, with Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three"﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hastjani narrated to us, Sa'id ibn al-Hakam ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, al-Fadl narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three"﴾, he said: It is the saying of the Jews: ﴿Uzair is the son of Allah﴾, and the saying of the Christians: ﴿The Messiah is the son of Allah﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:30], so they made Allah the third of three.

This is a strange opinion regarding the interpretation of the verse, that it refers to the two groups, the Jews and the Christians. The correct view is that it was revealed specifically concerning the Christians. This was said by Mujahid and others.

Then they differed about it. It was said: What is meant is their disbelievers in their saying of the three hypostases (aqanim), which are the hypostasis of the Father, the hypostasis of the Son, and the hypostasis of the Word emanating from the Father to the Son. Allah is exalted far above what they say by a great elevation. Ibn Jarir and others said: The three sects, the Melkites, the Jacobites and the Nestorians, say these hypostases, and they differ about them with extreme variance, which is not the place to expound, and each sect among them declares the others to be disbelievers. The truth is that all three are disbelievers.

Al-Suddi and others said: It was revealed concerning their making the Messiah and his mother two gods alongside Allah, so they made Allah the third of three in this sense. Al-Suddi said: It is like His saying at the end of the surah: ﴿And when Allah says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah'?" He will say, "Exalted are You"﴾ to the end of the verse [Al-Ma'idah 5:116].

This view is the most apparent, and Allah knows best. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there is no god except one God﴾, meaning: He is not plural, but rather He alone has no partner, the God of all creation and all existing things.

Then He said, warning and threatening them: ﴿And if they do not desist from what they say﴾, meaning: from this slander and lying, ﴿there will surely afflict those who disbelieve among them a painful punishment﴾, meaning: in the Hereafter, of shackles and torment.

Then He said: ﴿Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. This is from His generosity, bounty, kindness and mercy toward His creation, that despite this great sin and this fabrication, lying and falsehood, He calls them to repentance and forgiveness. Whoever turns to Him in repentance, He accepts his repentance. Then He said: ﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger; the messengers had passed on before him﴾, meaning: he is like his fellow messengers who came before him, and he is a servant of the servants of Allah and a messenger of His honored messengers, as He said: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 43:59].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And his mother was a truthful woman﴾, meaning: she was a believer in him, one who affirmed him. This is the highest of her ranks, and it indicates that she was not a prophetess, as Ibn Hazm and others claimed, those who held the prophethood of Sarah the mother of Isaac, the prophethood of the mother of Moses, and the prophethood of the mother of Jesus, relying on the angels' address to Sarah and Mary, and on His saying: ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses, "Nurse him"﴾ [Al-Qasas 28:7]. They said: and this is the meaning of prophethood. What the majority hold is that Allah did not send any prophet except from among men. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the cities﴾ [Yusuf 12:109]. Shaykh Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, related the consensus on this.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They both used to eat food﴾, meaning: they needed to be nourished by it and to expel it from themselves. So they are two servants like all people, and they are not two gods, as the ignorant sects of the Christians claimed, upon whom be the continuous curses of Allah until the Day of Resurrection.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Look how We make the signs clear to them; then look how they are turned away﴾, meaning: We explain them and make them manifest. ﴿Then look how they are turned away﴾, meaning: then consider, after this clarification, clarity and manifestation, where they go, to what statement they cling, and to which path of error they head?

He, exalted is He, informs that He cursed the disbelievers among the Children of Israel for a long time, as He revealed it upon His Prophet Dawud (David), upon him be peace, and through the tongue of Isa son of Maryam (Jesus son of Mary), because of their disobedience to Allah and their transgression against His creation.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: They were cursed in the Torah, the Injil (Gospel), the Zabur (Psalms), and the Furqan (the Qur'an).

Then He explained their condition regarding what they used to practise in their time, saying: ﴿They did not forbid one another from wrongful deeds they committed. Wretched indeed was what they used to do.﴾ That is: none of them would forbid another from committing sins and prohibited acts. Then He censured them for that, so that the like of what they did would be avoided, saying: ﴿Wretched indeed was what they used to do.﴾

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yazid narrated to us, Sharik ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Children of Israel fell into sins, their scholars forbade them, but they did not desist. So they sat with them in their gatherings — Yazid said: I think he said: and their markets — and ate and drank with them. So Allah struck their hearts, one against another, and cursed them through the tongue of Dawud and Isa son of Maryam, because they disobeyed and used to transgress." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reclining, then he sat up and said: "No, by Him in whose hand is my soul, you must restrain them upon the truth, restraining them firmly."

Abu Dawud said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Nufayli narrated to us, Yunus ibn Rashid narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing that entered deficiency upon the Children of Israel was that a man would meet another man and say: 'O such-and-such, fear Allah and leave off what you are doing, for it is not lawful for you.' Then he would meet him the next day, and that would not prevent him from being his eating companion, drinking companion and sitting companion. When they did that, Allah struck their hearts, one against another, then He said: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of Dawud and Isa son of Maryam﴾ until His saying: ﴿defiantly disobedient﴾." Then he said: "No, by Allah, you must enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, and you must take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer and restrain him firmly upon the truth, or you will confine him to the truth by confining."

This is also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, through the route of 'Ali ibn Badhimah, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib." Then he and Ibn Majah narrated it from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, as a mursal report.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj and Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, both saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim al-Aftas, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man from the Children of Israel, when he saw his brother committing a sin, would forbid him from it out of admonition. Then the next day, what he had seen from him would not prevent him from being his eating companion, his associate and his partner — and in the narration of Harun: and his drinking companion — then they both agreed on the text. When Allah saw that from them, He struck their hearts, one against another, and cursed them upon the tongue of their Prophet Dawud and Isa son of Maryam, because they disobeyed and used to transgress." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is good, you must forbid what is evil, you must take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer, and you must restrain him firmly upon the truth, or Allah will strike your hearts, one against another, or He will curse you as He cursed them." The wording is that of Abu Sa'id. Thus he said in the narration of this hadith.

Abu Dawud also narrated it from Khalaf ibn Hisham, from Abu Shihab al-Khayyat, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim — he is Ibn 'Ijlan al-Aftas — from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording. Then Abu Dawud said: Khalid also narrated it similarly, from al-'Ala', from 'Amr ibn Murrah. And al-Muharibi narrated it from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim al-Aftas, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah.

Our shaykh, the Hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, said: Khalid ibn 'Abdullah al-Wasiti narrated it from al-'Ala', from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Musa.

The ahadith on enjoining good and forbidding evil are very numerous, and we shall mention from them what is suitable for this place.

The hadith of Jarir has already been mentioned at His saying: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 63]. And it will come at His saying: ﴿O you who believe, keep to yourselves; those who go astray will not harm you if you are guided﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105], the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani [may Allah be pleased with them both] — Imam Ahmad said:

Sulayman al-Hashimi narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us, 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr informed me, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ashhali, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, or Allah will shortly send upon you a punishment from Him, then you will call upon Him and He will not answer you."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Ali ibn Hujr, from Isma'il ibn Ja'far, with the same chain, and said: "This is a hasan hadith."

Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn 'Uthman, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, before you call upon Him and you are not answered." He alone narrated it, and this 'Asim is unknown (majhul).

In the Sahih, through the route of al-A'mash, from Isma'il ibn Raja', from his father, from Sa'id — and from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri — who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is not able, then with his tongue; if he is not able, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith." Narrated by Muslim.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Sayf — he is Ibn Abi Sulayman — narrated to us: I heard 'Adi ibn 'Adi al-Kindi narrate from Mujahid, who said: A mawla of ours narrated to me that he heard my grandfather — meaning 'Adi ibn 'Umayrah, may Allah be pleased with him — say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah does not punish the common folk for the deed of the elite until they see the evil among them while they are able to denounce it, and they do not denounce it. When they do that, Allah punishes both the common folk and the elite."

Then Ahmad narrated it from Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sayf ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Adi ibn 'Adi al-Kindi: a mawla of ours narrated to me that he heard my grandfather say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, and he mentioned it. In this way Imam Ahmad narrated it through these two routes.

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Abu Bakr narrated to us, Mughirah ibn Ziyad al-Mawsili narrated to us, from 'Adi ibn 'Adi, from al-'Urs — meaning Ibn 'Umayrah — from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When a sin is committed on earth, whoever witnesses it and dislikes it — and he said once: and denounces it — is like one who was absent from it, and whoever was absent from it and approves of it is like one who witnessed it."

Abu Dawud alone narrated it, then he narrated it from Ahmad ibn Yunus, from Abu Shihab, from Mughirah ibn Ziyad, from 'Adi ibn 'Adi, as a mursal report.

And Abu Dawud said: Sulayman ibn Harb and Hafs ibn 'Umar narrated to us, both saying: Shu'bah narrated to us — and this is his wording — from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: One who heard the Prophet (ﷺ) informed me — and Sulayman said: a man from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) narrated to me — that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "People will not perish until they excuse themselves from themselves" — or: "until they excuse [their own faults]."

Ibn Majah said: 'Imran ibn Musa narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up delivering a sermon, and among what he said was: "Beware, let no man be prevented by fear of people from speaking the truth when he knows it." He said: Abu Sa'id wept and said: "By Allah, we have indeed seen things and feared."

In the hadith of Isra'il, from Muhammad ibn Hujadah, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best jihad is a word of truth before an unjust ruler."

Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah; al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib from this route."

Ibn Majah said: Rashid ibn Sa'id al-Ramli narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: A man confronted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the first pillar (jamrah) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, which jihad is best?" He remained silent. When he threw the second pillar, he asked him again, and he remained silent. When he threw the Jamrat al-'Aqabah and placed his foot in the stirrup to mount, he said: "Where is the questioner?" He said: "I am here, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "A word of truth spoken before an unjust ruler." He alone narrated it.

Ibn Majah said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from

**Ibn Abi Sa'id** (ﷺ's companion Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, رضي الله عنه) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "None of you should belittle himself." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does one of us belittle himself?" He said: "He sees a matter concerning Allah about which he has something to say, but then does not say it. Then Allah will say to him on the Day of Resurrection: 'What prevented you from saying such-and-such about Me?' He will say: 'The fear of people.' Then He will say: 'It was Me that you had more right to fear.'" Ibn Majah alone narrated it. [Footnote: Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4008. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/242): "This chain is sahih."]

He also said: Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman Abu Tuwalah narrated to us, Nahar al-Abdi narrated to us, that he heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah will indeed question the servant on the Day of Resurrection, until He says: 'What prevented you, when you saw the evil, from denouncing it?' And when Allah makes the servant forget his argument, he will say: 'O Lord, I hoped in You, and I feared people.'" Ibn Majah alone narrated it too, and its isnad (chain of narration) is acceptable. [Footnote: Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4017. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/244): "This chain is sahih."]

Imam Ahmad said: Amr ibn Asim narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Hasan, from Jundab, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It is not befitting for a Muslim to humiliate himself." It was said: "And how does he humiliate himself?" He said: "By exposing himself to trials he cannot bear."

At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah both narrated it in the same way, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Amr ibn Asim, with this chain. At-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith." [Footnote: Musnad Ahmad (5/405), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2254, and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4016.]

Ibn Majah said: Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Zayd ibn Yahya ibn Ubayd al-Khuza'i narrated to us, al-Haytham ibn Humayd narrated to us, Abu Ma'bad Hafs ibn Ghaylan al-Ru'ayni narrated to us, from Makhul, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, when will enjoining good and forbidding evil be abandoned?" He said: "When there appears among you what appeared among the nations before you." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what appeared among the nations before us?" He said: "Kingship among your young, immorality among your elders, and knowledge among your lowly." Zayd said: The meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) words "and knowledge among your lowly" is: when knowledge is found among the wicked (fussaq).

Ibn Majah alone narrated it. [Footnote: Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4015. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/244): "This chain is sahih and its narrators are trustworthy."] The evidence for this will come in the hadith of Abu Tha'labah, at the words of Allah: ﴿لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ مَنْ ضَلَّ إِذَا اهْتَدَيْتُمْ﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105], if Allah wills, and with Him is trust.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Thou seest many of them turning in friendship to those who disbelieve﴾. Mujahid said: By this He means the hypocrites.

As for His words: ﴿Evil indeed is what their souls have sent forward for them﴾, He means by it their friendship with the disbelievers and their abandonment of friendship with the believers, which resulted in hypocrisy in their hearts and provoked Allah's wrath against them, a continuous wrath until the day they return. Therefore He said: ﴿that Allah's wrath is upon them﴾, explaining the reason for which He censured them. Then He informed that ﴿in torment they will abide forever﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Maslamah ibn Ali narrated to us, from al-A'mash, with an isnad that he mentioned, who said: "O assembly of Muslims, beware of adultery, for it has six characteristics: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for the ones in this world: it removes radiance, brings poverty, and shortens life. As for the ones in the Hereafter: it brings on the Lord's wrath, evil reckoning, and eternal abode in the Fire." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Evil indeed is what their souls have sent forward for them, that Allah's wrath is upon them, and in torment they will abide forever﴾.

Thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn Ammar, from Maslamah, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned it. He also cited it through the route of Sa'id ibn Ghufayr, from Maslamah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Kufi, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar.

This hadith is weak in every case, and Allah knows best. [Footnote: Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (6/317) through these two routes, saying: (1) Abdan narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Maslamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, with it. (2) Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Bayan narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Ufayr narrated to us, Maslamah ibn Ali narrated to us, from Abu Ali al-Kufi, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, something similar. Then he said: "This from al-A'mash is not preserved, and it is munkar. Ibn Ufayr and Hisham differed in its isnad: Hisham said 'from Maslamah, from al-A'mash,' while Ibn Ufayr said 'from Maslamah, from Abu Ali al-Kufi, from al-A'mash,' and Abu Ali is unknown. This hadith is also narrated from Abd Allah ibn Usmah al-Nusaybi, from Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Bunani, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ). These hadiths are not preserved."]

Then He said: ﴿And had they believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies﴾, meaning: had they believed in Allah, His messengers and the Criterion (al-Furqan) with true belief, they would not have committed what they committed of befriending the disbelievers inwardly and opposing the believers. ﴿But many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: they have departed from obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and they oppose the verses of His revelation and His sending down.

He, exalted is He, informs that He cursed the disbelievers among the Children of Israel for a long time, as He revealed it upon His Prophet Dawud (David), upon him be peace, and through the tongue of Isa son of Maryam (Jesus son of Mary), because of their disobedience to Allah and their transgression against His creation.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: They were cursed in the Torah, the Injil (Gospel), the Zabur (Psalms), and the Furqan (the Qur'an).

In the hadith of Isra'il, from Muhammad ibn Hujadah, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best jihad is a word of truth before an unjust ruler."

Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah; al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib from this route."

Ibn Majah said: Rashid ibn Sa'id al-Ramli narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: A man confronted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the first pillar (jamrah) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, which jihad is best?" He remained silent. When he threw the second pillar, he asked him again, and he remained silent. When he threw the Jamrat al-'Aqabah and placed his foot in the stirrup to mount, he said: "Where is the questioner?" He said: "I am here, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "A word of truth spoken before an unjust ruler." He alone narrated it.

Ibn Majah said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from

**Ibn Abi Sa'id** (ﷺ's companion Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, رضي الله عنه) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "None of you should belittle himself." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does one of us belittle himself?" He said: "He sees a matter concerning Allah about which he has something to say, but then does not say it. Then Allah will say to him on the Day of Resurrection: 'What prevented you from saying such-and-such about Me?' He will say: 'The fear of people.' Then He will say: 'It was Me that you had more right to fear.'" Ibn Majah alone narrated it. [Footnote: Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4008. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/242): "This chain is sahih."]

He also said: Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman Abu Tuwalah narrated to us, Nahar al-Abdi narrated to us, that he heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah will indeed question the servant on the Day of Resurrection, until He says: 'What prevented you, when you saw the evil, from denouncing it?' And when Allah makes the servant forget his argument, he will say: 'O Lord, I hoped in You, and I feared people.'" Ibn Majah alone narrated it too, and its isnad (chain of narration) is acceptable. [Footnote: Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4017. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/244): "This chain is sahih."]

Imam Ahmad said: Amr ibn Asim narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Hasan, from Jundab, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It is not befitting for a Muslim to humiliate himself." It was said: "And how does he humiliate himself?" He said: "By exposing himself to trials he cannot bear."

At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah both narrated it in the same way, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Amr ibn Asim, with this chain. At-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith." [Footnote: Musnad Ahmad (5/405), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2254, and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4016.]

Ibn Majah said: Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Zayd ibn Yahya ibn Ubayd al-Khuza'i narrated to us, al-Haytham ibn Humayd narrated to us, Abu Ma'bad Hafs ibn Ghaylan al-Ru'ayni narrated to us, from Makhul, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, when will enjoining good and forbidding evil be abandoned?" He said: "When there appears among you what appeared among the nations before you." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what appeared among the nations before us?" He said: "Kingship among your young, immorality among your elders, and knowledge among your lowly." Zayd said: The meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) words "and knowledge among your lowly" is: when knowledge is found among the wicked (fussaq).

Ibn Majah alone narrated it. [Footnote: Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4015. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/244): "This chain is sahih and its narrators are trustworthy."] The evidence for this will come in the hadith of Abu Tha'labah, at the words of Allah: ﴿لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ مَنْ ضَلَّ إِذَا اهْتَدَيْتُمْ﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105], if Allah wills, and with Him is trust.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Thou seest many of them turning in friendship to those who disbelieve﴾. Mujahid said: By this He means the hypocrites.

As for His words: ﴿Evil indeed is what their souls have sent forward for them﴾, He means by it their friendship with the disbelievers and their abandonment of friendship with the believers, which resulted in hypocrisy in their hearts and provoked Allah's wrath against them, a continuous wrath until the day they return. Therefore He said: ﴿that Allah's wrath is upon them﴾, explaining the reason for which He censured them. Then He informed that ﴿in torment they will abide forever﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Maslamah ibn Ali narrated to us, from al-A'mash, with an isnad that he mentioned, who said: "O assembly of Muslims, beware of adultery, for it has six characteristics: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for the ones in this world: it removes radiance, brings poverty, and shortens life. As for the ones in the Hereafter: it brings on the Lord's wrath, evil reckoning, and eternal abode in the Fire." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Evil indeed is what their souls have sent forward for them, that Allah's wrath is upon them, and in torment they will abide forever﴾.

Thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn Ammar, from Maslamah, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned it. He also cited it through the route of Sa'id ibn Ghufayr, from Maslamah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Kufi, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar.

This hadith is weak in every case, and Allah knows best. [Footnote: Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (6/317) through these two routes, saying: (1) Abdan narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Maslamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, with it. (2) Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Bayan narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Ufayr narrated to us, Maslamah ibn Ali narrated to us, from Abu Ali al-Kufi, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, something similar. Then he said: "This from al-A'mash is not preserved, and it is munkar. Ibn Ufayr and Hisham differed in its isnad: Hisham said 'from Maslamah, from al-A'mash,' while Ibn Ufayr said 'from Maslamah, from Abu Ali al-Kufi, from al-A'mash,' and Abu Ali is unknown. This hadith is also narrated from Abd Allah ibn Usmah al-Nusaybi, from Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Bunani, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ). These hadiths are not preserved."]

Then He said: ﴿And had they believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies﴾, meaning: had they believed in Allah, His messengers and the Criterion (al-Furqan) with true belief, they would not have committed what they committed of befriending the disbelievers inwardly and opposing the believers. ﴿But many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: they have departed from obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and they oppose the verses of His revelation and His sending down.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 5, verses 78–81 (part 1 of 2):

He, exalted is He, informs that He cursed the disbelievers among the Children of Israel for a long time, as He revealed it upon His Prophet Dawud (David), upon him be peace, and through the tongue of Isa son of Maryam (Jesus son of Mary), because of their disobedience to Allah and their transgression against His creation.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: They were cursed in the Torah, the Injil (Gospel), the Zabur (Psalms), and the Furqan (the Qur'an).

Then He explained their condition regarding what they used to practise in their time, saying: ﴿They did not forbid one another from wrongful deeds they committed. Wretched indeed was what they used to do.﴾ That is: none of them would forbid another from committing sins and prohibited acts. Then He censured them for that, so that the like of what they did would be avoided, saying: ﴿Wretched indeed was what they used to do.﴾

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yazid narrated to us, Sharik ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Children of Israel fell into sins, their scholars forbade them, but they did not desist. So they sat with them in their gatherings — Yazid said: I think he said: and their markets — and ate and drank with them. So Allah struck their hearts, one against another, and cursed them through the tongue of Dawud and Isa son of Maryam, because they disobeyed and used to transgress." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reclining, then he sat up and said: "No, by Him in whose hand is my soul, you must restrain them upon the truth, restraining them firmly."

Abu Dawud said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Nufayli narrated to us, Yunus ibn Rashid narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing that entered deficiency upon the Children of Israel was that a man would meet another man and say: 'O such-and-such, fear Allah and leave off what you are doing, for it is not lawful for you.' Then he would meet him the next day, and that would not prevent him from being his eating companion, drinking companion and sitting companion. When they did that, Allah struck their hearts, one against another, then He said: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of Dawud and Isa son of Maryam﴾ until His saying: ﴿defiantly disobedient﴾." Then he said: "No, by Allah, you must enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, and you must take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer and restrain him firmly upon the truth, or you will confine him to the truth by confining."

This is also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, through the route of 'Ali ibn Badhimah, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib." Then he and Ibn Majah narrated it from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, as a mursal report.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj and Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, both saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim al-Aftas, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man from the Children of Israel, when he saw his brother committing a sin, would forbid him from it out of admonition. Then the next day, what he had seen from him would not prevent him from being his eating companion, his associate and his partner — and in the narration of Harun: and his drinking companion — then they both agreed on the text. When Allah saw that from them, He struck their hearts, one against another, and cursed them upon the tongue of their Prophet Dawud and Isa son of Maryam, because they disobeyed and used to transgress." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is good, you must forbid what is evil, you must take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer, and you must restrain him firmly upon the truth, or Allah will strike your hearts, one against another, or He will curse you as He cursed them." The wording is that of Abu Sa'id. Thus he said in the narration of this hadith.

Abu Dawud also narrated it from Khalaf ibn Hisham, from Abu Shihab al-Khayyat, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim — he is Ibn 'Ijlan al-Aftas — from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording. Then Abu Dawud said: Khalid also narrated it similarly, from al-'Ala', from 'Amr ibn Murrah. And al-Muharibi narrated it from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim al-Aftas, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah.

Our shaykh, the Hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, said: Khalid ibn 'Abdullah al-Wasiti narrated it from al-'Ala', from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Musa.

The ahadith on enjoining good and forbidding evil are very numerous, and we shall mention from them what is suitable for this place.

The hadith of Jarir has already been mentioned at His saying: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 63]. And it will come at His saying: ﴿O you who believe, keep to yourselves; those who go astray will not harm you if you are guided﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105], the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani [may Allah be pleased with them both] — Imam Ahmad said:

Sulayman al-Hashimi narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us, 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr informed me, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ashhali, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, or Allah will shortly send upon you a punishment from Him, then you will call upon Him and He will not answer you."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Ali ibn Hujr, from Isma'il ibn Ja'far, with the same chain, and said: "This is a hasan hadith."

Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn 'Uthman, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, before you call upon Him and you are not answered." He alone narrated it, and this 'Asim is unknown (majhul).

In the Sahih, through the route of al-A'mash, from Isma'il ibn Raja', from his father, from Sa'id — and from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri — who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is not able, then with his tongue; if he is not able, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith." Narrated by Muslim.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Sayf — he is Ibn Abi Sulayman — narrated to us: I heard 'Adi ibn 'Adi al-Kindi narrate from Mujahid, who said: A mawla of ours narrated to me that he heard my grandfather — meaning 'Adi ibn 'Umayrah, may Allah be pleased with him — say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah does not punish the common folk for the deed of the elite until they see the evil among them while they are able to denounce it, and they do not denounce it. When they do that, Allah punishes both the common folk and the elite."

Then Ahmad narrated it from Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sayf ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Adi ibn 'Adi al-Kindi: a mawla of ours narrated to me that he heard my grandfather say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, and he mentioned it. In this way Imam Ahmad narrated it through these two routes.

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Abu Bakr narrated to us, Mughirah ibn Ziyad al-Mawsili narrated to us, from 'Adi ibn 'Adi, from al-'Urs — meaning Ibn 'Umayrah — from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When a sin is committed on earth, whoever witnesses it and dislikes it — and he said once: and denounces it — is like one who was absent from it, and whoever was absent from it and approves of it is like one who witnessed it."

Abu Dawud alone narrated it, then he narrated it from Ahmad ibn Yunus, from Abu Shihab, from Mughirah ibn Ziyad, from 'Adi ibn 'Adi, as a mursal report.

And Abu Dawud said: Sulayman ibn Harb and Hafs ibn 'Umar narrated to us, both saying: Shu'bah narrated to us — and this is his wording — from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: One who heard the Prophet (ﷺ) informed me — and Sulayman said: a man from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) narrated to me — that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "People will not perish until they excuse themselves from themselves" — or: "until they excuse [their own faults]."

Ibn Majah said: 'Imran ibn Musa narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up delivering a sermon, and among what he said was: "Beware, let no man be prevented by fear of people from speaking the truth when he knows it." He said: Abu Sa'id wept and said: "By Allah, we have indeed seen things and feared."

In the hadith of Isra'il, from Muhammad ibn Hujadah, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best jihad is a word of truth before an unjust ruler."

Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah; al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib from this route."
