So Allah struck their hearts, one against another, and cursed them through the tongue of Dawud and Isa son of Maryam, because they disobeyed and used to transgress." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reclining, then he sat up and said: "No, by Him in whose hand is my soul, you must restrain them upon the truth, restraining them firmly."

Abu Dawud said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Nufayli narrated to us, Yunus ibn Rashid narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing that entered deficiency upon the Children of Israel was that a man would meet another man and say: 'O such-and-such, fear Allah and leave off what you are doing, for it is not lawful for you.' Then he would meet him the next day, and that would not prevent him from being his eating companion, drinking companion and sitting companion. When they did that, Allah struck their hearts, one against another, then He said: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of Dawud and Isa son of Maryam﴾ until His saying: ﴿defiantly disobedient﴾." Then he said: "No, by Allah, you must enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, and you must take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer and restrain him firmly upon the truth, or you will confine him to the truth by confining."

This is also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, through the route of 'Ali ibn Badhimah, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib." Then he and Ibn Majah narrated it from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, as a mursal report.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj and Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, both saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim al-Aftas, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man from the Children of Israel, when he saw his brother committing a sin, would forbid him from it out of admonition. Then the next day, what he had seen from him would not prevent him from being his eating companion, his associate and his partner — and in the narration of Harun: and his drinking companion — then they both agreed on the text. When Allah saw that from them, He struck their hearts, one against another, and cursed them upon the tongue of their Prophet Dawud and Isa son of Maryam, because they disobeyed and used to transgress." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is good, you must forbid what is evil, you must take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer, and you must restrain him firmly upon the truth, or Allah will strike your hearts, one against another, or He will curse you as He cursed them." The wording is that of Abu Sa'id. Thus he said in the narration of this hadith.

Abu Dawud also narrated it from Khalaf ibn Hisham, from Abu Shihab al-Khayyat, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim — he is Ibn 'Ijlan al-Aftas — from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording. Then Abu Dawud said: Khalid also narrated it similarly, from al-'Ala', from 'Amr ibn Murrah. And al-Muharibi narrated it from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim al-Aftas, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah.

Our shaykh, the Hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, said: Khalid ibn 'Abdullah al-Wasiti narrated it from al-'Ala', from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Musa.

The ahadith on enjoining good and forbidding evil are very numerous, and we shall mention from them what is suitable for this place.

The hadith of Jarir has already been mentioned at His saying: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 63]. And it will come at His saying: ﴿O you who believe, keep to yourselves; those who go astray will not harm you if you are guided﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105], the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani [may Allah be pleased with them both] — Imam Ahmad said:

Sulayman al-Hashimi narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us, 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr informed me, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ashhali, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, or Allah will shortly send upon you a punishment from Him, then you will call upon Him and He will not answer you."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Ali ibn Hujr, from Isma'il ibn Ja'far, with the same chain, and said: "This is a hasan hadith."

Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn 'Uthman, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, before you call upon Him and you are not answered." He alone narrated it, and this 'Asim is unknown (majhul).

In the Sahih, through the route of al-A'mash, from Isma'il ibn Raja', from his father, from Sa'id — and from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri — who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is not able, then with his tongue; if he is not able, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith." Narrated by Muslim.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Sayf — he is Ibn Abi Sulayman — narrated to us: I heard 'Adi ibn 'Adi al-Kindi narrate from Mujahid, who said: A mawla of ours narrated to me that he heard my grandfather — meaning 'Adi ibn 'Umayrah, may Allah be pleased with him — say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah does not punish the common folk for the deed of the elite until they see the evil among them while they are able to denounce it, and they do not denounce it. When they do that, Allah punishes both the common folk and the elite."

Then Ahmad narrated it from Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sayf ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Adi ibn 'Adi al-Kindi: a mawla of ours narrated to me that he heard my grandfather say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, and he mentioned it. In this way Imam Ahmad narrated it through these two routes.

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Abu Bakr narrated to us, Mughirah ibn Ziyad al-Mawsili narrated to us, from 'Adi ibn 'Adi, from al-'Urs — meaning Ibn 'Umayrah — from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When a sin is committed on earth, whoever witnesses it and dislikes it — and he said once: and denounces it — is like one who was absent from it, and whoever was absent from it and approves of it is like one who witnessed it."

Abu Dawud alone narrated it, then he narrated it from Ahmad ibn Yunus, from Abu Shihab, from Mughirah ibn Ziyad, from 'Adi ibn 'Adi, as a mursal report.

And Abu Dawud said: Sulayman ibn Harb and Hafs ibn 'Umar narrated to us, both saying: Shu'bah narrated to us — and this is his wording — from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: One who heard the Prophet (ﷺ) informed me — and Sulayman said: a man from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) narrated to me — that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "People will not perish until they excuse themselves from themselves" — or: "until they excuse [their own faults]."

Ibn Majah said: 'Imran ibn Musa narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up delivering a sermon, and among what he said was: "Beware, let no man be prevented by fear of people from speaking the truth when he knows it." He said: Abu Sa'id wept and said: "By Allah, we have indeed seen things and feared."

In the hadith of Isra'il, from Muhammad ibn Hujadah, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best jihad is a word of truth before an unjust ruler."

Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah; al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib from this route."

Ibn Majah said: Rashid ibn Sa'id al-Ramli narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: A man confronted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the first pillar (jamrah) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, which jihad is best?" He remained silent. When he threw the second pillar, he asked him again, and he remained silent. When he threw the Jamrat al-'Aqabah and placed his foot in the stirrup to mount, he said: "Where is the questioner?" He said: "I am here, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "A word of truth spoken before an unjust ruler." He alone narrated it.

Ibn Majah said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from

**Ibn Abi Sa'id** (ﷺ's companion Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, رضي الله عنه) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "None of you should belittle himself." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does one of us belittle himself?" He said: "He sees a matter concerning Allah about which he has something to say, but then does not say it. Then Allah will say to him on the Day of Resurrection: 'What prevented you from saying such-and-such about Me?' He will say: 'The fear of people.' Then He will say: 'It was Me that you had more right to fear.'" Ibn Majah alone narrated it. [Footnote: Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4008. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/242): "This chain is sahih."]

He also said: Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman Abu Tuwalah narrated to us, Nahar al-Abdi narrated to us, that he heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah will indeed question the servant on the Day of Resurrection, until He says: 'What prevented you, when you saw the evil, from denouncing it?' And when Allah makes the servant forget his argument, he will say: 'O Lord, I hoped in You, and I feared people.'" Ibn Majah alone narrated it too, and its isnad (chain of narration) is acceptable. [Footnote: Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4017. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/244): "This chain is sahih."]

Imam Ahmad said: Amr ibn Asim narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Hasan, from Jundab, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It is not befitting for a Muslim to humiliate himself." It was said: "And how does he humiliate himself?" He said: "By exposing himself to trials he cannot bear."

At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah both narrated it in the same way, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Amr ibn Asim, with this chain. At-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith." [Footnote: Musnad Ahmad (5/405), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2254, and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4016.]

Ibn Majah said: Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Zayd ibn Yahya ibn Ubayd al-Khuza'i narrated to us, al-Haytham ibn Humayd narrated to us, Abu Ma'bad Hafs ibn Ghaylan al-Ru'ayni narrated to us, from Makhul, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, when will enjoining good and forbidding evil be abandoned?" He said: "When there appears among you what appeared among the nations before you." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what appeared among the nations before us?" He said: "Kingship among your young, immorality among your elders, and knowledge among your lowly." Zayd said: The meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) words "and knowledge among your lowly" is: when knowledge is found among the wicked (fussaq).

Ibn Majah alone narrated it. [Footnote: Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4015. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/244): "This chain is sahih and its narrators are trustworthy."] The evidence for this will come in the hadith of Abu Tha'labah, at the words of Allah: ﴿لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ مَنْ ضَلَّ إِذَا اهْتَدَيْتُمْ﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105], if Allah wills, and with Him is trust.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Thou seest many of them turning in friendship to those who disbelieve﴾. Mujahid said: By this He means the hypocrites.

As for His words: ﴿Evil indeed is what their souls have sent forward for them﴾, He means by it their friendship with the disbelievers and their abandonment of friendship with the believers, which resulted in hypocrisy in their hearts and provoked Allah's wrath against them, a continuous wrath until the day they return. Therefore He said: ﴿that Allah's wrath is upon them﴾, explaining the reason for which He censured them. Then He informed that ﴿in torment they will abide forever﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Maslamah ibn Ali narrated to us, from al-A'mash, with an isnad that he mentioned, who said: "O assembly of Muslims, beware of adultery, for it has six characteristics: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for the ones in this world: it removes radiance, brings poverty, and shortens life. As for the ones in the Hereafter: it brings on the Lord's wrath, evil reckoning, and eternal abode in the Fire." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Evil indeed is what their souls have sent forward for them, that Allah's wrath is upon them, and in torment they will abide forever﴾.

Thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn Ammar, from Maslamah, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned it. He also cited it through the route of Sa'id ibn Ghufayr, from Maslamah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Kufi, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar.

This hadith is weak in every case, and Allah knows best. [Footnote: Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (6/317) through these two routes, saying: (1) Abdan narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Maslamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, with it. (2) Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Bayan narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Ufayr narrated to us, Maslamah ibn Ali narrated to us, from Abu Ali al-Kufi, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, something similar. Then he said: "This from al-A'mash is not preserved, and it is munkar. Ibn Ufayr and Hisham differed in its isnad: Hisham said 'from Maslamah, from al-A'mash,' while Ibn Ufayr said 'from Maslamah, from Abu Ali al-Kufi, from al-A'mash,' and Abu Ali is unknown. This hadith is also narrated from Abd Allah ibn Usmah al-Nusaybi, from Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Bunani, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ). These hadiths are not preserved."]

Then He said: ﴿And had they believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies﴾, meaning: had they believed in Allah, His messengers and the Criterion (al-Furqan) with true belief, they would not have committed what they committed of befriending the disbelievers inwardly and opposing the believers. ﴿But many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: they have departed from obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and they oppose the verses of His revelation and His sending down.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 82–86:

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: These verses were revealed concerning the Negus (al-Najashi) and his companions, who, when Ja'far ibn Abi Talib recited the Qur'an to them in Abyssinia, wept until their beards were drenched. But this view is questionable, because this verse is Medinan, while the story of Ja'far with the Negus took place before the Hijrah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi and others said: It was revealed concerning a delegation that the Negus sent to the Prophet ﷺ to hear his speech and see his qualities. When the Prophet ﷺ recited the Qur'an to them, they embraced Islam, wept and humbled themselves. Then they returned to the Negus and informed him.

al-Suddi said: So the Negus emigrated and died on the way.

This is a view held by al-Suddi alone, for the Negus died while he was the king of Abyssinia. The Prophet ﷺ prayed the funeral prayer over him on the day he died, informed his companions of it, and told them that he had died in the land of Abyssinia.

Then there was disagreement about the number of this delegation. It was said: twelve, seven priests (qasawisah) and five monks (rahabin). It was said the reverse. It was said: fifty. It was said: sixty-some. It was said: seventy men. And Allah knows best.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: They were a people from among the people of Abyssinia who embraced Islam when the Muslim emigrants to Abyssinia came to them. Qatadah said: They were a people who followed the religion of 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary), and when they saw the Muslims and heard the Qur'an, they embraced Islam without hesitation. Ibn Jarir preferred the view that this verse was revealed describing peoples of this kind, whether they were from Abyssinia or elsewhere.

So His saying ﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate partners with Allah﴾ is only because the disbelief of the Jews is obstinacy, denial, and defiant rejection of the truth, and contempt for people and belittling of the bearers of knowledge. For this reason they killed many of the prophets, and they resolved more than once to kill the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they practiced sorcery against him, and they incited against him their counterparts among the polytheists, upon them be Allah's successive curses until the Day of Resurrection.

The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh, commenting on this verse, said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sarri related to us: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Habib al-Raqqi related to us: Sa'id al-'Allaf ibn al-'Allaf related to us: Abu al-Nadr related to us, from al-Ashja'i, from Sufyan, from Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No Jew is ever alone with a Muslim without intending to kill him."

Then he narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Yashkuri: Ahmad ibn Sahl ibn Ayyub al-Ahwazi related to us: Faraj ibn 'Ubayd related to us: 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam related to us, from Yahya ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No Jew is ever alone with a Muslim but that his soul speaks to him of killing him." And this is an extremely strange hadith. [[Ibn Hibban narrated it in al-Majruhin (3/122) by way of Yahya ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, and said: "Yahya ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Mawhab al-Qurashi narrates from his father what has no basis. When this became frequent from him, he was dropped from being used as evidence."

al-Khatib al-Baghdadi narrated it in Tarikh Baghdad (8/316) by another route: by way of Jarir ibn Hazim, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "This is an extremely strange hadith from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Sirin from Abu Hurayrah, and from the hadith of Jarir ibn Hazim from Ibn Sirin; I have only written it from the hadith of Khalid ibn Yazid, from Wahb ibn Jarir."]]

His saying: ﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection toward those who believe those who say, "We are Christians"﴾ means those who claimed to be Christians, followers of the Messiah and upon the method of his Gospel. There is in them affection for Islam and its people in general, and that is only because of what is in their hearts, since they followed the religion of the Messiah, with its tenderness and compassion, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy﴾ [al-Hadid: 27]. And in their scripture: "Whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the left." Fighting is not prescribed in their religion. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is because among them are qissisin (priests) and monks, and because they are not arrogant﴾. That is, there are found among them the qissisin, who are their preachers and scholars. Its singular is qissis and also qass, and it may be plural qusus. The rahban (monks) is the plural of rahib, which means the worshipper, derived from rahbah (fear), as rakib is pluralized as rukban, and faris as furisan.

Ibn Jarir said: Rahban may be singular, and its plural is rahabin, like qurban and qarabin, and jurdan and jaradin. It may also be pluralized as rahabinah. As evidence that among the Arabs it is singular, the poet said:

Had they seen the monks of a monastery upon the heights,
the monk would have come down, walking and descending.

al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Bishr ibn Adam related to us: Nusayr ibn Abi al-Ash'ath related to us: al-Salt al-Dhahhan related to me, from Hamiyah ibn Ri'ab, who said: I asked Salman about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿That is because among them are qissisin and monks﴾. He said: Leave "qissisin" in the churches and the ruins. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited to me: "That is because among them are siddiqin (truthful ones) and monks." [[al-Bukhari narrated it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (8/116) by way of Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham, from Nusayr ibn Ziyad with the same.]]

Likewise Ibn Mardawayh narrated it by way of Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani, from Nusayr ibn Ziyad al-Ta'i, from Salt al-Dhahhan, from Hamiyah ibn Ri'ab, from Salman, with the same.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father mentioned it: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani related to us: Nusayr ibn Ziyad al-Ta'i related to us: Salt al-Dhahhan related to us, from Hamiyah ibn Ri'ab, who said: I heard Salman, and he was asked about His saying: ﴿That is because among them are qissisin and monks﴾, and he said: They are the monks who are in the monasteries and ruins, so call them in there. Salman said: I recited to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿That is because among them are qissisin and monks﴾, and he corrected me: "That is because among them are siddiqin and monks." [[al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/266) by way of Yahya al-Hammani with the same. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/17): "In it are Yahya al-Hammani and Nusayr ibn Ziyad, and both are weak."]]

So His saying: ﴿That is because among them are qissisin and monks, and because they are not arrogant﴾ includes describing them as having knowledge, worship and humility. Then He described them with submission to the truth, following it and fairness, saying: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth﴾, that is, from what is in their possession of the glad tidings of the sending of Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses"﴾, that is, among those who testify to the truth of this and believe in it.

al-Nasa'i narrated from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, from 'Umar ibn 'Ali ibn Muqaddam, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the Negus and his companions: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."﴾ [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11148).]]

al-Tabarani said: Abu Shubayl 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Waqid related to us: my father related to us: al-'Abbas ibn al-Fadl related to us, from 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Nafi' al-Dabbi, from Qatadah and Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning Allah's saying: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears﴾. He said: They were karabin, that is, farmers, who came with Ja'far ibn Abi Talib from Abyssinia. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the Qur'an to them, they believed and their eyes overflowed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Perhaps when you return to your land you will turn back to your religion." They said: "We will never turn away from our religion." So Allah revealed that statement of theirs. [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/55). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/18): "In it is al-'Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Ansari, who is weak."]]

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated by way of Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿So register us among the witnesses﴾, that is, with Muhammad ﷺ, and his community are the witnesses; they testify for their Prophet that he has conveyed, and for the messengers that they conveyed. Then al-Hakim said: Its isnad is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it. [[al-Mustadrak (2/313).]]

﴿And why should we not believe in Allah and what has come to us of the truth, while we aspire that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people?﴾ This category of Christians is the one mentioned in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submissive to Allah, not exchanging the verses of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord; indeed, Allah is swift in account﴾ [Al 'Imran: 199], and they are those about whom Allah said: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it, they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We believed in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed we were Muslims before it." Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and from what We have provided them, they spend. And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace be upon you; we do not seek the ignorant"﴾ [al-Qasas: 52–55]. That is, there are found among them the qissisin, who are their preachers and scholars. Its singular is qissis and also qass, and it may be plural qusus. Had they seen the monks of a monastery upon the heights,

al-Nasa'i narrated from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, from 'Umar ibn 'Ali ibn Muqaddam, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the Negus and his companions: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. Then al-Hakim said: Its isnad is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it. [[al-Mustadrak (2/313).]]

﴿And why should we not believe in Allah and what has come to us of the truth, while we aspire that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people?﴾ This category of Christians is the one mentioned in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submissive to Allah, not exchanging the verses of Allah for a small price. Then He informed about the state of the wretched, saying: ﴿But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs﴾, that is, they rejected them and opposed them, ﴿those are the companions of Hellfire﴾, that is, they are its people and those who enter it.

But this view is questionable, because this verse is Medinan, while the story of Ja'far with the Negus took place before the Hijrah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi and others said: It was revealed concerning a delegation that the Negus sent to the Prophet ﷺ to hear his speech and see his qualities. When the Prophet ﷺ recited the Qur'an to them, they embraced Islam, wept and humbled themselves. Then they returned to the Negus and informed him.

al-Suddi said: So the Negus emigrated and died on the way.

This is a view held by al-Suddi alone, for the Negus died while he was the king of Abyssinia. The Prophet ﷺ prayed the funeral prayer over him on the day he died, informed his companions of it, and told them that he had died in the land of Abyssinia.

Then there was disagreement about the number of this delegation. It was said: twelve, seven priests (qasawisah) and five monks (rahabin). It was said the reverse. It was said: fifty. It was said: sixty-some. It was said: seventy men. And Allah knows best.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: They were a people from among the people of Abyssinia who embraced Islam when the Muslim emigrants to Abyssinia came to them. Qatadah said: They were a people who followed the religion of 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary), and when they saw the Muslims and heard the Qur'an, they embraced Islam without hesitation. Ibn Jarir preferred the view that this verse was revealed describing peoples of this kind, whether they were from Abyssinia or elsewhere.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 87–88 (part 1 of 2):

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "We will castrate ourselves (naqta'u madhakirana), abandon the desires of this world, and wander through the earth as the monks do." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), who sent for them and mentioned this to them. They said: "Yes." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "But I fast and I break my fast, I pray and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever follows my Sunnah is of me, and whoever does not follow my Sunnah is not of me." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar report from Ibn 'Abbas through the route of al-'Awfi.

In the Sahihayn (the two Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim), from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) about his practice in private. Some of them said: "I will not eat meat." Some said: "I will not marry women." Some said: "I will not sleep on a bed." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "What is the matter with people who say such and such? But I fast and I break my fast, I sleep and I stand in prayer, I eat meat and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."

[[This is the wording of the hadith of Anas ibn Malik: al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih, no. (5063), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1401). As for the hadith of 'A'ishah, its wording is: The Prophet (ﷺ) did something permitted in which some people allowed themselves latitude and others avoided it. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), so he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "What is the matter with people who avoid things that I do? By Allah, I am the most knowledgeable of them about Allah and the most fearful of Him." Narrated by al-Bukhari, no. (7301), and Muslim, no. (2356).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn 'Isam al-Ansari narrated to us, Abu 'Asim al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from 'Uthman (i.e., Ibn Sa'd): Ikrimah informed me, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, when I eat meat, I become aroused towards women, and I have made meat forbidden to myself." So the verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾.

At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir both narrated it likewise, from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, from Abu 'Asim al-Nabil, with this chain.

At-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib." [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (3054).]] It has been narrated through another route as a mursal (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion), and it has been narrated as a mawquf (a report ending at a Companion's statement) attributed to Ibn 'Abbas. And Allah knows best.

Sufyan al-Thawri and Waki' said, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "We used to campaign with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and there were no women with us. So we said: 'Shall we not have ourselves castrated?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade us from that, and he permitted us to marry a woman with a garment for a set term." Then 'Abdullah recited: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you [and do not transgress; indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors]﴾. [[The addition is from R and A; in H it reads: "the verse".]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Isma'il.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4615), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1404).]] This was before the prohibition of temporary marriage (nikah al-mut'ah), and Allah knows best.

Al-A'mash said, from Ibrahim, from Hammam ibn al-Harith, from 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, who said: Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin came to 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and said: "I have forbidden my bed to myself." So he recited this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you [and do not transgress; indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors]﴾. [[The addition is from R and A; in H it reads: "the verse".]]

Al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: "We were with 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud when a dish of meat (dar') was brought. A man drew back, and 'Abdullah said to him, [to him] [[addition from A.]]: 'Come near.' He said: 'I have forbidden myself to eat it.' 'Abdullah said: 'Come near and eat, and make expiation for your oath,' and he recited this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾, to the end of the verse."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated all of these. Al-Hakim narrated this last report in his Mustadrak, through the route of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, from Jarir, from Mansur, with the same chain. Then he said: "It is according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not include it." [[al-Mustadrak (2/313).]]

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd informed me, that Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to him: that 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah hosted a guest from his family while he was with the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he returned to his family and found that they had not fed their guest, waiting for him. So he said to his wife: "You have held back my guest on my account; it is forbidden to me." His wife said: "It is forbidden to me." The guest said: "It is forbidden to me." When he saw this, he put his hand (to the food) and said: "Eat in the name of Allah." Then he went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned what had happened between them. Then Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾. This is a report with a broken chain (athar munqati').[[Mentioned by as-Suyuti in ad-Durr al-Manthur (3/143).]]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, in the story of al-Siddiq [may Allah be pleased with him] [[addition from A.]] with his guests, there is something similar to this, and in it [occurs the text].[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6140).]] In this story is evidence for those scholars, such as al-Shafi'i and others, who hold that whoever forbids a food, a garment, or anything else apart from women, it does not become forbidden to him, and there is no expiation (kaffarah) upon him either. This is based on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾; and because the one who forbade meat to himself, as in the hadith mentioned earlier, was not commanded by the Prophet (ﷺ) to make expiation.

Others, including the Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, held that whoever forbids a food or drink or any other thing, it becomes obligatory upon him to pay the expiation for an oath (kaffarat yamin), just as when one binds himself to abstaining from something by an oath. Thus he is held accountable for merely forbidding it upon himself, as a means of binding him to what he committed himself to, just as Ibn 'Abbas gave this ruling. This is like the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [At-Tahrim: 1]. Then He said: ﴿Allah has already prescribed for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾ and so on [At-Tahrim: 2]. Likewise here, when He mentioned this ruling, He followed it with the verse that explains the expiation for oaths. This indicates that this is treated as an oath with regard to the requirement of expiation. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 87–88 (part 1 of 2):

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "We will castrate ourselves (naqta'u madhakirana), abandon the desires of this world, and wander through the earth as the monks do." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), who sent for them and mentioned this to them. They said: "Yes." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "But I fast and I break my fast, I pray and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever follows my Sunnah is of me, and whoever does not follow my Sunnah is not of me." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar report from Ibn 'Abbas through the route of al-'Awfi.

In the Sahihayn (the two Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim), from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) about his practice in private. Some of them said: "I will not eat meat." Some said: "I will not marry women." Some said: "I will not sleep on a bed." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "What is the matter with people who say such and such? But I fast and I break my fast, I sleep and I stand in prayer, I eat meat and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."

[[This is the wording of the hadith of Anas ibn Malik: al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih, no. (5063), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1401). As for the hadith of 'A'ishah, its wording is: The Prophet (ﷺ) did something permitted in which some people allowed themselves latitude and others avoided it. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), so he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "What is the matter with people who avoid things that I do? By Allah, I am the most knowledgeable of them about Allah and the most fearful of Him." Narrated by al-Bukhari, no. (7301), and Muslim, no. (2356).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn 'Isam al-Ansari narrated to us, Abu 'Asim al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from 'Uthman (i.e., Ibn Sa'd): Ikrimah informed me, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, when I eat meat, I become aroused towards women, and I have made meat forbidden to myself." So the verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾.

At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir both narrated it likewise, from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, from Abu 'Asim al-Nabil, with this chain.

At-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib." [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (3054).]] It has been narrated through another route as a mursal (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion), and it has been narrated as a mawquf (a report ending at a Companion's statement) attributed to Ibn 'Abbas. And Allah knows best.

Sufyan al-Thawri and Waki' said, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "We used to campaign with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and there were no women with us. So we said: 'Shall we not have ourselves castrated?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade us from that, and he permitted us to marry a woman with a garment for a set term." Then 'Abdullah recited: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you [and do not transgress; indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors]﴾. [[The addition is from R and A; in H it reads: "the verse".]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Isma'il.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4615), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1404).]] This was before the prohibition of temporary marriage (nikah al-mut'ah), and Allah knows best.

Al-A'mash said, from Ibrahim, from Hammam ibn al-Harith, from 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, who said: Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin came to 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and said: "I have forbidden my bed to myself." So he recited this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you [and do not transgress; indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors]﴾. [[The addition is from R and A; in H it reads: "the verse".]]

A man drew back, and 'Abdullah said to him, [to him] [[addition from A.]]: 'Come near.' He said: 'I have forbidden myself to eat it.' 'Abdullah said: 'Come near and eat, and make expiation for your oath,' and he recited this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾, to the end of the verse."

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd informed me, that Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to him: that 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah hosted a guest from his family while he was with the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he returned to his family and found that they had not fed their guest, waiting for him. So he said to his wife: "You have held back my guest on my account; it is forbidden to me." His wife said: "It is forbidden to me." The guest said: "It is forbidden to me." When he saw this, he put his hand (to the food) and said: "Eat in the name of Allah." Then he went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned what had happened between them. Then Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾. This is a report with a broken chain (athar munqati').[[Mentioned by as-Suyuti in ad-Durr al-Manthur (3/143).]]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, in the story of al-Siddiq [may Allah be pleased with him] [[addition from A.]] with his guests, there is something similar to this, and in it [occurs the text].[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6140).]] In this story is evidence for those scholars, such as al-Shafi'i and others, who hold that whoever forbids a food, a garment, or anything else apart from women, it does not become forbidden to him, and there is no expiation (kaffarah) upon him either. This is based on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾; and because the one who forbade meat to himself, as in the hadith mentioned earlier, was not commanded by the Prophet (ﷺ) to make expiation.

Thus he is held accountable for merely forbidding it upon himself, as a means of binding him to what he committed himself to, just as Ibn 'Abbas gave this ruling. This is like the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [At-Tahrim: 1]. Then He said: ﴿Allah has already prescribed for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾ and so on [At-Tahrim: 2]. Ibn Kathir's Commentary on Surah 5, verse 89 (part 1 of 2)

It has already been discussed in Surah al-Baqarah what "lagh al-yamin" (the idle oath) is: it is a person's saying in speech without intention, "No, by Allah," or "Yes, by Allah." This is the position of al-Shafi'i. It has also been said that it is an oath in jest. It has been said that it is an oath in disobedience. It has been said that it is an oath based on a strong assumption, and this is the view of Abu Hanifah and Ahmad. It has been said that it is an oath made in anger. It has been said that it is an oath made in forgetfulness. It has been said that it is swearing to abstain from food, drink, clothing and the like, and they cite His saying: ﴿Do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you﴾.

The correct view is that it is an oath made without intention, based on His saying: ﴿But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have sworn deliberately﴾, meaning, for the oaths you have resolved upon and intended. Its expiation is feeding ten needy people, meaning poor people in need, and those who do not have enough to suffice them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿From the middle [standard] of what you feed your families﴾, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ikrimah said: that is, from the most moderate of what you feed your families.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: from the best of what you feed your families. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, who said: bread and milk, bread and ghee.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la informed us by reading, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Sulayman, that is Ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man would provide some of his family with a meager sustenance and others with ample provision, so Allah the Exalted said: ﴿From the middle of what you feed your families﴾, that is: from bread and olive oil.

Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj also narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from 'Amir, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿From the middle of what you feed your families﴾, he said: from their hardship and their ease.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalaf al-Himsi also narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, that is Ibn Shabur, narrated to us, Shayban ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Tamimi narrated to us, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from a man called 'Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn 'Umar that he said: ﴿From the middle of what you feed your families﴾, he said: bread and meat, bread and ghee, bread and milk, bread and olive oil, and bread and vinegar.

'Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili also narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Umar regarding His saying: ﴿From the middle of what you feed your families﴾, he said: bread and ghee, bread and olive oil, and bread and dates. And the best of what you feed your families is: bread and meat.

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Hannad and Ibn Waki', both of them from Abu Mu'awiyah. Then Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Ubaydah, al-Aswad, Shurayh al-Qadi, Muhammad ibn Sirin, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Abu Razin that they said something similar to that. Ibn Abi Hatim also related it from Makhul.

Ibn Jarir chose that what is meant by His saying: ﴿From the middle of what you feed your families﴾ is: in quantity and in quality (in the lesser and the greater amount).

Then the scholars differed regarding the quantity with which they feed them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Husayn al-Harithi, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Harith, from 'Ali [may Allah be pleased with him] regarding His saying: ﴿From the middle of what you feed your families﴾, he said: he feeds them at morning and evening.

Al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Sirin said: it suffices for him to feed ten needy people one meal, of bread and meat. Al-Hasan added: if he does not find (meat), then bread and ghee and milk; if he does not find that, then bread and olive oil and vinegar, until they are satisfied.

Others said: he feeds each one of the ten half a sa' of wheat or dates, or the like. This is the view of 'Umar, 'Ali, 'A'ishah, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Maymun ibn Mihran, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, al-Hakam, Makhul, Abu Qilabah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Abu Hanifah said: half a sa' of wheat, and one sa' of anything else.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Thaqafi narrated to us, 'Ubayd ibn al-Hasan ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Tufayl ibn Sakhbarah, the maternal nephew of 'A'ishah, narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Ya'la narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made expiation with one sa' of dates and commanded the people with it, and whoever does not find it, then half a sa' of wheat.

Ibn Majah also narrated it, from al-'Abbas ibn Yazid, from Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bakka'i, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ya'la al-Thaqafi, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, with it. [Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2112.]

This hadith is not authentic, because of the condition of this 'Umar ibn 'Abd Allah, for he is agreed to be weak, and they mention that he used to drink wine. Al-Daraqutni said: matruk (abandoned).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Dawud, that is Ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: one mudd of wheat, that is for each needy person, along with its condiment.

Then he said: It is narrated from Ibn 'Umar, Zayd ibn Thabit, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Mujahid, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, Abu al-Sha'tha', al-Qasim, Salim, Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, Sulayman ibn Yasar, al-Hasan, Muhammad ibn Sirin and al-Zuhri, something similar to that.

Al-Shafi'i said: what is obligatory in the expiation of an oath is one mudd by the mudd of the Prophet ﷺ for each needy person. He did not address condiments. He argued by the Prophet's ﷺ command to the one who had intercourse during Ramadan to feed sixty needy people from a measure that holds fifteen sa', giving each of them one mudd.

Another hadith explicit on this has also been transmitted. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Muqri narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj narrated to us, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Zurarah al-Kufi narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-'Umari, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pay the expiation of an oath with one mudd of wheat by the first mudd.

Its chain is weak, because of the condition of al-Nadr ibn Zurarah ibn 'Abd al-Akram al-Dhuhli al-Kufi, a resident of Balkh. Abu Hatim al-Razi said of him: he is unknown, although more than one has narrated from him. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy and said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated from him some sound things. Allah knows best. Then his shaykh al-'Umari is also weak.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: what is obligatory is one mudd of wheat, or two mudds of other things. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿or clothing them﴾, al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: if each one of the ten is given what truly qualifies as clothing, such as a shirt, trousers, a wrap, a turban or a head-covering, it suffices. His companions differed regarding the skullcap: whether it suffices or not, on two views. Some of them held that it is permissible, citing what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated:

Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj and 'Ammar ibn Khalid al-Wasiti both said: al-Qasim ibn Malik narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, who said: I asked 'Imran ibn Husayn about His saying: ﴿or clothing them﴾, and he said: If a delegation came to your ruler and he clothed them, a skullcap each, you would say: They have been clothed.

But this is a weak chain, because of the condition of this Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr. And Allah knows best. Likewise Shaykh Abu Hamid al-Isfara'ini related two views concerning the khuff (leather sock), and the sound view is that it does not suffice.

Malik and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: one must give each of them as much clothing as is valid for him to pray in, whether a man or a woman, each according to his circumstance. And Allah knows best.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: a cloak for each needy person, or a woolen garment.

Mujahid said: the least is a garment, and the most is whatever you wish.

Layth narrated from Mujahid: in the expiation of an oath anything suffices except the tubban (loose underwear).

Al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, 'Ata', Tawus, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman and Abu Malik said: one garment each.

Also from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i: a comprehensive garment, like a wrap or a mantle, and a coat of mail, a shirt or a khimar and the like are not considered comprehensive.

Al-Ansari narrated from Ash'ath, from Ibn Sirin and al-Hasan: two garments.

Al-Thawri narrated from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: a turban with which he wraps his head, and a cloak with which he wraps himself.

Ibn Jarir said: Hannad narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Musa: that he swore an oath and clothed two garments of Mu'aqqadah from Bahrain.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Mu'alla narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Sulayman, from Abu 'Uthman, from Abu 'Iyad, from 'A'ishah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding His saying: ﴿or clothing them﴾, he said: "A cloak for each needy person." [In its chain is Muqatil ibn Sulayman al-Balkhi, whom Waki' and al-Nasa'i declared a liar. al-Bukhari said: they remained silent about him. And Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash's narrations from non-Syrians are weak.] It is a strange hadith.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿or the freeing of a slave﴾, Abu Hanifah took its wording in its general sense and said: a disbelieving slave suffices just as a believing slave suffices. Al-Shafi'i and others said: it must be a believer. They took the restriction to faith from the expiation of killing, because the obligation is the same even though the cause differs, and from the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami, which is in the Muwatta' of Malik, the Musnad of al-Shafi'i and Sahih Muslim: that he mentioned that he owed the freeing of a slave, and he brought with him a black slave girl. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Where is Allah?" She said: In heaven. He said: "Who am I?" She said: You are the Messenger of Allah. He said: "Free her, for she is a believer." The hadith in full. [Muwatta' (2/777), Musnad al-Shafi'i no. 1196 (Bada'i' al-Minan), and Sahih Muslim no. 537.]

These are three options in the expiation of an oath: whichever of them the one who broke the oath does, it suffices for him by consensus. It begins with the easiest, then the easier: feeding is easier than clothing, just as clothing is easier than freeing, so it ascends from the lower to the higher. If the responsible person is unable to do any of these three, he expiates by fasting three days, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So whoever does not find [the means], then fasting three days﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan al-Basri that both of them said: whoever has three dirhams is obliged to feed; otherwise he fasts.

Ibn Jarir also said, reporting from some of the later jurists of his time, that he said: it is permissible for one who has no surplus beyond the capital with which he earns his livelihood to fast rather than feed as expiation, unless he has sufficiency and, from his wealth, what he uses for his livelihood, and from the surplus beyond that, what he expiates his oath with.

Then Ibn Jarir chose: that it is the one who has no surplus beyond his sustenance [[In A: "his maintenance" (mu'natahu).]] and the sustenance of his dependents on that day, from which he can pay the expiation of the oath. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (10/559).]]

The scholars differed: is consecutiveness (tatabu') obligatory in it, or is it recommended, with separation (tafriq) being permissible? There are two opinions. The first is that consecutiveness is not obligatory. This is the explicit statement of al-Shafi'i in the book "al-Ayman" (Oaths), and it is the view of Malik, based on the unrestricted wording of His saying: ﴿So fasting for three days﴾, and this applies both to the consecutive and the separated, as in making up the fast of Ramadan, based on His saying: ﴿then a number of other days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 184].

Al-Shafi'i stated in another place, in "al-Umm," that consecutiveness is obligatory, as is the view of the Hanafis and the Hanbalis, because it has been narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and others that they used to recite it: "So fasting three days consecutively" (fasiyam thalathati ayyamin mutatabi'at).

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he used to recite it: "So fasting three days consecutively."

Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, and Abu Ishaq related it from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.

Ibrahim said: In the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "So fasting three days consecutively."

Al-A'mash said: The companions of Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it like that.

If it is not established that this is Qur'an (mutawatir), then it is at least a single report (khabar wahid), or an explanation from a Companion, and it has the ruling of a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ).

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Ash'ari [[In A: "Ahmad".]] narrated to us, al-Haytham ibn Khalid al-Qurashi narrated to us, Yazid ibn Qays narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Yahya, from Ibn Abbas who said: When the verse of the expiations was revealed, Hudhayfah said: "O Messenger of Allah, do we have a choice?" He said: "You have a choice: if you wish, free a slave; if you wish, clothe; if you wish, feed; but whoever cannot find [the means], then fasting three days consecutively."

This is a very strange (gharib jiddan) hadith. [[Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/155) and did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Mardawayh. I think "Yazid ibn Qays" is "Yazid ibn Qays" and that it is corrupted here; and Isma'il ibn Yahya is Ibn Ubayd Allah, who used to fabricate hadith. Ibn Adi said: most of what he narrates is falsehoods. Furthermore, the chain is mu'dal (with two consecutive omissions), for between him and Ibn Abbas there is roughly a century.]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿That is the expiation of your oaths when you swear. And guard your oaths﴾. Ibn Jarir said: its meaning is: do not leave them without expiation. ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses﴾, i.e., He clarifies them and spreads them [[In R and A: "and explains them" (wa yufassiruha).]] ﴿so that you may be grateful﴾.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 5, verses 90–93 (part 1 of 4):

He, may He be exalted, says, forbidding His believing servants from indulging in wine (khamr) and gambling (maysir), which is qimar.

It has been reported from the Commander of the Faithful, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he said: "Chess (shatranj) is of the maysir." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from 'Ubays ibn Marhum, from Hatim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Ali, with it.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi (in manuscript A: "al-A'mashi") narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from 'Ata', Mujahid and Tawus — Sufyan said: "or two of them" — they said: "Everything of gambling is of the maysir, even children's play with walnuts."

It is also reported from Rashid ibn Sa'd and Hamzah ibn Habib (in manuscript A: "Habib similarly"), and they said: "Even knucklebones (ka'ab), walnuts, and the eggs with which children play." Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "The maysir is qimar."

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The maysir is qimar. They used to gamble in the Jahiliyyah until Islam came, so Allah forbade them these ugly behaviours."

Malik narrated from Dawud ibn al-Husayn that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: "The maysir of the people of the Jahiliyyah was selling meat for a sheep or two sheep."

Al-Zuhri narrated from al-A'raj, who said: "The maysir is also casting arrows (darb bil-qidah) for goods and fruits."

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: "Everything that distracts from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer is of the maysir."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated all of these.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: Sadaqah narrated to us: 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'Atikah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Avoid these marked knucklebones with which one is driven away by divination, for they are of the maysir." This is a gharib hadith. [Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned it in al-'Ilal (2/297), and said: "My father said: This hadith is baseless (batil); it comes from 'Ali ibn Yazid, while 'Uthman is not objectionable."]

It seems that what is meant here is nard (backgammon), which is mentioned in a hadith in Sahih Muslim, from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever plays with nardashir, it is as if he dipped his hand in the flesh and blood of swine." [Sahih Muslim, no. 2260.] Also in the Muwatta' of Malik, the Musnad of Ahmad, and the Sunan of Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever plays with nard has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger." [Muwatta' (2/958), Musnad (4/394), Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4938, Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3762.] It has also been reported as a statement of Abu Musa himself (mawquf), and Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us (in manuscript A: "'Ali ibn Ibrahim," which is an error): al-Ju'ayd narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Khatmi, that he heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b, while he was asking 'Abd al-Rahman: "Tell me, what did you hear your father say from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" 'Abd al-Rahman said: "I heard my father say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The likeness of one who plays with nard and then stands and prays is like the likeness of one who performs ablution with pus and the blood of swine and then stands and prays.'" [Musnad (5/370). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/113): "In it is Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Khatmi, whom I do not know; the rest of Ahmad's narrators are sahih narrators."]

As for chess (shatranj), 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar said: "It is worse than nard." And it has preceded from 'Ali that he said: "It is of the maysir." Malik, Abu Hanifah and Ahmad explicitly stated its prohibition, and al-Shafi'i disliked it, may Allah have mercy on them.

As for the ansab (idols/stone altars), Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan and others said: They are stones at which they used to slaughter their sacrifices.

As for the azlam, they also said: They are arrows with which they sought decisions (yastaqsimun).

* *

His saying ﴿rijsun min 'amal al-shaytan﴾ ("an abomination from the work of Satan"): 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "That is, a displeasure (sakhat) from the work of Satan." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Sin (ithm)." Zayd ibn Aslam said: "That is, an evil from the work of Satan."

﴿fajtanibuhu﴾ ("so avoid it"): the pronoun refers to the rijs, i.e., leave it. ﴿la'allakum tuflihun﴾ ("that you may succeed"): this is an encouragement.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Innama yuridu al-shaytanu an yuqi'a baynakumu al-'adawata wal-baghda'a fil-khamri wal-maysiri wa yasuddakum 'an dhikri Allahi wa 'anil-salati fahal antum muntahun﴾ ("Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you through wine and gambling, and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer. So will you not desist?"). This is a threat and a warning.

Mention of the hadiths concerning the prohibition of wine [its explanation]:

Imam Ahmad said: Surayj narrated to us (in manuscripts D and R: "Shurayj"): Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Abu Wahb, mawla of Abu Hurayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Wine was prohibited in three stages. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah, they were drinking wine and eating gambling gains, so they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about them, and Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin and benefit for people﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:219] to the end of the verse. The people said: 'It has not been forbidden to us; He only said: "In them is great sin."' And they continued drinking wine until one day a man from the Muhajirun led his companions in the Maghrib prayer and mixed up his recitation. So Allah, [Mighty and Majestic,] revealed a stricter verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated, until you know what you say﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:43]. The people continued drinking, until one of them would come to the prayer while sober. Then a yet stricter verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, indeed wine, gambling, the ansab and the azlam are an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may succeed﴾. They said: 'We have desisted, our Lord.' The people said: 'O Messenger of Allah, men were killed in the way of Allah and men died upon their drinking, while they used to drink wine and eat gambling gains, and Allah has made it an abomination from the work of Satan?' So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾ to the end of the verse. And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'If it had been forbidden to them, they would have abandoned it as you have abandoned it.'" Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad (2/351).]

Imam Ahmad also said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab [may Allah be pleased with him], that he said: "When the prohibition of wine was revealed, he said: 'O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a healing clarification.' So this verse in al-Baqarah was revealed: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin﴾. 'Umar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: 'O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a healing clarification.' Then the verse in Surat al-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated﴾. The caller of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he called the prayer, would call out: 'No intoxicated person shall approach the prayer.' 'Umar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: 'O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a healing clarification.' Then the verse in al-Ma'idah was revealed, and 'Umar was called and it was recited to him. When it reached ﴿So will you not desist?﴾, 'Umar said: 'We have desisted, we have desisted.'" [In manuscript A: "We have desisted, we have desisted."]

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it in the same way through several chains, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Sab'i, and from Abu Maysarah — whose name is 'Amr ibn Shurahbil al-Hamdani — from 'Umar, with it. He has no other narration from him except this one. Abu Zur'ah said: "He did not hear from him." 'Ali ibn al-Madini and al-Tirmidhi declared this hadith sahih. [Musnad (1/53); Sunan Abi Dawud no. 3670; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3049; Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/286).]

It is established in the two Sahihs from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said in his khutbah upon the minbar of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O people, the prohibition of wine has been revealed, and it is from five things: from grapes, dates, honey, wheat, and barley. Khamr is that which covers the intellect." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4619; Sahih Muslim no. 3032.]

Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us: Nafi' narrated to me, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "The prohibition of wine was revealed, and at that time in Madinah there were five drinks, none of which was a grape drink." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4616.]

Another hadith: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Muhammad ibn Abi Humayd narrated to us, from al-Misri — meaning Abu Tu'mah, the reciter of Egypt — who said: "I heard Ibn 'Umar say: Three verses were revealed concerning wine. The first thing revealed was ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:219], and it was said: 'Wine has been forbidden.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we benefit from it, as Allah the Exalted said.' He said: So he kept silent toward them. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:43]. It was said: 'Wine has been forbidden.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we do not drink it near the prayer.' So he kept silent toward them. Then it was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, indeed wine, gambling, the ansab and the azlam are an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may succeed﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Wine has been forbidden.'" [Musnad al-Tayalisi no. 1957.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'la narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa'lah said: "I asked Ibn 'Abbas about the sale of wine, and he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a friend from Thaqif — or from Daws — who met him on the day of the Conquest carrying a skin of wine as a gift for him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O so-and-so, did you not know that Allah has forbidden it?' The man turned to his servant and said: 'Go and sell it.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O so-and-so, what did you order him?' He said: 'I ordered him to sell it.' He said: 'Indeed, He who forbade its drinking has forbidden its sale.' So he ordered it, and it was poured out in al-Batha'."

Muslim narrated it through the chain of Ibn Wahb, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam; and also through the chain of Ibn Wahb, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Yahya ibn Sa'id — both of them — from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa'lah, from Ibn 'Abbas, with it. al-Nasa'i narrated it from Qutaybah, from Malik, with it. [Musnad (1/230); Muwatta' (2/846); Sahih Muslim no. 1579; Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/307).]

Another hadith: The Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Tamim al-Dari, that he used to present to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a skin of wine every year (in manuscript A: "to the Prophet (ﷺ) every year a skin"). When Allah revealed the prohibition of wine, he came with it. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw it, he laughed and said: "Indeed it has been forbidden after you." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I sell it and benefit from its price?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah curse the Jews. Fat of cattle and sheep was forbidden to them, so they melted it, sold it, and Allah has forbidden wine and its price."

[In its chain there is a break (inqita'). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/57) through the chain of Zayd ibn Akhzam, from Abu Bakr al-Hanafi, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from Tamim al-Dari, with it.]

Also narrated by Imam Ahmad, who said: Rawh narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bahram narrated to us, who said: I heard Shahr ibn Hawshab say: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm narrated to me that al-Dari (Tamim al-Dari) used to present the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a large waterskin (rawiyah) of wine every year. When the year came in which wine was prohibited, he brought a waterskin, and when the Prophet (ﷺ) saw it, he laughed and said: "Do you know that it has been prohibited after you?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, should I not sell it and benefit from its price?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah curse the Jews. They were told that the fat of cows and sheep was forbidden to them, so they melted it down and sold it, and ate its price. Indeed, wine is prohibited and its price is prohibited. Indeed, wine is prohibited and its price is prohibited. Indeed, wine is prohibited and its price is prohibited." [Musnad (4/226). al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (4/88): "In its chain is Shahr, whose narrations are good, but there is some criticism of him."]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Saʿid narrated to us, Ibn Lahiʿah narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Nafiʿ ibn Kaysan, that his father informed him that he used to trade in wine during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He came from Syria with wine in wineskins, intending to trade, and he brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have brought you a good drink." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Kaysan, it has been prohibited after you." He said: "Shall I sell it, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It has been prohibited, and its price is prohibited." So Kaysan went to the wineskins, took them by their bottoms, and poured them out. [Musnad (4/337). al-Haythami said: "In its chain is Nafiʿ ibn Kaysan, who is unknown (mustur)."]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: I used to pour drink for Abu ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Suhayl ibn Bayda' and a group of their companions at the house of Abu Talhah, and I was pouring for them, until the drink was almost taking hold of them. Then a man from the Muslims came and said: "Have you not heard that wine has been prohibited?" They said: "Not until we look into it and ask." Then they said: "O Anas, pour out what remains in your vessel." By Allah, they did not return to it. And it was only dates and unripe dates (busr), and that was their wine on that day. [Musnad (3/181).]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it through more than one route from Anas. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4620) and Sahih Muslim no. (1980).] In the narration of Hammad ibn Zayd, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: "I was the cupbearer of the people on the day wine was prohibited, in the house of Abu Talhah. Their drink was nothing but fadikh (a drink made from busr and tamr). Then a caller called out, and he said: 'Go out and look.' So I went out, and a caller was calling: 'Behold, wine has been prohibited!' It flowed through the streets of Madinah. Abu Talhah said to me: 'Go out and pour it out.' So I poured it out. Some of them said, or some of them said: 'So-and-so and so-and-so have been killed, and it was in their bellies.'" He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame on those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾, to the end of the verse. [This is the wording of Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1980).]

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Kabir ibn ʿAbd al-Majid narrated to me, ʿAbbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "While I was passing the cup around to Abu Talhah, Abu ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Muʿadh ibn Jabal, Suhayl ibn Bayda' and Abu Dujanah, until their heads were inclined from a mixture of busr and tamr, I heard a caller calling: 'Behold, wine has been prohibited!' He said: No one entered upon us and no one left from us until we had poured out the drink and broken the jars. Some of us performed wudu and some performed ghusl, and we used some of the perfume of Umm Sulaym. Then we went out to the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reciting: ﴿O you who believe, indeed wine, gambling, stone altars and divining arrows are an abomination of Satan's work, so avoid it that you may be successful﴾, up to his saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the status of one who died while drinking it?' So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame on those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten [when they fear Allah, believe and do righteous deeds]﴾, to the end of the verse." A man said to Qatadah: "Did you hear it from Anas ibn Malik?" He said: "Yes." And a man said to Anas ibn Malik: "Did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes" – or: "One who does not lie told me; we did not lie, and we did not know what lying was." [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/578). Al-Bazzar also narrated it in his Musnad, no. (2922), Kashf al-Astar, through ʿAbbad ibn Rashid, from Qatadah, from Anas, in similar words.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub informed me, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn Zahr, from Bakr ibn Sawadah, from Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed my Lord, blessed and exalted, has prohibited for me wine, al-kubah, and al-qinnin. Beware of al-ghubayra, for it is a third of the wine of the world." [Musnad (4/422). al-Haythami said in Majma' (5/54): "In its chain is ʿUbayd Allah ibn Zahr. Abu Zurʿah and al-Nasa'i deemed him reliable, but most scholars criticized him."]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Faraj ibn Fadalah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Rafiʿ, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has prohibited for my ummah wine, gambling, al-mizr, al-kubah and al-qinnin. And He added for me the prayer of witr." Yazid said: al-Qinnin is al-baraabit (a stringed instrument). Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad (2/163). al-Haythami said in Majma' (2/240): "In its chain is Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Rafiʿ, who is unknown."]

Ahmad also said: Abu ʿAsim (al-Nabil) narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Jaʿfar informed us, Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Walid, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says something about me that I did not say, let him take his seat in Hell." He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah has prohibited wine, gambling, al-kubah and al-ghubayra, and every intoxicant is prohibited." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad (2/171).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, from Abu Tuʿmah, their mawla, and from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Ghafiqi, that they both heard Ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Wine has been cursed in ten respects: wine itself is cursed, and its drinker, its server, its seller, its buyer, its presser, the one who has it pressed, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, and the one who consumes its price." [Musnad (2/25). Abu Dawud (no. 3674) and Ibn Majah (no. 3380) also narrated it through Waki'.]

Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahiʿah narrated to us, Abu Tuʿmah narrated to us: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to al-Mirbad (a marketplace in Madinah), and I went out with him, and I was on his right. Abu Bakr came and I stepped back from him, so he was on his right and I was on his left. Then ʿUmar came and I stepped aside for him, so he was on his left. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to al-Mirbad, and there was a wineskin there containing wine. Ibn ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me for a knife (mudyah) – Ibn ʿUmar said: "I did not know what a mudyah was until that day" – and he ordered the wineskin to be slit open. Then he said: "Wine has been cursed, along with its drinker, its server, its seller, its buyer, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, its presser, the one who has it pressed, and the one who consumes its price." [Musnad (2/71).]

Ahmad said: al-Hakam ibn Nafiʿ narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, from Damrah ibn Habib, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded me to bring him a mudyah, which is a shafrah (blade). I brought it to him, and he sharpened it and then gave it back to me and said: "Go out with it to me tomorrow." I did so. He went out with his companions to the markets of Madinah, where there were wineskins of wine that had been brought from Syria. He took the knife from me and slit open whatever wineskins were there in his presence. Then he gave it back to me and commanded his companions who were with him to go with me and help me. He ordered me to go to all the markets and not to find any wineskin of wine without slitting it open. I did so, and I did not leave a single wineskin in its markets without slitting it. [Musnad (2/132). al-Haythami said in Majma' (5/54): "Ahmad narrated it with two chains.
