Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Faraj ibn Fadalah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Rafiʿ, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has prohibited for my ummah wine, gambling, al-mizr, al-kubah and al-qinnin. And He added for me the prayer of witr." Yazid said: al-Qinnin is al-baraabit (a stringed instrument). Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad (2/163). al-Haythami said in Majma' (2/240): "In its chain is Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Rafiʿ, who is unknown."]

Ahmad also said: Abu ʿAsim (al-Nabil) narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Jaʿfar informed us, Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Walid, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says something about me that I did not say, let him take his seat in Hell." He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah has prohibited wine, gambling, al-kubah and al-ghubayra, and every intoxicant is prohibited." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad (2/171).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, from Abu Tuʿmah, their mawla, and from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Ghafiqi, that they both heard Ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Wine has been cursed in ten respects: wine itself is cursed, and its drinker, its server, its seller, its buyer, its presser, the one who has it pressed, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, and the one who consumes its price." [Musnad (2/25). Abu Dawud (no. 3674) and Ibn Majah (no. 3380) also narrated it through Waki'.]

Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahiʿah narrated to us, Abu Tuʿmah narrated to us: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to al-Mirbad (a marketplace in Madinah), and I went out with him, and I was on his right. Abu Bakr came and I stepped back from him, so he was on his right and I was on his left. Then ʿUmar came and I stepped aside for him, so he was on his left. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to al-Mirbad, and there was a wineskin there containing wine. Ibn ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me for a knife (mudyah) – Ibn ʿUmar said: "I did not know what a mudyah was until that day" – and he ordered the wineskin to be slit open. Then he said: "Wine has been cursed, along with its drinker, its server, its seller, its buyer, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, its presser, the one who has it pressed, and the one who consumes its price." [Musnad (2/71).]

Ahmad said: al-Hakam ibn Nafiʿ narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, from Damrah ibn Habib, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded me to bring him a mudyah, which is a shafrah (blade). I brought it to him, and he sharpened it and then gave it back to me and said: "Go out with it to me tomorrow." I did so. He went out with his companions to the markets of Madinah, where there were wineskins of wine that had been brought from Syria. He took the knife from me and slit open whatever wineskins were there in his presence. Then he gave it back to me and commanded his companions who were with him to go with me and help me. He ordered me to go to all the markets and not to find any wineskin of wine without slitting it open. I did so, and I did not leave a single wineskin in its markets without slitting it. [Musnad (2/132). al-Haythami said in Majma' (5/54): "Ahmad narrated it with two chains. In one is Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, who became confused in his memory; in the other is Abu Tuʿmah, whom Muhammad ibn ʿAmmar al-Mawsili deemed reliable, while Makhul criticized him. The rest of its narrators are reliable."]

Another hadith: ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh, Ibn Lahiʿah and al-Layth ibn Saʿd informed me, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Thabit ibn Yazid al-Khawlani, who informed him: He had a paternal uncle who sold wine and gave charity. I forbade him from it, but he did not stop. Then I came to Madinah and met Ibn ʿAbbas, and I asked him about wine and its price. He said: "It is prohibited, and its price is prohibited." Then Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O company of the ummah of Muhammad, if there were a Book after your Book and a Prophet after your Prophet, it would have been revealed about you as it was revealed about those before you. But Allah delayed that matter for you until the Day of Resurrection. And by my life, it is more severe upon you." Thabit said: I met ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar and asked him about the price of wine. He said: "I will inform you about wine. I was in the mosque with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and while he was sitting with his knees raised and his arms wrapped around them, he untied his hold and said: 'Whoever has any of this wine, let him bring it to us.' They began to bring it to him. One would say: 'I have a waterskin.' Another would say: 'I have a wineskin,' or: 'Whatever Allah willed for him to have.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Gather it in the open ground of such-and-such, then inform me.' They did so, then they informed him. He stood up and I stood with him. I walked on his right, leaning on me. Abu Bakr caught up with us, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed me behind him and put me on his left, and placed Abu Bakr in my place. Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, caught up with us, and he placed me behind him and put him on his left, so he walked between them. When he stopped at the wine, he said to the people: 'Do you recognize this?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, this is wine.' He said: 'You have spoken the truth.' Then he said: 'Indeed Allah has cursed wine, its presser, the one who has it pressed, its drinker, its server, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, its seller, its buyer, and the one who consumes its price.' Then he called for a knife and said: 'Sharpen it.' They did so, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it and slit open the wineskins with it." He said: The people said: "There is some benefit in these wineskins." He said: "Yes, but I only do this out of anger for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because of what is in them of His displeasure." ʿUmar said: "Shall I take care of it for you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "No."

Ibn Wahb said: Some of them add to others in the details of the story. Narrated by al-Bayhaqi. [al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/286).]

**Another hadith:** Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran informed us, Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Munadi narrated to us, Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd, who said: Four verses were revealed concerning wine. He then mentioned the hadith. He said: A man from the Ansar prepared food and invited us, and we drank wine before it was prohibited, until we became intoxicated. Then we boasted, and the Ansar said, "We are better," and the Quraysh said, "We are better." Then a man from the Ansar took the jawbone of a camel and struck Sa'd's nose with it, splitting it, and Sa'd's nose was split. Then the verse about wine was revealed: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful. Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ Muslim transmitted it from the hadith of Shu'bah.

**Another hadith:** Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Nasr ibn Qatadah informed us, Abu 'Ali al-Raffa' informed us, 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The prohibition of wine was revealed concerning two tribes from among the tribes of the Ansar. They drank, and when they became intoxicated, some of them acted foolishly toward others. When they became sober, a man would see the effect on his face, head, and beard and would say, "My brother so-and-so did this to me." They were brothers with no rancour in their hearts. [He said:] "By Allah, if he had been kind and merciful to me, he would not have done this to me." Then rancour entered their hearts, and Allah revealed this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan. So avoid it that you may be successful. Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ Then some over-zealous people said, "It is defilement, and so-and-so, who was killed on the day of Uhud, has it in his belly." So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten, when they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good. And Allah loves the doers of good.﴾

Al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Tafsir from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim Sa'iqah, from Hajjaj ibn Minhal.

**Another hadith:** Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Khalaf narrated to me, Sa'id ibn Muhammad al-Jarmi narrated to us, from Abu Tumaylah, from Salam, client of Hafs Abu al-Qasim, from Abu Burdah, from his father, who said: While we were sitting over a drink of ours, we were in Ramlah, three or four of us, with a large jar (baṭiyyah) of ours, and we were drinking wine lawfully, I got up to go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to greet him, and then the prohibition of wine was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants and gambling...﴾ until the end of the two verses ﴿So will you not desist?﴾. I came to my companions and recited it to them until His saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾. He said: Some of the people had a cup in their hand, having drunk some of it, and some remained in the vessel. He put the vessel under his upper lip, as a cupper does, and then they poured out what was in their jar. They said, "We have desisted, our Lord."

**Another hadith:** Al-Bukhari said: Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr, from Jabir, who said: Some people began the morning of the day of Uhud by drinking wine, and then they were all killed as martyrs that same day, and that was before its prohibition.

Al-Bukhari narrated this in his Tafsir in his Sahih. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn 'Abdah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, who heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: Some of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) drank wine in the morning, and then they were killed as martyrs on the day of Uhud. The Jews said, "Some of those who were killed have died while it was still in their bellies." So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten.﴾ Then he said: This chain is sound. It is as he said, but its wording contains something strange.

**Another hadith:** Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: When the prohibition of wine was revealed, they said, "What about the one who used to drink it before it was prohibited?" Then this was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾, the verse.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Bundar, Ghundar, from Shu'bah, with something similar, and said: Hasan sahih.

**Another hadith:** Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ja'far ibn Humayd al-Kufi narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Jariyah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: A man used to carry wine from Khaybar to Madinah and sell it to the Muslims. He was loaded with a quantity of it and came to Madinah with it. A man from the Muslims met him and said, "O so-and-so, indeed wine has been prohibited." So he placed it where he stopped, on a mound, and covered it with cloaks. Then he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, it has reached me that wine has been prohibited?" He said, "Yes." He said, "May I return it to the one from whom I bought it?" He said, "Its return is not permissible." He said, "May I give it as a gift to someone who will reciprocate with it?" He said, "No." He said, "But there is money in it belonging to orphans in my custody." He said, "When the wealth of Bahrain comes to us, come to us and we will compensate your orphans from their wealth." Then he called out in Madinah, and a man said, "O Messenger of Allah, may we benefit from the containers?" He said, "Then untie their stoppers." So it poured out until it settled in the bottom of the valley. This is a gharib hadith.

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Hubayrah, that is Yahya ibn 'Abbad al-Ansari, from Anas ibn Malik, that Abu Talhah asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about orphans in his custody who had inherited wine. He said, "Pour it out." He said, "Shall we not make it vinegar?" He said, "No."

Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, with something similar.

**Another hadith:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, Hilal ibn Abi Hilal narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: This verse in the Qur'an: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan; so avoid it that you may be successful﴾ is in the Torah: "Indeed Allah sent down the truth to remove falsehood by it and to nullify play, the flutes, the zafn, the kibarat—meaning the barabit—the zammarat—meaning the daff—the tanabir, poetry, and wine, once for whoever tastes it. Allah swore by His might and His majesty: whoever drinks it after I have prohibited it, I will make him thirsty on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever leaves it after I have prohibited it, I will give it to him to drink in the enclosure of holiness."

This is a sound chain.

**Another hadith:** 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated to them, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever abandons prayer in a state of intoxication once, it is as if he had the world and all that is in it, and then it is taken from him. And whoever abandons prayer in a state of intoxication four times, it is a right upon Allah to give him to drink from the clay of corruption (ṭīnat al-khabāl)." It was said, "And what is the clay of corruption?" He said, "The pus of the people of Hell."

Ahmad narrated it through the route of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb.

**Another hadith:** Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn 'Umar al-San'ani narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Nu'man—that is Ibn Abi Shaybah al-Jundi—say, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Every fermented drink is wine, every intoxicant is forbidden, and whoever drinks an intoxicant, his prayer is deprived of its reward for forty mornings. If he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he returns a fourth time, it is a right upon Allah to give him to drink from the clay of corruption." It was said, "And what is the clay of corruption, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "The pus of the people of the Fire. And whoever gives it to drink to a child who does not know his lawful from his unlawful, it is a right upon Allah to give him to drink from the clay of corruption."

Abu Dawud alone narrated it.

**Another hadith:** Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Malik informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever drinks wine in this world and does not repent from it, he will be deprived of it in the Hereafter."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Malik, with it.

Muslim narrated from Abu al-Rabi', from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every intoxicant is wine, and every intoxicant is forbidden. And whoever drinks wine and dies persisting in it, without repenting from it, will not drink it in the Hereafter."

**Another hadith:** Ibn Wahb said: 'Umar ibn Muhammad informed me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yasar, that he heard Salim ibn 'Abd Allah say: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three whom Allah will not look at on the Day of Resurrection: the one who disobeys his parents, the habitual drinker of wine, and the one who reminds of his giving (al-mannan)."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from 'Umar ibn 'Ali, from Yazid ibn Zuray', from 'Umar ibn Muhammad al-'Umari, with it.

Ahmad also narrated, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The one who reminds of his giving will not enter Paradise, nor will the disobedient son, nor the habitual drinker of wine."

Ahmad also narrated it from 'Abd al-Samad, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, with it. And from Marwan ibn Shuja', from Khasif, from Mujahid, with it. Al-Nasa'i narrated it from al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya, from al-Husayn al-Ju'fi, from Za'idah, from Ibn Abi Ziyad, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd and Mujahid, both from Abu Sa'id, with it.

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jaban, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The one who disobeys his parents will not enter Paradise, nor will a habitual drinker of wine, nor a man who reminds of his favors (given), nor the child of adultery." [Al-Musnad (2/203).]

Similarly, he narrated it from Yazid, from Hammam, from Mansur, from Salim, from Jaban, from Abdullah ibn Amr, with the same wording. [Al-Musnad (2/164).] It has also been narrated by Ghundar and others, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, from Salim, from Nubayt ibn Sharit, from Jaban, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The one who reminds of his favors will not enter Paradise, nor will the one who disobeys his parents, nor a habitual drinker of wine."

An-Nasa'i narrated it through Shu'bah in the same manner, then said: "We do not know of anyone who followed Shu'bah in (narrating) from Nubayt ibn Sharit." [Al-Musnad (2/201) and as-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i, no. (4914).]

Al-Bukhari said: "Jaban is not known to have heard from Abdullah, and Salim is not known to have heard from Jaban or Nubayt."

This hadith has also been narrated through Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, and through him also from Abu Hurairah. And Allah knows best.

Az-Zuhri said: Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham narrated to me that his father said: "I heard Uthman ibn Affan say: 'Avoid wine, for it is the mother of all evils. Indeed, there was a man among those who came before you who used to worship and withdraw from people, and a seductive woman fell in love with him. She sent her maidservant to him, saying: "We are calling you for a testimony." So he entered with her, and every time he entered a door she locked it behind him, until he reached a beautiful woman who had with her a boy and a jar of wine. She said: "By Allah, I did not call you for a testimony; rather I called you so that you would commit fornication with me, or kill this boy, or drink this wine." So she gave him a cup, and he said: "Give me more." He did not stop until he had committed fornication with her and killed the soul. So avoid wine, for it never gathers together with faith except that one of them soon expels the other.'"

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it [As-Sunan al-Kubra (8/287)], through Abdullah ibn Wahb, from Yunus ibn Yazid, from az-Zuhri with this chain. Yunus ibn Yazid was contradicted: Umar ibn Sa'id ibn as-Sirha narrated it from az-Zuhri as a marfu' report, as will come in the narration of Ibn Abi ad-Dunya. And this is a sahih chain.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi ad-Dunya narrated it in his book "Dhamm al-Muskir" from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bazi', from al-Fudayl ibn Sulayman an-Numayri, from Umar ibn Sa'id, from az-Zuhri, with this chain, as a marfu' report. [Dhamm al-Muskir, no. (1).] The narration of Yunus ibn Yazid is stronger than that of Umar ibn Sa'id ibn as-Sirha, for some imams weakened him, saying: "His narrations from az-Zuhri are not sound." The mawquf (companion's statement) is more sound, and Allah knows best.

It has a witness in the two Sahihs from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "A fornicator does not commit fornication while he is a believer, nor does a thief steal while he is a believer, nor does a drinker of wine drink it while he is a believer." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6810), and Sahih Muslim, no. (57).]

Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, Israil informed us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When wine was forbidden, some people said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what about our companions who died while drinking it?' So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾ (5:93), up to the end of the verse." He said: "And when the qiblah was changed, some people said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what about our companions who died while praying towards Bayt al-Maqdis?' So Allah revealed: ﴿And Allah would never make your faith ineffective﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]." [Al-Musnad (1/295).]

Imam Ahmad said: Dawud ibn Mihran ad-Dabbagh narrated to us, Dawud (i.e., al-Attar) narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma bint Yazid, that she heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever drinks wine, Allah will not be pleased with him for forty nights. If he dies, he dies as a disbeliever; if he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he returns (to it), it is a right upon Allah to make him drink from Tinat al-Khabal." She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is Tinat al-Khabal?" He said: "The pus of the people of the Fire." [Al-Musnad (6/460). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/69): "In it is Shahr ibn Hawshab, who is weak, though his hadith has been deemed good, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

Al-A'mash said, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said when the verse was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten, if they fear Allah and believe﴾, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It was said to me: You are among them."

Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it likewise through this chain. [Sahih Muslim, no. (2459); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3053); as-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i, no. (11153).]

Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: I read to my father: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, Ibrahim al-Hijri narrated to us, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of these two knucklebones, the marked ones, which are cast (in divination), for they are the gambling of the non-Arabs." [Al-Musnad (1/446). Its chain contains Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri, who is weak.]

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 5, verses 90–93 (part 1 of 4):

He, may He be exalted, says, forbidding His believing servants from indulging in wine (khamr) and gambling (maysir), which is qimar.

It has been reported from the Commander of the Faithful, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he said: "Chess (shatranj) is of the maysir." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from 'Ubays ibn Marhum, from Hatim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Ali, with it.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi (in manuscript A: "al-A'mashi") narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from 'Ata', Mujahid and Tawus — Sufyan said: "or two of them" — they said: "Everything of gambling is of the maysir, even children's play with walnuts."

It is also reported from Rashid ibn Sa'd and Hamzah ibn Habib (in manuscript A: "Habib similarly"), and they said: "Even knucklebones (ka'ab), walnuts, and the eggs with which children play." Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "The maysir is qimar."

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The maysir is qimar. They used to gamble in the Jahiliyyah until Islam came, so Allah forbade them these ugly behaviours."

Malik narrated from Dawud ibn al-Husayn that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: "The maysir of the people of the Jahiliyyah was selling meat for a sheep or two sheep."

Al-Zuhri narrated from al-A'raj, who said: "The maysir is also casting arrows (darb bil-qidah) for goods and fruits."

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: "Everything that distracts from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer is of the maysir."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated all of these.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: Sadaqah narrated to us: 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'Atikah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Avoid these marked knucklebones with which one is driven away by divination, for they are of the maysir." This is a gharib hadith. [Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned it in al-'Ilal (2/297), and said: "My father said: This hadith is baseless (batil); it comes from 'Ali ibn Yazid, while 'Uthman is not objectionable."]

It seems that what is meant here is nard (backgammon), which is mentioned in a hadith in Sahih Muslim, from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever plays with nardashir, it is as if he dipped his hand in the flesh and blood of swine." [Sahih Muslim, no. 2260.] Also in the Muwatta' of Malik, the Musnad of Ahmad, and the Sunan of Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever plays with nard has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger." [Muwatta' (2/958), Musnad (4/394), Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4938, Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3762.] It has also been reported as a statement of Abu Musa himself (mawquf), and Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us (in manuscript A: "'Ali ibn Ibrahim," which is an error): al-Ju'ayd narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Khatmi, that he heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b, while he was asking 'Abd al-Rahman: "Tell me, what did you hear your father say from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" 'Abd al-Rahman said: "I heard my father say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The likeness of one who plays with nard and then stands and prays is like the likeness of one who performs ablution with pus and the blood of swine and then stands and prays.'" [Musnad (5/370). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/113): "In it is Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Khatmi, whom I do not know; the rest of Ahmad's narrators are sahih narrators."]

As for chess (shatranj), 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar said: "It is worse than nard." And it has preceded from 'Ali that he said: "It is of the maysir." Malik, Abu Hanifah and Ahmad explicitly stated its prohibition, and al-Shafi'i disliked it, may Allah have mercy on them.

As for the ansab (idols/stone altars), Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan and others said: They are stones at which they used to slaughter their sacrifices.

As for the azlam, they also said: They are arrows with which they sought decisions (yastaqsimun).

* *

His saying ﴿rijsun min 'amal al-shaytan﴾ ("an abomination from the work of Satan"): 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "That is, a displeasure (sakhat) from the work of Satan." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Sin (ithm)." Zayd ibn Aslam said: "That is, an evil from the work of Satan."

﴿fajtanibuhu﴾ ("so avoid it"): the pronoun refers to the rijs, i.e., leave it. ﴿la'allakum tuflihun﴾ ("that you may succeed"): this is an encouragement.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Innama yuridu al-shaytanu an yuqi'a baynakumu al-'adawata wal-baghda'a fil-khamri wal-maysiri wa yasuddakum 'an dhikri Allahi wa 'anil-salati fahal antum muntahun﴾ ("Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you through wine and gambling, and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer. So will you not desist?"). This is a threat and a warning.

Mention of the hadiths concerning the prohibition of wine [its explanation]:

Imam Ahmad said: Surayj narrated to us (in manuscripts D and R: "Shurayj"): Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Abu Wahb, mawla of Abu Hurayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Wine was prohibited in three stages. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah, they were drinking wine and eating gambling gains, so they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about them, and Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin and benefit for people﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:219] to the end of the verse. The people said: 'It has not been forbidden to us; He only said: "In them is great sin."' And they continued drinking wine until one day a man from the Muhajirun led his companions in the Maghrib prayer and mixed up his recitation. So Allah, [Mighty and Majestic,] revealed a stricter verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated, until you know what you say﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:43]. The people continued drinking, until one of them would come to the prayer while sober. Then a yet stricter verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, indeed wine, gambling, the ansab and the azlam are an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may succeed﴾. They said: 'We have desisted, our Lord.' The people said: 'O Messenger of Allah, men were killed in the way of Allah and men died upon their drinking, while they used to drink wine and eat gambling gains, and Allah has made it an abomination from the work of Satan?' So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾ to the end of the verse. And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'If it had been forbidden to them, they would have abandoned it as you have abandoned it.'" Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad (2/351).]

Imam Ahmad also said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab [may Allah be pleased with him], that he said: "When the prohibition of wine was revealed, he said: 'O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a healing clarification.' So this verse in al-Baqarah was revealed: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin﴾. 'Umar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: 'O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a healing clarification.' Then the verse in Surat al-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated﴾. The caller of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he called the prayer, would call out: 'No intoxicated person shall approach the prayer.' 'Umar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: 'O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a healing clarification.' Then the verse in al-Ma'idah was revealed, and 'Umar was called and it was recited to him. When it reached ﴿So will you not desist?﴾, 'Umar said: 'We have desisted, we have desisted.'" [In manuscript A: "We have desisted, we have desisted."]

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it in the same way through several chains, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Sab'i, and from Abu Maysarah — whose name is 'Amr ibn Shurahbil al-Hamdani — from 'Umar, with it. He has no other narration from him except this one. Abu Zur'ah said: "He did not hear from him." 'Ali ibn al-Madini and al-Tirmidhi declared this hadith sahih. [Musnad (1/53); Sunan Abi Dawud no. 3670; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3049; Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/286).]

It is established in the two Sahihs from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said in his khutbah upon the minbar of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O people, the prohibition of wine has been revealed, and it is from five things: from grapes, dates, honey, wheat, and barley. Khamr is that which covers the intellect." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4619; Sahih Muslim no. 3032.]

Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us: Nafi' narrated to me, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "The prohibition of wine was revealed, and at that time in Madinah there were five drinks, none of which was a grape drink." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4616.]

Another hadith: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Muhammad ibn Abi Humayd narrated to us, from al-Misri — meaning Abu Tu'mah, the reciter of Egypt — who said: "I heard Ibn 'Umar say: Three verses were revealed concerning wine. The first thing revealed was ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:219], and it was said: 'Wine has been forbidden.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we benefit from it, as Allah the Exalted said.' He said: So he kept silent toward them. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:43]. It was said: 'Wine has been forbidden.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we do not drink it near the prayer.' So he kept silent toward them. Then it was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, indeed wine, gambling, the ansab and the azlam are an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may succeed﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Wine has been forbidden.'" [Musnad al-Tayalisi no. 1957.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'la narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa'lah said: "I asked Ibn 'Abbas about the sale of wine, and he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a friend from Thaqif — or from Daws — who met him on the day of the Conquest carrying a skin of wine as a gift for him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O so-and-so, did you not know that Allah has forbidden it?' The man turned to his servant and said: 'Go and sell it.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O so-and-so, what did you order him?' He said: 'I ordered him to sell it.' He said: 'Indeed, He who forbade its drinking has forbidden its sale.' So he ordered it, and it was poured out in al-Batha'."

Muslim narrated it through the chain of Ibn Wahb, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam; and also through the chain of Ibn Wahb, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Yahya ibn Sa'id — both of them — from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa'lah, from Ibn 'Abbas, with it. al-Nasa'i narrated it from Qutaybah, from Malik, with it. [Musnad (1/230); Muwatta' (2/846); Sahih Muslim no. 1579; Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/307).]

Another hadith: The Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Tamim al-Dari, that he used to present to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a skin of wine every year (in manuscript A: "to the Prophet (ﷺ) every year a skin"). When Allah revealed the prohibition of wine, he came with it. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw it, he laughed and said: "Indeed it has been forbidden after you." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I sell it and benefit from its price?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah curse the Jews. Fat of cattle and sheep was forbidden to them, so they melted it, sold it, and Allah has forbidden wine and its price."

[In its chain there is a break (inqita'). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/57) through the chain of Zayd ibn Akhzam, from Abu Bakr al-Hanafi, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from Tamim al-Dari, with it.]

Also narrated by Imam Ahmad, who said: Rawh narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bahram narrated to us, who said: I heard Shahr ibn Hawshab say: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm narrated to me that al-Dari (Tamim al-Dari) used to present the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a large waterskin (rawiyah) of wine every year. When the year came in which wine was prohibited, he brought a waterskin, and when the Prophet (ﷺ) saw it, he laughed and said: "Do you know that it has been prohibited after you?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, should I not sell it and benefit from its price?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah curse the Jews. They were told that the fat of cows and sheep was forbidden to them, so they melted it down and sold it, and ate its price. Indeed, wine is prohibited and its price is prohibited. Indeed, wine is prohibited and its price is prohibited. Indeed, wine is prohibited and its price is prohibited." [Musnad (4/226). al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (4/88): "In its chain is Shahr, whose narrations are good, but there is some criticism of him."]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Saʿid narrated to us, Ibn Lahiʿah narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Nafiʿ ibn Kaysan, that his father informed him that he used to trade in wine during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He came from Syria with wine in wineskins, intending to trade, and he brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have brought you a good drink." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Kaysan, it has been prohibited after you." He said: "Shall I sell it, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It has been prohibited, and its price is prohibited." So Kaysan went to the wineskins, took them by their bottoms, and poured them out. [Musnad (4/337). al-Haythami said: "In its chain is Nafiʿ ibn Kaysan, who is unknown (mustur)."]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: I used to pour drink for Abu ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Suhayl ibn Bayda' and a group of their companions at the house of Abu Talhah, and I was pouring for them, until the drink was almost taking hold of them. Then a man from the Muslims came and said: "Have you not heard that wine has been prohibited?" They said: "Not until we look into it and ask." Then they said: "O Anas, pour out what remains in your vessel." By Allah, they did not return to it. And it was only dates and unripe dates (busr), and that was their wine on that day. [Musnad (3/181).]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it through more than one route from Anas. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4620) and Sahih Muslim no. (1980).] In the narration of Hammad ibn Zayd, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: "I was the cupbearer of the people on the day wine was prohibited, in the house of Abu Talhah. Their drink was nothing but fadikh (a drink made from busr and tamr). Then a caller called out, and he said: 'Go out and look.' So I went out, and a caller was calling: 'Behold, wine has been prohibited!' It flowed through the streets of Madinah. Abu Talhah said to me: 'Go out and pour it out.' So I poured it out. Some of them said, or some of them said: 'So-and-so and so-and-so have been killed, and it was in their bellies.'" He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame on those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾, to the end of the verse. [This is the wording of Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1980).]

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Kabir ibn ʿAbd al-Majid narrated to me, ʿAbbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "While I was passing the cup around to Abu Talhah, Abu ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Muʿadh ibn Jabal, Suhayl ibn Bayda' and Abu Dujanah, until their heads were inclined from a mixture of busr and tamr, I heard a caller calling: 'Behold, wine has been prohibited!' He said: No one entered upon us and no one left from us until we had poured out the drink and broken the jars. Some of us performed wudu and some performed ghusl, and we used some of the perfume of Umm Sulaym. Then we went out to the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reciting: ﴿O you who believe, indeed wine, gambling, stone altars and divining arrows are an abomination of Satan's work, so avoid it that you may be successful﴾, up to his saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the status of one who died while drinking it?' So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame on those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten [when they fear Allah, believe and do righteous deeds]﴾, to the end of the verse." A man said to Qatadah: "Did you hear it from Anas ibn Malik?" He said: "Yes." And a man said to Anas ibn Malik: "Did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes" – or: "One who does not lie told me; we did not lie, and we did not know what lying was." [Tafsir al-Tabari (10/578). Al-Bazzar also narrated it in his Musnad, no. (2922), Kashf al-Astar, through ʿAbbad ibn Rashid, from Qatadah, from Anas, in similar words.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub informed me, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn Zahr, from Bakr ibn Sawadah, from Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed my Lord, blessed and exalted, has prohibited for me wine, al-kubah, and al-qinnin. Beware of al-ghubayra, for it is a third of the wine of the world." [Musnad (4/422). al-Haythami said in Majma' (5/54): "In its chain is ʿUbayd Allah ibn Zahr. Abu Zurʿah and al-Nasa'i deemed him reliable, but most scholars criticized him."]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Faraj ibn Fadalah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Rafiʿ, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has prohibited for my ummah wine, gambling, al-mizr, al-kubah and al-qinnin. And He added for me the prayer of witr." Yazid said: al-Qinnin is al-baraabit (a stringed instrument). Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad (2/163). al-Haythami said in Majma' (2/240): "In its chain is Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Rafiʿ, who is unknown."]

Ahmad also said: Abu ʿAsim (al-Nabil) narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Jaʿfar informed us, Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Walid, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says something about me that I did not say, let him take his seat in Hell." He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah has prohibited wine, gambling, al-kubah and al-ghubayra, and every intoxicant is prohibited." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad (2/171).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, from Abu Tuʿmah, their mawla, and from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Ghafiqi, that they both heard Ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Wine has been cursed in ten respects: wine itself is cursed, and its drinker, its server, its seller, its buyer, its presser, the one who has it pressed, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, and the one who consumes its price." [Musnad (2/25). Abu Dawud (no. 3674) and Ibn Majah (no. 3380) also narrated it through Waki'.]

Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahiʿah narrated to us, Abu Tuʿmah narrated to us: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to al-Mirbad (a marketplace in Madinah), and I went out with him, and I was on his right. Abu Bakr came and I stepped back from him, so he was on his right and I was on his left. Then ʿUmar came and I stepped aside for him, so he was on his left. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to al-Mirbad, and there was a wineskin there containing wine. Ibn ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me for a knife (mudyah) – Ibn ʿUmar said: "I did not know what a mudyah was until that day" – and he ordered the wineskin to be slit open. Then he said: "Wine has been cursed, along with its drinker, its server, its seller, its buyer, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, its presser, the one who has it pressed, and the one who consumes its price." [Musnad (2/71).]

Ahmad said: al-Hakam ibn Nafiʿ narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, from Damrah ibn Habib, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded me to bring him a mudyah, which is a shafrah (blade). I brought it to him, and he sharpened it and then gave it back to me and said: "Go out with it to me tomorrow." I did so. He went out with his companions to the markets of Madinah, where there were wineskins of wine that had been brought from Syria. He took the knife from me and slit open whatever wineskins were there in his presence. Then he gave it back to me and commanded his companions who were with him to go with me and help me. He ordered me to go to all the markets and not to find any wineskin of wine without slitting it open. I did so, and I did not leave a single wineskin in its markets without slitting it. [Musnad (2/132). al-Haythami said in Majma' (5/54): "Ahmad narrated it with two chains. In one is Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, who became confused in his memory; in the other is Abu Tuʿmah, whom Muhammad ibn ʿAmmar al-Mawsili deemed reliable, while Makhul criticized him. The rest of its narrators are reliable."]

Another hadith: ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh, Ibn Lahiʿah and al-Layth ibn Saʿd informed me, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Thabit ibn Yazid al-Khawlani, who informed him: He had a paternal uncle who sold wine and gave charity. I forbade him from it, but he did not stop. Then I came to Madinah and met Ibn ʿAbbas, and I asked him about wine and its price. He said: "It is prohibited, and its price is prohibited." Then Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O company of the ummah of Muhammad, if there were a Book after your Book and a Prophet after your Prophet, it would have been revealed about you as it was revealed about those before you. But Allah delayed that matter for you until the Day of Resurrection. And by my life, it is more severe upon you." Thabit said: I met ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar and asked him about the price of wine. He said: "I will inform you about wine. I was in the mosque with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and while he was sitting with his knees raised and his arms wrapped around them, he untied his hold and said: 'Whoever has any of this wine, let him bring it to us.' They began to bring it to him. One would say: 'I have a waterskin.' Another would say: 'I have a wineskin,' or: 'Whatever Allah willed for him to have.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Gather it in the open ground of such-and-such, then inform me.' They did so, then they informed him. He stood up and I stood with him. I walked on his right, leaning on me. Abu Bakr caught up with us, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed me behind him and put me on his left, and placed Abu Bakr in my place. Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, caught up with us, and he placed me behind him and put him on his left, so he walked between them. When he stopped at the wine, he said to the people: 'Do you recognize this?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, this is wine.' He said: 'You have spoken the truth.' Then he said: 'Indeed Allah has cursed wine, its presser, the one who has it pressed, its drinker, its server, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, its seller, its buyer, and the one who consumes its price.' Then he called for a knife and said: 'Sharpen it.' They did so, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it and slit open the wineskins with it." He said: The people said: "There is some benefit in these wineskins." He said: "Yes, but I only do this out of anger for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because of what is in them of His displeasure." ʿUmar said: "Shall I take care of it for you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "No."

Ibn Wahb said: Some of them add to others in the details of the story. Narrated by al-Bayhaqi. [al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/286).]

**Another hadith:** Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran informed us, Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Munadi narrated to us, Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd, who said: Four verses were revealed concerning wine. He then mentioned the hadith. He said: A man from the Ansar prepared food and invited us, and we drank wine before it was prohibited, until we became intoxicated. Then we boasted, and the Ansar said, "We are better," and the Quraysh said, "We are better." Then a man from the Ansar took the jawbone of a camel and struck Sa'd's nose with it, splitting it, and Sa'd's nose was split. Then the verse about wine was revealed: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful. Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ Muslim transmitted it from the hadith of Shu'bah.

**Another hadith:** Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Nasr ibn Qatadah informed us, Abu 'Ali al-Raffa' informed us, 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The prohibition of wine was revealed concerning two tribes from among the tribes of the Ansar. They drank, and when they became intoxicated, some of them acted foolishly toward others. When they became sober, a man would see the effect on his face, head, and beard and would say, "My brother so-and-so did this to me." They were brothers with no rancour in their hearts. [He said:] "By Allah, if he had been kind and merciful to me, he would not have done this to me." Then rancour entered their hearts, and Allah revealed this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan. So avoid it that you may be successful. Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ Then some over-zealous people said, "It is defilement, and so-and-so, who was killed on the day of Uhud, has it in his belly." So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten, when they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good. And Allah loves the doers of good.﴾

Al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Tafsir from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim Sa'iqah, from Hajjaj ibn Minhal.

**Another hadith:** Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Khalaf narrated to me, Sa'id ibn Muhammad al-Jarmi narrated to us, from Abu Tumaylah, from Salam, client of Hafs Abu al-Qasim, from Abu Burdah, from his father, who said: While we were sitting over a drink of ours, we were in Ramlah, three or four of us, with a large jar (baṭiyyah) of ours, and we were drinking wine lawfully, I got up to go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to greet him, and then the prohibition of wine was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants and gambling...﴾ until the end of the two verses ﴿So will you not desist?﴾. I came to my companions and recited it to them until His saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾. He said: Some of the people had a cup in their hand, having drunk some of it, and some remained in the vessel. He put the vessel under his upper lip, as a cupper does, and then they poured out what was in their jar. They said, "We have desisted, our Lord."

**Another hadith:** Al-Bukhari said: Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr, from Jabir, who said: Some people began the morning of the day of Uhud by drinking wine, and then they were all killed as martyrs that same day, and that was before its prohibition.

Al-Bukhari narrated this in his Tafsir in his Sahih. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn 'Abdah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, who heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: Some of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) drank wine in the morning, and then they were killed as martyrs on the day of Uhud. The Jews said, "Some of those who were killed have died while it was still in their bellies." So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten.﴾ Then he said: This chain is sound. It is as he said, but its wording contains something strange.

**Another hadith:** Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: When the prohibition of wine was revealed, they said, "What about the one who used to drink it before it was prohibited?" Then this was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾, the verse.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Bundar, Ghundar, from Shu'bah, with something similar, and said: Hasan sahih.

**Another hadith:** Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ja'far ibn Humayd al-Kufi narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Jariyah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: A man used to carry wine from Khaybar to Madinah and sell it to the Muslims. He was loaded with a quantity of it and came to Madinah with it. A man from the Muslims met him and said, "O so-and-so, indeed wine has been prohibited." So he placed it where he stopped, on a mound, and covered it with cloaks. Then he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, it has reached me that wine has been prohibited?" He said, "Yes." He said, "May I return it to the one from whom I bought it?" He said, "Its return is not permissible." He said, "May I give it as a gift to someone who will reciprocate with it?" He said, "No." He said, "But there is money in it belonging to orphans in my custody." He said, "When the wealth of Bahrain comes to us, come to us and we will compensate your orphans from their wealth." Then he called out in Madinah, and a man said, "O Messenger of Allah, may we benefit from the containers?" He said, "Then untie their stoppers." So it poured out until it settled in the bottom of the valley. This is a gharib hadith.

**Another hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Hubayrah, that is Yahya ibn 'Abbad al-Ansari, from Anas ibn Malik, that Abu Talhah asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about orphans in his custody who had inherited wine. He said, "Pour it out." He said, "Shall we not make it vinegar?" He said, "No."

Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, with something similar.

**Another hadith:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, Hilal ibn Abi Hilal narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: This verse in the Qur'an: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan; so avoid it that you may be successful﴾ is in the Torah: "Indeed Allah sent down the truth to remove falsehood by it and to nullify play, the flutes, the zafn, the kibarat—meaning the barabit—the zammarat—meaning the daff—the tanabir, poetry, and wine, once for whoever tastes it. Allah swore by His might and His majesty: whoever drinks it after I have prohibited it, I will make him thirsty on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever leaves it after I have prohibited it, I will give it to him to drink in the enclosure of holiness."

This is a sound chain.

**Another hadith:** 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated to them, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever abandons prayer in a state of intoxication once, it is as if he had the world and all that is in it, and then it is taken from him. And whoever abandons prayer in a state of intoxication four times, it is a right upon Allah to give him to drink from the clay of corruption (ṭīnat al-khabāl)." It was said, "And what is the clay of corruption?" He said, "The pus of the people of Hell."

Ahmad narrated it through the route of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb.

**Another hadith:** Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn 'Umar al-San'ani narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Nu'man—that is Ibn Abi Shaybah al-Jundi—say, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Every fermented drink is wine, every intoxicant is forbidden, and whoever drinks an intoxicant, his prayer is deprived of its reward for forty mornings. If he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he returns a fourth time, it is a right upon Allah to give him to drink from the clay of corruption." It was said, "And what is the clay of corruption, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "The pus of the people of the Fire. And whoever gives it to drink to a child who does not know his lawful from his unlawful, it is a right upon Allah to give him to drink from the clay of corruption."

Abu Dawud alone narrated it.

**Another hadith:** Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Malik informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever drinks wine in this world and does not repent from it, he will be deprived of it in the Hereafter."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Malik, with it.

Muslim narrated from Abu al-Rabi', from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every intoxicant is wine, and every intoxicant is forbidden. And whoever drinks wine and dies persisting in it, without repenting from it, will not drink it in the Hereafter."

**Another hadith:** Ibn Wahb said: 'Umar ibn Muhammad informed me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yasar, that he heard Salim ibn 'Abd Allah say: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three whom Allah will not look at on the Day of Resurrection: the one who disobeys his parents, the habitual drinker of wine, and the one who reminds of his giving (al-mannan)."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from 'Umar ibn 'Ali, from Yazid ibn Zuray', from 'Umar ibn Muhammad al-'Umari, with it.

Ahmad also narrated, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The one who reminds of his giving will not enter Paradise, nor will the disobedient son, nor the habitual drinker of wine."

Ahmad also narrated it from 'Abd al-Samad, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, with it. And from Marwan ibn Shuja', from Khasif, from Mujahid, with it. Al-Nasa'i narrated it from al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya, from al-Husayn al-Ju'fi, from Za'idah, from Ibn Abi Ziyad, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd and Mujahid, both from Abu Sa'id, with it.

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jaban, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The one who disobeys his parents will not enter Paradise, nor will a habitual drinker of wine, nor a man who reminds of his favors (given), nor the child of adultery." [Al-Musnad (2/203).]

Similarly, he narrated it from Yazid, from Hammam, from Mansur, from Salim, from Jaban, from Abdullah ibn Amr, with the same wording. [Al-Musnad (2/164).] It has also been narrated by Ghundar and others, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, from Salim, from Nubayt ibn Sharit, from Jaban, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The one who reminds of his favors will not enter Paradise, nor will the one who disobeys his parents, nor a habitual drinker of wine."

An-Nasa'i narrated it through Shu'bah in the same manner, then said: "We do not know of anyone who followed Shu'bah in (narrating) from Nubayt ibn Sharit." [Al-Musnad (2/201) and as-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i, no. (4914).]

Al-Bukhari said: "Jaban is not known to have heard from Abdullah, and Salim is not known to have heard from Jaban or Nubayt."

This hadith has also been narrated through Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, and through him also from Abu Hurairah. And Allah knows best.

Az-Zuhri said: Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham narrated to me that his father said: "I heard Uthman ibn Affan say: 'Avoid wine, for it is the mother of all evils. Indeed, there was a man among those who came before you who used to worship and withdraw from people, and a seductive woman fell in love with him. She sent her maidservant to him, saying: "We are calling you for a testimony." So he entered with her, and every time he entered a door she locked it behind him, until he reached a beautiful woman who had with her a boy and a jar of wine. She said: "By Allah, I did not call you for a testimony; rather I called you so that you would commit fornication with me, or kill this boy, or drink this wine." So she gave him a cup, and he said: "Give me more." He did not stop until he had committed fornication with her and killed the soul. So avoid wine, for it never gathers together with faith except that one of them soon expels the other.'"

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it [As-Sunan al-Kubra (8/287)], through Abdullah ibn Wahb, from Yunus ibn Yazid, from az-Zuhri with this chain. Yunus ibn Yazid was contradicted: Umar ibn Sa'id ibn as-Sirha narrated it from az-Zuhri as a marfu' report, as will come in the narration of Ibn Abi ad-Dunya. And this is a sahih chain.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi ad-Dunya narrated it in his book "Dhamm al-Muskir" from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bazi', from al-Fudayl ibn Sulayman an-Numayri, from Umar ibn Sa'id, from az-Zuhri, with this chain, as a marfu' report. [Dhamm al-Muskir, no. (1).] The narration of Yunus ibn Yazid is stronger than that of Umar ibn Sa'id ibn as-Sirha, for some imams weakened him, saying: "His narrations from az-Zuhri are not sound." The mawquf (companion's statement) is more sound, and Allah knows best.

It has a witness in the two Sahihs from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "A fornicator does not commit fornication while he is a believer, nor does a thief steal while he is a believer, nor does a drinker of wine drink it while he is a believer." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6810), and Sahih Muslim, no. (57).]

Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, Israil informed us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When wine was forbidden, some people said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what about our companions who died while drinking it?' So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾ (5:93), up to the end of the verse." He said: "And when the qiblah was changed, some people said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what about our companions who died while praying towards Bayt al-Maqdis?' So Allah revealed: ﴿And Allah would never make your faith ineffective﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]." [Al-Musnad (1/295).]

Imam Ahmad said: Dawud ibn Mihran ad-Dabbagh narrated to us, Dawud (i.e., al-Attar) narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma bint Yazid, that she heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever drinks wine, Allah will not be pleased with him for forty nights. If he dies, he dies as a disbeliever; if he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he returns (to it), it is a right upon Allah to make him drink from Tinat al-Khabal." She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is Tinat al-Khabal?" He said: "The pus of the people of the Fire." [Al-Musnad (6/460). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/69): "In it is Shahr ibn Hawshab, who is weak, though his hadith has been deemed good, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

Al-A'mash said, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said when the verse was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten, if they fear Allah and believe﴾, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It was said to me: You are among them."

Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it likewise through this chain. [Sahih Muslim, no. (2459); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3053); as-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i, no. (11153).]

Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: I read to my father: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, Ibrahim al-Hijri narrated to us, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of these two knucklebones, the marked ones, which are cast (in divination), for they are the gambling of the non-Arabs." [Al-Musnad (1/446). Its chain contains Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri, who is weak.]

Al-Walibi reported from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: ﴿Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your spears can reach﴾. He said: it is the weak of the game and its young, with which Allah tests His servants during their state of ihram, to the extent that they could take it with their hands. So Allah forbade them to approach it.

Mujahid said: ﴿that your hands can reach﴾ means the young of the game and its chicks, and ﴿your spears﴾ means its large ones.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse was revealed concerning the ʿUmrah of al-Hudaybiyyah, when wild animals, birds and game came to them in their camps in a way they had never seen before, so Allah forbade them to kill it while they were in ihram.

﴿That Allah may make evident who fears Him unseen﴾ means: He, the Exalted, tests them with the game that comes to them in their camps, and they are able to take it with their hands and spears, secretly and openly, so that He may make evident the obedience of those among them who obey in private and in public, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Mulk: 12].

* *

As for His statement here: ﴿So whoever transgresses after that﴾, al-Suddi and others said: meaning after this warning, admonition and advance notice. ﴿For him is a painful punishment﴾, that is, for his opposition to the command and law of Allah.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in ihram﴾. This is a prohibition from Him, the Exalted, against killing game while in the state of ihram, and a prohibition against engaging in it therein. This applies in meaning to the edible game and what results from it and from other than it. As for non-edible land animals, according to al-Shafi'i it is permissible for the muhrim to kill them. The majority hold that killing them is also prohibited, and no exception is made from this except what is established in the two Sahihs through the route of al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAisha, the Mother of the Believers, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Five harmful creatures may be killed both within the sacred area and outside it: the crow, the kite, the scorpion, the rat, and the rabid dog." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3314 and Sahih Muslim no. 1198.]

And Malik narrated from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Five creatures of the beasts, there is no sin upon the muhrim for killing them: the crow, the kite, the scorpion, the rat, and the rabid dog." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1826 and Sahih Muslim no. 1199.]

Ayyub narrated it from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, similarly. Ayyub said: I said to Nafi': what about the snake? He said: the snake, there is no doubt about it, and there is no disagreement about killing it. [Sahih Muslim no. 1199.]

Among the scholars, such as Malik and Ahmad, some extended the rabid dog to include the wolf, the predatory beasts, the tiger and the leopard, because they are more harmful than it, and Allah knows best. Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah and Zayd ibn Aslam said: the rabid dog includes all these aggressive predators. Whoever holds this view took as evidence what is narrated, that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against ʿUtbah ibn Abi Lahab, he said: "O Allah, set Your dog upon him in al-Sham." [Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/339) through the route of Zuhayr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ, from Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArubah, from Qatadah, mursal, and he mentioned the story. And Abu Nuʿaym narrated it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (p. 163) through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from ʿUthman ibn ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, and he mentioned the story. And al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/338) through the route of ʿAbbas ibn al-Fadl, from al-Aswad ibn Shayban, from Abu Nawfal ibn Abi ʿAqrab, from his father, and he mentioned the story.] So a lion ate him at al-Zarqa'. They said: if he kills other than these, he must pay compensation, such as the hyena, the fox, the wild cat and the like.

Malik said: Likewise, excepted from this are the young of these five mentioned creatures, and the young of the aggressive predators added to them.

Al-Shafi'i said: it is permissible for the muhrim to kill every animal whose meat is not eaten, and there is no difference between its young and its adult. He made the common reason the fact that it is not eaten.

Abu Hanifah said: the muhrim may kill the rabid dog and the wolf, because it is a wild dog. If he kills other than these two, he must pay compensation, except that if another predator attacks him and he kills it, then there is no compensation upon him. This is the view of al-Awza'i and al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy.

Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl said: he must pay compensation for whatever else, even if it attacks him.

Some people said: what is meant here by the crow is the abqa' (the piebald crow), which has whiteness on its belly and back, not the adra' (the black one) or the a'sam (the white one). This is based on what al-Nasa'i narrated from ʿAmr ibn ʿAli al-Fallas, from Yahya al-Qattan, from Shuʿbah, from Qatadah, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿAisha, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Five creatures the muhrim may kill: the snake, the rat, the kite, the abqa' crow, and the rabid dog."

The majority hold that what is meant by it is more general than that, based on the unrestricted wording established in the two Sahihs.

Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the muhrim may not kill the crow unless it attacks him and harms him.

Mujahid ibn Jabr and a group said: he does not kill it but throws at it. The same is reported from ʿAli.

Hushaym narrated: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Nuʿm, from Abu Saʿid, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he was asked what the muhrim may kill, and he said: "The snake, the scorpion, the fuwaysiqah (the rat), he may throw at the crow but not kill it, the rabid dog, the kite, and the aggressive predator."

Abu Dawud narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and al-Tirmidhi from Ahmad ibn Mani', both from Hushaym. And Ibn Majah narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, both from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, and he is weak, with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: this is a hasan hadith. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1848, Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 838 and Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3089.]

* *

As for His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever among you kills it intentionally, then the compensation is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saʿid al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, who said: I was informed from Tawus who said: one is not judged for someone who hits game by mistake; judgment is only made against the one who hits it intentionally.

This is a strange view from Tawus, and he adheres to the apparent meaning of the verse.

Mujahid ibn Jubayr said: what is meant here by the intentional one is the one who aims to kill the game while forgetting his ihram. As for the one who intentionally kills game while remembering his ihram, his matter is too grave to be covered by expiation, and his ihram is void.

Ibn Jarir narrated this from him through the route of Ibn Abi Najih, Layth ibn Abi Sulaym and others, from him. This too is a strange view. What the majority hold is that the intentional and the forgetful are equal in the obligation of compensation upon them. Al-Zuhri said: the Book indicates the intentional one, and the Sunnah established the forgetful one. The meaning of this is that the Qur'an indicates the obligation of compensation upon the intentional one and his sinfulness, by His saying: ﴿That he may taste the consequence of his deed. Allah has pardoned what is past; but whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾. And the Sunnah came with the rulings of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions establishing the obligation of compensation for error, just as the Book indicated it for the intentional. Also, killing game is destruction, and destruction is liable to compensation whether intentional or forgetful, but the intentional one is sinful, while the one who errs is not blameworthy.

* *

As for His statement: ﴿So the compensation is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock﴾. Ibn Jarir related that Ibn Mas'ud recited it: "So its compensation is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock."

In His statement: ﴿So the compensation is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock﴾, according to each of the two readings, there is evidence for what Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and the majority held: that compensation is obligatory from the like of what the muhrim killed, when it has a like among domestic animals. This is in contrast to Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, who required the value regardless of whether the game killed had a like or not. He said: he has the choice, if he wishes he gives its price in charity, and if he wishes he buys with it an offering. But what the Companions ruled regarding the like is more deserving of following, for they ruled concerning the ostrich with a camel, concerning the wild cow with a cow, and concerning the gazelle with a female goat. The reports of the Companions' judgments and their chains are established in the book "al-Ahkam." As for when the game has no like, Ibn ʿAbbas ruled concerning it with its price, to be carried to Makkah. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it. As for His statement: ﴿judged by two just men among you﴾, meaning that the compensation is judged, in the case of a like, or by value in the case of no like, by two just Muslims. The scholars differed concerning the killer: can he be one of the two judges? On two views: the first: no, because he may be suspected in judging in his own case, and this is the view of Malik. The second: yes, for the generality of the verse. This is the view of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad.

Those of the first view argued that a judge cannot be the one judged against in the same case.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Abu Nuʿaym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Jaʿfar, that is Ibn Burqan, narrated to us, from Maymun ibn Mihran: that a Bedouin came to Abu Bakr and said: I killed game while I was in ihram, so what do you think the compensation upon me is? Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who was sitting with him: What do you think about what he said? The Bedouin said: I came to you while you are the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking you, and now you ask someone else? Abu Bakr said: And what do you deny? Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So the compensation is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock, judged by two just men among you﴾. So I consulted my companion until we agreed on a matter, and we command you with it.

This is a good chain, but it is disconnected between Maymun and al-Siddiq, and such a thing may be tolerated here. Al-Siddiq explained the ruling to him gently and patiently, seeing him as an ignorant Bedouin, and the remedy for ignorance is teaching. As for when the one who raises the objection is attributed to knowledge, then Ibn Jarir has said:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 94–95 (part 2 of 2):

Hannad and Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, both saying: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Qabisah ibn Jabir, who said: "We set out as pilgrims (hujjaj). Whenever we had prayed the morning prayer (al-ghadah), we would walk alongside our mounts, conversing. One morning, while we were [walking], a gazelle (zaby) appeared to us, or he said: 'it crossed our path (barih).' A man who was with us threw a stone at it, and he did not miss its head, and it fell dead upon its back." He said: "We considered this a grave matter. When we arrived at Makkah, I went with him until we came to Umar, may Allah be pleased with him." He said: "So he related the story to him." He said: "Beside him was a man whose face was like a silver ingot (qalb fiddah), meaning Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. Umar turned to his companion and spoke with him. Then he turned to the man and said: 'Did you kill it intentionally or by mistake?' The man said: 'I intended to throw at it, but I did not intend to kill it.' Umar said: 'I see that you have combined intention and error (al-amd wal-khata'), go and take a sheep, slaughter it, give its meat in charity, and keep its hide.'" He said: "We rose from his presence, and I said to my companion: 'O man, honour the rites of Allah.' The Commander of the Faithful did not know what to rule for you until he asked his companion, and [the companion said]: 'Go and sacrifice your she-camel.' So he did that." Qabisah said: "And I do not recall the verse from Surah al-Ma'idah: ﴿Judged by two just men among you﴾." He said: "Umar was told of my remark, and he came upon us suddenly with his whip (al-dirrah) in hand." He said: "He struck my companion with the whip many times, saying: 'Did you kill [game] within the sacred precinct (al-haram) and make light of the ruling?'" He said: "Then he turned to me, and I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I will not make lawful for you today anything that is forbidden to you from me.'" He said: "[Umar] said: 'O Qabisah ibn Jabir, I see you are young in years, broad of chest, and eloquent of tongue, and a young man has nine good qualities and one bad quality, and the bad quality corrupts the good qualities. So beware of the slips of youth.'"

Hushaym narrated this story, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Qabisah, in a similar form. It was also narrated from Husayn, from al-Sha'bi, from Qabisah, in a similar form. And it was mentioned as a mursal report (with the Companion omitted) from Umar by Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani and Muhammad ibn Sirin.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, who said: Abu Jarir al-Bajali informed me: "I killed a gazelle while I was in the state of ihram (muhrim), so I mentioned that to Umar, and he said: 'Go to two men from among your brothers, and let them rule against you.' So I went to Abd al-Rahman and Sa'd, and they ruled against me [requiring] a male goat with a tawny-dark (a'far) colour (tays a'far)."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakî' narrated to us, Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Mukharriq, from Tariq, who said: "Arbad trampled a gazelle and killed it while he was in the state of ihram, so he came to Umar to be judged concerning it. Umar said to him: 'Judge with me.' So they ruled concerning it [requiring] a young male goat (jady), which had gathered water and trees (qad jama'a al-ma' wal-shajar). Then Umar said: ﴿Judged by two just men among you﴾."

In this there is evidence for the permissibility of the one who killed the game being one of the two judges, as stated by al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on them both.
