The scholars differed as to whether the ruling (al-hukumah) must be renewed for every case in which the muhrim commits [a violation], so that two just men must rule upon it even if the Companions had already ruled in a similar case, or whether one may suffice with the previous rulings of the Companions. There are two opinions. Al-Shafi'i and Ahmad said: one follows in this matter what the Companions ruled, and they made it an established legal ruling (shar'an muqarraran) from which one does not deviate; and what the Companions did not rule upon is referred to two just men. Malik and Abu Hanifah said: rather, a ruling is required in every single case, whether or not the Companions had a ruling in a similar case, based on the Most High's saying: ﴿Judged by two just men among you﴾.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿as an offering (hady) reaching the Ka'bah﴾, meaning: arriving at the Ka'bah. What is intended is its arrival at the sacred precinct (al-haram), by being slaughtered there and its meat distributed among the poor of the haram. This is agreed upon in this case.

* *

His saying: ﴿or expiation (kaffarah) [by] feeding the needy, or its equivalent in fasting﴾, meaning: if the muhrim does not find an animal equivalent to what he killed from the livestock, or if the game he killed is not of those that have equivalents, or if we say that in this context there is a choice (takhyir) among the compensation, the feeding, and the fasting, as is the view of Malik, Abu Hanifah, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, and the well-known view of Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on them all, based on the apparent wording of the verse, "or" (aw), for it denotes choice. The other view is that it is in sequence (tartib).

The form of this is that one turns to the monetary value: the killed game is assessed (yuqawwam) according to Malik, Abu Hanifah and his companions, Hammad, and Ibrahim. Al-Shafi'i said: its equivalent from the livestock is assessed, if it existed, and then food is bought with it and given in charity, so that each poor person receives one mudd of it according to al-Shafi'i, Malik, and the jurists of the Hijaz, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Abu Hanifah and his companions said: each poor person is fed two mudds, and this is the view of Mujahid.

Ahmad said: one mudd of wheat, or two mudds of other [grains]. If he does not find [food], or if we say there is choice, he fasts one day in place of feeding each poor person.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: he fasts one day in place of each sa' (saa'), as in the case of one who indulges in shaving [the head] and the like, for the Lawgiver (al-shari') commanded Ka'b ibn Ujrah to give a faraq (a measure) to six [people], or to fast three days, and the faraq is three sa's.

They differed concerning the place of this feeding. Al-Shafi'i said: its place is the haram, and this is the view of Ata'. Malik said: it is fed in the place where he hunted the game, or the nearest places to it. Abu Hanifah said: if he wishes he may feed [the poor] within the haram, and if he wishes he may feed them elsewhere.

Mention of the views of the early scholars (al-salaf) on this matter:

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿So its penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock, judged by two just men among you, as an offering reaching the Ka'bah, or an expiation [by] feeding the needy, or its equivalent in fasting﴾. He said: "When the muhrim kills game, its equivalent from the livestock is ruled upon him. If he finds its equivalent, he slaughters it and gives it in charity. If he does not find [it], he considers its price, then values that price in food, and fasts one day for each half sa' (nisf sa')." He said: "His saying: ﴿or an expiation [by] feeding the needy, or its equivalent in fasting﴾" — he said: "What is meant by food is fasting, that when food is available, its [compensation] is found."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the chain of Jarir.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿as an offering reaching the Ka'bah, or an expiation [by] feeding the needy, or its equivalent in fasting﴾: "When the muhrim kills any of the game, a ruling is made against him concerning it. If he kills a gazelle or the like, he must [sacrifice] a sheep to be slaughtered in Makkah. If he does not find one, [he must] feed six poor persons; if he does not find [the means], [he must] fast three days. If he kills a camel or the like, he must [sacrifice] a cow. If he does not find [one], he feeds twenty poor persons. If he does not find [the means], he fasts twenty days. If he kills an ostrich, a wild ass, or the like, he must [sacrifice] a camel (badanah) from the camels. If he does not find [one], he feeds thirty poor persons. If he does not find [the means], he fasts thirty days."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, and [Ibn Jarir] added: "And the food is one mudd for each [person] that satisfies them (tushbi'ahum)."

Jabir al-Ju'fi said, from Amir al-Sha'bi, Ata', and Mujahid: ﴿or its equivalent in fasting﴾. They said: "Food is only for one who cannot afford the offering (hady)." Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Similarly, Ibn Juraij narrated from Mujahid, and Asbat from al-Suddi, that it is in sequence (tartib).

Ata', Ikrimah, Mujahid (in the narration of al-Dahhak), and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: it is by choice (al-khiyar). This is a narration of al-Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir, may Allah the Most High have mercy on him, chose this view.

* *

His saying: ﴿that he may taste the consequence of his affair﴾, meaning: We have obligated upon him the expiation so that he may taste the punishment for his deed in which he committed the violation. ﴿Allah has pardoned what has passed﴾, meaning: in the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah), for whoever does good in Islam and follows the law of Allah and does not commit the disobedience.

Then He said: ﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾, meaning: whoever does that after its prohibition in Islam and after the legal ruling has reached him, Allah will take retribution from him. ﴿And Allah is Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution﴾.

Ibn Juraij said: I said to Ata': "What is ﴿Allah has pardoned what has passed﴾?" He said: "What occurred in the time of ignorance." I said: "And what is ﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾?" He said: "Whoever returns in Islam, Allah will take retribution from him, and in addition to that he is obliged to the expiation." I said: "Is there a prescribed penalty (hadd) for returning that you know of?" He said: "No." I said: "Do you see it as a right of the imam to punish him?" He said: "No. It is a sin he committed between himself and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but he must make atonement (yaftadi)." Ibn Jarir narrated it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (11/48).]

It was also said that its meaning is: Allah will take retribution from him through the expiation. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ata'.

Then the majority of the early and later scholars hold that whenever the muhrim kills game, the compensation becomes obligatory, and there is no difference between the first and the second [offence] (and the second and the third), however many times it recurs, whether the error in it or the intention.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: "Whoever kills any of the game by mistake while in the state of ihram, a ruling is made against him concerning it every time he kills it. But if he kills it intentionally, a ruling is made against him concerning it only once. If he returns [to it], it is said to him: 'Allah will take retribution from you, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said.'"

Ibn Jarir said: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id and Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us together, from Hisham (that is, Ibn Hassan), from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning one who killed game and a ruling was made against him, then he returned: "He is not ruled against; Allah takes retribution from him."

Likewise said Shurayh, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. Ibn Jarir narrated these, then he chose the first view.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Abbas ibn Yazid al-Abdi narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Zayd Abi al-Mu'alla, from al-Hasan al-Basri, that a man killed game, and [the ruling] was lenient toward him, then he returned and killed another game, so a fire descended from heaven and burned him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾.

Ibn Jarir said concerning His saying: ﴿And Allah is Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution﴾: "He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah is Impregnable in His dominion; no one overpowers Him, and nothing prevents Him from taking retribution against whomever He takes retribution from, nor from punishing whoever He wishes to punish, because the creation is His creation and the command is His command; to Him belong might and invincibility."

* *

His saying: ﴿Owner of Retribution﴾ means: He is One who punishes whoever disobeys Him for his disobedience toward Him.

Al-Walibi reported from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: ﴿Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your spears can reach﴾. He said: it is the weak of the game and its young, with which Allah tests His servants during their state of ihram, to the extent that they could take it with their hands. So Allah forbade them to approach it.

Mujahid said: ﴿that your hands can reach﴾ means the young of the game and its chicks, and ﴿your spears﴾ means its large ones.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse was revealed concerning the ʿUmrah of al-Hudaybiyyah, when wild animals, birds and game came to them in their camps in a way they had never seen before, so Allah forbade them to kill it while they were in ihram.

﴿That Allah may make evident who fears Him unseen﴾ means: He, the Exalted, tests them with the game that comes to them in their camps, and they are able to take it with their hands and spears, secretly and openly, so that He may make evident the obedience of those among them who obey in private and in public, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Mulk: 12].

* *

As for His statement here: ﴿So whoever transgresses after that﴾, al-Suddi and others said: meaning after this warning, admonition and advance notice. ﴿For him is a painful punishment﴾, that is, for his opposition to the command and law of Allah.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in ihram﴾. This is a prohibition from Him, the Exalted, against killing game while in the state of ihram, and a prohibition against engaging in it therein. This applies in meaning to the edible game and what results from it and from other than it. As for non-edible land animals, according to al-Shafi'i it is permissible for the muhrim to kill them. The majority hold that killing them is also prohibited, and no exception is made from this except what is established in the two Sahihs through the route of al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAisha, the Mother of the Believers, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Five harmful creatures may be killed both within the sacred area and outside it: the crow, the kite, the scorpion, the rat, and the rabid dog." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3314 and Sahih Muslim no. 1198.]

And Malik narrated from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Five creatures of the beasts, there is no sin upon the muhrim for killing them: the crow, the kite, the scorpion, the rat, and the rabid dog." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1826 and Sahih Muslim no. 1199.]

Ayyub narrated it from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, similarly. Ayyub said: I said to Nafi': what about the snake? He said: the snake, there is no doubt about it, and there is no disagreement about killing it. [Sahih Muslim no. 1199.]

Among the scholars, such as Malik and Ahmad, some extended the rabid dog to include the wolf, the predatory beasts, the tiger and the leopard, because they are more harmful than it, and Allah knows best. Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah and Zayd ibn Aslam said: the rabid dog includes all these aggressive predators. Whoever holds this view took as evidence what is narrated, that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against ʿUtbah ibn Abi Lahab, he said: "O Allah, set Your dog upon him in al-Sham." [Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/339) through the route of Zuhayr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ, from Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArubah, from Qatadah, mursal, and he mentioned the story. And Abu Nuʿaym narrated it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (p. 163) through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from ʿUthman ibn ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, and he mentioned the story. And al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/338) through the route of ʿAbbas ibn al-Fadl, from al-Aswad ibn Shayban, from Abu Nawfal ibn Abi ʿAqrab, from his father, and he mentioned the story.] So a lion ate him at al-Zarqa'. They said: if he kills other than these, he must pay compensation, such as the hyena, the fox, the wild cat and the like.

Malik said: Likewise, excepted from this are the young of these five mentioned creatures, and the young of the aggressive predators added to them.

Al-Shafi'i said: it is permissible for the muhrim to kill every animal whose meat is not eaten, and there is no difference between its young and its adult. He made the common reason the fact that it is not eaten.

Abu Hanifah said: the muhrim may kill the rabid dog and the wolf, because it is a wild dog. If he kills other than these two, he must pay compensation, except that if another predator attacks him and he kills it, then there is no compensation upon him. This is the view of al-Awza'i and al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy.

Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl said: he must pay compensation for whatever else, even if it attacks him.

Some people said: what is meant here by the crow is the abqa' (the piebald crow), which has whiteness on its belly and back, not the adra' (the black one) or the a'sam (the white one). This is based on what al-Nasa'i narrated from ʿAmr ibn ʿAli al-Fallas, from Yahya al-Qattan, from Shuʿbah, from Qatadah, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿAisha, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Five creatures the muhrim may kill: the snake, the rat, the kite, the abqa' crow, and the rabid dog."

The majority hold that what is meant by it is more general than that, based on the unrestricted wording established in the two Sahihs.

Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the muhrim may not kill the crow unless it attacks him and harms him.

Mujahid ibn Jabr and a group said: he does not kill it but throws at it. The same is reported from ʿAli.

Hushaym narrated: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Nuʿm, from Abu Saʿid, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he was asked what the muhrim may kill, and he said: "The snake, the scorpion, the fuwaysiqah (the rat), he may throw at the crow but not kill it, the rabid dog, the kite, and the aggressive predator."

Abu Dawud narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and al-Tirmidhi from Ahmad ibn Mani', both from Hushaym. And Ibn Majah narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, both from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, and he is weak, with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: this is a hasan hadith. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1848, Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 838 and Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3089.]

* *

As for His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever among you kills it intentionally, then the compensation is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saʿid al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, who said: I was informed from Tawus who said: one is not judged for someone who hits game by mistake; judgment is only made against the one who hits it intentionally.

This is a strange view from Tawus, and he adheres to the apparent meaning of the verse.

Mujahid ibn Jubayr said: what is meant here by the intentional one is the one who aims to kill the game while forgetting his ihram. As for the one who intentionally kills game while remembering his ihram, his matter is too grave to be covered by expiation, and his ihram is void.

Ibn Jarir narrated this from him through the route of Ibn Abi Najih, Layth ibn Abi Sulaym and others, from him. This too is a strange view. What the majority hold is that the intentional and the forgetful are equal in the obligation of compensation upon them. Al-Zuhri said: the Book indicates the intentional one, and the Sunnah established the forgetful one. The meaning of this is that the Qur'an indicates the obligation of compensation upon the intentional one and his sinfulness, by His saying: ﴿That he may taste the consequence of his deed. Allah has pardoned what is past; but whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾. And the Sunnah came with the rulings of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions establishing the obligation of compensation for error, just as the Book indicated it for the intentional. Also, killing game is destruction, and destruction is liable to compensation whether intentional or forgetful, but the intentional one is sinful, while the one who errs is not blameworthy.

* *

As for His statement: ﴿So the compensation is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock﴾. Ibn Jarir related that Ibn Mas'ud recited it: "So its compensation is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock."

In His statement: ﴿So the compensation is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock﴾, according to each of the two readings, there is evidence for what Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and the majority held: that compensation is obligatory from the like of what the muhrim killed, when it has a like among domestic animals. This is in contrast to Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, who required the value regardless of whether the game killed had a like or not. He said: he has the choice, if he wishes he gives its price in charity, and if he wishes he buys with it an offering. But what the Companions ruled regarding the like is more deserving of following, for they ruled concerning the ostrich with a camel, concerning the wild cow with a cow, and concerning the gazelle with a female goat. The reports of the Companions' judgments and their chains are established in the book "al-Ahkam." As for when the game has no like, Ibn ʿAbbas ruled concerning it with its price, to be carried to Makkah. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it. As for His statement: ﴿judged by two just men among you﴾, meaning that the compensation is judged, in the case of a like, or by value in the case of no like, by two just Muslims. The scholars differed concerning the killer: can he be one of the two judges? On two views: the first: no, because he may be suspected in judging in his own case, and this is the view of Malik. The second: yes, for the generality of the verse. This is the view of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad.

Those of the first view argued that a judge cannot be the one judged against in the same case.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Abu Nuʿaym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Jaʿfar, that is Ibn Burqan, narrated to us, from Maymun ibn Mihran: that a Bedouin came to Abu Bakr and said: I killed game while I was in ihram, so what do you think the compensation upon me is? Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who was sitting with him: What do you think about what he said? The Bedouin said: I came to you while you are the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking you, and now you ask someone else? Abu Bakr said: And what do you deny? Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So the compensation is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock, judged by two just men among you﴾. So I consulted my companion until we agreed on a matter, and we command you with it.

This is a good chain, but it is disconnected between Maymun and al-Siddiq, and such a thing may be tolerated here. Al-Siddiq explained the ruling to him gently and patiently, seeing him as an ignorant Bedouin, and the remedy for ignorance is teaching. As for when the one who raises the objection is attributed to knowledge, then Ibn Jarir has said:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 94–95 (part 2 of 2):

Hannad and Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, both saying: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Qabisah ibn Jabir, who said: "We set out as pilgrims (hujjaj). Whenever we had prayed the morning prayer (al-ghadah), we would walk alongside our mounts, conversing. One morning, while we were [walking], a gazelle (zaby) appeared to us, or he said: 'it crossed our path (barih).' A man who was with us threw a stone at it, and he did not miss its head, and it fell dead upon its back." He said: "We considered this a grave matter. When we arrived at Makkah, I went with him until we came to Umar, may Allah be pleased with him." He said: "So he related the story to him." He said: "Beside him was a man whose face was like a silver ingot (qalb fiddah), meaning Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. Umar turned to his companion and spoke with him. Then he turned to the man and said: 'Did you kill it intentionally or by mistake?' The man said: 'I intended to throw at it, but I did not intend to kill it.' Umar said: 'I see that you have combined intention and error (al-amd wal-khata'), go and take a sheep, slaughter it, give its meat in charity, and keep its hide.'" He said: "We rose from his presence, and I said to my companion: 'O man, honour the rites of Allah.' The Commander of the Faithful did not know what to rule for you until he asked his companion, and [the companion said]: 'Go and sacrifice your she-camel.' So he did that." Qabisah said: "And I do not recall the verse from Surah al-Ma'idah: ﴿Judged by two just men among you﴾." He said: "Umar was told of my remark, and he came upon us suddenly with his whip (al-dirrah) in hand." He said: "He struck my companion with the whip many times, saying: 'Did you kill [game] within the sacred precinct (al-haram) and make light of the ruling?'" He said: "Then he turned to me, and I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I will not make lawful for you today anything that is forbidden to you from me.'" He said: "[Umar] said: 'O Qabisah ibn Jabir, I see you are young in years, broad of chest, and eloquent of tongue, and a young man has nine good qualities and one bad quality, and the bad quality corrupts the good qualities. So beware of the slips of youth.'"

Hushaym narrated this story, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Qabisah, in a similar form. It was also narrated from Husayn, from al-Sha'bi, from Qabisah, in a similar form. And it was mentioned as a mursal report (with the Companion omitted) from Umar by Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani and Muhammad ibn Sirin.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, who said: Abu Jarir al-Bajali informed me: "I killed a gazelle while I was in the state of ihram (muhrim), so I mentioned that to Umar, and he said: 'Go to two men from among your brothers, and let them rule against you.' So I went to Abd al-Rahman and Sa'd, and they ruled against me [requiring] a male goat with a tawny-dark (a'far) colour (tays a'far)."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakî' narrated to us, Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Mukharriq, from Tariq, who said: "Arbad trampled a gazelle and killed it while he was in the state of ihram, so he came to Umar to be judged concerning it. Umar said to him: 'Judge with me.' So they ruled concerning it [requiring] a young male goat (jady), which had gathered water and trees (qad jama'a al-ma' wal-shajar). Then Umar said: ﴿Judged by two just men among you﴾."

In this there is evidence for the permissibility of the one who killed the game being one of the two judges, as stated by al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on them both.

The scholars differed as to whether the ruling (al-hukumah) must be renewed for every case in which the muhrim commits [a violation], so that two just men must rule upon it even if the Companions had already ruled in a similar case, or whether one may suffice with the previous rulings of the Companions. There are two opinions. Al-Shafi'i and Ahmad said: one follows in this matter what the Companions ruled, and they made it an established legal ruling (shar'an muqarraran) from which one does not deviate; and what the Companions did not rule upon is referred to two just men. Malik and Abu Hanifah said: rather, a ruling is required in every single case, whether or not the Companions had a ruling in a similar case, based on the Most High's saying: ﴿Judged by two just men among you﴾.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿as an offering (hady) reaching the Ka'bah﴾, meaning: arriving at the Ka'bah. What is intended is its arrival at the sacred precinct (al-haram), by being slaughtered there and its meat distributed among the poor of the haram. This is agreed upon in this case.

* *

His saying: ﴿or expiation (kaffarah) [by] feeding the needy, or its equivalent in fasting﴾, meaning: if the muhrim does not find an animal equivalent to what he killed from the livestock, or if the game he killed is not of those that have equivalents, or if we say that in this context there is a choice (takhyir) among the compensation, the feeding, and the fasting, as is the view of Malik, Abu Hanifah, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, and the well-known view of Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on them all, based on the apparent wording of the verse, "or" (aw), for it denotes choice. The other view is that it is in sequence (tartib).

The form of this is that one turns to the monetary value: the killed game is assessed (yuqawwam) according to Malik, Abu Hanifah and his companions, Hammad, and Ibrahim. Al-Shafi'i said: its equivalent from the livestock is assessed, if it existed, and then food is bought with it and given in charity, so that each poor person receives one mudd of it according to al-Shafi'i, Malik, and the jurists of the Hijaz, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Abu Hanifah and his companions said: each poor person is fed two mudds, and this is the view of Mujahid.

Ahmad said: one mudd of wheat, or two mudds of other [grains]. If he does not find [food], or if we say there is choice, he fasts one day in place of feeding each poor person.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: he fasts one day in place of each sa' (saa'), as in the case of one who indulges in shaving [the head] and the like, for the Lawgiver (al-shari') commanded Ka'b ibn Ujrah to give a faraq (a measure) to six [people], or to fast three days, and the faraq is three sa's.

They differed concerning the place of this feeding. Al-Shafi'i said: its place is the haram, and this is the view of Ata'. Malik said: it is fed in the place where he hunted the game, or the nearest places to it. Abu Hanifah said: if he wishes he may feed [the poor] within the haram, and if he wishes he may feed them elsewhere.

Mention of the views of the early scholars (al-salaf) on this matter:

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿So its penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock, judged by two just men among you, as an offering reaching the Ka'bah, or an expiation [by] feeding the needy, or its equivalent in fasting﴾. He said: "When the muhrim kills game, its equivalent from the livestock is ruled upon him. If he finds its equivalent, he slaughters it and gives it in charity. If he does not find [it], he considers its price, then values that price in food, and fasts one day for each half sa' (nisf sa')." He said: "His saying: ﴿or an expiation [by] feeding the needy, or its equivalent in fasting﴾" — he said: "What is meant by food is fasting, that when food is available, its [compensation] is found."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the chain of Jarir.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿as an offering reaching the Ka'bah, or an expiation [by] feeding the needy, or its equivalent in fasting﴾: "When the muhrim kills any of the game, a ruling is made against him concerning it. If he kills a gazelle or the like, he must [sacrifice] a sheep to be slaughtered in Makkah. If he does not find one, [he must] feed six poor persons; if he does not find [the means], [he must] fast three days. If he kills a camel or the like, he must [sacrifice] a cow. If he does not find [one], he feeds twenty poor persons. If he does not find [the means], he fasts twenty days. If he kills an ostrich, a wild ass, or the like, he must [sacrifice] a camel (badanah) from the camels. If he does not find [one], he feeds thirty poor persons. If he does not find [the means], he fasts thirty days."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, and [Ibn Jarir] added: "And the food is one mudd for each [person] that satisfies them (tushbi'ahum)."

Jabir al-Ju'fi said, from Amir al-Sha'bi, Ata', and Mujahid: ﴿or its equivalent in fasting﴾. They said: "Food is only for one who cannot afford the offering (hady)." Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Similarly, Ibn Juraij narrated from Mujahid, and Asbat from al-Suddi, that it is in sequence (tartib).

Ata', Ikrimah, Mujahid (in the narration of al-Dahhak), and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: it is by choice (al-khiyar). This is a narration of al-Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir, may Allah the Most High have mercy on him, chose this view.

* *

His saying: ﴿that he may taste the consequence of his affair﴾, meaning: We have obligated upon him the expiation so that he may taste the punishment for his deed in which he committed the violation. ﴿Allah has pardoned what has passed﴾, meaning: in the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah), for whoever does good in Islam and follows the law of Allah and does not commit the disobedience.

Then He said: ﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾, meaning: whoever does that after its prohibition in Islam and after the legal ruling has reached him, Allah will take retribution from him. ﴿And Allah is Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution﴾.

Ibn Juraij said: I said to Ata': "What is ﴿Allah has pardoned what has passed﴾?" He said: "What occurred in the time of ignorance." I said: "And what is ﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾?" He said: "Whoever returns in Islam, Allah will take retribution from him, and in addition to that he is obliged to the expiation." I said: "Is there a prescribed penalty (hadd) for returning that you know of?" He said: "No." I said: "Do you see it as a right of the imam to punish him?" He said: "No. It is a sin he committed between himself and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but he must make atonement (yaftadi)." Ibn Jarir narrated it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (11/48).]

It was also said that its meaning is: Allah will take retribution from him through the expiation. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ata'.

Then the majority of the early and later scholars hold that whenever the muhrim kills game, the compensation becomes obligatory, and there is no difference between the first and the second [offence] (and the second and the third), however many times it recurs, whether the error in it or the intention.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: "Whoever kills any of the game by mistake while in the state of ihram, a ruling is made against him concerning it every time he kills it. But if he kills it intentionally, a ruling is made against him concerning it only once. If he returns [to it], it is said to him: 'Allah will take retribution from you, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said.'"

Ibn Jarir said: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id and Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us together, from Hisham (that is, Ibn Hassan), from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning one who killed game and a ruling was made against him, then he returned: "He is not ruled against; Allah takes retribution from him."

Likewise said Shurayh, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. Ibn Jarir narrated these, then he chose the first view.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Abbas ibn Yazid al-Abdi narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Zayd Abi al-Mu'alla, from al-Hasan al-Basri, that a man killed game, and [the ruling] was lenient toward him, then he returned and killed another game, so a fire descended from heaven and burned him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾.

Ibn Jarir said concerning His saying: ﴿And Allah is Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution﴾: "He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah is Impregnable in His dominion; no one overpowers Him, and nothing prevents Him from taking retribution against whomever He takes retribution from, nor from punishing whoever He wishes to punish, because the creation is His creation and the command is His command; to Him belong might and invincibility."

* *

His saying: ﴿Owner of Retribution﴾ means: He is One who punishes whoever disobeys Him for his disobedience toward Him.

Ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn Abbas (in one narration from him), and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others, regarding His words: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you﴾, that it means what is hunted from it fresh, ﴿and its food﴾ means what is taken from it preserved, salted and dried for provision.

Ibn Abbas, in the well-known narration from him, said: its game is what is taken from it alive, and ﴿its food﴾ is what it casts up dead.

The same was related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Zayd ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Amr, and Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with them all, and from Ikrimah, Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and al-Hasan al-Basri.

Sufyan ibn Uyayna said, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq that he said: ﴿its food﴾ is all that is in it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd related to us, Jarir related to us, from Mughira, from Simak, who said: I was told from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr addressed the people and said: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food, as a provision for you﴾, and its food is what it casts up.

He said: Ya'qub related to us, Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food﴾, he said: ﴿its food﴾ is what it casts up.

Ikrimah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿its food﴾ is what it casts up of carrion. Ibn Jarir also narrated it.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: its food is what it casts up alive, or what recedes from it and dies. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar related to us, Abd al-Wahhab related to us, Ayyub related to us, from Nafi', that Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hurayra asked Ibn Umar, saying: The sea has cast up many dead fish; shall we eat them? He said: Do not eat them. When Abdullah returned to his family, he took the Mushaf and recited Surat al-Ma'ida, and came to this verse: ﴿and its food, as a provision for you and for the travellers﴾, and said: Go and tell him to eat it, for it is its food.

Thus Ibn Jarir chose that what is meant by "its food" is what dies in it. He said: A report has been transmitted concerning this, and some of them transmit it as a statement of a Companion (mawquf).

Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, he said: Abdah ibn Sulayman related to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Salama related to us, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food, as a provision for you﴾, and said: its food is what it casts up dead.

Then he said: Some of them stopped this hadith at Abu Hurayra: Hannad related to us, Ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra regarding His words: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food﴾, he said: its food is what it casts up dead.

As for His words: ﴿as a provision for you and for the travellers﴾, that is, a benefit and sustenance for you, O addressees, ﴿and for the travellers﴾, which is the plural of sayyar. Ikrimah said: for those who are at the sea's edge, and for the travellers (al-sayyara): the journey. 

Others said: its fresh part is for one who hunts it from those present by the sea, and ﴿its food﴾ is what dies in it or is hunted from it and salted and dried as provision for travellers and those far from the sea.

Something similar was related from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Suddi and others. The majority of scholars have used this noble verse as evidence for the permissibility of the carrion of the sea, together with what Imam Malik ibn Anas related from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment toward the coast and appointed Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah over them; they were three hundred, and I was among them. He said: We set out until, when we were on part of the way, the provisions ran out, so Abu Ubayda ordered the provisions of that army to be gathered, and it all came to two sacks of dates. He said: He would feed us a little each day, until it ran out, and we would get only one date each. I said: And what does one date avail? He said: We found its loss when it ran out. He said: Then we reached the sea, and there was a fish like a dune (zarib). That army ate from it for eighteen nights. Then Abu Ubayda ordered two of its ribs to be erected, then ordered a riding camel to be saddled, and it passed beneath them and did not touch them. [Muwatta' 2/930]

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2483 and Sahih Muslim no. 1935], and it has several chains from Jabir.

In Sahih Muslim, from the narration of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: there was on the sea-shore something like a huge sand-hill; we came to it, and there was a creature called the anbar. He said: Abu Ubayda said: it is carrion. Then he said: No, we are the messengers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and in the way of Allah, and you have been compelled, so eat. He said: We stayed on it for a month, and we were three hundred, until we grew fat. We would dip into the hollow of its eye with pitchers for the fat, and cut from it pieces like a bull's, or like the size of a bull. He said: Abu Ubayda took thirteen men of ours and seated them in the hollow of its eye, and took one of its ribs and erected it, then the largest camel with us was saddled and passed beneath it. We took provision of its meat in strips. When we came to Madina we came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and he said: "It is a provision that Allah brought forth for you; do you have any of its meat with you, that you might feed us?" He said: We sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) some of it, and he ate it. In some narrations of Muslim: they were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when they found this fish. Some said: it is a separate incident; others said: rather it is one event, but they were first with the Prophet (ﷺ), then he sent them as a detachment with Abu Ubayda, and they found this in that detachment with Abu Ubayda. And Allah knows best. [Sahih Muslim no. 1935]

Malik said, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Sa'id ibn Salama, of the family of Ibn al-Azraq, that al-Mughira ibn Abi Burda, who is of Banu Abd al-Dar, informed him that he heard Abu Hurayra say: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: O Messenger of Allah, we sail the sea and carry only a little water with us; if we perform wudu with it we become thirsty; shall we perform wudu with sea water? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Its water is pure, and its carrion is lawful."

This hadith was related by the two Imams al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and the people of the four Sunan, and it was authenticated by al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Khuzayma, Ibn Hibban and others. It has been related from a group of Companions from the Prophet (ﷺ) in similar terms.

Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related, by several routes, from Hammad ibn Salama: Abu al-Muhazzim related to us, he is Yazid ibn Sufyan, I heard Abu Hurayra say: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a Hajj or an Umra, and we encountered a swarm of locusts, and we began striking them with our sticks and whips and killing them, and we were troubled about it, and said: What shall we do, while we are in ihram? We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "There is no harm in the game of the sea." Abu al-Muhazzim is weak, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Majah said: Harun ibn Abd Allah al-Hammal related to us, Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us, Ziyad ibn Abd Allah related to us, from Ulatha, from Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Jabir and Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) when he invoked against locusts said: "O Allah, destroy their large ones, kill their small ones, spoil their eggs, cut off their offspring, and seize them by their mouths away from our livelihood and sustenance, for You are the Hearer of supplication." Khalid said: O Messenger of Allah, how do you invoke against an army of the armies of Allah to cut off its offspring? He said: "Locusts are the spawn of the fish in the sea." Hashim said: Ziyad said: one who saw the fish spawning them told me. Ibn Majah alone related it. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3221; al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "This chain is weak because of the weakness of Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim; Ibn al-Jawzi listed it among the fabrications through Harun ibn Abd Allah, and said: it is not sound from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Musa ibn Muhammad weakened it."]

Al-Shafi'i related, from Sa'id, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, that he disapproved of those who hunt locusts within the Sacred Precinct.

Those jurists who held that the sea creatures may be eaten, and did not exclude anything from that, have argued from this noble verse. It has already been mentioned from the Siddiq that he said: ﴿its food﴾ is all that is in it.

Some have excluded frogs and permitted all others, on the basis of what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i related, through the narration of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id ibn Khalid, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Uthman al-Taymi, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) "forbade the killing of the frog." [Musnad 3/453; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 5269; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/210.] And in al-Nasa'i, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade killing the frog, and said: its croaking is glorification. [I did not find it in my search of Sunan al-Nasa'i, and perhaps I will locate it later. It was related by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. 1852, through al-Hajjaj ibn Muhammad from Shu'ba, from Qatada, from Zurara ibn Awfa, from Abd Allah ibn Amr.]

Others said: Of the game of the sea, fish may be eaten, and frogs may not be eaten. They differed regarding the rest: it was said that all of that may be eaten, and it was said that it may not. It was also said: whatever has a counterpart on land that is eaten, its counterpart in the sea may be eaten, and whatever has a counterpart that is not eaten, it is not eaten. All these are views within the school of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: What dies in the sea may not be eaten, just as what dies on land may not be eaten, because of the generality of His words: ﴿Carrion is forbidden to you﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 3].

A hadith has come with something similar to that. Ibn Mardawayh said:

Abd al-Baqi (that is, Ibn Qani') related to us, al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tustari and Abd Allah ibn Musa ibn Abi Uthman related to us, both said: al-Husayn ibn Zayd al-Tabban related to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What you hunt while it is alive and it dies, eat it; and what the sea casts up dead and floating, do not eat it."

Then he related it through the route of Isma'il ibn Umayya and Yahya ibn Abi Unaysa, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, with the same. And it is munkar. [Its strangeness is because it contradicts the verse and the sound hadiths, such as the hadith "Its water is pure, its carrion is lawful," and the hadith of the anbar.]

The majority of the followers of Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal have argued with the hadith of the "anbar" mentioned earlier, and with the hadith "Its water is pure, its carrion is lawful," which has also been mentioned earlier.

Imam Abu Abd Allah al-Shafi'i related, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two carcasses and two bloods have been made lawful for us. As for the two carcasses, they are fish and locusts; as for the two bloods, they are liver and spleen."

Ahmad and Ibn Majah, al-Daraqutni and al-Bayhaqi also related it. It has supporting reports, and it has been related as a statement of a Companion (mawquf), and Allah knows best.

And His saying: ﴿The game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram (ihram: the sacred state entered for pilgrimage or 'umrah)﴾. That is, while you are in your state of ihram, hunting is forbidden to you. This indicates the prohibition of that. If the muhrim (one in ihram) hunts game deliberately, he sins and must pay compensation (jaza'). If he does so by mistake, he must still pay compensation, and it is unlawful for him to eat it, because for him it is like carrion (maytah). The same applies to others, whether they are in ihram or not, according to Malik and al-Shafi'i in one of his two opinions. This is also the view of 'Ata', al-Qasim, Salim, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and others.

If he eats it, or any part of it, is he obliged to pay compensation? On this, there are two opinions among the scholars:

The first: Yes. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', who said: "If he slaughters it and then eats it, he owes two expiations (kaffaratan)." A group held this view.

The second: He owes no compensation for eating it. Malik ibn Anas explicitly stated this.

Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: "This is the position of the jurists of the major cities and the majority of scholars." Then Abu 'Umar explained it by comparison with a man who commits intercourse, then again, then again, before being punished, for whom there is only one legal penalty (hadd).

Abu Hanifah said: he owes the value (qimah) of what he ate.

Abu Thawr said: "If the muhrim kills game, he owes its compensation, and it is lawful for him to eat that game, though I dislike it for the one who killed it, based on the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'The game of the land is lawful for you as long as you do not hunt it or it is not hunted for your sake.'"

This hadith will be explained later. His statement that it is permissible for the killer is unusual. As for others, there is disagreement. We have already mentioned the prohibition from earlier authorities. Others said it is permitted for someone other than the killer, whether muhrim or muhill (one not in ihram), based on this hadith. And Allah knows best.

As for when a lawful (hal) person hunts game and gives it as a gift to a muhrim, some have held that it is permitted absolutely, without distinguishing whether he hunted it for his sake or not. Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr narrated this view from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Abu Hurairah, al-Zubair ibn al-'Awwam, Ka'b al-Ahbar, Mujahid, 'Ata' (in one narration), and Sa'id ibn Jubair. He said: "The people of Kufa also held this view."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to him, from Abu Hurairah, that he was asked about the meat of game that a lawful person had hunted: may a muhrim eat it? He gave them a ruling permitting it. Then he met 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and informed him of what he had ruled. 'Umar said: "If you had ruled otherwise, I would have struck your head."

Others said: It is not permissible for a muhrim to eat game at all, and they prohibited it absolutely, based on the general wording of this noble verse.

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus and 'Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayyah, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he disliked the muhrim eating the meat of game. He said: "It is general (mubhamah)," meaning His statement: ﴿The game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram﴾.

He said: Ma'mar informed me, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn 'Umar: that he disliked for the muhrim to eat from the meat of game in every case.

Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, the same.

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: Tawus, Jabir ibn Zayd also held this view, and al-Thawri and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh (in one narration) adopted it. Something similar has also been narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. Ibn Jarir narrated it through Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that 'Ali disliked the meat of game for the muhrim in every case.

Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh (in one narration), and the majority said: If the lawful person intended the muhrim by that hunt, it is not permissible for the muhrim to eat it, based on the hadith of al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah: that he gave the Prophet ﷺ a wild donkey while he was at al-Abwa' (or Waddan), and he returned it to him. When he saw the effect on his face, he said: "We only returned it to you because we are in ihram."

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs, with many wordings. [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 1825, 2573; Sahih Muslim, no. 1193.] They said: its meaning is that the Prophet ﷺ thought it had been hunted for his sake, so he returned it for that reason. But if it was not hunted with him in mind, it is permissible for him to eat from it, based on the hadith of Abu Qatadah, when he hunted a wild ass, which was lawful (for him, as he was not in ihram), while his companions were in ihram, and they hesitated to eat it. Then they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Did any of you point to it, or help in killing it?" They said: "No." He said: "Then eat." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also ate from it.

This story is also established in the two Sahihs with many wordings. [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 2914, 5490; Sahih Muslim, no. 1196.]

Imam Ahmad said: Sa'id ibn Mansur and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, both saying: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from al-Mutallib ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hantab, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and Qutaybah said in his narration: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'The game of the land is lawful for you,'" [Sa'id said: "while you are in ihram"] "as long as you do not hunt it or it is not hunted for you."

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i all narrated it likewise from Qutaybah. Al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know that al-Mutallib heard from Jabir." [Footnote: Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1851; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 846; Sunan al-Nasa'i, 5/187.]

Imam Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i also narrated it through 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from his client al-Mutallib, from Jabir, then said: "This is the best and most analogically sound hadith narrated on this subject."

Malik narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, who said: "I saw 'Uthman ibn 'Affan at al-'Araj, while he was in ihram, on a hot day, having covered his face with a red velvet cloth (qatifah urjuwan). Then meat of game was brought to him, and he said to his companions: 'Eat.' They said: 'Will you not eat?' He said: 'I am not like your condition; it was hunted for my sake.'" [Footnote: Al-Muwatta', 1/354.] [Footnote: Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, did not address the explanation of the remaining verses, as in all the manuscript copies; perhaps that is, Allah knows best, because he had already touched on their meanings in the similar passages in Surat al-Baqarah.]

Ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn Abbas (in one narration from him), and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others, regarding His words: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you﴾, that it means what is hunted from it fresh, ﴿and its food﴾ means what is taken from it preserved, salted and dried for provision.

Ibn Abbas, in the well-known narration from him, said: its game is what is taken from it alive, and ﴿its food﴾ is what it casts up dead.

The same was related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Zayd ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Amr, and Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with them all, and from Ikrimah, Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and al-Hasan al-Basri.

Sufyan ibn Uyayna said, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq that he said: ﴿its food﴾ is all that is in it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd related to us, Jarir related to us, from Mughira, from Simak, who said: I was told from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr addressed the people and said: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food, as a provision for you﴾, and its food is what it casts up.

He said: Ya'qub related to us, Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food﴾, he said: ﴿its food﴾ is what it casts up.

Ikrimah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿its food﴾ is what it casts up of carrion. Ibn Jarir also narrated it.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: its food is what it casts up alive, or what recedes from it and dies. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar related to us, Abd al-Wahhab related to us, Ayyub related to us, from Nafi', that Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hurayra asked Ibn Umar, saying: The sea has cast up many dead fish; shall we eat them? He said: Do not eat them. When Abdullah returned to his family, he took the Mushaf and recited Surat al-Ma'ida, and came to this verse: ﴿and its food, as a provision for you and for the travellers﴾, and said: Go and tell him to eat it, for it is its food.

Thus Ibn Jarir chose that what is meant by "its food" is what dies in it. He said: A report has been transmitted concerning this, and some of them transmit it as a statement of a Companion (mawquf).

Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, he said: Abdah ibn Sulayman related to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Salama related to us, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food, as a provision for you﴾, and said: its food is what it casts up dead.

Then he said: Some of them stopped this hadith at Abu Hurayra: Hannad related to us, Ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra regarding His words: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food﴾, he said: its food is what it casts up dead.

As for His words: ﴿as a provision for you and for the travellers﴾, that is, a benefit and sustenance for you, O addressees, ﴿and for the travellers﴾, which is the plural of sayyar. Ikrimah said: for those who are at the sea's edge, and for the travellers (al-sayyara): the journey. 

Others said: its fresh part is for one who hunts it from those present by the sea, and ﴿its food﴾ is what dies in it or is hunted from it and salted and dried as provision for travellers and those far from the sea.

Something similar was related from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Suddi and others. The majority of scholars have used this noble verse as evidence for the permissibility of the carrion of the sea, together with what Imam Malik ibn Anas related from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment toward the coast and appointed Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah over them; they were three hundred, and I was among them. He said: We set out until, when we were on part of the way, the provisions ran out, so Abu Ubayda ordered the provisions of that army to be gathered, and it all came to two sacks of dates. He said: He would feed us a little each day, until it ran out, and we would get only one date each. I said: And what does one date avail? He said: We found its loss when it ran out. He said: Then we reached the sea, and there was a fish like a dune (zarib). That army ate from it for eighteen nights. Then Abu Ubayda ordered two of its ribs to be erected, then ordered a riding camel to be saddled, and it passed beneath them and did not touch them. [Muwatta' 2/930]

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2483 and Sahih Muslim no. 1935], and it has several chains from Jabir.

In Sahih Muslim, from the narration of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: there was on the sea-shore something like a huge sand-hill; we came to it, and there was a creature called the anbar. He said: Abu Ubayda said: it is carrion. Then he said: No, we are the messengers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and in the way of Allah, and you have been compelled, so eat. He said: We stayed on it for a month, and we were three hundred, until we grew fat. We would dip into the hollow of its eye with pitchers for the fat, and cut from it pieces like a bull's, or like the size of a bull. He said: Abu Ubayda took thirteen men of ours and seated them in the hollow of its eye, and took one of its ribs and erected it, then the largest camel with us was saddled and passed beneath it. We took provision of its meat in strips. When we came to Madina we came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and he said: "It is a provision that Allah brought forth for you; do you have any of its meat with you, that you might feed us?" He said: We sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) some of it, and he ate it. In some narrations of Muslim: they were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when they found this fish. Some said: it is a separate incident; others said: rather it is one event, but they were first with the Prophet (ﷺ), then he sent them as a detachment with Abu Ubayda, and they found this in that detachment with Abu Ubayda. And Allah knows best. [Sahih Muslim no. 1935]

Malik said, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Sa'id ibn Salama, of the family of Ibn al-Azraq, that al-Mughira ibn Abi Burda, who is of Banu Abd al-Dar, informed him that he heard Abu Hurayra say: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: O Messenger of Allah, we sail the sea and carry only a little water with us; if we perform wudu with it we become thirsty; shall we perform wudu with sea water? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Its water is pure, and its carrion is lawful."

This hadith was related by the two Imams al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and the people of the four Sunan, and it was authenticated by al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Khuzayma, Ibn Hibban and others. It has been related from a group of Companions from the Prophet (ﷺ) in similar terms.

We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "There is no harm in the game of the sea." Abu al-Muhazzim is weak, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Majah said: Harun ibn Abd Allah al-Hammal related to us, Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us, Ziyad ibn Abd Allah related to us, from Ulatha, from Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Jabir and Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) when he invoked against locusts said: "O Allah, destroy their large ones, kill their small ones, spoil their eggs, cut off their offspring, and seize them by their mouths away from our livelihood and sustenance, for You are the Hearer of supplication." Khalid said: O Messenger of Allah, how do you invoke against an army of the armies of Allah to cut off its offspring? He said: "Locusts are the spawn of the fish in the sea." Hashim said: Ziyad said: one who saw the fish spawning them told me. Ibn Majah alone related it. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3221; al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "This chain is weak because of the weakness of Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim; Ibn al-Jawzi listed it among the fabrications through Harun ibn Abd Allah, and said: it is not sound from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Musa ibn Muhammad weakened it."]
