Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: Tawus, Jabir ibn Zayd also held this view, and al-Thawri and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh (in one narration) adopted it. Something similar has also been narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. Ibn Jarir narrated it through Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that 'Ali disliked the meat of game for the muhrim in every case.

Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh (in one narration), and the majority said: If the lawful person intended the muhrim by that hunt, it is not permissible for the muhrim to eat it, based on the hadith of al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah: that he gave the Prophet ﷺ a wild donkey while he was at al-Abwa' (or Waddan), and he returned it to him. When he saw the effect on his face, he said: "We only returned it to you because we are in ihram."

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs, with many wordings. [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 1825, 2573; Sahih Muslim, no. 1193.] They said: its meaning is that the Prophet ﷺ thought it had been hunted for his sake, so he returned it for that reason. But if it was not hunted with him in mind, it is permissible for him to eat from it, based on the hadith of Abu Qatadah, when he hunted a wild ass, which was lawful (for him, as he was not in ihram), while his companions were in ihram, and they hesitated to eat it. Then they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Did any of you point to it, or help in killing it?" They said: "No." He said: "Then eat." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also ate from it.

This story is also established in the two Sahihs with many wordings. [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 2914, 5490; Sahih Muslim, no. 1196.]

Imam Ahmad said: Sa'id ibn Mansur and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, both saying: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from al-Mutallib ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hantab, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and Qutaybah said in his narration: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'The game of the land is lawful for you,'" [Sa'id said: "while you are in ihram"] "as long as you do not hunt it or it is not hunted for you."

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i all narrated it likewise from Qutaybah. Al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know that al-Mutallib heard from Jabir." [Footnote: Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1851; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 846; Sunan al-Nasa'i, 5/187.]

Imam Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i also narrated it through 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from his client al-Mutallib, from Jabir, then said: "This is the best and most analogically sound hadith narrated on this subject."

Malik narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, who said: "I saw 'Uthman ibn 'Affan at al-'Araj, while he was in ihram, on a hot day, having covered his face with a red velvet cloth (qatifah urjuwan). Then meat of game was brought to him, and he said to his companions: 'Eat.' They said: 'Will you not eat?' He said: 'I am not like your condition; it was hunted for my sake.'" [Footnote: Al-Muwatta', 1/354.] [Footnote: Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, did not address the explanation of the remaining verses, as in all the manuscript copies; perhaps that is, Allah knows best, because he had already touched on their meanings in the similar passages in Surat al-Baqarah.]

Ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn Abbas (in one narration from him), and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others, regarding His words: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you﴾, that it means what is hunted from it fresh, ﴿and its food﴾ means what is taken from it preserved, salted and dried for provision.

Ibn Abbas, in the well-known narration from him, said: its game is what is taken from it alive, and ﴿its food﴾ is what it casts up dead.

The same was related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Zayd ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Amr, and Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with them all, and from Ikrimah, Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and al-Hasan al-Basri.

Sufyan ibn Uyayna said, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq that he said: ﴿its food﴾ is all that is in it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd related to us, Jarir related to us, from Mughira, from Simak, who said: I was told from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr addressed the people and said: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food, as a provision for you﴾, and its food is what it casts up.

He said: Ya'qub related to us, Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food﴾, he said: ﴿its food﴾ is what it casts up.

Ikrimah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿its food﴾ is what it casts up of carrion. Ibn Jarir also narrated it.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: its food is what it casts up alive, or what recedes from it and dies. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar related to us, Abd al-Wahhab related to us, Ayyub related to us, from Nafi', that Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hurayra asked Ibn Umar, saying: The sea has cast up many dead fish; shall we eat them? He said: Do not eat them. When Abdullah returned to his family, he took the Mushaf and recited Surat al-Ma'ida, and came to this verse: ﴿and its food, as a provision for you and for the travellers﴾, and said: Go and tell him to eat it, for it is its food.

Thus Ibn Jarir chose that what is meant by "its food" is what dies in it. He said: A report has been transmitted concerning this, and some of them transmit it as a statement of a Companion (mawquf).

Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, he said: Abdah ibn Sulayman related to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Salama related to us, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food, as a provision for you﴾, and said: its food is what it casts up dead.

Then he said: Some of them stopped this hadith at Abu Hurayra: Hannad related to us, Ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra regarding His words: ﴿The game of the sea is made lawful for you and its food﴾, he said: its food is what it casts up dead.

As for His words: ﴿as a provision for you and for the travellers﴾, that is, a benefit and sustenance for you, O addressees, ﴿and for the travellers﴾, which is the plural of sayyar. Ikrimah said: for those who are at the sea's edge, and for the travellers (al-sayyara): the journey. 

Others said: its fresh part is for one who hunts it from those present by the sea, and ﴿its food﴾ is what dies in it or is hunted from it and salted and dried as provision for travellers and those far from the sea.

Something similar was related from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Suddi and others. The majority of scholars have used this noble verse as evidence for the permissibility of the carrion of the sea, together with what Imam Malik ibn Anas related from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment toward the coast and appointed Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah over them; they were three hundred, and I was among them. He said: We set out until, when we were on part of the way, the provisions ran out, so Abu Ubayda ordered the provisions of that army to be gathered, and it all came to two sacks of dates. He said: He would feed us a little each day, until it ran out, and we would get only one date each. I said: And what does one date avail? He said: We found its loss when it ran out. He said: Then we reached the sea, and there was a fish like a dune (zarib). That army ate from it for eighteen nights. Then Abu Ubayda ordered two of its ribs to be erected, then ordered a riding camel to be saddled, and it passed beneath them and did not touch them. [Muwatta' 2/930]

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2483 and Sahih Muslim no. 1935], and it has several chains from Jabir.

In Sahih Muslim, from the narration of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: there was on the sea-shore something like a huge sand-hill; we came to it, and there was a creature called the anbar. He said: Abu Ubayda said: it is carrion. Then he said: No, we are the messengers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and in the way of Allah, and you have been compelled, so eat. He said: We stayed on it for a month, and we were three hundred, until we grew fat. We would dip into the hollow of its eye with pitchers for the fat, and cut from it pieces like a bull's, or like the size of a bull. He said: Abu Ubayda took thirteen men of ours and seated them in the hollow of its eye, and took one of its ribs and erected it, then the largest camel with us was saddled and passed beneath it. We took provision of its meat in strips. When we came to Madina we came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and he said: "It is a provision that Allah brought forth for you; do you have any of its meat with you, that you might feed us?" He said: We sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) some of it, and he ate it. In some narrations of Muslim: they were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when they found this fish. Some said: it is a separate incident; others said: rather it is one event, but they were first with the Prophet (ﷺ), then he sent them as a detachment with Abu Ubayda, and they found this in that detachment with Abu Ubayda. And Allah knows best. [Sahih Muslim no. 1935]

Malik said, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Sa'id ibn Salama, of the family of Ibn al-Azraq, that al-Mughira ibn Abi Burda, who is of Banu Abd al-Dar, informed him that he heard Abu Hurayra say: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: O Messenger of Allah, we sail the sea and carry only a little water with us; if we perform wudu with it we become thirsty; shall we perform wudu with sea water? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Its water is pure, and its carrion is lawful."

This hadith was related by the two Imams al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and the people of the four Sunan, and it was authenticated by al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Khuzayma, Ibn Hibban and others. It has been related from a group of Companions from the Prophet (ﷺ) in similar terms.

Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related, by several routes, from Hammad ibn Salama: Abu al-Muhazzim related to us, he is Yazid ibn Sufyan, I heard Abu Hurayra say: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a Hajj or an Umra, and we encountered a swarm of locusts, and we began striking them with our sticks and whips and killing them, and we were troubled about it, and said: What shall we do, while we are in ihram? We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "There is no harm in the game of the sea." Abu al-Muhazzim is weak, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Majah said: Harun ibn Abd Allah al-Hammal related to us, Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us, Ziyad ibn Abd Allah related to us, from Ulatha, from Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Jabir and Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) when he invoked against locusts said: "O Allah, destroy their large ones, kill their small ones, spoil their eggs, cut off their offspring, and seize them by their mouths away from our livelihood and sustenance, for You are the Hearer of supplication." Khalid said: O Messenger of Allah, how do you invoke against an army of the armies of Allah to cut off its offspring? He said: "Locusts are the spawn of the fish in the sea." Hashim said: Ziyad said: one who saw the fish spawning them told me. Ibn Majah alone related it. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3221; al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "This chain is weak because of the weakness of Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim; Ibn al-Jawzi listed it among the fabrications through Harun ibn Abd Allah, and said: it is not sound from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Musa ibn Muhammad weakened it."]

Al-Shafi'i related, from Sa'id, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, that he disapproved of those who hunt locusts within the Sacred Precinct.

Those jurists who held that the sea creatures may be eaten, and did not exclude anything from that, have argued from this noble verse. It has already been mentioned from the Siddiq that he said: ﴿its food﴾ is all that is in it.

Some have excluded frogs and permitted all others, on the basis of what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i related, through the narration of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id ibn Khalid, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Uthman al-Taymi, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) "forbade the killing of the frog." [Musnad 3/453; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 5269; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/210.] And in al-Nasa'i, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade killing the frog, and said: its croaking is glorification. [I did not find it in my search of Sunan al-Nasa'i, and perhaps I will locate it later. It was related by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. 1852, through al-Hajjaj ibn Muhammad from Shu'ba, from Qatada, from Zurara ibn Awfa, from Abd Allah ibn Amr.]

Others said: Of the game of the sea, fish may be eaten, and frogs may not be eaten. They differed regarding the rest: it was said that all of that may be eaten, and it was said that it may not. It was also said: whatever has a counterpart on land that is eaten, its counterpart in the sea may be eaten, and whatever has a counterpart that is not eaten, it is not eaten. All these are views within the school of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: What dies in the sea may not be eaten, just as what dies on land may not be eaten, because of the generality of His words: ﴿Carrion is forbidden to you﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 3].

A hadith has come with something similar to that. Ibn Mardawayh said:

Abd al-Baqi (that is, Ibn Qani') related to us, al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tustari and Abd Allah ibn Musa ibn Abi Uthman related to us, both said: al-Husayn ibn Zayd al-Tabban related to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What you hunt while it is alive and it dies, eat it; and what the sea casts up dead and floating, do not eat it."

Then he related it through the route of Isma'il ibn Umayya and Yahya ibn Abi Unaysa, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, with the same. And it is munkar. [Its strangeness is because it contradicts the verse and the sound hadiths, such as the hadith "Its water is pure, its carrion is lawful," and the hadith of the anbar.]

The majority of the followers of Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal have argued with the hadith of the "anbar" mentioned earlier, and with the hadith "Its water is pure, its carrion is lawful," which has also been mentioned earlier.

Imam Abu Abd Allah al-Shafi'i related, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two carcasses and two bloods have been made lawful for us. As for the two carcasses, they are fish and locusts; as for the two bloods, they are liver and spleen."

Ahmad and Ibn Majah, al-Daraqutni and al-Bayhaqi also related it. It has supporting reports, and it has been related as a statement of a Companion (mawquf), and Allah knows best.

And His saying: ﴿The game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram (ihram: the sacred state entered for pilgrimage or 'umrah)﴾. That is, while you are in your state of ihram, hunting is forbidden to you. This indicates the prohibition of that. If the muhrim (one in ihram) hunts game deliberately, he sins and must pay compensation (jaza'). If he does so by mistake, he must still pay compensation, and it is unlawful for him to eat it, because for him it is like carrion (maytah). The same applies to others, whether they are in ihram or not, according to Malik and al-Shafi'i in one of his two opinions. This is also the view of 'Ata', al-Qasim, Salim, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and others.

If he eats it, or any part of it, is he obliged to pay compensation? On this, there are two opinions among the scholars:

The first: Yes. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', who said: "If he slaughters it and then eats it, he owes two expiations (kaffaratan)." A group held this view.

The second: He owes no compensation for eating it. Malik ibn Anas explicitly stated this.

Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: "This is the position of the jurists of the major cities and the majority of scholars." Then Abu 'Umar explained it by comparison with a man who commits intercourse, then again, then again, before being punished, for whom there is only one legal penalty (hadd).

Abu Hanifah said: he owes the value (qimah) of what he ate.

Abu Thawr said: "If the muhrim kills game, he owes its compensation, and it is lawful for him to eat that game, though I dislike it for the one who killed it, based on the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'The game of the land is lawful for you as long as you do not hunt it or it is not hunted for your sake.'"

This hadith will be explained later. His statement that it is permissible for the killer is unusual. As for others, there is disagreement. We have already mentioned the prohibition from earlier authorities. Others said it is permitted for someone other than the killer, whether muhrim or muhill (one not in ihram), based on this hadith. And Allah knows best.

As for when a lawful (hal) person hunts game and gives it as a gift to a muhrim, some have held that it is permitted absolutely, without distinguishing whether he hunted it for his sake or not. Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr narrated this view from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Abu Hurairah, al-Zubair ibn al-'Awwam, Ka'b al-Ahbar, Mujahid, 'Ata' (in one narration), and Sa'id ibn Jubair. He said: "The people of Kufa also held this view."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to him, from Abu Hurairah, that he was asked about the meat of game that a lawful person had hunted: may a muhrim eat it? He gave them a ruling permitting it. Then he met 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and informed him of what he had ruled. 'Umar said: "If you had ruled otherwise, I would have struck your head."

Others said: It is not permissible for a muhrim to eat game at all, and they prohibited it absolutely, based on the general wording of this noble verse.

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus and 'Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayyah, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he disliked the muhrim eating the meat of game. He said: "It is general (mubhamah)," meaning His statement: ﴿The game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram﴾.

He said: Ma'mar informed me, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn 'Umar: that he disliked for the muhrim to eat from the meat of game in every case.

Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, the same.

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: Tawus, Jabir ibn Zayd also held this view, and al-Thawri and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh (in one narration) adopted it. Something similar has also been narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. Ibn Jarir narrated it through Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that 'Ali disliked the meat of game for the muhrim in every case.

Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh (in one narration), and the majority said: If the lawful person intended the muhrim by that hunt, it is not permissible for the muhrim to eat it, based on the hadith of al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah: that he gave the Prophet ﷺ a wild donkey while he was at al-Abwa' (or Waddan), and he returned it to him. When he saw the effect on his face, he said: "We only returned it to you because we are in ihram."

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs, with many wordings. [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 1825, 2573; Sahih Muslim, no. 1193.] They said: its meaning is that the Prophet ﷺ thought it had been hunted for his sake, so he returned it for that reason. But if it was not hunted with him in mind, it is permissible for him to eat from it, based on the hadith of Abu Qatadah, when he hunted a wild ass, which was lawful (for him, as he was not in ihram), while his companions were in ihram, and they hesitated to eat it. Then they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Did any of you point to it, or help in killing it?" They said: "No." He said: "Then eat." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also ate from it.

This story is also established in the two Sahihs with many wordings. [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 2914, 5490; Sahih Muslim, no. 1196.]

Imam Ahmad said: Sa'id ibn Mansur and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, both saying: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from al-Mutallib ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hantab, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and Qutaybah said in his narration: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'The game of the land is lawful for you,'" [Sa'id said: "while you are in ihram"] "as long as you do not hunt it or it is not hunted for you."

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i all narrated it likewise from Qutaybah. Al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know that al-Mutallib heard from Jabir." [Footnote: Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1851; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 846; Sunan al-Nasa'i, 5/187.]

Imam Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i also narrated it through 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from his client al-Mutallib, from Jabir, then said: "This is the best and most analogically sound hadith narrated on this subject."

Malik narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, who said: "I saw 'Uthman ibn 'Affan at al-'Araj, while he was in ihram, on a hot day, having covered his face with a red velvet cloth (qatifah urjuwan). Then meat of game was brought to him, and he said to his companions: 'Eat.' They said: 'Will you not eat?' He said: 'I am not like your condition; it was hunted for my sake.'" [Footnote: Al-Muwatta', 1/354.] [Footnote: Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, did not address the explanation of the remaining verses, as in all the manuscript copies; perhaps that is, Allah knows best, because he had already touched on their meanings in the similar passages in Surat al-Baqarah.]

Something similar was related from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Suddi and others. The majority of scholars have used this noble verse as evidence for the permissibility of the carrion of the sea, together with what Imam Malik ibn Anas related from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment toward the coast and appointed Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah over them; they were three hundred, and I was among them. He said: We set out until, when we were on part of the way, the provisions ran out, so Abu Ubayda ordered the provisions of that army to be gathered, and it all came to two sacks of dates. He said: He would feed us a little each day, until it ran out, and we would get only one date each. I said: And what does one date avail? He said: We found its loss when it ran out. He said: Then we reached the sea, and there was a fish like a dune (zarib). That army ate from it for eighteen nights. Then Abu Ubayda ordered two of its ribs to be erected, then ordered a riding camel to be saddled, and it passed beneath them and did not touch them. [Muwatta' 2/930]

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2483 and Sahih Muslim no. 1935], and it has several chains from Jabir.

In Sahih Muslim, from the narration of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: there was on the sea-shore something like a huge sand-hill; we came to it, and there was a creature called the anbar. He said: Abu Ubayda said: it is carrion. Then he said: No, we are the messengers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and in the way of Allah, and you have been compelled, so eat. He said: We stayed on it for a month, and we were three hundred, until we grew fat. We would dip into the hollow of its eye with pitchers for the fat, and cut from it pieces like a bull's, or like the size of a bull. He said: Abu Ubayda took thirteen men of ours and seated them in the hollow of its eye, and took one of its ribs and erected it, then the largest camel with us was saddled and passed beneath it. We took provision of its meat in strips. When we came to Madina we came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and he said: "It is a provision that Allah brought forth for you; do you have any of its meat with you, that you might feed us?" He said: We sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) some of it, and he ate it. In some narrations of Muslim: they were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when they found this fish. Some said: it is a separate incident; others said: rather it is one event, but they were first with the Prophet (ﷺ), then he sent them as a detachment with Abu Ubayda, and they found this in that detachment with Abu Ubayda. And Allah knows best. [Sahih Muslim no. 1935]

Malik said, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Sa'id ibn Salama, of the family of Ibn al-Azraq, that al-Mughira ibn Abi Burda, who is of Banu Abd al-Dar, informed him that he heard Abu Hurayra say: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: O Messenger of Allah, we sail the sea and carry only a little water with us; if we perform wudu with it we become thirsty; shall we perform wudu with sea water? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Its water is pure, and its carrion is lawful."

This hadith was related by the two Imams al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and the people of the four Sunan, and it was authenticated by al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Khuzayma, Ibn Hibban and others. It has been related from a group of Companions from the Prophet (ﷺ) in similar terms.

Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related, by several routes, from Hammad ibn Salama: Abu al-Muhazzim related to us, he is Yazid ibn Sufyan, I heard Abu Hurayra say: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a Hajj or an Umra, and we encountered a swarm of locusts, and we began striking them with our sticks and whips and killing them, and we were troubled about it, and said: What shall we do, while we are in ihram? We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "There is no harm in the game of the sea." Abu al-Muhazzim is weak, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Majah said: Harun ibn Abd Allah al-Hammal related to us, Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us, Ziyad ibn Abd Allah related to us, from Ulatha, from Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Jabir and Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) when he invoked against locusts said: "O Allah, destroy their large ones, kill their small ones, spoil their eggs, cut off their offspring, and seize them by their mouths away from our livelihood and sustenance, for You are the Hearer of supplication." Khalid said: O Messenger of Allah, how do you invoke against an army of the armies of Allah to cut off its offspring? He said: "Locusts are the spawn of the fish in the sea." Hashim said: Ziyad said: one who saw the fish spawning them told me. Ibn Majah alone related it. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3221; al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "This chain is weak because of the weakness of Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim; Ibn al-Jawzi listed it among the fabrications through Harun ibn Abd Allah, and said: it is not sound from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Musa ibn Muhammad weakened it."]

Al-Shafi'i related, from Sa'id, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, that he disapproved of those who hunt locusts within the Sacred Precinct.

Those jurists who held that the sea creatures may be eaten, and did not exclude anything from that, have argued from this noble verse. It has already been mentioned from the Siddiq that he said: ﴿its food﴾ is all that is in it.

Some have excluded frogs and permitted all others, on the basis of what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i related, through the narration of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id ibn Khalid, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Uthman al-Taymi, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) "forbade the killing of the frog." [Musnad 3/453; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 5269; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/210.] And in al-Nasa'i, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade killing the frog, and said: its croaking is glorification. [I did not find it in my search of Sunan al-Nasa'i, and perhaps I will locate it later. It was related by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. 1852, through al-Hajjaj ibn Muhammad from Shu'ba, from Qatada, from Zurara ibn Awfa, from Abd Allah ibn Amr.]

Others said: Of the game of the sea, fish may be eaten, and frogs may not be eaten. They differed regarding the rest: it was said that all of that may be eaten, and it was said that it may not. It was also said: whatever has a counterpart on land that is eaten, its counterpart in the sea may be eaten, and whatever has a counterpart that is not eaten, it is not eaten. All these are views within the school of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: What dies in the sea may not be eaten, just as what dies on land may not be eaten, because of the generality of His words: ﴿Carrion is forbidden to you﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 3].

A hadith has come with something similar to that. Ibn Mardawayh said:

Abd al-Baqi (that is, Ibn Qani') related to us, al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tustari and Abd Allah ibn Musa ibn Abi Uthman related to us, both said: al-Husayn ibn Zayd al-Tabban related to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What you hunt while it is alive and it dies, eat it; and what the sea casts up dead and floating, do not eat it."

Then he related it through the route of Isma'il ibn Umayya and Yahya ibn Abi Unaysa, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, with the same. And it is munkar. [Its strangeness is because it contradicts the verse and the sound hadiths, such as the hadith "Its water is pure, its carrion is lawful," and the hadith of the anbar.]

The majority of the followers of Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal have argued with the hadith of the "anbar" mentioned earlier, and with the hadith "Its water is pure, its carrion is lawful," which has also been mentioned earlier.

Imam Abu Abd Allah al-Shafi'i related, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two carcasses and two bloods have been made lawful for us. As for the two carcasses, they are fish and locusts; as for the two bloods, they are liver and spleen."

Ahmad and Ibn Majah, al-Daraqutni and al-Bayhaqi also related it. It has supporting reports, and it has been related as a statement of a Companion (mawquf), and Allah knows best.

And His saying: ﴿The game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram (ihram: the sacred state entered for pilgrimage or 'umrah)﴾. That is, while you are in your state of ihram, hunting is forbidden to you. This indicates the prohibition of that. If the muhrim (one in ihram) hunts game deliberately, he sins and must pay compensation (jaza'). If he does so by mistake, he must still pay compensation, and it is unlawful for him to eat it, because for him it is like carrion (maytah). The same applies to others, whether they are in ihram or not, according to Malik and al-Shafi'i in one of his two opinions. This is also the view of 'Ata', al-Qasim, Salim, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and others.

If he eats it, or any part of it, is he obliged to pay compensation? On this, there are two opinions among the scholars:

The first: Yes. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', who said: "If he slaughters it and then eats it, he owes two expiations (kaffaratan)." A group held this view.

The second: He owes no compensation for eating it. Malik ibn Anas explicitly stated this.

Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: "This is the position of the jurists of the major cities and the majority of scholars." Then Abu 'Umar explained it by comparison with a man who commits intercourse, then again, then again, before being punished, for whom there is only one legal penalty (hadd).

Abu Hanifah said: he owes the value (qimah) of what he ate.

Abu Thawr said: "If the muhrim kills game, he owes its compensation, and it is lawful for him to eat that game, though I dislike it for the one who killed it, based on the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'The game of the land is lawful for you as long as you do not hunt it or it is not hunted for your sake.'"

This hadith will be explained later. His statement that it is permissible for the killer is unusual. As for others, there is disagreement. We have already mentioned the prohibition from earlier authorities. Others said it is permitted for someone other than the killer, whether muhrim or muhill (one not in ihram), based on this hadith. And Allah knows best.

As for when a lawful (hal) person hunts game and gives it as a gift to a muhrim, some have held that it is permitted absolutely, without distinguishing whether he hunted it for his sake or not. Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr narrated this view from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Abu Hurairah, al-Zubair ibn al-'Awwam, Ka'b al-Ahbar, Mujahid, 'Ata' (in one narration), and Sa'id ibn Jubair. He said: "The people of Kufa also held this view."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to him, from Abu Hurairah, that he was asked about the meat of game that a lawful person had hunted: may a muhrim eat it? He gave them a ruling permitting it. Then he met 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and informed him of what he had ruled. 'Umar said: "If you had ruled otherwise, I would have struck your head."

Others said: It is not permissible for a muhrim to eat game at all, and they prohibited it absolutely, based on the general wording of this noble verse.

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus and 'Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayyah, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he disliked the muhrim eating the meat of game. He said: "It is general (mubhamah)," meaning His statement: ﴿The game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram﴾.

He said: Ma'mar informed me, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn 'Umar: that he disliked for the muhrim to eat from the meat of game in every case.

Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, the same.

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: Tawus, Jabir ibn Zayd also held this view, and al-Thawri and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh (in one narration) adopted it. Something similar has also been narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. Ibn Jarir narrated it through Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that 'Ali disliked the meat of game for the muhrim in every case.

Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh (in one narration), and the majority said: If the lawful person intended the muhrim by that hunt, it is not permissible for the muhrim to eat it, based on the hadith of al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah: that he gave the Prophet ﷺ a wild donkey while he was at al-Abwa' (or Waddan), and he returned it to him. When he saw the effect on his face, he said: "We only returned it to you because we are in ihram."

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs, with many wordings. [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 1825, 2573; Sahih Muslim, no. 1193.] They said: its meaning is that the Prophet ﷺ thought it had been hunted for his sake, so he returned it for that reason. But if it was not hunted with him in mind, it is permissible for him to eat from it, based on the hadith of Abu Qatadah, when he hunted a wild ass, which was lawful (for him, as he was not in ihram), while his companions were in ihram, and they hesitated to eat it. Then they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Did any of you point to it, or help in killing it?" They said: "No." He said: "Then eat." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also ate from it.

This story is also established in the two Sahihs with many wordings. [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 2914, 5490; Sahih Muslim, no. 1196.]

Imam Ahmad said: Sa'id ibn Mansur and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, both saying: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from al-Mutallib ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hantab, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and Qutaybah said in his narration: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'The game of the land is lawful for you,'" [Sa'id said: "while you are in ihram"] "as long as you do not hunt it or it is not hunted for you."

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i all narrated it likewise from Qutaybah. Al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know that al-Mutallib heard from Jabir." [Footnote: Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1851; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 846; Sunan al-Nasa'i, 5/187.]

Imam Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i also narrated it through 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from his client al-Mutallib, from Jabir, then said: "This is the best and most analogically sound hadith narrated on this subject."

Malik narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, who said: "I saw 'Uthman ibn 'Affan at al-'Araj, while he was in ihram, on a hot day, having covered his face with a red velvet cloth (qatifah urjuwan). Then meat of game was brought to him, and he said to his companions: 'Eat.' They said: 'Will you not eat?' He said: 'I am not like your condition; it was hunted for my sake.'" [Footnote: Al-Muwatta', 1/354.] [Footnote: Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, did not address the explanation of the remaining verses, as in all the manuscript copies; perhaps that is, Allah knows best, because he had already touched on their meanings in the similar passages in Surat al-Baqarah.]

The Exalted says to His Messenger ﷺ: "Say," O Muhammad: "Not equal are the bad and the good, even if the abundance of the bad impresses you." That is, O humankind: the little that is lawful and beneficial is better than the much that is unlawful and harmful. As came in the hadith: "What is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and distracting."

Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said in his Mu'jam: Ahmad ibn Zuhayr narrated to us; al-Hawti narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us; Mu'an [in D: "Ya'la"] ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, from Abu Abd al-Malik Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, that he informed him, from Tha'labah ibn Hatib al-Ansari, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, supplicate Allah that He grant me wealth." The Prophet ﷺ said: "A little of which you can render its thanks is better than a lot which you cannot bear."

[Footnote: Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated it in al-Isti'ab (1/201) and Ibn al-Athir in Usd al-Ghabah (1/284) by way of Mu'an ibn Rifa'ah, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman, similarly. In its chain is Ali ibn Yazid al-Alhani, who is matruk (abandoned in narration). Al-Fadil 'Adhab al-Hamish has a treatise defending Tha'labah ibn Hatib, in which he explains the strangeness of this story and expands on it.]

﴿So fear Allah, O people of understanding﴾: that is, O people of sound and upright minds. Avoid the unlawful and leave it, be content with the lawful and suffice with it, ﴿that you may prosper﴾: that is, in this world and the Hereafter.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you.﴾ This is a discipline from Allah [Exalted] [addition from D] to His believing servants, and a prohibition for them from asking ﴿about things﴾ which hold no benefit for them in asking about or probing into. For if those matters were made apparent to them, they might sadden them, and it would be grievous for them to hear them. As came in the hadith: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Let no one convey to me anything about anyone else, for I love to come out to you with a sound heart."

[Footnote: Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan (no. 4860) and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (no. 3896), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and its full wording will come.]

Al-Bukhari said: Munthir ibn al-Walid ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Jarudi narrated to us; my father narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Musa ibn Anas, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ gave a sermon the like of which I had never heard before. He said: "If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much." He said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ covered their faces, and there was sobbing from them. A man said: "Who is my father?" He said: "So-and-so." So this verse was revealed: ﴿Do not ask about things...﴾

It was narrated by al-Nadr and Rawh ibn Ubadah, from Shu'bah [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4621]. Al-Bukhari narrated it in other places, as did Muslim, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, by way of various chains from Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj, with the same wording [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. 6486, 7295; Sahih Muslim no. 2359; al-Musnad 3/210; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3056].

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us; Yazid narrated to us; Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked persistently until they pressed him with questions. One day he came out to them and climbed the pulpit, and said: "Do not ask me today about anything except that I will make it clear to you." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became apprehensive that something of a matter had drawn near. I looked to my right and my left and found everyone with his head wrapped in his garment, weeping. Then a man who used to be disputed with, and who was called by other than his father's name, stood up and said: "O Prophet of Allah, who is my father?" He said: "Your father is Hudhafah." Then Umar stood up [or he said: then Umar arose] and said: "We are content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger, seeking refuge in Allah [or he said: I seek refuge in Allah] from the evil of trials." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have never seen in good and evil the like of today. Paradise and Hellfire were displayed to me until I saw them beyond the wall." Both al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it by way of Sa'id [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/100; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 7091; Sahih Muslim no. 2359].

Ma'mar narrated it from al-Zuhri, from Anas, with something similar or close to it. Al-Zuhri said: The mother of Abdullah ibn Hudhafah said: "I have never seen a child more disobedient than you! Did you feel secure that your mother might have committed what the people of the Jahiliyyah committed, so that you would disgrace her before the people?" He said: "By Allah, if he had attached me to a black slave, I would have been attached to him." [Al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (11/102) by way of Ma'mar.]

Ibn Jarir also said: al-Harith narrated to us; Abd al-Aziz narrated to us; Qays narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out, angry, his face reddened, until he sat on the pulpit. A man stood up to him and said: "Where is my father [in D: 'Where am I']?" He said: "In the Fire." Another stood up and said: "Who is my father?" He said: "Your father is Hudhafah." Then Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: "We are content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, with Muhammad as Prophet, and with the Qur'an as leader. O Messenger of Allah, we are people recently out of the Jahiliyyah and polytheism, and Allah knows who our fathers are." He said: So his anger subsided, and this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/103]. Its chain is good [in D: "a good chain"].

Some of the early scholars narrated this story as a mursal report (one in which a Companion is omitted from the chain), among them Asbat from al-Suddi, that he said concerning His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry one day, and he rose to give a sermon and said: 'Ask me, for you will not ask me about anything except that I will inform you of it.' A man of Quraysh, from the Banu Sahm, called Abdullah ibn Hudhafah, who was being slandered concerning his parentage, stood up to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who is my father?' He said: 'Your father is so-and-so,' and he called him by his father's name. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab came to him, kissed his foot and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we are content with Allah as Lord, with you as Prophet, with Islam as religion, and with the Qur'an as leader. So pardon us, may Allah pardon you.' He did not cease with him until he was satisfied. On that day he said: 'The child belongs to the bed, and for the adulterer, the stone.'"

Then al-Bukhari said: al-Fadl ibn Sahl narrated to us; Abu al-Nadr narrated to us; Abu Khaythamah narrated to us; Abu al-Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Some people used to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mockingly. One would say: "Who is my father?" and another, whose camel had strayed, would say: "Where is my camel?" So Allah revealed concerning them this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾, until He finished the whole verse. Al-Bukhari alone narrated it [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4622].

Imam Ahmad said: Mansur ibn Wardan al-Asadi narrated to us; Ali ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who is Sa'id ibn Fayruz, from [in D: "and from"] Ali, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And for Allah is a duty upon the people, the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97], they said: "O Messenger of Allah, every year?" He was silent. They said: "Every year?" He was silent. Then they said: "Every year?" He said: "No. Had I said yes, it would have become obligatory." So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it likewise by way of Mansur ibn Wardan [al-Musnad 1/113; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3055; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 2884]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib (singular) from this route." And I heard al-Bukhari say: "Abu al-Bakhtari did not meet Ali."

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us; Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari, from Abu Iyad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has prescribed the Hajj upon you." A man said: "Every year, O Messenger of Allah?" He turned away from him until the man repeated it two or three times. Then he said: "Who is the questioner?" The man said: "So-and-so." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory upon you, you would not have been able to bear it; and if you had left it, you would have disbelieved." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ until He completed the verse.

Then Ibn Jarir narrated it by way of al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, and he said: "Then Mihsan al-Asadi stood up." In another version by this route: "Ukashah ibn Mihsan," and this is more likely [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/105]. Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari is weak (da'if).

Ibn Jarir also said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to me, saying: Abu Zayd Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Ghamr narrated to us; Abu Mut'i Mu'awiyah ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Amr, from Sulaym ibn Amir, who said: "I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among the people and said: 'Hajj has been prescribed for you.' A Bedouin man stood up and said: 'Every year?' He said: The speech of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cut short, he fell silent, and he appeared angry. He remained silent for a long time, then spoke and said: 'Who is the questioner?' The Bedouin said: 'Here I am.' He said: 'Woe to you! What makes you secure that I would say yes? By Allah, if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory, you would have disbelieved. Indeed, what destroyed those before you was the excess of their questioning and their disputing with their prophets. By Allah, if I had made lawful for you everything on the earth and forbidden to you a place the size of a sole, you would have fallen into it.'" He said: So Allah revealed at that time: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ to the end of the verse [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/107]. There is weakness in its chain.

The apparent meaning of the verse is a prohibition against asking about those things which, if a person came to know of them, would sadden him. So the better course is to turn away from them and leave them. How excellent is the hadith which Imam Ahmad narrated, where he said:

Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: I heard Isra'il ibn Yunus, from al-Walid ibn Abi Hisham, the client of al-Hamdani, from Zayd ibn Za'id, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions: "Let no one convey to me anything about anyone else, for I love to come out to you with a sound heart," the hadith in full.

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Isra'il [al-Musnad 1/395; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4860; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3896]; Abu Dawud said "from al-Walid," and al-Tirmidhi said "from Isra'il," from al-Suddi, from al-Walid ibn Abi Hashim, with the same wording. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib from this route."

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be disclosed to you﴾: that is, if you ask about these matters which you were forbidden to ask about, while revelation is descending upon the Messenger, they will be made clear to you. And that is easy for Allah [addition from D: "upon Allah"].

Then He said [in D: "And His saying"]: ﴿Allah has pardoned what is past of it﴾: that is, what came from you before that. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾

It is also said: the meaning of His words, ﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you﴾, is: do not ask about things that you would be starting to ask about anew, for perhaps a ruling may be revealed on account of your question, a tightening or a restriction. [[In manuscript D: "or hardship".]] And there has come in a hadith: "The greatest of the Muslims in crime is the one who asks about something that was not forbidden, and it becomes forbidden because of his asking." [[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (7289), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2358), from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.]] But if the Qur'an has revealed something in a general form, and you ask about its clarification at that time, it will be made clear to you, since you have need of it. [[In manuscript D: "need of it" (singular pronoun).]] ﴿God has pardoned what is past of it﴾, meaning: whatever He did not mention in His Book is among what He has pardoned, so you should remain silent about it just as He remained silent about it. And in the Sahih, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, he said: "Leave me alone as long as I leave you alone, for those before you were destroyed only by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets."

[[Sahih Muslim, no. (1337).]]

And in another sound hadith also: "God has prescribed obligations, so do not neglect them; He has set limits, so do not transgress them; He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; and He has remained silent about things out of mercy for you, not out of forgetfulness, so do not ask about them."

[[Related by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (10/13), through the route of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Makhul, from Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani, with it traced to the Prophet ﷺ.]]

Then He said: ﴿A people before you had asked such things, then they became disbelievers because of them﴾. That is: a people before you asked these forbidden matters, and they were answered, yet they did not believe in them, so they became disbelievers because of them, that is, through them. They were made clear to them, but they did not benefit from them, because they did not ask seeking guidance; rather they asked in a spirit of obstinacy and defiance.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾. The reason was that the Messenger of God ﷺ called out to the people and said: "O people, the Hajj has been prescribed for you." A man from the Banu Asad stood up and said: "O Messenger of God, is it every year?" The Messenger of God ﷺ became extremely angry and said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, if I had said 'Yes', it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory you would not have been able to manage it, and then you would have disbelieved. So leave me alone as long as I leave you alone; when I command you to do something, do it, and when I forbid you from something, avoid it." Then God revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾. He forbade them from asking about the like of what the Christians asked about regarding the table (al-Ma'idah), and they became disbelievers. So God forbade that and said: Do not ask about things which, if the Qur'an were revealed concerning them with severity, would trouble you; but wait, and when the Qur'an is revealed you will not ask about anything without finding its explanation. Ibn Jarir related it.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you; and if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you﴾. He said: When the verse of Hajj was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ called out to the people and said: "O people, God has prescribed the Hajj for you, so perform it." They said: "O Messenger of God, once, or every year?" He said: "No, rather once; and if I had said 'every year', it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory you would have disbelieved." Then God the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things﴾ up to His words: ﴿then they became disbelievers because of them﴾. Ibn Jarir related it.

Khasif said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Do not ask about things﴾, he said: these are the bahirah, the wasilah, the sa'ibah and the ham. Do you not see that He says after that: "God has not appointed any bahirah, nor such, nor such"? He said: As for 'Ikrimah, he said: They used to ask him about the signs (ayat), so they were forbidden from that. Then He said: ﴿A people before you had asked such things, then they became disbelievers because of them﴾. Ibn Jarir related it.

That is, 'Ikrimah, may God have mercy on him, meant that the intent of this prohibition is against asking for the occurrence of signs (miracles), as the Quraysh asked that rivers be made to flow for them, and that Safa be turned into gold for them, and other such things, and as the Jews asked that a book be sent down to them from heaven. God the Exalted has said: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them; We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her; and We send the signs only as a warning﴾ [al-Isra' 17:59]. And God the Exalted has said: ﴿And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say: The signs are only with God, and what will make you aware that when they come they will not believe? And We turn their hearts and their eyes, just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly. And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them every thing face to face, they would not have believed, unless God willed; but most of them are ignorant﴾ [al-An'am 6:109–111].

The Exalted says to His Messenger ﷺ: "Say," O Muhammad: "Not equal are the bad and the good, even if the abundance of the bad impresses you." That is, O humankind: the little that is lawful and beneficial is better than the much that is unlawful and harmful. As came in the hadith: "What is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and distracting."

Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said in his Mu'jam: Ahmad ibn Zuhayr narrated to us; al-Hawti narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us; Mu'an [in D: "Ya'la"] ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, from Abu Abd al-Malik Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, that he informed him, from Tha'labah ibn Hatib al-Ansari, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, supplicate Allah that He grant me wealth." The Prophet ﷺ said: "A little of which you can render its thanks is better than a lot which you cannot bear."

[Footnote: Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated it in al-Isti'ab (1/201) and Ibn al-Athir in Usd al-Ghabah (1/284) by way of Mu'an ibn Rifa'ah, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman, similarly. In its chain is Ali ibn Yazid al-Alhani, who is matruk (abandoned in narration). Al-Fadil 'Adhab al-Hamish has a treatise defending Tha'labah ibn Hatib, in which he explains the strangeness of this story and expands on it.]

﴿So fear Allah, O people of understanding﴾: that is, O people of sound and upright minds. Avoid the unlawful and leave it, be content with the lawful and suffice with it, ﴿that you may prosper﴾: that is, in this world and the Hereafter.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you.﴾ This is a discipline from Allah [Exalted] [addition from D] to His believing servants, and a prohibition for them from asking ﴿about things﴾ which hold no benefit for them in asking about or probing into. For if those matters were made apparent to them, they might sadden them, and it would be grievous for them to hear them. As came in the hadith: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Let no one convey to me anything about anyone else, for I love to come out to you with a sound heart."

[Footnote: Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan (no. 4860) and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (no. 3896), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and its full wording will come.]

Al-Bukhari said: Munthir ibn al-Walid ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Jarudi narrated to us; my father narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Musa ibn Anas, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ gave a sermon the like of which I had never heard before. He said: "If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much." He said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ covered their faces, and there was sobbing from them. A man said: "Who is my father?" He said: "So-and-so." So this verse was revealed: ﴿Do not ask about things...﴾

It was narrated by al-Nadr and Rawh ibn Ubadah, from Shu'bah [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4621]. Al-Bukhari narrated it in other places, as did Muslim, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, by way of various chains from Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj, with the same wording [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. 6486, 7295; Sahih Muslim no. 2359; al-Musnad 3/210; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3056].

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us; Yazid narrated to us; Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked persistently until they pressed him with questions. One day he came out to them and climbed the pulpit, and said: "Do not ask me today about anything except that I will make it clear to you." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became apprehensive that something of a matter had drawn near. I looked to my right and my left and found everyone with his head wrapped in his garment, weeping. Then a man who used to be disputed with, and who was called by other than his father's name, stood up and said: "O Prophet of Allah, who is my father?" He said: "Your father is Hudhafah." Then Umar stood up [or he said: then Umar arose] and said: "We are content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger, seeking refuge in Allah [or he said: I seek refuge in Allah] from the evil of trials." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have never seen in good and evil the like of today. Paradise and Hellfire were displayed to me until I saw them beyond the wall." Both al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it by way of Sa'id [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/100; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 7091; Sahih Muslim no. 2359].

Ma'mar narrated it from al-Zuhri, from Anas, with something similar or close to it. Al-Zuhri said: The mother of Abdullah ibn Hudhafah said: "I have never seen a child more disobedient than you! Did you feel secure that your mother might have committed what the people of the Jahiliyyah committed, so that you would disgrace her before the people?" He said: "By Allah, if he had attached me to a black slave, I would have been attached to him." [Al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (11/102) by way of Ma'mar.]

Ibn Jarir also said: al-Harith narrated to us; Abd al-Aziz narrated to us; Qays narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out, angry, his face reddened, until he sat on the pulpit. A man stood up to him and said: "Where is my father [in D: 'Where am I']?" He said: "In the Fire." Another stood up and said: "Who is my father?" He said: "Your father is Hudhafah." Then Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: "We are content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, with Muhammad as Prophet, and with the Qur'an as leader. O Messenger of Allah, we are people recently out of the Jahiliyyah and polytheism, and Allah knows who our fathers are." He said: So his anger subsided, and this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/103]. Its chain is good [in D: "a good chain"].

Some of the early scholars narrated this story as a mursal report (one in which a Companion is omitted from the chain), among them Asbat from al-Suddi, that he said concerning His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry one day, and he rose to give a sermon and said: 'Ask me, for you will not ask me about anything except that I will inform you of it.' A man of Quraysh, from the Banu Sahm, called Abdullah ibn Hudhafah, who was being slandered concerning his parentage, stood up to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who is my father?' He said: 'Your father is so-and-so,' and he called him by his father's name. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab came to him, kissed his foot and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we are content with Allah as Lord, with you as Prophet, with Islam as religion, and with the Qur'an as leader. So pardon us, may Allah pardon you.' He did not cease with him until he was satisfied. On that day he said: 'The child belongs to the bed, and for the adulterer, the stone.'"

Then al-Bukhari said: al-Fadl ibn Sahl narrated to us; Abu al-Nadr narrated to us; Abu Khaythamah narrated to us; Abu al-Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Some people used to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mockingly. One would say: "Who is my father?" and another, whose camel had strayed, would say: "Where is my camel?" So Allah revealed concerning them this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾, until He finished the whole verse. Al-Bukhari alone narrated it [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4622].

Imam Ahmad said: Mansur ibn Wardan al-Asadi narrated to us; Ali ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who is Sa'id ibn Fayruz, from [in D: "and from"] Ali, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And for Allah is a duty upon the people, the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97], they said: "O Messenger of Allah, every year?" He was silent. They said: "Every year?" He was silent. Then they said: "Every year?" He said: "No. Had I said yes, it would have become obligatory." So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it likewise by way of Mansur ibn Wardan [al-Musnad 1/113; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3055; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 2884]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib (singular) from this route." And I heard al-Bukhari say: "Abu al-Bakhtari did not meet Ali."

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us; Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari, from Abu Iyad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has prescribed the Hajj upon you." A man said: "Every year, O Messenger of Allah?" He turned away from him until the man repeated it two or three times. Then he said: "Who is the questioner?" The man said: "So-and-so." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory upon you, you would not have been able to bear it; and if you had left it, you would have disbelieved." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ until He completed the verse.

Then Ibn Jarir narrated it by way of al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, and he said: "Then Mihsan al-Asadi stood up." In another version by this route: "Ukashah ibn Mihsan," and this is more likely [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/105]. Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari is weak (da'if).

Ibn Jarir also said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to me, saying: Abu Zayd Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Ghamr narrated to us; Abu Mut'i Mu'awiyah ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Amr, from Sulaym ibn Amir, who said: "I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among the people and said: 'Hajj has been prescribed for you.' A Bedouin man stood up and said: 'Every year?' He said: The speech of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cut short, he fell silent, and he appeared angry. He remained silent for a long time, then spoke and said: 'Who is the questioner?' The Bedouin said: 'Here I am.' He said: 'Woe to you! What makes you secure that I would say yes? By Allah, if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory, you would have disbelieved. Indeed, what destroyed those before you was the excess of their questioning and their disputing with their prophets. By Allah, if I had made lawful for you everything on the earth and forbidden to you a place the size of a sole, you would have fallen into it.'" He said: So Allah revealed at that time: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ to the end of the verse [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/107]. There is weakness in its chain.

The apparent meaning of the verse is a prohibition against asking about those things which, if a person came to know of them, would sadden him. So the better course is to turn away from them and leave them. How excellent is the hadith which Imam Ahmad narrated, where he said:

Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: I heard Isra'il ibn Yunus, from al-Walid ibn Abi Hisham, the client of al-Hamdani, from Zayd ibn Za'id, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions: "Let no one convey to me anything about anyone else, for I love to come out to you with a sound heart," the hadith in full.

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Isra'il [al-Musnad 1/395; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4860; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3896]; Abu Dawud said "from al-Walid," and al-Tirmidhi said "from Isra'il," from al-Suddi, from al-Walid ibn Abi Hashim, with the same wording. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib from this route."

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be disclosed to you﴾: that is, if you ask about these matters which you were forbidden to ask about, while revelation is descending upon the Messenger, they will be made clear to you. And that is easy for Allah [addition from D: "upon Allah"].

Then He said [in D: "And His saying"]: ﴿Allah has pardoned what is past of it﴾: that is, what came from you before that. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾

It is also said: the meaning of His words, ﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you﴾, is: do not ask about things that you would be starting to ask about anew, for perhaps a ruling may be revealed on account of your question, a tightening or a restriction. [[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (7289), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2358), from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.]] But if the Qur'an has revealed something in a general form, and you ask about its clarification at that time, it will be made clear to you, since you have need of it. And in the Sahih, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, he said: "Leave me alone as long as I leave you alone, for those before you were destroyed only by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets."

[[Sahih Muslim, no. (1337).]]

And in another sound hadith also: "God has prescribed obligations, so do not neglect them; He has set limits, so do not transgress them; He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; and He has remained silent about things out of mercy for you, not out of forgetfulness, so do not ask about them."

[[Related by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (10/13), through the route of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Makhul, from Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani, with it traced to the Prophet ﷺ.]]

Then He said: ﴿A people before you had asked such things, then they became disbelievers because of them﴾. They said: "O Messenger of God, once, or every year?" He said: "No, rather once; and if I had said 'every year', it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory you would have disbelieved." Then God the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things﴾ up to His words: ﴿then they became disbelievers because of them﴾. Ibn Jarir related it.
