In its chain is Ali ibn Yazid al-Alhani, who is matruk (abandoned in narration). Al-Fadil 'Adhab al-Hamish has a treatise defending Tha'labah ibn Hatib, in which he explains the strangeness of this story and expands on it.]

﴿So fear Allah, O people of understanding﴾: that is, O people of sound and upright minds. Avoid the unlawful and leave it, be content with the lawful and suffice with it, ﴿that you may prosper﴾: that is, in this world and the Hereafter.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you.﴾ This is a discipline from Allah [Exalted] [addition from D] to His believing servants, and a prohibition for them from asking ﴿about things﴾ which hold no benefit for them in asking about or probing into. For if those matters were made apparent to them, they might sadden them, and it would be grievous for them to hear them. As came in the hadith: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Let no one convey to me anything about anyone else, for I love to come out to you with a sound heart."

[Footnote: Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan (no. 4860) and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (no. 3896), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and its full wording will come.]

Al-Bukhari said: Munthir ibn al-Walid ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Jarudi narrated to us; my father narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Musa ibn Anas, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ gave a sermon the like of which I had never heard before. He said: "If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much." He said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ covered their faces, and there was sobbing from them. A man said: "Who is my father?" He said: "So-and-so." So this verse was revealed: ﴿Do not ask about things...﴾

It was narrated by al-Nadr and Rawh ibn Ubadah, from Shu'bah [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4621]. Al-Bukhari narrated it in other places, as did Muslim, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, by way of various chains from Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj, with the same wording [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. 6486, 7295; Sahih Muslim no. 2359; al-Musnad 3/210; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3056].

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us; Yazid narrated to us; Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked persistently until they pressed him with questions. One day he came out to them and climbed the pulpit, and said: "Do not ask me today about anything except that I will make it clear to you." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became apprehensive that something of a matter had drawn near. I looked to my right and my left and found everyone with his head wrapped in his garment, weeping. Then a man who used to be disputed with, and who was called by other than his father's name, stood up and said: "O Prophet of Allah, who is my father?" He said: "Your father is Hudhafah." Then Umar stood up [or he said: then Umar arose] and said: "We are content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger, seeking refuge in Allah [or he said: I seek refuge in Allah] from the evil of trials." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have never seen in good and evil the like of today. Paradise and Hellfire were displayed to me until I saw them beyond the wall." Both al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it by way of Sa'id [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/100; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 7091; Sahih Muslim no. 2359].

Ma'mar narrated it from al-Zuhri, from Anas, with something similar or close to it. Al-Zuhri said: The mother of Abdullah ibn Hudhafah said: "I have never seen a child more disobedient than you! Did you feel secure that your mother might have committed what the people of the Jahiliyyah committed, so that you would disgrace her before the people?" He said: "By Allah, if he had attached me to a black slave, I would have been attached to him." [Al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (11/102) by way of Ma'mar.]

Ibn Jarir also said: al-Harith narrated to us; Abd al-Aziz narrated to us; Qays narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out, angry, his face reddened, until he sat on the pulpit. A man stood up to him and said: "Where is my father [in D: 'Where am I']?" He said: "In the Fire." Another stood up and said: "Who is my father?" He said: "Your father is Hudhafah." Then Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: "We are content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, with Muhammad as Prophet, and with the Qur'an as leader. O Messenger of Allah, we are people recently out of the Jahiliyyah and polytheism, and Allah knows who our fathers are." He said: So his anger subsided, and this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/103]. Its chain is good [in D: "a good chain"].

Some of the early scholars narrated this story as a mursal report (one in which a Companion is omitted from the chain), among them Asbat from al-Suddi, that he said concerning His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry one day, and he rose to give a sermon and said: 'Ask me, for you will not ask me about anything except that I will inform you of it.' A man of Quraysh, from the Banu Sahm, called Abdullah ibn Hudhafah, who was being slandered concerning his parentage, stood up to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who is my father?' He said: 'Your father is so-and-so,' and he called him by his father's name. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab came to him, kissed his foot and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we are content with Allah as Lord, with you as Prophet, with Islam as religion, and with the Qur'an as leader. So pardon us, may Allah pardon you.' He did not cease with him until he was satisfied. On that day he said: 'The child belongs to the bed, and for the adulterer, the stone.'"

Then al-Bukhari said: al-Fadl ibn Sahl narrated to us; Abu al-Nadr narrated to us; Abu Khaythamah narrated to us; Abu al-Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Some people used to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mockingly. One would say: "Who is my father?" and another, whose camel had strayed, would say: "Where is my camel?" So Allah revealed concerning them this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾, until He finished the whole verse. Al-Bukhari alone narrated it [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4622].

Imam Ahmad said: Mansur ibn Wardan al-Asadi narrated to us; Ali ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who is Sa'id ibn Fayruz, from [in D: "and from"] Ali, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And for Allah is a duty upon the people, the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97], they said: "O Messenger of Allah, every year?" He was silent. They said: "Every year?" He was silent. Then they said: "Every year?" He said: "No. Had I said yes, it would have become obligatory." So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it likewise by way of Mansur ibn Wardan [al-Musnad 1/113; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3055; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 2884]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib (singular) from this route." And I heard al-Bukhari say: "Abu al-Bakhtari did not meet Ali."

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us; Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari, from Abu Iyad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has prescribed the Hajj upon you." A man said: "Every year, O Messenger of Allah?" He turned away from him until the man repeated it two or three times. Then he said: "Who is the questioner?" The man said: "So-and-so." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory upon you, you would not have been able to bear it; and if you had left it, you would have disbelieved." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ until He completed the verse.

Then Ibn Jarir narrated it by way of al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, and he said: "Then Mihsan al-Asadi stood up." In another version by this route: "Ukashah ibn Mihsan," and this is more likely [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/105]. Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari is weak (da'if).

Ibn Jarir also said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to me, saying: Abu Zayd Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Ghamr narrated to us; Abu Mut'i Mu'awiyah ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Amr, from Sulaym ibn Amir, who said: "I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among the people and said: 'Hajj has been prescribed for you.' A Bedouin man stood up and said: 'Every year?' He said: The speech of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cut short, he fell silent, and he appeared angry. He remained silent for a long time, then spoke and said: 'Who is the questioner?' The Bedouin said: 'Here I am.' He said: 'Woe to you! What makes you secure that I would say yes? By Allah, if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory, you would have disbelieved. Indeed, what destroyed those before you was the excess of their questioning and their disputing with their prophets. By Allah, if I had made lawful for you everything on the earth and forbidden to you a place the size of a sole, you would have fallen into it.'" He said: So Allah revealed at that time: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾ to the end of the verse [Tafsir al-Tabari 11/107]. There is weakness in its chain.

The apparent meaning of the verse is a prohibition against asking about those things which, if a person came to know of them, would sadden him. So the better course is to turn away from them and leave them. How excellent is the hadith which Imam Ahmad narrated, where he said:

Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: I heard Isra'il ibn Yunus, from al-Walid ibn Abi Hisham, the client of al-Hamdani, from Zayd ibn Za'id, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions: "Let no one convey to me anything about anyone else, for I love to come out to you with a sound heart," the hadith in full.

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Isra'il [al-Musnad 1/395; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4860; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3896]; Abu Dawud said "from al-Walid," and al-Tirmidhi said "from Isra'il," from al-Suddi, from al-Walid ibn Abi Hashim, with the same wording. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib from this route."

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be disclosed to you﴾: that is, if you ask about these matters which you were forbidden to ask about, while revelation is descending upon the Messenger, they will be made clear to you. And that is easy for Allah [addition from D: "upon Allah"].

Then He said [in D: "And His saying"]: ﴿Allah has pardoned what is past of it﴾: that is, what came from you before that. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾

It is also said: the meaning of His words, ﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you﴾, is: do not ask about things that you would be starting to ask about anew, for perhaps a ruling may be revealed on account of your question, a tightening or a restriction. [[In manuscript D: "or hardship".]] And there has come in a hadith: "The greatest of the Muslims in crime is the one who asks about something that was not forbidden, and it becomes forbidden because of his asking." [[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (7289), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2358), from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.]] But if the Qur'an has revealed something in a general form, and you ask about its clarification at that time, it will be made clear to you, since you have need of it. [[In manuscript D: "need of it" (singular pronoun).]] ﴿God has pardoned what is past of it﴾, meaning: whatever He did not mention in His Book is among what He has pardoned, so you should remain silent about it just as He remained silent about it. And in the Sahih, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, he said: "Leave me alone as long as I leave you alone, for those before you were destroyed only by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets."

[[Sahih Muslim, no. (1337).]]

And in another sound hadith also: "God has prescribed obligations, so do not neglect them; He has set limits, so do not transgress them; He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; and He has remained silent about things out of mercy for you, not out of forgetfulness, so do not ask about them."

[[Related by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (10/13), through the route of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Makhul, from Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani, with it traced to the Prophet ﷺ.]]

Then He said: ﴿A people before you had asked such things, then they became disbelievers because of them﴾. That is: a people before you asked these forbidden matters, and they were answered, yet they did not believe in them, so they became disbelievers because of them, that is, through them. They were made clear to them, but they did not benefit from them, because they did not ask seeking guidance; rather they asked in a spirit of obstinacy and defiance.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾. The reason was that the Messenger of God ﷺ called out to the people and said: "O people, the Hajj has been prescribed for you." A man from the Banu Asad stood up and said: "O Messenger of God, is it every year?" The Messenger of God ﷺ became extremely angry and said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, if I had said 'Yes', it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory you would not have been able to manage it, and then you would have disbelieved. So leave me alone as long as I leave you alone; when I command you to do something, do it, and when I forbid you from something, avoid it." Then God revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you﴾. He forbade them from asking about the like of what the Christians asked about regarding the table (al-Ma'idah), and they became disbelievers. So God forbade that and said: Do not ask about things which, if the Qur'an were revealed concerning them with severity, would trouble you; but wait, and when the Qur'an is revealed you will not ask about anything without finding its explanation. Ibn Jarir related it.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you; and if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you﴾. He said: When the verse of Hajj was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ called out to the people and said: "O people, God has prescribed the Hajj for you, so perform it." They said: "O Messenger of God, once, or every year?" He said: "No, rather once; and if I had said 'every year', it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory you would have disbelieved." Then God the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things﴾ up to His words: ﴿then they became disbelievers because of them﴾. Ibn Jarir related it.

Khasif said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Do not ask about things﴾, he said: these are the bahirah, the wasilah, the sa'ibah and the ham. Do you not see that He says after that: "God has not appointed any bahirah, nor such, nor such"? He said: As for 'Ikrimah, he said: They used to ask him about the signs (ayat), so they were forbidden from that. Then He said: ﴿A people before you had asked such things, then they became disbelievers because of them﴾. Ibn Jarir related it.

That is, 'Ikrimah, may God have mercy on him, meant that the intent of this prohibition is against asking for the occurrence of signs (miracles), as the Quraysh asked that rivers be made to flow for them, and that Safa be turned into gold for them, and other such things, and as the Jews asked that a book be sent down to them from heaven. God the Exalted has said: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them; We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her; and We send the signs only as a warning﴾ [al-Isra' 17:59]. And God the Exalted has said: ﴿And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say: The signs are only with God, and what will make you aware that when they come they will not believe? And We turn their hearts and their eyes, just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly. And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them every thing face to face, they would not have believed, unless God willed; but most of them are ignorant﴾ [al-An'am 6:109–111].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 103–104:

Al-Bukhari said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "Al-Bahirah (a she-camel whose milk was forbidden to the idols/tawaghit, so no one among the people would milk her)." "As-Sa'ibah: they would let them loose for their gods, and nothing would be carried upon them." He said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw 'Amr ibn 'Amir al-Khuza'i dragging his intestines in the Fire; he was the first to let loose the sawa'ib." "Al-Wasilah: the young she-camel that gives birth to a female at the first birth of the camels, then gives birth to another female after it. They would let them loose for their idols if one female was joined to another with no male between them." "Al-Ham: the stallion camel that has served a counted number of mares. When he had finished his service, they would leave him for the idols and spare him from being burdened, so nothing would be carried upon him. They called him al-Hami."

Muslim and an-Nasa'i also narrated it in the same way, from the narration of Ibrahim ibn Sa'd. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4623) and Sahih Muslim no. (2856).]

Then al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Yaman said to me: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: I heard Sa'id relate this. And Abu Hurayrah said, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar. Ibn al-Hadi also narrated it, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ). [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4623).]

Al-Hakim said: Al-Bukhari intended that Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hadi narrated it from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Bukht, from al-Zuhri. Our shaykh Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi mentioned this in "al-Atraf" and remained silent without drawing attention to it. There is room for scrutiny in what al-Hakim said, for Imam Ahmad and Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir both narrated it from the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Ibn al-Hadi, from al-Zuhri himself. [Al-Musnad (2/366) and Tafsir al-Tabari (11/116).] And Allah knows best.

Then al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Abi Ya'qub Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kirmani narrated to us, Hassan ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, that 'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw Hell, some of it crushing other parts of it, and I saw 'Amr dragging his intestines, and he was the first to let loose the sawa'ib." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4624).]

Ibn Jarir said: Hannad narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith narrated to me, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to Aktham ibn al-Jawn: "O Aktham, I saw 'Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah ibn Khindif dragging his intestines in the Fire, and I have never seen a man more like a man than you are like him, nor he like you." Aktham said: "Do you fear that his resemblance will harm me, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No, you are a believer and he is a disbeliever. He was the first to change the religion of Ibrahim, to slit the ears of the bahirah, to let loose the sa'ibah, and to protect the hami." Then he narrated it from Hannad, from 'Abdah, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording or the same. [Tafsir al-Tabari (11/117); Ibn Hisham narrated it in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (1/78) through the chain of Muhammad ibn Ishaq.]

These two chains are not in the books (of hadith).

Imam Ahmad said: 'Amr ibn Mujama' narrated to us, Ibrahim al-Hajari narrated to us, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The first to let loose the sawa'ib and to worship idols was Abu Khuza'ah 'Amr ibn 'Amir, and I saw him dragging his intestines in the Fire." Ahmad alone narrated it by this route. [Al-Musnad (1/446). Its chain includes Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari, who is weak, but the hadith has supporting narrations from the hadith of 'A'ishah and Abu Hurayrah mentioned above. See the words of Shaykh Nasir al-Din al-Albani in al-Silsilah al-Sahihah no. (1677).]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I know the first to let loose the sawa'ib, and the first to change the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)." They said: "Who is he, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "'Amr ibn Luhayy, brother of Bani Ka'b. I saw him dragging his intestines in the Fire, his stench harming the people of the Fire. And I know the first to slit the ears of the bahair (plural of bahirah)." They said: "Who is he, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "A man from Bani Mudlij. He had two she-camels, so he slit their ears, forbade their milk, and then afterwards drank their milk. I saw him in the Fire, and the two camels were biting him with their mouths and trampling him with their hooves." [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/191); al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (11/120) through 'Abd al-Razzaq.]

So this 'Amr is Ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah, one of the leaders of Khuza'ah, who took charge of the House after Jurhum. He was the first to change the religion of Ibrahim the Friend (al-Khalil). He brought idols into the Hijaz, called the common people to worship them and to seek nearness to them, and established for them these pagan laws concerning livestock and other things, as Allah the Exalted mentioned in Surah al-An'am, at His words: ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He created of the crops and livestock﴾ [al-An'am: 136], and the verses after it on this subject.

As for al-Bahirah, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it is the she-camel that has given birth to five offspring; they looked at the fifth, and if it was a male they slaughtered it, and only the men ate it, not the women. If it was a female, they slit its ears and said: "This is a bahirah."

As-Suddi and others mentioned something close to this.

As for as-Sa'ibah, Mujahid said: it is from the sheep, similar to what was explained for the bahirah, except that it is the offspring born from a litter that came between it and six offspring that were in its condition. If it gave birth to a seventh that was a male or two males, they slaughtered it, and only their men ate it, not their women.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The sa'ibah is the she-camel that has given birth to ten females, with no male among them. She was let loose and not ridden, her wool was not shorn, and no one milked her milk except a guest.

Abu Rawq said: The sa'ibah: when a man set out and his need was fulfilled, he let loose a she-camel or something else from his property and dedicated it to the tawaghit. Whatever it bore was its own.

As-Suddi said: When one of them had his need fulfilled, or recovered from an illness, or his wealth increased, he let loose some of his property for the idols. Whoever from the people came across it was punished with a worldly punishment.

As for al-Wasilah, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it is the ewe that has given birth to seven litters. They looked at the seventh; if it was a male or a female and was dead, the men shared in it, not the women. If it was a female, they let it live. If in one litter there was a male and a female, they let them both live and said: "Her sister joined her, so she has forbidden her to us." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, concerning: ﴿nor wasilah﴾. He said: The wasilah is from the camels: the she-camel would give birth to a female first, then to another female after it. They named it the wasilah, and they would say: "She joined two females with no male between them." So they would slit its ear for their tawaghit.

This is also narrated from Imam Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The wasilah from the sheep: when a ewe gave birth to ten females in five litters, two twins in each litter, it was called the wasilah and left alone. Whatever it bore after that, male or female, was dedicated to the males and not the females. If it was dead, they shared in it.

As for al-Ham, al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When a man's stallion camel had served ten times, it was said: "Ham," so leave him alone.

Abu Rawq and Qatadah said the same. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: As for al-Ham, it is the stallion camel: when his offspring had offspring, they said: "This one has protected his back, so they do not burden him with anything, do not shear his wool, and do not prevent him from pasture or from a watering-place from which he drinks, even if the watering-place belongs to someone other than its owner."

Ibn Wahb said: I heard Malik say: As for al-Ham, it is from the camels. He would serve the camels, and when his serving was finished, they would place peacock feathers on him and let him loose.

Other explanations of this verse have been given. A hadith has been narrated concerning it, which Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through the route of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Abu al-Ahwas al-Jushami, from his father Malik ibn Nadlah, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) wearing worn-out clothes. He said to me: "Do you have any wealth?" I said: "Yes." He said: "What kind of wealth?" I said: "Of every kind: camels, sheep, horses, and slaves." He said: "When Allah gives you wealth, let its effect be seen on you." Then he said: "Do your camels give birth with their ears intact?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Do camels give birth except in that way?" Then he said: "Perhaps you take a knife and cut the ears of some of them, saying: 'This is a bahir,' and slit the ears of some of them, saying: 'This is a haram'?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Do not do that, for everything Allah has given you is lawful." Then he recited: ﴿Allah did not ordain any bahirah, nor sa'ibah, nor wasilah, nor ham﴾. As for the bahirah, it is the one whose ears they slit, so that his wife, his daughters, and no one of his household benefits from its wool, its hair, its fur, or its milk. When it died, they shared in it. As for the sa'ibah, it is the one they let loose for their gods and go to their gods and let it loose. As for the wasilah, the sheep gives birth to six litters, and when it gives birth to the seventh, it is slit and its horn is cut, so they say: "It has been joined," so they do not slaughter it, do not mate it, and do not prevent it, wherever it comes to a watering-place. Thus the explanation of this is given as interpolated into the hadith. It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas 'Awf ibn Malik, as his own statement, and this is more likely.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/122), narrated through the route of Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from his father.]

Imam Ahmad also narrated this hadith from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Abu al-Za'ra' 'Amr ibn 'Amr, from his paternal uncle Abu al-Ahwas 'Awf ibn Malik ibn Nadlah, from his father, with the same wording. But it does not contain the explanation of these terms. [Al-Musnad (4/136).] And Allah knows best.

As for His words: ﴿But those who disbelieve fabricate lies against Allah, and most of them do not reason﴾: that is, Allah did not legislate these things, nor are they an act of worship in His sight. Rather the polytheists fabricated them, made them a law for themselves, and a means of drawing near to Him by which they seek nearness. But this does not benefit them; rather it is a burden upon them.

﴿And when it is said to them: "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," they say: "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon"﴾: that is, when they are called to the religion of Allah and His law, to what He has made obligatory and to abandoning what He has forbidden, they say: "What we found our fathers and forefathers upon of ways and paths is sufficient for us." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Even though their fathers knew nothing﴾, that is, they did not understand the truth, did not recognize it, and were not guided to it. So how would they follow them in this state? Only one more ignorant than them and further astray in the way would follow them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 103–104:

Al-Bukhari said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "Al-Bahirah (a she-camel whose milk was forbidden to the idols/tawaghit, so no one among the people would milk her)." "As-Sa'ibah: they would let them loose for their gods, and nothing would be carried upon them." He said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw 'Amr ibn 'Amir al-Khuza'i dragging his intestines in the Fire; he was the first to let loose the sawa'ib." "Al-Wasilah: the young she-camel that gives birth to a female at the first birth of the camels, then gives birth to another female after it. They would let them loose for their idols if one female was joined to another with no male between them." "Al-Ham: the stallion camel that has served a counted number of mares. When he had finished his service, they would leave him for the idols and spare him from being burdened, so nothing would be carried upon him. They called him al-Hami."

Muslim and an-Nasa'i also narrated it in the same way, from the narration of Ibrahim ibn Sa'd. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4623) and Sahih Muslim no. (2856).]

Then al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Yaman said to me: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: I heard Sa'id relate this. And Abu Hurayrah said, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar. Ibn al-Hadi also narrated it, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ). [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4623).]

Al-Hakim said: Al-Bukhari intended that Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hadi narrated it from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Bukht, from al-Zuhri. Our shaykh Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi mentioned this in "al-Atraf" and remained silent without drawing attention to it. There is room for scrutiny in what al-Hakim said, for Imam Ahmad and Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir both narrated it from the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Ibn al-Hadi, from al-Zuhri himself. [Al-Musnad (2/366) and Tafsir al-Tabari (11/116).] And Allah knows best.

Then al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Abi Ya'qub Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kirmani narrated to us, Hassan ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, that 'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw Hell, some of it crushing other parts of it, and I saw 'Amr dragging his intestines, and he was the first to let loose the sawa'ib." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4624).]

Ibn Jarir said: Hannad narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith narrated to me, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to Aktham ibn al-Jawn: "O Aktham, I saw 'Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah ibn Khindif dragging his intestines in the Fire, and I have never seen a man more like a man than you are like him, nor he like you." Aktham said: "Do you fear that his resemblance will harm me, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No, you are a believer and he is a disbeliever. He was the first to change the religion of Ibrahim, to slit the ears of the bahirah, to let loose the sa'ibah, and to protect the hami." Then he narrated it from Hannad, from 'Abdah, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording or the same. [Tafsir al-Tabari (11/117); Ibn Hisham narrated it in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (1/78) through the chain of Muhammad ibn Ishaq.]

These two chains are not in the books (of hadith).

Imam Ahmad said: 'Amr ibn Mujama' narrated to us, Ibrahim al-Hajari narrated to us, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The first to let loose the sawa'ib and to worship idols was Abu Khuza'ah 'Amr ibn 'Amir, and I saw him dragging his intestines in the Fire." Ahmad alone narrated it by this route. [Al-Musnad (1/446). Its chain includes Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari, who is weak, but the hadith has supporting narrations from the hadith of 'A'ishah and Abu Hurayrah mentioned above. See the words of Shaykh Nasir al-Din al-Albani in al-Silsilah al-Sahihah no. (1677).]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I know the first to let loose the sawa'ib, and the first to change the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)." They said: "Who is he, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "'Amr ibn Luhayy, brother of Bani Ka'b. I saw him dragging his intestines in the Fire, his stench harming the people of the Fire. And I know the first to slit the ears of the bahair (plural of bahirah)." They said: "Who is he, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "A man from Bani Mudlij. He had two she-camels, so he slit their ears, forbade their milk, and then afterwards drank their milk. I saw him in the Fire, and the two camels were biting him with their mouths and trampling him with their hooves." [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/191); al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (11/120) through 'Abd al-Razzaq.]

So this 'Amr is Ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah, one of the leaders of Khuza'ah, who took charge of the House after Jurhum. He was the first to change the religion of Ibrahim the Friend (al-Khalil). He brought idols into the Hijaz, called the common people to worship them and to seek nearness to them, and established for them these pagan laws concerning livestock and other things, as Allah the Exalted mentioned in Surah al-An'am, at His words: ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He created of the crops and livestock﴾ [al-An'am: 136], and the verses after it on this subject.

As for al-Bahirah, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it is the she-camel that has given birth to five offspring; they looked at the fifth, and if it was a male they slaughtered it, and only the men ate it, not the women. If it was a female, they slit its ears and said: "This is a bahirah."

As-Suddi and others mentioned something close to this.

As for as-Sa'ibah, Mujahid said: it is from the sheep, similar to what was explained for the bahirah, except that it is the offspring born from a litter that came between it and six offspring that were in its condition. If it gave birth to a seventh that was a male or two males, they slaughtered it, and only their men ate it, not their women.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The sa'ibah is the she-camel that has given birth to ten females, with no male among them. She was let loose and not ridden, her wool was not shorn, and no one milked her milk except a guest.

Abu Rawq said: The sa'ibah: when a man set out and his need was fulfilled, he let loose a she-camel or something else from his property and dedicated it to the tawaghit. Whatever it bore was its own.

As-Suddi said: When one of them had his need fulfilled, or recovered from an illness, or his wealth increased, he let loose some of his property for the idols. Whoever from the people came across it was punished with a worldly punishment.

As for al-Wasilah, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it is the ewe that has given birth to seven litters. They looked at the seventh; if it was a male or a female and was dead, the men shared in it, not the women. If it was a female, they let it live. If in one litter there was a male and a female, they let them both live and said: "Her sister joined her, so she has forbidden her to us." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, concerning: ﴿nor wasilah﴾. He said: The wasilah is from the camels: the she-camel would give birth to a female first, then to another female after it. They named it the wasilah, and they would say: "She joined two females with no male between them." So they would slit its ear for their tawaghit.

This is also narrated from Imam Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The wasilah from the sheep: when a ewe gave birth to ten females in five litters, two twins in each litter, it was called the wasilah and left alone. Whatever it bore after that, male or female, was dedicated to the males and not the females. If it was dead, they shared in it.

As for al-Ham, al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When a man's stallion camel had served ten times, it was said: "Ham," so leave him alone.

Abu Rawq and Qatadah said the same. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: As for al-Ham, it is the stallion camel: when his offspring had offspring, they said: "This one has protected his back, so they do not burden him with anything, do not shear his wool, and do not prevent him from pasture or from a watering-place from which he drinks, even if the watering-place belongs to someone other than its owner."

Ibn Wahb said: I heard Malik say: As for al-Ham, it is from the camels. He would serve the camels, and when his serving was finished, they would place peacock feathers on him and let him loose.

Other explanations of this verse have been given. A hadith has been narrated concerning it, which Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through the route of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Abu al-Ahwas al-Jushami, from his father Malik ibn Nadlah, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) wearing worn-out clothes. He said to me: "Do you have any wealth?" I said: "Yes." He said: "What kind of wealth?" I said: "Of every kind: camels, sheep, horses, and slaves." He said: "When Allah gives you wealth, let its effect be seen on you." Then he said: "Do your camels give birth with their ears intact?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Do camels give birth except in that way?" Then he said: "Perhaps you take a knife and cut the ears of some of them, saying: 'This is a bahir,' and slit the ears of some of them, saying: 'This is a haram'?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Do not do that, for everything Allah has given you is lawful." Then he recited: ﴿Allah did not ordain any bahirah, nor sa'ibah, nor wasilah, nor ham﴾. As for the bahirah, it is the one whose ears they slit, so that his wife, his daughters, and no one of his household benefits from its wool, its hair, its fur, or its milk. When it died, they shared in it. As for the sa'ibah, it is the one they let loose for their gods and go to their gods and let it loose. As for the wasilah, the sheep gives birth to six litters, and when it gives birth to the seventh, it is slit and its horn is cut, so they say: "It has been joined," so they do not slaughter it, do not mate it, and do not prevent it, wherever it comes to a watering-place. Thus the explanation of this is given as interpolated into the hadith. It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas 'Awf ibn Malik, as his own statement, and this is more likely.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/122), narrated through the route of Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from his father.]

Imam Ahmad also narrated this hadith from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Abu al-Za'ra' 'Amr ibn 'Amr, from his paternal uncle Abu al-Ahwas 'Awf ibn Malik ibn Nadlah, from his father, with the same wording. But it does not contain the explanation of these terms. [Al-Musnad (4/136).] And Allah knows best.

As for His words: ﴿But those who disbelieve fabricate lies against Allah, and most of them do not reason﴾: that is, Allah did not legislate these things, nor are they an act of worship in His sight. Rather the polytheists fabricated them, made them a law for themselves, and a means of drawing near to Him by which they seek nearness. But this does not benefit them; rather it is a burden upon them.

﴿And when it is said to them: "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," they say: "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon"﴾: that is, when they are called to the religion of Allah and His law, to what He has made obligatory and to abandoning what He has forbidden, they say: "What we found our fathers and forefathers upon of ways and paths is sufficient for us." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Even though their fathers knew nothing﴾, that is, they did not understand the truth, did not recognize it, and were not guided to it. So how would they follow them in this state? Only one more ignorant than them and further astray in the way would follow them.

The Most High says, commanding His believing servants to reform themselves and to do good with all their effort and ability, and informing them that whoever sets his own affairs right, the corruption of those among the people who have become corrupt will not harm him, whether they are near to him or far from him.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the tafsir of this verse: The Most High says: when the servant obeys Me in what I have commanded him of the lawful and the unlawful ["in Dal: 'and what I have forbidden him from'"], the one who goes astray after him will not harm him, when he acts upon what I have commanded him.

Al-Walibi narrated likewise from him, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said the same. As for His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves; the one who has strayed will not harm you when you are guided﴾, the phrase "upon you is yourselves" is in the accusative under the construction of al-Ighra' (a form of urging or exhortation, where the speaker directs the listener to something he must take hold of). ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, meaning: He will repay every doer for his deed, if good then good, and if evil then evil.

There is no proof in the verse for abandoning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, when doing so is possible. Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah ["i.e., Ibn Mu'awiyah"] narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us: Qays narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood up, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said: "O people, you recite this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves; the one who has strayed will not harm you when you are guided﴾" until the end of the verse, and you place it in other than its proper place. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When people see the evil and do not change it, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is near to send His punishment upon them all." He said: And I heard Abu Bakr say: "O people, beware of lying, for lying is far from faith."

This hadith has been related by the authors of the Four Sunan, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and others, through many chains from a large number of narrators, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with it connected and traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) [marfu', i.e., traced to the Prophet]. Some of them related it from him with it stopping at al-Siddiq [mawquf, i.e., stopping at the Companion]. Al-Daraqutni and others have preferred its being marfu'. We have mentioned its chains and the discussion about it at length in the Musnad of al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Sa'id ibn Ya'qub al-Talaqani narrated to us, and 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us: 'Utbah ibn Abi Hakim narrated to us: 'Amr ibn Jariya ["in Dal: 'ibn al-Harith'"] al-Lakhmi narrated to us, from Abu Umayya al-Sha'bani ["in Dal: 'al-Sha'thani'"], who said: I came to Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani and said to him: How do you deal with this verse? He said: Which verse? I said: His saying [Most High] ["addition from Dal"] ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves; the one who has strayed will not harm you when you are guided﴾. He said: By Allah, you have asked about it one who is well informed. I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it, and he said: "Rather, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, until you see stinginess obeyed, desire followed, the world preferred, and every person of opinion pleased with his own opinion. Then keep to your own self and leave the common people, for behind you are days in which patience is like grasping a live coal; for the one who acts in them is like the reward of fifty men who act as you act." 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: Other than 'Utbah added: It was said: O Messenger of Allah, the reward of fifty men from among them, or from among us? He said: "Rather, the reward of fifty from among you."

Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan gharib sahih hadith. Likewise Abu Dawud related it through the route of Ibn al-Mubarak, and Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it from 'Utbah ibn Abi Hakim. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3058), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4341), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4014), and Tafsir al-Tabari (11/145).]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, that a man asked Ibn Mas'ud about His saying ["in Dal: 'was asked about his saying'"] ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves; the one who has strayed will not harm you when you are guided﴾. He said: This is not its time; today it is accepted. But its time is about to come, when you enjoin and it is done to you such and such—or he said: it is not accepted from you—then at that time: ﴿upon you is yourselves; the one who has strayed will not harm you﴾.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi related it from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ibn Mas'ud concerning His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves; the one who has strayed will not harm you when you are guided﴾, the verse. He said: They were sitting with 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, and there was between two men some of what happens among people, until each of them stood up to the other. A man from among the companions of 'Abd Allah said: Shall I not stand up and command them to what is right and forbid them from what is wrong? Another beside him said: Keep to yourself, for Allah says: ﴿[O you who have believed] ["addition from Dal"] upon you is yourselves﴾, the verse. He said: Ibn Mas'ud heard it ["in Dal: 'so he rejected it'"] and said: Stop! The interpretation of this has not yet come. The Qur'an was revealed as it was revealed, and among it are verses whose interpretation passed before they were revealed, and among it are verses whose interpretation occurred in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and among it are verses whose interpretation occurred a little after the Prophet (ﷺ), and among it are verses whose interpretation will occur after today, and among it are verses whose interpretation will occur at the Hour concerning what has been mentioned of the Hour, and among it are verses whose interpretation will occur on the Day of Reckoning concerning what has been mentioned of the reckoning, Paradise and the Fire. So as long as your hearts are one, and your desires are one, and you have not been divided into factions, and some of you have not tasted the violence of others, then enjoin and forbid. But when hearts and desires differ, and you are divided into factions, and some of you taste the violence of others, then each person is for himself; at that time the interpretation of this verse will come to us. Related by Ibn Jarir. [Tafsir al-Tabari (11/143).]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa narrated to us: Shababa ibn Sawwar narrated to us: al-Rabi' ibn Subayh narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn 'Iqal, who said: It was said to Ibn 'Umar: If you sat in these days and did not command or forbid, for Allah has said: ﴿Upon you is yourselves; the one who has strayed will not harm you when you are guided﴾? Ibn 'Umar said: It does not belong to me or to my companions, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let the one who is present convey it to the one who is absent." So we were the present ones and you are the absent ones; but this verse is for peoples who will come after us, and if they say it, it will not be accepted from them. [Tafsir al-Tabari (11/139).]

He also said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Abu 'Asim narrated to us, both saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from Sawwar ibn Shabib, who said: I was with Ibn 'Umar when a man came to him, strong in the eye and sharp in tongue, and said: O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, six men, all of whom have read the Qur'an and hastened in it, all of whom strive and do not fall short, yet all of whom are disliked by one another for wanting to come to lowness; and in that they testify against one another with shirk. A man from the people said: What lowness do you want more than that some of them testify against others with shirk?

The man said: I am not asking you, I am asking the shaykh. He repeated the hadith to 'Abd Allah, and 'Abd Allah said: Perhaps you think, may you have no father, that I will command you to go and kill them! Admonish them and forbid them; if they disobey you, then upon you is your own self, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves﴾, the verse.

He also said: Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to me: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us: I heard my father: Qatada narrated to us, from Abu Mazin, who said: I went during the time of 'Uthman to Medina, and there were a group of Muslims sitting, and one of them recited this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves; the one who has strayed will not harm you﴾. The eldest ["in Dal: 'the most numerous'"] of them said: The interpretation of this verse has not come today.

He said: al-Qasim narrated to us: al-Husayn narrated to us: Ibn Fadala narrated to us, from Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: I was in a circle in which were companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I was the youngest of the people. They discussed enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and I said: Does not Allah say in His Book: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves; the one who has strayed will not harm you when you are guided﴾? They turned toward me with one tongue and said: You pluck a verse from the Qur'an and do not know it, and you do not know what its interpretation is!! Until I wished I had not spoken. Then they turned to conversing, and when the time of their standing up came, they said: You are a young lad, and you have plucked a verse and do not know what it is? Perhaps you will live to see that time, when you see stinginess obeyed, desire followed, and every person of opinion pleased with his own opinion: then keep to yourself; the one who has strayed will not harm you when you are guided. [Tafsir al-Tabari (11/142).]

Ibn Jarir said: 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us: Dhamra ibn Rabi'a narrated to us, who said: al-Hasan recited this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves; the one who has strayed will not harm you when you are guided﴾. Then al-Hasan said: Praise be to Allah for it, and praise be to Allah for what it contains. There was no believer in the past, nor any believer in what remains, except that beside him is a hypocrite who dislikes his deed.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: When you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, the one who has strayed will not harm you when you are guided.

Ibn Jarir related it. It was also narrated through the route of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abu al-'Umays, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Hudhayfa, the like of it. Likewise said many of the predecessors.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us: Hisham ibn Khalid al-Dimashqi narrated to us: al-Walid narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Ka'b, concerning His saying: ﴿Upon you is yourselves; the one who has strayed will not harm you when you are guided﴾, who said: When the church of Damascus is demolished and made into a mosque, and the wearing of silk ["al-'asb" is a striped Yemeni cloth] appears, then at that time will be the interpretation of this verse.

This noble verse contains a weighty ruling. It has been said that it is abrogated (*mansukh*), and this was related by al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman also said, on the authority of Ibrahim, that it is abrogated. Others, who are the majority according to what Ibn Jarir said, held that it is definitive (*muhkam*). Whoever claims abrogation must provide the proof.

As for Allah's words, ﴿O you who believe, the testimony between you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest should be two [witnesses]﴾, this is the predicate, since His words ﴿the testimony between you﴾ require one. It was said that the implied meaning is "the testimony of two," the first noun being omitted and the second put in its place. It was also said that the sentence indicates the supposition that two persons should bear witness.
* *
His words ﴿of just character﴾ describe the two, that they should be just.
* *
His words ﴿from among you﴾ mean from among the Muslims. This is the view of the majority. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿of just character from among you﴾, that he said: "From among the Muslims." Ibn Abi Hatim related it and then said: It was also narrated from 'Ubaydah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Yahya ibn Ya'mur, al-Suddi, Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, something similar to this.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said that what is meant by ﴿of just character from among you﴾ is from the clan of the one making the bequest. This view was related from 'Ikrimah, 'Ubaydah, and several others.
* *
His words ﴿or two others from outside your own﴾: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sa'id ibn 'Awn narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Habib ibn Abi 'Amrah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said concerning His words ﴿or two others from outside your own﴾: "From outside the Muslims," meaning the People of the Book.

Then he said: It was also related from 'Ubaydah, Shurayh, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Muhammad ibn Sirin, Yahya ibn Ya'mur, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Qatadah, Abu Mijlaz, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, something similar to this.

According to what Ibn Jarir related from 'Ikrimah and 'Ubaydah concerning His words ﴿from among you﴾, meaning from the clan of the one making the bequest, the meaning here of ﴿or two others from outside your own﴾ is from outside the clan of the one making the bequest. Ibn Abi Hatim also related something similar from al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Zuhri, may Allah have mercy on them both.
* *
His words ﴿if you are travelling in the land﴾, meaning you are journeying, ﴿and the calamity of death befalls you﴾. These are two conditions for permitting the testimony of dhimmis (protected non-Muslims) when Muslims are absent: that it occur during a journey, and that it concern a bequest. Shurayh the judge explicitly stated this.

Ibn Jarir said: Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us, both saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Shurayh, who said: The testimony of a Jew or a Christian is not valid except during a journey, and it is not valid during a journey except in a bequest.

Then he related it from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, who said: Shurayh said, and he mentioned something similar.

Something similar has also been related from Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him. This issue is one in which he stood alone, and the three other imams disagreed with him, saying: The testimony of dhimmis against Muslims is not valid. Abu Hanifah permitted it among them with respect to one another.

Ibn Jarir also said: Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Salih ibn Abi al-Akhdar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: The Sunnah has passed that the testimony of an unbeliever is not valid whether at home or on a journey; it is only [valid] among Muslims.

Ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed concerning a man who died with no Muslim present with him. That was at the beginning of Islam, when the land was at war and the people were unbelievers, and people used to inherit through bequest. Then the bequest was abrogated, the obligatory shares were prescribed, and the people acted accordingly.

Ibn Jarir related this, but there is room for consideration in it, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir also said: There has been disagreement over His words ﴿the testimony between you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest should be two, of just character from among you, or two others from outside your own﴾: does it mean that he should make them his executors, or that he should call them as witnesses? There are two views:

The first is that he should appoint them as executors, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, who said: Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about this verse and said: This is a man who travelled with wealth, and his appointed time overtook him. If he finds two men among the Muslims, he hands over his estate to them and calls two just Muslims as witnesses over them.

Ibn Abi Hatim related it, and there is a break in its chain.

The second view is that the two are to be witnesses. This is the apparent context of the noble verse. If there is no third executor with them, both qualities, executorship and testimony, are combined in them, as in the story of Tamim al-Dari and 'Adi ibn Bada', as will be mentioned shortly, if Allah wills. And success is from Allah.

Ibn Jarir found it problematic that they should be witnesses, saying: "Because we do not know of any ruling in which a witness swears an oath." But this does not prevent the ruling contained in this noble verse, which is an independent ruling that does not necessarily have to follow the analogy of all rulings. Moreover, this is a ruling specific to a particular testimony in a particular context, and in it are allowed matters that are not allowed elsewhere. When signs of suspicion arise, this witness takes an oath according to what this noble verse indicates.
* *
His words, may He be exalted, ﴿you shall detain them both after the prayer﴾. Ibn 'Abbas [, from al-'Awfi,] said: This means the afternoon prayer (*salat al-'asr*). Similarly, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Qatadah, 'Ikrimah, and Muhammad ibn Sirin said. al-Zuhri said: It means the prayer of the Muslims. al-Suddi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: It means the prayer of their religious community.

The intended meaning is that these two witnesses are to stand after a prayer at which people have gathered in their presence, ﴿and they will swear by Allah﴾, meaning they will take an oath by Allah, ﴿if you doubt﴾, meaning if suspicion about them appears to you, that they have betrayed or embezzled, ﴿then they will swear by Allah﴾ at that time, ﴿that we will not sell it﴾, meaning our oaths, as said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan, ﴿for any price﴾, meaning we will not exchange it for a small compensation of the perishable, transient worldly life, ﴿even if it were a near relative﴾, meaning even if the one testified against were close to us, we would not show favouritism toward him, ﴿nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah﴾. He attributed it to Allah to honour it and to magnify its matter.

Some read: "nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah (*ālLāh*)" in the genitive, as an oath. Ibn Jarir related it from 'Amir al-Sha'bi. It was also reported from some that they read: "nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah (*Allāhu*)," but the first reading is the well-known one.

﴿Indeed, we would then be among the sinful﴾, meaning if we did any of that, by distorting the testimony, altering it, changing it, or concealing it entirely.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿But if it becomes known that the two had incurred sin﴾, meaning if it becomes widely known, manifest, and established against the two witnesses who were executors that they betrayed or embezzled some of the property bequeathed to them, and this became evident against them, ﴿then two others will take their place from among those who have a rightful claim against them, the nearest of kin﴾. This is the reading of the majority: "*istuhiqqa* ('alayhimu al-awlayan)" (passive). It is related from 'Ali, Ubayy, and al-Hasan al-Basri that they read it: ﴿istahaqqa 'alayhimu al-awlayan﴾ (active).

Al-Hakim related in al-Mustadrak, through the route of Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Farawi, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that the Prophet ﷺ recited: ﴿from among those who have a rightful claim, the nearest of kin﴾, and then said: "Sound according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." (*al-Mustadrak* 2/237, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.)

Some read, among them Ibn 'Abbas: "from among those who have a rightful claim, the first ones" (*al-awwalin*). al-Hasan read: "from among those who have a rightful claim, the first two" (*al-awwalan*), as related by Ibn Jarir.

According to the reading of the majority, the meaning is: whenever it is established by a sound report that they betrayed, then two of the heirs who are entitled to the estate, and who are the most rightful of those who inherit that property, should stand, ﴿and they will swear by Allah: our testimony is more worthy than their testimony﴾, meaning, regarding our claim that they betrayed, our testimony is more worthy, more correct, and more firmly established than their earlier testimony. ﴿And we have not transgressed﴾, meaning in what we have said of betrayal. ﴿Indeed, we would then be among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning if we have lied about them.

This oath is for the heirs, and the reliance on their statement in such a situation is like the oath taken by the relatives of a murdered person when a *lawth* (indication of guilt) appears against the killer. The entitled ones swear against the killer, and he is handed over to them in full, as is established in the chapter on *al-Qasama* (the oath of fifty) in the rulings.

The Sunnah has also come with the same as what this noble verse indicates. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Abu al-Nadr, from Badhan, meaning Abu Salih, freed slave of Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Tamim al-Dari concerning this verse: ﴿O you who believe, the testimony between you when death approaches one of you﴾. He said: "People were absolved of it except for me and 'Adi ibn Bada'. They were both Christians, who travelled to Syria before Islam. They came to Syria for their trade, and there came to them a freed slave of the clan of Sahm, called Budayl ibn Abi Maryam, with merchandise, and with him was a silver cup, which he intended for the king, and it was the greatest of his trade. He fell ill, and he made them his executors and instructed them to deliver what he had left to his family." Tamim said: "When he died, we took that cup and sold it for a thousand dirhams, and then we divided it between myself and 'Adi ibn Bada'. When we returned to his family, we handed over to them what we had with us, but they missed the cup and asked us about it. We said: 'He left nothing but this, and nothing else was handed to us.'" Tamim said: "When I embraced Islam after the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, I felt guilty about that. So I went to his family, informed them of the matter, and paid them five hundred dirhams, and I told them that my companion had the same amount. They rushed at him to make him swear by what is held in high regard among their religious community. He swore, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, the testimony between you﴾ up to His words: ﴿they will swear by Allah: our testimony is more worthy than their testimony﴾. Then 'Amr ibn al-'As and another man from among them stood and swore, and the five hundred were taken from 'Adi ibn Bada'."

Thus it was also related by Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir, both from al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb al-Harrani, from Muhammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, with it, and he mentioned it [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3059), and Tafsir al-Tabari (11/186).]] - and in his version: they brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he asked them for evidence, but they found none, so he ordered them to have him swear by that which is held in greatest reverence among the people of his religion. He swore, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when death approaches one of you, let there be testimony between you﴾ up to His words: ﴿or fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths﴾. Then 'Amr ibn al-'As and another man stood up and swore, and the five hundred were taken from 'Adi ibn Bada'.

Then he said: This is a strange hadith, and its chain is not sound. Abu al-Nadr, from whom Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this hadith, is in my view Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, kunyah Abu al-Nadr, and the people of hadith have abandoned him, and he is the author of the Tafsir. I heard Muhammad ibn Isma'il say: Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, kunyah Abu al-Nadr. Then he said: And we do not know of a narration from Salim Abu al-Nadr from Abu Salih, the mawla of Umm Hani'. Something of this has been related from Ibn 'Abbas in summary, by a route other than this one.

Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Ibn Abi Za'idah, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man from the Banu Sahm went out with Tamim al-Dari and 'Adi ibn Bada'. The Sahmi died in a land where there was no Muslim. When they returned with his estate, they lacked a silver goblet inlaid with gold. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had them take an oath, and the goblet was found in Makkah. It was said: We bought it from Tamim and 'Adi. Then two men from the heirs of the Sahmi stood up and swore by Allah that our testimony is more worthy than theirs, and that the goblet belongs to our companion. Concerning them the verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you﴾.

Likewise Abu Dawud related it from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Yahya ibn Adam, with it. Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a fine, strange hadith, and it is the hadith of Ibn Abi Za'idah. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3606), and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3060); its origin is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2780), but al-Bukhari did not report it as a narration (tahdith) but as a report of a statement (hikayah).]]

Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim is Kufan. It is said that he is salih al-hadith (acceptable in narration). This story was related in mursal form (without a companion named) by more than one of the Tabi'un (Successors), among them 'Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Sirin, and Qatadah. They also mentioned that the oath-taking was after the 'Asr prayer; Ibn Jarir related it. Likewise Mujahid, al-Hasan, and al-Dahhak related it in mursal form. This indicates its fame among the early generations (al-salaf) and its authenticity.

Among the supporting evidences for the authenticity of this story is also what Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir related:

Ya'qub related to me: Hushaym related to us: Zakariyya informed us, from al-Sha'bi, that a man from the Muslims was near death at Daquqa. He said: Death came upon him, and he did not find any Muslim to witness his bequest, so he called two men from the People of the Book as witnesses. He said: They came to Kufa and went to al-Ash'ari - meaning Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him - and informed him, and presented his estate and his bequest. Al-Ash'ari said: This is a matter that did not occur after what occurred in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: He had them take an oath after the 'Asr prayer: By Allah, they did not betray, nor lie, nor change, nor conceal, nor alter, and indeed it is the bequest of the man and his estate. He said: So he upheld their testimony.

Then he related it from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Shu'bah, from Mughirah al-Azraq, from al-Sha'bi, that Abu Musa judged at Daquqa. [[In D: "with it".]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/165).]]

These are two sound chains to al-Sha'bi, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.

As for his saying: "This is a matter that did not occur after what occurred in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that he meant by it the story of Tamim and 'Adi ibn Bada'. They mentioned that the Islam of Tamim ibn Aws al-Dari, may Allah be pleased with him, was in the ninth year of the Hijrah. Accordingly this ruling is later, and whoever claims it was abrogated (naskh) needs a decisive proof in this matter, and Allah knows best.

Asbat related from al-Suddi concerning: ﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you when death approaches one of you, at the time of bequest, two just men from among you﴾. He said: This refers to the bequest at the time of death; he makes a bequest and calls two Muslim men as witnesses to what he has and what he owes. He said: This is in the case of residence (hadar), ﴿or two others from other than you﴾ in travel (safar), ﴿if you are traveling in the land and the affliction of death befalls you﴾: this is a man whom death overtakes during his journey, with no Muslim present. He calls two men from the Jews, Christians, or Magians, and makes a bequest to them, and hands over his inheritance to them, and they accept it. If the heirs of the deceased accept the bequest and recognize the property of their companion, they leave the two men alone; but if they doubt, they bring the two before the ruler (sultan). That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You detain them after the prayer, and they swear by Allah if you doubt﴾. Abdullah ibn 'Abbas said: It is as if I look at the two non-Arabs when they were brought to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari at his house. He opened the document, and the heirs of the deceased denied it and accused them of betrayal. Abu Musa wanted to have them swear after the 'Asr prayer. I said to him: They do not care about the 'Asr prayer, but have them swear after their own prayer in their religion. So the two men are made to stand after their prayer in their religion, and they swear: By Allah, we will not sell it for a small price, even if it were a relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed we would then be among the sinners; that their companion did indeed make this bequest, and that this is indeed his estate. The ruler then says to them before they swear: If you conceal or betray, I will expose you before your people, your testimony will not be admitted, and I will punish you. When he says that to them, that is closer to their giving the testimony in its proper form. Ibn Jarir related it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/175).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn related to us: Hushaym related to us: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that they both said concerning this verse: ﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you﴾ to the end of the verse: When death approaches a man during a journey, let him call two Muslim men as witnesses. If he does not find two Muslim men, then two men from the People of the Book. When they come with his estate, if the heirs confirm them, their word is accepted; but if they accuse them, they are made to swear after the 'Asr prayer: By Allah, we did not conceal, nor lie, nor betray, nor alter.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the interpretation of this verse: If doubt is cast on their testimony, the two swear after the prayer by Allah: "We did not buy with our testimony a small price." If the guardians (awliya') discover that the two disbelievers lied in their testimony, two men from the guardians stand and swear by Allah that the testimony of the two disbelievers is void, and that we did not transgress. That is His saying: ﴿But if it is discovered that the two had incurred sin﴾, meaning: if it is discovered that the two disbelievers lied; ﴿then two others shall stand in their place﴾, meaning: from the guardians, and they swear by Allah that the testimony of the disbelievers is void and that we did not transgress; so the testimony of the two disbelievers is rejected, and the testimony of the guardians is accepted.

Al-'Awfi related the same from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Jarir related both.

Likewise this ruling in accordance with the requirement of this verse was upheld by more than one of the leading Successors and the early generation (al-salaf), may Allah be pleased with them, and it is the school (madhhab) of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is closer to their giving the testimony in its proper form﴾ means: the legislation of this ruling in this acceptable manner, by making the two dhimmi witnesses swear when they are suspected, is closer to their establishing the testimony in its acceptable form.

* *

His saying: ﴿or fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths﴾ means: what moves them to give the testimony in its proper form is the glorification of the oath by Allah, observing His right and reverence for Him, and fear of disgrace among the people if the oath is returned to the heirs, so they swear and claim what they seek. For this reason He said: ﴿or fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths﴾.

Then He said: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, meaning: in all your affairs, ﴿and listen﴾, meaning: and obey. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾, meaning: those who depart from His obedience and from following His law.

This noble verse contains a weighty ruling. It has been said that it is abrogated (*mansukh*), and this was related by al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman also said, on the authority of Ibrahim, that it is abrogated. Others, who are the majority according to what Ibn Jarir said, held that it is definitive (*muhkam*). Whoever claims abrogation must provide the proof.

As for Allah's words, ﴿O you who believe, the testimony between you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest should be two [witnesses]﴾, this is the predicate, since His words ﴿the testimony between you﴾ require one. It was said that the implied meaning is "the testimony of two," the first noun being omitted and the second put in its place. It was also said that the sentence indicates the supposition that two persons should bear witness.
