His words, may He be exalted, ﴿you shall detain them both after the prayer﴾. Ibn 'Abbas [, from al-'Awfi,] said: This means the afternoon prayer (*salat al-'asr*). Similarly, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Qatadah, 'Ikrimah, and Muhammad ibn Sirin said. al-Zuhri said: It means the prayer of the Muslims. al-Suddi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: It means the prayer of their religious community.

The intended meaning is that these two witnesses are to stand after a prayer at which people have gathered in their presence, ﴿and they will swear by Allah﴾, meaning they will take an oath by Allah, ﴿if you doubt﴾, meaning if suspicion about them appears to you, that they have betrayed or embezzled, ﴿then they will swear by Allah﴾ at that time, ﴿that we will not sell it﴾, meaning our oaths, as said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan, ﴿for any price﴾, meaning we will not exchange it for a small compensation of the perishable, transient worldly life, ﴿even if it were a near relative﴾, meaning even if the one testified against were close to us, we would not show favouritism toward him, ﴿nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah﴾. He attributed it to Allah to honour it and to magnify its matter.

Some read: "nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah (*ālLāh*)" in the genitive, as an oath. Ibn Jarir related it from 'Amir al-Sha'bi. It was also reported from some that they read: "nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah (*Allāhu*)," but the first reading is the well-known one.

﴿Indeed, we would then be among the sinful﴾, meaning if we did any of that, by distorting the testimony, altering it, changing it, or concealing it entirely.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿But if it becomes known that the two had incurred sin﴾, meaning if it becomes widely known, manifest, and established against the two witnesses who were executors that they betrayed or embezzled some of the property bequeathed to them, and this became evident against them, ﴿then two others will take their place from among those who have a rightful claim against them, the nearest of kin﴾. This is the reading of the majority: "*istuhiqqa* ('alayhimu al-awlayan)" (passive). It is related from 'Ali, Ubayy, and al-Hasan al-Basri that they read it: ﴿istahaqqa 'alayhimu al-awlayan﴾ (active).

Al-Hakim related in al-Mustadrak, through the route of Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Farawi, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that the Prophet ﷺ recited: ﴿from among those who have a rightful claim, the nearest of kin﴾, and then said: "Sound according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." (*al-Mustadrak* 2/237, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.)

Some read, among them Ibn 'Abbas: "from among those who have a rightful claim, the first ones" (*al-awwalin*). al-Hasan read: "from among those who have a rightful claim, the first two" (*al-awwalan*), as related by Ibn Jarir.

According to the reading of the majority, the meaning is: whenever it is established by a sound report that they betrayed, then two of the heirs who are entitled to the estate, and who are the most rightful of those who inherit that property, should stand, ﴿and they will swear by Allah: our testimony is more worthy than their testimony﴾, meaning, regarding our claim that they betrayed, our testimony is more worthy, more correct, and more firmly established than their earlier testimony. ﴿And we have not transgressed﴾, meaning in what we have said of betrayal. ﴿Indeed, we would then be among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning if we have lied about them.

This oath is for the heirs, and the reliance on their statement in such a situation is like the oath taken by the relatives of a murdered person when a *lawth* (indication of guilt) appears against the killer. The entitled ones swear against the killer, and he is handed over to them in full, as is established in the chapter on *al-Qasama* (the oath of fifty) in the rulings.

The Sunnah has also come with the same as what this noble verse indicates. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Abu al-Nadr, from Badhan, meaning Abu Salih, freed slave of Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Tamim al-Dari concerning this verse: ﴿O you who believe, the testimony between you when death approaches one of you﴾. He said: "People were absolved of it except for me and 'Adi ibn Bada'. They were both Christians, who travelled to Syria before Islam. They came to Syria for their trade, and there came to them a freed slave of the clan of Sahm, called Budayl ibn Abi Maryam, with merchandise, and with him was a silver cup, which he intended for the king, and it was the greatest of his trade. He fell ill, and he made them his executors and instructed them to deliver what he had left to his family." Tamim said: "When he died, we took that cup and sold it for a thousand dirhams, and then we divided it between myself and 'Adi ibn Bada'. When we returned to his family, we handed over to them what we had with us, but they missed the cup and asked us about it. We said: 'He left nothing but this, and nothing else was handed to us.'" Tamim said: "When I embraced Islam after the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, I felt guilty about that. So I went to his family, informed them of the matter, and paid them five hundred dirhams, and I told them that my companion had the same amount. They rushed at him to make him swear by what is held in high regard among their religious community. He swore, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, the testimony between you﴾ up to His words: ﴿they will swear by Allah: our testimony is more worthy than their testimony﴾. Then 'Amr ibn al-'As and another man from among them stood and swore, and the five hundred were taken from 'Adi ibn Bada'."

Thus it was also related by Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir, both from al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb al-Harrani, from Muhammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, with it, and he mentioned it [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3059), and Tafsir al-Tabari (11/186).]] - and in his version: they brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he asked them for evidence, but they found none, so he ordered them to have him swear by that which is held in greatest reverence among the people of his religion. He swore, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when death approaches one of you, let there be testimony between you﴾ up to His words: ﴿or fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths﴾. Then 'Amr ibn al-'As and another man stood up and swore, and the five hundred were taken from 'Adi ibn Bada'.

Then he said: This is a strange hadith, and its chain is not sound. Abu al-Nadr, from whom Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this hadith, is in my view Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, kunyah Abu al-Nadr, and the people of hadith have abandoned him, and he is the author of the Tafsir. I heard Muhammad ibn Isma'il say: Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, kunyah Abu al-Nadr. Then he said: And we do not know of a narration from Salim Abu al-Nadr from Abu Salih, the mawla of Umm Hani'. Something of this has been related from Ibn 'Abbas in summary, by a route other than this one.

Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Ibn Abi Za'idah, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man from the Banu Sahm went out with Tamim al-Dari and 'Adi ibn Bada'. The Sahmi died in a land where there was no Muslim. When they returned with his estate, they lacked a silver goblet inlaid with gold. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had them take an oath, and the goblet was found in Makkah. It was said: We bought it from Tamim and 'Adi. Then two men from the heirs of the Sahmi stood up and swore by Allah that our testimony is more worthy than theirs, and that the goblet belongs to our companion. Concerning them the verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you﴾.

Likewise Abu Dawud related it from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Yahya ibn Adam, with it. Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a fine, strange hadith, and it is the hadith of Ibn Abi Za'idah. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3606), and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3060); its origin is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2780), but al-Bukhari did not report it as a narration (tahdith) but as a report of a statement (hikayah).]]

Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim is Kufan. It is said that he is salih al-hadith (acceptable in narration). This story was related in mursal form (without a companion named) by more than one of the Tabi'un (Successors), among them 'Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Sirin, and Qatadah. They also mentioned that the oath-taking was after the 'Asr prayer; Ibn Jarir related it. Likewise Mujahid, al-Hasan, and al-Dahhak related it in mursal form. This indicates its fame among the early generations (al-salaf) and its authenticity.

Among the supporting evidences for the authenticity of this story is also what Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir related:

Ya'qub related to me: Hushaym related to us: Zakariyya informed us, from al-Sha'bi, that a man from the Muslims was near death at Daquqa. He said: Death came upon him, and he did not find any Muslim to witness his bequest, so he called two men from the People of the Book as witnesses. He said: They came to Kufa and went to al-Ash'ari - meaning Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him - and informed him, and presented his estate and his bequest. Al-Ash'ari said: This is a matter that did not occur after what occurred in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: He had them take an oath after the 'Asr prayer: By Allah, they did not betray, nor lie, nor change, nor conceal, nor alter, and indeed it is the bequest of the man and his estate. He said: So he upheld their testimony.

Then he related it from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Shu'bah, from Mughirah al-Azraq, from al-Sha'bi, that Abu Musa judged at Daquqa. [[In D: "with it".]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/165).]]

These are two sound chains to al-Sha'bi, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.

As for his saying: "This is a matter that did not occur after what occurred in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that he meant by it the story of Tamim and 'Adi ibn Bada'. They mentioned that the Islam of Tamim ibn Aws al-Dari, may Allah be pleased with him, was in the ninth year of the Hijrah. Accordingly this ruling is later, and whoever claims it was abrogated (naskh) needs a decisive proof in this matter, and Allah knows best.

Asbat related from al-Suddi concerning: ﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you when death approaches one of you, at the time of bequest, two just men from among you﴾. He said: This refers to the bequest at the time of death; he makes a bequest and calls two Muslim men as witnesses to what he has and what he owes. He said: This is in the case of residence (hadar), ﴿or two others from other than you﴾ in travel (safar), ﴿if you are traveling in the land and the affliction of death befalls you﴾: this is a man whom death overtakes during his journey, with no Muslim present. He calls two men from the Jews, Christians, or Magians, and makes a bequest to them, and hands over his inheritance to them, and they accept it. If the heirs of the deceased accept the bequest and recognize the property of their companion, they leave the two men alone; but if they doubt, they bring the two before the ruler (sultan). That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You detain them after the prayer, and they swear by Allah if you doubt﴾. Abdullah ibn 'Abbas said: It is as if I look at the two non-Arabs when they were brought to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari at his house. He opened the document, and the heirs of the deceased denied it and accused them of betrayal. Abu Musa wanted to have them swear after the 'Asr prayer. I said to him: They do not care about the 'Asr prayer, but have them swear after their own prayer in their religion. So the two men are made to stand after their prayer in their religion, and they swear: By Allah, we will not sell it for a small price, even if it were a relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed we would then be among the sinners; that their companion did indeed make this bequest, and that this is indeed his estate. The ruler then says to them before they swear: If you conceal or betray, I will expose you before your people, your testimony will not be admitted, and I will punish you. When he says that to them, that is closer to their giving the testimony in its proper form. Ibn Jarir related it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/175).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn related to us: Hushaym related to us: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that they both said concerning this verse: ﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you﴾ to the end of the verse: When death approaches a man during a journey, let him call two Muslim men as witnesses. If he does not find two Muslim men, then two men from the People of the Book. When they come with his estate, if the heirs confirm them, their word is accepted; but if they accuse them, they are made to swear after the 'Asr prayer: By Allah, we did not conceal, nor lie, nor betray, nor alter.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the interpretation of this verse: If doubt is cast on their testimony, the two swear after the prayer by Allah: "We did not buy with our testimony a small price." If the guardians (awliya') discover that the two disbelievers lied in their testimony, two men from the guardians stand and swear by Allah that the testimony of the two disbelievers is void, and that we did not transgress. That is His saying: ﴿But if it is discovered that the two had incurred sin﴾, meaning: if it is discovered that the two disbelievers lied; ﴿then two others shall stand in their place﴾, meaning: from the guardians, and they swear by Allah that the testimony of the disbelievers is void and that we did not transgress; so the testimony of the two disbelievers is rejected, and the testimony of the guardians is accepted.

Al-'Awfi related the same from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Jarir related both.

Likewise this ruling in accordance with the requirement of this verse was upheld by more than one of the leading Successors and the early generation (al-salaf), may Allah be pleased with them, and it is the school (madhhab) of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is closer to their giving the testimony in its proper form﴾ means: the legislation of this ruling in this acceptable manner, by making the two dhimmi witnesses swear when they are suspected, is closer to their establishing the testimony in its acceptable form.

* *

His saying: ﴿or fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths﴾ means: what moves them to give the testimony in its proper form is the glorification of the oath by Allah, observing His right and reverence for Him, and fear of disgrace among the people if the oath is returned to the heirs, so they swear and claim what they seek. For this reason He said: ﴿or fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths﴾.

Then He said: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, meaning: in all your affairs, ﴿and listen﴾, meaning: and obey. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾, meaning: those who depart from His obedience and from following His law.

This noble verse contains a weighty ruling. It has been said that it is abrogated (*mansukh*), and this was related by al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman also said, on the authority of Ibrahim, that it is abrogated. Others, who are the majority according to what Ibn Jarir said, held that it is definitive (*muhkam*). Whoever claims abrogation must provide the proof.

As for Allah's words, ﴿O you who believe, the testimony between you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest should be two [witnesses]﴾, this is the predicate, since His words ﴿the testimony between you﴾ require one. It was said that the implied meaning is "the testimony of two," the first noun being omitted and the second put in its place. It was also said that the sentence indicates the supposition that two persons should bear witness.
* *
His words ﴿of just character﴾ describe the two, that they should be just.
* *
His words ﴿from among you﴾ mean from among the Muslims. This is the view of the majority. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿of just character from among you﴾, that he said: "From among the Muslims." Ibn Abi Hatim related it and then said: It was also narrated from 'Ubaydah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Yahya ibn Ya'mur, al-Suddi, Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, something similar to this.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said that what is meant by ﴿of just character from among you﴾ is from the clan of the one making the bequest. This view was related from 'Ikrimah, 'Ubaydah, and several others.
* *
His words ﴿or two others from outside your own﴾: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sa'id ibn 'Awn narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Habib ibn Abi 'Amrah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said concerning His words ﴿or two others from outside your own﴾: "From outside the Muslims," meaning the People of the Book.

Then he said: It was also related from 'Ubaydah, Shurayh, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Muhammad ibn Sirin, Yahya ibn Ya'mur, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Qatadah, Abu Mijlaz, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, something similar to this.

According to what Ibn Jarir related from 'Ikrimah and 'Ubaydah concerning His words ﴿from among you﴾, meaning from the clan of the one making the bequest, the meaning here of ﴿or two others from outside your own﴾ is from outside the clan of the one making the bequest. Ibn Abi Hatim also related something similar from al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Zuhri, may Allah have mercy on them both.
* *
His words ﴿if you are travelling in the land﴾, meaning you are journeying, ﴿and the calamity of death befalls you﴾. These are two conditions for permitting the testimony of dhimmis (protected non-Muslims) when Muslims are absent: that it occur during a journey, and that it concern a bequest. Shurayh the judge explicitly stated this.

Ibn Jarir said: Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us, both saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Shurayh, who said: The testimony of a Jew or a Christian is not valid except during a journey, and it is not valid during a journey except in a bequest.

Then he related it from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, who said: Shurayh said, and he mentioned something similar.

Something similar has also been related from Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him. This issue is one in which he stood alone, and the three other imams disagreed with him, saying: The testimony of dhimmis against Muslims is not valid. Abu Hanifah permitted it among them with respect to one another.

Ibn Jarir also said: Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Salih ibn Abi al-Akhdar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: The Sunnah has passed that the testimony of an unbeliever is not valid whether at home or on a journey; it is only [valid] among Muslims.

Ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed concerning a man who died with no Muslim present with him. That was at the beginning of Islam, when the land was at war and the people were unbelievers, and people used to inherit through bequest. Then the bequest was abrogated, the obligatory shares were prescribed, and the people acted accordingly.

Ibn Jarir related this, but there is room for consideration in it, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir also said: There has been disagreement over His words ﴿the testimony between you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest should be two, of just character from among you, or two others from outside your own﴾: does it mean that he should make them his executors, or that he should call them as witnesses? There are two views:

The first is that he should appoint them as executors, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, who said: Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about this verse and said: This is a man who travelled with wealth, and his appointed time overtook him. If he finds two men among the Muslims, he hands over his estate to them and calls two just Muslims as witnesses over them.

Ibn Abi Hatim related it, and there is a break in its chain.

The second view is that the two are to be witnesses. This is the apparent context of the noble verse. If there is no third executor with them, both qualities, executorship and testimony, are combined in them, as in the story of Tamim al-Dari and 'Adi ibn Bada', as will be mentioned shortly, if Allah wills. And success is from Allah.

Ibn Jarir found it problematic that they should be witnesses, saying: "Because we do not know of any ruling in which a witness swears an oath." But this does not prevent the ruling contained in this noble verse, which is an independent ruling that does not necessarily have to follow the analogy of all rulings. Moreover, this is a ruling specific to a particular testimony in a particular context, and in it are allowed matters that are not allowed elsewhere. When signs of suspicion arise, this witness takes an oath according to what this noble verse indicates.
* *
His words, may He be exalted, ﴿you shall detain them both after the prayer﴾. Ibn 'Abbas [, from al-'Awfi,] said: This means the afternoon prayer (*salat al-'asr*). Similarly, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Qatadah, 'Ikrimah, and Muhammad ibn Sirin said. al-Zuhri said: It means the prayer of the Muslims. al-Suddi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: It means the prayer of their religious community.

The intended meaning is that these two witnesses are to stand after a prayer at which people have gathered in their presence, ﴿and they will swear by Allah﴾, meaning they will take an oath by Allah, ﴿if you doubt﴾, meaning if suspicion about them appears to you, that they have betrayed or embezzled, ﴿then they will swear by Allah﴾ at that time, ﴿that we will not sell it﴾, meaning our oaths, as said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan, ﴿for any price﴾, meaning we will not exchange it for a small compensation of the perishable, transient worldly life, ﴿even if it were a near relative﴾, meaning even if the one testified against were close to us, we would not show favouritism toward him, ﴿nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah﴾. He attributed it to Allah to honour it and to magnify its matter.

Some read: "nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah (*ālLāh*)" in the genitive, as an oath. Ibn Jarir related it from 'Amir al-Sha'bi. It was also reported from some that they read: "nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah (*Allāhu*)," but the first reading is the well-known one.

﴿Indeed, we would then be among the sinful﴾, meaning if we did any of that, by distorting the testimony, altering it, changing it, or concealing it entirely.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿But if it becomes known that the two had incurred sin﴾, meaning if it becomes widely known, manifest, and established against the two witnesses who were executors that they betrayed or embezzled some of the property bequeathed to them, and this became evident against them, ﴿then two others will take their place from among those who have a rightful claim against them, the nearest of kin﴾. This is the reading of the majority: "*istuhiqqa* ('alayhimu al-awlayan)" (passive). It is related from 'Ali, Ubayy, and al-Hasan al-Basri that they read it: ﴿istahaqqa 'alayhimu al-awlayan﴾ (active).

Al-Hakim related in al-Mustadrak, through the route of Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Farawi, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that the Prophet ﷺ recited: ﴿from among those who have a rightful claim, the nearest of kin﴾, and then said: "Sound according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." (*al-Mustadrak* 2/237, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.)

Some read, among them Ibn 'Abbas: "from among those who have a rightful claim, the first ones" (*al-awwalin*). al-Hasan read: "from among those who have a rightful claim, the first two" (*al-awwalan*), as related by Ibn Jarir.

According to the reading of the majority, the meaning is: whenever it is established by a sound report that they betrayed, then two of the heirs who are entitled to the estate, and who are the most rightful of those who inherit that property, should stand, ﴿and they will swear by Allah: our testimony is more worthy than their testimony﴾, meaning, regarding our claim that they betrayed, our testimony is more worthy, more correct, and more firmly established than their earlier testimony. ﴿And we have not transgressed﴾, meaning in what we have said of betrayal. ﴿Indeed, we would then be among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning if we have lied about them.

This oath is for the heirs, and the reliance on their statement in such a situation is like the oath taken by the relatives of a murdered person when a *lawth* (indication of guilt) appears against the killer. The entitled ones swear against the killer, and he is handed over to them in full, as is established in the chapter on *al-Qasama* (the oath of fifty) in the rulings.

The Sunnah has also come with the same as what this noble verse indicates. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Abu al-Nadr, from Badhan, meaning Abu Salih, freed slave of Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Tamim al-Dari concerning this verse: ﴿O you who believe, the testimony between you when death approaches one of you﴾. He said: "People were absolved of it except for me and 'Adi ibn Bada'. They were both Christians, who travelled to Syria before Islam. They came to Syria for their trade, and there came to them a freed slave of the clan of Sahm, called Budayl ibn Abi Maryam, with merchandise, and with him was a silver cup, which he intended for the king, and it was the greatest of his trade. He fell ill, and he made them his executors and instructed them to deliver what he had left to his family." Tamim said: "When he died, we took that cup and sold it for a thousand dirhams, and then we divided it between myself and 'Adi ibn Bada'. When we returned to his family, we handed over to them what we had with us, but they missed the cup and asked us about it. We said: 'He left nothing but this, and nothing else was handed to us.'" Tamim said: "When I embraced Islam after the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, I felt guilty about that. So I went to his family, informed them of the matter, and paid them five hundred dirhams, and I told them that my companion had the same amount. They rushed at him to make him swear by what is held in high regard among their religious community. He swore, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, the testimony between you﴾ up to His words: ﴿they will swear by Allah: our testimony is more worthy than their testimony﴾. Then 'Amr ibn al-'As and another man from among them stood and swore, and the five hundred were taken from 'Adi ibn Bada'."

Thus it was also related by Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir, both from al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb al-Harrani, from Muhammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, with it, and he mentioned it [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3059), and Tafsir al-Tabari (11/186).]] - and in his version: they brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he asked them for evidence, but they found none, so he ordered them to have him swear by that which is held in greatest reverence among the people of his religion. He swore, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when death approaches one of you, let there be testimony between you﴾ up to His words: ﴿or fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths﴾. Then 'Amr ibn al-'As and another man stood up and swore, and the five hundred were taken from 'Adi ibn Bada'.

Then he said: This is a strange hadith, and its chain is not sound. Abu al-Nadr, from whom Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this hadith, is in my view Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, kunyah Abu al-Nadr, and the people of hadith have abandoned him, and he is the author of the Tafsir. I heard Muhammad ibn Isma'il say: Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, kunyah Abu al-Nadr. Then he said: And we do not know of a narration from Salim Abu al-Nadr from Abu Salih, the mawla of Umm Hani'. Something of this has been related from Ibn 'Abbas in summary, by a route other than this one.

Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Ibn Abi Za'idah, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man from the Banu Sahm went out with Tamim al-Dari and 'Adi ibn Bada'. The Sahmi died in a land where there was no Muslim. When they returned with his estate, they lacked a silver goblet inlaid with gold. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had them take an oath, and the goblet was found in Makkah. It was said: We bought it from Tamim and 'Adi. Then two men from the heirs of the Sahmi stood up and swore by Allah that our testimony is more worthy than theirs, and that the goblet belongs to our companion. Concerning them the verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you﴾.

Likewise Abu Dawud related it from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Yahya ibn Adam, with it. Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a fine, strange hadith, and it is the hadith of Ibn Abi Za'idah. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3606), and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3060); its origin is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2780), but al-Bukhari did not report it as a narration (tahdith) but as a report of a statement (hikayah).]]

Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim is Kufan. It is said that he is salih al-hadith (acceptable in narration). This story was related in mursal form (without a companion named) by more than one of the Tabi'un (Successors), among them 'Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Sirin, and Qatadah. They also mentioned that the oath-taking was after the 'Asr prayer; Ibn Jarir related it. Likewise Mujahid, al-Hasan, and al-Dahhak related it in mursal form. This indicates its fame among the early generations (al-salaf) and its authenticity.

Among the supporting evidences for the authenticity of this story is also what Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir related:

Ya'qub related to me: Hushaym related to us: Zakariyya informed us, from al-Sha'bi, that a man from the Muslims was near death at Daquqa. He said: Death came upon him, and he did not find any Muslim to witness his bequest, so he called two men from the People of the Book as witnesses. He said: They came to Kufa and went to al-Ash'ari - meaning Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him - and informed him, and presented his estate and his bequest. Al-Ash'ari said: This is a matter that did not occur after what occurred in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: He had them take an oath after the 'Asr prayer: By Allah, they did not betray, nor lie, nor change, nor conceal, nor alter, and indeed it is the bequest of the man and his estate. He said: So he upheld their testimony.

Then he related it from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Shu'bah, from Mughirah al-Azraq, from al-Sha'bi, that Abu Musa judged at Daquqa. [[In D: "with it".]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/165).]]

These are two sound chains to al-Sha'bi, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.

As for his saying: "This is a matter that did not occur after what occurred in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that he meant by it the story of Tamim and 'Adi ibn Bada'. They mentioned that the Islam of Tamim ibn Aws al-Dari, may Allah be pleased with him, was in the ninth year of the Hijrah. Accordingly this ruling is later, and whoever claims it was abrogated (naskh) needs a decisive proof in this matter, and Allah knows best.

Asbat related from al-Suddi concerning: ﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you when death approaches one of you, at the time of bequest, two just men from among you﴾. He said: This refers to the bequest at the time of death; he makes a bequest and calls two Muslim men as witnesses to what he has and what he owes. He said: This is in the case of residence (hadar), ﴿or two others from other than you﴾ in travel (safar), ﴿if you are traveling in the land and the affliction of death befalls you﴾: this is a man whom death overtakes during his journey, with no Muslim present. He calls two men from the Jews, Christians, or Magians, and makes a bequest to them, and hands over his inheritance to them, and they accept it. If the heirs of the deceased accept the bequest and recognize the property of their companion, they leave the two men alone; but if they doubt, they bring the two before the ruler (sultan). That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You detain them after the prayer, and they swear by Allah if you doubt﴾. Abdullah ibn 'Abbas said: It is as if I look at the two non-Arabs when they were brought to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari at his house. He opened the document, and the heirs of the deceased denied it and accused them of betrayal. Abu Musa wanted to have them swear after the 'Asr prayer. I said to him: They do not care about the 'Asr prayer, but have them swear after their own prayer in their religion. So the two men are made to stand after their prayer in their religion, and they swear: By Allah, we will not sell it for a small price, even if it were a relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed we would then be among the sinners; that their companion did indeed make this bequest, and that this is indeed his estate. The ruler then says to them before they swear: If you conceal or betray, I will expose you before your people, your testimony will not be admitted, and I will punish you. When he says that to them, that is closer to their giving the testimony in its proper form. Ibn Jarir related it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/175).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn related to us: Hushaym related to us: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that they both said concerning this verse: ﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you﴾ to the end of the verse: When death approaches a man during a journey, let him call two Muslim men as witnesses. If he does not find two Muslim men, then two men from the People of the Book. When they come with his estate, if the heirs confirm them, their word is accepted; but if they accuse them, they are made to swear after the 'Asr prayer: By Allah, we did not conceal, nor lie, nor betray, nor alter.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the interpretation of this verse: If doubt is cast on their testimony, the two swear after the prayer by Allah: "We did not buy with our testimony a small price." If the guardians (awliya') discover that the two disbelievers lied in their testimony, two men from the guardians stand and swear by Allah that the testimony of the two disbelievers is void, and that we did not transgress. That is His saying: ﴿But if it is discovered that the two had incurred sin﴾, meaning: if it is discovered that the two disbelievers lied; ﴿then two others shall stand in their place﴾, meaning: from the guardians, and they swear by Allah that the testimony of the disbelievers is void and that we did not transgress; so the testimony of the two disbelievers is rejected, and the testimony of the guardians is accepted.

Al-'Awfi related the same from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Jarir related both.

Likewise this ruling in accordance with the requirement of this verse was upheld by more than one of the leading Successors and the early generation (al-salaf), may Allah be pleased with them, and it is the school (madhhab) of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is closer to their giving the testimony in its proper form﴾ means: the legislation of this ruling in this acceptable manner, by making the two dhimmi witnesses swear when they are suspected, is closer to their establishing the testimony in its acceptable form.

* *

His saying: ﴿or fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths﴾ means: what moves them to give the testimony in its proper form is the glorification of the oath by Allah, observing His right and reverence for Him, and fear of disgrace among the people if the oath is returned to the heirs, so they swear and claim what they seek. For this reason He said: ﴿or fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths﴾.

Then He said: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, meaning: in all your affairs, ﴿and listen﴾, meaning: and obey. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾, meaning: those who depart from His obedience and from following His law.

This is a report about what Allah will address to the messengers on the Day of Resurrection, concerning the answer they were given by their peoples to whom He sent them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Surely We will question those to whom messengers were sent, and surely We will question the messengers﴾ [al-A'raf: 6], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾ [al-Hijr: 92-93].

As for the words of the messengers: ﴿We have no knowledge﴾, Mujahid, al-Hasan al-Basri, and al-Suddi said: they only said that out of the terror of that Day.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from al-Thawri, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid: ﴿The Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?"﴾ They will be seized with fear and say: ﴿We have no knowledge﴾. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Hakkam narrated to us, 'Anbasa narrated to us, saying: I heard a shaykh say: I heard al-Hasan say concerning His words: ﴿The Day when Allah will gather the messengers﴾ [to the end of the verse], he said: "out of the terror of that Day."

Asbat said, from al-Suddi: ﴿The Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?" They will say, "We have no knowledge"﴾ — that is: they will be brought to a station where minds are bewildered, and when they are asked, they will say: ﴿We have no knowledge﴾. Then they will be brought to another station, and they will bear witness against their peoples. Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Then Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning his words: ﴿The Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?"﴾ — "What did they do after you? And what did they innovate after you?" They will say: ﴿We have no knowledge. Surely You, You are the Knower of the unseen﴾.

'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿The Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Surely You, You are the Knower of the unseen"﴾ — they say to the Lord, mighty and majestic is He: "We have no knowledge, except the knowledge You know better than us."

Ibn Jarir narrated it. Then he preferred it over these three statements. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/211).]] There is no doubt that it is a good statement, and it is part of the etiquette with the Lord, mighty and majestic is He, i.e.: we have no knowledge in comparison to Your all-encompassing knowledge of everything. Although we responded and knew who responded to us, among them are some whose outward condition alone we perceived, and we have no knowledge of their inner state. You are the All-Knowing of everything, the One who is aware of everything. So our knowledge in comparison to Your knowledge is as if it were no knowledge at all, for You are ﴿the Knower of the unseen﴾.

The commentary of Ibn Kathir on Surah al-Ma'idah, verses 110–111:

God, may He be exalted, mentions what He bestowed upon His servant and messenger, Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, of the miracles and extraordinary signs He caused to occur through him. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿When God said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favour upon you"﴾. That is, [remember it] in My creating you from a mother without a father, and My making you a sign and a decisive proof of the completeness of My power over things. ﴿And upon your mother﴾, in that I made you a proof for her of her innocence from the indecency that the wrongdoing, ignorant people attributed to her. ﴿When I supported you with the Holy Spirit﴾, which is Gabriel, peace be upon him, and I made you a prophet calling to God in your youth and in your old age. I made you speak in the cradle as a child, so you testified to your mother's innocence from every blemish, acknowledged My lordship by servitude to Me, and informed [people] of My sending you and your call to worship Me. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿You speak to people in the cradle and in maturity﴾. That is, you call people to God in your youth and in your old age. The meaning of "speak" includes "call," because his speaking to people in his maturity is not a strange matter.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when I taught you the Book and wisdom﴾, that is, writing and understanding, ﴿and the Torah﴾, which was revealed to Moses son of Imran, the one who spoke with God. The word "Torah" may occur in a hadith and be intended in a broader sense than that.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when you shaped from clay the likeness of a bird by My permission﴾, that is, you fashion it and form it into the shape of a bird by My permission to you in that, so it becomes a bird by My permission. That is, you breathe into that figure which you shaped by My permission to you in that, so it becomes a living bird by the permission and creation of God.

* *

His saying: ﴿And you heal the blind and the leper by My permission﴾. The discussion of this has already preceded in Surat Al 'Imran, enough to make its repetition unnecessary.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when you bring forth the dead by My permission﴾, that is, you call them and they rise from their graves by the permission of God, His power, His will and His determination.

It has been said by Ibn Abi Hatim: My father narrated to us, Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Talhah, meaning Ibn Musarrif, narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Abu al-Hudhayl, who said: When Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, wished to revive the dead, he would pray two rak'ahs, reciting in the first: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion﴾ [Surat al-Mulk], and in the second: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The revelation of the Book﴾ [Surat as-Sajdah]. When he finished them, he praised God and extolled Him, then he called upon seven names: "O Eternal, O Hidden, O Everlasting, O Single, O Odd, O One, O Self-Sufficient." And when hardship befell him, he called upon seven others: "O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O God, O Most Merciful, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour, O Light of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and Lord of the Mighty Throne, O Lord."

This is a very strange report. [[It is among the reports from the Children of Israel for which no supporting evidence has been transmitted, and its invalidity is the more likely.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs, and those of them who disbelieved said, "This is nothing but manifest magic"﴾. That is, remember My favour upon you in My restraining them from you when you came to them with the evidences and decisive arguments for your prophethood and your messengership from God to them. They denied you, accused you of being a sorcerer, and strove to kill you and crucify you. So I saved you from them, raised you up to Me, purified you from their filth, and sufficed you against their evil. This indicates that this favour was from God to him after his being raised to the lowest heaven, or that this favour will occur on the Day of Resurrection, and it was expressed in the past tense to show that it will certainly take place. This is among the hidden matters which God revealed to His messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

His saying: ﴿And when I inspired the disciples: "Believe in Me and in My messenger"﴾. This too is one of the favours upon him, peace be upon him, in that He made for him companions and helpers. It has been said that the intended meaning of this revelation is inspiration (wahy al-ilham), as He said: ﴿And We inspired the mother of Moses: "Suckle him"﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-Qasas: 7]. This is inspiration without fear. And as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee: "Take for yourself houses in the mountains and in the trees and in what they build. Then eat from all the fruits and follow the ways of your Lord, made easy"﴾ up to the end of the verse [An-Nahl: 68–69]. Similarly, some of the early Muslims said regarding this verse: ﴿And when I inspired the disciples: "Believe in Me and in My messenger," they said: "We believe; and bear witness that we are Muslims"﴾ [that is, in God and in the messenger of God]. ﴿Bear witness that we are Muslims﴾, that is, they were inspired to that and complied with what they were inspired to.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: God, mighty and majestic, inspired them with that. As-Suddi said: He cast that into their hearts.

It is also possible that the intended meaning is: "And when I revealed to them through you, so you called them to belief in God and His messenger, and they responded to you, submitted and followed you, and they said: 'We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims.'"

This is the story of the Table (al-Ma'idah), and the surah is named after it, so it is called "Surat al-Ma'idah." It is one of the blessings God bestowed on His servant and messenger Isa (Jesus), upon him be peace, when He answered his supplication by sending it down. God sent it down as a sign, a manifest miraculous proof, and a decisive argument.

Some of the imams have mentioned that the story of the Table is not mentioned in the Gospel, and that the Christians know of it only from the Muslims. God knows best.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When the disciples said﴾, and they are the followers of Isa, upon him be peace: ﴿O Isa, son of Maryam, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?﴾ This is the reading of most reciters. Others read: "Can you ask your Lord (hal tastati'u rabbaka)," meaning: can you ask your Lord ﴿to send down to us a table from heaven﴾.

The ma'idah (table) is the tray (khiwan) on which there is food. Some have mentioned that they asked for this because of their need and poverty, so they asked that a table be sent down to them each day from which they could eat and by which they could strengthen themselves for worship.

He said: ﴿Fear God, if you are believers﴾. That is, Isa, upon him be peace, answered them, telling them: "Fear God, and do not ask for this, for it may be a trial for you. And put your trust in God in seeking provision, if you are believers."

﴿They said: We wish to eat from it﴾, that is, we are in need of eating from it; ﴿and that our hearts may be reassured﴾ when we witness its descent as provision for us from heaven; ﴿and that we may know that you have spoken truly to us﴾, that is, and that our faith in you and our knowledge of your prophethood may increase; ﴿and that we may be among its witnesses﴾, that is, and that we may testify that it is a sign from God, and a proof and argument for your prophethood and the truth of what you have brought.

﴿Isa, son of Maryam, said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, which will be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us﴾. Al-Suddi said: that is, we will take that day on which it descends as a festival, which we and those after us will honour. Sufyan al-Thawri said: meaning a day on which we pray. Qatadah said: they wished that it would be for their descendants after them. From Salman al-Farisi: a lesson for us and for those after us. It was also said: a sufficiency for the first of us and the last of us.

﴿And a sign from You﴾, that is, a proof that You establish of Your power over things and of Your answering my supplication, so that they will believe me in what I convey from You. ﴿And provide for us﴾, that is, from Your presence, provision that is wholesome, without hardship or toil. ﴿And You are the best of providers.﴾

﴿God said: Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you﴾, that is, whoever among your community, O Isa, denies it and opposes it, ﴿I will surely punish him with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds﴾, that is, among the worlds of your time. This is like His saying: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established: Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 46] [[In (D) and (H): "the Day of Resurrection," which is an error.]], and like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire﴾ [An-Nisa: 145].

Ibn Jarir narrated, by way of 'Awf al-A'rabi, from Abu al-Mughirah al-Qawwas, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: "Indeed, the most severely punished people on the Day of Resurrection are three: the hypocrites, those among the people of the Table who disbelieved, and the family of Pharaoh." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/233).]]

Mention of reports transmitted from the early generations (al-salaf) concerning the descent of the Table upon the disciples:

Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Layth, from Uqayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to relate concerning Isa ibn Maryam that he said to the Children of Israel: "Would you be willing to fast for God thirty days, and then ask Him, and He will give you what you ask? For the reward of the worker is due from the one for whom he works." So they did so. Then they said: "O teacher of goodness, you told us that the reward of the worker is due from the one for whom he works, and you commanded us to fast thirty days, so we did. We never worked for anyone for thirty days without him feeding us, when we finished, a meal. So can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" Isa said: ﴿Fear God, if you are believers. They said: We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured, and that we may know that you have spoken truly to us, and that we may be among its witnesses. Isa, son of Maryam, said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, which will be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You; and provide for us, and You are the best of providers. God said: Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you, I will surely punish him with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds﴾. He said: Then the angels came flying with a table from heaven, upon which were seven fish and seven loaves, until they placed it before them. The last of the people ate from it just as the first of them did.

Thus Ibn Jarir narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, from Layth, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ibn 'Abbas used to narrate, and he mentioned something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to us, Abu Zur'a Wahb Allah ibn Rashid narrated to us, Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to us, that Ibn Shihab informed him, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the disciples said to Isa ibn Maryam: "Ask God to send down to us a table from heaven." He said: So the angels descended with a table they carried, upon which were seven fish and seven loaves, and the last of the people ate from it just as the first of them did.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah al-Bahili narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Habib narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar ibn Yasir, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The table descended from heaven, upon it were bread and meat, and they were commanded not to betray, and not to keep any of it for the next day. But they betrayed, stored, and kept some, so they were transformed into apes and swine."

Likewise Ibn Jarir narrated it, from al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/228). Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan, no. (3061), and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hadith which Abu 'Asim and more than one narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar ibn Yasir, as a mawquf (stopping at the companion). We do not know it as marfu' (traced to the Prophet) except from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, who narrated from Hamid ibn Mas'adah, from Sufyan ibn Habib, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, similarly, but without raising it. This is more correct than the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, and we know of no basis for the marfu' hadith."]]. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ibn Bashshar, from Ibn Abi 'Adi, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar, who said: "The table descended, and upon it was fruit from the fruits of Paradise. They were commanded not to betray, not to hide, and not to store. So the people betrayed, hid, and stored, and God transformed them into apes and swine." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/229).]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from a man from the Banu 'Ijl, who said: "I prayed beside Ammar ibn Yasir, and when he finished he said: 'Do you know how the matter of the table of the Children of Israel was?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'They asked Isa ibn Maryam for a table upon which there would be food they could eat from that would never run out.' He said: 'It was said to them: Indeed, it will remain for you as long as you do not hoard it, betray it, or lift it up. If you do, I will surely punish you with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds.' He said: 'Their day had not passed before they hoarded, lifted, and betrayed, so they were punished with a punishment that no one among the worlds had been punished with.' And you, O assembly of the Arabs, used to follow the tails of camels and sheep, then God sent among you a messenger from yourselves, whose lineage and descent you know. He informed you that you would prevail over the non-Arabs, and forbade you to hoard gold and silver. By God, night and day will not pass until you hoard them, and God will punish you with a painful punishment." [[In (D): "they said." In (D): "you hoard them" written as "تكفروهما" (you disbelieve them). Tafsir al-Tabari (11/228).]]

He also said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah, that the table descended upon Isa ibn Maryam, upon it were seven loaves and seven fish, and they ate from it whatever they wished. He said: Some of them stole from it and said: "Perhaps it will not descend tomorrow." So it was lifted up.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: It descended upon Isa ibn Maryam and the disciples, a tray upon which was bread and fish, and they ate from it wherever they alighted, whenever they wished. Khasif said, from Ikrimah and Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas: The table was a fish and loaves. Mujahid said: It was food that descended upon them wherever they alighted. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami said: The table descended as bread and fish. Atiyyah al-Awfi said: The table was fish containing the taste of everything.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He sent it down from heaven upon the Children of Israel, and each day from that table there would descend fruit from Paradise, and they ate whatever they wished of various kinds. Four thousand would sit around it, and when they had eaten, God would replace it with the like of it for others. They remained in this state as long as God willed.

Wahb ibn Munabbih also said: He sent down upon them a loaf of barley and fish, and God placed blessing within their folds, so a group would eat and then leave, then another would come and eat and leave, until all of them had eaten and there was surplus.

Al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, said: Everything descended upon it except meat.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan and Maysarah, and Jarir, from Ata, from Maysarah: When the table was set before the Children of Israel, hands would reach for every kind of food upon it except meat.

From Ikrimah: The bread of the table was made of rice. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn Ali informed us, in what he wrote to me: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, my uncle Abu Abd Allah Abd al-Quddus ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Mirdas al-Abdari, client of the Banu Abd al-Dar, narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman al-Khayr, that he said: When the disciples asked Isa ibn Maryam for the table, he disliked that greatly and said: "Be content with what God has provided you on the earth, and do not ask for a table from heaven. For if it descends upon you, it will be a sign from your Lord. Thamud were only destroyed when they asked their prophet for a sign, and they were tested with it until their ruin came through it. Yet they refused unless he brought it to them." Therefore they said: ﴿We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured﴾, to the end of the verse.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 112–115 (part 2 of 3):

When Jesus saw that they had refused except to ask him to pray for them with it, he stood up, cast off the wool, and put on black hair-cloth, a jubba of hair, and an 'aba' (cloak) of hair. Then he performed wudu' and ghusl, entered his place of prayer, and prayed as much as Allah willed. When he had finished his prayer, he stood upright, facing the qiblah, and set his feet together until they were level, joining the heel to the heel and aligning the toes. He placed his right hand upon his left, above his chest, lowered his gaze, and bowed his head in humility. Then he let his eyes weep, and his tears kept flowing down his cheeks and dripping from the edges of his beard, until the ground in front of his face was wet from his humility. When he saw that, he called upon Allah, saying: ﴿O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven﴾. So Allah sent down upon them a red spread (sufrah) between two clouds: a cloud above it and a cloud beneath it, while they watched it in the air, descending swiftly from the firmament of the sky, coming down toward them. Jesus was weeping out of fear of the conditions that Allah had imposed upon them concerning it, namely that He would punish whoever among them disbelieved after its descent with a punishment He had not inflicted upon anyone among the worlds. He was calling upon Allah from his place and saying: "O Allah, make it a mercy, O my God, do not make it a punishment. O my God, how many a wondrous thing have I asked You for and You have given it to me. O my God, make us grateful to You. O my God, I seek refuge in You from that You should send it down in anger and as a retribution. O my God, make it a safety and a well-being, and do not make it a trial and a mutilation."

He continued to supplicate until the spread settled before Jesus, while the disciples and his companions were around him, smelling a fragrant scent such as they had never smelled before. Jesus and the disciples fell down in prostration to Allah, thanking Him for providing for them from where they had not reckoned, and He showed them in it a great sign, full of wonder and lesson. The Jews came and looked, and they saw a wondrous matter that caused them grief and distress; then they departed in intense rage. Jesus and the disciples and his companions came and sat around the spread, and upon it was a covering cloth. Jesus said: "Who among us is the boldest in uncovering the cloth from this spread, the most trusting of himself, and the best in trial before his Lord? Let him uncover this sign so that we may see it, praise our Lord, mention His name, and eat from His provision which He has given us." The disciples said: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, you are the first of us to do that, and the most worthy of uncovering it." Jesus, peace be upon him, stood, renewed his wudu', then entered his place of prayer and prayed similarly for some rak'ahs, then wept a long weeping and called upon Allah to permit him to uncover it, and to make for him and his people in it blessing and provision. Then he turned and sat by the spread, took the cloth, and said: "In the name of Allah, the best of providers," and he uncovered the spread, and there upon it was a large roasted fish, without scales, with no bones in its interior, from which the fat flowed in a stream, and around it were arranged herbs of every kind except leeks, and at its head was vinegar, and at its tail was salt, and around the herbs were five loaves of bread, on one of which was olives, on another dates, and on another five pomegranates.

Shim'un, the head of the disciples, said to Jesus: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, is this food of the world or food of Paradise?" He said: "Has the time not come for you to take heed from the signs you see, and to desist from probing questions? How I fear for you that you will be punished concerning the cause of the revelation of this verse!" Shim'un said: "By the God of Israel, I did not intend by it a question, O son of the truthful woman." Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "None of what you see is from the food of Paradise or from the food of the world. It is something that Allah brought into being in the air by His lofty, overpowering and subduing power, and He said to it: 'Be!' and it was, quicker than the blink of an eye. So eat of what you have asked for, in the name of Allah, and praise Him for it, your Lord will give you more from it and increase you, for He is Originator, Capable, and Grateful."

They said: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, we want you to show us a sign in this sign." Jesus said: "Glory be to Allah! Are you not content with what you have seen in this sign, that you ask for yet another sign?" Then Jesus, peace be upon him, turned to the fish and said: "O fish, return by the permission of Allah alive as you were." So Allah gave it life by His power, and it convulsed and returned, by the permission of Allah, alive and fresh, licking its lips as a lion licks, its eyes turning with a glitter, and its scales returned to it. The people were terrified of it and drew back. When Jesus saw that from them, he said: "What is the matter with you that you ask for a sign, and when your Lord shows it to you, you dislike it? How I fear for you that you will be punished for what you are doing! O fish, return by the permission of Allah as you were." So it returned, by the permission of Allah, roasted as it had been in its first creation.

They said to Jesus: "You, O Spirit of Allah, begin by eating from it, and then we will follow." Jesus said: "God forbid from that! Let the one who sought it begin eating." When the disciples and their companions saw their prophet's refusal of it, they feared that its descent was a wrath and that eating it would be a mutilation, so they shunned it. When Jesus saw that, he called the poor and the chronically ill to it and said: "Eat of the provision of your Lord and the supplication of your prophet, and praise Allah who sent it down to you, so that its wholesome benefit will be yours and its punishment will be upon others. Begin your eating with the name of Allah and end it with the praise of Allah." They did so, and there ate from it one thousand and three hundred people, men and women, each of them departing satisfied and belching. Jesus and the disciples looked, and the spread was in the same state as when it had been sent down from heaven; nothing had been diminished from it. Then it was raised to heaven while they watched. Every poor person who ate from it became rich, and every chronically ill person who ate from it was healed, and they remained wealthy and healthy until they left the world.

The disciples and their companions who had refused to eat from it regretted with great remorse; their eyelids flowed with tears from it, and the sorrow of it remained in their hearts until the day of death. He said: So whenever the table came down after that, the Children of Israel came to it from every place, running, pushing one another: the rich and the poor, the young and the old, the healthy and the sick, some of them mounting upon others. When he saw that, he made it intermittent: it would descend one day and not descend the next. They remained in that state for forty days, descending upon them every other day at the height of the forenoon, and it would not cease to be set down, and they would eat from it, until when they rose, it was lifted from them by Allah's permission toward the atmosphere of the sky, while they watched its shadow on the earth until it vanished from them.

He said: Then Allah revealed to His prophet Jesus, peace be upon him, that he should make My provision the table for the orphans, the poor and the chronically ill, and not for the rich among the people. When he did that, the rich among the people doubted it and despised that, until they doubted it in themselves and cast doubt on it among the people, and they spread ugly and objectionable talk about the matter. Satan obtained his aim from them and cast his whisperings into the hearts of the doubters, until they said to Jesus: "Inform us about the table and its descent from heaven: is it true, for many of our people have doubted it?" Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "You are ruined, by the God of the Messiah! You asked your prophet to ask your Lord for the table, and when He did so and sent it down to you as mercy and provision, and showed you in it signs and lessons, you denied it and doubted it. So rejoice in the punishment, for it is descending upon you unless Allah has mercy upon you."

Allah revealed to Jesus: "I will seize the deniers according to My condition: I will punish among them whoever disbelieved in the table after its descent with a punishment I have not inflicted upon anyone among the worlds." He said: When the doubters about it reached the evening and lay down on their beds in the finest form with their women, secure, then when it was the last part of the night, Allah transformed them into pigs, and in the morning they were pursuing filth in the rubbish heaps.

This is a very strange report. Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Nawadir al-Usul, as cited in the tafsir of al-Qurtubi (6/369), through Zakariyya ibn Hakim, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, with something similar; and al-Qurtubi said: "There is discussion regarding this hadith, and it is not authentic in terms of its chain." Ibn Abi Hatim cut it into pieces in various places of this story, and I have gathered it for him so that its wording is more complete and perfect. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

All these reports indicate that the table was sent down upon the Children of Israel in the days of Jesus son of Mary, as an answer from Allah to his supplication, and as the apparent context of the Noble Qur'an indicates: ﴿Allah said: I am sending it down upon you﴾, the verse.

Some have said that it was never sent down. Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿Send down to us a table from heaven﴾, that he said: "It is a parable that was struck, and nothing descended." This was related by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. Then Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith narrated to me, al-Qasim (that is Ibn Sallam) narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "A table upon which there was food, which they requested when the punishment was presented to them, should they disbelieve; but they refused, so it did not descend upon them."

He also said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan, that he said concerning the table: "It did not descend."

And Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: "al-Hasan used to say: When it was said to them: ﴿Whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds﴾, they said: 'We have no need for it,' so it did not descend."

These are sound chains to Mujahid and al-Hasan. This may be strengthened by the fact that the Christians do not know the report of the table, and it is not in their scripture; had it descended, the motives to transmit it would have been strong, and it would have been present in their scripture as a widely transmitted report, or at least as an individual report. And Allah knows best. However, the majority hold that it did descend, and this is what Ibn Jarir preferred, saying: "Because He, exalted is He, informed of its descent by His saying: ﴿I am sending it down upon you; whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds﴾." He said: "And Allah's promise and threat are true and sincere."

This view, God knows best, is the correct one, as the reports and narrations from the early generations (al-salaf) and others indicate.

The historians mention that Musa ibn Nusayr, the deputy of the Banu Umayyah in the conquest of the lands of the Maghrib, found the table there adorned with pearls and various kinds of jewels. He sent it to the Commander of the Faithful, al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik, the builder of the Mosque of Damascus, but he died while it was on the way. It was then carried to his brother Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who succeeded him as caliph. People saw it and were greatly amazed at it, because of the precious rubies and the unique jewels in it. It is said that this table belonged to Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both. God knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Imran ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Ask your Lord to turn al-Safa into gold for us, and we will believe in you." He said: "Will you really do that?" They said: "Yes." He said: So he supplicated, and Jibril came to him and said: "Your Lord sends you His greetings and says to you: If you wish, al-Safa will become gold for them, but whoever among them disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment that I will not inflict on anyone among the worlds. And if you wish, I will open for them the door of repentance and mercy." He said: "Rather, the door of repentance and mercy."

Then Ahmad, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with this chain.

[[Al-Musnad (1/242) and al-Mustadrak (1/53). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/152) through the route of Sufyan with this chain, and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/196): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

This is the story of the Table (al-Ma'idah), and the surah is named after it, so it is called "Surat al-Ma'idah." It is one of the blessings God bestowed on His servant and messenger Isa (Jesus), upon him be peace, when He answered his supplication by sending it down. God sent it down as a sign, a manifest miraculous proof, and a decisive argument.

Some of the imams have mentioned that the story of the Table is not mentioned in the Gospel, and that the Christians know of it only from the Muslims. God knows best.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When the disciples said﴾, and they are the followers of Isa, upon him be peace: ﴿O Isa, son of Maryam, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?﴾ This is the reading of most reciters. Others read: "Can you ask your Lord (hal tastati'u rabbaka)," meaning: can you ask your Lord ﴿to send down to us a table from heaven﴾.

The ma'idah (table) is the tray (khiwan) on which there is food. Some have mentioned that they asked for this because of their need and poverty, so they asked that a table be sent down to them each day from which they could eat and by which they could strengthen themselves for worship.

He said: ﴿Fear God, if you are believers﴾. That is, Isa, upon him be peace, answered them, telling them: "Fear God, and do not ask for this, for it may be a trial for you. And put your trust in God in seeking provision, if you are believers."

﴿They said: We wish to eat from it﴾, that is, we are in need of eating from it; ﴿and that our hearts may be reassured﴾ when we witness its descent as provision for us from heaven; ﴿and that we may know that you have spoken truly to us﴾, that is, and that our faith in you and our knowledge of your prophethood may increase; ﴿and that we may be among its witnesses﴾, that is, and that we may testify that it is a sign from God, and a proof and argument for your prophethood and the truth of what you have brought.

﴿Isa, son of Maryam, said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, which will be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us﴾. Al-Suddi said: that is, we will take that day on which it descends as a festival, which we and those after us will honour. Sufyan al-Thawri said: meaning a day on which we pray. Qatadah said: they wished that it would be for their descendants after them. From Salman al-Farisi: a lesson for us and for those after us. It was also said: a sufficiency for the first of us and the last of us.

﴿And a sign from You﴾, that is, a proof that You establish of Your power over things and of Your answering my supplication, so that they will believe me in what I convey from You. ﴿And provide for us﴾, that is, from Your presence, provision that is wholesome, without hardship or toil. ﴿And You are the best of providers.﴾

﴿God said: Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you﴾, that is, whoever among your community, O Isa, denies it and opposes it, ﴿I will surely punish him with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds﴾, that is, among the worlds of your time. This is like His saying: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established: Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 46] [[In (D) and (H): "the Day of Resurrection," which is an error.]], and like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire﴾ [An-Nisa: 145].

Ibn Jarir narrated, by way of 'Awf al-A'rabi, from Abu al-Mughirah al-Qawwas, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: "Indeed, the most severely punished people on the Day of Resurrection are three: the hypocrites, those among the people of the Table who disbelieved, and the family of Pharaoh." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/233).]]

Mention of reports transmitted from the early generations (al-salaf) concerning the descent of the Table upon the disciples:

Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Layth, from Uqayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to relate concerning Isa ibn Maryam that he said to the Children of Israel: "Would you be willing to fast for God thirty days, and then ask Him, and He will give you what you ask? For the reward of the worker is due from the one for whom he works." So they did so. Then they said: "O teacher of goodness, you told us that the reward of the worker is due from the one for whom he works, and you commanded us to fast thirty days, so we did. We never worked for anyone for thirty days without him feeding us, when we finished, a meal. So can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" Isa said: ﴿Fear God, if you are believers. They said: We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured, and that we may know that you have spoken truly to us, and that we may be among its witnesses. Isa, son of Maryam, said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, which will be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You; and provide for us, and You are the best of providers. God said: Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you, I will surely punish him with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds﴾. He said: Then the angels came flying with a table from heaven, upon which were seven fish and seven loaves, until they placed it before them. The last of the people ate from it just as the first of them did.

Thus Ibn Jarir narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, from Layth, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ibn 'Abbas used to narrate, and he mentioned something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to us, Abu Zur'a Wahb Allah ibn Rashid narrated to us, Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to us, that Ibn Shihab informed him, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the disciples said to Isa ibn Maryam: "Ask God to send down to us a table from heaven." He said: So the angels descended with a table they carried, upon which were seven fish and seven loaves, and the last of the people ate from it just as the first of them did.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah al-Bahili narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Habib narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar ibn Yasir, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The table descended from heaven, upon it were bread and meat, and they were commanded not to betray, and not to keep any of it for the next day. But they betrayed, stored, and kept some, so they were transformed into apes and swine."

Likewise Ibn Jarir narrated it, from al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/228). Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan, no. (3061), and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hadith which Abu 'Asim and more than one narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar ibn Yasir, as a mawquf (stopping at the companion). We do not know it as marfu' (traced to the Prophet) except from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, who narrated from Hamid ibn Mas'adah, from Sufyan ibn Habib, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, similarly, but without raising it. This is more correct than the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, and we know of no basis for the marfu' hadith."]]. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ibn Bashshar, from Ibn Abi 'Adi, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar, who said: "The table descended, and upon it was fruit from the fruits of Paradise. They were commanded not to betray, not to hide, and not to store. So the people betrayed, hid, and stored, and God transformed them into apes and swine." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/229).]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from a man from the Banu 'Ijl, who said: "I prayed beside Ammar ibn Yasir, and when he finished he said: 'Do you know how the matter of the table of the Children of Israel was?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'They asked Isa ibn Maryam for a table upon which there would be food they could eat from that would never run out.' He said: 'It was said to them: Indeed, it will remain for you as long as you do not hoard it, betray it, or lift it up. If you do, I will surely punish you with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds.'
