He said: 'Their day had not passed before they hoarded, lifted, and betrayed, so they were punished with a punishment that no one among the worlds had been punished with.' And you, O assembly of the Arabs, used to follow the tails of camels and sheep, then God sent among you a messenger from yourselves, whose lineage and descent you know. He informed you that you would prevail over the non-Arabs, and forbade you to hoard gold and silver. By God, night and day will not pass until you hoard them, and God will punish you with a painful punishment." [[In (D): "they said." In (D): "you hoard them" written as "تكفروهما" (you disbelieve them). Tafsir al-Tabari (11/228).]]

He also said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah, that the table descended upon Isa ibn Maryam, upon it were seven loaves and seven fish, and they ate from it whatever they wished. He said: Some of them stole from it and said: "Perhaps it will not descend tomorrow." So it was lifted up.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: It descended upon Isa ibn Maryam and the disciples, a tray upon which was bread and fish, and they ate from it wherever they alighted, whenever they wished. Khasif said, from Ikrimah and Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas: The table was a fish and loaves. Mujahid said: It was food that descended upon them wherever they alighted. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami said: The table descended as bread and fish. Atiyyah al-Awfi said: The table was fish containing the taste of everything.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He sent it down from heaven upon the Children of Israel, and each day from that table there would descend fruit from Paradise, and they ate whatever they wished of various kinds. Four thousand would sit around it, and when they had eaten, God would replace it with the like of it for others. They remained in this state as long as God willed.

Wahb ibn Munabbih also said: He sent down upon them a loaf of barley and fish, and God placed blessing within their folds, so a group would eat and then leave, then another would come and eat and leave, until all of them had eaten and there was surplus.

Al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, said: Everything descended upon it except meat.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan and Maysarah, and Jarir, from Ata, from Maysarah: When the table was set before the Children of Israel, hands would reach for every kind of food upon it except meat.

From Ikrimah: The bread of the table was made of rice. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn Ali informed us, in what he wrote to me: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, my uncle Abu Abd Allah Abd al-Quddus ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Mirdas al-Abdari, client of the Banu Abd al-Dar, narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman al-Khayr, that he said: When the disciples asked Isa ibn Maryam for the table, he disliked that greatly and said: "Be content with what God has provided you on the earth, and do not ask for a table from heaven. For if it descends upon you, it will be a sign from your Lord. Thamud were only destroyed when they asked their prophet for a sign, and they were tested with it until their ruin came through it. Yet they refused unless he brought it to them." Therefore they said: ﴿We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured﴾, to the end of the verse.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 112–115 (part 2 of 3):

When Jesus saw that they had refused except to ask him to pray for them with it, he stood up, cast off the wool, and put on black hair-cloth, a jubba of hair, and an 'aba' (cloak) of hair. Then he performed wudu' and ghusl, entered his place of prayer, and prayed as much as Allah willed. When he had finished his prayer, he stood upright, facing the qiblah, and set his feet together until they were level, joining the heel to the heel and aligning the toes. He placed his right hand upon his left, above his chest, lowered his gaze, and bowed his head in humility. Then he let his eyes weep, and his tears kept flowing down his cheeks and dripping from the edges of his beard, until the ground in front of his face was wet from his humility. When he saw that, he called upon Allah, saying: ﴿O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven﴾. So Allah sent down upon them a red spread (sufrah) between two clouds: a cloud above it and a cloud beneath it, while they watched it in the air, descending swiftly from the firmament of the sky, coming down toward them. Jesus was weeping out of fear of the conditions that Allah had imposed upon them concerning it, namely that He would punish whoever among them disbelieved after its descent with a punishment He had not inflicted upon anyone among the worlds. He was calling upon Allah from his place and saying: "O Allah, make it a mercy, O my God, do not make it a punishment. O my God, how many a wondrous thing have I asked You for and You have given it to me. O my God, make us grateful to You. O my God, I seek refuge in You from that You should send it down in anger and as a retribution. O my God, make it a safety and a well-being, and do not make it a trial and a mutilation."

He continued to supplicate until the spread settled before Jesus, while the disciples and his companions were around him, smelling a fragrant scent such as they had never smelled before. Jesus and the disciples fell down in prostration to Allah, thanking Him for providing for them from where they had not reckoned, and He showed them in it a great sign, full of wonder and lesson. The Jews came and looked, and they saw a wondrous matter that caused them grief and distress; then they departed in intense rage. Jesus and the disciples and his companions came and sat around the spread, and upon it was a covering cloth. Jesus said: "Who among us is the boldest in uncovering the cloth from this spread, the most trusting of himself, and the best in trial before his Lord? Let him uncover this sign so that we may see it, praise our Lord, mention His name, and eat from His provision which He has given us." The disciples said: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, you are the first of us to do that, and the most worthy of uncovering it." Jesus, peace be upon him, stood, renewed his wudu', then entered his place of prayer and prayed similarly for some rak'ahs, then wept a long weeping and called upon Allah to permit him to uncover it, and to make for him and his people in it blessing and provision. Then he turned and sat by the spread, took the cloth, and said: "In the name of Allah, the best of providers," and he uncovered the spread, and there upon it was a large roasted fish, without scales, with no bones in its interior, from which the fat flowed in a stream, and around it were arranged herbs of every kind except leeks, and at its head was vinegar, and at its tail was salt, and around the herbs were five loaves of bread, on one of which was olives, on another dates, and on another five pomegranates.

Shim'un, the head of the disciples, said to Jesus: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, is this food of the world or food of Paradise?" He said: "Has the time not come for you to take heed from the signs you see, and to desist from probing questions? How I fear for you that you will be punished concerning the cause of the revelation of this verse!" Shim'un said: "By the God of Israel, I did not intend by it a question, O son of the truthful woman." Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "None of what you see is from the food of Paradise or from the food of the world. It is something that Allah brought into being in the air by His lofty, overpowering and subduing power, and He said to it: 'Be!' and it was, quicker than the blink of an eye. So eat of what you have asked for, in the name of Allah, and praise Him for it, your Lord will give you more from it and increase you, for He is Originator, Capable, and Grateful."

They said: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, we want you to show us a sign in this sign." Jesus said: "Glory be to Allah! Are you not content with what you have seen in this sign, that you ask for yet another sign?" Then Jesus, peace be upon him, turned to the fish and said: "O fish, return by the permission of Allah alive as you were." So Allah gave it life by His power, and it convulsed and returned, by the permission of Allah, alive and fresh, licking its lips as a lion licks, its eyes turning with a glitter, and its scales returned to it. The people were terrified of it and drew back. When Jesus saw that from them, he said: "What is the matter with you that you ask for a sign, and when your Lord shows it to you, you dislike it? How I fear for you that you will be punished for what you are doing! O fish, return by the permission of Allah as you were." So it returned, by the permission of Allah, roasted as it had been in its first creation.

They said to Jesus: "You, O Spirit of Allah, begin by eating from it, and then we will follow." Jesus said: "God forbid from that! Let the one who sought it begin eating." When the disciples and their companions saw their prophet's refusal of it, they feared that its descent was a wrath and that eating it would be a mutilation, so they shunned it. When Jesus saw that, he called the poor and the chronically ill to it and said: "Eat of the provision of your Lord and the supplication of your prophet, and praise Allah who sent it down to you, so that its wholesome benefit will be yours and its punishment will be upon others. Begin your eating with the name of Allah and end it with the praise of Allah." They did so, and there ate from it one thousand and three hundred people, men and women, each of them departing satisfied and belching. Jesus and the disciples looked, and the spread was in the same state as when it had been sent down from heaven; nothing had been diminished from it. Then it was raised to heaven while they watched. Every poor person who ate from it became rich, and every chronically ill person who ate from it was healed, and they remained wealthy and healthy until they left the world.

The disciples and their companions who had refused to eat from it regretted with great remorse; their eyelids flowed with tears from it, and the sorrow of it remained in their hearts until the day of death. He said: So whenever the table came down after that, the Children of Israel came to it from every place, running, pushing one another: the rich and the poor, the young and the old, the healthy and the sick, some of them mounting upon others. When he saw that, he made it intermittent: it would descend one day and not descend the next. They remained in that state for forty days, descending upon them every other day at the height of the forenoon, and it would not cease to be set down, and they would eat from it, until when they rose, it was lifted from them by Allah's permission toward the atmosphere of the sky, while they watched its shadow on the earth until it vanished from them.

He said: Then Allah revealed to His prophet Jesus, peace be upon him, that he should make My provision the table for the orphans, the poor and the chronically ill, and not for the rich among the people. When he did that, the rich among the people doubted it and despised that, until they doubted it in themselves and cast doubt on it among the people, and they spread ugly and objectionable talk about the matter. Satan obtained his aim from them and cast his whisperings into the hearts of the doubters, until they said to Jesus: "Inform us about the table and its descent from heaven: is it true, for many of our people have doubted it?" Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "You are ruined, by the God of the Messiah! You asked your prophet to ask your Lord for the table, and when He did so and sent it down to you as mercy and provision, and showed you in it signs and lessons, you denied it and doubted it. So rejoice in the punishment, for it is descending upon you unless Allah has mercy upon you."

Allah revealed to Jesus: "I will seize the deniers according to My condition: I will punish among them whoever disbelieved in the table after its descent with a punishment I have not inflicted upon anyone among the worlds." He said: When the doubters about it reached the evening and lay down on their beds in the finest form with their women, secure, then when it was the last part of the night, Allah transformed them into pigs, and in the morning they were pursuing filth in the rubbish heaps.

This is a very strange report. Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Nawadir al-Usul, as cited in the tafsir of al-Qurtubi (6/369), through Zakariyya ibn Hakim, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, with something similar; and al-Qurtubi said: "There is discussion regarding this hadith, and it is not authentic in terms of its chain." Ibn Abi Hatim cut it into pieces in various places of this story, and I have gathered it for him so that its wording is more complete and perfect. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

All these reports indicate that the table was sent down upon the Children of Israel in the days of Jesus son of Mary, as an answer from Allah to his supplication, and as the apparent context of the Noble Qur'an indicates: ﴿Allah said: I am sending it down upon you﴾, the verse.

Some have said that it was never sent down. Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿Send down to us a table from heaven﴾, that he said: "It is a parable that was struck, and nothing descended." This was related by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. Then Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith narrated to me, al-Qasim (that is Ibn Sallam) narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "A table upon which there was food, which they requested when the punishment was presented to them, should they disbelieve; but they refused, so it did not descend upon them."

He also said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan, that he said concerning the table: "It did not descend."

And Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: "al-Hasan used to say: When it was said to them: ﴿Whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds﴾, they said: 'We have no need for it,' so it did not descend."

These are sound chains to Mujahid and al-Hasan. This may be strengthened by the fact that the Christians do not know the report of the table, and it is not in their scripture; had it descended, the motives to transmit it would have been strong, and it would have been present in their scripture as a widely transmitted report, or at least as an individual report. And Allah knows best. However, the majority hold that it did descend, and this is what Ibn Jarir preferred, saying: "Because He, exalted is He, informed of its descent by His saying: ﴿I am sending it down upon you; whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds﴾." He said: "And Allah's promise and threat are true and sincere."

This view, God knows best, is the correct one, as the reports and narrations from the early generations (al-salaf) and others indicate.

The historians mention that Musa ibn Nusayr, the deputy of the Banu Umayyah in the conquest of the lands of the Maghrib, found the table there adorned with pearls and various kinds of jewels. He sent it to the Commander of the Faithful, al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik, the builder of the Mosque of Damascus, but he died while it was on the way. It was then carried to his brother Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who succeeded him as caliph. People saw it and were greatly amazed at it, because of the precious rubies and the unique jewels in it. It is said that this table belonged to Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both. God knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Imran ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Ask your Lord to turn al-Safa into gold for us, and we will believe in you." He said: "Will you really do that?" They said: "Yes." He said: So he supplicated, and Jibril came to him and said: "Your Lord sends you His greetings and says to you: If you wish, al-Safa will become gold for them, but whoever among them disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment that I will not inflict on anyone among the worlds. And if you wish, I will open for them the door of repentance and mercy." He said: "Rather, the door of repentance and mercy."

Then Ahmad, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with this chain.

[[Al-Musnad (1/242) and al-Mustadrak (1/53). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/152) through the route of Sufyan with this chain, and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/196): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

This is the story of the Table (al-Ma'idah), and the surah is named after it, so it is called "Surat al-Ma'idah." It is one of the blessings God bestowed on His servant and messenger Isa (Jesus), upon him be peace, when He answered his supplication by sending it down. God sent it down as a sign, a manifest miraculous proof, and a decisive argument.

Some of the imams have mentioned that the story of the Table is not mentioned in the Gospel, and that the Christians know of it only from the Muslims. God knows best.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When the disciples said﴾, and they are the followers of Isa, upon him be peace: ﴿O Isa, son of Maryam, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?﴾ This is the reading of most reciters. Others read: "Can you ask your Lord (hal tastati'u rabbaka)," meaning: can you ask your Lord ﴿to send down to us a table from heaven﴾.

The ma'idah (table) is the tray (khiwan) on which there is food. Some have mentioned that they asked for this because of their need and poverty, so they asked that a table be sent down to them each day from which they could eat and by which they could strengthen themselves for worship.

He said: ﴿Fear God, if you are believers﴾. That is, Isa, upon him be peace, answered them, telling them: "Fear God, and do not ask for this, for it may be a trial for you. And put your trust in God in seeking provision, if you are believers."

﴿They said: We wish to eat from it﴾, that is, we are in need of eating from it; ﴿and that our hearts may be reassured﴾ when we witness its descent as provision for us from heaven; ﴿and that we may know that you have spoken truly to us﴾, that is, and that our faith in you and our knowledge of your prophethood may increase; ﴿and that we may be among its witnesses﴾, that is, and that we may testify that it is a sign from God, and a proof and argument for your prophethood and the truth of what you have brought.

﴿Isa, son of Maryam, said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, which will be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us﴾. Al-Suddi said: that is, we will take that day on which it descends as a festival, which we and those after us will honour. Sufyan al-Thawri said: meaning a day on which we pray. Qatadah said: they wished that it would be for their descendants after them. From Salman al-Farisi: a lesson for us and for those after us. It was also said: a sufficiency for the first of us and the last of us.

﴿And a sign from You﴾, that is, a proof that You establish of Your power over things and of Your answering my supplication, so that they will believe me in what I convey from You. ﴿And provide for us﴾, that is, from Your presence, provision that is wholesome, without hardship or toil. ﴿And You are the best of providers.﴾

﴿God said: Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you﴾, that is, whoever among your community, O Isa, denies it and opposes it, ﴿I will surely punish him with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds﴾, that is, among the worlds of your time. This is like His saying: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established: Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 46] [[In (D) and (H): "the Day of Resurrection," which is an error.]], and like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire﴾ [An-Nisa: 145].

Ibn Jarir narrated, by way of 'Awf al-A'rabi, from Abu al-Mughirah al-Qawwas, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: "Indeed, the most severely punished people on the Day of Resurrection are three: the hypocrites, those among the people of the Table who disbelieved, and the family of Pharaoh." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/233).]]

Mention of reports transmitted from the early generations (al-salaf) concerning the descent of the Table upon the disciples:

Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Layth, from Uqayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to relate concerning Isa ibn Maryam that he said to the Children of Israel: "Would you be willing to fast for God thirty days, and then ask Him, and He will give you what you ask? For the reward of the worker is due from the one for whom he works." So they did so. Then they said: "O teacher of goodness, you told us that the reward of the worker is due from the one for whom he works, and you commanded us to fast thirty days, so we did. We never worked for anyone for thirty days without him feeding us, when we finished, a meal. So can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" Isa said: ﴿Fear God, if you are believers. They said: We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured, and that we may know that you have spoken truly to us, and that we may be among its witnesses. Isa, son of Maryam, said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, which will be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You; and provide for us, and You are the best of providers. God said: Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you, I will surely punish him with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds﴾. He said: Then the angels came flying with a table from heaven, upon which were seven fish and seven loaves, until they placed it before them. The last of the people ate from it just as the first of them did.

Thus Ibn Jarir narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, from Layth, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ibn 'Abbas used to narrate, and he mentioned something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to us, Abu Zur'a Wahb Allah ibn Rashid narrated to us, Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to us, that Ibn Shihab informed him, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the disciples said to Isa ibn Maryam: "Ask God to send down to us a table from heaven." He said: So the angels descended with a table they carried, upon which were seven fish and seven loaves, and the last of the people ate from it just as the first of them did.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah al-Bahili narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Habib narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar ibn Yasir, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The table descended from heaven, upon it were bread and meat, and they were commanded not to betray, and not to keep any of it for the next day. But they betrayed, stored, and kept some, so they were transformed into apes and swine."

Likewise Ibn Jarir narrated it, from al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/228). Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan, no. (3061), and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hadith which Abu 'Asim and more than one narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar ibn Yasir, as a mawquf (stopping at the companion). We do not know it as marfu' (traced to the Prophet) except from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, who narrated from Hamid ibn Mas'adah, from Sufyan ibn Habib, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, similarly, but without raising it. This is more correct than the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, and we know of no basis for the marfu' hadith."]]. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ibn Bashshar, from Ibn Abi 'Adi, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar, who said: "The table descended, and upon it was fruit from the fruits of Paradise. They were commanded not to betray, not to hide, and not to store. So the people betrayed, hid, and stored, and God transformed them into apes and swine." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/229).]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from a man from the Banu 'Ijl, who said: "I prayed beside Ammar ibn Yasir, and when he finished he said: 'Do you know how the matter of the table of the Children of Israel was?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'They asked Isa ibn Maryam for a table upon which there would be food they could eat from that would never run out.' He said: 'It was said to them: Indeed, it will remain for you as long as you do not hoard it, betray it, or lift it up. If you do, I will surely punish you with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds.' He said: 'Their day had not passed before they hoarded, lifted, and betrayed, so they were punished with a punishment that no one among the worlds had been punished with.' And you, O assembly of the Arabs, used to follow the tails of camels and sheep, then God sent among you a messenger from yourselves, whose lineage and descent you know. He informed you that you would prevail over the non-Arabs, and forbade you to hoard gold and silver. By God, night and day will not pass until you hoard them, and God will punish you with a painful punishment." [[In (D): "they said." In (D): "you hoard them" written as "تكفروهما" (you disbelieve them). Tafsir al-Tabari (11/228).]]

He also said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah, that the table descended upon Isa ibn Maryam, upon it were seven loaves and seven fish, and they ate from it whatever they wished. He said: Some of them stole from it and said: "Perhaps it will not descend tomorrow." So it was lifted up.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: It descended upon Isa ibn Maryam and the disciples, a tray upon which was bread and fish, and they ate from it wherever they alighted, whenever they wished. Khasif said, from Ikrimah and Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas: The table was a fish and loaves. Mujahid said: It was food that descended upon them wherever they alighted. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami said: The table descended as bread and fish. Atiyyah al-Awfi said: The table was fish containing the taste of everything.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He sent it down from heaven upon the Children of Israel, and each day from that table there would descend fruit from Paradise, and they ate whatever they wished of various kinds. Four thousand would sit around it, and when they had eaten, God would replace it with the like of it for others. They remained in this state as long as God willed.

Wahb ibn Munabbih also said: He sent down upon them a loaf of barley and fish, and God placed blessing within their folds, so a group would eat and then leave, then another would come and eat and leave, until all of them had eaten and there was surplus.

Al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, said: Everything descended upon it except meat.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan and Maysarah, and Jarir, from Ata, from Maysarah: When the table was set before the Children of Israel, hands would reach for every kind of food upon it except meat.

From Ikrimah: The bread of the table was made of rice. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn Ali informed us, in what he wrote to me: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, my uncle Abu Abd Allah Abd al-Quddus ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Mirdas al-Abdari, client of the Banu Abd al-Dar, narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman al-Khayr, that he said: When the disciples asked Isa ibn Maryam for the table, he disliked that greatly and said: "Be content with what God has provided you on the earth, and do not ask for a table from heaven. For if it descends upon you, it will be a sign from your Lord. Thamud were only destroyed when they asked their prophet for a sign, and they were tested with it until their ruin came through it. Yet they refused unless he brought it to them." Therefore they said: ﴿We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured﴾, to the end of the verse.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 112–115 (part 2 of 3):

When Jesus saw that they had refused except to ask him to pray for them with it, he stood up, cast off the wool, and put on black hair-cloth, a jubba of hair, and an 'aba' (cloak) of hair. Then he performed wudu' and ghusl, entered his place of prayer, and prayed as much as Allah willed. When he had finished his prayer, he stood upright, facing the qiblah, and set his feet together until they were level, joining the heel to the heel and aligning the toes. He placed his right hand upon his left, above his chest, lowered his gaze, and bowed his head in humility. Then he let his eyes weep, and his tears kept flowing down his cheeks and dripping from the edges of his beard, until the ground in front of his face was wet from his humility. When he saw that, he called upon Allah, saying: ﴿O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven﴾. So Allah sent down upon them a red spread (sufrah) between two clouds: a cloud above it and a cloud beneath it, while they watched it in the air, descending swiftly from the firmament of the sky, coming down toward them. Jesus was weeping out of fear of the conditions that Allah had imposed upon them concerning it, namely that He would punish whoever among them disbelieved after its descent with a punishment He had not inflicted upon anyone among the worlds. He was calling upon Allah from his place and saying: "O Allah, make it a mercy, O my God, do not make it a punishment. O my God, how many a wondrous thing have I asked You for and You have given it to me. O my God, make us grateful to You. O my God, I seek refuge in You from that You should send it down in anger and as a retribution. O my God, make it a safety and a well-being, and do not make it a trial and a mutilation."

He continued to supplicate until the spread settled before Jesus, while the disciples and his companions were around him, smelling a fragrant scent such as they had never smelled before. Jesus and the disciples fell down in prostration to Allah, thanking Him for providing for them from where they had not reckoned, and He showed them in it a great sign, full of wonder and lesson. The Jews came and looked, and they saw a wondrous matter that caused them grief and distress; then they departed in intense rage. Jesus and the disciples and his companions came and sat around the spread, and upon it was a covering cloth. Jesus said: "Who among us is the boldest in uncovering the cloth from this spread, the most trusting of himself, and the best in trial before his Lord? Let him uncover this sign so that we may see it, praise our Lord, mention His name, and eat from His provision which He has given us." The disciples said: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, you are the first of us to do that, and the most worthy of uncovering it." Jesus, peace be upon him, stood, renewed his wudu', then entered his place of prayer and prayed similarly for some rak'ahs, then wept a long weeping and called upon Allah to permit him to uncover it, and to make for him and his people in it blessing and provision. Then he turned and sat by the spread, took the cloth, and said: "In the name of Allah, the best of providers," and he uncovered the spread, and there upon it was a large roasted fish, without scales, with no bones in its interior, from which the fat flowed in a stream, and around it were arranged herbs of every kind except leeks, and at its head was vinegar, and at its tail was salt, and around the herbs were five loaves of bread, on one of which was olives, on another dates, and on another five pomegranates.

Shim'un, the head of the disciples, said to Jesus: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, is this food of the world or food of Paradise?" He said: "Has the time not come for you to take heed from the signs you see, and to desist from probing questions? How I fear for you that you will be punished concerning the cause of the revelation of this verse!" Shim'un said: "By the God of Israel, I did not intend by it a question, O son of the truthful woman." Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "None of what you see is from the food of Paradise or from the food of the world. It is something that Allah brought into being in the air by His lofty, overpowering and subduing power, and He said to it: 'Be!' and it was, quicker than the blink of an eye. So eat of what you have asked for, in the name of Allah, and praise Him for it, your Lord will give you more from it and increase you, for He is Originator, Capable, and Grateful."

They said: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, we want you to show us a sign in this sign." Jesus said: "Glory be to Allah! Are you not content with what you have seen in this sign, that you ask for yet another sign?" Then Jesus, peace be upon him, turned to the fish and said: "O fish, return by the permission of Allah alive as you were." So Allah gave it life by His power, and it convulsed and returned, by the permission of Allah, alive and fresh, licking its lips as a lion licks, its eyes turning with a glitter, and its scales returned to it. The people were terrified of it and drew back. When Jesus saw that from them, he said: "What is the matter with you that you ask for a sign, and when your Lord shows it to you, you dislike it? How I fear for you that you will be punished for what you are doing! O fish, return by the permission of Allah as you were." So it returned, by the permission of Allah, roasted as it had been in its first creation.

They said to Jesus: "You, O Spirit of Allah, begin by eating from it, and then we will follow." Jesus said: "God forbid from that! Let the one who sought it begin eating." When the disciples and their companions saw their prophet's refusal of it, they feared that its descent was a wrath and that eating it would be a mutilation, so they shunned it. When Jesus saw that, he called the poor and the chronically ill to it and said: "Eat of the provision of your Lord and the supplication of your prophet, and praise Allah who sent it down to you, so that its wholesome benefit will be yours and its punishment will be upon others. Begin your eating with the name of Allah and end it with the praise of Allah." They did so, and there ate from it one thousand and three hundred people, men and women, each of them departing satisfied and belching. Jesus and the disciples looked, and the spread was in the same state as when it had been sent down from heaven; nothing had been diminished from it. Then it was raised to heaven while they watched. Every poor person who ate from it became rich, and every chronically ill person who ate from it was healed, and they remained wealthy and healthy until they left the world.

The disciples and their companions who had refused to eat from it regretted with great remorse; their eyelids flowed with tears from it, and the sorrow of it remained in their hearts until the day of death. He said: So whenever the table came down after that, the Children of Israel came to it from every place, running, pushing one another: the rich and the poor, the young and the old, the healthy and the sick, some of them mounting upon others. When he saw that, he made it intermittent: it would descend one day and not descend the next. They remained in that state for forty days, descending upon them every other day at the height of the forenoon, and it would not cease to be set down, and they would eat from it, until when they rose, it was lifted from them by Allah's permission toward the atmosphere of the sky, while they watched its shadow on the earth until it vanished from them.

He said: Then Allah revealed to His prophet Jesus, peace be upon him, that he should make My provision the table for the orphans, the poor and the chronically ill, and not for the rich among the people. When he did that, the rich among the people doubted it and despised that, until they doubted it in themselves and cast doubt on it among the people, and they spread ugly and objectionable talk about the matter. Satan obtained his aim from them and cast his whisperings into the hearts of the doubters, until they said to Jesus: "Inform us about the table and its descent from heaven: is it true, for many of our people have doubted it?" Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "You are ruined, by the God of the Messiah! You asked your prophet to ask your Lord for the table, and when He did so and sent it down to you as mercy and provision, and showed you in it signs and lessons, you denied it and doubted it. So rejoice in the punishment, for it is descending upon you unless Allah has mercy upon you."

Allah revealed to Jesus: "I will seize the deniers according to My condition: I will punish among them whoever disbelieved in the table after its descent with a punishment I have not inflicted upon anyone among the worlds." He said: When the doubters about it reached the evening and lay down on their beds in the finest form with their women, secure, then when it was the last part of the night, Allah transformed them into pigs, and in the morning they were pursuing filth in the rubbish heaps.

This is a very strange report. Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Nawadir al-Usul, as cited in the tafsir of al-Qurtubi (6/369), through Zakariyya ibn Hakim, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, with something similar; and al-Qurtubi said: "There is discussion regarding this hadith, and it is not authentic in terms of its chain." Ibn Abi Hatim cut it into pieces in various places of this story, and I have gathered it for him so that its wording is more complete and perfect. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

All these reports indicate that the table was sent down upon the Children of Israel in the days of Jesus son of Mary, as an answer from Allah to his supplication, and as the apparent context of the Noble Qur'an indicates: ﴿Allah said: I am sending it down upon you﴾, the verse.

Some have said that it was never sent down. Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿Send down to us a table from heaven﴾, that he said: "It is a parable that was struck, and nothing descended." This was related by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. Then Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith narrated to me, al-Qasim (that is Ibn Sallam) narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "A table upon which there was food, which they requested when the punishment was presented to them, should they disbelieve; but they refused, so it did not descend upon them."

He also said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan, that he said concerning the table: "It did not descend."

And Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: "al-Hasan used to say: When it was said to them: ﴿Whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds﴾, they said: 'We have no need for it,' so it did not descend."

These are sound chains to Mujahid and al-Hasan. This may be strengthened by the fact that the Christians do not know the report of the table, and it is not in their scripture; had it descended, the motives to transmit it would have been strong, and it would have been present in their scripture as a widely transmitted report, or at least as an individual report. And Allah knows best. However, the majority hold that it did descend, and this is what Ibn Jarir preferred, saying: "Because He, exalted is He, informed of its descent by His saying: ﴿I am sending it down upon you; whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds﴾." He said: "And Allah's promise and threat are true and sincere."

This view, God knows best, is the correct one, as the reports and narrations from the early generations (al-salaf) and others indicate.

The historians mention that Musa ibn Nusayr, the deputy of the Banu Umayyah in the conquest of the lands of the Maghrib, found the table there adorned with pearls and various kinds of jewels. He sent it to the Commander of the Faithful, al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik, the builder of the Mosque of Damascus, but he died while it was on the way. It was then carried to his brother Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who succeeded him as caliph. People saw it and were greatly amazed at it, because of the precious rubies and the unique jewels in it. It is said that this table belonged to Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both. God knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Imran ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Ask your Lord to turn al-Safa into gold for us, and we will believe in you." He said: "Will you really do that?" They said: "Yes." He said: So he supplicated, and Jibril came to him and said: "Your Lord sends you His greetings and says to you: If you wish, al-Safa will become gold for them, but whoever among them disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment that I will not inflict on anyone among the worlds. And if you wish, I will open for them the door of repentance and mercy." He said: "Rather, the door of repentance and mercy."

Then Ahmad, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with this chain.

[[Al-Musnad (1/242) and al-Mustadrak (1/53). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/152) through the route of Sufyan with this chain, and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/196): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

This is the story of the Table (al-Ma'idah), and the surah is named after it, so it is called "Surat al-Ma'idah." It is one of the blessings God bestowed on His servant and messenger Isa (Jesus), upon him be peace, when He answered his supplication by sending it down. God sent it down as a sign, a manifest miraculous proof, and a decisive argument.

Some of the imams have mentioned that the story of the Table is not mentioned in the Gospel, and that the Christians know of it only from the Muslims. God knows best.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When the disciples said﴾, and they are the followers of Isa, upon him be peace: ﴿O Isa, son of Maryam, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?﴾ This is the reading of most reciters. Others read: "Can you ask your Lord (hal tastati'u rabbaka)," meaning: can you ask your Lord ﴿to send down to us a table from heaven﴾.

The ma'idah (table) is the tray (khiwan) on which there is food. Some have mentioned that they asked for this because of their need and poverty, so they asked that a table be sent down to them each day from which they could eat and by which they could strengthen themselves for worship.

He said: ﴿Fear God, if you are believers﴾. That is, Isa, upon him be peace, answered them, telling them: "Fear God, and do not ask for this, for it may be a trial for you. And put your trust in God in seeking provision, if you are believers."

﴿They said: We wish to eat from it﴾, that is, we are in need of eating from it; ﴿and that our hearts may be reassured﴾ when we witness its descent as provision for us from heaven; ﴿and that we may know that you have spoken truly to us﴾, that is, and that our faith in you and our knowledge of your prophethood may increase; ﴿and that we may be among its witnesses﴾, that is, and that we may testify that it is a sign from God, and a proof and argument for your prophethood and the truth of what you have brought.

﴿Isa, son of Maryam, said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, which will be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us﴾. Al-Suddi said: that is, we will take that day on which it descends as a festival, which we and those after us will honour. Sufyan al-Thawri said: meaning a day on which we pray. Qatadah said: they wished that it would be for their descendants after them. From Salman al-Farisi: a lesson for us and for those after us. It was also said: a sufficiency for the first of us and the last of us.

﴿And a sign from You﴾, that is, a proof that You establish of Your power over things and of Your answering my supplication, so that they will believe me in what I convey from You. ﴿And provide for us﴾, that is, from Your presence, provision that is wholesome, without hardship or toil. ﴿And You are the best of providers.﴾

﴿God said: Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you﴾, that is, whoever among your community, O Isa, denies it and opposes it, ﴿I will surely punish him with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds﴾, that is, among the worlds of your time. This is like His saying: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established: Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 46] [[In (D) and (H): "the Day of Resurrection," which is an error.]], and like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire﴾ [An-Nisa: 145].

Ibn Jarir narrated, by way of 'Awf al-A'rabi, from Abu al-Mughirah al-Qawwas, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: "Indeed, the most severely punished people on the Day of Resurrection are three: the hypocrites, those among the people of the Table who disbelieved, and the family of Pharaoh." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/233).]]

Mention of reports transmitted from the early generations (al-salaf) concerning the descent of the Table upon the disciples:

Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Layth, from Uqayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to relate concerning Isa ibn Maryam that he said to the Children of Israel: "Would you be willing to fast for God thirty days, and then ask Him, and He will give you what you ask? For the reward of the worker is due from the one for whom he works." So they did so. Then they said: "O teacher of goodness, you told us that the reward of the worker is due from the one for whom he works, and you commanded us to fast thirty days, so we did. We never worked for anyone for thirty days without him feeding us, when we finished, a meal. So can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" Isa said: ﴿Fear God, if you are believers. They said: We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured, and that we may know that you have spoken truly to us, and that we may be among its witnesses. Isa, son of Maryam, said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, which will be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You; and provide for us, and You are the best of providers. God said: Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you, I will surely punish him with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds﴾. He said: Then the angels came flying with a table from heaven, upon which were seven fish and seven loaves, until they placed it before them. The last of the people ate from it just as the first of them did.

Thus Ibn Jarir narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, from Layth, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ibn 'Abbas used to narrate, and he mentioned something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to us, Abu Zur'a Wahb Allah ibn Rashid narrated to us, Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to us, that Ibn Shihab informed him, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the disciples said to Isa ibn Maryam: "Ask God to send down to us a table from heaven." He said: So the angels descended with a table they carried, upon which were seven fish and seven loaves, and the last of the people ate from it just as the first of them did.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah al-Bahili narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Habib narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar ibn Yasir, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The table descended from heaven, upon it were bread and meat, and they were commanded not to betray, and not to keep any of it for the next day. But they betrayed, stored, and kept some, so they were transformed into apes and swine."

Likewise Ibn Jarir narrated it, from al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/228). Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan, no. (3061), and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hadith which Abu 'Asim and more than one narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar ibn Yasir, as a mawquf (stopping at the companion). We do not know it as marfu' (traced to the Prophet) except from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, who narrated from Hamid ibn Mas'adah, from Sufyan ibn Habib, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, similarly, but without raising it. This is more correct than the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, and we know of no basis for the marfu' hadith."]]. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ibn Bashshar, from Ibn Abi 'Adi, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Khilas, from Ammar, who said: "The table descended, and upon it was fruit from the fruits of Paradise. They were commanded not to betray, not to hide, and not to store. So the people betrayed, hid, and stored, and God transformed them into apes and swine." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (11/229).]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from a man from the Banu 'Ijl, who said: "I prayed beside Ammar ibn Yasir, and when he finished he said: 'Do you know how the matter of the table of the Children of Israel was?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'They asked Isa ibn Maryam for a table upon which there would be food they could eat from that would never run out.' He said: 'It was said to them: Indeed, it will remain for you as long as you do not hoard it, betray it, or lift it up. If you do, I will surely punish you with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds.' He said: 'Their day had not passed before they hoarded, lifted, and betrayed, so they were punished with a punishment that no one among the worlds had been punished with.' And you, O assembly of the Arabs, used to follow the tails of camels and sheep, then God sent among you a messenger from yourselves, whose lineage and descent you know. He informed you that you would prevail over the non-Arabs, and forbade you to hoard gold and silver. By God, night and day will not pass until you hoard them, and God will punish you with a painful punishment." [[In (D): "they said." In (D): "you hoard them" written as "تكفروهما" (you disbelieve them). Tafsir al-Tabari (11/228).]]

He also said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah, that the table descended upon Isa ibn Maryam, upon it were seven loaves and seven fish, and they ate from it whatever they wished. He said: Some of them stole from it and said: "Perhaps it will not descend tomorrow." So it was lifted up.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: It descended upon Isa ibn Maryam and the disciples, a tray upon which was bread and fish, and they ate from it wherever they alighted, whenever they wished. Khasif said, from Ikrimah and Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas: The table was a fish and loaves. Mujahid said: It was food that descended upon them wherever they alighted. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami said: The table descended as bread and fish. Atiyyah al-Awfi said: The table was fish containing the taste of everything.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He sent it down from heaven upon the Children of Israel, and each day from that table there would descend fruit from Paradise, and they ate whatever they wished of various kinds. Four thousand would sit around it, and when they had eaten, God would replace it with the like of it for others. They remained in this state as long as God willed.

Wahb ibn Munabbih also said: He sent down upon them a loaf of barley and fish, and God placed blessing within their folds, so a group would eat and then leave, then another would come and eat and leave, until all of them had eaten and there was surplus.

Al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, said: Everything descended upon it except meat.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan and Maysarah, and Jarir, from Ata, from Maysarah: When the table was set before the Children of Israel, hands would reach for every kind of food upon it except meat.

From Ikrimah: The bread of the table was made of rice. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn Ali informed us, in what he wrote to me: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, my uncle Abu Abd Allah Abd al-Quddus ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Mirdas al-Abdari, client of the Banu Abd al-Dar, narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman al-Khayr, that he said: When the disciples asked Isa ibn Maryam for the table, he disliked that greatly and said: "Be content with what God has provided you on the earth, and do not ask for a table from heaven. For if it descends upon you, it will be a sign from your Lord. Thamud were only destroyed when they asked their prophet for a sign, and they were tested with it until their ruin came through it. Yet they refused unless he brought it to them." Therefore they said: ﴿We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured﴾, to the end of the verse.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 5, verses 112–115 (part 2 of 3):

When Jesus saw that they had refused except to ask him to pray for them with it, he stood up, cast off the wool, and put on black hair-cloth, a jubba of hair, and an 'aba' (cloak) of hair. Then he performed wudu' and ghusl, entered his place of prayer, and prayed as much as Allah willed. When he had finished his prayer, he stood upright, facing the qiblah, and set his feet together until they were level, joining the heel to the heel and aligning the toes. He placed his right hand upon his left, above his chest, lowered his gaze, and bowed his head in humility. Then he let his eyes weep, and his tears kept flowing down his cheeks and dripping from the edges of his beard, until the ground in front of his face was wet from his humility. When he saw that, he called upon Allah, saying: ﴿O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven﴾. So Allah sent down upon them a red spread (sufrah) between two clouds: a cloud above it and a cloud beneath it, while they watched it in the air, descending swiftly from the firmament of the sky, coming down toward them. Jesus was weeping out of fear of the conditions that Allah had imposed upon them concerning it, namely that He would punish whoever among them disbelieved after its descent with a punishment He had not inflicted upon anyone among the worlds. He was calling upon Allah from his place and saying: "O Allah, make it a mercy, O my God, do not make it a punishment. O my God, how many a wondrous thing have I asked You for and You have given it to me. O my God, make us grateful to You. O my God, I seek refuge in You from that You should send it down in anger and as a retribution. O my God, make it a safety and a well-being, and do not make it a trial and a mutilation."

He continued to supplicate until the spread settled before Jesus, while the disciples and his companions were around him, smelling a fragrant scent such as they had never smelled before. Jesus and the disciples fell down in prostration to Allah, thanking Him for providing for them from where they had not reckoned, and He showed them in it a great sign, full of wonder and lesson. The Jews came and looked, and they saw a wondrous matter that caused them grief and distress; then they departed in intense rage. Jesus and the disciples and his companions came and sat around the spread, and upon it was a covering cloth. Jesus said: "Who among us is the boldest in uncovering the cloth from this spread, the most trusting of himself, and the best in trial before his Lord? Let him uncover this sign so that we may see it, praise our Lord, mention His name, and eat from His provision which He has given us." The disciples said: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, you are the first of us to do that, and the most worthy of uncovering it." Jesus, peace be upon him, stood, renewed his wudu', then entered his place of prayer and prayed similarly for some rak'ahs, then wept a long weeping and called upon Allah to permit him to uncover it, and to make for him and his people in it blessing and provision. Then he turned and sat by the spread, took the cloth, and said: "In the name of Allah, the best of providers," and he uncovered the spread, and there upon it was a large roasted fish, without scales, with no bones in its interior, from which the fat flowed in a stream, and around it were arranged herbs of every kind except leeks, and at its head was vinegar, and at its tail was salt, and around the herbs were five loaves of bread, on one of which was olives, on another dates, and on another five pomegranates.

Shim'un, the head of the disciples, said to Jesus: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, is this food of the world or food of Paradise?" He said: "Has the time not come for you to take heed from the signs you see, and to desist from probing questions? How I fear for you that you will be punished concerning the cause of the revelation of this verse!" Shim'un said: "By the God of Israel, I did not intend by it a question, O son of the truthful woman." Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "None of what you see is from the food of Paradise or from the food of the world. It is something that Allah brought into being in the air by His lofty, overpowering and subduing power, and He said to it: 'Be!' and it was, quicker than the blink of an eye. So eat of what you have asked for, in the name of Allah, and praise Him for it, your Lord will give you more from it and increase you, for He is Originator, Capable, and Grateful."

They said: "O Spirit of Allah and His Word, we want you to show us a sign in this sign." Jesus said: "Glory be to Allah! Are you not content with what you have seen in this sign, that you ask for yet another sign?" Then Jesus, peace be upon him, turned to the fish and said: "O fish, return by the permission of Allah alive as you were." So Allah gave it life by His power, and it convulsed and returned, by the permission of Allah, alive and fresh, licking its lips as a lion licks, its eyes turning with a glitter, and its scales returned to it. The people were terrified of it and drew back. When Jesus saw that from them, he said: "What is the matter with you that you ask for a sign, and when your Lord shows it to you, you dislike it? How I fear for you that you will be punished for what you are doing! O fish, return by the permission of Allah as you were." So it returned, by the permission of Allah, roasted as it had been in its first creation.

They said to Jesus: "You, O Spirit of Allah, begin by eating from it, and then we will follow." Jesus said: "God forbid from that! Let the one who sought it begin eating." When the disciples and their companions saw their prophet's refusal of it, they feared that its descent was a wrath and that eating it would be a mutilation, so they shunned it. When Jesus saw that, he called the poor and the chronically ill to it and said: "Eat of the provision of your Lord and the supplication of your prophet, and praise Allah who sent it down to you, so that its wholesome benefit will be yours and its punishment will be upon others. Begin your eating with the name of Allah and end it with the praise of Allah." They did so, and there ate from it one thousand and three hundred people, men and women, each of them departing satisfied and belching. Jesus and the disciples looked, and the spread was in the same state as when it had been sent down from heaven; nothing had been diminished from it. Then it was raised to heaven while they watched. Every poor person who ate from it became rich, and every chronically ill person who ate from it was healed, and they remained wealthy and healthy until they left the world.

The disciples and their companions who had refused to eat from it regretted with great remorse; their eyelids flowed with tears from it, and the sorrow of it remained in their hearts until the day of death. He said: So whenever the table came down after that, the Children of Israel came to it from every place, running, pushing one another: the rich and the poor, the young and the old, the healthy and the sick, some of them mounting upon others. When he saw that, he made it intermittent: it would descend one day and not descend the next. They remained in that state for forty days, descending upon them every other day at the height of the forenoon, and it would not cease to be set down, and they would eat from it, until when they rose, it was lifted from them by Allah's permission toward the atmosphere of the sky, while they watched its shadow on the earth until it vanished from them.

He said: Then Allah revealed to His prophet Jesus, peace be upon him, that he should make My provision the table for the orphans, the poor and the chronically ill, and not for the rich among the people. When he did that, the rich among the people doubted it and despised that, until they doubted it in themselves and cast doubt on it among the people, and they spread ugly and objectionable talk about the matter. Satan obtained his aim from them and cast his whisperings into the hearts of the doubters, until they said to Jesus: "Inform us about the table and its descent from heaven: is it true, for many of our people have doubted it?" Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "You are ruined, by the God of the Messiah! You asked your prophet to ask your Lord for the table, and when He did so and sent it down to you as mercy and provision, and showed you in it signs and lessons, you denied it and doubted it. So rejoice in the punishment, for it is descending upon you unless Allah has mercy upon you."

Allah revealed to Jesus: "I will seize the deniers according to My condition: I will punish among them whoever disbelieved in the table after its descent with a punishment I have not inflicted upon anyone among the worlds." He said: When the doubters about it reached the evening and lay down on their beds in the finest form with their women, secure, then when it was the last part of the night, Allah transformed them into pigs, and in the morning they were pursuing filth in the rubbish heaps.

This is a very strange report. Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Nawadir al-Usul, as cited in the tafsir of al-Qurtubi (6/369), through Zakariyya ibn Hakim, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, with something similar; and al-Qurtubi said: "There is discussion regarding this hadith, and it is not authentic in terms of its chain." Ibn Abi Hatim cut it into pieces in various places of this story, and I have gathered it for him so that its wording is more complete and perfect. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

All these reports indicate that the table was sent down upon the Children of Israel in the days of Jesus son of Mary, as an answer from Allah to his supplication, and as the apparent context of the Noble Qur'an indicates: ﴿Allah said: I am sending it down upon you﴾, the verse.

Some have said that it was never sent down. Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿Send down to us a table from heaven﴾, that he said: "It is a parable that was struck, and nothing descended." This was related by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. Then Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith narrated to me, al-Qasim (that is Ibn Sallam) narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "A table upon which there was food, which they requested when the punishment was presented to them, should they disbelieve; but they refused, so it did not descend upon them."

He also said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan, that he said concerning the table: "It did not descend."

And Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: "al-Hasan used to say: When it was said to them: ﴿Whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds﴾, they said: 'We have no need for it,' so it did not descend."

These are sound chains to Mujahid and al-Hasan. This may be strengthened by the fact that the Christians do not know the report of the table, and it is not in their scripture; had it descended, the motives to transmit it would have been strong, and it would have been present in their scripture as a widely transmitted report, or at least as an individual report. And Allah knows best. However, the majority hold that it did descend, and this is what Ibn Jarir preferred, saying: "Because He, exalted is He, informed of its descent by His saying: ﴿I am sending it down upon you; whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds﴾." He said: "And Allah's promise and threat are true and sincere."

This view, God knows best, is the correct one, as the reports and narrations from the early generations (al-salaf) and others indicate.

The historians mention that Musa ibn Nusayr, the deputy of the Banu Umayyah in the conquest of the lands of the Maghrib, found the table there adorned with pearls and various kinds of jewels. He sent it to the Commander of the Faithful, al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik, the builder of the Mosque of Damascus, but he died while it was on the way. It was then carried to his brother Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who succeeded him as caliph. People saw it and were greatly amazed at it, because of the precious rubies and the unique jewels in it. It is said that this table belonged to Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both. God knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Imran ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Ask your Lord to turn al-Safa into gold for us, and we will believe in you." He said: "Will you really do that?" They said: "Yes." He said: So he supplicated, and Jibril came to him and said: "Your Lord sends you His greetings and says to you: If you wish, al-Safa will become gold for them, but whoever among them disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment that I will not inflict on anyone among the worlds. And if you wish, I will open for them the door of repentance and mercy." He said: "Rather, the door of repentance and mercy."

Then Ahmad, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with this chain.

[[Al-Musnad (1/242) and al-Mustadrak (1/53). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/152) through the route of Sufyan with this chain, and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/196): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

This too is among the things that Allah, exalted is He, addresses to His servant and messenger Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, saying to him on the Day of Resurrection in the presence of those who took him and his mother as two gods besides Allah: ﴿And when Allah says, "O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'"﴾. This is a warning to the Christians and a rebuke and reproach before all the witnesses. This is what Qatadah and others said, and Qatadah cited as evidence for it the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿This is a day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness﴾.

Al-Suddi said: this address and reply take place in the world (dunya).

Ibn Jarir said: this is the correct view, and it occurred when Allah raised him to the heaven of this world. Ibn Jarir argued for this on two grounds:

The first: that the statement uses the past tense.

The second: the words ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants﴾ and ﴿If You forgive them﴾.

These two proofs are open to scrutiny, because many matters of the Day of Resurrection are mentioned in the past tense, to indicate that they are certain and established. The meaning of the words ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants﴾ and so on is disavowal of them and referring the matter of their fate to Allah, and making that conditional does not imply that the condition occurs, as in similar verses.

What Qatadah and others said is the most evident, and Allah knows best: that this will happen on the Day of Resurrection, to show the warning to the Christians and their rebuke and reproach before all the witnesses on the Day of Resurrection. A hadith with a raised (marfu') chain has been related to this effect, narrated by the hafiz Ibn Asakir in the biography of Abu 'Abd Allah, the freedman of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, who was trustworthy. He said: I heard Abu Burdah narrating to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from his father Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the prophets will be called with their nations. Then Jesus will be called, and Allah will remind him of His blessing upon him, and he will acknowledge it. He will say: ﴿O Jesus son of Mary, remember My blessing upon you and upon your mother﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 110], then He will say: ﴿Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'﴾. He will deny that he said it. Then the Christians will be brought and questioned, and they will say: 'Yes, he commanded us to do that.' He said: Then the hair of Jesus, peace be upon him, will be lengthened, and every angel will take hold of a strand of hair from his head and body. He will kneel before Allah, mighty and majestic, for the length of a thousand years, until the proof is established against them, the cross is raised over them, and they are taken to the Fire." This is a strange (gharib) and rare (aziz) hadith. [Tarikh Dimashq (19/128, manuscript section) and al-Mukhtasar of Ibn Manzur (29/54).]

* *

His words: ﴿Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say﴾ are a demonstration of perfect courtesy in the reply, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Tawus, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Jesus will be confronted with his argument, and Allah will address him with the words: ﴿O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?"﴾. Abu Hurayrah said, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Then Allah addressed him: ﴿Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say﴾," up to the end of the verse.

Al-Thawri narrated it, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from Tawus, in a similar form.

* *

His words: ﴿If I had said it, You would have known it﴾ mean: if this came from me, You would have known it, O Lord, for nothing that I said or intended or concealed in my soul is hidden from You. Therefore He said: ﴿You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Yours. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen. I did not say to them except what You commanded me, that "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord"﴾ [to convey], ﴿that "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾ That is: I only called them to that with which You sent me and commanded me to convey, ﴿"Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord"﴾, meaning: this is what I said to them. ﴿And I was a witness over them while I was among them﴾, meaning: I bore witness over their deeds while I was among them. ﴿But when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things﴾.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I and Sufyan al-Thawri went to al-Mughirah ibn al-Nu'man, and he dictated it to Sufyan while I was with him. When he stood up, I copied it from Sufyan. He narrated to us, saying: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us and gave a sermon, saying: "O people, you will be gathered to Allah, mighty and majestic, barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, just as We began the first creation, We shall bring it back. The first of creation to be clothed will be Abraham. Behold, some men of my nation will be brought and taken to the left side, and I will say: 'My companions!' It will be said: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.' Then I will say as the righteous servant said: ﴿And I was a witness over them while I was among them. But when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things. If You punish them, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾. It will be said: 'These have not ceased to turn back on their heels since you departed from them.'"

Al-Bukhari narrated it under this verse from al-Walid, from Abu Shu'bah; and from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from Sufyan al-Thawri, both from al-Mughirah ibn al-Nu'man, with the same wording. [Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (2638); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4625); and Muslim related it in his Sahih, no. (3023).]

* *

His words: ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ comprise the handing over of the matter to Allah, mighty and majestic, for He is the One who does what He wills, who is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. It also includes disavowal of the Christians who lied against Allah and His messenger, and who made for Allah rivals, a consort and a son. Exalted is Allah far above what they say. This verse is of great significance and a wondrous report. It has been related in a hadith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood in prayer with it throughout the night until morning, repeating it.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, Fulayt al-'Amiri narrated to me, from Jasrah al-'Amiriyyah, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed one night, reciting one verse until morning, bowing with it and prostrating with it: ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾. When morning came, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you kept reciting this verse until morning, bowing and prostrating with it?" He said: "I asked my Lord, mighty and majestic, for intercession for my nation, and He gave it to me, and it will be attained, Allah willing, by whoever does not associate anything with Allah." [Al-Musnad (5/149).]

Another route and another context: Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, Qudamah ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Jasrah bint Dajajah narrated to me: that she set out for 'Umrah, and reached al-Rabadhah, and heard Abu Dharr say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood one night for the 'Isha prayer, led the people in prayer, then some of his companions remained behind praying. When he saw their standing and their staying behind, he went back to his dwelling. When he saw that the people had cleared the place, he returned to his place and prayed. I came and stood behind him, and he gestured to me with his right hand, so I stood on his right. Then Ibn Mas'ud came and stood behind me and behind him, and he gestured to him with his left hand, so he stood on his left. Thus the three of us stood, each praying by himself, reciting from the Qur'an whatever Allah willed. He stood with one verse of the Qur'an, repeating it until the morning prayer. When morning came, I gestured to 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud to ask him what he intended by what he did last night. Ibn Mas'ud gestured with his hand: "I will not ask him about anything until he tells me." I said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, you stood with one verse of the Qur'an while the whole Qur'an was with you! If one of us had done this, we would have been blamed for it." He said: "I supplicated for my nation." I said: "And what were you answered? Or what was your reply?" He said: "I was answered with that which, if many of them had glimpsed it, they would have abandoned the prayer." I said: "Shall I not give the good news to the people?" He said: "Yes." So I went off at a brisk pace, about the distance of a stone's throw. 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you send this news to the people, they will shrink back from worship." So he called out to him: "Come back," and he came back. And that verse was: ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾. [Al-Musnad (5/149).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to him, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited the words of Jesus: ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾, then raised his hands and said: "O Allah, my nation," and wept. Allah said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad, and your Lord knows best, and ask him what makes him weep." Jibril came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told him what he had said. Allah said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad and say: 'We shall indeed please you concerning your nation, and We will not grieve you.'" [Also related by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (202), by the route of Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la from Ibn Wahb, in a similar form.]

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Ibn Hubayrah narrated to us, that he heard Abu Tamim al-Jaishani say: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib narrated to me, I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was absent from us one day and did not come out, until we thought he would not come out. When he came out, he prostrated a prostration, and we thought his soul had been taken in it. When he raised his head, he said: "My Lord, mighty and majestic, consulted me about my nation: 'What shall I do with them?' I said: 'Whatever You will, O Lord, they are Your creation and Your servants.' He consulted me a second time, and I said to Him the same. He said: 'I will not disgrace you concerning your nation, O Muhammad.' He gave me the good news that the first of my nation to enter Paradise with me will be seventy thousand, with each thousand seventy thousand, with no reckoning for them. Then He sent to me and said: 'Ask, and you will be given; petition, and you will be granted.'" I said to His messenger: "Will my Lord give me my request?"
